seo.description: Trek to Everest Base Camp in 3 days and return to Kathmandu by a helicopter. Checkout our itinerary, cost and contact us for booking.

overview:
Trekking in the foothills of the highest mountain in the world is an incredible adventure. Everest Base Camp trek is the most famous among these Himalayan adventures. This excellent trek takes you to the base camp of Mt Everest (8848.86m), passing through magical landscapes.

This short-duration EBC trek is ideal for those travelers who have a short time in their schedule. This trek package includes the luxury of helicopter travel in the itinerary as well. It is also perfect for those who cannot trek or do not want to trek for a long duration in these challenging terrains.

However, you will get ample opportunity to explore and observe the beautiful region. This shortest itinerary to Everest Base Camp saves you time so that you can complete this journey in a quick time. There are natural trails and diverse wildlife that are of great ecological significance. You will also pass through forested trails and other natural landmarks of these regions.

The trek journey starts as you take a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. You will then travel to Everest Base Camp from Lukla on a helicopter the next day and return. You can also fly to Namche on a helicopter and then trek your way back to Lukla. If you arrive on time and the weather remains good, you can also return to Kathmandu on the same day.

However, if the weather remains unfavorable, you will rest for the evening, at Lukla. You can return to Kathmandu on a scenic flight from Lukla the next day. This short trekking journey is relatively cheaper than Everest Base Camp helicopter tour. You will also get to explore the region more in this itinerary.

We provide this incredible 3 days Everest Base Camp trek package at a reasonable cost. Read on to know more about this wonderful trek and other related information in detail.

Highlights of This Trip

  • Awe-inspiring views of snow-capped mountains of the region, including Mt. Everest, Mt Cho Oyu, Mt Ama Dablam, Mt Makalu, Mt Lhotse, Mt Cholatse, Mt Nuptse, Mt Tawache, and others
  • The incredible atmosphere of the Everest Base Camp and its surrounding
  • Majestic view of Mount Everest from an extraordinary perspective
  • Exploring culture and heritage of local Sherpa people
  • Passing alongside the Dudh Koshi river and crossing various suspension bridges
  • Birdseye aerial view from the helicopter trip
  • Passing through Rhododendron forested trails and other natural vegetation of the region
  • Incredible welcome and warm hospitality of local people

itinerary.title: Fly From Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft) and Trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html:
We will start our 3 day trek to Everest Base Camp journey with a scenic early morning flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. Our representative will pick you up and then transfer you to TIA airport from where you can take a flight. Moreover, we can observe majestic views of the snow-capped mountains of the region.

There are various other natural landmarks, including green hills, serene rivers, and deep mountain valleys. Besides that, you can also observe landmarks of the region from a different perspective during this flight. It takes around 35-40 minutes to arrive at Lukla.

The Lukla airport, also known as Tenzing Hillary airport, is also considered one of the most dangerous airports in the world. It has a runway of just 500 m with a cliffside on one side. There you can observe incredible natural landmarks of the region.

After arriving in Lukla, you can have your breakfast enjoying the beautiful scenery. Then, you will trek to Phakding which marks an official start of your adventure. You will cross suspension bridges to reach the settlements.

On the first day of your trek you will pass through beautiful villages like Cheplung. The first day itself is full of breathtaking scenery.  Your first overnight stay will be in a beautiful village of Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek From Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
After breakfast in the lodge and observing the beautiful Himalayan sunrise, we will continue our journey to Namche Bazar.

Namche Bazaar is a famous Himalayan town and commercial capital of the region. People from all around the Khumbu region come to trade in the Namche Bazaar. The trek to Namche would take anywhere between 6 to 7 hours, based on your walking speed. The beautiful green vegetation and natural landscapes of the region will enchant any traveler. Trekkers will also pass through forested trails with rhododendron, juniper, and oak trees along banks of the Dudhkoshi River. We will pass through various suspension bridges along the route as well. The trail also provides you with a view of the tip of Mount Everest from viewpoints along the trail. The scenic journey will finally lead you to Namche Bazar, where you will spend the night in a guest house.

itinerary.title: Fly from Namche Bazaar (5,545 m / 18,192 ft) to Kala Patthar for a landing then fly over Everest Base Camp (5,364 m / 17,598 ft) before continuing to Kathmandu, 2-3 hours.
itinerary.html: Today is an exciting day as you will fly from Namche Bazaar to Kala Patthar with fly over to Everest Base Camp. Kala Patthar is the highest point of your entire Everest Base Camp trip. As a matter of fact, you will see the entire Everest region much closer than anywhere else. The highest peak in the world, covered with snow, offers you the best experience with Several other stunning mountains can also be seen from this viewpoint. However, it is important to note that the flight landing duration is determined by the weather condition of that particular day and hence, can fluctuate. After taking off from Kala Patthar, you will fly directly toward Kathmandu. The helicopter may make a brief stop in Lukla for refueling before continuing to Kathmandu.

sections.title: Why Take This Everest Base Camp Trek 3 Days?
sections.html:
Why Take This Everest Base Camp Trek 3 Days?

Incredible scenic vista from a helicopter

This incredible trek provides an opportunity to observe the beautiful Himalayan scenic vista of the region. There you can also observe magical views of snow-capped mountains and green hills, serene water streams, and deep mountain valleys. Observing these beautiful trails from the top of the helicopter is an incredible once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

Cheaper than a helicopter trip

This incredible short-duration Everest Base Camp trek is cheaper than other helicopter trips in the region. This outstanding trek takes you to Lukla on a mountain flight and then to Everest Base Camp on a helicopter. On returning, you also have the option of trekking your way back to Lukla from Namche. This trip will cost you less than the short round helicopter trip that takes place in a single day.

Exploration of Everest region

Trekkers will also have a longer duration of exploring around the region in this short trek. You can explore the rare flora and fauna of the area. There are various beautiful, naturally diverse trails along the part. You can explore other cultural landmarks of these regions as well. There are Buddhist monasteries, mani walls, chortens, and small temples that will enchant you along the trail.

Short and swift itinerary

The three-day Everest Base Camp trek is a short itinerary trek in the Himalayan region that provides an incredible experience. The trip skips the challenging long-distance trekking route, which would take around two weeks to reach EBC. Therefore, this 3-day trek to Everest Base Camp is quite popular.

Safe and convenient tour

Our trip is conducted by highly experienced helicopter pilots and team members. Therefore, it is safe and convenient to take this tour with us. Various safety measures remain in place for your safety and comfort. There are facilities for first aid and other emergencies, including supplementary oxygen.

How Difficult is 3 Days Everest Base Camp Trek?

This 3 day trek to Everest Base Camp is a relatively less challenging trek in the region. This short-duration adventure will take you to the Everest Base Camp in a short amount of time. You do not have to trek uphill through rugged terrains at all. However, if you want to explore the region on foot, you can trek from Namche to Lukla while returning from EBC. This trek itinerary allows you to explore the region comfortably. There are high chances of unpredictable weather with heavy snowfall and overcast conditions. Besides that, you should also carry warm clothes and trekking gear to trek along in these terrains. You should also need to tackle altitude sickness as you will cover a lot of altitude in a short amount of time. There are high chances of you getting acute mountain sickness, so you should prepare well with rest and regular hydration. Overall, Everest Base Camp trek 3 days is ideal with proper packing and preparation.

Best Time for 3 Days Everest Base Camp Trek

This Everest Base Camp trek is ideal in the peak time of the Autumn and Spring season. Moreover, these seasons bring perfect and stable weather conditions and moderate temperatures. There are no weather-related delays and obstacles like heavy precipitation and snowfall. Therefore, thousands of trekkers choose this season as the ideal time for their 3 day trek to Everest Base Camp.

Autumn season

The Autumn season is the best time for this 3 days trek to Everest Base Camp. Moreover, there are other beautiful aspects of trekking in Autumn as well. You will get the best views of snow-capped mountains in a clear blue sky. There are mild temperatures that are ideal for trekking in the daytime. This incredible season is also a cultural time in the region, with many festivals, including Dashain, Tihar, and others. You can therefore explore the area and observe the beautiful cultural landscapes of the region.

Spring season

Spring is another ideal time for this trek in this Everest region. There are excellent weather conditions, with wildflowers blooming all over the hills. These colorful trails and pleasant atmosphere are a highlight of the trek in this season. There are moderate temperatures with less precipitation in the area. Trekkers can continue their trek in a tranquil and peaceful atmosphere. Besides that, there are a large number of trekkers taking this trek this season. This means that you can have a fabulous group trekking atmosphere in the region.

Offseasons trek

Off-season treks are also possible, but it comes with its own set of challenges. There are various challenging weather conditions in winters, including heavy snowfall and extremely cold weather. Other weather-related challenges in the region make these off-seasons quite tricky along trails. Monsoon season provides heavy rainfall and slippery, muddy trails that are difficult to cross. There are various weather-related delays and cancelations in the monsoon season as well. Therefore, Autumn and Spring are ideal for trekking to the Everest Base Camp.

Essential Tips for 3 Day trek to Everest Base Camp

  • Get proper acclimatization along the route as you will gain a lot of altitude in a short amount of time
  • Carry warm clothes and trekking gear for this trek
  • Add spare days on your trip for delays and cancellations
  • Carry sunscreens and moisturizers to preventing sunburns
  • Carry water, snacks, like protein bars, chocolate bars, and others along the trail
  • Trek in a group or hire a professional trekking guide and porter
  • Carry a proper camera to take incredible pictures along the trail
  • Start your journey early to arrive at your destination before dark
  • Get proper travel insurance along these trails

Final Say

Everest Base Camp trek is a famous Himalayan trek popular among trekkers all around the world. This incredible trek leads you to the base camp of the highest mountain in the world. This short-duration EBC trek allows you to complete your journey in a short amount of time. This makes this outstanding trip ideal for those who do not have much time in their schedule. This short trip also provides you with a helicopter tour along with a trekking opportunity. These magical forested trails and wildlife, and other landmarks are highlights of these regions. The itinerary has the option of taking a helicopter trip to Namche and then trekking back to Lukla. You can also return to Kathmandu on the same day if the weather remains suitable. Moreover, this short trekking journey is relatively cheaper than the Everest Base Camp helicopter tour. We hope you learned about this incredible 3 days Everest Base Camp trek package through this article. Contact us for more information about this trek.

title: 3 Days Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek
summary: Embark on a 3 Days Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek, offering stunning sunrise views over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Experience the rich culture, scenic landscapes, and vibrant local villages of Nepal's Himalayas on this short yet unforgettable adventure.

seo.title: 3 Days Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek
seo.description: Embark on a 3 Days Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek, offering stunning sunrise views over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Experience the rich culture, scenic landscapes, and vibrant local villages of Nepal's Himalayas on this short yet unforgettable adventure.

overview:
The 3 Days Ghrepani Poon Hill Trek is one of the most preferred short and easy adventures in the Annapurna region in central Nepal. It is an exciting and adventurous undertaking in the Himalayas, which is ideal for both beginners and experienced trekkers. Though the trek is for a short period of time, it covers the entire highlights that longer Himalayan treks could offer. Poon Hill Trek 3 days is a perfect blend of the natural beauty and cultural richness in the Annapurna region. It is a must-do short trek in the Nepal Himalayas to experience the magnificence of untouched nature and the untampered culture of the mountain. The 3 days Poon Hill Trek starts and ends in Pokhara. Setting off and wrapping up in the vibrant Pokhara city, this enchanting journey ensures stunning mountain vistas, hospitable locals, and picturesque trails from start to finish. The Poon Hill Trek 3 days take you across diverse, captivating landscapes of the Annapurna Himalayan region, ranging from lowland forests to alpine meadows, being accompanied by the awe-inspiring views of the towering mountains. It encounters you with the several traditional villages of Gurung and Magar, where you can explore the vibrant culture and lifestyle of these mountainside communities. The 3 Days Poon Hill Trek passes through the vast biodiversity of the Annapurna Conservation Area. While traversing this conserved area, you can explore the diverse vegetation and wildlife of the region with several species of birds and butterflies, enriching your journey immensely. The major highlight of this trek is Poon Hill, a popular viewpoint in the region to access the panoramic views of the Himalayas and a magical sunrise over their summits. From the top of Poon Hill station, you will be treated to the rewarding vistas of Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, Machhapuchchhre, Ganesh Himal, Hiunchuli, Nilgiri, Gangapurna, and numerous other adjoining mountains. The Poon Hill Trek is renowned for its sunrise splendor, with mesmerizing rays of sun casting their golden pink hues over the pristine white Himalayas. The short Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is an ideal adventure for all categories of trekkers with straightforward and comfortable trails. If you are a beginner trekker and want to step into the world of adventure trekking through a short trek in the Annapurna region, the 3 days Poon Hill Trek is the best option for you. It is also an ideal choice for adventure enthusiasts seeking a remarkable and serene escape to the mounatins within a limited timeframe.

itinerary.title: Drive From Pokhara to Ghandruk and Trek to Tadapani
itinerary.html: Pokhara Elevation: 822 m Ghandruk Elevation: 1,940 m Tadapani Elevation: 2,630 m Pokhara to Ghandruk: 50 - 60 kilometers, 3-4 hours Ghandruk to Tadapani: 8 kilometers, 3-5 hours The exciting journey of Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek 3 Days begins with a scenic drive from the hotspot tourist destination of Pokhara to charming Ghandruk village in the Annapurna Himalayan region. Departing Pokhara after a hearty breakfast, we will begin to head northwest through the scenic black-topped hillside roads. We will pass through the rural countryside villages of Hemja, Kande, Lumle, etc on the way. After driving for some time along the Prithvi Highway with the occasional views of the distant Himalayas, we will reach Nayapul. From Nayapul, we will continue to drive further, following the winding graveled roads towards Birethanti. We will cross Modi Khola (River) through a bridge in this section of the drive. At the Birethanti checkpost, we will register or ACAP and TIMS permits. Gradually, the roads from Birethanti start to become narrower and more rugged as we continue to drive. As we make our way towards Ghandruk, we will ride alongside the Modi Khola River and pass by several charming traditional settlements adorned with terraced fields. En route, we will pass through popular stops like Syauli Bazaar and Kimche. Finally, we will arrive at the quaint hamlet of Ghandruk predominantly inhabited by the Gurung communities. Ghandruk is only our halfway journey. It is the starting point of our exhilarating 3 days Poon Hill Trek. We will enjoy a delicious lunch at this cultural village, immersing in the delectable flavor of local Gurung cuisines. We will take a brief rest after a satisfying, tummy-filling lunch. Then, we will prepare to set off on an adventurous trek toward this day’s destination, Tadapani. Leaving Ghanduk behind, we will start on the picturesque Annapurna region trails. Initially, we will descend through the terraced fields and vibrant and thick forest of colorful rhododendron trees. The trails are properly marked and easy. We will cross various small rivers on the way. Enjoying the captivating vistas of the surrounding mountains, we will reach a flat pasture land, Bhaisi Kharka. From Bhaisi Kharka, we will continue to trek further, ascending through the lush forested trails of oak and rhododendrons. We will again cross a few small rivers via wooden bridges along the way. During the last leg of the trek, we will ascend steeply towards Tadapani. The forest starts to clear, and the views of the Himalayas become more prominent as we approach this charming hamlet. After reaching Tadapani, you can unwind at the cozy teahouse. Immerse yourself in the authentic flavor of local cuisines prepared freshly in the teahouses. We will spend the first night of our Poon Hill Trek itinerary 3 days in comfortable teahouse beds.

itinerary.title: Trek From Tadapani to Ghorepani
itinerary.html: Ghorepani Elevation: 2,874 m Trek Distance: 10 kilometers Trek Duration: 5-6 hours We will wake up early in the morning in Tadapani village. After waking up, our day kicks off with a steaming cup of tea or coffee in the teahouse. Soon after, we will get a hot, fresh-cooked breakfast from the teahouse owners. Warming up with delicious meals and packing our backpacks, we will begin on the second day of our Poon Hill Trek 3 days itinerary. With the enthralling view of the snow-covered peaks of Annapurna and Macchapuchre, we will leave Tadapani. Descending through the dense forested trails, we will make our way. Traversing through the shades of tree branches amidst the tranquility of nature, the intermittent views of the closing-up Himalayas keep fascinating us. On the way, we will navigate a few small shimmering rivers. After a short walk of around 2 hours, we will reach Banthanti, a popular stop for rest, rejuvenation, and enjoyment of the magnificent natural environment. After a short break at Banthanti, we will continue on our trekking journey. Gradually, the forests start to thin out as we ascend towards the Deurali Pass. With the sweeping views of the hills, valleys, and mountains, we will steadily cross and descend to the other side of the pass. We will reach Deurali village after a pass crossing. After Deurali, we will begin to descend through the scenic forested trails. Following the well-trodden routes with some steep sections, we will pass several small settlements of people. Glimpsing into the distinctive culture and way of life of people in these villages, we will finally reach our destination village, Ghorepani. Ghorepani is a larger village of indigenous Gurung and Magar. It is a popular stop for a hike to the Poon Hill viewpoint. We will stay for the night at one of the finest teahouses in the Ghorepani.

itinerary.title: Morning Hike to Poon Hill and Trek Down to Hile, Then Drive to Pokhara
itinerary.html: Poon Hill Elevation: 3,210 m Hile Elevation: 1,430 m Trek Distance: 15-16 kilometers Trek Duration: 5-6 hours Drive Distance: 55 kilometers Drive Duration: 3-4 hours Today is the last day of our short 3 days Poon Hill Trek itinerary and the most important day as well. We will hike the stunning viewpoint of Poon Hill to enjoy a magical sunrise and sweeping Himalayan views. We will wake up before dawn and set off on an enticing hike toward the Poon Hill. With the path illuminated by our headlamp lights, we will gradually follow the well-marked uphill trails. We will ascend through the colorful forests of rhododendrons by climbing on the stone staircases towards Poon Hill. Continuing on the hike, gradually, the outlines of mountains in the early morning sky start to reveal. Standing atop the wonderful Poon Hill viewpoint, the hypnotic sight of the first ray of the sun rising over the lofty Himalayas and illuminating them in colorful hues of golden pink will leave you spellbound. Soon after the sunrise, the snow-coated peaks shimmer with the gentle touch of the sunrays, luring the beholders. Immerse in the magnificent scenery as seen from the Poon Hilltop and take some photographs to relish the moment as a memory for the years to come. After exploring the breathtaking views from Poon Hill, we will retrace our footsteps all the way back to the Ghorepani teahouse. We will enjoy a heartwarming lunch before heading to the trails for the final time. Tying the trekking boots laces, we will begin on the trail. We will start to walk down towards Hile, the ending point of our Ghorepani Poon Hill trek 3 days journey. Initially, we will head southeast, descending through the lush forests of oak, birch, and rhododendron trees. En route, we will traverse the small settlements of Banthanti and Nangethanti. Continuing further on the downhill routes, we will navigate the steep stone-paved stairs and reach Ulleri. From Ulleri, we will descend through several small hamlets dotted with colorful terraced farmlands, one of which is Tikhedhunga. Finally, we will trek down to Hile through the gently descending routes. After reaching Hile, we will come to the end of our short and adventurous trekking journey. From here, we will take a vehicle to drive back to the Pokhara city. Leaving Hile, we will drive downhill, passing through the villages with terraced fields. With the views of surrounding hills and Modi River, we will continue to drive on the mix of pitched and graveled roads. We will arrive at Nayapul after some time and head further southwards, passing through lush hills and small settlements of people. En route, we will drive past the popular villages of Lumle and Kande before entering the cityscape of Pokhara. Upon reaching Pokhara, our rewarding journey of the Poon Hill trek itinerary 3 days culminates. Thank you very much for choosing Base Camp Adventure for your Himalayas trip to Nepal. We are excited to meet you again soon in the next adventurous journey.

sections.title: Useful Info
sections.html:
Difficulty of 3 days Poon Hill Trek

The 3 days Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is a moderate-level adventure. The short duration of the Poon Hill trek, which is only for the 3 days, will make it a fast-paced journey. You need to complete long hours of walking per day to cover the total distance of the trek. During the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek 3 days, you will walk for around 6-7 hours each day on average. While the trails are mostly well-marked and straightforward, some sections of them involve steep descends and long climbs. If you are a seasonal hiker, it will be easy for you to cover the daily distance. However, inexperienced or first-time trekkers who are not habitual of walking for longer hours can find the trek difficult. The highest altitude point reached during the 3 days of Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is 3,210 m, which is not extremely high. Still, trekkers can feel mild altitude symptoms like headache, dizziness, and nausea. So, it is essential to be mindful of the altitude symptoms and keep your body well hydrated. Also, a slow pace of ascent is essential to allow enough time to acclimatize and key the altitude sickness at a bay. The unpredictable weather conditions can also raise the difficulty level of the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek. The weather and temperature in the elevated regions change frequently. A warm and sunny day can turn wet and rainy with dark clouds in the sky in a flash. So, you need to be prepared with the right gear and clothing to accommodate diverse temperatures and weather patterns during the journey. Also, staying updated about the weather forecasts and being flexible with itineraries in case of delays due to bad weather is essential. The remoteness of the trekking region also adds to the difficulty level of the journey. During your three-day period, you will be trekking across the rural mountainside landscapes. You will pass through dense forest areas and rustic villages. You will be staying at the teahouses with basic and limited facilities. So, being self-sufficient and well-equipped with all the required trek items is strongly recommended. This will help to raise your well-being and comfort level during the remote journey.

Preparations for Poon Hill Trek 3 days

3 days Poon Hill Trek doesn't demand excessive preparations. It is a short and sweet journey in the mid-Himalayas. Having said that, a few things need to be thought of cautiously. For any adventure in the mountains, you need to be prepared both physically and mentally. Physical preparation is essential to deal with and come out of the challenges presented by the trekking routes. Whereas mental preparation is a must to stay calm and composed and handle any situation smoothly. For the sustained energy supply required during the consecutive trekking days, you need to have proper strength and endurance capacity. To build up your stamina, you can be involved in physical workouts several days prior to the start of the Ghorepani Poon Hill trekking journey. Consider engaging in the following exercises to upgrade yourself for the Poon Hill Trek. Cardiovascular workouts:
  • Jogging
  • Swimming
  • Cycling
  • Brisk walking
  • Dancing
  • Running
  • Rowing
  • Jumping rope/skipping
  • Stair climbing
Strength training:
  • Push-ups
  • Plunges
  • Deadlifts
  • Squats
  • Pull-ups
  • Planks
  • Bicep curls
  • Shoulder presses
Likewise, mental preparation starts with research of the journey and destination. It is essential to understand the difficulty level of the trek beforehand. Mental readiness for the long trekking days and potential weather challenges during the journey allows you to have an expected experience. It also plays a necessary role in maintaining a positive attitude and better adaption to changing conditions in the mountains. Mental preparation lets you stay focused, resilient, determined, and flexible. It makes you capable of overcoming any obstacles/discomforts during your remote wilderness journey.

Altitude Sickness During 3 Days Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek

The 3 days Poon Hill Trek is a moderate-altitude Himalayan journey. The highest elevation reached during this trek is 3,210 m at Poon Hill. While the trek doesn't take you to the breathtaking heights in the mountains, it still carries the risk of being affected by altitude sickness. This is because the symtoms of altitude sickness are experienced after going up the elevation of 2,500 m The prime cause of altitude sickness is the thinning air in high altitudes. As we ascend more into the alpine locations, the air pressure continues to decrease. The oxygen level in the depleting air is relatively lower, which causes breathing difficulty. Our body finds it difficult to adjust to the lower oxygen levels of the higher grounds and faces several other health complexities, ultimately leading to altitude sickness. The general symptoms of altitude sickness are headache, dizziness, fatigue, shortness of breath, sleeping difficulty, rapid heartbeat, nausea etc. If you experience any of these symptoms during the trek, it will be best to descend to the familiar altitudes immediately. Stay there until the symptoms disappear and only ascend to the elevations after your body fully recovers. To prevent the altitude sickness from prevailing, you can consider the following mitigating measures
  • Stay well-hydrated by drinking adequate water, juices, and other fluids
  • Ascend at a slow pace, taking regular breaks and allowing ample time for the body to adapt to the changing altitudes
  • Do not smoke or drink alcohol, which will dehydrate your body and exacerbate the altitude sickness
  • Take anti-altitude sickness medications such as a diamox pill
  • Avoid the intake of sleeping pills
  • Eat a healthy diet and nutritious meals rich in vitamins, proteins, and minerals

Food and Accomodation

The food and accommodation during the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek 3 days are provided by traditional teahouses along the trekking routes. Teahouses are commonly available forms of accommodation in the villages during the journey. They are usually operated by family members, providing basic amenities for stays to visitors. The ordinary accommodation in the teahouse comprises shared living spaces with two to three beds in a single room. The bed comes with a mattress, a set of pillows, and a warm blanket. The toilets are usually traditional squat styles and communal. Likewise, bathrooms and dining halls are also available for common use. During the Ghorepani Poon Hill trekking journey, you will have all three meals, i.e., breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Teahouses serve you healthy and nutritious dishes prepared from locally grown crops and vegetables. Their menu comprises a variety of traditional food items and some popular continental cuisines. Dal bhat (rice, lentils, and pickles) is a main meal in the teahouse. Apart from that, you can get to taste the delectable delicacies of momo (dumpling), chowmein, thukpa, flatbread, eggs (boiled, fried, scrambled), noodles, mushroom soups, etc. You can also sample the local taste of Western dishes such as pizza, burgers, sandwiches, and pasta. Likewise, you can enjoy a variety of hot and cold drinks in teahouses. Tea (black, milk, ginger, lemon, honey, green, etc.) and coffee (black and milk) are usually available for drinks. Besides fresh fruit juices, soft drinks like Coca-Cola and Fanta, hot/bottled water, and local beverages like Chhyang and Tongba etc, are available. Gain Insights On:

faqs.q: What is the Highest Altitude Point of the 3 days Poon Hill Trek Itinerary?
faqs.a: The highest altitude reached during the 3 days Poon Hill trek itinerary is Poon Hill at 3,210 m From the vantage point of Poon Hill, you will be treated to the breathtaking panorama of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges, Machhapuchhare, Nilgiri, Hiunchuli, and several other adjoining mountains. Moreover, the captivating sunrise view from Poon Hill is the major attraction of the trek.

faqs.q: When is the Best Time to Go for 3 Days Poon Hill Trek?
faqs.a: Spring and autumn are the best times to embark on the 3 days Poon Hill trek. You can expect stable weather and milder temperatures during these seasons, which will help for an effortless, seamless, and comfortable journey. Additionally, the relatively cloud-free sky at this time will reward you with uninterrupted views of the pristine Himalayas peaks.

faqs.q: What Permits Do I Need to Obtain for the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek?
faqs.a:
Following are the permits that you need to acquire for the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek
  • Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) Permit
  • Trekkers' Information Management System (TIMS) card

faqs.q: How Difficult is the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek?
faqs.a: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is graded as an easy to moderate-level trek. The trekking trails are well-marked and straightforward. However, you need to have a basic level of physical fitness and considerable stamina to overcome 5-6 hours of walking during each day of the journey.

faqs.q: Should I Need to Hire a Guide for the Poon Hill Trek?
faqs.a: As per the rule of the Nepal Tourism Board, it is mandatory to hire a guide for the remote Himalayan treks in Nepal, including the Poon Hill Trek. Moreover, guides help in the safe navigation of the unfamiliar routes of the trekking regions. They also provide information and immersion in the nature and culture of the place, enriching your adventure experience.

faqs.q: Are There ATMs Along the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek Route?
faqs.a: There is no availability of banking or ATM facilities along the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek. The trek takes place in the remote mountainside areas that pass through the rural villages where these services have not reached. However, there are abundant ATMs in Pokhara where you can withdraw money. Ensure you have enough cash (Nepali rupee) for daily expenses and emergency usage during the journey.

faqs.q: Is Travel Insurance Required for Poon Hill Trek?
faqs.a: Yes, travel insurance is essential for the Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek. It is a vital document you need to acquire for traveling in the remorse corners of Nepal. With travel insurance, you can have quick access to medical services in case of accidents, injuries, and illnesses, along with the financial protection incurred during the treatment. Moreover, it also takes care of other unforeseen happenings such as lost/delayed/stolen baggage, trip delays due to bad weather and other reasons, trip cancellations, etc.

overview:
Advanced Base Camp with Lhasa Tour. Tibet is cautiously opening up to the western world offering travel seekers a fulfilling authentic experience, which can be adventurous and unpredictable due to the lack of infrastructure which is poor to non-existent, making a simple road trip a complete adventure.

After centuries of virtual isolation local monasteries are striving to find a place in a country that's crashing into the twentieth century. Tibet is the perfect destination to try exotic foods while embarking on a spiritual journey, leaving you feeling internally rejuvenated whilst stepping back in time. For the culture lover’s witness displays of people so optimistic yet so proud of their religion and beliefs, remaining much the same as they did one hundred years ago.

The majority of this land rests above 4,000 m (13,000 feet), housing many secrets which present the perfect opportunity to explore the highest Himalayas in the world giving you ultimate thrill of climbing, trekking and other challenging adventurous activities.

North East Ridge Advance Base Camp

The northeast ridge route begins from the north side of Everest in Tibet. Expeditions trek to the Rongbuk Glacier, setting up Base Camp at 5,180 m (17,000 ft) on a gravel plain just below the glacier. To reach Camp II, climbers ascend the medial moraine of the east Rongbuk Glacier up to the base of Changtse at around 6,100 m (20,000 ft). Camp III (ABC - Advanced Base Camp) is situated below the North Col at 6,500 m (21,300 ft).

China is paving a 108-km (66-mile) dirt road from Tingri County to its Base Camp in order to accommodate growing numbers of climbers on their side of the mountain. It will become the highest asphalt-paved road in the world. Construction began on June 18, 2007, at a cost of 150 million yuan (US$19.7 million). China also plans on routing the 2008 Olympic Torch Relay over Everest, going up the South Col route and back down the North Col route, on the way to the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing.

cover.alt: Amphu Lapcha Pass with Mera Peak Climb

overview:
The trek to Amphu Lapcha Pass goes through wilder upper Hongu valley. Amphu Lapcha is to be passed technically to Chukkung Valley. The crossing of the pass requires the use of technical climbing equipment and trekkers must be skilled in the use of this and be prepared. Amphu Lapcha Pass holds the views of Himalayas and hearty scenery of lakes Hongu lakes and Panch Pokhari lakes.
Most commonly visited as a two week trek starting and finishing at Lukla. After 40 minute flight from Kathmandu to Lukla is tiny airstrip, the adventure really begins from the beginning. We spend the next few days trekking and interacting among the mountain people also known as Sherpa staying at local lodges and trek into the heartland of their villages. Everything is organized in conjunction with local Sherpa guides.

While passing Buddhist monasteries views of Everest get closer every day. Acclimatizing is very important so we will have rest days in the villages of Namche and Dingboche that will allow us to explore the region and acclimatize. Although this trek is called Everest Base Camp Trek, our goal is the summit of Kalapattar at an elevation of 5,553 m, which is higher than Everest Base Camp. After trekking to Kalapattar we return at our leisurely pace back to Namche and Lukla for our return flight to Kathmandu. For the more adventurous trekkers you have the option of returning over the Cho La pass to the Gokyo valley, and then ascending Gokyo Ri. Or if you are really fit, you can attempt the summit of Island Peak.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
summary: Annapurna Base Camp Trek offers an unforgettable Himalayan adventure through traditional villages, lush forests, and stunning views of the Annapurna mountain range.

seo.title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek | 12 Day Itinerary | Guide | Map | Cost
seo.description: Annapurna Base Camp Trek offers an unforgettable Himalayan adventure through traditional villages, lush forests, and stunning views of the Annapurna mountain range.

gallery.alt: Annapurna Base Camp Helicopter Tour with Landing

overview:
Annapurna Base Camp trek has been recognized as one of the world’s best trekking trails. The walk-into the Sanctuary offers exceptional scenery of high mountains, as well as gives chance to witness some of the marsh towns of the Annapurna Region. This world's renowned trek to the lap of the Annapurna Himalayas leaves you thrilled with the views of exotic mountains like Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna II (7,939 m), Annapurna III (7,555 m), Annapurna IV (7,525 m) and Annapurna South (7,219 m) as the name itself suggests. Furthermore, the 360-degree Himalayan view of Dhaulagiri (8,167 m), Nilgiri (7,041 m) and Lamjung Himal (6,986 m) will leave your mind astonished.

 Annapurna Base Camp trek starts after seven hours bus from Kathmandu to Pokhara. It is not only the gateway of Annapurna Base Camp Trek but also the most beautiful city of Nepal.  The typical route of Annapurna Base Camp heads directly to Ghorepani via Ulleri and Nayapul. The trek endures through Modi River, dense stands of rhododendron forest and bamboo bushes to one of most beautiful viewpoints: Poon Hill. Popularly known as Photographer’s Paradise, Poon Hill lets you capture some of the best snaps of impressive Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges.

The astonishing sunrise view from Poon Hill is just outstanding. Continuing the Annapurna adventure trek trail leads to Chommrong, Himalaya, and finally to Annapurna Base Camp. You can undoubtedly get captivated by the scenic Himalayan views of Annapurna, Manaslu, Himchuli, Machhapuchre, Dhaulagiri, and other snow-capped mountains all around you.

To get to the Annapurna Base Camp, trekker has to pass through many villages of different ethnic societies having different cultures and lifestyles with ridged forests of rhododendron and a wide range of floras and faunas. Hence, the Annapurna Base Camp trekking is sure to provide you non-stop natural diversity with beautiful Mountain View and Himalayan landscape. The subtropical forests come alive with a huge variety of birds, waterfall thunders, and monkeys chatter from the treetops which makes the trek truly magical.

All things considered, this Annapurna Base Camp trekking has so much to offer to you including a view of outlandish mountains to exploring the local culture and tradition of various ethnic gatherings including Magars and Gurungs who have lived in these precarious slopes for quite long time. Thus, explore the unexplored, live through the magnificence of nature, and dedicate yourself completely to the obscure and be part of our Annapurna Base Camp trek to enlighten yourself with knowledge and life changing experience.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Kathmandu airport and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu (1,400 m), you will be warmly welcomed and picked by our representative who will then drop you at the hotel. Overnight in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Toursit bus drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara (820 m / 2,690 ft), 6–7 hours.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, we will drive to Pokhara via Prithvi Highway on a tourist bus. Experience picturesque landscapes along the highway as you drive alongside rivers, terraced farms, and many villages and towns until you reach Pokhara. In Pokhara, you can spend the evening relaxing by the lakeside/Phewa Lake. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Drive to Nayapul (1,010 m / 3,314 ft) and trek to Ulleri (1,920 m / 6,299 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: We leave Pokhara as we drive through the countryside to Nayapul. After the 2-hour drive to Nayapul, we start our trek by crossing the suspension bridge over Modi River and heading towards Birethanti. Walking on stone steps, we pass through the villages of Mathathanti, Sudame, Hille, and Tikhedhunga to arrive in Ulleri. Glimpses of Annapurna South (7,219 m) and Patal Hiunchuli (6,441 m) can be seen from Ulleri. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ulleri to Ghorepani (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: We walk on an easy trail through thick forests of rhododendron and cross the villages of Banthanti and Nangethanti on our way to Ghorepani. Ascending uphill on stone stairs, we enter the village of Ghorepani. Upon arrival, we are embraced with a panorama of the Annapurna massif and its adjacent peaks. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Early morning hike to Poon Hill (3,210 m / 10,531 ft) for sunrise views, followed by a trek to Tadapani (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 6–7 hours.
itinerary.html: We start the day with an early morning ascent to Poon Hill along the snowy trails to witness the majestic sunrise over the peaks of Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges along with Nilgiri(7,061 m), Lamjung Himal (6,983 m), and Machhapuchhre (6,993 m). We then retrace our way back to Ghorepani and continue to climb down to the village of Tadapani. Overnight at guest house.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tadapani to Chommrong (2,170 m / 7,119 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Ascend uphill and then downhill on a forested trail before crossing the suspension bridge over Kimrong Khola to reach the hot spring of Jhinu Danda. We can take a short rest in the hot spring before entering the mesmerizing village of Chhomrong. Upon reaching Chhomrong, we are rewarded with an amazing view of Annapurna South (7,219 m) and Machhapuchhre (6,993 m). Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chhomrong to Himalaya (2,920 m / 9,580 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today is an easy walk through rhododendron forest adorned with orchids and ferns. We descend down stone stairs, and upon crossing Chhomrong Khola, we ascend to Sinuwa. We then descend through stone staircases to reach Bamboo. From Bamboo, we walk through the forested trail to reach Dobhan and then Himalaya. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Himalaya to Annapurna Base Camp ( 4,130 m / 13,550 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: We ascend to Deurali and walk along stone stairs to reach a picturesque area featuring alluring vista of snow-capped mountains to reach Machhapuchhre Base Camp (3,700 m). Then, following the moraines of South Annapurna Glacier, we reach the base camp of Annapurna South (7,219 m). We get to experience a 360-degree view of snow-capped peaks including the Annapurna massif, Annapurna South (7,219 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), Patal Hiunchuli (6,441 m), and several other wonderful peaks. Overnight at base camp.

itinerary.title: Trek back from Annapurna Base Camp to Bamboo (2,920 m / 9,580 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: We start the day by descending to Machhapuchhre Base Camp through the moraine route. Enjoying the view of the snowy peaks, we follow the trails of Modi Khola through the forest of rhododendron and fir and climb down past Deurali and Himalaya to finally reach Bamboo. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bamboo to Jhinu Hot Spring, followed by a drive to Pokhara (2,345 m / 7,694 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: We first ascend through an amusing forest to Sinuwa, then head down to Chhomrong Khola to finally ascend the stone stairs to upper Chhomrong. We then descend to Jhinu Danda. Upon reaching Jhinu, take some time to relax and enjoy the natural hot springs. Afterward, drive to Pokhara (1,780 m),  6-7 hours in total.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive to Kathmandu, 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Early in the morning, we leave Pokhara as we drive back to Kathmandu on a tourist bus. Enjoying the amazing greenery and the villages along the highway, we arrive in the capital. Upon arrival, you can either rest in your hotel room or explore the nearby markets. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Transfer to International Airport for your onward destination.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, enjoy some free time in Kathmandu for last-minute shopping or relaxation, depending on your flight schedule. Later, our representative will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu for your onward destination.

sections.html:
We are advised to consider the following equipment as these are essentials while packing for the Annapurna Base Camp Trek. Adjustments to the list can be managed according to the requirements, interests, duration of trip, and season of trip.  We can find variety of these gears to rent or buy in Kathmandu and Pokhara. Majority of the gears which are in sale in Kathmandu and Pokhara are locally manufactured and some are imported from china and they are much cheaper. And there are some famous branded gear shops in Thamel, Kathmandu.

– Lightweight and comfortable hiking boots: fit them with hiking socks and wear them wherever possible before you go to trekking. Get the best hiking boots for plantar fasciitis, if you face plantar fasciitis problem.
– Sleeping bag and liner
– Sandals/ Flip flop
– Hiking socks – at least 4 pairs of cotton socks and 2 pair of wool socks
– Lightweight long sleeve hiking shirts
– Windproof/Waterproof pants and jacket
– Plastic rain poncho
– Light weather protection and warmer weather
– Hat for sun and wind
– Windproof gloves
– Warmer clothes
– Long underwear
– Thermals (socks, t-shirts, sweater)
– Wool hat/beanie (for winter)
– Shorts
– Hiking trousers
– Best down jacket

Accessories:

– Sunglasses with good UV protection
– Sunscreen
– Lightweight bag to carry your personal needs during the day
– Insect repellent
– Camera with extra battery
– Flashlight
– Backpack
– Aluminum water bottle
– Head lamp
– Trekking Poles

faqs.q: I’ve never trekked before. Can I do this trek?
faqs.a: As long as you are reasonably fit, mentally prepared and can walk for 6-7-hours a day then no matter who you are and what your background is, a bit of training may be necessary, but even that is not 100% essential for most.

faqs.q: Can children go the Annapurna Base Camp trek?
faqs.a: Yes in the general rule. It’s advisable that your child is reasonable and able to understand and follow instructions immediately. Your child should be mature enough to recognize altitude sickness symptoms.

faqs.q: How many days does the Annapurna Base Camp Trek take to complete?
faqs.a:
The Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Base Camp Adventure takes thirteen days to finish. This includes arrival and departure days in Kathmandu, the overland ride between Kathmandu and Pokhara and trekking days. 

You can also make the Annapurna Base Camp Trek shorter or longer depending on the time you have, your fitness and experience level and your travel preferences.

faqs.q: Why is the Annapurna Base Camp trek a classic?
faqs.a:
• Spectacular close-ups of Himalayan giants
  • The magnificent Annapurna Sanctuary
  • Rhododendron forests and changing scenery
  • Authentic village experience
  • Sunrise view from Poon Hill
  • Hearty local Gurung culture
  • Home-style lodgings.
  • Beginner friendly trekking experience to the Himalayas.

faqs.q: How high does the Annapurna Base Camp trek go?
faqs.a: At 4,130 m (13,550 feet) Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) is the peak of your trekking journey. You’ll be surrounded by spectacular mountain ranges which include Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and Hiunchuli.

faqs.q: How does the Annapurna Base Camp Trek begin?
faqs.a:
The Annapurna Base Camp Trek normally begins with a trip from Kathmandu to Pokhara via tourist bus. From there you will be taken by private transport to Nayapul or any other trailhead as per your chosen itinerary. 

You will start your trek and continue with your journey on foot passing through some picturesque villages, forest areas and mountainous terrain on the way to the Annapurna Base Camp.

faqs.q: Are trekking permits included in the tour package?
faqs.a:
Yes, the necessary trekking permits and the fees are included in the tour package.  You will only need a single permit for this trek which is to enter the Annapurna Conservation Area. 

Our team will arrange the Annapurna Conservation Area Entry Project (ACAP) permit for you before you start the trek.

faqs.q: Will I sleep in the Annapurna Base Camp?
faqs.a: Yes, the Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130 m is the highest sleeping altitude of this trek. Spending a night surrounded by the Annapurna mountain range is one of the highlights of the trek.

faqs.q: Is Poon Hill included in the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: Poon Hill (3,210 m) is part of the 13 days Annapurna Base Camp Trek itinerary with Base Camp Adventure. It is one of the best places to watch the sunrise in Nepal and enjoy the view of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges.

faqs.q: How difficult is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: In terms of terrain there are no ropes needed and no ice picks needed. There is no vertical climbing involved. The ground is not paved. It is rough, rocky and gravel strewn. Most of the trek involves long paths that go up and then down. People with weak ankles should take caution. Depending on the time of year you go there can also be snow and ice in the trails. There are some boulders that need climbing, but you can also walk around many.

faqs.q: What cultural aspects will I get to enjoy while doing the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: During the ABC trek, you will have chances to explore the lifestyle of the Gurung and Magar communities, stay in mountain villages, know the customs of the region and understand its unique culture.

faqs.q: Is there age limit for Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: There isn’t any official age limit saying you can and cannot trek to Annapurna Base Camp Trek .

faqs.q: Is there bottled water available on the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: Yes, there’s bottled water from Nayapul to all the way up to Annapurna Base Camp. But, the price goes up the higher you go. One liter bottle of water cost start around 50 rupees and at base camp cost well over 200 (around $2). A budget solution to this is to use water treatment solution or use water purifier tablets. Some purification tabs and drops make the water taste weird. Please be aware of that too. In some places there is safe drinking water station from where you can buy drinking water for the day. Buying boiled water can be a solution to save money from expensive bottled water but make sure if water was fully boiled or not before you buy.

faqs.q: Can I do laundry on the trek?
faqs.a: Yes, you can. You can take this service with guest house. This will not be by machine, it will be by hand. Or, you can do your own laundry in a bucket.

faqs.q: What is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek's Difficulty Level?
faqs.a:
Annapurna Base Camp trek is a moderate mountain adventure. It doesn't involve technical climbing nor require prior mountaineering expertise and experience. But the trekkers need to spend long days of walking steep stone steps both uphill and downhill, sections of rocks and uneven mountain trails in variable mountain weather. 

A Good level of fitness and mental attitude will ensure an enjoyable experience for this trail.

faqs.q: Is the Annapurna Base Camp trek suitable for beginners?
faqs.a:
Yes, an Annapurna Base Camp trek will be enjoyed by beginners as long as you are fit and healthy. You need to be able to walk continuously for several hours each day. Previous trekking experience is helpful but not mandatory. 

Exercises such as walking, jogging, biking, dancing, squats, planks etc can prior to trekking can prepare you physically for the journey.

faqs.q: How many hours do I have to walk every day?
faqs.a:
During the first week, you will typically walk for 4 to 6 hours per day. As you gain altitude some trekking days may take 5 to 7 hours to complete. The length of the walking times depends on the schedule, terrain, weather and altitude of the day. 

There will be a comfortable pace with regular breaks for rest, meals and enjoying mountain views.

faqs.q: Is there an age limit for the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
No. There isn’t any specific age limit to do the Annapurna Base Camp trek. As long as you are in good physical and health condition, able to walk for hours with good endurance and can acclimatize properly to altitude you can do the Annapurna base camp trek. 

Children and older travelers can participate if they are properly prepared and medically fit.

faqs.q: Can children do the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: Yes. Children if properly trained, have sound health, are physically fit and have the mental toughness to deal with alpine trekking hardship can do the Annapurna Base Camp Trek. Parents must be alert to know the signs of altitude sickness (headache, vomiting, nausea and dizziness), let children walk slowly and make them eat and drink enough.

faqs.q: How many miles do you walk each day?
faqs.a: In average you walk around 4-7 miles per day while going up and 8-12 miles while coming down.

faqs.q: What’s the best time to trek to Annapurna Base Camp?
faqs.a:
Spring season - March to May is considered the best time for this trek with stunning views of rhododendron bloom, moderate temperature, and crystal clear Himalayan panoramas.

Autumn season - September to November offers the best time for trekking due to clear skies, excellent visibility and dry, stable weather.

faqs.q: Can I trek to Annapurna Base Camp in winter?
faqs.a: Yes, you can trek to Annapurna Base Camp during winter. It may be extremely cold and snow falls heavily so trekkers must take proper care with adequate warm clothes and cold winter gear.

faqs.q: Can we trek to Annapurna Base Camp in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Yes, the monsoon ABC trek is possible but you should be prepared for continuous rain, slippery trails and the possible landslides. The mountains get mostly hidden in clouds and mist and leeches infest the lower forested trails. Bring proper rain gear and have a flexible schedule for potential delays.

faqs.q: What if the weather disturbs the trekking plan?
faqs.a: The weather in the mountains is unpredictable. In case the weather disturbs the trekking plan we will adjust the schedule accordingly and make sure that the travelers remain safe and the journey remains smooth.

faqs.q: What are the accommodation options available for trekking?
faqs.a:
Accommodation is arranged in standard tea houses and guest houses which are comfortable places to rest and spend nights. Rooms feature double beds, blankets and basic furniture with shared bathroom facilities. 

Our package includes the best available guesthouse accommodation, mainly on a twin-sharing basis.

faqs.q: Is there luxury lodging available on an Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: A regular ABC Trek offers fine teahouse lodges. Luxury options can be custom-made to your specifications which may include higher-end hotels in Kathmandu, Pokhara, and a few places within the trek where premium accommodations exist.

faqs.q: Do the tea houses have private rooms and bathrooms?
faqs.a: The tea houses generally have twin sharing rooms with shared bathroom facilities. At some lower altitude tea houses, you can expect to get attached bathrooms or private facilities depending on availability. However, at higher altitudes, facilities are mostly provided on a shared basis.

faqs.q: Is there a provision of hot showers on the way?
faqs.a: Yes, hot showers can be used at most of the tea houses on the way at extra charges. Availability may become limited at higher elevations.

faqs.q: Do the tea houses have blankets available?
faqs.a: Yes. Blankets are provided at the tea houses on the Annapurna Base Camp trek. But the rooms usually do not have heating and the temperature tends to get really cold, particularly at high altitudes and in winter. It is therefore highly advisable to carry sleeping bags.

faqs.q: Do I have to carry snacks for the trek?
faqs.a: Yes. You can carry personal snacks like energy bars, chocolates, nuts, dry fruits and any other light food items for additional energy during treks. They may cost more on the trekking trail, so it is better to bring your favourite snacks before you depart.

faqs.q: What kind of foods can we eat on the trip?
faqs.a:
You can expect to eat three meals every day on the Annapurna Base Camp trekking trip: breakfast, lunch and dinner. common meals include;

  • Dal Bhat – lentil, rice, vegetable or meat curry
  • Noodles
  • Pasta
  • Soups
  • Rice
  • Leafy greens
  • Eggs
  • Tibetan Bread
  • Pancakes
  • Tea/coffee

You can also place a special order for vegetarians, vegans and other specific dietary needs.

faqs.q: Is meat available at the teahouse?
faqs.a: Most of the tea houses provide you with different meat options such as chicken, yak meat, buffalo meat, and sometimes mutton. But the availability depends on the location and season and becomes limited when the elevation increases. It is preferred by many trekkers to have vegetarian food on the trek due to freshness and better digestion.

faqs.q: Am I able to charge my electronic gadgets on the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes. Charging facilities are available in most teahouses along the ABC trail by means of electricity or solar power. It is possible to charge phones, cameras and power banks during your stay. 

However, at higher altitudes, there might be a cost to pay for the service, depending on the prevailing weather conditions and the energy source. To avoid running out of power in your device, it is advisable to carry a charged power bank and backup batteries.

faqs.q: Is there a Wi-Fi connection in the teahouse?
faqs.a: Yes, it is possible to get Wi-Fi connection on some of the lower and mid region teahouses along the trekking routes. The connection speed and reliability may vary from one point to another depending on the location, weather and network conditions. Likewise, there is also a small fee associated with using the internet.

faqs.q: Are the guides for the Annapurna Base Camp trek provided?
faqs.a:
Yes. We arrange a government authorized, knowledgeable, English speaking and experienced trekking guide. All the guides are expertly trained in First Aid and emergency management. 

They provide altitude awareness, acclimatization information, trekking safety guidance, route navigation and insights into local customs and traditions throughout the trek.

faqs.q: Is Porter available?
faqs.a: Yes. Porter service is optional. If requested, porters can be provided to carry your trekking equipment, with one porter typically carrying the luggage of two trekkers. All porter-related expenses are covered, including wages, insurance, meals, accommodation, and essential equipment such as clothing, a bed, mattress, and sleeping bag. Necessary local food and logistical support for the porters are also included.

faqs.q: Is it possible for a solo traveler to participate in the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: Yes, solo trekkers are welcome to join the trip. You have the option of going for a group trek along with other trekkers, or you can book a private trek tailored just for yourself.

faqs.q: How many people are normally in the group?
faqs.a: Normally, there will be 2-14 travelers in a group. Smaller groups trekking through the trails offer the best safety, flexibility, personalized trekking experience and prompt service.

faqs.q: Is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek safe?
faqs.a: Yes, the Annapurna Base Camp Trek is known to be a safe trekking trail when well prepared. Our professional guides constantly keep track of weather, altitude, physical fitness, and trail conditions during your trek.

faqs.q: Is travel insurance necessary for the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes. Travel insurance is a must. The policy must include:

  • High altitude trekking adventure up to 4,500 m
  • Emergency medical needs
  • Accident and injury
  • Helicopter evacuation
  • Cancellation of the trip

Trekkers must bring proof of insurance during trekking.

faqs.q: Is altitude sickness a possibility during the ABC trek?
faqs.a:
ABC trek is not considered to be an extreme altitude hike; however, altitude sickness may occur once beyond 3,000 m To avoid it,

  • Walk slowly
  • Drink enough water
  • Have proper food
  • Follow the guide's instructions
  • Tell the guide about any signs
  • Avoid cigarettes and alcohols
  • Rest enough 
  • Take preventive medication such as Diamox

faqs.q: What are the symptoms of altitude sickness?
faqs.a:
Some of the common symptoms of altitude sickness include:

  • Headache
  • Nausea
  • Vomiting
  • Dizziness
  • Fatigue
  • Loss of appetite
  • Sleep difficulty

Signs that need urgent attention include breathing problems, confusion and loss of balance.

faqs.q: What will be done in case of an emergency?
faqs.a:
In case of need for an emergency evacuation during the trek, the preparations will be made in relation to the particular situation and place of occurrence. Immediate medical help and a helicopter arrangement are usually provided. 

As evacuation in emergency situations is usually very costly, it is advisable to ensure that your travel insurance covers the cost of helicopter rescue and any other medical expenses.

faqs.q: Is there any provision of medical aid while trekking?
faqs.a: Yes, medical aid will be provided by way of experienced trekking guides who have undergone training in first aid. They have a first aid kit with them all the time. Guides also carry other important medical supplies like a pulse oximeter to measure the oxygen level and heart rate to ensure that you stay healthy and safe throughout.

faqs.q: What are the items I should carry for the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
The recommended gear that you should consider taking while going for the trek includes trekking boots, trekking socks, sleeping bag, rain jacket and pants, down jacket, thermal wear, gloves, hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, trekking sticks, headlight, water bottle, backpack and camera with extra batteries.

Having appropriate clothing and gear will make you ready for any weather condition during the trek.

faqs.q: Is it possible to rent trekking gear in Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. You can rent or buy several trekking essentials in Nepal especially in major cities such as Kathmandu and Pokhara. Some of the rental options are a sleeping bag, a down jacket, trekking poles etc. Renting equipment can be a convenient option for travelers who do not want to carry all their gear from home.

faqs.q: How much will the Annapurna Base Camp Trek cost?
faqs.a: The cost of the Annapurna Base Camp Trek will be based on group size, the time of the trek and whether you opt for a group or private trek. The cost of the 13 day ABC trek with Base Camp Adventure costs you just USD 925 per person. It covers logistics like accommodation, meals, permits, guide, porter, transport and other trekking support.

faqs.q: What expenses do I need to budget for the trek?
faqs.a:
You need to have money for your personal expenses that include drinks, snacks, WiFi, battery charging, hot showers, laundry, additional beverages, tips for guides and porters, equipment rental, and emergencies. 

The trail expenses increase as you reach higher elevations due to the difficulties in transportation of supplies to higher mountains and limited resources.

faqs.q: How much money should I carry for personal expenses during the trek?
faqs.a:
We suggest you carry around USD 200 to 400 for personal expenses for the 13 day Annapurna Base Camp Trek. The amount can be more or less depending on your spending habits and personal needs. 

The money may be spent on additional expenses such as hot showers, Internet access, recharging your phone batteries, snacks, additional drinks, dessert, laundry and tips for the trekking crew members.

faqs.q: Should I convert the cash into local currency for the trail expenses?
faqs.a: Yes. Withdraw and exchange money beforehand in the city. Since there are no reliable ATMs along the trekking trail, it is better to take the required amount of Nepalese currency before leaving for trekking either in Kathmandu or Pokhara. The remaining money may be exchanged later in Kathmandu or Pokhara.

faqs.q: Can I pay for my trek using credit cards?
faqs.a: It is generally difficult to use credit cards in trekking regions as shops and teahouses prefer cash payments. It is advisable to carry money in Nepalese rupees.

faqs.q: What preparations should be done for the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: Regular aerobic exercise, strength training, and hiking practice should be done prior to joining the ABC trek. Such exercises like hiking up the hill, running, cycling, stair climbing, squatting, planking and core workouts will help build endurance for hiking long days.

faqs.q: How far in advance of my trek should I be in Nepal?
faqs.a: You should be in Nepal at least a day or two before the trek. This is important so as to have time to land at the airport, do the necessary preparations, engage in last minute shopping and meet with your guide for the journey.

faqs.q: Do I need any prior trekking experience to do the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: No prior trekking experience is necessary. The Annapurna Base Camp Trek is ideal for those who are new to trekking but are in good physical and mental condition to undertake the journey.

faqs.q: What are the documents that I am supposed to have during the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: You should have the following documents: passport, travel insurance papers, passport size photographs, flight details, emergency contacts and copies of all travel documents.

faqs.q: Do I need to carry a map of my own?
faqs.a: No. Base Camp Adventure will provide you with the map of the Annapurna Base Camp Trek as part of the package. But it is still good to carry your personal offline map or trekking app.

faqs.q: What is the amount of the deposit for booking the trek?
faqs.a: In order to reserve the Annapurna Base Camp Trek, it is mandatory to pay a 30% non refundable deposit of the total cost of the trip. The rest of the payment can be done after you reach Kathmandu. This ensures all the arrangements of permits, transportation, accommodation, and trek preparations.

faqs.q: What is the cancellation policy?
faqs.a:
Any cancellation request must be submitted in written form. The general cancellation charge of 30% of the total cost of the trip applies when the cancellation occurs. In case of cancellation made 7 days prior to the departure date, a cancellation charge can go up to 100% of the service cost based on the arrangements that have been made. 

It is recommended to take trip cancellation insurance to cover yourself from unforeseen circumstances.

faqs.q: Why Should I Book Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Base Camp Adventure?
faqs.a:
Base Camp Adventure offers:

  • Guides with local expertise
  • Trekking team of professionals
  • The real Nepalese experience
  • Tailored tour itinerary
  • High regard for safety
  • Groups departing in small sizes
  • Excellent customer service

We strive to give you a safe and memorable Himalayan experience.

faqs.q: What type of trail will I encounter on the Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: The trail includes stone steps, forested areas, rocky moraines, suspension bridges, village trail and alpine glaciers and uneven mountainous terrain. Some parts may also be steep, particularly those near Ulleri, Chhomrong and higher zones.

faqs.q: Does the ABC Trek include any technical climbing parts?
faqs.a: No, ABC trek does not include any technical climbing or the use of ropes or mountaineering tools. But trekkers must expect a challenging day's walk, steep ascents and weather changes.

faqs.q: What kinds of animals will I come across during my Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: There are various types of wildlife found in the Annapurna region. Some of the animals which you might see are monkeys, Himalayan Tahr, Musk Deer, Langurs and Himalayan birds like eagles and pheasants.

faqs.q: Is there battery charging facility?
faqs.a: The tea houses have charging facilities with both electricity and via their solar panels but if it has been cloudy for several days, there may not be enough reserves to charge barberries for your camera, and thus it is better to have an extra battery. If there is electricity only from solar panels then the tea houses usually charge for it – maybe a 100-200 rupees per hour. Many people want to charge their batteries so try to plug your stuff in as soon as you arrive.

reviews.author: Fusun63-Istanbul, Turkey
reviews.body: We will visit Kathmandu and Annapurna Trakking.They organize wedding seromony for us.I feel myself in paradise. It is lively holiday.Thanks to Shree and his team.I hope I can make new organization with them

reviews.author: sunita-b-London, United Kingdom
reviews.body: We were introduced to this agency by someone we had come across in the shop opposite who was also a guide himself. When we spoke to Shree at the agency we felt assured that the info we were given suited what we were looking for, more importantly Shree designed us an itinerary based on what we wanted and didn't just try to sell us pre designed package! I personally was really happy with all the effort he made for us as it hadn't been the case with a previous agency that I was in contact with who had tried to sell me a packaged tour that was going to cost two of us $100 per day? This seemed to be the norm when they found out I lived abroad and was with a foreigner (I come from Nepal and my other half is an Aussie) so they all wanted to charge me tourist price despite being nepalese! Shree kindly provided us a porter guide, Ray(his nepalese name is Rebati) who was an outstanding chap went out of his way to accommodate our request, ensured that we were looked after and was very friendly yet professional. I can't rave enough about this agency, Ray's excellent porter guide service and Shree's honesty in providing us with necessary information to make our first trekking to Annapurna Basecamp an experience of a life time. I would highly recommend these guys to my friends and family who may wish to come to Nepal for trekking.

reviews.author: Lee N-Penang Island, Malaysia
reviews.body: We were a group of 9 people booked a pre day tour of kathmandu to nagarkot and trek to abc with Base Camp Adventure. we found Mr. Shree (the director of BCA) himself is a very active and understang person who always resplied our inquiries without any hasitation. we found all BCA team are so helpful and understanding even we changed the plan in the middle of the tour they easily accepted our purposal. now we love to recommend them as one of the best trek and tour organizer of nepal. no dout that you will get the best service and best team of guide, porter and driver as they look like so professional and well trainned. Namaste!

reviews.author: Gitendrap
reviews.body: I had a wonderful time trekking through the foothills of the Annapurna region with some close friends and Prakash, our benevolent, cheery tour guide. We spent our days exploring the cinematic landscape and nights resting and relaxing at one of the many teahouses along the trail. The raw beauty and majesty of the Annapurna range doesn't hit you till you see it up close and personal with your very own eyes. We were eager to cover a fair bit of the region, starting at Shyauli bazaar, through to Poon Hill and ending at Tatopani (hot springs) with just three full days on hand, but Shree and the team at Basecamp adventures had the expertise and experience to craft an itinerary to suit. They acted professional at all times and were very well priced given the calibre of service. Prakash is an able and experienced guide and was sensitive to our needs as beginners, often revealing interesting facts about life in the mountains - we even got to visit a Gurung culture museum. I would highly recommend going on a trek with these guys, I know I'll be going back for a possible Everest base camp expedition!

reviews.author: daviozopl-Johor Bahru
reviews.body: 9 of us (from 14 - 55 y/o) did a 9-day Annapurna Base Camp Trek. Fantastic trip! Although some of us are sick during the trek due to the High Altitude, our guide Mr. Prakash and the trekking team (Ganesh, Ozune, Krishna, Govind and Bikash) backed us up with lots of care and help. They are truly our guardian angels during the trek. We really appreciated that! Amendments of initial itinerary was done professionally by Mr. Prakash and the team due to our health condition. Well done Mr. Prakash and the team! Credit also goes to Mr. Shree for arranging everything before our arrival in Kathmandu, as well as the airport pick-up. Also Mr. Ramesh, our cultural guide for Kathmandu Valley sightseeing. Its a professional team that you can trust! Will definitely recommend this company if you're thinking of trekking in Nepal!
