overview:
Annapurna Base Camp via Poon Hill is a prime destination for avid trekkers all around the world. This outstanding trek in the Annapurna region is quite famous among trekkers all over the world. Trekkers will pass through the Himalayan foothills and green hills of the region. The beautiful surrounding environment of this area includes hills, lakes, glaciers, rivers, waterfalls, and others.

The trails pass through cultural settlements of the Gurung, Tamang, Magar, and other ethnic communities. Trekkers can also observe various Buddhist monasteries, chortens, mani walls, and others during their journey. Their incredible cultural heritage, lifestyle, and traditions will provide you with a unique perspective.

Moreover, this outstanding trek passes through the narrow valleys of Machhapuchhre and Himchuli mountains. The forested trails, green terrains, and other fantastic landscapes are excellent landmarks of this trek. A professional guide and porter will help you navigate along paths and interact with locals. Their incredible hospitality and delicious cuisine will spellbind you.

This incredible trek to Annapurna Base Camp starts from Kathmandu as you take a scenic drive to Pokhara and Nayapul. Furthermore, the hike passes through Tirkha Dhunga and other settlements of Chhomrong, Bamboo, and Deurali. Trekkers can explore ABC and trek back to Bamboo, Jhinu Danda, and Nayapul to arrive at Pokhara. You will also get to observe gorgeous sunrises from the Poon Hill viewpoint as well.

Moreover, accommodations during your trek are teahouses and lodges. You will get basic facilities of a room with beds, pillows, and warm blankets. The tranquil atmosphere of this region will make you fall in love with this place. Furthermore, this outstanding trek in the foothills of Annapurna massif comes at a reasonable cost. Read on for the Annapurna Base Camp trek via Poon Hill itinerary and other information in detail.

Highlights of the Trip

  • Awe-inspiring views of snow-capped mountains including majestic snow-capped mountains including Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, and Machhapuchhre
  • Breathtaking sunrise and sunset views overlooking snow-capped mountains from Poon Hill
  • Passing through various traditional settlements of Chhomrong and Bamboo
  • Observing the rare and endangered flora and fauna
  • Accommodation facilities at various tea houses and homestays
  • Tasting exotic cuisine of local people
  • Exploring the unique culture, beautiful tradition, and rural lifestyle of the ethnic Gurung and Magar community
  • Incredible welcome and hospitality of local people
  • Relaxing hot water bath at Jhinu Danda hot springs

Some Essential Tips For Trek

  • Get Nepali rupees in cash and keep them in separate pockets.
  • Acclimatization regularly with proper hydration along the trek.
  • Pack only necessary items.
  • Get an adequate trekking professional guide and porters.
  • Trek at a gentle pace, and do not rush during your tour.
  • Advance book all accommodations and meal facilities
  • Check weather forecasts.
  • Start trekking early so that you can arrive before dark
  • Carry protein bars, granola bars, chocolate bars, and other snacks

itinerary.title: Arrival at Kathmandu and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: Upon your arrival at Kathmandu, our supporting staff will transfer you to a hotel and brief you about the tour. Our staff will pick you from the <a href="https://www.tiairport.com.np/">Tribhuvan international airport</a> and transfer you to your chosen accommodation. You will receive a traditional Nepalese-style welcome with garlands and tika. After having a short briefing, you can stroll around the city. You will return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara.
itinerary.html: <strong>Drive Distance</strong>: 40.8 km <strong>Drive Duration</strong>: 6-7 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude</strong>: 1,400 m We will continue our journey from Kathmandu to Pokhara on a scenic drive. It only <strong>takes around 6-7 hours</strong> to arrive at <a href="https://basecampadventure.com/beautiful-pokhara/">Pokhara</a> from Kathmandu. Our supporting staff will take you to your hotel. There are many sightseeing points in this city including many natural beauties. Phewa lake, Davis falls, Chamero cave, Mahendra Cave, and others are some of the famous sightseeing points in the city. You can also observe many other spots, including the World Peace Pagoda, Bindabasini temple, Tal Barahi Temple, etc. Furthermore, there are bungee jumping, skydiving, <a href="https://basecampadventure.com/paragliding-in-pokhara/">paragliding</a>, zip-lining, and other <strong>adventure sports</strong> in the region. You will return to your hotel in Pokhara, where you will rest for the night.

itinerary.title: Drive from Pokhara to Nayapul, Trek to Ulleri (1920 meters)
itinerary.html: <strong>Drive Distance</strong>: 40.8 km <strong>Drive Duration</strong>: 2 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude</strong>: 1,920 m After leaving Pokhara, you will drive to Nayapul. Trekkers will trek for 2 hours to arrive at Nayapul, covering a distance of 40.8 km. The trail passes through the spectacular Modi River and foothills of the Himalayas. The <strong>scenic landscapes</strong> of the region will provide you with an outstanding trekking opportunity. We will drive for 2-hours to arrive at Nayapul. From there, trekkers will need to cross the suspension bridge and then head towards Birethanti. The trail of this trek moves through Mathathanti, Tikhedhunga, Hille before arriving at Ulleri. Trekkers can observe Annapurna South (7,219 m), Patal Hiunchuli (6,441 m), and other snow-capped mountains from Ulleri.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ulleri to Ghorepani (2860 meters)
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek Duration</strong>: 4-5 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude</strong>: 2,860 m We will trek through various thick forests of rhododendron trees and settlements of Banthanti and Nangethanti. Moreover, We will enter the village of Ghorepani, trekking uphill along the way. You can observe beautiful settlements of the Annapurna massif and other snow-capped mountains of the region. We will have rest in a teahouse in Ulleri in the evening.

itinerary.title: Hike early in the morning to Poon Hill (3210 meters) and then trek to Tadapani (2610 meters).
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek Duration: </strong>6-7 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude: </strong>3,210 m We will start our trek from Ulleri to <strong>Poon Hill viewpoint.</strong> Trails to observe beautiful views of the <a href="https://basecampadventure.com/destinations/nepal/annapurna-region/">Annapurna region</a>'s snow-capped mountains is quite beautiful. The majestic view of the sunrise overlooking snow-capped mountains is the highlight of this trek. You can watch various snow-capped mountains, including Mt. Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Lamjung Himal (6,983 m), Nilgiri (7,061 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), and others. After arriving at Ghorepani, you will observe beautiful surroundings and trek back to Tadapani.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tadapani to Chomrong (2170 meters.)
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek Duration: </strong>5-6 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 2,170 m After observing gorgeous sunrise early in the morning, we will ascend from the Tadapani village settlement on a forested trail to reach Chomrong. There are beautiful suspension bridges that you need to cross over Kimrong Khola. You will arrive at Jhinu Danda hot water spring on this trail. We will take a dip in this beautiful hot water spring and move into the Chhomrong path. From Chhomrong, you can observe stunning views of <strong>Machhapuchhre (6,993 m),</strong> Annapurna South (7,219 m), and others. You can spend overnight at a teahouse after exploring around the region.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chhomrong to Himalaya (2920 meters)
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek Duration:</strong> 6-7 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 2,920 m We will start our trek from Chhomrong on an easy path through thick forests of rhododendron, orchids, and ferns. After descending on stone stairs, we will cross Chhomrong Khola on a suspension bridge and then trek uphill to Sinuwa. We will descend back to stone staircases to arrive at the settlement of Bamboo. The trail continues on a forested path from Bamboo to reach Himalaya via Dobhan. We will observe around the region and stay overnight at guest houses in the area.

itinerary.title: Trek from Himalaya to Annapurna Base Camp (4130 meters)
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek Duration:</strong> 6-7 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 4,130 m The trail on this day leads you to ABC as we ascend to Deurali on a stone staircase. Beautiful views of snow-capped mountains along the route will enchant any traveler. You will arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (3,700 m), where you can stay and explore for some time. The trail then follows South Annapurna Glacier moraines to arrive at Annapurna Base Camp. It is the base camp of <strong>Annapurna South (7,219 m).</strong> Breathtaking views of Patal Hiunchuli (6,441 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), Mt. Annapurna South (7,219 m), and others are prime attractions of this trek. We will explore around and rest at a local teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from ABC back to Bamboo (2345 meters)
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek Duration:</strong> 6-7 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 2,345 m After breakfast, we will continue our trek from ABC to Machhapuchhre Base Camp. The trail passes through the moraine route observing the snowy peaks, Modi Khola, and other forests. You will observe the region's natural beauties passing through Deurali and Himalaya's settlements to arrive at Bamboo. We will rest for the evening at a teahouse in Bamboo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bamboo to Jhinu hot spring (1780 meters)
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek Duration:</strong> 6-7 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 1,780 m We will ascend along a trail passing through Bamboo to arrive at Sinuwa. Then, we will trek through <strong>Chhomrong Khola</strong> on a descending path to finally climb the upper Chhomrong on a rocky trail. After descending to Jhinu Danda, we will dip and relax at a natural hot spring after an arduous trekking journey. We will rest in the Jhinu danda area teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Jhinu danda to Nayapul (1010 meters) and drive to Pokhara.
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek Duration:</strong> 5-6 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 1,400 m After relaxing in Jhinu danda, we will trek on a descending trail to arrive at Nayapul. We will follow the Modi Khola trail as we observe the scenic natural beauty of the region. We will finally drive back to Pokhara from Nayapul. We will stroll around the evening in Lakeside, a tourist hub with many cafes, restaurants, nightclubs, bars, etc. We will come back to our hotel in Lakeside, Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Drive back from Pokhara to Kathmandu (1345 meters).
itinerary.html: Drive Duration: 6-7 hours <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 1,400 m We will leave Pokhara and continue our journey to Kathmandu on a tourist bus. The beautiful scenic tour passes through green hills and <strong>highway settlements. </strong>After arrival, you will get transferred to the hotel with the help of our supporting staff. You can stroll around the Thamel area in the evening and celebrate the completion of our journey. Our Annapurna Base Camp Trek via Poon Hill itinerary comes to an end in Kathmandu.

sections.title: When Is Ideal Time For Annapurna Base Camp Trek Via Poon Hill?
sections.html:
When Is Ideal Time For Annapurna Base Camp Trek Via Poon Hill?

Annapurna region treks are ideal in Spring and Autumn. The beautiful natural scenery of the place in a tranquil atmosphere is the main highlight of trekking in these seasons.

Spring (March-May)

A scenic environment and stable weather conditions in the Spring season are ideal for trekking in Nepal. Moreover, there are wildflowers like rhododendron blooming all over the trails of this trek. Trekkers can observe these beautiful landscapes in an incredible trekking environment.

You can experience warm weather with moderate temperatures that do not exceed 25 degrees Celsius. There are unobstructed views of snow-capped mountains on the backdrop of a clear blue sky. Therefore, the Spring season is one of the best times for this trek.

Autumn (September-November)

Trekking the Annapurna Base Camp in Autumn is another excellent adventure. Trekkers can experience clear blue skies, soothing weather, and mild temperatures in Autumn. The weather remains calm, and there are breathtaking views of snow-capped mountains.

The temperature stays at 15-20 degrees Celsius, which is ideal for trekking. The most exciting aspect of trekking in Autumn is that it is a cultural time in the region. Many festivals get celebrated by locals, which allows you to go on a cultural exploration. Moreover, you can also trek the seasons of monsoon or winter.

There are many weather-related challenges in these off-seasons. Winters are cold with heavy snowfall all around. Furthermore, The summer monsoon brings heavy precipitation and muddy trails. The temperature can drop below -20 degrees Celsius in the winter season, especially at night and mornings.

Avalanches and landslides are quite common during the summer monsoon. However, with immense enthusiasm and proper preparation, you can take this trek any time of the year.

Read more on: Seasons in Nepal

Difficulties of Annapurna Base Camp trek via Poon Hill

Annapurna Base Camp trek is a challenging adventure in the foothills of Annapurna massif. The primary difficulty factor of this trek is altitude sickness. The trails of this trek lie at a high altitude of above 5,000 m There are fewer oxygen levels and air pressure, which makes breathing difficult for trekkers.

Acclimatization is essential to tackle altitude sickness. Your guide will help you set up acclimatization points in your journey. Besides, you will also need to drink water at regular intervals while trekking as dehydration is the primary cause of altitude sickness in the region. Anti-nausea tablets like Diamox will help you prevent symptoms of altitude sickness.

This trek requires a 6 to 7 hours taxing trekking journey in uphill and downhill terrains. You will need to trek rugged landscapes, steep uphills, and stoney paths. Therefore, a good training regime before the start of the trek is vital for all trekkers. This training will help you to gain the physical fitness and stamina required for this trek.

You also need to stay in tea houses and lodges that do not have any fancy facilities. Meals in these teahouses are basic too as you will get served a local Nepalese dish of "Dal Bhat." With proper preparation, you can take this trek in the Annapurna region with ease.

Things to consider for Annapurna Base Camp Trek Via Poon Hill

Acclimatize and hydrate regularly

Acclimatization and hydration are essential parts of any trekking journey. This Annapurna Base Camp trek via Poon Hill is one of the best treks in the country. You should acclimatize so that you can adapt to high altitude conditions. Besides that, you should not gain more than 600 m in altitude on a trekking day.

Hydration helps you tackle altitude sickness along trails. You can also take Diamox tablets to prevent altitude sickness symptoms, including nausea, headache, dizziness, shortness of breath, insomnia, and others.

Get professional trek guides and porters.

Hiring a professional trekking guide is essential for navigating along trails. They also help you interact with the local people, explore their culture, tradition, and heritage. Porters will carry your luggage along the route. These porters will allow you to trek with ease. Besides, there are porter-guides available as well who work both as porter and guides. They will cost you less and are ideal if you are trekking on a budget.

Train well for the trek

Annapurna Base Camp trek is a challenging trek that requires proper training. You need to trek at least two months before the start of this trek. Trails of this trek move uphill and downhill a lot in the rugged landscapes. A Training regime will help you gain proper physical fitness and stamina.

Moreover, You can perform various activities, including cycling, swimming, jogging, hiking, etc. These cardiovascular activities or aerobics will help you adapt to high altitude regions. Mental preparation is essential, as well as it can help you prepare for this challenging trek. You can also trek well with a positive attitude.

Time of travel

Time of travel is another factor that you should consider for your trekking journey. Autumn and Spring are peak seasons for travel. Stable weather conditions and tranquil atmosphere is the highlight in these seasons. You can also trek in Winters and Monsoon, which are off-seasons. But you need proper packing and preparation whenever you decide to hike in the Annapurna region.

Get Travel insurance.

Travel insurance is essential for the Annapurna Base Camp trek via Poon Hill. Moreover, Trekkers should get proper travel insurance. It should cover medical emergencies, accidents, helicopter evacuation, flight cancellations, theft, and others. Hence, you should get adequate travel insurance before traveling on this trek.

Food and Accommodation facilities in the Annapurna Base Camp Trek via Poon Hill

The Annapurna Base Camp trek has many tea houses and lodges in its trail. The accommodation facilities are basic with facilities like beds, a pillow, sheets, a mattress, and a blanket. There are squat-style toilets in these teahouses. However, you need to bring your toiletries.

The food that gets served twice a day is "Dal Bhat." This local Nepalese dish is ideal for trekking adventures. Different varieties of bread, toast, boiled eggs, porridge, and others are available for breakfast in the tea house. You can get burgers, pizza, pasta, noodles, momo, and other cuisines as well.

Hot beverages like tea, coffee, and garlic soup are also available along the trail. Moreover, You can carry tea bags and coffee powder to save costs. Snickers, chocolate bars, protein bars, granola bars, and others will keep your hunger away during the trek.

Read more on: Nepalese Food

Why Take The Annapurna Base Camp Trek Via Poon Hill?

Staying at Ghorepani village

Ghorepani Village, among magical forests, is one of the scenic settlements of the Annapurna region. Furthermore, the stunning view of Annapurna and Dhaulagiri will enchant any travelers. Full bloom rhododendrons all through the hills is a highlight of this trek. You will stay in one of the slated roof houses in the village. A homestay allows you to observe the beautiful culture and lifestyle of locals.

Breathtaking views of snow-capped Mountains

This Annapurna region trek provides you with the best views of the snow-capped mountains. Trekkers can observe the glorious sunrise from the Poon Hill viewpoint. Furthermore, The majestic view of Annapurna massif in a clear blue sky is the prime attraction of this trek. You can observe other Himalayas from the trails, including Mt. Annapurna II, Dhampus, Gangapurna, and others.

Relaxing Jhinu Danda Hot Water Spring

Jhinu Danda Hot Water Spring is one of the best aspects of this Annapurna Base Camp trek via Poon Hill. Moreover, Dipping in the hot waters of Jhinu Danda is quite relaxing after a long, taxing trekking adventure. Jhinu Danda is just 20 minutes away from the Bamboo settlement.

Cultural tour

This incredible trek is also a great cultural tour. There are small mini settlements around the Annapurna base camp trail. The settlements of local people provide you with a unique aspect of the region. There are many ethnic groups in the Annapurna region.

The culture, heritage, and lifestyles of different communities will enchant you. A professional trekking guide is essential during this trip as it will help you interact with the locals. They will also act as a translator.

Gorgeous Sunrise views from Poon Hill

Poon Hill is a scenic viewpoint in Annapurna base camp trail. The gorgeous sunrise overlooking Annapurna III, Dhampus, Gurja Himal, and others are quite an attraction of this trek. The green forests and terraced farmed hills are some of the best parts of this trek.

Pokhara Sightseeing tour

Pokhara is a Lake City with many lakes and sightseeing points. There are many waterfalls, lakes, monasteries, temples, and caves in Pokhara. You can also relax in cafes, nightclubs, bars, and restaurants in Lakeside. Hence, this tourist hub of Pokhara is a great sightseeing spot.

More details on: Annapurna Base Camp Trek Packing List

Final Say

Annapurna Base Camp Trek via Poon Hill is a scenic trek in the foothills of Nepal's Himalayas. This incredible trek provides you with the best views of snow-capped mountains and the cultural beauty of the Annapurna region. This article provides you with complete details regarding this Annapurna Base Camp trek via Poon Hill. Contact us for further information on this trip. Book your trip now!

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return
summary: Embark on the adventure of a lifetime with our Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return. Trek through breathtaking landscapes, ancient villages, and lush forests to reach the iconic Annapurna Base Camp.

seo.title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return - 7 Days
seo.description: Embark on the adventure of a lifetime with our Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return. Trek through breathtaking landscapes, ancient villages, and lush forests to reach the iconic Annapurna Base Camp.

cover.alt: Annapurna Base Camp Trekking with Helicopter Return

map.alt: Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return Map

overview: Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return is one of the most fascinating and distinct trekking prospects in the mainstream Annapurna region. Unlike the regular trekking adventures, in this exciting excursion, you will fly back to Pokhara from Annapurna Base Camp enjoying the epic aerial views of the north-central Himalayan peaks. The Annapurna Base Camp Trek is one of the oldest and iconic trekking opportunities in the Nepali Himalayas. This remarkable trek takes you across the beautiful traditional settlements of Gurung and Tamang where you will get the opportunity to gain first-hand experience with their unique culture, traditions, and warm hospitality. Similarly, this Himalayan trek also doesn’t fall behind the natural allurements as well. Popular as the second most popular Himalayan trekking destination, the Annapurna region boasts an incredible bio-diversity as it is home to one of the most popular conservation areas in the country, Annapurna Conservation Area, which conserves the endangered Himalayan flora and fauna. This exciting fascinating Himalayan excursion starts with the exploration with exploration of the sub-tropical forested areas with bright and colorful flowers. Navigating your way across the enchanting streams, waterfalls, and rivers, you will then reach the glacial moraines after crossing the alpine meadows. So, this trek is most definitely a fulfilling and gratifying Himalayan journey. The helicopter flight, on top of that, adds a luxurious and enthralling experience to the trek.
highlights: Trekking on one of the most iconic and oldest Himalayan trekking routes
Traversing across the charming Gurung, Magar, Thakali, and Tamanag settlements
Magnificent views of the north-central Himalayan peaks like Annapurna South, Annapurna I, Annapurna III, Khangsar Kang, Macchapuchhre, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, and other surrounding peaks
Hike to the popular vantage point of Annapurna region, Poon Hill
Rich flora and fauna of the Annapurna Conservation Area
Exploration of two base Camp in a single trek; Annapurna Base Camp and Machhapuchhre Base Camp
Aerial views of the Himalayan peaks as you fly over the base camp

itinerary.title: Drive from Pokhara to Nayapul (1,010 m / 3,314 ft) and trek to Ulleri (1,920 m / 6,299 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Accommodation:Guest House
Ulleri Elevation: 1,920 m
Altitude Gain: 1,098 m
Trek Distance: 10 km
Trekking Hours: 5-6 hrs

You exciting journey of the Annapurna Base Camp start after a nourishing breakfast at Pokhara. You will then board a comfortable vehicle from Pokhara heading toward the Nayapul. This exciting drive will take about one and a half hours; you will pass through the charming Gurung village of Lumle perched on the mountainside before reaching Nayapul.

From here, you will commence your exciting trekking journey, and in about 30 minutes of uphill trekking, you will reach Birethanti. Then, enjoying the scenic views of the terraced farmlands alongside the Bhurungdi Khola, you will pass through Tikhedunga, Sudame Village, and Hile Village before reaching Ulleri.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ulleri to Ghorepani (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html:
Accommodation: Guest House
Ghorepani Elevation: 2,860 m
Trek Distance: 10.3 km
Trekkinmg Hours: 4-5 hrs

Its an exciting day’s trekking adventure today, after breakfast, you will move along the gradually inclining trail immersing in the enchanting views of Annapurna, Macchapuchhre, and Hiunchuli. Trekking past the Banthanti Village, you will then enter the lush trail surrounded by colorful rhododendron forests.

You will move along the forested trail for a while and cross a small bridge to reach Ghorepani Village, situated at the ridgeline. From the vantage point of this beautiful Gurung village, you will be able to catch breathtaking panoramas of the north-central Himalayan mountain ranges as you settle in for the night.

itinerary.title: Early morning hike to Poon Hill (3,210 m / 10,531 ft) for sunrise views, followed by a trek to Tadapani (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 6–7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Accommodation: Guest House
Tadapani Elevation : 2,610 m
Altitude Gain: 2,610 m
Trek Distance: 11 km (with Poon Hill)
Walking Hours: 6-7 hrs

Today’s trekking journey takes you to the one of the most popular vantage point in the lower Annapurna region, Poon Hill (3,210 m). You will do the hike to this vatage point early in the morning to enjoy a magical sunrise view glittering on the sparkling snow-clad peaks.

From the Poon Hill vantage point, you will be able to enjoy the panoramic views of the Himalayan peaks like Annapurna I, II, and III, Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Tukuche Peak, Lamjung Himal, Nilgiri, Barah Sikhar and other surrounding peaks.

After completing the hike and enjoying a hearty breakfast at Ghorepani, you will then commence your trekking journey toward Tadapani. In this scenic trail, you will pass Deurali before reaching your resting destination today.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tadapani to Chommrong (2,170 m / 7,119 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Accommodation: Guesthouse
Chhomrong Elevation: 2,170 m
Trek Distance: 8.6 km
Trekking Hours: 6-7 hrs

On today’s uphill trekking adventure, you first trek past the terraced farmlands and move along charming trails alongside the Kimrong Khola. You will also occasionally cross the cascading waterfalls and also trek past the beautiful villages of Ghandruk and Chuile.

Enjoy the epic views of the sparkling massifs; you will cross a bridge during the last stretch and follow the steep stone staircase to reach the Gurung village of Chhomrong. From this charming village situated at the lap of the towering Annapurna massif, you can enjoy the spectacular views of the Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chhomrong to Himalaya (2,920 m / 9,580 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Accommodation:Guest House
Himalaya Altitude: 2,920 m
Trek Distance: 8.6 km
Walking Hours: 6-7 hrs

Heading toward the further elevation points in your Himalayan journey, you will trek along the beautiful trail alongside Chromrong Khola. Then, ascending on the steep stone stairs, you will trek through lush oak, bamboo, and rhododendron forests to reach Sinuwa Village.

Enjoying on the stunning views of Annapurna and Machhapuchhre on the way, you will move along the route that stretches all the way to Khuldigar Village. From here, it is an easy descent to Bamboo, which caters to trekkers in its bamboo lodges, and the final ascend will bring you to Himalaya, your resting destination tonight.

itinerary.title: Trek from Himalaya to Annapurna Base Camp (4,130 m / 13,550 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Accommodation: Guest House
ABC Altitude: 4,130 m
Trek Distance: 9.2 km
Walking Hours: 6-7 hrs

This day’s trek will lead you to the main objective of this Himalayan adventure. After leaving Himalaya, you will follow the route across the narrow gorge of the Modi Khola Valley and follow the steep forested trail to reach Hinku Cave.

Then, you will traverse across the Deurali Village before entering the Annapurna Sanctuary which will eventually lead you to the Annapurna Base Camp. You will also trek across Machhapuchhre Base Camp (3,700 m) in this trekking route to reach the lap of Annapurna.

From Annapurna Base Camp, you will be able to relish the magnificent views of the Himalayan ranges like Annapurna South, Annapurna I, Annapurna III, Khangsar Kang, Macchapuchhre, Hiunchuli and Gangapurna.

You will forever treasure this day, immersing in the mystical ambiance of the Himalayas at its foothills. After a long and exciting journey to reach your goal, you will definitely have won yourself the right to intake to an incredible atmosphere to your heart’s content. Thus, on this day, you will spend your night at the base camp enjoying the magical views under the starry sky.

itinerary.title: Helicopter return from Annapurna Base Camp to Pokhara (820 m / 2,690 ft), 15-20 minutes.
itinerary.html:
Flight Duration: 15-20 mins

After admiring the mystical allurements of the Himalayas from its base and enjoying the magnificent up-close views of the snow-clad peaks, it is time to pull the curtain on your exploration. On this day, after enjoying a hearty breakfast, you will bid farewell to the Himalayas and board a chartered helicopter.

Your flight will then gradually hover over from the base of the pristine Annapurna and provide you the opportunity to enjoy the breathtaking Himalayan panorama of the north-central Himalayan prospects.

Then, flying over the mainstream trail, you will hover over the beautiful settlements, fascinating terraced farms, lush valleys, cascading waterfalls, and rivers; you head down toward Pokhara.

After landing at Pokhara, you will be transported back to your respective hotel; you can enjoy a leisurely afternoon exploring the popular tourist destination in this beautiful city of lakes. Thank you for trekking with Base Camp Adventure, Happy journey!

sections.title: Useful Info
sections.html:
Best Time for Trek

For the best experience, the peak seasons like spring and autumn are considered the ultimately ideal period to take part in this Himalayan exploration. Both of these seasons have the best climatic conditions and add their own charms to the trekking adventure, which makes the excursion valuable. Spring (March, April, and May) is the peak point of nature, meaning your trekking trails will be decorated with the colorful vistas of nature. If you do Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return in spring, you will trek amidst the colorful wildflowers and lush greenery. The melting snow also adds momentum to the cascading rivers, streams, and waterfalls, which will make the excursion magical. Similarly, autumn (September, October, and November) has the most stable weather conditions and temperatures, which are ideal for outdoor adventures. The hues of grey and crimson, which represent this fall season, add a unique experience to this Himalayan excursion. On top of that, the autumn is known as the harvest and festive season. Nepal celebrates some of the major festivals like Dashain, Tihar, Chhath, Teej, Gai Jatra, and Mani Rimdu in this period. So, if you want a first-hand experience of the cultural aspects of the country, this it the time to be in Nepal.

Temperatures of Annapurna Region During Spring and Autumn

Temperature of Annapurna Region in Spring (March to May): 10°C to 20°C Temperature of Annapurna Region in Autumn (September to November): 5°C to 18°C You may also like:
  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek in June
  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek Map
  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek Cost
  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek Distance

How Difficult is Annapurna Base Camp Trek With Helicopter Return?

The Annapurna Base Camp Trek is a moderate and comfortable trekking experience in the mainstream Annapurna region. It is, in fact, one of the beginner-friendly exploration prospects in the Himalayas. The difficulty factors of this adventure are on a moderate scale, and the overall trip isn’t typically as demanding as other treks that take you across Himalayan passes and high-altitude points. Regardless, you will still need to overcome a few hurdles in this exciting trekking adventure that takes you along one of the oldest and classical routes in the Himalayas. You will begin your trekking adventure at Nayapul (1,070 m) and slowly navigate along the high-altitude points of the trek, reaching the maximum altitude at Annapurna Base Camp (4,130 m). Thus, the overall altitude gain in this trip is about 3,060 m (10,039 feet) from the starting point. So, even if the overall trek isn’t that physically challenging, you will still need to be careful about the Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS). Similarly, the Annapurna Base Camp trekking distance is approximately 115 km (71 miles); you will need to trek for about 4 to 6 hours on average during each day of the exploration. However, in the Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return, as you will fly back to Pokhara directly from the base camp, your trekking distance will be cut by half. So, the difficulty level drops to an even further level, making this exploration a comfortable and remarkable journey.

Training and Preparation

Needless to say, as you are embarking on an iconic Himalayan adventure that takes you to significant altitudes, you need to train adequately to relish the experience. Your comfort level during the trip and how much you are enjoying the experience will entirely depend on the effort you put in during the training. So, make sure you are well-prepared; otherwise, you may have to drag yourself throughout the trek, completely missing out on relishing the journey part. The general training recommended period for high-altitude treks in Nepal is about 3 to 8 weeks. You can decide on the duration of your training after going through a physical assessment and working out on your weak aspects. Remember, preparation doesn’t mean that you will have to get in the best shape of your life; emphasize the endurance and stamina part to easily overcome the minor hurdles of this Himalayan journey. Endurance Training Exercises: Squat, Lunge, Plank, Deadlift, Hollow Hold, Plank, Leg Extension, Calf Raise, Woodchop, Push Up, Overhead Press, etc. Stamina Training Exercises: Jumping Jack, Jogging, Swimming, Dancing, Kick Boxing, Jumping Rope, Rowing, Cycling, etc.

Permits Necessary for Annapurna Base Camp Trek

During the Annapurna Base Camp Trek, you will need to trek through the protected areas of the mainstream region. You will generally require two major permits for doing Himalayan adventure:
  • Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) Entry Permit
  • Trekker’s Information Management System (TIMS) Card
Both of these permits are mandatory for this trek, and if trekkers are found to be trekking, they will be liable for the fine and may even get banned from the region. The cost of an ACAP Permit is about US$ 30, and the TIMS Card costs about US$ 17. These permits can be obtained from the Nepal Tourism Board’s office located in Kathmandu or from their outlet in Pokhara. For the Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return, Base Camp Adventure will collect all the required permits on your behalf.

What Kind of Food and Accommodation Can You Expect During Trek?

Annapurna region is only behind the Everest region for the most iconic trekking experiences in the Himalayas. It means as a mainstream trekking region, the food and accommodation of the Annapurna region are more developed than other remote trekking parts. So, during your Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return, you will be able to enjoy a moderate to luxurious level of facilities. In this exciting Himalayan trekking package, you will spend six nights on the mountain, including one night at the Annapurna Base Camp. From the accommodation aspects, even in a standard trekking package, the lodging facilities are pretty cozy and on a moderate scale. You will stay in private rooms with two or three shared beds in a standard trekking package. Similar to the sleeping arrangements, the bathroom facilities are also on a shared basis; they may be attached to the room or outer vicinity of the teahouses. During your trek, you will stay at warm and comfortable teahouses that offer basic amenities like shower, internet, TV, and charging facilities. There are also communal areas at the teahouses/lodges where trekkers can interact with other adventurers. Note: We also provide the luxurious trekking package option if you are looking for a more personalized experience. You will not have to pay any extra fees for basic amenities in the luxury package.

Food and Beverage

Like the accommodation facilities, the food and beverages on this trekking trail are available on different standards, from basic to luxurious. During your trekking days, you will be able to enjoy a diverse range of menus in this mainstream route, which comprises of delightful cultural delicacies and other Asia culture-inspired dishes as well as a popular Western menu. You can generally expect the following menus at the teahouses/lodges during your Annapurna Base Camp Trek. For Breakfast: Egg, Toast, Jam, Butter, Honey, Cornflakes, Oats, Museli, Fruits, Gurung Bread, Muesli, Selroti, Paratha, Chapati, Pancake, etc For Lunch and Dinner: Traditional Dal Bhaat, Thakali Set, Dhindo, Gundruk, Pakoda, Momo, Chowmein, Thukpa, Shyaphale, Rilduk, Pizza, Sandwich, Burger, Pasta, Steak, Fries, etc Similarly, for the beverages, you can enjoy refreshing cold drinks, fruit juice, warm savory delights, and alcoholic drinks. However, you should either completely avoid alcoholic beverages or drink them in moderation, as they can affect your acclimatization process.

Trip Safety

Your Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return with Base Camp Adventure will be only be handled by a group of experts. A government-licensed trekking guide with relevant years of guiding experience in the route will lead your team through the laps of the pristine Himalayas. We will prioritize the safety and comfort aspects of your Himalayan journey to ensure that you have a memorable experience. Even though the altitude gain in this trip isn’t that significant, we will moderate physical conditions and how well you are adapting to the new altitudes. Furthermore, we also make immediate arrangements for supplementary oxygen bottles if necessary. In case of any kind of emergency or unforeseen circumstances, your high altitude and first-aid guide will take an appropriate measure to coordinate with the main office. As this is a fully guided trekking adventure, you don’t have to worry about anything during your trip. Let us take care of every aspect of your exhilarating Himalayan trek so you can just immerse in the experience and make memories.

Is Annapurna Base Camp Trek With Helicopter Return Worth It?

Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return is one of the most exciting Himalayan trekking adventures in the Nepali Himalayas. Not only will you traverse across one of the oldest trekking routes in the Himalayas, immersing in its incredible allurements, but you will also have the opportunity to enjoy aerial views of the north-central Himalayan prospects. The memory of hovering over from the base of the gigantic Annapurna massifs and relishing the bird-eye views of the pristine Himalayan peaks will be something that you wil treasure for your lifetime. This luxury experience of aerial Himalayan view is something trekking enthusiasts all over the world yearn for. Furthermore, this classical trek blended with helicopter return significantly reduces the overall difficulty level of this trekking adventure. So, even trekkers who are conscious of the physical demands of this iconic route can partake in it. Thus, this exciting journey that explores the second most popular trekking region in the Himalayas in an easy mode and concludes the journey hovering over sparkling Himalayan peaks from their foothills and unfolds the hypnotizing aerial vistas, is certainly worth it.

Who Can Do This Trek?

Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return is suitable for any trekking enthusiast who is willing to put some effort into the physical preparation. This Himalayan exploration doesn’t take trekkers to significant altitudes, nor does it have any technically demanding sections. Thus, anyone with good health and reasonable fitness can take part in this trekking adventure. The overall success rate of the Annapurna Base Camp Trek is a complete 100%; trekkers who are well-prepared hardly fail to conquer this classical route. You also won’t have to trek over Himalayan passes or significant altitudes above 5,000 m So, this base cam trek is also perfect for a beginner trekker who wants to build up Himalayan trekking prospects. This trek doesn’t have any kind of age restrictions as well; in its trekking history, even families with children as young as 5 years old and elderly trekkers in their 70s have successfully conquered this classical route. So, if you are looking for a fulfilling Himalayan trekking experience with a relatively moderate difficulty level, Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return is the most ideal and complete trekking package. Note: If you have any kind of health condition, you should consult the trekking guide and your physician about the trek.

faqs.q: What is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return cost?
faqs.a: The general ABC Trek with helicopter return can cost somewhere between US$ 1,400 to US$ 2,000.

faqs.q: How long is the trek?
faqs.a: This exciting Himalayan adventure can last somewhere between 7 to 9 days depending on the itinerary plan and starting location.

faqs.q: What is Annapurna Base Camp Trek altitude?
faqs.a: The maximum altitude you reach in this trek is Annapurna Base Camp, which is situated at an elevation of 4,130 m (13,549 feet) from the sea level.

faqs.q: Can a beginner do this trek?
faqs.a: Yes, due to the milder scale of difficulty factors, this trek is perfect for beginner trekkers who want to gain some experience in high-altitude adventures.

faqs.q: What is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek best time?
faqs.a: For the best value experience, we recommend the high seasons like spring (March to May) and autumn (Septemeber to November).

faqs.q: Is there a shower facility available on the trekking route?
faqs.a: At the major destinations, Base Camp Adventure arranges accommodation at the teahouses/lodges with shower facilities. However, at the base camps water bucket is provided for bathing.

faqs.q: Are internet and charging facilities available in this trek?
faqs.a: Yes, teahouses at major destinations do have internet facilities, and you can also charge your devices. You will have to pay around US$ 1 to US$ 5 to use these services, which may vary depending on the altitudes.

faqs.q: I am vegetarian. Is that a problem in this trek?
faqs.a: Almost all of the teahouses along the trail do offer vegetarian and vegan variants. So, no, it will not be a problem if you are a vegetarian.

faqs.q: Can children do Annapurna Base Camp?
faqs.a: If your child is healthy and can adhere to the instructions (well-behaved), then he/she can certainly take part in this trek. In the past, children as young as 5 years old have successfully completed this trek.

faqs.q: What is the drinking water facility in this trek?
faqs.a: You can buy water bottles till Chhomrong at US$ 2 to US$ 4; however, above Chhomrong, you cannot take plastic bottles as they are banned inside the conservation area. You can either fill your reusable bottles at a clean station and filter them or buy boiled water at the teahouses.

seo.description: Explore the Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Himal Trek, combining two spectacular trails with stunning mountain views and unforgettable high-altitude experiences.

overview:
Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Himal Trek – A Perfect Himalayan Adventure

The Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Himal Trek is an incredible Himalayan adventure that combines two of Nepal's most beautiful trekking destinations into one unforgettable journey. This combined trek offers a wonderful opportunity to explore the spectacular Annapurna region, experience traditional mountain villages, walk through beautiful rhododendron forests, and enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of some of the world's highest mountains.

This trek is an excellent choice for adventure seekers who want to experience both the famous Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) and the less-crowded, scenic Mardi Himal trail in a single trip. From traditional Gurung villages and terraced farmlands to high alpine landscapes and dramatic mountain viewpoints, the journey offers remarkable diversity.

Explore the Magnificent Annapurna Base Camp

he Annapurna Base Camp section takes you deep into the heart of the Annapurna Sanctuary, surrounded by an impressive collection of Himalayan peaks. Along the trail, you pass through beautiful villages such as Ghandruk, Chhomrong, Bamboo, Dovan, and Deurali. These traditional settlements provide an insight into local Gurung culture, hospitality, and mountain lifestyles.

As you ascend, the landscape gradually changes from lush green forests and flowing rivers to rugged alpine terrain. The highlight is reaching Annapurna Base Camp at an elevation of 4,130 m (13,550 feet), where you are surrounded by spectacular Himalayan giants, including Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail).

The sunrise and sunset views from Annapurna Base Camp are particularly memorable, as the surrounding snow-covered mountains glow with beautiful golden colours.

Discover the Beautiful Mardi Himal Trek

After exploring Annapurna Base Camp, the adventure continues towards the beautiful Mardi Himal trail. Compared to the popular Annapurna Base Camp route, Mardi Himal offers a quieter trekking experience with peaceful forest trails, spectacular ridgelines, and incredible mountain scenery.

The trail passes through enchanting rhododendron forests, traditional teahouses, and open alpine landscapes. As you gain elevation, the views become increasingly impressive, with close-up perspectives of Machhapuchhre, Annapurna South, and the surrounding Himalayan peaks.

One of the major highlights is Mardi Himal High Camp, followed by the hike towards Mardi Himal Viewpoint, where you can enjoy magnificent views of the Annapurna range and the iconic Machhapuchhre mountain. The viewpoint reaches approximately 4,200 m, making it one of the most rewarding high-altitude experiences in the region.

A Unique Combination of Two Himalayan Trails

Combining Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Himal creates a more diverse trekking experience than completing either route independently. You enjoy the dramatic mountain amphitheatre of Annapurna Base Camp as well as the peaceful ridgeline trails and panoramic viewpoints of Mardi Himal.

The best seasons for this combined trek are spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November), when the weather is generally favourable and mountain visibility is often excellent.

The trek is moderately challenging and suitable for trekkers with reasonable fitness and a sense of adventure. Proper acclimatisation, gradual ascent, and preparation are important because the journey reaches elevations above 4,000 m

Whether you are visiting Nepal for the first time or returning to explore more of the Himalayas, the Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Himal combined trek offers an exceptional opportunity to experience Nepal's natural beauty, mountain culture, and unforgettable Himalayan landscapes in one remarkable adventure.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu Arrival in Kathmandu via international flight. Transfer to accommodation.
Kathmandu – Pokhara (Flight), Jeep drive from, Pokhara- Ulleri and Banthanti – Trek to Ghorepani (2675 m).
itinerary.html: After an early morning flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara, enjoy a scenic drive through rural villages and terraced farmland to Ulleri. From Ulleri, the trek begins with a steady uphill climb along stone staircases and forested trails, passing through rhododendron and oak forests. Continue ascending to reach Ghorepani, a beautiful mountain village offering stunning Himalayan views. Overnight at a teahouse.

itinerary.title: Early morning hike to Poon Hill (3210 meters) and then to Chuile or Tadapani (2610 meters).
itinerary.html: We start the day with an early morning ascent to Poon Hill along the snowy trails to witness the majestic sunrise over the peaks of Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges along with Nilgiri(7,061 m), Lamjung Himal (6,983 m), and Machhapuchhre (6,993 m). We then retrace our way back to Ghorepani and continue to climb down to the village of  Tadapani. Overnight at guest house.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tadapani or Chuile to Sinuwa.
itinerary.html: Ascend uphill and then downhill on a forested trail before crossing the suspension bridge over Kimrong Khola to reach the hot spring of Jhinu Danda. We can take a short rest in the hot spring before entering the mesmerizing village of Chhomrong. Upon reaching Chhomrong, we are rewarded with an amazing view of Annapurna South (7,219 m) and Machhapuchhre (6,993 m). And then We descend stone stairs, and upon crossing Chhomrong Khola, we ascend to Sinuwa. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sinuwa to Himalaya.
itinerary.html: Today we walk through rhododendron forest adorned with orchids and ferns. We then descend through stone staircases to reach Bamboo. From Bamboo, we walk through the forested trail to reach Himalaya hotels.

itinerary.title: Trek from Himalaya to Annapurna Base Camp.
itinerary.html: Today we reach start your trek Chhomrong to Deurali. The journey continues where we cross a narrow gorge of Mt. Machhapuchhre on the right side and Himchuli and Annapurna South on the left side. The stream flowing down from the Annapurna Base Camp produces a beautiful melancholy that makes walking enjoyable. We stay overnight at Deurali

itinerary.title: Trek from Annapurna Base Camp to Bamboo
itinerary.html: As we have explored the Annapurna Base Camp now, it is time for us to head back to Bamboo. But, before leaving the campsite, we will catch a glimpse of the stunning sunrise view over Annapurna and enjoy the delicious breakfast. Shortly after that, we will retrace our steps back to Bamboo, following the previous trail. Walking on our way to the village, we will pass Machhapuchhre Base Camp, Hinko Cave, Himalayan Hotel Dobhan, and Bamboo. It takes us around 7 hours to descend the trail to Bamboo. Overnight in a guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bamboo to Jhinu Danda Hot Spring.
itinerary.html: Start the day early with a gentle descent through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests. Pass through small settlements like Sinuwa and Chhomrong, enjoying panoramic views of Annapurna South and Machapuchare. Descend the long stone staircases down to the Chhomrong Khola and then climb up to Chhomrong village for lunch or a short break. After lunch, make your final descent to Jhinu Danda.   In Jhinu Daaaanda, natural hot springs are located on the banks of the Modi Khola, a 20-minute walk away, ideal for relaxation.

itinerary.title: Trek from Jhinu Danda – Forest Camp (2,600 m)
itinerary.html: Aafter breakfast, trek toward Forest Camp. From this day onward, you follow the Mardi Himal route. The trail leads through rhododendron forests.

itinerary.title: Trek from Forest Camp – High Camp (3600 m)
itinerary.html:
Continuous ascent through rhododendron and oak forests. Beautiful views open up of Annapurna South (7,219 m), Hiunchuli (6,441 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), and Mardi Himal (5,553 m). 

There are no settlements along this quiet forest stretch leading to High Camp. 

Overnight in High Camp.

itinerary.title: High Camp – Mardi Himal Base Camp / Upper View Point (4200 m) – Low Camp or Sidding (1800 m)
itinerary.html:
After breakfast, ascend through forested paths to the Upper View Point (4,200 m). 

From here, enjoy stunning views of Mardi Himal (5,553 m), Annapurna I (8,091 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), and other peaks. 

Return to High Camp, then continue the long trek down to Sidding. 

Overnight in a guest house.

itinerary.html:
After an early breakfast, depart via private jeep for Pokhara. Afternoon sightseeing in Pokhara. 
Overnight in a hotel in Pokhara.

overview:
Annapurna Circuit Trek Introduction

Annapurna circuit trek provides a chance to explore the local culture, natural land, and breath-taking scenery of the Himalayas. In particular, the classic Annapurna circuit trek is one of the three major trekking routes in the Annapurna region. Likewise, it is a highly admired and remarkable trekking route in the Annapurna region. Moreover, this glorious trek leads you to the villages inhabited by a widely diverse people from different ethnic groups. The picturesque villages sit alongside the white Himalayas offering spectacular and majestic views.

Annapurna circuit Trek fulfills your adventure desire to be in the bosom of high Himalayan ranges. Firstly, this 18 days trek starts from Bhulbhule. Then it goes along the Marshyangdi River, terraced fields, and small Hindu villages.

This route greets us with scenic views of Himal Chuli and Manaslu to the east. As you climb through the trail, you will reach a high desert country- Manang (3,597 m). The scenery from Manang is equally breath-taking with distinct medieval feel to it. Finally, continuing through the dry aired landscape of Manang leads you to Thorang-La Pass. In fact, this is the highest point of the Annapurna Circuit Trek. Thorang La pass is at the top of the valley at 5,416 m

This is a challenging ascent but the trails reward you with the view of some magnificent mountains. Ultimately, you go downhill to Muktinath in the lower Mustang region. Muktinath is one of the most divine pilgrimage sites for Buddhist and Hindu people. Continuing the descent leads you to Tatopani– natural hot springs. Tatopani is a great place to soak, soothe and refresh your tired muscles. Rejuvenate yourself for more adventurous days to come.

The final section of the trek includes climbing up to Poon Hill via Ghorepani. It is popularly known as “Photographer’s Paradise”. Poon Hill lets you capture some of the best snaps of impressive Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. From Poon hill, you head to Nayapul. From there a vehicle will transport you to the beautiful lakeside town of Pokhara and then to Kathmandu.

Be a part of this remarkable trip with us. We have magnificent crew members. Their care and experience would definitely make your trip one of the most memorable and rewarding.

Annapurna Circuit Trek Altitude Chart

itinerary.title: Arrive at Tribhuwan International Airport, Kathmandu and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, our representative will pick you up and escort you to the hotel. Overnight at hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Bhulbhule (840 m / 2,756 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: We begin our journey by driving along the highway to Dumre.  Following the winding road to Besisahar, we get a view of amazing mountain peaks and picturesque villages as we drive. After 7 hours’ drive and mesmerizing view of Marsayangdi River, we reach Bhulbhule. Overnight at a guest house.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bhulbhule to Chyamche (1,430 m / 4,692 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail today first climbs steeply on a cliff-face above the riverbed and then descends to the stone village of Jagat and into the mesmerizing Marsayangdi valley. We then trek through a winding trail through the forested path to reach Chamje. A stunning view of Lamjung Himal (6,983 m) awaits us in Chyamche. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chamje to Bagarchhap (2,160 m / 7,087 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Ascending from Chamje, we pass through stunning terraced fields and walk uphill through rhododendron forests. Crossing several suspension bridges over Marsayangdi River, we climb steeply on curving trails to reach the confluence of Marsayangdi River and Dudh Khola at Bagarchhap. Here, you can get an unobstructed view of the magnificent Annapurna II (7,937 m) and Lamjung Himal (6,983 m). Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bagarchhap to Chame (2,670 m / 8,760 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: We continue to climb through pine and oak forests as we pass through Danakyu on our way to the village of Timang, which lies at the bottom of Lamjung Himal (6,983 m). We then walk through the flat trail alongside Marsayangdi River past the villages of Thanchowk and Koto to reach Chame. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chame to Pisang (3,200 m / 10,499 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Crossing a bridge over Marsayangdi River, we continue walking through the pine forest towards Bhratang. We ascend uphill to Dhikur Pokhari and walk ahead to Pisang enjoying the view of the Annapurna massif on one side and Pisang Peak (6,091 m) on the other side. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pisang to Manang (3,540 m / 11,614 ft) via Ngawal, 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: We leave Pisang and walk towards Braga village where we visit the 900 years old monastery. Then, continuing to walk towards Manang, we cross a bridge over Marsayangdi River and climb uphill through pine forest to Ghyaru. We climb uphill to Ngawal and downhill to Mungji to meet the lower route to Manang. Overnight at a guest house.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day in Manang (3,540 m / 11,614 ft).
itinerary.html: Today, we spend the day exploring the outskirts of Manang. We hike up to the beautiful Gangapurna Lake from where an amazing panorama of Marsayangdi River valley, the Annapurna range, Gangapurna (7,454 m), and Tilicho Peak (7,134 m) can be seen. We also visit the ancient monasteries and the old village of Tengi while in Manang. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Manang to Ledar (4,250 m / 13,944 ft), 4-5 hours
itinerary.html: Climb uphill to Tengi and continue to walk towards Ghunsang with stunning views of the Annapurna range and Gangapurna (7,454 m). The walk continues to Yak Kharka where we can see wide meadows with grazing blue sheep and yaks. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ledarto to Thorung Phedi (4,450 m / 14,600 ft) and to High Camp (4,925 m / 16,158 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Climb uphill and cross a stream. Ascend uphill to a tea shop and walk to Thorung Phedi. This is one of the difficult days of the trek as we walk along steep graveled trails to reach Thorung Phedi. Later, we climb to High Camp where we get to see the 360-degree view of the mountains. The view is surreal at such high altitude. Descend back to Thorung Phedi. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from High camp to Thorung La (5,416 m / 17,769 ft) to Muktinath (3,800 m / 12,467 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Ascend to high camp and climb to Thorung La (5,416 m), the highest pass in Nepal, to get a view of the amazing Kali Gandaki valley and the surrounding mountain peaks like the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri massifs. Walking through the moraines, we climb steeply downhill to reach the holy temple of Muktinath. Muktinath is a popular Shiva Temple with 108 holy water taps. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Muktinath to Marpha (2,670 m / 8,760 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: We visit Muktinath Temple in the morning and offer our prayers to the God of Salvation. Later, we climb down to Jharkot and descend to Khingar. We follow the trails of Thorong Khola and walk to reach the beautiful village of Kagbeni. We walk downhill through the apple orchards and then continue walking on the riverbed of Kali Gandaki River to reach the windy town of Jomsom. The trek continues until we reach the apple capital of Nepal, Marpha. This village is famous for its apple garden, apple brandy, and the local Thakali people. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Marpha to Kalopani (2,460 m / 8,071 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Continue to walk on the riverbed of Kali Gandaki River and pass the villages of Tukuche and Larjung. Relishing the view of the Dhaulagiri massif, descend through the riverbed and cross several suspension bridges to finally reach Kalopani. In Kalopani, we visit the Cultural Thakali Museum and relish the view of Dhaulagiri massif and Annapurna massif that surround the small village from two sides. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kalopani to Tatopani (1,190 m / 3,904 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Descend to Ghasa passing a Mani wall and walk to the beautiful waterfall called Rupse Chhahara. We then climb down to Dana village where we will find another waterfall. Then, crossing several suspension bridges over Kali Gandaki River, we reach Tatopani. You can take a dip in the natural hot spring in Tatopani to relax your aching muscles. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tatopani to Ghorepani (2,870 m / 9,416 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Ascend to the Shikha village via Ghara village. Here, we get astonished by the view of Annapurna South (7,219 m) and Machhapuchhre (6,993 m). Walking on stone steps through the rhododendron forest while enjoying the continuous view of snow-capped mountains, we arrive in Ghorepani. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ghorepani to Banthanti, followed by a jeep drive to Pokhara (820 m / 2,690 ft), 7–8 hours.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, begin your final day of trekking from Ghorepani and descend through beautiful rhododendron forests toward Banthanti. Enjoy the peaceful surroundings and scenic views of the hills and mountains along the trail. From Banthanti, we will find a sharing jeep  to Pokhara, passing through picturesque villages and countryside. Upon arrival in Pokhara, check into your hotel and relax after the trek.

itinerary.title: Drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu by tourist bus, 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: We leave Pokhara behind and return back to Kathmandu via a tourist bus. Enjoy the landscape and the countryside view throughout the drive. Upon arrival in Kathmandu, you will be dropped at your hotel.

itinerary.title: Transfer to airport for your onward destination.
itinerary.html: Our representative will drop you at the airport 3 hours prior to the flight time.

sections.title: More information
sections.html: Q: I’ve never trekked before.  Can I do this trek? Answer: As long as you are reasonably fit, mentally prepared and can walk for 6-7-hours a day then no matter who you are and what your background is, a bit of training may be necessary, but even that is not 100% essential for most. Q: How many miles do you walk each day? Answer: In average you walk around 4-7 miles per day while going up and 8-12 miles while coming down. Q: Is there battery charging facility? Answer: The tea houses have charging facilities with both electricity and via their solar panels but both of them are uncertain thus it is better to have an extra battery. If there is electricity only from solar panels then the tea houses usually charge for it – maybe a 100-200 rupees per hour but if it from regular electricity then it is free of cost. Q: Can I do laundry on the trek? Answer: Yes, you can. You can take this service with guest house. This will not be by machine, it will be by hand. Or, you can do your own laundry in a bucket. Q: Is there bottled water on the Annapurna Circuit Trek? Answer: Yes, there is bottled water from Bishisahar  to all the way to Nayapul. But, the price goes up the higher you go. One liter bottle of water cost start around 50 rupees and at base camp cost well over 200 (around $2). A budget solution to this is to use water treatment solution or use water purifier tablets. Some purification tabs and drops make the water taste weird. Please be aware of that too. In majority villages there is safe drinking water station where they sell safe drinking water in cheaper cost. If you are thinking of buying boiled water then make sure if water was fully boiled or not. Q: Is there age limit for Annapurna Circuit Trek? Answer: There isn’t any official age limit saying you can and cannot trek to Annapurna Circuit Trek . Q: How difficult is the Annapurna Circuit Trek? Answer: In terms of terrain there are no ropes needed and no ice picks needed. There is no vertical climbing involved. The ground is not paved. It is rough, rocky and gravel strewn. Most of the trek involves long paths that go up and then down. People with weak ankles should take caution. Depending on the time of year you go there can also be snow and ice in the trails. Q: Can children go to the Annapurna Circuit trek? Answer: Yes in the general rule. It’s advisable that your child is reasonable and able to understand and follow instructions immediately. Your child should be mature enough to recognize altitude sickness symptoms.
