faqs.q: How Long does the Annapurna Circuit Trek Take?
faqs.a:
Annapurna Circuit Trek generally takes between 14 and 18 days based on the itinerary that you choose, your walking speed and the number of acclimatization days. Some travelers prefer short routes on the same trail while others choose to do it leisurely in order to fully explore all scenic landscapes and enjoy an enriching cultural experience along the way.

At Base Camp Adventure, we have designed an 18-day Annapurna Circuit Trek itinerary including all scenic highlights of the region.

faqs.q: What is the Highest Point of Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a: Thorong La Pass is the highest point of the Annapurna Circuit Trek. It is situated at 5,416 m. This pass offers panoramic views of Himalayan vistas. It also rewards trekkers with a thrilling experience which makes it one of the notable highlights of the trek.

faqs.q: What is the Average Time Needed to Cross Thorong La Pass?
faqs.a:
Usually it takes about 7 to 10 hours to cross Thorong La Pass. The exact time depends on your speed, weather and the start point. Trekkers usually start very early in the morning to make it to the top of the pass before the afternoons come with stronger winds.

The walking time also varies depending on whether you begin from Thorong Phedi or High Camp. If you start from High Camp, then it offers a shorter but steeper approach.

faqs.q: What Makes the Annapurna Circuit Trek Unique?
faqs.a:
The Annapurna Circuit Trek is unique. It takes you through varying terrains ranging from green valleys and forests to arid Himalayan terrain.

The trek offers spectacular mountain views, enriching cultural experiences, excellent hospitality and a thrilling experience by letting you navigate the high altitude areas and enchanting Thorong La Pass.

faqs.q: What is Maximum Duration of Stay Allowed on Nepal Tourist Visa?
faqs.a: Nepal tourist visas are available in various durations such as 15, 30 and 90 days. Most tourists prefer to take 30 day visa. It provides enough time for the Annapurna Circuit Trek preparation and additional travel time to other parts of the country.

faqs.q: Can I Get a Nepal Visa On Arrival?
faqs.a:
Yes. Most of the foreign nationals can get visa on arrival. They can get the visa at the Kathmandu Airport or designated land borders. For Nepal tourist visa you will need valid passport. In addition, the completed visa application form, recent passport size photo and applicable visa fee are also required.

However, people from some nationalities might need to apply for visa in advance at the Nepalese consulate/embassy of their country before visiting Nepal. So we suggest you check visa requirements for your country before travelling.

faqs.q: How Can I Reach the Starting Point of Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a: The start point of the Annapurna Circuit trek depends on the chosen itinerary. However, the most popular trailheads that are selected by many trekkers are Bhulbhule, Besisahar or Dharapani.

faqs.q: How Difficult Is the Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
Annapurna Circuit Trek is moderate to challenging in terms of difficulty as it combines long trekking days, steep uphill and downhill terrain and uneven terrain and takes you to high altitudes. 

Crossing Thorong La Pass (5,416 m) is one of the challenging parts of the trek. However, with good preparations, acclimatization and willpower, most fit trekkers can complete it smoothly.

faqs.q: Can Beginners Join the Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes, beginners can join the Annapurna Circuit Trek smoothly. The trek is moderate to challenging. However, the trails are well-maintained. Also, trekkers will get to stay at comfortable teahouse accommodation after a long day of trekking. Furthermore, technical skills are also not required. 

However, beginners who wish to undertake this trek must be well prepared and physically fit. In addition, they should choose a well organized and gradual itinerary that includes acclimatization days. The training before the trek and daily walking consistently help first time trekkers complete the trek safely.

faqs.q: What are the Biggest Challenges Trekkers Face on the Annapurna Circuit?
faqs.a:
The major challenges that the trekkers have to overcome on Annapurna Circuit include high altitudes, long days of walking, unpredictable mountain weather and crossing the Thorong La Pass which is at an elevation of 5,416 m

Acclimatization, physical fitness and proper preparation will allow you to overcome the challenges letting you enjoy a safe and rewarding trekking experience.

faqs.q: Is Guide's Support Required for Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes. We highly recommend that you trek with licensed guide. With their assistance, you can navigate the remote and difficult passes such as Thorong La Pass. In addition, guides are familiar with the trail conditions and will teach you how to cross the tricky spots safely. 

Furthermore, they will check your health, help you adapt and even arrange evacuation when needed. When you opt for a guided journey, you can ensure a secure journey in the Annapurna region.

faqs.q: What Weather Conditions Can Make the Annapurna Circuit Trek More Difficult?
faqs.a:
Extreme mountain weather including heavy snowand rainfall can make trekking more difficult. Heavy snow can block the trekking paths and the rain can make the path slippery and muddy.

Strong winds and poor visibility can also affect the trekking trails. So you should check weather forecasts and trail conditions before heading out. This ensures an enjoyable experience on trails.

faqs.q: When Is Best Time for Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) are best times for Annapurna Circuit Trek. These ideal seasons offer favorable weather, moderate temperatures and clear views of Himalayas.

The spring season features beautiful rhododendrons. Autumn rewards clear blue skies after monsoon season ends enhancing the overall experience.

faqs.q: Which Month Offers Clear Mountain Views?
faqs.a:
Autumn months, especially October and November, are known for offering the clearest mountain views. This is the post-monsoon season. So, after the monsoon season, you can see the fantastic mountain ranges like Annapurna, Dhaulagiri and nearby snowy peaks. 

Spring also offers stunning Himalayan scenery under clear skies with the added charm of blooming flora on hill sides and in forested areas.

faqs.q: What Are the Conditions of Annapurna Circuit in Winter?
faqs.a:
The winter season (December and February) brings low temperatures and chilly weather, especially at high altitude areas. Sometimes some sections of the route may also be covered with snow. 

However, this season sees lower crowds and offers the clearest mountain scenery. So, special preparations are required for trekking safely.

faqs.q: How Are the Trail Conditions in Monsoon?
faqs.a:
The rains in monsoon season can make trails muddy and slippery. So, it can be more difficult to navigate. Sometimes landslides may also occur and can affect certain sections, especially at the lower elevations. Also in lower forested sections, leeches may be present adding to the discomfort.

Visibility can also be affected because of heavy rains and cloud cover. So, finding the right way can be challenging. That's why only experienced trekkers undertake the journey with this season with experienced guides.

faqs.q: Can Rhododendrons Be Seen on Trail During Spring?
faqs.a:
Yes. You can. Spring is the time when the forests and hillsides are covered with different colorful wildflowers, including the rhododendrons. So, if you choose to trek in any of the spring months, then you can see blooming flora and wildflowers along the route. 

The enchanting flowers and beautiful snowy mountains in the background look ethereal. The blooming rhododendrons are one of the major attractions of the spring season that draws the attention of several trekkers.

faqs.q: How Can I Prepare Physically for the Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
For the Annapurna Circuit trek, you may train atleast 3 to 4 months in advance doing cardio exercise, strength training, and hiking. You may do cardio exercises like cycling, jogging, swimming, and stair climbing to build endurance. Likewise, you may also do strength training like squats, deadlifts, step-ups, lunges, planks, and calf raises. 

Hiking to nearby high altitude areas can also help you get familiar with the challenges that you can probably face while trekking.

faqs.q: What Documents Should I Bring for the Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
For Annapurna Circuit Trek you will need valid passport, Nepal Tourist Visa, 2 to 4 copies of passport size photographs, your passport and its photocopy, trekking permits and travel insurance. If you book this trek with us, we will obtain the trekking permits for you.

If you book this trek with us, we will obtain the trekking permits for you.

faqs.q: Do I Need Travel Insurance for the Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes. Comprehensive travel insurance is needed while trekking in Nepal. The trekking journey is indeed rewarding. But there are certain risks involved, like altitude sickness, accidents and trip interruption due to bad weather.

So, for financial protection against such risks it is highly recommended to get travel insurance that covers high altitude trekking.

faqs.q: Do I Need to Have Travel Insurance Before Joining the Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
The travel insurance for the Annapurna Circuit trek should cover the possible risks that can arise during high-altitude trekking, medical bills, emergency helicopter evacuation, trip interruption and loss of baggage. 

Before buying the insurance, we recommend you check the inclusions so that you can be assured that you are financially protected against the risk that might arise during the adventure.

faqs.q: Can I Trek the Annapurna Circuit Without Permits?
faqs.a: No, you cannot legally trek the Annapurna Circuit without permits. There are checkpoints on the way. Not having the permits can result in fines or entry can be denied. So, you must have permits before trekking.

faqs.q: Which Permit is Required for the Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a: During the Annapurna Circuit trek, you will traverse through the protected area. So, to enter this conserved region you will need to have an Annapurna Conservation Area Permit.

faqs.q: Will the Permit Be Checked Along the Route?
faqs.a: Yes. The permit will be checked at different checkpoints along the route. If you book the trekking package with us, then we will get the required permit on your behalf. Furthermore, our guide will help get it verified along the trail.

faqs.q: Where Do Trekkers Stay During Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a: Trekkers generally stay in the local teahouses and lodges on the Annapurna Circuit trek route. The teahouses provide simple facilities, like a cozy room with twin beds and a common dining area. Most places offer simple facilities at high-altitude villages, whereas low altitude villages offer relatively better accommodation facilities.

faqs.q: Are Rooms Available With Private Bathrooms?
faqs.a: Yes. There are private bathroom facilities in some teahouses in lower-altitude and popular villages on the trekking route. But at high-altitude remote sections, most of the teahouse facilities offer shared bathrooms. The availability mainly depends upon the location and teahouse.

faqs.q: What Types of Food Can I Expect During Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
There are several food items that you can get at the teahouses on the Annapurna Circuit Trek route. Some popular items include dal bhat, veggie soups, Tibetan Bread, noodles, pasta, rice, pancakes, eggs and different kinds of vegetables. 

The food varieties may be limited at higher altitudes. However, at every stop you will be served with delicious and warm meals.

faqs.q: Can I Get Vegetarian and Vegan Food On the Trail?
faqs.a:
Yes. Vegetarian food options available. Teahouses usually serve vegetarian dishes like dal bhat, vegetable curry, noodles, soups, potatoes, rice and pasta.

Vegan dishes are also easily available. In fact, many dishes served at the teahouses are already vegan friendly. Still we suggest you inform us beforehand if you are vegan so that we can make arrangements accordingly.

faqs.q: Is Safe Drinking Water Available During the Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes, safe drinking water is available if you follow the proper purification process. You can get bottled water at the teahouses. However, it can get costly with rising elevations because of the transportation issues. That's why the most recommended method is to buy boiled water from a teahouse. 

You may bring a reusable water bottle and fill it at different points along the trail. Likewise, another preferred method of purifying the water is by using water purification tablets or UV filters.

faqs.q: Is Wi fi Available on the Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a: Yes, Wi-Fi is available at several teahouses on the route. However, at high-altitude remote sections it may be weak and limited. For Wi Fi, most of the teahouses charge extra. You may also choose to buy a local SIM card and buy a data package for relatively better coverage in the mountain villages.

faqs.q: Can I Get to Charge My Phone and Other Electronics During the Trek?
faqs.a: Yes, you can charge phones and other electronic devices at almost all teahouses on the Annapurna Circuit Trek. However, for this facility you have to pay a small additional cost, especially at upper sections as electricity supply is limited.

faqs.q: Can I Rent Essential Trekking Gear Instead of Buying It in Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Yes. You can. You can get gear for rent at several stores in Thamel area of Kathmandu at an affordable price. However, make sure to check its quality before buying it.

faqs.q: What Kind of Clothing is Required for the Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a: For the Annapurna Circuit trek, you need layered clothing so that you can add and remove it as per the requirement. You can bring moisture wicking base layers, warm mid layers and waterproof outer layers and adjust it according to the weather. In addition, you also need rain gears, gloves, socks, scarf and warm hat, especially for the cold nights.

faqs.q: Do I Need a Sleeping Bag for the Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes. Carrying warm sleeping bag for Annapurna Circuit trek is highly recommended. With warm sleeping bag, you can ensure a comfortable journey.

Even though teahouses provide blankets they might not be able to provide enough warmth on colder nights while trekking at high altitudes. So by carrying a sleeping bag you can stay warm and be prepared for the next day’s journey.

faqs.q: Is a Personal Medical Kit Required?
faqs.a: Yes. Having a personal medical kit while trekking Annapurna Circuit is a smart choice. Although the guide will bring a common first aid kit for everyone your personal kit will definitely be useful in unexpected emergencies that may arise while trekking.

faqs.q: Should I Carry Snacks for Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a: It is a wise decision to bring snacks to get refueled between meals. You may bring snacks that are light but nutrient-rich. Some examples are energy bars, nuts, dried fruits, chocolate or trail mix. Though snacks are available in the teahouses on the route, the price may increase with the altitude.

faqs.q: Is The Annapurna Circuit Trek Safe?
faqs.a:
The Annapurna Circuit Trek is generally considered safe. Well prepared trekkers who follow right itinerary and ensure proper acclimatization can complete the trek safely.

There are well established teahouses along the path where you can get rest after long day on the trail. Also, if any kind of emergency arises, the guides will be there to help you. Good preparation before the trek will help you avoid the common risks.

faqs.q: What Are The Symptoms Of Altitude Sickness?
faqs.a:
One major concerning factor of the Annapurna Circuit trek is altitude sickness. Some common symptoms include:

  • Headache
  • Nausea 
  • Fatigue
  • Dizziness
  • No appetite
  • Difficulty Sleeping
  • Breathlessness

faqs.q: How to Prevent Altitude Sickness?
faqs.a:
To avoid the likelihood of altitude sickness, you need to trek gradually, adhere to your acclimatization plan, drink enough water, have well balanced meals and avoid alcoholic drinks.

Make sure to walk at an easy pace, and be attentive to how you feel at the high altitude. If you start developing symptoms which doesn't get better or turn worse, then head to a lower elevation immediately.

faqs.q: Do I Need Medicine For Altitude Sickness?
faqs.a: Yes. You may take medicine such as Diamox. But consult your doctor prior to traveling. It can help prevent altitude sickness. However, proper acclimatization still should be your main focus. Descending is the most efficient and safe thing to do in case you suffer from severe symptoms.

faqs.q: Is Emergency Evacuation Available?
faqs.a:
Yes. Helicopter evacuation can be arranged during emergencies. The evacuation will be handled by your guide by coordinating with us, the local and the rescue team.

As evacuation can be very costly without insurance, make sure that you have travel insurance wich covers for high altitude trekking and helicopter evacuation.

faqs.q: How Much Does the Annapurna Circuit Trek Cost?
faqs.a: Annapurna Circuit Trek cost starts from US$ 1350. This 18 day trek package is designed by including all necessary services and stops in the popular villages that are major highlights of the adventure.

faqs.q: What Is Included in a Trekking Package?
faqs.a:
Our Annapurna Circuit Trek package covers everything you need for smooth journey on the Annapurna trails. It offers services such as airport pickup, hotel accommodations in Kathmandu and Pokhara including breakfasts, and tea house accommodation during your trek. Full board meals during the are also provided.

In addition, you will be accompanied by an English speaking guide and strong porters for the trek. The package also includes permits, trekking crew insurance, ground transportation and first aid kit.

faqs.q: Is It Possible to Get Customized Itinerary for Annapurna Circuit Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes. It is. You can. It can be designed depending on your preferences, available time, fitness levels and kind of journey you have envisioned.

We can modify trekking duration. Likewise, daily hiking hours, number of rest days, accommodation options can also be adjusted that suits the individual requirements. Whether you want or a slow paced journey or short itinerary, we are here to help you design an itinerary accordingly.

Booking Annapurna Circuit Trek with Base Camp Adventure is a simple process. You can visit our website, visit the package page and click "Book This Trip" option. Then you can select the departure date, number of people traveling, fill out the booking form and pay 30% deposit of total trip cost.

For more information, please contact us on 977-1-4517875 (landline) or +977 9851029616 (whatsapp/ viber) or send an email to info@basecampadventure.com.

faqs.q: How Much Money Should I Carry During the Trek?
faqs.a:
You will need cash to cover for the personal expenses during the trek. Reliable ATMs are not available in remote mountain areas. Also, in such areas, teahouses and local stores mainly prefer cash. So, you need to withdraw cash from the city area. 

You can bring around US$ 250 to US$ 350 (converted into Nepali rupees) to cover personal expenses such as snacks, beverages, charging electronics, internet connection, hot shower, and souvenirs.

faqs.q: Is Tipping Expected?
faqs.a: Yes. Tipping is expected. It is a good way of appreciating your guides and porters. They put lot of effort and dedication throughout the trek. Though tipping is not mandatory it is a good way to acknowledge the service you received. You may tip the amount you prefer. Usually, trekkers tip around 10% to 15 % of the total package cost.

reviews.author: Robbie-s, Sydney, Australia
reviews.body: A friend and I did a two week trek around the Annapurna Circuit with Shiva. He was great company to hike with and very flexible with the specifics of our trip. He took excellent care of me when I got sick from the water (the expensive bottled water at the top of the mountain is worth it) and his well-stocked medical kit came in handy when altitude sickness inevitably kicked in. Even though he is half my size, he can eat twice as much dal bhat as me - I guess this is why he is such a strong trekker. All the other travelers we met that didn't have a guide all gravitated towards Shiva for his guidance and excellent knowledge of the area. I would strongly recommend Shiva as a friendly, reliable guide.

reviews.author: AdelaideG2013-London, England, United Kingdom
reviews.body: Outstanding. I would highly recommend Base Camp Adventures for single women, a couple of people to a group. I was blown away with the service Shree provided, he is fluent in English, honest, very professional and flexible. His priority is to ensure you have a once in a life time experience and I certainly did! A friend and I wanted to do the Annapurna Circuit and we visited numerous companies in Khatmandu, but were dissatisfied with them all. However we then found Shree at Base Camp Adventures, recommend to us by another group of travellers having done Everest BC with them. Instantly we liked him and after a lovely long chat (these can sometimes go on for hours, but are always interesting and funny!) we decided to go with his company. We wanted to leave the next day and this was absolutely fine - much to our surprise! Everything that Shree said would happen, happened and it was an incredible trip. We weren’t sure about a guide, but after talking with Shree we decided to hire one - Jwala. Jwala made our trip, he was our guide as well as a friend and I am very happy that we took him with us. He is very kind, professional, thoughtful, incredibly knowledgable about Nepal and high altitude treks (having a great extent of experience himself) and most importantly, I always felt safe. Jwala also took us off the beaten trek when possible and helped us experience a truly unique Nepal. When I was unwell in Langtang he looked after me as a dear friend, always making sure I was warm, comfortable and eating/drinking enough - once I recovered, I made it to the top of the mountain, which I could not have done without him! I was hesitant being a solo female traveller and hiring a guide on my own, but with Jwala I knew I was in good hands! Having completed with Jwala and a friend the Annaourna Circuit, I decided to take him with me to the Langtang Valley. It was the best decision I made, as I had a fantastic time with him! We were able to go into the locals homes and he managed to have the Glacier research hut opened for me! Shree also organised for my friend and I to go to Chitwan, which was a great trip too! I have Shree, Jwala and Base Camp Adventues to thank for such a wonderful time in Nepal. I hope to go back in the near future to visit Nepal and will be going with Base Camp Adventures (who I have recommended to so many people already!)

reviews.author: Jayde T
reviews.body: My partner and I had arrived in Nepal and wanted to organize a trekking trip from Kathmandu. We went to Base Camp adventure and organized a trip to Poon Hill, a popular destination along the Annapurna Mountain circuit, and Base Camp Adventures were so awesome and accommodating every step of the journey. They arranged our bus to Pokhara (And from Pokhara), where we stayed for a few days before leaving to begin our trek, where our guide Jwala met us and we drove to the beginning of the Annapurna circuit and set off on our trek. What followed were 5 days of pure bliss, around every corner of the trek were breathtaking views, magnificent and ever changing fauna and terrain, walking in peace among chirping birds and taking in all the surroundings, this trek opened my eyes up to an amazing piece of the world. The accommodation and food was covered with in our package and to the highest standard where we could choose whatever we liked to eat on the menu. Our journey smooth and seamless as we ventured from Ulleri to Ghorepani to Ghandruk etc, we were always comfortable at nights, felt safe, and had great conversations and many hours of playing cards were spent with Jwala our amazing guide who has a big heart and gave us a unique perspective of Nepal, sharing his knowledge and wisdom with us as a experience trekking guide. My only wish is that I could have stayed longer, it was truly an amazing trip of a lifetime. Nepal and Base Camp Adventure, I will be back and look forward to seeing you both again. Thankyou so much. 10/10 !!!!

title: Annapurna Panorama Trek
summary: Annapurna Panorama Trek is a classic trek offering stunning views of the Annapurna range, scenic mountain landscapes, and charming local villages.

seo.title: Annapurna Panorama Trek | Route | Cost | Review | 2026 & 2027
seo.description: Annapurna Panorama Trek is a classic trek offering stunning views of the Annapurna range, scenic mountain landscapes, and charming local villages.

overview:
Annapurna Panorama Trek is a short trek on the foothills of Annapurna massif that provides you with unlimited views of wonderful sceneries and the heart-pounding vista of snow-capped mountains. This trek also gives you an opportunity to explore beautiful villages and look into the lifestyle and culture of the Gurung community.

Your journey begins with a drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara. The drive will present you beautiful views of villages, hills, rivers, and you also get to have a glimpse of the lifestyle of the locals. After reaching Pokhara, you drive to Nayapul from where your trek begins. You will pass through scenic landscapes, small villages, and rhododendron forests as you ascend and descend on flag-stone steps. A quick hike from Ghorepani will take you to Poon Hill which is rightfully famous for its stunning sunrise view.

The highest point of the trek is Poon Hill (3,210 m), features a mind-blowing sunrise view over the high Himalayas, making this trek a must for all nature lovers.From Poon Hill, you can also witness stunning views of snow-capped mountains like Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna III (7,555 m), Annapurna IV (7,525 m), Annapurna South (7,219 m), Dhaulagiri (8,167 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), Himchuli (6,441 m) and many others.

You will then descend to Tadapani for the overnight stay. The next day we trek through Ghandruk Village, which is a picturesque typical Gurung village with its own lifestyle, culture, and customs. You will get to interact with the Gurung people on this journey and know about their life. The trek will also take you to the Gurung village of Landruk before heading down to Dhampus via Pothana. Throughout this Annapurna Panorama Trek, you will find yourself in the calming environment where you can relax with the wonderful scenery and chirping of birds.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Tribhuwan International Airport (TIA), Kathmandu and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA). Our representatives will be at the airport to pick you up, and you will directly be taken to your hotel. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara, 6-7 hours
itinerary.html: Today you will drive to Pokhara, situated 200 km west of Kathmandu. The drive will present you radiant views of Trishuli River followed by the upstream junction of Marsayangdi River. You will see beautiful terraced fields, small hill towns, and also get a chance to have a glimpse on the life of locals. Pokhara is a picturesque valley with lakes, monasteries, temples, caves along with a stunning view of Machhapuchhre (6,993 m) and Annapurna Range.

itinerary.title: Drive for approximately one hour from Pokhara to Nayapul, followed by a scenic trek to Ulleri (1,920 m / 6,299 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will take a short drive from Pokhara to Nayapul. After reaching Nayapul, your trek will begin. The trail will go through various beautiful small villages and settlements. You will walk through the lush forest on carefully placed flag-stone steps while relishing the view of beautiful landscapes. You will reach Ulleri. Overnight in Ulleri.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ulleri to Ghorepani (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Your trek begins with an hour ascend on the steep path to Banthanti. This village is specially resided by Magar people, and you will also get to see their lifestyle, tradition, and culture. The trail will also present you gorgeous views of Hiunchuli (6,441 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), and Annapurna South (7,219 m). From these villages, your trail becomes easy, and you will pass through rhododendron forests to reach the Magar village of Ghorepani. Overnight in Ghorepani.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ghorepani to Poon Hill (3,210 m / 10,531 ft) for sunrise views, then return to Ghorepani and continue trekking to Tadapani (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 6–7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will begin your day early morning trip to Poon Hill View Point to enjoy the most beautiful sunrise along with stunning views of snow-capped mountains like Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna South (7,219 m), Annapurna III (7,555 m), Dhaulagiri (8167), Nilgiri (7,061 m), Varaha Shikhar (7,847 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), Tukuche Peak (6,920 m), Lamjung Himal (6,983 m), and several other mountains. After having some good time, you will trek back to Ghorepani. From here, you will trek to Tadapani passing through dense forests of oak, rhododendron, and bamboo. Tadapani is a beautiful small village with gorgeous views of Hiunchuli (6,441 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), Annapurna South (7,219 m), and Annapurna I (8,091 m). Overnight in Tadapani.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tadapani to Jhinu Danda / Hot Spring (1,950 m / 6,398 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: We first descend through an amusing forest to Gurjung Khola, then up and again descend to Jhinu Danda and enjoy a warm dip in the natural hot spring to let our sore muscles relax. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Jhinu Danda to Pothana (1,990 m / 6,529 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: You will begin your trek by descending on a steep path following a stone staircase and ascends to reach the Gurung village of Landruk. From here, you will ascend amid the rich forests of rhododendron and oak forest on your way to Pitam Deurali (2,142 m). From Pitam Deurali, you will descend to the village of Pothana for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pothana to Australian Camp and Kande, followed by a drive to Pokhara 820 m / 2,690 ft), 3–4 hours.
itinerary.html: After having a delicious breakfast, you will begin your trek. You will trek downhill along with gorgeous views of tall mountains and Australian Camp and the turn right to go to Kada to catch a taxi to Pokhara. From here, you will take a short drive to Pokhara. After reaching Pokhara, you will rest, and in the late afternoon, you will visit the Lakeside area to do boating in Phewa Lake. Overnight at a hotel in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu, 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today, you will drive back to Kathmandu, (you can also choose to take a flight). Both of these options offer you a beautiful view of the hills and the mountains. After reaching Kathmandu, you will be escorted to your hotel. You can take rest all day or can also explore nearby places.

itinerary.title: Transfer to international Airport.
itinerary.html: Depending on your flight schedule, transfer to the airport for your onward flight back home.

title: Arun Valley Trekking
summary: Arun Valley lies between two highest mountains, Everest and Makalu. This beautiful trek takes you to Salpa Bhanjyang, highest point of Arun Valley.

seo.title: Arun Valley Trekking | Itinerary, Guide, Cost and Map
seo.description: Arun Valley lies between two highest mountains, Everest and Makalu. This beautiful trek takes you to Salpa Bhanjyang, highest point of Arun Valley.

overview:
Arun Valley Trek route is situated in the Makalu region, Arun Valley is blessed with the vast diversity of natural wonders and indigenous culture. This valley lies between the world's highest mountain, Mt. Everest (8,848 m), and the fifth highest mountain, Makalu (8,463 m), and boasts of an abundance of nature. Due to the presence of these mighty Himalayas, the quiet trails through the Rai and Sherpa settlements of Arun Valley Trek become more gorgeous and heartwarming.

The Arun Valley Trek starts with your flight from Kathmandu to Tumlingtar, the starting point of the trek. The trek features traversing through deep forests with mixed vegetation leading to the beautiful Rai and Sherpa villages in the Arun Valley. One of the main highlights of this trek is the holy pond named Salpa Pokhari, which holds fair during the month of October for Hindu pilgrims from all over the world.

Another highlight of the trek is the view of Chamlang (7,321 m) and Makalu (8,463 m) seen from the top of Salpa Bhanjyang. The trek takes you to Makalu Barun Conservation Area and leads you alongside Hinku valley to reach Sagarmatha National Park via the vast pasturelands and small Sherpa villages. The trek also features the various Sherpa settlements of lower and upper Khumbu regions, including Namche Bazaar, the commercial hub of Khumbu. From the quiet trails of the Arun valley to the bustling towns of Dudh Koshi valley, Arun Valley Trek gives it all to the trekkers with an exclusive opportunity to get to know about the Rai and Sherpa culture by visiting the many temples and monasteries en route.

We, Base Camp Adventure, assure you that with our travel packages, you are bound to gain invaluable and incomparable insights into the wonderful nature and culture of Nepal. Be a part of this complete adventure with Base Camp Adventure, featuring experienced and caring crew, for one of the most memorable trips of your life.

itinerary.title: Arrival at Kathmandu Airport and transfer to hotel
itinerary.html: Upon arrival in Kathmandu, you will be kindly welcomed by our team and later you will be taken to your hotel. Feel free to enjoy your day here in Kathmandu. You will stay overnight in a hotel.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Tumlingtar and trek to Kartike (523 m / 1,715 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: The early morning flight from Kathmandu gives us attractive views of the hills, gorges, and the eastern Himalayas until we land in Tumlingtar. Upon arrival in Tumlingtar, you walk through the forested trail and descend through the farms to reach Kumal Gaon, situated on the edge of a broad hill. We move through the eastern bank of Arun River, crossing it on a bridge leading to the settlement of Bheteni. From here, walk to Chewabesi (250m) and stop here to take the lunch. Passing through the sub-tropical forest, continue south along the east bank of Arun River through Rai, Chettri, and Brahmin villages to reach the lively village of Kartike. Overnight in Kartike.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kartike to Gothe (775 m / 2,543 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Walk through the meadows to pass the bridge over Arun River to reach the tiny village of Baluwa Besi. The trail climbs into Sal forest and passes several villages before continuing on a trail through rice terraces to reach the Rai village of Marduwa. The trail then continues along the Irkhuwa Khola through rice and banana farms to arrive in Gothe Bazaar. Overnight in Gothe.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gothey to Phedi (1,680m / 5,512ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Ascend through Rai and Sherpa villages crossing suspension bridges over Irkhuwa Khola to reach Dobane. Pass through the beautiful villages of Tendor and Tallo Phedi, and ascend through terraced fields and later through damp forest area following the south bank of Irkhuwa Khola. A winding trail through the riverbed of Irkhuwa Khola brings us to Phedi. Overnight in Phedi.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phedi to Gurase (2,880m / 9,449ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Ascend from Phedi to climb along small streams through the densely forested trail. After ascending, reach the village of Thulo Fokte and cross the stone path through the forest, with lots of sunny clearings for occasional rests. Climb up towards the forest of oak, birch, and rhododendron, and drop down from the top of Bilbate. Further walking for about 30 minutes, we reach the village of Gurase. Overnight in Gurase.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gurase to Sanam (2,850m / 9,350ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Today the trail begins after passing through lush rhododendron forest to reach Salpa Pokhari. Situated in Salpa Bhanjyang, Salpa Pokhari is a holy pond, visited by throngs of Hindu pilgrims each year during the full moon of October. The area is bounded by hemlock and fir trees and is abundant with various birds, flora, and fauna. Glimpses of Makalu (8,463 m) and Chamlang (7,321 m) can be seen from Salpa Bhanjyang. Reach the open part with loose stones and rhododendrons above Salpa Bhanjyang and descend to the mainstream. Move on the path across the hillside and through the moist forest to reach Sanam. Overnight in Sanam.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sanam to Bung (1,900m / 6,234ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Descend through the forest of rhododendron, brown oaks, and chir pines towards the village of Sorung. About two hours trek from Shorung, we reach the Rai village of Gudel. Cross Hinku River on a steel suspension bridge, after which the main trail descends through a collage of rice, millet and soybean terraces to reach the village of Bung. We need our Makalu Barun Conservation Area entry permit to enter Bung. Overnight in Bung.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bung to Gaikharka (2,300m / 7,546ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Descend steeply through the cliff of a hill covered in wispy bamboo. Pass Najindingma village and enter a clear area of savannah, used as summer grazing of yaks by the people from surrounding settlements. Another one and the half hour drop across damp forest takes us to Gaikharka. Here, you'll have pleasing views of green terraces and dispersed farmhouses. Overnight in Gaikharka.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gaikharka to Vasme (2,500 m / 8,202 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: Descend through the edge to walk through numerous ups and downs across the ravines and old moraines. The trail slowly descends and later ascends through the rhododendron and juniper forest alongside Hinku River to reach Vasme. Vasme offers a distant view of Mera Peak (6,476 m) along with the glimpses of the Upper Khumbu region. Overnight in Vasme.

itinerary.title: Trek from Vasme to Panggom (2,804m / 9,199ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Begin by passing the small village of Vasme through the rhododendron forest. A steep ascend through the forest takes us to the top of Panggom La Pass (3,174 m), from where amazing views of the snow covered Mera Peak (6,476 m), Kusum Kanguru (6,367 m), Kangtega (6,685 m), and other peaks can be seen. Then a steep descend through the ridge takes us takes us to the beautiful Sherpa village of Panggom. Here, we can visit the PaldiOrken Choling Gompa and Hillary School. Overnight in Panggom.

itinerary.title: Trek from Panggom to Paiya (2,730m / 8,957ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Ascending through the lush forest of rhododendron and oak, we head towards the village of Paiya. A gradual ascend through the ridge takes us to the top of Kari La (3,145 m), which serves as a vantage point to view the beauty of Kusum Kanguru (6,367 m), Thamserku (6,608 m), and Kangtega (6,685 m). Afterward, descend gradually and cross a wooden bridge above Paiya Khola and head towards Paiya. Overnight in Paiya.

itinerary.title: Trek from Paiya to Phakding (2,610m / 8,563ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: From Paiya, ascend gradually through the lush forest with mixed vegetation to arrive in Chutok La (2,945 m). Then a slow descend takes us to Surke, from where the trail ascends through Chheplung and Nurning to reach Phakding. En route, we pass many small monasteries and Mani walls before reaching the small Sherpa village of Phakding. Phakding hosts an amazing view of Kusum Kangaru (6,367 m) and Thamserku (6,608 m). Overnight in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Lukl (2,860m / 9,383ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: Leaving Phakding, cross the suspension bridge over Dudh Koshi River and descend through rhododendron and pine forests to reach Lukla. We cross many Buddhist villages and their prayer flags on the way to Lukla. On reaching Lukla, we celebrate our accomplishment. Overnight in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly From Lukla to Kathmandu (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html: We fly back to Kathmandu from Lukla (40 minutes) with the views of the mighty Himalayas. From the airport, we drive you to the hotel, after which you can enjoy the whole day resting in your room or shopping in the nearby markets.  Overnight at a 3-star hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu.
itinerary.html: Today is your final day in Nepal. After breakfast, our team will drop you at the airport before the scheduled time.

seo.title: Bardia National Park | Mid-Far Western Terai Nepal
seo.description: Bardia National Park is best to experience natural environment. This National park offers opportunity to watch 30 unique vertebrates and 250 types of birds.

overview:
Nepal is rightly perceived as a heaven for climbers and trekkers for it has the most astounding Mountain in the earth, Mt. Everest alongside numerous other superb mountains in the north. However, the sub-tropical jungles of the Terai region of Nepal have some of the best wildlife habitat in the subcontinent and your trip to Nepal is definitely incomplete if you have not been on a jungle safari. Among various options, Bardia National Park is one of the best destinations for jungle safari in Nepal.

Situated in the mid-far western Terai, Bardia National Park is the most un-spoilt expanse of wilderness in southern Nepal. Originally, a hunting reserve, the park became a conservation area in 1976. Finally in the year 1988 AD, it attained National Park status.The park covers the total area of 968 sq. km and about 70 percent of the total area is dominated by Saal forest. Along with that, it is home to many endangered species including tiger, wild elephant, blackbuck, gharial crocodile and marsh mugger crocodile. The national park is full of open grassland and glades making it an ideal place for game-viewing.

The jungle Safari involvement in Bardia National Park is stunning and remunerating as it provides a chance to investigate and appreciate the wild. This National park offers you opportunity to watch 30 unique vertebrates and 250 types of birds. The Wild Boar, Hog Deer, Blue Bull, Porcupine, Sloth Bear, Wild Dog, Jungle Cats, Rhesus Monkey, Barking Deer, Sambar Deer, Otter, Jackal, Hyena, Common Leopard, Fishing Cat, Langur Monkey, Mongoose, Civets, and so forth are ordinarily seen. Furthermore, The Woodpecker (10 species), Bulbul (5 species), Dove (5 species), Heron (5 species), Egret (4 species), Parakeets, King fisher, Bee Eater, Barbet, Pigeon, Stork, Sunbird, Babbler, Warble, flycatcher and Bar-headed Goose are found in this park. This park is also considered as bird lover’s paradise.

Getting perspectives of a wide range of such natural life and winged creatures sitting on the uniquely prepared Elephant top happens to be a lifetime memory for you. The breathtaking Jeep Safari is yet another chance to have a fast recap over the delightful and uncommon natural life wilderness enterprise. Last but not the least, you will make the most of your minutes finding the one of a kind convention and society of an intriguing ethnic individuals of Nepal – the Tharu, making your exploration even more exciting.

The park and its adjacent areas are famous region to provide an excellent wilderness experience for visitors or wildlife researchers. So, if you are someone who love adventure, wants to experience natural environment at its best, and is someone who is eager to discover and acquire new knowledge, then jungle safari in Bardia National Park is for you. Our accomplished proficient team are constantly dedicated for giving the best conceivable administration with wellbeing and security. We, base camp adventure, guarantee that the time you go through with us will be worth recalling.

seo.title: Bhutan Cultural Tours – 04 Days / 03 Nights
seo.description: Bhutan cultural tours 4 Days | Bhutan is cradled in the deep folds of the Himalayas. Very little has been heard of Bhutan and to most people it is a

overview: Bhutan is cradled in the deep folds of the Himalayas. Very little has been heard of Bhutan and to most people it is a hidden kingdom shrouded in mystery. It is classed as one of the most exotic destinations in the world today. This kingdom often referred to as the last Shangri-la, a land of outstanding people, remarkable scenery, natural wonders with proud and vibrant culture. A unique and rare place that few people have the privilege of visiting. Bhutan is bounded by Tibetan regions of China in the north and sweltering plains of India in the south. This mountainous kingdom is well defined by Last Shangri-La or Land of the Thunder Dragon. The significant features of Bhutan vary from climatic conditions ranging from the sub-tropical to the cold reaches of the almost 25,000 ft of the Tibetan border. This 04 days Bhutan Cultural tour will give you a complete cultural experiences in Bhutan

itinerary.title: Arrival in Bhutan
itinerary.html: Landing in the Paro valley, surrounded by 4000 meter high mountains stretching across the west of Bhutan, enables you to have a visual landing which is indispensable and that makes your day an unforgettable one. Our Bhutanese representative will welcome you on arrival and drive you through the beautiful valley of Paro to the capital city Thimphu. (2 hrs drive) On the way to Thimphu visit Tamchhog Lhakhang, which is located on the opposite side of the river. This is a temple built by Thang Thong Gyalpo of Tibet.Later visit: Zorig Chusum Institute: 13 traditional arts and crafts. It was established in 1971 by the Royal Government in order to preserve the invaluable heritage and promote the arts of Bhutan. Hand Made Paper Factory: Jungshi Paper Factory was established in November 1990 as an undertaking of the Royal Government of Bhutan. Textile Museum: The foundation was laid in 2000 under the Royal Patronage of Her Majesty the Queen Ashi Sangay Choden Wangchuck. It was established with the aim of preserving and promoting Bhutanese textile arts. Thangtong Dewachen (nunnery): It was founded in 1976 by Rikey Jadrel, who is considered as emanation of Thangthong Gyalpo(1363 – 1485), the builder of numerous iron chain bridges across the Himalayas. Tashichho Dzong: Means Fortress of Glorious Religion. It was built in 1641 by Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel and was reconstructed into present structure by the late King. Sangaygang View Point: As well as being the location of the transmitter tower of the only national television tower in the country (BBS), the view point is also the perfect place to take in some truly breathtaking views of the entire city of Thimphu. Mini Zoo: Here we can see Bhutan’s national animal known as Takin. This is an extremely rare member of the goat family. Found in herds in the very high altitudes (13,125ft and over). Later you can stroll around the city and if you wish you can do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Drive from Thimpu to Paro
itinerary.html: Morning visit the weekend market. Market days are absolutely central to the lives of the Bhutanese, but there are many reasons to visit other than the icious fresh food on offer every Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Later take a hike to Cheri Monastery (includes Dodina and Jigme Dorji Wild life Sanctuary): The hike of about 2hrs leads to Cheri Goemba (Cheri Dorji Dhen). The trail starts by crossing a lovely covered bridge that spans the Wang Chu, and then climbs to the monastery. After visiting Cheri Monastery lunch and drive to Paro Valley (2 hours drive) In Paro visit the National Museum at Ta Dzong. Ta Dzong means watchtower and it actually served as a watchtower in the 17th century to guard to region from a possible Tibetan invasion. The interesting museum houses a fine collection of for example Bhutanese art, relics, religious Thangka`s. After Ta Dzong we also take you to Paro Rimpung Dzong. Rimpung Dzong means fortress in the heap of jewels. It was build in 1644 by Zhabdrung, who till today is deeply revered by the Bhutanese people as a dynamical political and spiritual leader. Especially from the other side of the river very nice pictures can be taken of the majestic Paro Dzong with Ta Dzong at the background.

itinerary.title: Paro: Morning hike to Taktsang Monastery
itinerary.html: Generally regarded as Bhutan’s most recognizable cultural icon, the Taktsang Monastery, or Tiger`s Nest, is strikingly iconic of the country’s culture and traditions. Farmhouse: Bhutan is justly not famous for its cuisine, which is somewhat predictable. Eating at a local farmhouse at least gives a slightly different variation.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.html: After breakfast in the hotel drive to Paro airport in time to catch up your onward flight. Your escort from Bhutan Discovery will bid you farewell and soon the remote and legendary Dragon Kingdom disappears again behind its guardian mountains.

title: Bhutan Heritage Tour
summary: Bhutan Heritage Tours offers an in depth look at the culture of Bhutan. We will also get to know why Bhutanese are among the world's most happiest people.

seo.title: Bhutan Heritage Tours | 1 Week Bhutan Cultural Tours Package
seo.description: Bhutan Heritage Tours offers an in depth look at the culture of Bhutan. We will also get to know why Bhutanese are among the world's most happiest people.

overview:
Bhutan is cradled in the deep folds of the Himalayas. Very little has been heard of Bhutan and to most people it is a hidden kingdom shrouded in mystery. Bhutan Heritage Tours is classed as one of the most exotic tours in the world today.

This kingdom often referred to as the last Shangri-la, a land of outstanding people, remarkable scenery, natural wonders with proud and vibrant culture. A unique and rare place that few people have the privilege of visiting. Bhutan is bounded by Tibetan regions of China in the north and sweltering plains of India in the south. This mountainous kingdom is well defined by Last Shangri-La or Land of the Thunder Dragon.

The significant features of Bhutan vary from climatic conditions ranging from the sub-tropical to the cold reaches of the almost 25,000 ft of the Tibetan border. Today when almost all parts of the world has seen a surge in tourist numbers, Bhutan has continued to followed a policy of regulated tourism in order to safeguard the country’s natural environment, rich cultural heritage and the unique way of life for its people; making Bhutan one of the least traveled countries in the world.

Come, explore and unravel the untouched wonders of Bhutan for yourself. Snow-capped mountains, emerald green landscapes, fascinating wildlife and gentle people all await you. Experience the hospitality of the Bhutan in the Bhutan Heritage Tours.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Bhutan
itinerary.html: Flying in to the country’s only airport, in the beautiful Paro valley, the clear mountain air, forested ridges, imposing monasteries and welcoming Bhutanese people in their striking national dress, provides a breath-taking first impression. On arrival at Paro airport, after immigration and custom formalities, your guide from Discovery Bhutan for the trip will receive you and transfer you to Tashi Namgay Resort or Khangkhu Resort. After Lunch visit, National Museum of Bhutan. After the advent of modernism in the country the Royal Government of Bhutan, with an aim to showcase the country’s rich culture and traditions, initiated the idea to introduce a museum for the first time and in 1968 the watchtower above Paro Dzong was chosen to initially house a modest collection of murals, numismatics, philately, etc. Over the years, after much renovation the museum accumulated more and more objects from different parts of the country and is today a storehouse of Bhutan’s cultural and traditional treasures. With over thirteen galleries, each holding exhibits from different periods and places in the country, the National Museum of Bhutan takes pride in its effort to educate its visitors, be they local or foreign, about the country’s cultural history that date back to as early as 2000 B.C and its metamorphism over the ages into what it is today. After more than three decades, the museum has established itself not only as a huge tourist attraction but also as an institution of learning for both scholars and visitors; considering the history of the building, the National Museum of Bhutan can rightly be termed as a ‘museum within a museum’. This museum is also one of the best museums in Asia. Thereafter visit Rinpung Dzong, which means the “fortress on a heap of jewels”. Take a leisure walk through a traditional covered bridge to the Dzong and enjoy a breathtaking view of its architectural wonder. The Dzong is now the Paro Monastic School and the office of the civil administration.

itinerary.title: Hike to Tiger’s Nest (04 -05 hours)
itinerary.html: Today, we hike up to the famous cliff-hermitage called Taktsang, the “Tiger’s Nest.” This day hike is not only historically and culturally interesting, but also incredibly scenic! It takes about two hours to reach the cafeteria, which gives a breathtaking view of the Tiger’s Nest. From Cafeteria it takes 1 hour to reach the main temple. This day hike is not only historically and culturally interesting, but also incredibly scenic! This monastic retreat is built into a sheer cliff face high above the Paro valley. Legend has it that the Tibetan Buddhist saint Padmasambhava flew across the Himalayas on the back of a tiger and landed here, bringing Buddhism to Bhutan. The trail to the monastery climbs through beautiful pine forest and an occasional grove of fluttering prayer flags. After Lunch, visit drive to Drugyel Dzong which is built by Shabdrung Ngawang Namgyal in 1646 to commemorate his victory over the Tibetan invaders. Though largely destroyed by fire in 1951, the towering outer walls and central keep remain an imposing sight. On clear day you can see the splendid view of Mt. Chomolhari (Alt.7321). Afternoon, drive to Thimphu the capital city of Bhutan, passing through idyllic countryside, with villages and paddy fields on either side of the road. Thimphu has a special charm and it is fascinating to sit and watch a gathering of local people in the town square, wearing their traditional dress and going about their business in a typically unhurried Bhutanese way.

itinerary.title: Thimphu City Sightseeing
itinerary.html: After Breakfast, go to Bhutan National Bank for currency exchange and then you can get an opportunity to purchase exquisite collector Bhutanese stamps. Then visit National Library where ancient texts and manuscripts are preserved; The Indigenous Hospital where traditional medicines are still practiced; Woodcraft and Painting school where traditional art and crafts are still kept alive; Handicrafts Emporium where Bhutanese textiles are displayed and can be purchased. After noon drive to the Buddha Dordenma sited amidst the ruins of Kuensel Phodrang, the palace of Sherab Wangchuck, the 13th Desi Druk, overlooking the southern approach to Thimphu. It is one of the largest Buddha rupas in the world, at a height of 169 feet (51.5 meters). You can also enjoy the view of the Thimphu city clearly from here. In the evening explore the busy Thimphu town with your guide or on your own. Note: If you are there on a Friday, Saturday and Sunday, the tour will include a visit to the local vegetable market. You will get to meet many Bhutanese people and valley dwellers on the bank of the river where the weekend market is held.

itinerary.title: Thimphu to Wangdue Via Punakha
itinerary.html: Drive early to Punakha, the ancient capital of Bhutan taking about 03 hours across Dochu-La Pass at 3,050 m from where snow-capped eastern Himalayan ranges can be seen on a clear day. Prayer flags will flutter you over the pass taking you deeper into the essence of Bhutan. Once you cross the pass, you wind down into a warm fertile valley and meander along a gently flowing aquamarine river that leads you to the Punakha valley. Then visit the Punakha dzong, the winter residence of the Je khempo (chief abbot). Punakha dzong is the second dzong system built in Bhutan by Shebdrung Nawang Namgyel in the year 1637. The Dzong is said to be the most beautiful of Dzong in Bhutan; it is an outstanding structure with intense artwork. After lunch short hike to Khamsum Yulley Namgyal Chorten in the northern part of the valley. Newly built and it is a more elaborate version of the Memorial Chorten in Thimphu. It has an astounding work of frescoes and intricate statues.

itinerary.title: Wangdue- Phobjikha
itinerary.html: Today drive to Phobjikha valley. Phobjikha is a glacial valley on the periphery of the north western tip of the Black Mountain National Park at the altitude of 9,840 feet. The valley is a wide, beautiful alpine wetland valley and is a conservation area and lies on the northern boundary of the Jowo Durshing range. The hill side vegetation is mostly pine forest, interspersed with Rhododendron trees. Phobjikha valley is also one of the roosting grounds of the Black-necked cranes that migrate each year in winter from its northern habitats in Tibet and Siberia. These elegant and shy birds can be observed from early November to end of the March. RSPN and Phobjikha community are now working together to protect the habitat of endangered Black Necked Cranes. You will visit Gangtey Goenpa which is the only Nyingmapa monastery in western Bhutan and is situated on a ridge overlooking the Phobjikha Valley. According to a legend Gangtey Goenpa was founded by the grandson of Pema lingpa, Gyalse Pema Thinley in 1613 and later was expanded by Tenzin Legpau Dhendup. It was renovated by present Gangtey Tulku Kunzang Rinzin Pema Namgyel and was consecrated in October 2008.

itinerary.title: Gangtey Paro
itinerary.html: Morning walk to explore the village, then return to Thimphu (about 05 hours drive). From Gangtey, the road gradually descends into the balmy Punakha valley, and then begins a long climb back up to the Dochu La, where a stunning field of white chortens and colorful prayer flags send blessings up to the Himalayan sky; snow peaks line the horizon. From the La, it is only another hour to Thimphu. Stop here for lunch, then continue to Paro (just under 2 hrs), one of the most beautiful valleys in Bhutan with its slate-roofed farmhouses, graceful willow trees and rushing glacial river beneath snow covered peaks. En route visit Botanical garden and Takchok lhakhang built by Drupthop Thangthong Gyelpo the Iron chain bridge builder. Still you can see the iron chain bridge which is built by him.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.html: After breakfast in the hotel drive to Paro airport in time to catch up your onward flight. Your escort from Bhutan Discovery will bid you farewell and soon the remote and legendary Dragon Kingdom disappears again behind its guardian mountains.

title: Buddhist Tour in Nepal
summary: Experience Nepal’s sacred Buddhist heritage on a spiritual pilgrimage tour, visiting ancient monasteries, sacred sites, and important Buddhist landmarks.

seo.title: Buddhist Tour in Nepal | Buddhist Heritage Tour Booking
seo.description: Experience Nepal’s sacred Buddhist heritage on a spiritual pilgrimage tour, visiting ancient monasteries, sacred sites, and important Buddhist landmarks.

overview:
Buddhism is a significant religion in the world followed by a large number of people. The rich Buddhist culture and heritage of Nepal bring hundreds of pilgrims to this country. There are many ancient monuments and pilgrimage sites as well. This Buddhist Tour is an ideal opportunity for travelers to explore the cultural landscapes of the country.

Lord Buddha was born as Siddharth Gautam in Lumbini, Nepal. The landmarks like the Birthplace of Lord Buddha, Mayadevi Temple, Lord Buddha's seven steps are pretty significant. This beautiful tour is also informational and educational. You can explore the different cultural heritage of the region as well.

Our Buddhist tour starts with a hike to scenic Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple) and Boudhanath. We also visit the significant Pharping Monastery and explore Taudaha lake. The travelers will visit the Kapan Monastery on the next day.

Namo Buddha monastery on the outskirts of the Kathmandu valley will enchant all travelers. The beautiful architecture and majestic views of snow-capped mountains are a highlight of this tour. After exploring these incredible Buddhist monuments, we will travel outside the Kathmandu valley.

Firstly, we will fly to Bharatpur and make our way to the Lumbini and visit the birthplace of Lord Buddha. The monastic region in Lumbini has many monasteries of different countries, including Japanese Monastery, Chinese Monastery, Thailand Monastery, and others. The Buddhist pilgrimage site is of great religious and spiritual significance.

Moreover, you will also get to visit the famous Ashoka pillar, Maya Devi temple, Seven Steps in Lumbini. You will visit places like Kapilvastu, Kudan, Tilaurakot, and other Buddhist monuments. Read on for the detailed itinerary of the Buddhist Tour in Nepal and additional related information.

You may also like: Nepal Cultural Tour, Nepal Heritage Tour, Nepal Historical Tours

Highlights of the Tour

  • Exploring incredible Buddhist landmarks including Swayambhunath and Boudhanath of Kathmandu valley
  • Visiting the monasteries like Pharping, Namobuddha, Kapan monastery, and Taudaha
  • Visiting Lumbini, the birthplace of Lord Buddha
  • Exploring Tilaurakot and Kudan and other Buddhist monuments
  • Experiencing the peaceful atmosphere of the Lumbini monastic zone
  • The pilgrimage of Maya Devi temple and the Ashok pillar
  • Incredible hospitality of the Nepalese people

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu and transfer to your hotel.
itinerary.html: After arrival in Kathmandu, our staff and representative will pick you up from the Tribhuvan international airport and then transfer you to your hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Tour of Swayambhunath, Boudhanath, and Pharping (7-8 hours).
itinerary.html:
After breakfast, we will start our Buddhist Tour in Nepal with a scenic drive to Pharping. Pharping village settlement remains located along the way to the famous Dakshinkali temple. You can explore around the villages providing incredible local heritages.
The Buddhist monastery in Pharping also has many students, both local and international, studying dharma practice and teaching. There is also Taudaha, a beautiful lake that is also mentioned in mythologies. Taudaha is also the place where Manjushree kept all the Nagas from the vast lake of Kathmandu.
After exploring Pharping, we will continue our tour to Kathmandu, where we will have lunch. We then make our way to Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), located at a hilltop. Swayambhunath stupa is one of the significant landmarks of the city revered by both Hindu and Buddhist pilgrims. The beautiful stupa premises is home to monkeys. You can observe many of them playing around the steps to this temple.
Furthermore, we can also travel to one of the largest stupas in Asia, Boudhanath stupa. Hundreds of pilgrims perform the Buddhist ritual of Kora of the dome, where they circumnavigate chanting prayers and circulating main wheels. The stupa has eyes that signify and send out the message of peace. We will return to our hotel and spend the night at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Kopan Monastery and Namobuddha Monastery tour (7-8 hours).
itinerary.html:
After our meal, we will start our trip to Kopan Gompa (Monastery). Monks around the world come to this monastery to study Buddhist philosophy and spirituality. After meditating, we explore around and observe the peaceful atmosphere. We will continue our trip to Namo Buddha. You will explore a small village in Kathmandu.
According to mythologies, a starving tigress and her cubs were saved by Lord Buddha. After a beautiful exploration around the monastery, we will take a scenic flight to Bhairawa airport. Lumbini is a beautiful settlement and our next destination.

itinerary.title: Flight to Bhairahawa from Kathmandu and Transfer to Lumbini.
itinerary.html:
After taking a scenic flight from Kathmandu, we will continue our tour at the Bhairawa airport, from where we will travel to Lumbini. You will then visit Lord Buddha's birthplace, Ashok pillar, Maya Devi temple, and other regional landmarks.
Gautam Buddha was born as Siddhartha Gautam, King Sudhodhan, prince of the royal family in the region. Queen Maya Devi gave birth to Lord Buddha in May 642 BC in Devdaha while traveling to her home. Buddha took seven immediate steps after birth, and on each of those steps, lotus flowers bloomed.
Moreover, there are other incredible landmarks like the Ashoka pillar constructed by King Ashoka in 249 BC. German archaeologists found the birthplace of Lord Buddha, Lumbini, in 1895 with the help of this inscription in this pillar. UNESCO subsequently named Lumbini as a World Heritage Site in 1997. After exploring the beautiful sites, we will explore Lumbini Garden. We will rest and spend the night at a hotel in Lumbini.

itinerary.title: Explore around Tilaurakot and Kudan (6-7 hours).
itinerary.html:
After breakfast, we will explore Tilaurakot and Kudan near Lumbini. Tilaurakot is an important historical site located around 29 km west of Lumbini. Tilaurakot Palace is the place where Lord Buddha spent his life as Prince Siddhartha Gautam.
There is a fantastic meadow along the banks of the Ban-Ganga River. You can also observe a large residential compound around the area. There is a beautiful temple dedicated to Maya Devi, mother of Lord Budhha. After touring around Tilaurakot, we will travel to Kudan. Kudan is only around 4.5 km south of Tilaurakot.
Moreover, there are ruins of old structures, stupas, ponds, monasteries, and others. There is a Kasaya stupa where Lord Buddha was given a Kasaya (yellow robe worn by monks) after he attained cosmic enlightenment. We will return to the hotel and spend the night at a hotel in Lumbini.

itinerary.title: Drive from Lumbini to Bhairahawa airport to fly to Kathmandu.
itinerary.html:
After we have our breakfast, we will take a scenic drive from Lumbini to Ramgram, where you can visit the Ramgram Stupa built around 2500 years ago. The Ramgram stupa contains the relics of Lord Buddha as it is the only standing stupa from ancient times. This excellent historical site is of great religious importance.
We can observe the great 7 m (23 ft) high stupa buried on the ground. After touring around Ramgram, we will have lunch and drive back to Bhairawa airport. We will then fly back to Kathmandu and spend the night at a hotel.

itinerary.title: Transfer to the International Airport for your onward journey.

sections.title: Major Attractions of the Buddhist Tour in Nepal
sections.html:
Major Attractions of the Buddhist Tour in Nepal

The major attractions of the Buddhist Tour in Nepal are as follows:

Swayambhunath

Swayambhunath is a beautiful stupa located on a hilltop in Kathmandu. Many monkeys are living around this beautiful stupa temple and therefore known as the "Monkey Temple." You can also observe awe-inspiring views of sunrise and sunset from the viewpoint in this stupa premises.

Boudhanath

Boudhanath is a beautiful stupa located in Kathmandu. The stupa was built around the fifth century and had a massive mandala structure. It is considered most significant in Asia. You can also explore the area, including many cafes, Thangka galleries, restaurants, around Boudhanath. The Boudhanath has many Tibetan refugees around the region and is known as "Little Tibet."

Pharping

Pharping is a small village settlement in Newari town located around 19 km south of Kathmandu. Moreover, the ancient Pharping monastery is another important Buddhist pilgrimage site. There are several Tibetan refugees along with the settlement as well. You can also explore around the Taudaha lake while on the way to Pharping.

Kapan Monastery

Kapan Monastery is another beautiful Tibetan Buddhist monastery located on the outskirts of Kathmandu. Kapan Monastery is a member of Gelugpa Dharma centers which is an international group of monasteries. The gompa also works in the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition (FPMT).

Namo Buddha

Namo Buddha remains located away from the urban capital of Kathmandu. According to legend, this is the same place where Siddhartha Gautam gave his body to a starving tigress and her cubs. Hence, this Namo Buddha monastery is a significant landmark both historically and religiously.

Lumbini (Birthplace of Lord Buddha)

Lumbini is significant in Buddhist as it is Lord Buddha and hence quite an important pilgrimage site for Buddhists worldwide. The spiritual landmark lies in the Rupandehi District of Nepal. Queen Mayadevi traveled to Devdaha, her parent's home, when she gave birth to Siddhartha Gautam in 642 BC. Lord Buddha is widely believed to have walked seven steps immediately after his birth. According to mythology, on those steps, a lotus flower bloomed. You can also explore the Ashok Pillar built by King Ashok in 249 BC. The Ashok Pillar was an instrumental landmark that provided evidence in discovering the old ruins of Lumbini and eventually the birthplace of Lord Buddha. German archaeologists discovered the Ashok Pillar in 1895 with the help of Chinese pilgrim Fa Xian and his inscription. UNESCO provided Lumbini with the World Heritage Site in 1997.

Kapilvastu

Kapilvastu is also the palace region of King Śuddhodana and his Shakya Kingdom. Moreover, Lord Buddha was born as his son Prince Siddhartha Gautama. You can visit the ancient ruins of Lord Buddha's palace in Kapilvastu. The tranquil and peaceful region will enchant any traveler.

Tilaurakot and Kudan

Tilaurakot is a historical site that lies around 29 km west of Lumbini. It is the place where Lord Buddha spent his first 29 years as Prince Siddhartha Gautam. Similarly, the peaceful meadow near the banks of the BanGanga River is another highlight of this place. There are ruins of a large residential compound and Maya Devi shrine in Tilaurakot. Kudan remains located around 4.5 km south of Tilaurakot. Structural ruins, stupas, ponds, and monasteries are highlights of this tour. There is a Kasaya stupa where Lord Buddha was given a Kasaya, a yellow robe, after attaining enlightenment.

Ramgram Stupa

Ramgram stupa is among the stupas built by King Ashok. The King wanted throughout the Maurya Empire to construct 84,000 stupas. However, while making the stupa, the serpent Naga king was too powerful guarding the Ramagrama stupa. This did not allow Ashoka to unearth the relic. It is an integral Buddhist heritage landmark of this region.

Best time for this Buddhist Tour in Nepal?

Buddhist Tour in Nepal is ideal in all seasons. There are incredible landscapes of the region that provide travelers with astonishing adventure. However, traveling in the peak season of Spring and Autumn is ideal for all travelers. Spring seasons in March to May provide travelers with stable weather conditions and perfect temperatures for traveling in the daytime. There are clear skies and less precipitation, which makes it ideal for traveling. Wildflowers are blooming over hills like rhododendrons that makes it a pretty beautiful scenario along trails. Besides that, the Autumn season (September to November) is another peak season in the region. There are beautiful weather conditions all around the area that provide travelers with an incredible adventure. There are clear blue skies and stable weather conditions with minimal precipitation that are ideal for travel. Besides that, cultural exploration is another highlight of this trip. Travelers can observe local people busy in local festivities like Dashain, Tihar, and Chaath. Another off-season like winter and monsoon has challenging weather along trails, making it quite difficult for travelers to tour around the region. Winters bring freezing weather conditions and harsh winds, especially at night time. The monsoon season brings heavy precipitation and chilly weather. There are landslides, avalanches, floods, and muddy roads as well. However, if you prepare and pack well, you can travel any time in the region. Therefore, a Buddhist tour in Nepal is ideal in the spring and autumn seasons.

Why take this Buddhist helicopter tour?

Religious pilgrimage

This incredible Buddhist helicopter tour takes you to some of the significant landmarks of Buddhism in and around the country. Thousands of devotees take this beautiful tour every year to visit one of the most spiritual lands in Buddhist mythologies. The birthplace of Lord Buddha in Lumbini is probably the most sacred site in all of Buddhism. There are various temples, stupas, and bars in Kathmandu valley that provide a unique religious and cultural heritage of this ancient city. Besides that, there are multiple monasteries, gompas in the outskirts of Kathmandu, and other hilly landscapes of the country. Siddharth Gautam's various ancient palaces in and around Lumbini and Kapilvastu make this region quite significant. Travelers will cover all essential Buddhist heritage regions quickly, which makes their tour package quite substantial.

Scenic natural vista

This incredible Buddhist helicopter tour passes through scenic landscapes of green hills and the vast landscapes of Terai. Travelers can also observe magical views of snow-capped mountains from various viewpoints along the trail. Other natural landmarks like the green forest, serene waterfalls, vast rivers, and others that you will encounter during your journey make this tour quite an incredible opportunity to explore. Travelers can observe entire landscapes of regions from various viewpoints along trails, including multiple monasteries and stupas located atop a hill. Besides that, there are different cultural heritages that you can observe while traveling on this tour. The various landmarks of UNESCO-listed world heritage sites provide travelers with incredible and unique insight into local history, culture, and tradition.

Short duration tour

This incredible Buddhist tour is ideal for those travelers who want to complete their trip in a short amount of time. This quick duration tour provides travelers with a beautiful opportunity to traverse across major Buddhist landmarks and sites in a short schedule. This outstanding tour takes around seven days to complete. It takes you on a complete tour of Buddhist heritage sites in and around Kathmandu and various critical Buddhist cities like Lumbini and Kapilvastu. This short tour is packed with many places to visit with incredible religious and cultural significance. Hence, this Buddhist tour in Nepal is quite popular among travelers.

High-end facility

This Buddhist tour in Nepal provides travelers with incredible high-end facilities of meals and accommodation. Travelers will stay in luxury hotels and eat well-balanced nutritious, and delicious meals during their journey. There are various other facilities, including deluxe private transportation while traveling to different parts of the country. Travelers Will get the incredible best tour experience as they will travel safely and comfortably to experience this spiritual travel without any hassle. Therefore, this high-end facility makes this Buddhist tour in Nepal quite popular among travelers.

Friendly and convenient service

The team member and tour guide of this you're pretty friendly. Travelers will get professional directions and local heritage experts who will provide you with an incredible guided tour of various Buddhist heritage sightseeing points around the region. This fantastic tour is an ideal experience for those travelers that want a safe and comfortable experience around the various Buddhist sites. They will provide you with the best local insights and also allow you to interact with locals. Besides that, they will also provide you with all services regarding logistics along the trail so that you can travel without any hassle. Therefore, this aspect makes this Buddhist tour in Nepal one of the best tours.

The Final Say

Buddhism is a significant religion in Nepal. Various Buddhist landmarks make it ideal for a Buddhist Tour in Nepal. The Buddhist culture and heritage of Nepal provide travelers with a great spiritual experience. There are incredible monuments, ancient stupas, and other pilgrimage sites around the region. This tour passes through the beautiful landscapes and green landscapes of the area. Lumbini, the Birthplace of Lord Buddha, Mayadevi Temple, Lord Buddha's seven steps are some of the significant Buddhist heritage of the region. Our Buddhist temples, including Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple) and Boudhanath, Pharping Monastery, the Kapan Monastery, Namo Buddha monastery, are some of the significant landmarks of the region. We hope you learned about Buddhist Tour in Nepal and other related information in detail. Contact us for more information on this incredible tour.
