title: Chitwan National Park
summary: Chitwan National Park has been the most popular destination for tourists wanting to have amazing flora and fauna exploration.

seo.title: Chitwan National Park | First National Park of Nepal
seo.description: Chitwan National Park has been the most popular destination for tourists wanting to have amazing flora and fauna exploration.

overview:
Established in 1973 AD, Chitwan National Park is the most famous and the first National Park of Nepal. Ever since UNESCO declared it as a Natural World Heritage Site, it has been the most popular destination for tourists wanting to have amazing wildlife and flora and fauna filled exploration. Situated in the Central development region of Nepal and covering an area of 932 sq. km, Chitwan National Park is the home to more than 500 Asian one horned rhinoceros and Royal Bengal Tigers along with many other animal and birds species.

Back in 19th Century, Chitwan used to be a favourite hunting ground for Nepal’s ruling class only. Consequently, it became a favourite spot for big game safari hunters in the late nineteenth century which resulted in the drastic decrease in jungle habitat and animal populations. The falling number of Rhino (less than 200) and tiger (less than 30) in the present park, led to the declaration of two-third of the park as sanctuary in 1963. Since then, the wild life population has definitely rebound. Latest census figure shows rhino number are substantially recovering to 503 individuals and tiger number are steadily increasing to 120 adults in 2013.

Chitwan National Park is perhaps the best park in Nepal for seeing animals in their natural habitat. Here, you will find a lost universe of towering trees and winding vines, pre-notable rhino and ambling elephants, crocodile, python and deer; splendidly colored birds and on the off chance that you are blessed – the heavenly Royal Bengal Tiger. Imparting home to these are different other creatures like rhesus monkey, grey langur, deer, panthers and wild cats and so on. Another most vital component adding to the chitwan experience is the beautiful Tharu Culture, their method for living, society and convention and heart touching Tharu Dance.

To observe the rare great one horned rhino, exclusive tigers, leopards and many other rare and exotic animals and birds you can either take elephant back safari, or take nature walks with trained local naturalists. A jungle jeep drive through the park and boat ride down the river can also be done to experience close encounter with armour-plated one horned rhinoceros and follow tiger tracks through the thick jungles. All these adventurous activities are enough to make your trip one memorable and rewarding trip of your life.

All in all, Chitwan National Park provides you an escape from the polluted atmosphere and the noise of the big cities and takes you closer to the nature. If you are someone who wants to experience natural environment at its best, visit to Chitwan National Park is the right option for you. So, if you are prepared to have bold visit to Chitwan National Park, so are we! Our accomplished proficient team are constantly dedicated for giving the best conceivable administration with wellbeing and security. We, base camp adventure, guarantee that the time you go through with us will be worth recalling.

His priority is to ensure you have a once in a life time experience and I certainly did! A friend and I wanted to do the Annapurna Circuit and we visited numerous companies in Khatmandu, but were dissatisfied with them all. However we then found Shree at Base Camp Adventures, recommend to us by another group of travellers having done Everest BC with them. Instantly we liked him and after a lovely long chat (these can sometimes go on for hours, but are always interesting and funny!) we decided to go with his company. When I was unwell in Langtang he looked after me as a dear friend, always making sure I was warm, comfortable and eating/drinking enough - once I recovered, I made it to the top of the mountain, which I could not have done without him! I was hesitant being a solo female traveller and hiring a guide on my own, but with Jwala I knew I was in good hands! Having completed with Jwala and a friend the Annaourna Circuit, I decided to take him with me to the Langtang Valley. It was the best decision I made, as I had a fantastic time with him! reviews.author: fongben-Hayward, California
reviews.body: We booked a combination Everest View Trek (Lukla to Namche Bazaar) and Chitwan National Park from Dec 20 to Jan 1. Once we arrived into Kathmandu, BA arranged everything (airport pickup, hotel, guides, etc), so that my wife and I did not need to worry about any aspect of our trip. The only thing we had to decide for ourselves was where to eat during a few meals when we were on our own in Kathmandu. The accommodation was very reasonable and located in a very good part of Kathmandu perfect for shopping and sightseeing. We had a great trekking guide, Shiva, that took us from the Kathmandu hotel to Lukla, via a short flight. Shiva really took care of us each step of the way. Even though we went in the middle of winter, BA provided us sleeping bags and down coats that kept us warm during the cold nights up in the Himalayas. Additionally, BA also arranged for a porter to carry a lot of our gears so that it made our trip much more enjoyable. Even though I couldn't hike very fast, Shiva was very patient and professional as he waited for us patiently. Unfortunately, Shiva had a family emergency. But BA and Shree made sure my wife and I were taken cared of. Without wasting time, they found a local guide, An Tsering from Khumjung. Without any problems, my wife had a great time enjoying the food, sights, and sounds as we trek around the Namche Bazaar area. To fill out the rest of our trip, we went to Chitwan National Park. The accommodation was very good. The cultural show, elephant ride, canoe ride, and safari was well done. To cap it off we were up close to baby elephants in the breeding center. I'm already recommending my friends to go with BA if they were ever going to Nepal and trek in the Himalayas. The pricing was very reasonable and we were satisfied with all areas of service provided by BA. Shree and his coworkers are main reason my wife and I enjoyed this trip so much. We look forward to going back to Nepal in the near future!

seo.description: Chomolhari Trekking is an ideal adventure for nature lovers who are seeking a Himalayan wilderness immersion. Trek to Jangothang will take you upto 4044m.

overview:
Chomolhari Trekking also known as Jumolhari Trek, this intimate wilderness trek offers a great variety of trekking conditions, from remote farmland and blue pine forests, to alpine pastureland and breathtaking mountain views. It is an ideal adventure for nature lovers who are seeking a Himalayan wilderness immersion. It’s comfortable, low-impact, and absolutely unforgettable!
From the ruins of Drukgyal Dzong (fortress of the Victorous Drukpas), below such beautiful peaks, you will hike through the heart of wildlife-rich. The sky-piercing peaks, thunderous waterfalls, turquoise lakes and streams, rolling meadows filled with wildflowers, remote yak herders villages, and forests of rhododendron, pine, juniper and fir provide the perfect backdrop for this inspiring and challenging adventure. You will be rewarded with up-close views of Bhutan’s most beautiful peaks with Chomolhari Trekking .

title: Chulu West Peak Climbing
summary: Among the two chulus, Chulu West Peak Climbing is the higher peak. The Base Camp of this peak is situated in a small valley North of Manang.

seo.title: Chulu West Peak Climbing | 27 Days Trek to Chulu West Peak
seo.description: Among the two chulus, Chulu West Peak Climbing is the higher peak. The Base Camp of this peak is situated in a small valley North of Manang.

overview: Among the two chulus, Chulu West Peak Climbing is the higher peak. It was first climbed in 1952 by a Japanese Expedition team. The Base Camp of this peak is situated in a small valley North of Manang, the main trail to the Thorang La. There is a controversy regarding the name and location of the Chulu peaks. There are several peaks close by and are also a part of Chulu massif but are not indicated in the map. Thus it is difficult to differentiate between the two Chulus. However, the Chulu group comprises of four peaks: two in the east and two in the west. Chulu West may also be called Chulu Central. There is no technical difficulty in ascending this peak but progress can be slow as the slopes are vulnerable to avalanches in certain conditions.

seo.title: Damodar Kund Trek | Damodar Kund lake Trekking
seo.description: The elevation of the Damodar Kund trek is just 4890 m. It is cold and windy place. We will recommend to you visit during the full moon of August every year.

overview:
Made fully itinerary and finalized for Damodar Kund trek year of 2002 & open for all trekker & Pilgrimage foreigners. It is beautiful itinerary with acclimatization day during the trek period because it is important to us that you dream of seeing to Damodar Kund.
The Damodar Kund (lake) is famous for Hindu religion, it is situated rain shadow are of High Himalayas north of Annapurna range. The elevation of the Damodar Kund Trek is just 4,890 m; it is cold and windy place. We will recommend to you visit during the full moon of August every year, because every year there is a big festival up there many pilgrimages Hindu and Buddhist. Usually, you can visit April to September every year. Festival time will be great time to visit Damodar Kund.
From Damodar Kund, the views are great from some viewpoints a bit higher than the lakes, just a short climb up some of the hills. The Tibetan plateau & Damodar Himal to the north and the massive Annapurna Himalayan range to the south.
The walk to the Damodar Kund (lake) is not so difficult but quite long walking distance and only sometimes a bit steep and almost flat. Only problem is the altitude and I have been aware of this while working out the itinerary for you. Don’t worry about the altitude, we will arrange Gammo air pressure bag. The highest camp is at the Damodar Kund just 4,890 m
The Damodar lakes are located three days walk north east of the main Mustang trekking route & very close to the border with Tibet

title: Dhaulagiri Round Trek
summary: Dhaulagiri Round Trek is a challenging trek. This area is relatively strenuous and needs some mountaineering knowledge to do this trek.

seo.title: Dhaulagiri Round Trek | Guide, Cost, Itinerary, Route Map
seo.description: Dhaulagiri Round Trek is a challenging trek. This area is relatively strenuous and needs some mountaineering knowledge to do this trek.

overview:
Dhaulagiri Round Trek is a challenging and adventurous trek around the Dhaulagiri massif (8,167 m) which is also the seventh highest mountain in the world. The trekking in this region is comparatively strenuous and you have to be physically fit and have some trekking experience.  The trail goes through icy glaciers, snow-covered slopes, and lateral moraines, so only a true adventurer can complete this trek.

The trail of Dhaulagiri Round Trek goes through terraced fields connected to some of the mountain villages where you will see tea houses, shops, and also get to witness daily lifestyle and culture of the people of Magar, Gurung, and Thakali communities. You will also walk through rocky paths, dense forests, and suspension bridges. You will witness stunning views of Dhaulagiri I (8,167 m), Dhaulagiri II (7,751 m), Dhaulagiri III (7,715 m), Dhaulagiri IV (7,661 m), and Dhaulagiri V (7,618 m) during this trek. Many parts of the trail are capped with snow and glaciers as it crosses French Col (5,300 m), traverses the top of Hidden Valley, and crosses Thapa Pass (5,200 m). The amazing French Pass (5,300 m) is the highest point of this trek and also the connecting dot between the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna regions.

The trek features some of the prominent places of the Annapurna region such as Marpha, Tatopani, Ghorepani, and Poon Hill, a famous vantage point to witness the glory of the high Himalayas along with a stunning sunrise. All in all, Dhaulagiri Round Trek is a beautiful blend of nature and adventure in an off-the-beaten trail that awaits keen explorers.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Beni (830m / 2,723ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Moving out of the Kathmandu valley, we ascend to the connection of Trishuli River with the Marsayangdi River. We follow the Marsayangdi River upwards through terraced meadows and minor hill towns to the Seti River that leads us to Pokhara. The drive from Pokhara inclines through a twisting road up to Nayapul with views of Annapurna South (7,219 m) and Machhapuchhre (6,997 m). To reach Beni, we drive along the bank of Modi River and then Kali Gandaki River. Overnight in Beni.

itinerary.title: Trek from Beni to Tatopani / Babiyachaur (950m / 3,117ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: After our breakfast, we begin our trek from Beni on the bank of Myagdi River through numerous small settlements. Then we will cross two bridges near the village of Simalchaur and head north along the trails to the village of Babiyachaur. Passing through lush forests, meadows, amazing villages, and suspension bridges, we reach Babiyachaur via Tatopani. Overnight in Tatopani.

itinerary.title: Trek from Babiyachaur to Durbang (1,180m / 3,871ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Gradually ascend passing through forests with diversities of oaks, rhododendron, and so on. We can hear the chirping of the local birds as we walk on the trails passing through the river.  The path goes through the damp road alongside small villages. We cross many bridges over Myagdi Khola to reach the village of Darbang. Overnight in Darbang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Durbang to Sibang (1,770m / 5,807ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: We move north crossing the river and ascending on steep trails which lead us to Sibang. We cross a bridge over Dang Khola and ascend through the lush hill to reach the Magar village of Dharapani. We then keep ascending on the ridge until reaching Sibang. Enjoy the first view of Dhaulagiri (8,167 m) from Sibang. Overnight in Sibang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sibang to Muri / Jugepani (1,850m / 6,070ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Descend and walk through settlements, cross a suspension bridge over the river and turn uphill. The moderate ascending trail continues through villages, thick forests, and picturesque terraces to reach another ridge. Trek gently over a traditional trail until you reach Muri, a small village of Magar community. If the weather is clear, we can get a sight of Manapathi Himal (6,380 m) and the whole of Dhaulagiri range. Stay overnight in Muri.

itinerary.title: Trek from Muri / Jugepani to Bagar (2,080m / 6,824ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: From Muri, we have to walk down and cross a river and then walk past terraced fields. Descend to Myagdi Khola and trek alongside its west bank until we reach the village of Naura. Ascend, cross a lush hill, and climb a steep slope where the trails are zigzag and then descend through the forest and meadows to reach Bagar. Overnight in Bagar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bagar to Dovan (2,520m / 8,268ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Descend through adjoining meadows passing a small ridge. Arrive at a forest region to reach Jyardan. After that, a tall, winding trail leads to a stony area and reaches Lipshe, where there is no single hut. The track goes through a forest to Lapche Kharka and then ascends to Dobhan through tough trails. Overnight in Dobhan.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dovan to Sallaghari (2,820m / 9,252ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: The first part of the trek requires a moderate ascending through the forest of bamboo, pine, and rhododendron. After, the road goes uphill and downhill until we reach Sallaghari. Our camping spot lies in between the forest, surrounded by pine trees on the bank of Myagdi River. Stay overnight in Sallaghari.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sallaghari to Upper Vungini / Italian base camp (3,660m / 12,008ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail is surrounded by bamboo forest all the way to Italian Base Camp (3,660 m). In some places, we cross small bridges and jungles which make the track quite active, risky, and difficult. There is an open ground at Italian Base Camp. There are two small tea houses available that deliver a nominal quantity of basic items. At this base camp, you experience wonderful views of the Dhaulagiri range, Manapathi Peak (6,380 m), Dhaulagiri II (7,751 m), and other snow-covered mountains. Stay overnight in Italian Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Rest at Italian base camp for acclimatization (3,660m / 12,008ft).
itinerary.html: Today is our acclimatization day to explore around and adjust with the elevation. We visit the surrounding camps like Puchhar Base Camp, American Base Camp, Swiss Base Camp, French Base Camp, and Japanese Base Camp, all of which serve amazing views of Dhaulagiri range along with Tsaurabong (6,395 m). Overnight in Italian Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek from Italian Camp to Glacier camp (4,200m / 13,780ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, we start our trek and cross the first glacier using ropes. We climb onto the main glacier, where the surroundings are outstanding amid the rough and unsteady trail. This is a tough day where the trail gets more difficult as we go further, for the trail is covered in icy moraines of Dhaulagiri Glacier. Overnight in Glacier Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek to Glacier Camp to Dhaulagiri Base Camp (4,740m / 15,551ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: We begin our trek today through the bumpy trails on the flat ice of the snow-white glacier. We will climb gradually to the course and chilling yet remarkable Dhaulagiri Base Camp. The views from here are fabulous, could literally stop your breath for a few seconds. Get your cameras ready! You will experience best view of Dhaulagiri I (8,167 m), II (7,751 m), III (7,715 m) and IV (7,661 m). Stay overnight at Dhaulagiri Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dhaulagiri Base Camp to Hidden valley via French Col Pass (5,360m / 17,585ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Moving off the glacier above the base camp often involves the proper use of the rope. After climbing the vertical moraine walls, we reach a relatively easier trail. As we reach the top of French Col (5,300 m), there are astonishing views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges. After a breathless climb to the top of French Col (5,300 m), the views of Hidden Valley open out. The valley is evocative of Tibet and Ladakh and so are the temperatures. Overnight in Hidden Valley.

itinerary.title: Trek from Hidden Valley to Yak Kharka (3,680m / 12,073ft) crossing Thapa Pass (5,250m / 17,224ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: On this day, we will climb across Thapa Pass (5,200 m), pass through swamped slopes, and then descend sharply to reach Yak Kharka. The Thapa Pass (5,200 m), also known as Dhampus Pass, is situated between Tukuche peak (6,920 m) and Thapa Peak (6,012 m) and hosts alluring views of the Annapurna range. Overnight in Yak Kharka.

itinerary.title: Trek from Yak Kharka to Marpha (2,670m / 8,760ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Descend to the magnificent Kali Gandaki Valley, which is the deepest valley in the world. Pass Alu Bari to the gorge floor and head towards Marpha. Marpha is renowned for its apple orchards and their byproducts of apple cider and dried apple, apricot, and peach alcohol. Enjoy a delicious Thakali meal in Marpha. Overnight in Marpha.

itinerary.title: Trek from Marpha to Jomsom (2,720m / 8,924ft) and fly Pokhara (1-2 hours).
itinerary.html: After an hour early morning walk to Jomsom, we then take flight from Jomsom-Pokhara. You can spend your time in Pokhara by going for a boat ride in Phewa Lake and visiting Tal Barahi Mandir that is situated on an island in the middle of the lake or you can hire a mountain bike and explore the city as you please. In the evening, you can enjoy the vibrant restaurants and pubs lined in the Lakeside Street. Overnight at a hotel in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu (6-7 hours.)
itinerary.html: Drive back to Kathmandu by passing Damauli, Dumre, Mugling, and Kurintar. Enjoy the green sceneries, small settlements, and glimpses of local people. From Naubise, we ascend to Thankot, entryway of Kathmandu. Upon arrival in Kathmandu, you will be transferred to your hotel for the overnight stay.

seo.title: Dolpo Trek
seo.description: Dolpo is one of the most remote of Nepal’s regions. Dolpo Trek need special permit where trekkers spend 6-8 hours a day trekking.

overview:
Dolpo! The word conjures up visions of mysterious monasteries of snow leopards and blue sheep and called a land beyond the Himalaya.
Laying in western Nepal, Dolpo is one of the most remote of Nepal’s regions. By special permit for Dolpo Trek, we are able to offer these-days trek through upper and lower Dolpo.
Our route follows much of the route taken by Peter Mathiessen and George Shaller as described in “The snow Leopard”. We trek 200 miles, averaging 10 miles a day. We spend 6-8 hours a day trekking. Several layover days are planned. Porters carry a day pack with the things you need for the day.

Participants should be in good shape. We are at high elevation much of the time on this trip. Five passes, over 16,500 feet, are crossed. Steep climbs and descents are made.

title: Druk Path Trekking
summary: Druk Path Trekking is an excellent short trek, for those who are in Bhutan for a short time. Experience the countryside, alpine meadows, glacial lakes.

seo.title: Druk Path Trekking | 9 Days Druk Path Trek in Bhutan
seo.description: Druk Path Trekking is an excellent short trek, for those who are in Bhutan for a short time. Experience the countryside, alpine meadows, glacial lakes.

overview:
Following the ancient high-level route between Paro and Thimpu, the Druk Path Trekking is an excellent short trek, ideal for those who are in Bhutan only for a short duration.
You will experience the countryside, mountains, alpine meadows, glacial lakes and monasteries. The first day’s walk leads to the ruined Jeli Dzong which sits on a high ridge above the Paro Valley and commands breathtaking views across to Chomolhari.

During the succeeding 4 days of trekking, we climb above the tree-line and cross several passes. En route, we camp beside clear mountain lakes, visit yak herders encampments and enjoy splendid panoramas of the peaks on the border with Tibet, including Jitchu Drake and Gangkar Puensum. We visit the ever impressive Taktsang Monastery in the Paro Valley and to visit the Tashichho dzong at Thimpu.

itinerary.title: Day 01 : Arrival at Paro Airport. Overnight at hotel.
Day 02 : Day excursion from Paro to the Taktsang Monastery. Overnight at hotel.
Day 03 : Leave Paro trekking to Jele Dzong (Trek starts) Overnight at tented camp.
Day 04 : Trek from Jele Dzong to Jangchulakha. Overnight at tented camp.
Day 05 : Leave Jangchulakha and trek to Jimilang Tsho Overnight at tented camp.
Day 06 : Trek from Jimilang Tsho to Simkotra Overnight at tented camp.
Day 07 : Leaving Simkotra behind we trek through Phazoding onto Thimphu (finish trek) Overnight at hotel.
Day 08 : After a full day sightseeing in Thimphu we drive back to Paro. Overnight at hotel.
Day 09 : Transfer to international airport for your final departure.

overview:
Everest Base Camp Trek is an incredible journey in the beautiful Himalayan landscapes. This exciting trek package from Base Camp Adventure takes you through diverse landscapes. Trekkers will arrive at the base camp of the highest mountain peak in the world in just a few days.

Everest Base Camp is a stunning area with incredible mountains all around, including Mt. Everest (8848.86m). Trekkers can observe majestic mountain vista and wonderful natural surroundings. They will also get to observe the spectacular view of Mt. Ama Dablam, Lhotse, Nuptse, Khumbutse, Pumori, Cho Oyu, and other Himalayan mountains.

Moreover, this trek in the Everest region passes through rugged terrains and is moderately challenging. With some proper training and preparation, anyone can take this trek with ease. Tea houses along the trail will keep you warm and safe during the night. These teahouses are essential and provide standard facilities along the route. The incredible hospitality will make you fall in love with the place.

Besides that, trekkers will also have an opportunity to explore the cultural landscapes of this region. Various Buddhist landmarks along these trails include monasteries, chortens, and gompas. Travelers will pass through Sherpa settlements with Tibetan heritage. You can have a spiritual experience while trekking through the region.

After you book your trip, we will set up a meeting with you either at our office or a specified hotel. There you will get a complete briefing about this incredible trek journey. You can join a group of trekkers for this once-in-a-lifetime adventure in the Himalayas. We at Base Camp Adventure are providing this outstanding trek at a reasonable cost. Read on to know more about the Everest Base Camp trek group joining in detail.

Highlights of the Trip

  • Magical Himalayan sunrise from various viewpoints, including Kala Patthar.
  • Experiencing the incredible atmosphere of Everest Base Camp and other natural landscapes
  • Exploration of Namche Bazaar and its various cafes, bars, restaurants, souvenir shops of the region.
  • Scenic mountain flight with best Himalayan views to and from Lukla
  • The exploration of Tengboche monastery and its spiritual premises.
  • Trekking through incredible landscapes of Khumbu Icefalls and glaciers.
  • Cultural exploration of lifestyle, heritage, and tradition of the Sherpa community
  • The warm hospitality of local people

EBC Trek Altitude Chart

Everest Base Camp Trek Group Joining Route

Our trek journey starts as you take a scenic flight to Lukla from Kathmandu. Lukla is the gateway of the Mount Everest region. You will trek to Phakding from Lukla. From Phakding, you will trek to Namche Bazaar. The commercial town has many ancient Sherpa settlements, hotels, pubs, cafes, and others.

The culture, tradition, and heritage of Sherpas will enchant all travelers. After arriving at Tengboche, you can observe the ancient monastery of this region. Trekkers will pass through the settlements of Dingboche, Lobuche, Gorakshep. Finally, you will arrive at Everest Base Camp, which is our primary destination. This 360-degree panoramic view of the snow-capped mountains of the region will welcome you.

The trail goes uphill and downhill, passing through forests of rhododendron, juniper, and pine trees. Glaciers, glacial lakes, and green hills are another highlight of this trek. Travelers will travel to Kala Patthar (5,545 m), another incredible viewpoint for gorgeous Himalayan sunrises. You can observe Mt. Everest (8848.86m), Lhotse (8,414 m), Khumbutse (6,636 m), Pumori (7,161 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), Lingtren (6,749 m) and others.

After exploring the base camp area and taking incredible pictures of this region, you will return to Gorak Shep. Kala Pathar hike the next day is another challenging journey through rugged terrains. You will get majestic views of Mount Everest from Kalapathar. After Kala Pathar, you will return to Pheriche and pass through an earlier route of Namche Bazar and Phakding to Lukla. Finally, you will take a scenic mountain flight from Lukla to Kathmandu as your trip comes to an end.

You can Join 15 Days Everest Base Camp trek or Short Everest Base Camp trek.

Or, Send us your available days, we can customize the package for you.

Best Season for Everest Base Camp Trek Group Joining

The treks in the Everest region are perfect in peak seasons of Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November). These seasons are ideal for trekking in the area. There is stable weather with moderate temperatures in the Everest region, making it suitable for trekking.

Weather in Spring

Spring is generally considered perfect for trekking and hence is peak time for adventures. There is less precipitation in the foothills of the Himalayas, which makes it favorable for trekking. Moreover, moderate temperatures in the daytime and a serene environment are other advantages. Trekkers will pass through green hills, fast-flowing rivers, water streams, and beautiful landscapes. Overall, there is a tranquil environment in Spring in the Everest region.

Weather in Autumn

Autumn is a beautiful time for the EBC trek as there is an excellent daytime trekking environment. There is minimal precipitation and less challenges like floods, landslides, and avalanches. Besides, you can also go on a complete cultural exploration of this region.

There are many cultural festivals in this season, and the atmosphere remains quite lively. There are various cultural landmarks in the region, including monasteries and temples.

Offseason treks

Everest Base Camp in the off-season of winters and monsoons is also possible. However, they are pretty challenging as the weather remains unpredictable. There is extremely cold weather and heavy rainfall in these seasons. Hence, trekkers should pack well for this trip and train well for a safe and comfortable experience.

Difficulties of Everest Base Camp Trek

This Everest region is remote, with rugged and challenging terrains. Altitude sickness is quite a challenge in this high-altitude trek. Moreover, trekkers should acclimatize well during this trek with proper rest and hydration to trek with ease. Diamox tablets can also help you tackle altitude sickness along trails.

Moreover, trekkers will pass through the harsh terrains of these regions. The steep uphill trails are a challenge for even the most experienced of trekkers. Trekkers also need to train well with proper physical strength, endurance, and stamina. This trek has facilities of accommodation in teahouses.

These teahouses have basic facilities so you will have to compromise in this aspect. The food is also essential as ingredients need to get transported through porters or yaks along the trail. Everest Base Camp Trek is therefore difficult in these aspects. However, if you trek with proper packing and preparation, you can complete this trek. Read more at How difficult is EBC trek?

itinerary.html:

You can board your scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla from Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. It takes around 35-40 minutes to complete this journey. Lukla is the gateway of the Everest region with few hotels, teahouses, lodges, and others. After we finally arrive at Lukla airport, we will head to Phakding on our trekking journey.

You will trek along the left bank of Dudh Koshi River and then travel downhill to arrive at Phakding. You can get majestic views of mountains, including Kusum Kanguru (6,367 m), from the Phakding viewpoint. We will rest in the Phakding teahouse.

Namche Elevation: 3,450 m
Trek Duration: 6-7 hours

We will start our trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar alongside a rugged trail. Moreover, Namche Bazaar is a beautiful settlement of local Sherpa people. There are many cafes, restaurants, bars, shops, and others. It is the central trading hub of the Everest/Khumbu region.

You will pass along trails that are remote and rugged and then cross rivers through suspension bridges. Trekkers will pass through Monjo village (2,835 m) during their journey. They will then enter Sagarmatha National Park premises. You will pass the Dudh Koshi River through the suspension bridge before reaching Jorsalle.

From this point, we will climb uphill on the steep path to arrive at Namche Bazaar. You can observe the first view of Mt. Everest from this point along the trail. We will finally arrive at our destination of Namche Bazaar after trekking for a few hours, where we rest for the night at a lodge.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization at Namche Bazaar (3,440 meters).
itinerary.html:
Trekking at high altitude conditions is quite challenging as you will have to face altitude sickness along trails. Therefore, acclimatization is essential when it comes to high-altitude trekking. You will explore for some duration, even on acclimatization days. There are opportunities to hike to Sir Edmund Hillary foundation's Khunde Hospital.

From this Syangboche airstrip, you can observe Mt. Everest (8848.86m), Thamserku (6,608 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), Kusum Kanguru (6,367 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), and Ama Dablam (6,856 m). Trekkers can explore various points for an hour before returning to Namche. Besides that, you can also explore Namche, and it's beautiful cafes, restaurants, bars, souvenir shops, and others. We will return to our teahouse in Namche Bazaar in the evening and spend the night.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche (3,860 meters), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Tengboche Elevation: 3,865 m
Trek duration: 5-6 hours

After waking up early and having a delicious breakfast, we will begin our trek. We will pass through remote trails as we trek to Tengboche. You will walk alongside Dudh Koshi River, passing through various village settlements of the region. You can observe mountains through multiple viewpoints along the trail.

After crossing the Dudh Koshi River through the suspension bridge at PhunkeTenga (3,250 m), we will arrive at Tengboche. Tengboche is generally known for its ancient monastery and provides you with majestic views of Mt. Everest (8,848 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), AmaDablam (6,856 m), and others. Trekkers can observe monks and nuns busy in their daily lifestyles. You can also observe evening prayers and chants that will enchant you spiritually. You will stay in a teahouse in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche (4,410 meters), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Dingboche Elevation: 4,410 m
Trek duration: 5-6 hours

The trail on this day passes through rugged terrains along the descending path to Dingboche (4,410 m). We will cross Imja Khola and take an uphill climb to Pangboche village. This incredible village located just opposite Ama Dablam (6,856 m) provides you with majestic views of the Himalayas. You will get magical views of pine trees, Buddhist gompas, and mani walls.

From this point, you will climb uphill through dense juniper forests for around 2.5 hrs to arrive at Dingboche. We will rest and spend the night in the Dingboche teahouse.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization at Dingboche (4,410 meters).
itinerary.html:
Dingboche is another beautiful settlement where we will acclimatize for the second time. On this day, we will explore the region and go on small hikes. You can visit Nakartsang Gompa from where you can get an incredible view of Mt. Everest (8848) and other Himalayan mountains.

These mountains include Makalu (8,481 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), Baruntse (7,129 m), Mt. Ama Dablam (6,856 m), and Island Peak (6,189 m). You can also hike to Chhukhung to observe surrounding views of green hills, water streams, rivers, and others. We will rest and spend the night in Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche (4,940 meters), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Lobuche Elevation: 4,940 m
Trek Duration: 5-6 hours

The trek today starts from Dingboche and takes you to Lobuche. You can observe a panoramic view of mountains along the trail as you pass through various settlements, including Dughla. You will then climb the rocky glacial moraines on an uphill path.

You will pass through small Chortens or memorials dedicated to Sherpas who perished on their way to Mt Everest (8848.86 m). From here, you will climb towards a glacier to arrive at Lobuche, where you will spend the night at a teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche (4,940 meters) to Gorakshep (5,140 meters), then continue to Everest Base Camp (5,364 meters). After exploring the base camp, trek back to Gorakshep. 7–8 hours.
itinerary.html:
EBC Elevation: 5,364 m
Trek duration: 7-8 hours

You will start your trek from Lobuche, climbing uphill along rugged terrains. We will pass through various settlements before finally arriving at Gorak Shep, where we will rest and have lunch. Gorakshep is a beautiful sandbed and site of the original base camp to Mount Everest.

We will then trek to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m), which takes about three to four hours to arrive. The trails of this trek pass through many glaciers and rocks. You can observe majestic frozen lakes on your way to the Everest Base Camp.

After arriving at the base camp, you can watch a wide vista of the Himalayas plus other landscapes. You can take as many pictures of this region and then finally trek back to Gorakshep. You will spend the night at a local teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gorakshep to Kala Patthar (5,545 meters), then descend to Gorakshep before continuing to Pheriche (4,243 meters). 7–8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Pheriche Elevation: 4,371 m
Trek duration: 6-7 hrs

The trail on this day starts with a scenic early sunrise overlooking the snow-capped mountains of the region. We will then observe majestic views of the region's mountains as we trek to Kala Patthar (5,545 m). Kala Patthar trek is early in the morning in the dark. Therefore, it can get quite challenging, especially for first-time travelers.

From there, you can get a stunning view of Mt. Everest (8,848 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), Khumbutse (6,636 m), Pumori (7,161 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), Lingtren (6,749 m), and others. After arriving at Kala Patthar, you will get majestic views of snow-capped mountains, including the best views of Mount Everest. After taking pictures and exploring the region, we will return to Gorak Shep and then finally to Pheriche, where we will stay overnight.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar (3,440 meters), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Namche Elevation: 3,540 m
Trek Duration: 7-8 hrs

Today, you will start your trek through the juniper and rhododendron forests, where flowers bloom over hills in the Spring season. You will pass through Tengboche, where you will have your lunch and continue to Namche Bazaar.

We can observe majestic views of Lhotse (8,414 m) and Everest (8848.86 m) from here. You can take a hot shower and sleep overnight at a teahouse in Namche Bazaar. You can also explore the Namche Bazaar and take various souvenir items for your family back home.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2,860 meters), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Lukla Elevation: 2,840 m
Trek duration: 6-8 hours

This trail today starts from Namche Bazaar to Lukla as you pass through the rugged and remote terrains of the region. You can observe the incredible views and pass through steep and rocky terrain.

After crossing a suspension bridge over the Dudh Koshi River, we will continue our journey. On the same route, we will get a different perspective of the region. You will pass through pine forests and green hills as you can observe majestic snow-capped mountains of the region. We will rest for the night at a local teahouse or a lodge.

itinerary.title: Early morning flight from Lukla to Kathmandu (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html:
Flight Duration: 35-40 minutes

Our Everest Base Camp Trek group joining itinerary ends as you take an early morning flight back to Kathmandu. The incredible flight provides you with magical views of the snow-capped mountains. After arriving in Kathmandu, you can then proceed to your desired destination.

sections.title: Why Take This Everest Base Camp Trek Group Joining Tour?
sections.html:
Why Take This Everest Base Camp Trek Group Joining Tour?

Snow-capped mountain vista

This beautiful trek provides you with an opportunity to observe snow-capped Himalayan vista. There are various mountain views, including Mt. Everest (8848.86m), Nuptse (7,861 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), Lingtren (6,749 m), Khumbutse (6,636 m), Pumori (7,161 m), and others. Besides that, travelers can also observe other natural landmarks. These include green hills, mountain valleys, waterfalls, glaciers, lakes, and others. Hence, these beautiful mountain vista makes this EBC trek ideal for all travelers.

Exploration of rare and endangered wildlife

Trekkers can explore the region's beautiful landscapes and spot rare and endangered wildlife of the area. Moreover, these include Himalayan Tahr, snow leopard, red panda, danfe, and others during this trek. You can also explore various vegetation and medical herbs in this region. There are diverse trails that will provide you with a complete trekking adventure of the area.

Cultural exploration

You can also culturally explore these regions. There are many Buddhist monasteries, chortens, mani walls, and gompas. These Himalayan landmarks make this trip quite appealing. Besides that, if you travel in a particular season, you can also experience a festive atmosphere. Locals will celebrate their festivals and ancient traditions quite vibrantly. You can gel with locals and learn about their culture and heritage. These cultural exploration opportunities make this trek quite popular among trekkers.

Proper facilitated trail

This outstanding Everest base camp trail lies in a remote region. However, due to its popularity many teahouses, and lodges have recently opened on this trail. There are no fancy accommodations, but these local stays are standard and neat enough to spend your night warmly. Other meal facilities exist in hotels, restaurants, cafes, and others, especially in lower regions.

Safe and convenient tour

Our EBC trek team comprises highly experienced members and group leaders. Hence, you will have a safe and convenient journey. There are various safety protocols that we follow so that in case of an emergency, you will have swift and complete protection. First aid facilities are also available in case of any medical emergency. You can trek with ease in this Everest Base Camp trek group joining tour.

Essential Tips for Everest Base Camp Trek

  • Warm clothes and proper trekking gear are a must in this Himalayan trek.
  • Proper acclimatization is essential when it comes to high-altitude trekking in the region.
  • Delays and cancellations in flights are pretty common. Hence, you should add extra days to your trip if possible.
  • Carry snacks and drinking water along this trail. Water purification tablets and water bottles for clean drinking water are also essential
  • Hire professional guides and porters along this trail
  • Book your meal and accommodations in advance
  • Start trekking early so that you will reach your destination in time.
  • Sunburns are pretty common due to harsh sun rays reflecting from the silver mountains. Hence, you should carry sunscreens and sunblocks along this journey.
  • Get travel insurance coverage will remain safe and trek hassle-free along these trails.

Final Say

Everest Base Camp trek is a beautiful trek that leads you to the base camp of the highest mountain in the world. This outstanding trek provides you with magical views of the snow-capped mountains of the Everest region. Moreover, trekkers can complete this trek in a short amount of time. These trails pass through enchanted forests, diverse landscapes, rich wildlife, and other landmarks. Contact us at Base Camp Adventure for additional information on Everest Base Camp trek group joining tour.

Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche

overview:
Everest Base Camp is located in the Khumbu region of Solukhumbu district. Most trekkers trek on foot for several days to see Mount Everest up close and enjoy the adventure. But you don't need to trek for 2 weeks through the Khumbu to see Mount Everest. Helicopter tours are a thrilling way to explore the Himalayas for those who don't like trekking or are short on time. The Everest Base Camp Helicopter tour is a one-day aerial journey that offers a close look at the beautiful Himalayan ranges, valleys, and diverse landscapes and landmarks. Instead of walking a long uphill journey, travellers can enjoy aerial views of the mountains in a few hours.

Depending on the weather, air traffic, and helicopter availability, the whole experience takes around 3-4 hours. Travellers can see Mount Everest from the closest viewpoint, Kalapatthar, and capture and enjoy the moment. The Everest Base Camp helicopter tour will take you to Everest Base Camp at an altitude of 5,364 m or 17,598 ft, from where you can gaze upon the most mesmerising view of Mount Everest, Mount Lhotse, Mount Makalu, Mount Cho Oyu, Mount Nuptse, Mount Ama Dablam, and other peaks of the Himalayas.

The tour begins early in the morning in Kathmandu with a helicopter flight directly to Namche, landing near Hotel Everest View at an elevation of 3,440 m (11,286 ft). In Namche Bazaar, travellers have time to explore, enjoy the surroundings, and take in the mountain views before boarding the helicopter again. From the Hotel Everest View, the flight continues toward Kala Patthar, where the helicopter lands, and you can spend a short time enjoying a close view of Mount Everest and other peaks of the Himalayas. The return journey begins directly from Kala Patthar to Kathmandu. On the way back, it may land at Tenzing-Hillary Airport in Lukla for refuelling; it is considered one of the most challenging and thrilling airports because of its mountainous terrain.​

Travellers will reach the highest point at Kalapatthar, which lies at an elevation of 5,545 m (18,192 ft). Kalapatthar offers the best view of Mount Everest. From the helicopter, travellers can enjoy the views of the Khumbu Glacier, the Khumbu Icefall, and many snow-capped mountains. You can also see beautiful forests, river valleys, and Sherpa settlements built on mountain slopes, surrounded by green hills and deep valleys. Witnessing a wide aerial view of the UNESCO-listed World Heritage Site, Sagarmatha National Park, with its breathtaking mountains, glaciers, deep valleys, and beautiful landscape, is truly worth the experience.

Spring and Autumn are the most preferred seasons for Everest Base Camp Helicopter tours. These seasons offer clearer skies and drier weather, providing better visibility. Helicopter tours are best for those with limited time or who prefer not to walk but still want to enjoy panoramic views of Mount Everest and other Himalayan peaks. Although they offer the quickest way to experience the Khumbu region, flights depend heavily on weather conditions and visibility. Flight delays and route changes are possible during bad weather.
highlights: Experience the Everest region in a single day without trekking for almost 2 weeks through the Khumbu.
Enjoy thrilling helicopter journeys from Kathmandu while also seeing the changing landscape, deep valleys, and glaciers from the air.
Land in Namche Bazaar, where trekkers spend their acclimatisation day by exploring the area and enjoying the mountain views.
Continue the flight toward Kalapatthar, the highest viewpoint at 5,545 meters, to see Mount Everest.
Witness the four tallest Himalayan peaks above 8,000 meters, like Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu, and other Himalayan peaks.
See Everest Base Camp from the air, with its dramatic high-altitude landscape and the changing terrain of the Khumbu region.
Enjoy aerial views of Sagarmatha National Park and mesmerising views of mountains, glaciers, icefalls, valleys, and alpine landscapes.
Watch the landscape transform from lower green hills that grow beautiful rhododendrons and other flora to deep valleys, rocky alpine terrain, and glaciers.
Watch the Sherpa settlement in a high-altitude area built on mountain slopes surrounded by green hills and forests.
Experience the famous and thrilling Tenzing-Hillary Airport in Lukla, a possible refuelling stop.
Enjoy the iconic aerial photography opportunities of snowcapped mountains and glaciers from different angles during the flight.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu - Lukla – Pheriche-Everest Base Camp (EBC) (flyover) - Kala Patthar (flyover) - Hotel Everest View (landing for breakfast or drinks) - Lukla - Kathmandu.
itinerary.html:
Starting Point: Kathmandu (Tribhuvan International Airport)

The helicopter will land at Hotel Everest View, located at an altitude of 3,880 m (12,729 feet), one of the highest hotels in the world. Here, you can enjoy panoramic views of the Everest region and take some time to appreciate the stunning mountain scenery.

Fly Over Kala Patthar

After taking in the view at Hotel Everest View, the helicopter will head towards Kala Patthar, a famous viewpoint near Everest Base Camp. It offers one of the best 360-degree views of Mount Everest and surrounding peaks, including Lhotse, Nuptse, and Makalu. While you won’t land, the aerial view is awe-inspiring, offering unparalleled photo opportunities.

Fly Over Everest Base Camp

The helicopter will fly over the iconic Everest Base Camp, where climbers begin their journey toward the summit. While you won’t land here either (due to altitude restrictions and safety reasons), the aerial view of Base Camp and the Khumbu Icefall is still breathtaking.

Return Flight to Kathmandu

After exploring the Everest region from the sky, the helicopter will head back to Kathmandu, concluding your thrilling adventure.

Kathmandu to Hotel Everest View: 60-80 minutes
Hotel Everest View to Kala Patthar and Everest Base Camp fly over: 20-30 minutes
Return flight to Kathmandu: 60-80 minutes

sections.title: Does the Helicopter Land at Everest Base Camp?
sections.html:
Does the Helicopter Land at Everest Base Camp?

No, the Everest Base Camp Helicopter doesn’t land directly at Everest Base Camp; it flies over the base camp and Khumbu glaciers, allowing passengers to see the camp and surrounding landscape through the helicopter. It uses Kala Patthar or another approved high-altitude location for sightseeing, as the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN) forbids landings at the Everest Base camp.  

​At the high altitude of the EBC, landing is restricted because the camp sits on moving glacier terrain with no suitable landing space. At this altitude, thin air also reduces helicopter performance, making the landing and takeoff highly risky and challenging. So for better options the landing takes place in Kalapatthar (5,545 m).

Best time for One Day Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour

Choosing the right season for the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour is important because weather conditions affect both safety and the quality of the experience. Helicopters flying into the Everest region depend on conditions such as wind, weather, and visibility, especially around the high mountain valleys and landing area.

​Flying during the off-season can be dangerous because unfavourable weather can cause delays or cancellations. Temperature, rainfall, snow, cloud, and wind all affect flights and their schedules. Conditions change throughout the year; for example, autumn mornings can be cloudy and cold, and winter can bring harsh winds. Spring and autumn are the most popular and favoured seasons for the tour because of their weather conditions. The clouds are clear and mountain visibility is good, but the crowds can be heavy, so you must book your flight well in advance.

​Spring (March to May)

Spring (March-May) is a preferable and popular time for the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour. The weather warms after the cold winter, and the region offers good visibility and stable flying conditions. Rain might be occasional and could increase cloud cover towards late May.  Spring brings changes to the landscape view. Snow covers the peaks of the Himalayas, while the lowlands become greener and lusher, giving rhododendrons time to bloom across the hills and forests. The combination of snowy mountains and colourful valleys makes spring beautiful, especially from the air.  

​The main advantages of spring are good mountain visibility, stable weather, long daylight hours, and the region's beautiful scenery. Temperatures around Everest Base Camp and Kalapatthar range from -5 °C to 8 °C during the day and drop to -15 °C to 5 °C at night, with March being the coldest month. It is also the peak climbing season, so expedition activity in the Everest region may be more visible.  However, spring tours do come with some drawbacks, mainly because it's a popular travel season. The helicopter tours will be in high demand, and getting a ticket might take longer than usual. So the best option is to book in advance to avoid the crowd.

​Monsoon (June to August)

Monsoon (June-August) is one of the off-seasons for helicopter flights in the Everest region. Excessive rainfall makes the trails muddy and slippery, while cloudy weather and fog reduce visibility, disrupting helicopter tours. Heavy rain can also increase the risk of landslides and flash floods, which can delay flights. Despite this, the landscape becomes greener and lusher, with full rivers, forests, and fresh agriculture across Khumbu.

​The main advantages of the monsoon are fewer crowds due to lower demand, a peaceful atmosphere, and lower travel prices. Around the camp, daytime temperatures range from 10°C to 16°C (50°F to 61°F), while at night they can drop to 0°C to 6°C (32°F to 43°F). July is typically the wettest and cloudiest month, with rough weather. However, monsoon travel by helicopter requires extensive preparation because of flight delays, cancellations, challenging conditions, and changing weather. Travellers should allow extra days because delays and cancellations are more common than you might expect. Overall, the monsoon is a less favourable season for the tour, mainly because conditions are difficult to predict.

​Autumn (September to November)

Autumn (September-November) is one of the best and most popular seasons for helicopter tours to Everest Base Camp. After the monsoon, rainfall decreases and the weather starts stabilising, clearing the skies, and creating a perfect window for helicopter operations. Green hills, forests, and valleys are still fresh in September, and the vegetation slowly changes as the season moves towards November. Clear skies and clean air offer excellent views of the Himalayan peaks surrounding the Everest Region.

​This season is popular for its stable weather, excellent visibility, comfortable trekking conditions, and reliable flight forecasts. Temperatures also remain warmer at lower elevations and colder at higher elevations towards the camp. Daytime temperatures range from 5°C to 12°C (41°F to 54°F), while nighttime temperatures can drop to around -5°C to -15°C (23°F to 5°F). Autumn is also the busiest trekking season, and popular routes can get crowded, especially in October. Accommodations and helicopter tours are in high demand, so you must book in advance.

​Winter (December to February)

Winter (December-February) is one of the off-seasons for helicopter tours in the Everest region. The main reason is that, as it becomes extremely cold and there is snow and ice, flying conditions become difficult. Cloudy weather, snowfall, and strong winds can reduce visibility and obstruct helicopter tours. At high elevations, trekkers and passengers face significant risks of hypothermia, frostbite, and avalanches. Daytime temperatures range from -5°C to 5°C (23°F to 41°F), and they can drop to around -15°C to -25°C (5°F to -13°F) at night.

​The main advantage of winter is the smaller crowds and easy access to helicopters. Lower demand can also reduce total costs and increase the availability of good helicopter services. A winter helicopter tour is possible; however, extra preparation is important. Although clear winter days can still

Food in Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour

Although the journey is shorter than the trek to the camp, food is still an important part of the tour. The helicopter reaches high altitude very quickly, so eating a proper meal and being hydrated will help you stay comfortable during the trip. Food depends on the package you choose; you might have breakfast before departure, at the landing stop, or after you return. The food variety includes a mix of Nepali, Tibetan, and Western dishes.

What Foods are Available on the Everest Base Camp Heli Tour?

The available food depends on the stops. Kathmandu has the biggest selection, and choices will be limited as you move into the higher Everest region. If your tour includes a meal at a lodge or hotel, the menu depends on them and weather conditions. Some packages include breakfast, and extra snacks will cost extra, so check what is included before you book.

Are there vegetarian options?

In the Everest region, it is better to stick to a vegetarian diet since meat takes longer to digest and requires more energy to burn. Also, meat products are stored and might not be fresh on the trail, raising food-hygiene concerns. So, many vegetarian options are available during the trek, and the place provides meat-free meals. Most vegetarian choices include dal bhat with veggies, curry, noodles, pasta, soup, potatoes and fried rice, pancakes, porridge, and breads.

In case of diet restrictions (eg: allergies, diary/glute free food), you should first consult with the authority of Base Camp Adventure. Your guide will help you inform the accommodation about the requirements and cater to your needs accordingly.

Other Locations to Start the 1-Day Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour

1. Everest Helicopter Tour from Lukla

This helicopter tour starts after reaching Lukla at 2,860 m From here, the helicopter flies through the Khumbu, passing above Namche, Tengboche, Pangboche, Pheriche, and Gorak Shep, then lands at Kalapatthar. The flight from Lukla to Kala Patthar takes 20-25 minutes. After sightseeing, the helicopter follows the same route for return.

2. Everest Helicopter Tour from Phakding

For the Everest Helicopter Tour from Phakding, you reach Lukla and have to trek to Phakding, and instead of continuing the trek, you get to board a helicopter and fly through Khumbu towards the EBC area. The flight continues to Kala Patthar for the main landing,, where you can experience the mountain view; Afterward, you return to Kathmandu according to the flight itinerary.

3. Everest Helicopter Tour from Namche

For this tour, you will trek to Namche via the Phakding route and won't have to spend more days trekking. From Namche, the helicopter flies to the upper Everest in 15 minutes, passes through the camp area, and lands at Kala Patthar for sightseeing. After the visit, you can fly back to your arranged return destination.

4. Everest Helicopter Tour from Tengboche

After multiple days of walking and trekking to reach Tengboche, you can board the helicopter and quickly fly over the higher Khumbu passing settlements and Himalayan views you get to enjoy from a different perspective. The trip includes landing on Kala Patthar to enjoy the view of different mountains and concludes with the return.

5. Everest Helicopter Tour from Pangboche

The tour from Pangboche starts after trekking far into the Khumbu at 3,900 m From the village, the helicopter quickly reaches the higher Everest region, which saves several days of trekking. The chopper flies around the base camp and lands at Kala Patthar, where you can enjoy close-up views of Everest and the surrounding peaks before flying back to your destination.

Everest Helicopter Tour from Kathmandu VS Lukla

Kathmandu and Lukla can be the starting point for an Everest Helicopter Tour, depending on the package, but the overall experience differs.

Who is the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour Suitable for?

The tour suits travellers who want to experience the Everest Region without harsh trekking.

  1. Travellers with limited time: The tour is ideal for visitors with only a few days in Nepal; instead of trekking for 2 weeks, you can experience the Everest region in a single day.
  2. ​Families: Families who don't want to, or are unable to, take on the challenge of a long and physically difficult trek may find the helicopter tour more practical. However, parents should still be aware of the effects of the altitude, mainly if they are travelling with children.
  3. Older travellers: Older travellers who are healthy but don't want to torture their bodies with the trek, yet still want to experience Everest, prefer this tour. Anyone with medical conditions must consult a doctor before travelling.
  4. Travellers who do not want a multi-day trek: Not everyone wants to spend days walking and staying in basic accommodation; this tour offers an easier way to see the high region without doing the full trek.
  5. Photographers: The flight is suitable for photographers because it offers beautiful views of multiple mountains, glaciers and settlements. The changing perspective from the helicopter offers opportunities you won't see from the trekking trail.
  6. First-time Nepal Visitors: For first-time visitors to Nepal, the helicopter tour offers a quick, solid introduction to the Himalayas and Everest. It's a good option for those who want to include Everest in their itinerary without spending their entire trip on one trek.

​How Difficult is Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour?

The Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour is physically easier than trekking to EBC because most of the journey is by air and requires little walking. The tour still involves high altitude, cold weather, and exposure to thin air, so it shouldn’t be treated as completely effortless.

  • High altitude: Altitude is the main challenge on this tour, as the helicopter reaches above 5,000 m quickly, giving the body little to no time to adjust. At this height, breathing can feel harder, and some people may experience headaches, dizziness, nausea, tiredness, or shortness of breath, which is why landing time is short.
  • Low oxygen level: The oxygen available to the body decreases as altitude increases. Even simple activities like walking a short distance and moving around at the landing point will feel tiring. Move slowly and avoid unnecessary physical exertion at altitude.
  • Cold temperature: Temperatures at Everest Base Camp are already cold and can be colder during early morning flights and in winter. Wind at high-altitude landing points like Kalapatthar can make it feel even colder, so carry warm layers, gloves, a windproof jacket, and a warm cap, even if you're only outside the helicopter briefly.
  • Unstable weather: Weather changes quickly in the mountains and directly affects helicopter operations. Strong winds, snowfall, rain, clouds, and poor visibility can delay, change, or cancel the flight. Even during peak seasons, the final decision will depend on the weather.

How to Prepare for Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour?

This tour doesn’t require the same physical preparation needed for the full trek, but you should still prepare properly before flying into the high Everest region. The helicopter gains altitude quickly, taking you from Kathmandu to elevations above 5,000 m in a short time, so low oxygen, altitude, cold temperatures, and weather changes are bigger concerns than your physical endurance. To have a good, comfortable experience, you need to understand what to expect and how to handle it.

1. Prepare for Altitude

High altitude during the tour is the main concern because your body will not get enough time to adjust. Physical fitness alone will not prevent altitude sickness, and even healthy travellers can experience tiredness, headache, dizziness and nausea. Move slowly during stops and avoid unnecessary physical activity; if you experience symptoms, inform your guide immediately.

2. Stay Hydrated and Eat Properly

Drink enough water before and during the trip because dehydration at altitude makes it worse. Have a nutritious meal before departure instead of flying on an empty stomach, and avoid alcohol before flights because it will cause dehydration and raise altitude concerns.

3. Proper Clothing

Even if Kathmandu feels warm, the Everest region won’t be welcoming you warmly; the conditions there can be very cold. Wear clothes in layers so you can adjust as temperatures change. A warm insulated jacket, thermal layers, warm socks, gloves, hat and comfortable shoes are useful during the high-altitude landing.

4. Check Your Health

People with lung conditions, high blood pressure, heart disease or other medical concerns should discuss this with a professional before booking the tour. The rapid elevation change can worsen symptoms, so it is important to understand any personal health limitations before travelling.

5. Be Mentally Prepared

The flight is physically easy, but flying between the mountains and landing at high altitude can feel intense, especially for first-time visitors. Learn about the route, landing stops, altitude, and safety instructions before departure, because knowing what to expect helps you stay calm and fully enjoy the experience.

Why Go on the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour?

The Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour is a good option for travellers who want to experience the Everest region without spending many days trekking. It gives you the chance to fly over and see some of the world's highest mountains and reach high altitudes within a short time. Here are a few reasons to go on the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour:

  • Save time: A normal Everest Base Camp trek takes many days, while a helicopter tour can cover the main region within a day. For visitors with a short stay in Nepal who still want to see Everest, this tour is ideal.
  • ​Avoid long trekking days: The helicopter tour means you don't have to walk and trek for 6-8 hours every day. It's much easier than the full trek, but the high altitude can still be challenging.
  • ​Aerial View of Mountains: The biggest reason to choose the tour is the view. On a clear day, the flight provides a completely different perspective of Mount Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, glaciers, valleys, rivers and Sherpa settlements. This perspective is a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
  • Everest View Hotel: Many tours include a landing stop here because it is a good place for a short break, breakfast or drinks, and to wide mountain views before continuing the flight. The hotel offers views of Everest, Ama Dablam, Lhotse, and other peaks.
  • ​Kalapatthar Landing: Kalapatthar is one of the region's best-known viewpoints, offering a clear view of Mount Everest; people say it’s clearer than from Base Camp itself.
  • ​View of Khumbu Glacier and Khumbu Icefall: The helicopter flight offers an aerial view of the Khumbu Glacier and Khumbu Icefall, the most majestic features of the Everest region. From the flight, you can see huge glaciers and broken sections of ice that would be difficult to admire from the trail.
  • Photography: This tour gives photography enthusiasts opportunities for mountain photography. From the air, you can capture Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, glaciers, valleys and settlements- something you can't do when on foot.

Permits for Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour

The tour requires permission to enter the protected Everest region, mainly to land inside the Khumbu. The two main permits are for landing: the Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality permit and the Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit. Tour companies arrange these permits before the flight, so passengers do not need to visit and obtain them.

Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit

The Everest region falls under the Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality, which collects a tourism fee from visitors entering the area. The fee is currently:

  • NRS 3,000 for countries outside SAARC
  • NRS 2,000 for SAARC and Chinese visitors.

The municipality requires a passport and a recent photograph for this permit. For the helicopter tour, the company will arrange this as part of the flight preparation. Check whether the permit fee is already included or if you have to pay for it separately.

Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit

Most of the region is inside the Sagarmatha National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, so visitors entering this park need a national park permit. The entry fee is:

  • NRS 3,000 per person
  • NRS 1,500 for SAARC nationals
  • NRS 100 for Nepali citizens.  

For trekkers, the permit is available in Kathmandu or at the park entrance., For helicopter tours, the agency handles it before departure.

Note: A representative from Base Camp Adventure will obtain the permit on your behalf after the booking confirmation or upon your arrival in Kathmandu.

Altitude Sickness During Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour

Since you spend a short time in Kalapatthar (5,545 m), the chances of sickness are very low. For passengers on the Everest Base Camp Heli Tour, altitude sickness won't be a concern if you spend a short time and return immediately. However, the helicopter takes you from Kathmandu to elevations above 5,000 m in a short time. In that sense, if you spend a long time in Kalapatthar, you will get altitude sickness. So, to understand it better, you need to know what it is.

What is Altitude Sickness?

When your body fails to adapt to the low oxygen level that exists at high altitude, you will be susceptible to altitude sickness or Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS). The risk of altitude sickness rises once you are well above 3,000 m

Common Symptoms of Altitude Sickness

Some common early symptoms of altitude sickness are:

  • Headache
  • Dizziness
  • Nausea
  • Loss of appetite
  • Shortness of breath
  • Tiredness
  • Difficulty sleeping
  • Vomiting
  • Weakness

Mild symptoms can appear soon after reaching a high landing point. Don't ignore them, especially if they worsen or other symptoms develop. Since the helicopter tour reaches altitude quickly, passengers should immediately tell their guide or pilot if they begin to feel unwell.

Based on your schedule, you will spend only a short time in Kalapatthar, so altitude sickness and its symptoms are minimal. However, to be on the safe side, it is better to understand its causes and symptoms.

Weight Limit for EBC Helicopter Tour

The weight limit for the Everest Base Camp helicopter tour is around 500 kgs (1,102 lbs). Helicopter ride also depends on the weight of the person. Every helicopter may have a different weight limit. The maximum number in a helicopter is 5 people.

Safety tips for Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour

  • Fasten your seat belt, it may be a scary ride.
  • Smoking is not allowed on the flight, be careful.
  • Don’t stand or change your seat during the flight.
  • Some time Pilot needs to rearrange the helicopter position, so wait for the operator call.

Conclusion

The Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour is the fastest and easiest way to experience Everest without long days of trekking. In a short time, you can fly through Khumbu, see Everest and other peaks as well as the Khumbu glaciers and icefall from the air.

​This tour is great for travellers with limited time, families, older travellers, photographers, and people who don't like trekking. The cold temperatures, altitude and weather still need to be taken seriously, and everyone should understand that flight plans can change depending on visibility and mountain conditions. When properly prepared with everything needed and a structured itinerary, the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour is a convenient way to see the world's highest mountain and one of its most famous mountain regions. So, contact Base Camp Adventure for your first Everest Helicopter Tour.

faqs.q: Can I trek to Everest Base Camp and still get a flight from Kala Patthar?
faqs.a: Of course, you can get a flight on a return from Everest Base Camp despite having trekked. In fact, you can get a pick up in the charter from any feasible places and your convenience. Just make sure to book the flight and we’ll get you as per your instruction.

faqs.q: Can I have the helicopter stay a bit longer at Everest Base Camp?
faqs.a: You may not want the helicopter to stay much longer in the Everest base camp as it’s menacing. Because of the high altitude and low oxygen level, it’s not safe for heli to stop over more than 2 minutes. Hence, it’s the most time that we can get on the delayed flight.

faqs.q: Is oxygen available during the flight?
faqs.a: No need to get anxious over the availability of oxygen during the flight. As we help all our clientele struggling with altitude sickness by providing oxygen. Not to forget to notify us before the flight boards.

faqs.q: What is so best about Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour?
faqs.a:
Trekking may be the ultimate way for an in-depth exploration of the secluded region of the Himalayas. Yet, not everyone can withstand the extremity and severe weather of the Everest region.

So for those, the helicopter tour to the Everest Base Camp comes as a rescue. It’s most relevant for the trekkers who can’t hike after reaching a certain altitude. Flying over the sky of Himalayas offers you a scenic view of Everest, cultural sites and topography.

faqs.q: Does Helicopter fly over Mount Everest?
faqs.a: Flying over Everest is not viable for any helicopter. As you scale up from the base camp, the air gets thinner, causing the helicopter to lose balance. Therefore, almost every helicopter takes down at the base camp.

faqs.q: For how long the helicopter put up at Syangboche?
faqs.a: On the way around from Everest Base Camp, the helicopter stays at Syangboche for about 30 minutes. This is the utmost time you get to have breakfast at the Everest view hotel. You can ply the spare time sightseeing the villages and mesmerizing monasteries.

faqs.q: Who leads the trip to the Everest Base Camp?
faqs.a:
Not to worry as you’re in the hands of the country’s best flyer, who’re experts in their field. They are well-trained, professional and have been doing the job for years.

Henceforth, they’re clear about what they’re doing. They make it sure not to pull down the natural beauty of the region.

faqs.q: What is the highest altitude a helicopter has traveled so far?
faqs.a: The last helicopter that had ascended till the summit of 8,848 m was Eurocopter AS350 Squirrel. The single-engine light helicopter had touched down the summit of Mt. Everest. Didier Delsalle, a fighter pilot was the one who flew the helicopter. Onwards, the name of this French native was listed in the Guinness World Record.

faqs.q: How will the crew members in-flight see medical emergencies?
faqs.a: All our ground staff including pilots are trained under different circumstances. They have strong medical knowledge and know-how to work in such situations. We have a first aid kit available anytime and can even evacuate the patient in case of an emergency.

faqs.q: Does the flight have food and drink service?
faqs.a: Unfortunately, we don’t have a service of food and drink on the flight. Instead, we’ll help you find a quality hotel at Syangboche where you can get delicious food. The hotel at Syangboche will accord you with the sublime beauty of Mt. Everest.

faqs.q: Will I fly to the top of Everest?
faqs.a: No. You will only fly to the base camp of the tallest mountain not the top of it.

faqs.q: Can we stop longer in all the places?
faqs.a: Yes, we can add a few more minutes as per your request but we cannot hold it for long. The high altitude makes it difficult for us to hold the helicopter for long.

faqs.q: Can I go around the places nearby?
faqs.a: Of course, you can go around and explore the area. But remember that we are not staying in any area for a long time and therefore you have to be quick!

faqs.q: Can I get a discount on the trip?
faqs.a: We offer this trip at a very reasonable price. If you come to a large group, we will offer you a discount as per our company rules.

faqs.q: How can I book for the trip?
faqs.a: You can contact us via phone or email us. You need to send your full name and preferred date. It is advised to pay for your trip beforehand to confirm your seats.

overview:
Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel is one of the wondrous ways to explore the beauty of the most popular trekking destination in the Himalayas. This Everest Base Camp helicopter touring prospect will let you enjoy an immersive journey in the easter Himalayas, which is popular as the home of the tallest mountain peak in the world, Mt. Everest (8,848.86 meters). This helicopter tour is undoubtedly an iconic experience, which offers you the opportunity to explore and enjoy the beauty of the Everest region within a single day. As this short and sweet exploration is a comfortable seated journey, anyone who has dreamed of venturing into the Everest region but has not been able to do so due to the physical demands of the trail or the long duration of the trek can happily partake in it. This aerial exploration starts from Kathmandu and after reaching Lukla, you will slowly hover over the mainstream route heading toward the main objective. You will also have the opportunity to soak in the pristine atmosphere of the Himalayas as the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel also has landing options. So, it will be a truly immersive journey to relish the magnificence of the Everest region, skipping the physically demanding parts of the trail.

Best Time for Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour

As for the helicopter flights to operate smoothly without any hurdles, the peak seasons like autumn (September to November) and spring (March to May) are the top picks. During these seasons, the weather in Nepal is very stable and you will not need to deal with any challenging weather factors during your Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel in these seasons. As for the helicopter to operate smoothly, the wind, visibility, and temperatures need to be at an optimum level. During the off-season, such as monsoon (June to August) and winter (December to February), these factors are not stable, which can put the flight operation at risk. Thus, for the most remarkable and hassle-free experience, you should consider doing this helicopter tour during one of the high seasons. If you are taking part in the exploration of the Himalayan region during the springtime, you will be enchanted with stunning visuals. The landscape of the country is covered with emeralds of green and colorful flowers. So, enjoying the aerial views of such diverse and spectacular landscapes is a magical experience. The shades of grey, crimson, brown, and yellow of the fall season are also captivating as they show the beauty of the Himalayas in different colors.
