itinerary.title: Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Kalapatthar
itinerary.html:
Kathmandu to Lukla Flight

Kathmandu Altitude: 1,400 m

Lukla Altitude: 2,840 m

Altitude Gain: 1,440 m

You will get started on your Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel with a morning flight. Our representative will receive you from your hotel and take you to the flight-designated area. After the whole team and flying crew are ready, you will then gradually hover over the heart of Kathmandu and, flying over the colorful settlements, you will head toward the hills. After leaving the bowl of valleys, you will fly over the lush hills and other deep valleys, slowly heading toward the Himalayan region.

During this flight, you will have the chance to enjoy the aerial views of the pristine Himalayas, and as you get closer to your destination, the view of the eastern Himalayan peaks gets even more grandeur. It will take you around 40 minutes to reach Lukla from Kathmandu. After reaching the vibrant Sherpa town, you will not get started immediately with a follow-up flight. Your helicopter will fuel at Lukla for the journey up ahead, which will take around 10 minutes. During this time, you can stretch yourself and enjoy the serene atmosphere of this popular Sherpa town.

Flight Duration: 40 minutes

Flight Distance: 136.17 km

Lukla to Everest Base Camp Flight

Everest Base Camp Altitude: 5,364 m

Altitude Gain: 2,524 m

After your helicopter finishes fueling up for the journey from Lukla, you will head directly toward the main objective of this helicopter tour. Your helicopter will fly over the major highlights of this mainstream route and during the peak seasons, you will see the trekkers slowly navigating on the trail. From Lukla, your helicopter will fly over Phakding, Monjo, Namche Bazaar, Tengboche, Dingboche, Lobuche, and Gorakshep to reach Kala Patthar for landing and  Everest Base Camp.

This is the most exciting part of this helicopter flight, and you will be able to enjoy the spectacular Himalayan scenery as you head toward the foothills of the towering peaks in the eastern Himalayan region. But that’s not all; the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel package of Base Camp Adventure will also make a touchdown at the most popular base camp in the world. You will get some time to relish and explore the magnificent surroundings beneath the grandest peak on the planet.

Flight Duration: 30 minutes

Flight Distance: 38.8 km

Kala Patthar Altitude: 5,644 m

Altitude Gain: 280 meters/ 918 feet

You will board back to your helicopter after completing the exploration of the Everest Base Camp. For the next part of the journey, you will head toward the most popular and iconic viewpoint in the Khumbu Valley. This viewpoint is a trekker’s favorite for enjoying the epic sunrise views and the panoramic views of the surrounding peaks. From Kala Patthar, you will be able to enjoy wide views of Everest, Nuptse, Changtse, Pumori, and other surrounding peaks. You will take your time to enjoy the magical Himalayan views from Kala Patthar, and after soaking in the magical atmosphere, your tour will commence toward the returning part.

Flight Duration: 12 minutes

Flight Distance: 10.6 km

Flight From Kala Patthar to Everest View Hotel, Syangboche

Everest View Hotel Altitude: 3,962 m

Altitude Loss: 1,682 m

After enjoying the iconic views of the Himalayan massifs from Kala Patthar, your helicopter tour will then lead you toward the next major attraction of this trip, Everest View Hotel. This is the highest-placed hotel on earth, and you will enjoy your warm breakfast here after completing your incredible Himalayan tour. This is one of the most popular acclimatization hike destinations during the standard Everest Base Camp Trek. From this high-altitude hotel, you will be able to enjoy the wide vistas of Everest, Lhotse, Ama Dablam, Taboche, Thamerku, and others.

So, you will be enjoying your breakfast in a magical setting with sparkling views of the pristine peaks on the backdrop. After your lunch, you will relax here for a bit, enjoying the epic scenery, and then continue descending toward the next point of your Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel.

Flight Duration: 45 minutes

Flight Distance: 21.7 km

Everest View Hotel to Lukla

Lukla Altitude: 2,840 m

Altitude Loss: 1,122 m

Flying over the mainstream trek route of the region, you will make your return to Lukla. Like during the start of the tour, you will take a short break here as your helicopter refuels for the journey back home. Landing at the mainstream trekking region in the Himalayas one more time, you will bid farewell to it and then fly back to Kathmandu. You will get around a 10-minute break here, and you can check out the views and vibrant town before parting ways with it.

Flight Duration: 7 to 11 minutes

Flight Distance: 14 km

Fly Back From Lukla to Kathmandu

Kathmandu Altitude: 1,400 m

Altitude Loss: 1,440 m

Your journey back to the capital valley is also quite immersive; you will fly over the thick green hills, beautiful valley, cascading rivers, and widely spread settlements before making your touchdown. You will be able to relish the true diversity of landscapes during this flight back, and with a heart full of memories, you will step out of the helicopter.

Base Camp Adventure will arrange a transport facility to drop you back at your hotel. After getting some rest, you can then continue with the itinerary plans, as you will have the rest of the day to explore this vibrant capital city.

Flight Duration: 40 minutes

Flight Distance: 136.17 km

sections.title: Useful Info
sections.html:
Who Can Do Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel?

One of the most loveable things about this iconic Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel is that anyone can do it. As only exceptional professionals can climb the tallest peak in the world, and even the journey to its base camp is a physically challenging endeavor, both of these adventures require a good level of fitness and preparation. Similarly, the overall duration of the exploration can be too long for general travelers who don’t have enough vacation. Thus, if you were ever wondering about a short journey that doesn’t require weeks-long training to match the physical demands of the trail, this Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour is your answer. You will be enjoying this thrilling journey from the comfort level of your couch. There isn’t any physically demanding section that you will have to overcome during this journey, nor will you need to spend a long period to get to the most popular base camp in the world.

What Makes This Helicopter Tour Special?

Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel is a wonderful and luxurious experience to explore the magical ambiance of the eastern Himalayan region that houses the tallest peak in the world, Mt. Everest. If you are wondering what makes this trip distinct and exciting from other general exploration options in the region, the overall experience takes the first spot. This is the most incredible option available to explore the Everest region with a completely luxurious experience. You will not need to take on the physically demanding and long trekking route like the regular trekking journey. You will be able to enjoy the experience in a comfortable and cozy environment with a comfort level that is similar to the luxury of your home. As this is just a one-day itinerary plan for an incredible Himalayan experience, pretty much anyone, even travelers who are on a short vacation, can enjoy this trip. Furthermore, there isn’t any kind of age restriction on this Everest heli tour, so it is a perfect adventure if you are looking forward to spending quality time with your friends and family. However, the best part of this helicopter tour is still the view, the incredible bird-eye view of the majestic Himalayan ranges, which will be a fond memory that you will treasure forever. Even the mountaineers cannot relish the breathtaking aerial views of the sparkling Himalayan peaks that this helicopter tour offers.

Altitude Sickness

Naturally, as this is a high-altitude journey in the Himalayas, you may be concerned about the risk of altitude sickness during your Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel. You will start your journey from Kathmandu and make your landing at the starting point for adventures in the Everest region, Lukla (2,840 m). The flight gradually takes you across other high-elevation points in the region, like Everest Base Camp (5,364 m), Kala Patthar (5,644 m), and Everest View Hotel (3,962 m). Thus, there is a need for proper acclimatization while doing the trek following the general route. However, as you will only spend a few minutes at the high-altitude points of the trek, you will not need to worry about the risk of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS). You will spend around 10-15 minutes at the landing zones at the foothills of Everest, and the breakfast point in this helicopter tour, Everest View Hotel, doesn’t have any risk of altitude sickness. However, you will still need to follow the proper precautionary methods in order to not risk altitude sickness. For this Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel, drinking enough fluids and keeping yourself warm at the higher region will be sufficient to keep the inconveniences caused by altitude sickness. Base Camp Adventure will also arrange supplementary oxygen if you feel like you need it. So, you can enjoy this iconic journey with us without the need to worry about anything.

Packing for Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel

During your Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel, you will get the opportunity to experience the diverse regions of the country and the climatic conditions of each zone. So, in total, you will traverse across six climatic zones, from the starting point, Kathmandu to the highest point of the entire helicopter tour, Kala Patthar. Light layers will be quite sufficient for the exploration part at the lower region, i.e., Lukla, where the temperature is warmer if you are doing this trek in one of the peak seasons. However, at the very top level of the region, i.e. alpine zone (4,000- 5,000 m) and trans-Himalayan zone (above 5,000 m), the temperatures are generally cold and chilly. So, to keep yourself warm during those regions, you will need to bring warm and heavy layers. The most efficient way to pack for this Everest heli tour is to practice the layer system; wear light layers for the lower regions and warm-insulated as an outer layer for the alpine zone and above. As for the other packing items for this one-day itinerary exploration, you can include sanitary, personal hygiene items, a powerbank, snacks, electrolytes, etc.

Permits for Helicopter Tour

Although this is a one-day itinerary plan for exploration in the Everest region, and you may feel like you will not need permits for this short exploration, it isn’t like that. Despite being short, this Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel explores some of the major parts of the region. Thus, you will need the necessary permits to explore the region, even if it is just an aerial adventure. Here are the permits that you will need to acquire for the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour.
  • Sagarmatha National Park Permit
  • Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit
The Sagarmatha National Park Permit can be obtained from the office of the Tourism Board in Kathmandu and it costs around US$ 30. However, the Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit is only issued in Lukla. So, you will have to get it after reaching Lukla, and the cost for this permit is around US$ 20. In order to ensure a seamless journey and to avoid the need for going through the paperwork hassles, Base Camp Adventure will obtain all the required permits for this helicopter tour on your behalf.

Other Flight Options for Helicopter Tour With Base Camp Adventure

Besides this thrilling Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel prospects, Base Camp Adventure also offers other options for you to enjoy the incredible aerial experience during your adventure in the Everest region. With these options, you will be able to enjoy this thrilling helicopter tour from different points in the Everest region.

Lukla to Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour and Return to Kathmandu

If you have completed your adventure in the Everest region and want to add the fascinating aerial exploration experience to your adventure from the very starting point, this flight option from Lukla is an ideal option for you. You will follow the itinerary plans like the standard Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel and return back to Kathmandu skipping the Lukla to Kathmandu plane flight.

Namche Bazaar to Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour and Return to Kathmandu

Namche Bazaar is a famous acclimatization destination in the Everest region. Base Camp Adventure also operates the Everest heli tour flight from this acclimatization destination for the convenience of the trekkers in the region. You will hover over from Namche and move along the mainstream route to explore Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar before returning back to Kathmandu via Lukla.

Tengboche to Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour and Return to Kathmandu

Tengboche, which is more famously known as the spiritual hub of the Everest region is another popular point to get started with this helicopter tour. Generally, the Everest Paranoma Trek, one of the most popular mild forms of exploration in the Everest region, takes you upto Tengboche only. Thus, the Everest Base Camp Helicopter tour from this point is a great way to pull the curtain to your iconic Himalayan exploration.

Pangboche to Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour and Return to Kathmandu

The Pangboche village in Khumbu is one of the most fascinating traditional villages of the region that is rich in culture, Sherpa architecture and stunning scenery. This is another popular operating point for our Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour; you will fly to the base of the tallest mountain in the world and follow the return journey back to Kathmandu via Lukla.

Pheriche Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour and Return to Kathmandu

Pheriche Village, one of the high-altitude villages in the Everest region and a popular acclimatization destination, is another ideal destination to get started with this aerial exploration. Pheriche is generally used as the landing destination for shuttle flight to Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar. So, it is a perfect place to enjoy this magical experience after completing your base camp adventure.

Everest Base Camp to Lukla via Helicopter and Return to Kathmandu

The physical demand of Everest Base Camp Trek route can be very demanding for trekkers who are not in their prime, both physically and age-wise. Thus, after taking on the thrilling journey all the way to base camp to relish the breathtaking ambiance, for the return journey, you will not need to retrace your steps on the same route with this option. After enjoying the aerial flight from the base camp, you will make your return back to Kathmandu via Lukla skipping the physical demands of the return trek journey all the way to Lukla. **Note: All of these helicopter tour options for Everest Base Camp follow a similar itinerary plan to our standard Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour With Landing at Everest View Hotel. There is an optional landing option for Kalapatthar and Everest Base Camp, or you can just enjoy the flyover. The return route will follow the first flight back to Lukla, and after refueling, you will then head toward Kathmandu**

overview:
Who doesn’t enjoy a quiet walk into the wild, surrounded by exceptional views, diverse landscapes, and lofty mountains? Avid trekkers surely enjoy it the most, particularly when they get to witness the raw beauty of Mt. Everest, rocky hills, and frozen lakes.

Visitors who maneuver the classic trail of Khumbu will be delighted to experience the unreal tranquility, scenic hikes, and geological wonders. Significant landmarks, ancient pilgrimages, and monasteries make the walk more exciting and whole as trekkers will get to know people’s unique culture, traditions, and lifestyle in the Himalayas.

Everest Base Camp Luxury Lodge Trek turns a long and challenging walk into an unforgettable adventure. It unfolds the scenic beauty of Khumbu and makes them visit many picturesque sites and hidden places. In addition, the hike provides trekkers an impressive view of lush meadows, steep valleys, pristine mountain lakes, and alluring villages.

Everest Base Camp is almost 144km far from Kathmandu in north-eastern Nepal. It’s just beneath the Khumbu Glacier at 17,598 ft, between towering mountains, steep rocks, and icefalls.

The trek kicks off with an uphill walk to Phakding after flying to the beautiful town of Lukla. It then makes its way from Dudh Koshi River Valley below and ascends a steep trail heading to Namche. Trekkers walk through pine and rhododendron forest before entering the Sagarmatha National Park and crossing suspension bridges.

It passes several remote villages like Dingboche and Lobuche to reach the Everest Base Camp. Up to this point, the trail is rugged but not as hard as the one leading to base camp. Trekkers will have to climb steep hills and walk from the edge of the valley to arrive at the small settlement.

The trail running from Gorakshep to Everest Base Camp is composed of dirt and loose rocks with a few steep sections. This may cause hikers to feel little discomfort and use more energy than the lower level. But, once they reach the campsite, trekkers will get to watch the magnificent view of Khumbu Icefall, glacial moraine, and

After exploring the base camp, the trail returns to Lukla, passing through Pangboche and Namche Bazaar. It takes around three days to descend the trail and fly to Kathmandu, which comes with a fantastic view of glistening snow peaks, alluring villages, and hilltops.

Highlights of Everest Base Camp Luxury Lodge Trek

  • A pristine view of glistening snow-capped mountains, including Mt. Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, and Cho Oyu
  • Explore significant landmarks and cultural heritage sites, including Tengboche monastery and Chortens
  • Participate in the local festivals, ceremonies, and rituals
  • Encounter Himalayan wild animals and birds including, Himalayan Tahr, snow leopard, and musk deer
  • Ascend Kala Patthar to watch the sunrise view and catch the glimpses of gleaming snow peaks and glaciers

When is the Best Time?

Since Everest Base Camp is fantastic any time of the year, hikers can travel it whenever they want. However, most of them still prefer to visit the camp in spring and autumn when the weather is warm and bright.

Mid-October and April is the best time to walk the main EBC trail as they put a breathtaking view of stunning snow-capped mountains, rolling green hills, and vibrant valleys. The weather is mild around these months, making it easy for trekkers to walk the trail.

The month between June and September is considered an off-season for trekking as there is continuous downpour around this time. Nothing seems great about the weather, especially the dark clouds looming in the sky.

Spring Season

Everest Base Camp draws thousands of trekkers each year in spring for an incredible atmosphere and great views. The season offers a great walk to the visitors with overwhelming surroundings, warm sunshine, and pleasant weather conditions.

The temperature is slightly chillier at the beginning of March. But, with passing time, the weather gets more comfortable and better. The climate can be a little cold at a higher altitude, but down in the valley, it’s temperate with beautiful sunny days.

Walking along the path, trekkers can witness the spectacular scenery of the hilly countryside, verdant hills, and steep-sided valleys. Everything comes to life in spring, whether it’s the blooming flowers or wildlife waking up from hibernation.

The average temperature of the Everest Base Camp is 10 Degree Celsius between April and May. But after the end of the season, the temperature rises gradually, reaching up to 14 Degree Celsius. The days start to get a lot hotter from June, following which trekkers prefer walking into the forest or under the canopy, which provides shade.

Autumn Season

Autumn is another beautiful time of the year to trek Everest Base Camp. Hikers can expect mellowy and warm weather conditions in the season. Autumn offers mild climate with high humidity and precipitation, which makes the trekking more convenient.

The air is crisp and often clear from mid-September to November. In the presence of colorful fall foliage, chilly air, and crowded trails, trekkers get a strong vibe of autumn during October.

Autumn brings a different festival to the valley and ensures to introduce it to the trekkers. Celebrations are happening in the villages, and even visitors are allowed to participate in them. They can perform songs and other traditional rituals followed by the locals.

November marks the end of the autumn season, following which the weather gets cold and a bit harsh. From the end of the month, days get shorter and darker, so trekkers will have to keep track of time. They'll have to make it quick on the trail, or it'll be impossible for them to reach the destination.

Off-Season

If you intend to go solo on the trail without any crowd, winter and monsoon can be the season for hikers. The weather is a bit harsh during the season, and extra precaution has to be taken. In monsoon, trekkers will have to deal with continuous showers, which makes the trail filthy.

As they become slippery, it gets tough to walk the murky trail. Trekkers can expect rainfall every day for three months, starting from mid-June to the end of September. Monsoon also witnesses some of the hottest days of the year, with temperatures rising up to 22 Degree Celsius in the daytime.

But, once the rain has stopped, trekkers will get a crystal clear view of soaring snow peaks, vivid valleys. As the rain washes the dirt, trekkers will get a fresh breath of air.

Far off, the weather is quietly cold in winter with light snowfall and high winds. Temperatures are generally below Degree Celsius in the month, causing trekkers to shiver. The freezing weather and cold make the trek to Base Camp much more challenging than it actually is.

The trail at higher elevations is often layered in snow so, walking the path doesn't get any easier in winter. Trekkers may even have to use spikes and hiking poles on the snowy trail for better traction. With it, they can easily scale the ice-covered rocks and snowfield without suffering from frostbite.

Wearing gaiters also helps a lot to stay warm and avoid injuries while traveling the icefields and snow slopes. The views in winter are nothing less than a fairy tale with a dust of snow coats over houses and trees. Frozen lakes, snow-covered valleys, and mountains look magical in winter.

toc.text: Highlights of Everest Base Camp Luxury Lodge Trek

itinerary.title: Arrive at Kathmandu airport and transfer to your hotel.
itinerary.html: Upon your arrival, our officials will meet you at the Tribhuvan International Airport. After a warm welcome, they’ll transfer you to the hotel where you can freshen up. Get some rest, and we’ll meet you in the afternoon for last-minute preparation. In the meeting, we’ll briefly discuss the trek and introduce the trekkers with the crew members. If there is any trekking equipment you need to grab, get it right now. Overnight stay in a hotel.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla and trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html:
Phakding Elevation: 2,610 m
Walking Duration: 3-4 hours.

We’ll fly to Lukla early in the morning to avoid traffic and heat. The direct flight from Tribhuvan Airport will last half an hour before we land at the beautiful Sherpa town. Throughout the whole journey, we’ll get stunning glimpses of Himalayan ranges, sweeping hills, lush meadows, and waterfalls.

After arriving at the town of Lukla, we’ll take some time to have breakfast. Shortly afterward, we’ll leave for the trek to Phakding, which typically requires almost 3 hours. It starts with an uphill walk from the left bank of Dudh Koshi River and then a short descent through the pine forest.

From there, we navigate mixed terrains with several highs and lows to arrive at the village of Phakding. It is located in the Dudh Koshi River Valley, just south of Monjo at 2,610 m Overnight stay in a lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m
Walking Hours: 6-7 hours

The journey from Phakding to Namche starts easy, following the Dudh Koshi River Valley and steep stone stairs through the rhododendron forest. Passing several small villages, we arrive at the Sagarmatha National Park, where the entry fee is collected.

We’ll cross the Dudh Koshi River several times using a suspension bridge and ascend the rugged hill. Navigating the winding trails, we appear at the top of a ridge, which provides a magnificent view of Lhotse.

The last few hours of the trek are quite stressful as it continuously gains elevation. There’s no downward or plain walk, making the trek more strenuous and challenging. After walking the course for nearly 6 hours, we’ll arrive at the Namche Bazaar. Tonight we’ll stay in a lodge at Namche.

itinerary.title: Rest at Namche Bazar for acclimatization (3,440 m / 11,286 ft).
itinerary.html: The trail out of Namche is incredibly steep and uphill, increasing the risk of altitude sickness. So, instead of forging ahead, we’ll stop at Namche and take proper rest. We’ll spend the morning walking a rough trail to Syangboche at 12,400 ft high. It takes 2-3 hours to reach the Hotel Everest View and enjoy mesmerizing views of diverse landscapes, towering hills, and vivid valleys. We’ll also get a close snap of Mt. Everest and its surrounding snow peaks, including Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and Lhotse. After the sightseeing is over, we’ll have a warm breakfast at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazzar to Deboche (3820m/1253ft): 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Deboche Elevation: 3,820 m
Walking Hours: 5-6 hours

After a day off at Namche, it’s time for us to get back to the trail and make our way to Deboche. We’ll walk from the edge of the hill out of the village before descending to the river at Phungi Thenga. After stopping at the village for lunch, we continue the trek uphill from the valley’s edge.

The trek gets easier after coming off the level ground as we can see the pace increasing. Following one or two hours of walk, the trail descends to the river and crosses the wooden bridge. After arriving at Tengboche, we’ll visit the famous Tibetan monastery and offer our prayers.

We’ll climb down the hill and make our way through the rhododendron forest upon exploring the pilgrimage. Along the path, we can witness an old memorial made in honor of the lost lives in the mountain. From here, we’ll trek a few more miles to get to Deboche, a small Sherpa village in Khumbu. There are ample tea houses and lodges here to spend the night for trekkers.

itinerary.title: Trek from Deboche to Dingboche (4,360 m / 14,304 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html:
Dingboche Elevation: 4,360 m
Walking Hours: 4-5 hours

After breakfast, we’ll gently descend the trail through the lush forest, full of juniper, pine, and birch. Crossing the pontoon bridge over Imja Khola, we ascend the trail to the village of Pangboche. As we reach there, the impressive view of Ama Dablam starts to show up, making the trek even more exciting.

The rising altitude makes the trek a little strenuous and causes trekkers to suffer from altitude sickness. The trail leading to Dingboche has a series of large old chortens, prayer walls, and painted rock faces.

Walking through the forest, we’ll encounter many wild animals, including Himalayan Tahr, brown mountain goats, and giant bearded vultures. Before reaching the lower Pangboche, we’ll move through a stunning archway that stretches the opening in the rocks.

Traveling the rugged trail from below, we end up at the Upper Pangboche. Another 30 minutes walk from Phortse and we reach Shomare, a common stop for trekkers to have lunch.

After enjoying the scenic view and some delicious lunch, we continue hiking the mountainous terrains and lush meadows where you can see herds of yak grazing. Crossing the Lobuche river, we make another half an hour climb up the steep hills to get to Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Rest at Dingboche for acclimatization (4,360 m / 14,304 ft).
itinerary.html:
Following the demanding and challenging route trip to Dingboche, a day off for trekkers seems fair enough. So, instead of preceding the trail, we’ll stop at this Sherpa village and take a side trek. Early in the morning, we’ll hike up to Nakartsang Gompa, which takes around two hours.

Its trails are steep and continuously upwards, which hikers may find upsetting. But, once they reach the monastery, they’ll be delighted by the unreal charm of dramatic hills, mountainous terrains, rocky cliffs, and glaciers.

We’ll get an incredible view of picturesque snow peaks, including Ama Dablam, Pumori, Mt. Everest, Nuptse, and Island Peak from the hilltop. Shortly after visiting the monastery and enjoying the magnificent view, we’ll climb down the trail back to the village.

If there’s any spare time left, we’ll visit Chhukung to have a close shot of Imja Valley and Imja Tse. We can also witness Imja Glacier and beautiful rhododendron forests from the valley. Overnight stay in a lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche (4,910 m / 16,109 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Lobuche Elevation: 4,910 m
Walking Hours: 6-7 hours

After the day off at Dingboche, we’ll once again get back to the trail, which kicks off with a steep climb from the edge of the hill. The path here provides a lovely view of Chukhung Valley and Island Peak at a far distance.

Walking over the rocky paths, we arrive at Dugla, a small settlement at 4,595 m The trail slowly heads towards the river fed by Khumbu Glacier, which we cross using a wooden bridge. We’ll briefly stop at Dugla to have lunch and then start climbing uphill for almost an hour.

En route, the trail offers us an impressive view of Ama Dablam, Mt. Pumori, and Everest. We keep following the rugged trail until it arrives at Lobuche. It's the last overnight stop for lodging on the trail to the Everest Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche (4,910 m / 16,109 ft) to Gorak Shep (5,170 m / 16,962 ft), continue to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m / 17,599 ft), and return to Gorak Shep, 8-9 hours.
itinerary.html:
Gorakshep Elevation: 5,180 m
Everest Base Camp Elevation: 5,364 m
Walking Hours: 6-7 hrs

Gorakshep has one of the most challenging trails on the entire trek. So, we’ll start the hike earlier and take roughly 3-4 hours to cover the distance of 5 hours. Though the trail doesn’t seem much, it still is difficult to walk, following huge rocks and boulders.

We’ll spend the first few hours ascending steep hills to the top of a mountain pass. From there, the trail follows a rocky moraine beside the ice slopes and glacial lakes. After passing the last rocky moraine dunes, the course takes us to the small settlement of Gorakshep.

The village is perched on the side of the frozen lakebed, right at the foot of Kala Patthar. After making a final stop at the hamlet for lunch, we’ll continue hiking to the base camp from the south. The trek takes 2-3 hours, depending on the pace and effects of altitude on hikers.

The trail takes over the Khumbu Glacier and finally ends at the base of Khumbu Icefall, providing a lovely view of the snow-capped mountains. While at the base camp, we’ll do some exploration and watch the surrounding mountains, including Mt. Everest and Nuptse.

As soon as the sightseeing is over, we’ll retrace the steps back to Gorakshep, which is a dry flat field. We’ll stay the night in the village and continue with the rest of the trek on the following day.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gorak Shep (5,170 m / 16,962 ft) to Kala Patthar (5,545 m / 18,192 ft) and back to Gorak Shep, then continue trekking to Pheriche (4,280 m / 14,042 ft), 8-9 hours.
itinerary.html:
Kala Patthar Elevation: 5,644 m
Walking Hours: 8-9 hours.

To watch the sunrise view from Kalapathar, we’ll trek the mountain early in the morning. We’ll start ascending the rocky trail from ground level at Gorakshep and navigate the rugged and bumpy course, which takes about 2 hours.

After a few minutes of the easy start, the trek gets intense with boulders and sandy fields. Upon reaching the summit of Kala Patthar, we’ll get a stunning view of Mt. Everest and the south face of Mt. Pumori.

We’ll also spot the icefalls and glaciers sparkling on the shaft of morning sunlight. After having a wonderful time at the clifftop, we’ll descend the trail back to Gorakshep. We’ll stop there for about half an hour to have breakfast and slowly start to climb down the path to Pheriche.

The trail is mostly downhill, but in-between, we’ll have to take a few steep hills. Passing the windswept cliffs and steppes, we’ll manage to get to Pheriche. It’s a small village, perched above the Tsola River in eastern Nepal. Pheriche is a famous Sherpa village where trekkers seek lodging and food while on the base camp trek.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pheriche to Namche Bazzar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: After getting proper rest at Pheriche, we’ll yet again descend the trail. After few minutes walk, we will head for Phungi Thanga. After an uphill hike from Kyangjuma for almost an hour, we’ll enter the Sherpa capital of Namche Bazaar. While approaching the village, we can see many small white chortens and Tibetan monasteries. Overnight stay in a lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2,840 m / 9,318 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Today is the last day of our classic trail of Khumbu. We’ll make a final descent from Namche to Lukla by walking through the Dudh Koshi River valley and passing several villages, including Manjo.

We’ll make our way through the densely forested area and take a short uphill climb before descending to the Bhote Koshi River, which we’ll cross several times. After making a final ascend over the rugged hill, we’ll ultimately end up at Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu. 35-40 minutes.
itinerary.html: Today, we’ll board the flight to Kathmandu early in the morning. For a good half an hour, we’ll get to enjoy the aerial view of sky-scraping snow peaks, sweeping hills, and villages. After landing at Tribhuvan Airport, we’ll transfer you to the hotel where you can get some sleep and have delicious food.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kthmandu..
itinerary.html: After having a delicious breakfast, you will be escorted to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) to take the scheduled flight back to your home.

sections.title: Packing List
sections.html: We are advised to consider the following equipment as these are essentials while packing for the Everest Base Camp Trek. Adjustments to the list can be managed according to the requirements, interests, duration of trip, and season of trip.  We can find variety of these gears to rent or buy in Kathmandu. Majority of the gears which are in sale in Kathmandu are locally manufactured and some are imported from china and they are much cheaper. And there are some famous branded gear shops in Kathmandu, Thamel. Equipment List: – Lightweight and comfortable hiking boots: fit them with hiking socks and wear them wherever possible before you go to trekking. – Sleeping bag and liner – Sandals/ Flip flop – Hiking socks – at least 4 pairs of cotton socks and 2 pair of wool socks – Lightweight long sleeve hiking shirts – Windproof/Waterproof pants and jacket – Plastic rain poncho – Light weather protection and warmer weather – Hat for sun and wind – Windproof gloves – Warmer clothes – Long underwear – Thermals (socks, t-shirts, sweater) – Wool hat/beanie (for winter) – Shorts – Hiking trousers – Down jacket Accessories: – Sunglasses with good UV protection – Sunscreen – Lightweight bag to carry your personal needs during the day – Insect repellent – Camera with extra battery – Flashlight – Backpack – Aluminum water bottle – Head lamp – Trekking Poles

Leaving Lhasa in our 4 wheel drive, we’ll travel through this amazing country, staying in the best traditional hotels Tibet has to offer. Thoroughly exploring the towns of Gyantse and Shigatse we visit traditional monasteries and fully immerse ourselves in the Buddhist culture.

Along the Highway we travel through some of the most amazing landscapes on Earth. We pass small Tibetan settlements, nomadic herdsmen wandering across the wide arid plains and awe-inspiring mountain peaks. Equally as fascinating is the wealth of cultural interest and there is plenty of opportunity to explore this side of Tibet, both in Lhasa and the other towns we pass through on our journey back to Kathmandu.

title: Everest Base Camp Trek
summary: Book the Everest Base Camp Trek in Nepal with local guides. Explore Sherpa culture, reach Everest Base Camp, and enjoy breathtaking Himalayan scenery.

seo.title: 14 Days Everest Base Camp Budget Trek | 2026 & 2027
seo.description: Book the Everest Base Camp Trek in Nepal with local guides. Explore Sherpa culture, reach Everest Base Camp, and enjoy breathtaking Himalayan scenery.

overview:
Everest Base Camp Trek is one of the most popular and fulfilling trekking destinations in Nepal. In fact, every year thousands of trekkers visit Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar to witness stunning views of the mighty Everest (8,848 m) along with other snow-capped mountains with wonderful scenery. Moreover, Everest Base Camp Trek allows you to stand on the base of the highest peak in the world without having prior trekking experience.

Everest Base Camp trek experience can give you one of the most incredible times of your life. Your trek begins by taking a short flight from Lukla to Kathmandu. Thereafter, you will trek from Lukla and reach Namche Bazaar, one of the biggest residential areas of the legendary Sherpas.

Generally, you will observe the daily life, tradition, and culture of Sherpas. Reaching Tengboche, you will visit the oldest and beautiful monastery of this region. From Tengboche, you will head to Dingboche, Lobuche, Gorakshep, and ultimately reach Everest Base Camp to have an astonishing panorama of the high mountains of the Khumbu region.

In particular. the trail is full of ascends and descends along with beautiful rhododendron and pine forests, rivers, hills, stunning views snow-capped mountains, and glaciers. Besides, you will also climb to Kala Patthar (5,545 m), which presents you with a stunning sunrise view over the peaks of Mt. Everest (8,848 m), Khumbutse (6,636 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), Pumori (7,161 m), Lingtren (6,749 m) and so on.

You will normally visit the Everest base camp in the afternoon on the same day of your arrival in Gorek Shep. Also, you stop for lunch at Gorak Shep before finally making your way to Everest base camp. After enjoying the views in Everest Base Camp you return to Gorak Shep for the overnight stay. As you can find no lodge or camp to stay in Everest Base Camp. Likewise, the next day we leave the early morning session to climb Kala Pathar for a breath-taking view of Mount Everest. After enjoying the views from Kala Pathar you return to Gorak Shep and repeat your steps to Lukla. Furthermore, you will trek back to Lukla with a heart full of unforgettable memories that will live with you for a lifetime.

EBC Trek Altitude Chart

Highlights of the Everest Base Camp Trek

  • Walkthrough dense forests of various flora and fauna
  • Reach the base of Mount Everest
  • Marvelous view of mighty Everest
  • Stunning view of several magnificent peaks
  • Beautiful sunrise view from Kala Patthar
  • Explore culturally and traditionally rich villages
  • Thrilling flight to Lukla
  • Exciting journey on the paths of the Himalayas

Best Time to Visit Everest Base Camp Trek

Everest Base Camp trek has one of the most exciting and thrilling trails of Nepal. Traveling in these routes are filled with wonderful greenery, marvelous peaks, and endangered wildlife.

There are four seasons you can choose to travel from Spring, Monsoon, Autumn, and Winter. Among these, Spring and Autumn are the best time to visit Everest Base Camp Trek.

During these seasons, the weather and temperature are also favorable. The days are sunny and sweaty while nights are windy and cool. During these times, the skies are also clear giving the stunning view of peaks and landscapes.

As for Winter and Monsoon, these seasons are also favorable for trekking. But there might be various weather complications that might delay or cancel your trek.

Other than that, these seasons give a wonderful experience in the Himalayas. Snowy paths, snow-capped mountains, new species of flora are some of the attractions during these times.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu and transfer to your hotel.
itinerary.html: You will meet with one of our representatives at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) who will take you to your hotel. Later, you will meet your trekking guide who will brief you about the trek and help you make the necessary preparation. Overnight at hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft) and then same day trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: Your trek begins after a short 40 minutes flight over the hills and mountains from Kathmandu to Lukla. Lukla is a small town with few hotels, lodges, and general stores. Shortly after reaching Lukla, you will begin your trek to Phakding. You will climb up on the left bank of DudhKoshi River and descend to join the Everest route to reach Phakding. You will have a close-up view of KusumKanguru (6,367 m) from Phakding. Overnight in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will begin your trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar. Namche Bazaar is a large Sherpa town and also the main trading area of Khumbu region. You will cross the river on a high suspension bridge and reach Monjo village (2,835 m). You will enter Sagarmatha National Park in Monjo and cross the suspension bridge over the DudhKoshi River to enter Jorsalle. From here, you will ascend on the steep path and reach Namche Bazaar. On a clear day, you will get to see the first view of Mt. Everest (8,848 m).

itinerary.title: Extra day in Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft) for acclimatization.
itinerary.html: Today you will take a rest to get acclimatized with high altitude. You will hike up to Khunde Hospital (built by Sir Edmund Hillary), or take an hour-long walk to the Everest View Hotel (3,962 m). From here, you will see stunning views of Mt. Everest (8,848 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), Thamserku (6,608 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), KusumKanguru (6,367 m), and AmaDablam (6,856 m). Overnight in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche (3,860 m / 12,664 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: After having a warm delicious breakfast, you will begin your trek to Tengboche. You will walk on the side of the valley, high above DudhKoshi River, and after crossing a few beautiful villages and several tea shops, you will descend on the steep path. After that, you will cross the bridge over DudhKoshi River at PhunkeTenga (3,250 m) and reach Tengboche, where you will see the most famous and the oldest monastery of the Khumbu region. The trail will present you with gorgeous views of Mt. Everest (8,848 m), AmaDablam (6,856 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), and so on. Overnight in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche (4,410 m / 14,468 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Today, you will gradually begin to descend to Dingboche (4,410 m), and crossing ImjaKhola, you will climb up to Pangboche village. This village is opposite to AmaDablam (6,856 m) and presents you stunning views of snow-capped mountains behind beautiful pine trees, Mani walls, and gompas. From here, you will ascend through dense forests of juniper bushes, and after two and half an hour walk, you reach Dingboche. Overnight in Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Rest at Dingboche (4,410 m / 14,468 ft) for acclimatization.
itinerary.html: Today, you will take a day for acclimatization and explore the surrounding areas. You can steeply climb to Nakartsang Gompa for an exceptional view of Mt. Everest (8,848 m), Makalu (8,481 m), Baruntse (7,129 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), AmaDablam (6,856 m), and Island Peak (6,189 m). You can also choose to go on a small side trip to Chhukhung to have some delicious food. Overnight in Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche (4,910 m / 16,109 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: With the panoramic view of mountains, you will begin your trek to Lobuche via Dughla. You will climb up on the zigzag path through rocky glacial moraines. You will find several stone Chortens at the top, built in the memories of Sherpas who died while climbing the mighty Everest (8,848 m). From here, you will gradually climb along the glacier to reach Lobuche. Overnight in Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche to Gorakshep (5,164 m / 16,942 ft), continue to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m / 17,598 ft), and return to Gorak Shep, 7–8 hours.
itinerary.html: You will begin your trek and reach Gorakshep where you will take rest, and if feeling okay, you will climb to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m), which will take about four and half hours to reach and get back to Gorakshep. The trail is covered with glaciers and rocks. You will also see beautiful small frozen lakes around the Everest Base Camp. At the base camp, a wide vista of the Khumbu Himalayas makes up an enticing landscape. You will later hike down to Gorakshep for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gorakshep to Kala Patthar (5,545 m / 18,192 ft), return to Gorak Shep, and continue to Pheriche (4,371 m / 14,340 ft), 6–7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will wake up early in the morning to witness the beautiful sunrise from Kala Patthar (5,545 m). After a tough climb to Kala Patthar, you will get a stunning view of Mt. Everest (8,848 m), Khumbutse (6,636 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), Pumori (7,161 m), Lingtren (6,749 m), and many other peaks. After having a good time at Kala Patthar, you will return to Pheriche for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Today, you will begin your trek through the hillside covered by juniper trees, and in spring, you will find beautiful pink and red rhododendrons all around you. You will have lunch in Tengboche and then continue to Namche Bazaar. We want to take a long last look (and picture) of Lhotse (8,414 m) and the tip of Everest (8,848 m) from here. On reaching your lodge, you can take a nice hot shower and have the very relaxed sleep in your room in Namche Bazaar. Overnight in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Today, you will slowly and carefully descend on the steep path and rocky terrain. After that, you will cross a suspension bridge over the DudhKoshi River, and you will find climate getting warmer. Regardless of walking back on the same route, you will get completely different views. You will get into open plains and beautiful pine forests with snow-capped mountains at a far distance. Crossing small Sherpa villages, you will reach Lukla for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Fly back from Lukla to Kathmandu, (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html: Today you will take an early morning flight back to Kathmandu. The short flight will give you the outstanding view of snow-capped mountains. After reaching Kathmandu, you can rest and further explore nearby areas. Overnight at hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu to your onward destination.
itinerary.html: Today, you will be transferred to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for your onward flight home.

sections.title: Routes of Everest Base Camp Trek
sections.html:
Routes of Everest Base Camp Trek

Kathmandu - Lukla - Phakding - Namche Bazaar - Tengboche - Dingboche - Lobuche - Everest Base Camp - Gorakshep - Kala Patthar - Pheriche - Namche Bazaar- Lukla - Kathmandu

Your trip begins and ends in Kathmandu. You catch an early flight to Lukla from where you start your Everest Base Camp Trek journey. Viewing wonderful scenarios of peaks and greenery you arrive at Lukla.

Then from there, you trek towards Phakding where you stay for the night. The next day, you head towards Namche Bazaar, a beautiful Sherpa town. Your first acclimatization is held in this town.

After a relaxing day, you again begin your EBC trek by heading towards Tengboche. This small village is popular for its ancient Monastery, the largest gompa of the Khumbu region.

Waking up early, you explore the monastery and head towards Dingboche, where your second acclimatization is held. The next day you trek towards Lobuche from there.

From Lobuche, you head towards the highlight of this trip Everest Base Camp. The excitement of reaching the base of Mount Everest will overwhelm you. Viewing the marvelous peak and spending some time there, you trek towards Gorakshep.

Then the following day, you hike to Kala Patthar to view the beautiful sunrise and magnificent peaks. After enjoying the view, you trek down to Pheriche and stay the night.

From there, you head towards Namche Bazaar, stay the night then trek back to Lukla. You catch your flight back to Kathmandu from here. Your return ends the Everest Base Camp Trek.

Route Difficulty

When trekking to Everest Base Camp, trekkers usually wonder how difficult are its routes? Well, the route difficulty of the trek depends upon each individual.

The routes are suitable for both beginner and experienced trekkers. But the trails can be harsher for the new ones. As there are several ups, downs, twists, and turns.

You will also be walking for about 5 to 6 hours each day which can be tiring for newcomers. However, with proper preparation and planning, you can complete the trek with ease so, do not panic.

Various Difficulty Faced During the Trek

Other than route difficulties, you can face various other difficulties when trekking to Everest Base Camp. We have mentioned a few of the difficulty faced in Everest Base Camp Trek below:

Altitude Sickness

One of the common problems faced while traveling in high elevation is altitude sickness. This is mostly caused due to lack of oxygen in high places. The air gets thinner as you climb high in elevation.

Some common symptoms are nausea, headache, vomiting, breathing difficulty, sleeping difficulty, etc. if you notice any of the symptoms inform your guide or trek down to lower altitudes immediately.

Accommodation

Finding accommodation can be hard when traveling during peak seasons. As during this time the rooms are packed with travelers from around the world. Also, the price of rooms are high during these times.

So, do not travel in the hopes of finding room on the spot during peak time.

Weather and Temperature

Weather and temperature always play a major role in deciding how your trip turns out to be. The climatic conditions are unpredictable in the higher regions. So always be prepared beforehand for your trek.

It can be sunny one moment and windy in the next minute. The weather tends to change as you climb higher. It gets cold and windy in high places. However, the lower regions are warm and less windy.

No Atm Machine

There are no ATM machines available after Namche Bazaar in this trek. Also, sometimes the atm machine in Namche doesn’t work properly. So, always change your cash or take it before the trek begins.

Alternative Routes to Reach Everest Base Camp

Usually, people follow the standard Everest Base Camp route to complete their trek. But there are various alternative routes to reach the Base Camp. Mentioned below are some of the alternative routes:

Jiri to Everest Base Camp

Traveling through Jiri leads you through the Classic Everest Base Camp Trek route. This is the route that Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay Sherpa walked in. Taking this route, you will be following their footprints.

Before people used to begin their trek from Jiri as there were no flights available till Lukla. However, as the flights are available nowadays, most people begin their journey from Lukla. So, the trails of classic routes are quite isolated making it perfect for peace lovers.

Your trip will cost less as you will be driving to Jiri from Kathmandu and trek to Lukla from there. On this trail, you will be passing through several small settlements of Newar, Brahmins, Chhetri, etc.

This alternative route has days that are longer than the standard route. You will be trekking through rough routes, dense forests of flora, and fauna viewing beautiful scenarios.

On this trek, you get to see various snow-capped peaks such as Lhotse, Nuptse, Everest, and many more. If you are lucky you might even spot various endangered animals such as Tar, Himalayan Black Bear, red panda, etc.

This fun-filled trek lasts about 20 days if you choose the classic Everest trek. For the next few weeks get ready to be lost in the beauty of nature while exploring the regions.

Tumlingtar to Everest Base Camp

Another way to begin your trek is from Tumlingtar. Choosing this path lets you explore two regions i.e. Makalu and Everest. This trek is full of exciting adventures and beautiful views of scenarios.

To begin your journey, you will be flying to Tumlingtar from Kathmandu. Then following the isolated trails through various hills and terrains join the traditional Everest base camp trek route.

On this trek, you will be seeing many magnificent peaks such as Ama Dablam, Makalu, Everest, etc. Also, passing through two national parks i.e Sagarmatha and Makalu-Barun National Park.

While passing these national parks, you might spot various endangered animals. Like red panda, golden jackal, Indian leopard, Himalayan Black Bear, wild boar, etc. Also, you will be needing entry permits to walk through these parks.

People from various ethnicities have made their home in these trails. Walking through Sherpa and Rai villages you descend to villages of Chettri and Brahmin. This journey gives you an opportunity to know more about the lifestyle of these people. And experience their warm hospitality provided by them.

Crossing several rivers, forests and walking past ancient monasteries you stay nights in the culturally rich villages. You will be visiting several popular villages like Namche Bazaar, Arun Valley, Tengboche, etc.

Three passes and EBC Trek

If you are looking for ways to stay longer in the Everest region. Then the Three Passes and Everest Base Camp Trek is the one for you. This trek is full of beautiful wonders of nature.

On this trek, you will be reaching the three high passes of the Everest region while following the traditional route. Renjo La, Cho La, and Kongma La are the names of these passes. These passes lie above 5,000 m altitude making the trek more thrilling for trekkers.

Following the trail lets you circuit around the whole Everest region. This trail is quite popular among trekkers. But still, the routes are not much crowded compared to other trails. Thus, making this route the best for trekkers who love walking in silence.

You will be viewing several magnificent peaks like Lhotse, Nuptse, Everest, Island Peak, and many more. Also, while traveling through the Sagarmatha national park you might see various endangered animals.

Walking through forests of rhododendron while enjoying the scenarios is quite a trip. The trails are quite challenging but with proper preparation and planning you can complete it with ease.

When traveling to 5,000 m elevation altitude sickness is common, so be well prepared for it. But the views of the beautiful peaks will mesmerize you from the top.

Gokyo Lakes and EBC Trek

This trek is one of the best alternative routes. These routes are quite popular making it crowded throughout the year. Most trekkers choose to travel through these routes to reach the base camp.

This trek is the combination of two popular treks of the Everest region i.e. Gokyo Lake and Everest Base Camp. You get to visit two famous destinations in one trek.

Each day takes you on an interesting journey in the Himalayas. You will be viewing various peaks such as Nuptse, Pumori, Makalu, Everest, and Cho Oyu. And pass through dense forests of juniper, fir, pines, oaks, and rhododendron.

You will be first visiting the Hidden Gokyo Valley and the Gokyo Lakes. Then crossing one of the high passes (Cho La Pass) head towards Base Camp then Kala Patthar.

Reaching Kala Patthar you get to see the beautiful view of sunrise from there. This viewpoint is popular for its excellent view of mountains and landscapes as well.

This trek lasts more than 2 weeks in the Everest region. But these weeks will be the most memorable ones for you. Staying in traditional villages, experiencing warm hospitality, and many more.

Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour

You are short on time but have a desire to visit the Everest region. Then choosing the Everest Base Camp Helicopter tour is the best alternative option for you.

Nowadays, the Everest Helicopter tour has gained popularity among travelers. Most travelers due to limited time don’t have time to trek till EBC. So, this option was made available for most travelers like them.

Usually, the trekking takes about 7 to 11 days in this region. But with the helicopter option, you can reach the base camp and return within a few hours. It lasts about 2 to 3 hours at most.

On this flight, you get to see the scenic view of peaks, landscapes, valleys, and lush green forest from above. The peaks are mesmerizingly beautiful from out the window.

You will catch your flight from the Tribhuvan airport and head towards Lukla. It lands for about 15 to 25 minutes for fueling. Then from there, they fly you to the Kalapatthar.

Landing time is about 10 to 15 minutes due to altitude problems. After a wonderful time, you fly to Everest View Hotel for a delicious breakfast. Then head back to Kathmandu from there.

Useful Tips

Carry water bottle

The Himalayas are still underdeveloped so you won’t find shops in every nook. Thus for time like that carrying your personal bottle will come in handy. You can find bottled water but they will be quite expensive in these trails. So, always carry a bottle and fill them before beginning the trek.

Carry Extra Cash

The estimated budget might not be enough during treks. So, it is better to carry extra cash than be sorry later. As you climb higher the price of goods and services also rises. So, the budget can sometimes go over.

Physical Exercises

Being mentally and physically fit is the first priority of the trek. So, for that, you need to do some physical exercises such as running, swimming, long walks, etc. These exercises can be done along with your daily schedule so you do not need to hit the gym or hire a trainer.

sections.title: Packing List
sections.html:
We are advised to consider the following equipment as these are essentials while packing for the Everest Base Camp Trek. Adjustments to the list can be managed according to the requirements, interests, duration of trip, and season of trip.  We can find variety of these gears to rent or buy in Kathmandu. Majority of the gears which are in sale in Kathmandu are locally manufactured and some are imported from china and they are much cheaper. And there are some famous branded gear shops in Kathmandu.

– A good backpacking sleeping bag and liner
– Lightweight and comfortable hiking boots: fit them with hiking socks and wear them wherever possible before you go to trekking.
– Sandals/ Flip flop
– Hiking socks – at least 4 pairs of cotton socks and 2 pair of wool socks

faqs.q: How many days does it take for the Everest Base Camp Trek by Base Camp Adventure?
faqs.a: The usual Everest Base Camp Trek package offered by Base Camp Adventure covers 14 days in total, including your trip to Kathmandu, preparation process, trekking to Everest Base Camp, going back to Lukla, and your final day of leaving Nepal. These 14 days also include acclimatization days at Namche Bazaar and Dingboche.

faqs.q: How high is the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
When you are on the Everest Base Camp Trek you will have the chance to hike to these high altitudes:

  • Gorakshep: 5,164 m
  • Everest Base Camp: 5,364 m
  • Kala Patthar: 5,545 m

Kala Patthar viewpoint is the highest point that you can reach while trekking to the Everest Base Camp. It is the most popular place for watching the sunrise over Mount Everest and the surrounding Himalayan peaks.

faqs.q: What makes the Everest Base Camp Trek special?
faqs.a:
Mountain flight to Lukla from Kathmandu

Trekking in the Khumbu valley

Visit to Namche Bazaar, the capital of the Sherpas

Tengboche Monastery

Understanding of Sherpa culture and tradition

Walk through the Sagarmatha National Park

Beautiful rhododendron and pine forests

Hanging bridges over Himalayan rivers

Everest Base Camp

Sunrise view from Kala Patthar

Panoramic view of Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam and Pumori

faqs.q: Why is the Everest Base Camp Trek popular?
faqs.a:
Everest Base Camp Trek is popular since travelers have a chance to explore the fabled Everest region without any special climbing abilities. The trek offers a blend of adventure, culture, nature, and personal achievement for travelers. 

You can walk in the traditional Sherpa settlements, know about the Himalayan lifestyle, Buddhist monasteries and be at the base of the world's tallest mountain.

faqs.q: Is the trek to the Everest Base Camp feasible for those without any climbing skills?
faqs.a: Yes. The trek to the Everest Base Camp does not demand any prior climbing skills or mountaineering experience. This trekking journey follows the well established paths of the mountains. But it becomes essential to be physically fit and ready to face the long hiking days, steep hills, and also the high-altitude environment.

faqs.q: Why choose Base Camp Adventure for the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Base Camp Adventure specializes in offering you a safe, genuine and tailor-made Himalayan experience. We offer you experienced local guides, professional services, customized packages, small group treks, safe and secure trekking arrangements, authentic Himalayan experience along with responsible tourism. 

The professional crew will make sure that your trip to Everest is comfortable and enjoyable.

faqs.q: What kind of customization can be made to the Everest Base Camp Trek itinerary?
faqs.a: We provide customized packages for trekking according to the traveling dates, physical fitness, duration of time available and personal preferences. From extra days for acclimatization to shorter durations of trek or adding other destinations like Gokyo Lakes and Island Peak to your schedule, all is possible.

faqs.q: How tough is the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: The Everest Base Camp Trek is moderately difficult. No technical skill is required; the difficulty lies in altitude, long walking days, rough paths and variable weather. The daily walking takes around 5-7 hours, except on some days like ascending to Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar.

faqs.q: Is the Everest Base Camp Trek for beginners?
faqs.a: Yes. The beginners can do the Everest Base Camp Trek if they are physically fit and well-prepared. Trekking experience is useful but not mandatory. The guides at Base Camp Adventure help you pace and progress through the trek.

faqs.q: What kind of preparations am I supposed to have for the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
A person must have:

  • Cardiovascular endurance
  • Strong legs
  • The ability to walk a long distance
  • Mental strength

Exercises such as hiking, walking, running, cycling, swimming, stair climbing, sit ups, push ups, squats etc are essential to prepare you physically. Similarly, meditation, breathing exercises, visualization etc. are key for mental preparation and also boost confidence for the trek.

faqs.q: Is there any age restriction for the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: There is no official age restriction. The physical fitness and health condition of people are important factors for this trek. Children and elderly people can complete this trek as long as they are healthy and well-prepared. It is recommended to consult your physician before undertaking any alpine trekking.

faqs.q: Is there a provision for acclimatization days in the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes, there are some acclimatization days planned for:

  • Namche Bazaar
  • Dingboche

These days will enable you to adjust yourself slowly to the increasing mountain heights.

faqs.q: What are the signs of altitude sickness?
faqs.a:
In case your body cannot adapt to the lower oxygen concentration at high altitudes then you may suffer from altitude sickness. These are some of the symptoms:

  • Headaches
  • Nausea
  • Dizziness
  • Loss of appetite
  • Sleeplessness
  • Tiredness

faqs.q: How can I avoid altitude sickness?
faqs.a:
In order to avoid suffering from altitude sickness you need to:

  • Walk slowly
  • Drink plenty of water
  • Eat nutritious food
  • Follow acclimatization procedures
  • Stay away from alcohol
  • Inform your guide of any discomfort you experience

faqs.q: What if I get altitude sickness while trekking?
faqs.a: Your guide will keep an eye on you and help you in whatever way he can. Depending on your situation, it could be a matter of resting, adjusting the pace, moving to a lesser altitude, or evacuating in case of emergency.

faqs.q: When is the right time for the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Everest Base Camp Trek is best to go in the spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) seasons. During spring, there will be stable weather, mild temperatures, and crystal-clear views of the magnificent Himalayan mountains. 

Similarly, the autumn season brings clear sky, moderate temperatures, excellent visibility, and dry climate conditions, which makes the trek safe, easy and memorable.

faqs.q: Is it possible to do the Everest Base Camp trek in winter?
faqs.a: It is possible to go for the EBC trek in winter. Winter offers good visibility and less crowded trails, but the temperature is extremely cold, especially in high altitudes. Likewise, heavy snowfall can block some sections of the trail and make navigation more difficult.

faqs.q: Will the monsoon affect the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: It is possible to make a monsoon trek; however, rain may interfere with the visibility and your travel schedule. Flights to and from Lukla are also frequently delayed or postponed at this time due to weather related disruptions.

faqs.q: What temperatures will be there during the trek?
faqs.a: Temperature depends on altitude and the season. The low and mid elevation regions have favorable daytime trekking temperature (10-20 degrees Celcius), whereas high altitude regions like the Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar are very cold (5 to -5 degrees Celcius).

faqs.q: What should I pack for the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
The following items will be most needed

  • Trekking boots
  • Layered clothing
  • Down jacket
  • Sleeping bag
  • Rain jacket
  • Gloves
  • Hat
  • Sunglasses
  • Water bottle
  • Headlight
  • Trekking poles
  • First aid kit and basic medicines
  • Personal hygiene items
  • Backpack and a daypack

faqs.q: Is there a possibility to rent trekking equipment in Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Yes, it is possible to rent or buy different kinds of trekking gear like sleeping bags, down jackets and trekking poles etc in Kathmandu. Thamel is the ideal place to shop for your trekking essentials.

faqs.q: What kind of trekking shoes are recommended?
faqs.a: The use of high-quality waterproof boots is advisable. Your boots need to be worn before you go on the trek to make sure that they fit well and prevent any occurrence of blisters and other discomforts while on the journey.

faqs.q: What amount of luggage can be carried by the porter?
faqs.a: Each porter will carry the luggage of two trekkers with a total weight capacity of around 20-25 kg. Hence, each trekker must ensure that their duffel bag weighs only around 10-12 kg.

faqs.q: What must be packed inside the day pack?
faqs.a: Your day pack must comprise your water bottle, snacks, rain jacket, extra clothes, gloves, sunglasses, sunscreen lotion, camera, medicines, passport, money, and other essential personal belongings.

faqs.q: What sort of accommodation is offered in the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Base Camp Adventure offers:

  • Hotel accommodation in Kathmandu
  • Teahouse/Guest House accommodation on the trek

Teahouses provide basic but comfortable lodging including beds, toilets, eating areas and shared facilities at most places. Higher elevation regions have more basic accommodations because of the remote mountainous locations.

faqs.q: What sort of food is provided on the trek?
faqs.a:
On the trek, you get three meals a day:

  • Breakfast
  • Lunch
  • Dinner

Teahouses provide various types of food like:

  • Dal Bhat (rice, lentil, and vegetables)
  • Noodles
  • Pasta
  • Soup
  • Tibetan cuisine
  • Basic Continental food

Proper nutrition meals help maintain energy on trekking days.

faqs.q: Is there electricity during the trek and can I charge my gadgets?
faqs.a:
There will be an electricity supply at most of the teahouses along the trekking trail. The availability of charging facilities may be reduced at high altitudes. Charging usually requires an extra payment of USD 2-10 per device per charge depending on the altitude and location of a teahouse. 

It is also recommended to carry a power bank as a backup especially for the higher sections of the trek.

faqs.q: Is the internet available on the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes, there is internet available in most of the teahouses during the Everest Base Camp Trek especially in the lower and mid altitude villages through Everest Link. 

However, the internet is usually provided on a chargeable basis and its speed depends on location and weather conditions. As you climb further, the connection becomes slow and unreliable.

faqs.q: Will there be vegetarian food on the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Certainly, there are a lot of vegetarian food options available during the Everest Base Camp trek. You will get dal bhat (rice, lentil soup, and vegetables), noodle soup with vegetables, fried rice, soups, pasta, potatoes, pancakes and porridge. 

If you prefer other food choices such as vegan or gluten free or if you have any food allergies, then let us know in advance.

faqs.q: Is water available while on the trekking route?
faqs.a:
Yes. Drinking water is available throughout the trek. Your water bottles can be refilled either by purchasing boiled water from the tea house or by using purified water through the use of a water filter or water purification drops/tablets. 

It is recommended that you always have a water bottle handy so that you do not have to use bottled water that causes plastic pollution.

faqs.q: Is it possible to take hot showers?
faqs.a: Yes. You can get hot showers at most of the teahouses along the trail for a fee (USD 2-7). Availability can depend on the popularity of the village, altitude and location of a teahouse and climatic conditions.

faqs.q: Is there availability of toilets while trekking?
faqs.a: Yes, each teahouse has toilets which become more primitive as you trek up high elevation. While Western flush toilets are found in some popular and established teahouses, there will usually be basic squat toilets at upper zones. There are also public toilets in some villages on the trekking trail.

faqs.q: Are there private rooms in teahouses?
faqs.a: There can be private rooms available in teahouses at low and mid elevations. However, the availability decreases once you ascend the higher altitude zones and during the peak trekking season, shared twin rooms are the norm.

faqs.q: What permits are needed for the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Permits are mandatory, they are:

  • Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit
  • Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Entry Permit

Base Camp Adventure will handle all the paperwork and arrange the permits required for the trek.

faqs.q: Do you provide guides and porters?
faqs.a: Yes. Base Camp Adventure provides an English speaking government-licensed trekking guide along with porter services to carry your luggage (one porter for two trekkers).

faqs.q: What happens if the Lukla flight is delayed?
faqs.a:
The weather is the key factor that determines the Lukla flight schedules. In case of a delay in flights, it gets rescheduled to the next available one. So it is necessary to have flexibility in your travel schedule. 

If required we can also assist in arranging a helicopter flight as an alternative, subject to availability. But any additional cost for the helicopter service must be borne by you.

faqs.q: Do I require a Nepal visa?
faqs.a:
Yes. Almost all foreigners traveling to Nepal require a visa for the purpose of entering Nepal. You can apply for their visa upon arriving at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu depending on eligibility.
The necessary documents required for obtaining a visa include a valid passport, duly filled visa application form, passport-size photos and the relevant visa fees.

faqs.q: What should be the validity of my passport?
faqs.a: A passport should be valid for a period of at least six months from the time you enter Nepal. In addition, there should be adequate space in your passport for visa stickers and any other immigration procedures. We advise you to carry print-outs as well as scanned versions of your passport and other travel documents.

faqs.q: Is it compulsory for me to buy travel insurance?
faqs.a:
Yes. The Everest Base Camp Trek needs travel insurance that will provide coverage for

  • High altitude trekking
  • Medical expense incurred
  • Emergency evacuation
  • Helicopter rescue
  • Trip cancellation
  • Delay or loss of baggage

It is recommended that you carry your travel insurance document in both printed and digital form.

faqs.q: What is the deposit that needs to be paid for booking the trekking package?
faqs.a: A non-refundable deposit of 30% of the total cost needs to be paid while making the booking for the trek with us. The rest of the amount could be paid once you arrive in Kathmandu.

faqs.q: What are the modes of payment that can be accepted?
faqs.a:
Payment could be done via:

  • Bank transfer
  • Credit card
  • Debit card
  • Cash
  • Other secure online payment methods

faqs.q: What are the cancellation policies?
faqs.a:
In case you have to cancel your Everest Base Camp Trek package, you have to inform us through email. Cancellation fee will be applicable depending on the time of cancellation. 

If you cancel after making the booking, there is 30% cancellation fee applicable and the deposit is non-refundable. In case you cancel 7 days prior to the trip, the deposit will not be refunded. No refund policy applies for unused services or early departure if cancellation is done after the trip starts.

faqs.q: How do I make a booking for the Everest Base Camp Trek with Base Camp Adventure?
faqs.a: You can contact us through the website, email and phone. You will be able to book your trek after confirming your availability, providing the required details and making the deposit payment.

faqs.q: Am I allowed to take a private Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: Yes. Base Camp Adventure provides private Everest Base Camp Trek packages to solo travelers, couples or families/groups. You can enjoy the trip based on your fitness, experience, preferences, schedule and budget.

faqs.q: When should I book my Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: It is advisable to book at least a few months ahead particularly during the peak seasons of spring and autumn when flights, hotels and permits may not be available and hard to arrange.

faqs.q: Is there a possibility for the itinerary to be changed?
faqs.a: Yes. The weather conditions, flight delays, trail conditions, health issues or any other unexpected situation might need the itinerary to be modified accordingly.

faqs.q: Is the Everest Base Camp Trek safe?
faqs.a:
Yes. The trek to Everest Base Camp is among the safest Himalayan journeys that can be undertaken if done with appropriate acclimatization and with proper preparations and guidance. 

Base Camp Adventure cares for your safety and ensures it through professional guides, first aid kits, effective communication systems and well planned itineraries.

faqs.q: What safety measures does Base Camp Adventure offer?
faqs.a: We care about your safety the most. We have government licensed guides, enough acclimatization days, first aid medical kits, health check-ups, emergency communication facilities and even assistance for the arrangement of a helicopter evacuation when needed.

faqs.q: Will the oxygen be available during the trek?
faqs.a: Use of supplemental oxygen is not usually needed on the Everest Base Camp Trek. But in case of a severe altitude sickness, use of emergency oxygen and helicopter evacuation can be arranged.

faqs.q: What will happen in case of an emergency?
faqs.a: The guide will instantly evaluate the situation and offer first aid in case of need. Depending on the severity of the condition, you will rest, go down to a low altitude, seek help from the nearest health center or be evacuated by helicopter.

faqs.q: Is the mobile network signal available on the EBC trail?
faqs.a: Yes, you can have the mobile network signal at several locations in the Everest region via NTC (Nepal Telecom)  and NCELL service providers. But the coverage becomes limited and the connection may be weak or unreliable at the higher elevation points. NTC generally has better coverage than Ncell in the Everest region.

faqs.q: Can my family get in touch with me on the trek?
faqs.a:
Yes. It is possible for you to communicate with your family and friends through your mobile network or Wi-Fi. An internet connection is usually available in many tea houses on the route to Everest Base Camp.

However, you might not always get to stay in touch because of limited connectivity at high altitudes.
