reviews.body: we just did a Everest Trek with base camp adventure it was so amazing and never forget their service.

reviews.author: CatherineHumphries-Perth, Australia
reviews.body: My partner and I did the 13 day trek to Everest Base camp with Base Camp Adventure and it was amazing. Shree what great, he organised everything for us, from the minuet we arrive in Kathmandu he was there to meet us at the airport and waved us farewell after our incredible experience. Shree and the team made us feel very comfortable, safe and welcome, and went through everything pre trek. Our guide Shiva was amazing, he took care of us really well and was always there to talk things through, and play cards with us. We were even able to modify our itinerary so we could visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Statue! We would highly recommend Base Camp Adventure, Shree and his team.

reviews.author: Alexandra H
reviews.body: I booked my Everest Base Camp trek with Base Camp Adventure and I cannot fault any of my experience! Shree made sure everything was taken care of and all had been thought out. Prior to the trek I was given a full briefing of what would happen and what to expect. My guide on the trek was Shiva who was amazing and so knowledgable of our surroundings. He was friendly and always caring. Unfortunately I suffered from altitude sickness towards the end of the trip and had to be helicoptered back to Kathmandu, I made a very swift recovery but through all of this Shree and his team were by my side to ensure I was ok and to look after all the insurance details. Throughout my whole experience I felt so well looked after and cannot appreciate what they did for me enough! I would not recommend anyone but this company if you are interested in trekking in Nepal and believe me, it will be the best thing you ever do!

reviews.author: Oliver Marshall
reviews.body:
My friend and I completed our base trek from mid to late December and it was one of the most incredible experiences, if not the most incredible, that I have had in my life. This was significantly aided by our awesome guide, Jwala. He was one of the kindest and most generous men you will meet. He would fill his thermos up with hot tea just for us to drink while trekking (which is an absolute godsend when the rest of you water bottle is so cold you can barely drink it) as well as when my friend was getting sick, and it helped his throat at night. He also took heaps of awesome photos for us (my camera ran out of battery) and shard them with us through whattsapp! These are just examples which indicated how awesome he was.

He was the sort of guy who made friends where-ever he went, whether it was playing cards with us and a French couple we met along the way, or it was chatting with this dude on one of our rest stops (who he hadn't seen in 15 years!)

He was also incredibly knowledgeable about the whole area, which made you feel confident and safe, which is ultimately incredible important.

Thank you so much Base Camp Adventures (and Jwala) for such an incredible journey!

overview:
Everest Base Camp is famous as an incredible trek destination among trekkers around the globe. This adventurous Everest Base Camp trek fixed departures package from Base Camp Adventure is an excellent adventure. This wonderful trek journey will take you through significant landmarks while exploring the diverse natural trails. Trekkers will have an immense opportunity for natural as well as cultural exploration. This spectacular journey takes you to the foot of the gigantic Mt. Everest (8848.86m). Moreover, the mountain vista of Mt. Ama Dablam, Khumbutse, Pumori, Lhotse, Nuptse, Cho Oyu, etc will enthrall trekkers. The stunning beauty of Himalayan sunrise and sunsets is an experience of a lifetime. The trek is moderately complex, but anyone can easily take this trek with enough preparation. The preparation required for this trek includes proper training and packing. Trekkers will spend their nights in teahouses and lodges that provide a warm meal and a place to stay at night. While there are no fancy services, you can experience the warm welcome and hospitality in these places. The Tibetan heritage of the Sherpa ethnic community is quite evident in their lifestyle and tradition. Trekkers will trail past significant cultural landmarks, including Buddhist monasteries and chortens. Trekkers will have a spiritual experience while trekking on these trails. We are providing this incredible Everest Base Camp trek fixed departures package at a reasonable price. You can contact us to book your trip and join fellow trekkers on this outstanding trip. You might also check: Everest base camp trek with helicopter return

Highlights of the Trip

  • Exploring the beautiful landscapes of Everest Base Camp
  • Trekking on the foothills of Mount Everest massif
  • Scenic mountain flight observing the beautiful Himalayan vista of the Everest region
  • Exploring the cultural landscapes, including ancient settlements, Tibetan heritage, and traditions
  • Scenic sunrise from Kala Patthar.
  • Exploring the Tengboche monastery and its spiritual surroundings
  • Passing through Icefalls, glaciers, passes, and other natural diversities along the trail.
  • Exploration of the culture, and tradition of the Sherpa community.
  • The incredible welcome and hospitality in the teahouses

Everest Base Camp Trek Route

This Everest base camp trek fixed departure itinerary begins in Kathmandu. From Kathmandu, you will take a mountain flight to Lukla. The incredible journey will provide you with great views of natural landscapes like mountains and hills. Lukla to Phakding is our first trek section in the itinerary. You will pass through various regional settlements, including Monjo and Jorsale, to arrive at Phakding. Namche Bazaar is the next destination of our trek. The settlement of Namche Bazaar offers incredible views of the Himalayas. There are various significant landmarks, including hotels, restaurants, cafes, bars, pubs, souvenir shops, and others in the region. The trekkers will pass through the settlements of the local Sherpa community exploring their cultural heritage. You will then trek to the Tengboche and explore the religiously significant gompa in the region. The tracks then pass through the settlement of Dingboche and Lobuche. We will stay in these regions for a day before continuing trekking to Gorakshep. From Gorak Shep, we will travel to the majestic Everest Base Camp. This incredible base camp remains surrounded by snow-clad mountains. We will then explore the beautiful atmosphere of EBC. There you can find colorful tents and climbers training for the ascent of Mount Everest. Kala Patthar (5,545 m) is the most famous viewpoint from where you will get 360-degree sweeping views. The mountain peaks of Mt. Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, Cho Oyu are the gorgeous Himalayan peaks you can view from the viewpoint. We will pass through glacial paths, green hills, and forested trails tracing the earlier routes. The trail will take you through Pheriche, Namche Bazar, and Phakding to finally arrive at Lukla. Finally, your trip ends as you will take a flight from the gateway of Lukla to the capital of Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Flight from Kathmandu to Lukla and Trek to Phakding (2600m)<
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Phakding (2,600 m) Flight duration: 35-40 minutes Walk duration: 3-4 hrs Overnight: Phakding Our members of the staff will pick you up from your location, and transfer to the airport in Kathmandu. From the airport, you can take the flight to Lukla. It takes around 35-40 minutes and provides you with views of the greatest Himalayan vista. After arriving at Lukla, which is the entry point of the Everest region, you will start your trek to Everest base camp. The next step in the trekking journey is Phakding. You will arrive there passing through the incredible landscapes on the left bank of Dudh Koshi River. The trail then passes through some of the most adventurous courses. From this viewpoint, you can observe the majestic silver mountains. We will then rest after having our meal at the teahouse in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3450 m)
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Namche Bazaar (3,450 m) Walk duration: 6-7 hours Overnight: Namche Bazaar Our trek journey takes you to the beautiful settlements of Namche on this day from Phakding. Namche is a tourist hub where you can find many hotels, restaurants, cafes, bakery shops, Souvenir shops, and others. In this journey, you will find beautiful local settlements of the Sherpa community. Trekkers will have to cross numerous suspension bridges to arrive at the destination. After crossing the villages of Monjo (2,835 m), you will enter the Sagarmatha National Park premises. After completing formalities and showing your permits at the entry point, you will continue your trek. You will pass alongside the Dudh Koshi River to arrive at Jorsale. This Namche Bazaar Viewpoint is the first place where you can get a glimpse of Mt. Everest during the trek. After trekking for a couple of hours you will arrive at Namche Bazar, where you will explore the region and rest for the night at the tea house.

itinerary.title: Rest and Acclimatization at Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Namche Bazaar (3,450 m) Walk duration: 1-2 hours Overnight: Namche Bazaar On this day during your trek, you will continue to acclimatize at Namche Bazaar. The process of acclimatization is essential when it comes to high-altitude trekking. Trekkers have to face various challenges along the trails as they gain a lot of altitude in a short amount. Hence you will need to acclimatize, hydrate, and rest properly to trek without any hassle. To acclimatize in the high altitude conditions, you will hike to various points near Namche. Sir Edmund Hillary Hospital and the Sherpa museum are great exploration points. Besides that, you can also hike to the Syangboche airstrip. The airstrip provides you with an all-encompassing view of the Himalayas including Mt. Everest (8848.86m). Kusum Kanguru, Thamserku, Ama Dablam, Lhotse, Nuptse, etc are the other mountains you can observe. After exploring the beautiful region, you will return to Namche. You can explore the town’s landmarks, including restaurants, hotels, souvenir shops, and others. We will stay in Namche Bazaar for the night and prepare for the trek the next day.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche (3865 m)
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Tengboche (3,865 m) Walk duration: 5-6 hours Overnight: Tengboche We will continue our trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche on this day. We will trek early as we have to arrive at your destination before it gets dark. After waking up early and washing up, we will continue our journey by having breakfast at the tea house. On this day, we will trek through remote trails to arrive at the destination of Tengboche. The trail passes alongside Dudh Koshi River crossing various local settlements. The mountain’s views from multiple viewpoints look breathtaking. We will finally arrive at the Phunki Tenga (3,250 m) before trekking for a few hours to reach Tengboche. Tengboche monastery is a famous landmark of the village. The monastery is also known as the spiritual center of the region. The viewpoint near the monastery offers you gorgeous views of Mt. Everest (8,848 m), Ama Dablam (6,856 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), and others. Trekkers can observe the spiritual scenes of local nuns and monks chanting prayers in the evening at the monastery. After experiencing this beautiful sight, you can call it a day and rest in the teahouse in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche (4410m)
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Dingboche (4,410 m) Walk duration: 5-6 hours Overnight: Dingboche On this day of the trek, you will start your journey from Tengboche to Dingboche. The trail passes through some of the most adventurous trails to arrive at your destination in Dingboche (4,410 m). Trekkers will cross Imja Khola suspension bridges and then take an uphill climb to Pangboche village. This small village located just below the Ama Dablam (6,856 m) provides you with majestic views of the Himalayas. You will trek through various local settlements and Buddhist monasteries. Trekkers will then climb through dense juniper forested trails to arrive at their destination. After arriving at the destination, you will stay and rest in the teahouse.

itinerary.title: Rest and Acclimatization at Dingboche
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Dingboche (4,410 m) Walk duration: 1-2 hours Overnight: Dingboche On this day of the trek, you will acclimatize at Dingboche, a beautiful settlement in the region. There are various exploration points along the area where you can go on small hikes. You can visit the religious landmark of Nakartsang Gompa near the region. The viewpoint near the gompa provides trekkers with the most outstanding views of snow-clad silver mountains, including Mt. Everest (8,848 m). Makalu, Mt. Ama Dablam, Island Peak, Lhotse, Baruntse, etc look incredible from the viewpoint as well. You will then hike through various small hills around the region, passing through natural terrains. After exploring these beautiful landscapes, you will return to your tea house or lodge and rest for the night.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche (4940m)
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Lobuche (4,940 m) Walk duration: 5-6 hours Overnight: Lobuche The trail of this trek starts from Dingboche as you trek through the various challenging remote terrains to arrive at Lobuche. You will then walk through multiple local settlements of the region, including Dughla. The trails then take you through rocky glacial moraines while climbing up the hilly area. The trails then will lead you to the chorten memorial made in dedication to all the climbers who perished on their way. You will then take a beautiful climb to an icy glacier from these terrains. You will finally cross the glacier and trek for some time to arrive at a teahouse in Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche (4940m) to Everest Base Camp (5364m) via Gorakshep (5140m)
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Everest Base Camp (5,364 m) Walk duration: 4-5 hrs Overnight: Gorakshep The trail of this trek takes you on an incredible adventure on this section of the walk as you trek to EBC from Lobuche. You will travel through various rugged terrains to arrive at Gorak Shep, an old base camp. We will have lunch and keep our bags at the teahouse and then continue our journey. We will explore the beautiful region that provides an incredible adventure. The trails of this trek pass through some of the most challenging terrains. The beautiful natural diversities will make you fall in love with the place. You can enjoy the beautiful vista of Everest Base Camp and take pictures. Finally, you can return to Gorak Shep after trekking for a few hours and spend the night at a teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gorakshep to Kala Patthar (5545m), and then trek back to Pheriche (4243m)
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Kala Patthar (5,545 m) Walk duration: 6-7 hrs Overnight: Pheriche On this trekking day, we will continue our journey from Gorak Shep to Kala Pathar. Kalapathar is a beautiful viewpoint in the region from where you can observe the incredible majestic Himalayan vista, including Mount Everest. Mount Everest views are the best from this point. The Kala Patthar (5,545 m) is a beautiful viewpoint, where you will need to trek early in the morning before sunrise. Hence, you can take incredible pictures of the region. After exploring the viewpoint, you will return to Gorakshep. The incredible Himalayan vista includes sweeping views of Mt. Everest (8,848 m). We will explore the Gorakshep region before returning to Pheriche to stay overnight at a teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pheriche to Namche Bazaar (3450 m)
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Pheriche (4,243 m) Walk duration: 7-8 hrs Overnight: Namche Bazaar The trail on this trek passes through the forested trails of rhododendron and juniper trees. You will start your tour by passing through various settlements before arriving at Tengboche. You will have your lunch and then continue trekking to Namche Bazaar. The trails on this provide you with the majestic view of Lhotse (8,414 m) and Everest (8848.86 m). After arriving at the Namche Bazaar, you can explore the beautiful region and buy gifts in the souvenir shops. You will rest overnight at a teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2860m)
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Namche Bazaar (3,450 m) Walk duration: 6-8 hrs Overnight: Lukla On this trekking day, you will start your trek by passing through the downhills trails to arrive at Lukla from Namche Bazaar. The tracks then take you through rugged, remote, steep, and rocky terrain. After that, there are several various bridges through which you can cross the Dudh Koshi River. The region passes through pine-forested trails and green hills. We will observe the majestic views of the snow-capped mountains and rest in the evening.

itinerary.title: Flight from Lukla to Kathmandu
itinerary.html: Maximum altitude: Lukla (2,860 m) Flight duration: 35-40 minutes Our incredible Everest Base Camp trek fixed departures tour ends as you will leave Lukla on a scenic mountain flight to Kathmandu. The astonishing flight offers you the greatest views of snow-capped mountains. You will get transported to your location after arriving at the airport in Kathmandu.

sections.title: Best Time for the Everest Base Camp Trek
sections.html:
Best Time for the Everest Base Camp Trek

The best time for a trek in the Everest region in the high altitude Himalayas is in the Spring and Autumn. In the Autumn season, you will get beautiful blue skies and clear views of snow-capped mountains. There is great weather with an incredible climate that is perfect for trekking and traveling. Travelers can also observe beautiful cultural trails as various festivals get celebrated in the season. There are moderate daytime temperatures that range around mid 20 degrees during the day and drop to around single degrees at night. Hence, the Autumn season is perfect for this EBC trek. Spring in the region is beautiful as it is a pre-monsoon season. There is gorgeous weather with bright sunshine days. Green vegetation and colorful flowers blooming in the wild are highlights of this season. There are perfect temperatures that make this trek ideal for this season. Trekkers can complete this trek with ease as there are no challenges like landslides, avalanches, and others in the season. However, there might be clouds covering the sky on some days during the trek. In the off-seasons, the weather remains quite challenging in the high-altitude region. These challenges include avalanches, landslides, slippery trails, heavy rain, snow, and others. Hence, you should prepare well if you want to trek in the off-season. But if you want to travel safely and comfortably, you should travel in the peak season of either Autumn or Spring.

The difficulty of Everest Base Camp Trek

Any trekking adventure in the foothills of the Himalayas is generally considered difficult. And this moderately challenging trek is also quite tough. The difficulty of this trek includes various altitude issues like acute mountain sickness. Acute mountain sickness is the primary reason for the trek’s difficulty. Less oxygen and air pressure lead to difficulty in breathing, nausea, headache, etc. To avoid altitude sickness, trekkers must acclimatize well in this long duration trek. Moreover, you should also rest well and hydrate to adapt to the quickly changing conditions. One pro tip is to avoid alcoholic beverages and not climb too much in altitude. Another challenging aspect of this trek includes trekking trails that are both remote and rugged. The trails courses are quite rugged and move up and down a lot, which means that trekkers must have an intense level of fitness. To tackle this problem, trekkers must train in physical and mental exercises. Long duration of the trek can also be a challenge if you are not used to such trekking. You will have to take 5 to 6 hours a day for ten to twelve days on a stretch. Accommodations can be a problem for the trekkers as well. The trek passes through remote areas with no fancy accommodations besides local tea houses and lodges. The trekkers must compromise with their meal, stay, and accommodations. The meals in these teahouses do not have much variety as transporting ingredients is tough in this high altitude. Facilities for stay include basic rooms with beds. Toiletries need to get managed by the trekkers themselves. Hence these were the various challenges that you will encounter while trekking the Everest Base Camp.

overview:
Everest Base Camp is at the foot of the tallest mountain in the world, Mt Everest. It is situated at 5,364 m in the Khumbu region of Solukhumbu district of northeastern Nepal. Everest Base Camp is a classic trekking route that allows trekkers the privilege of standing at the base of the world’s highest mountain, with amazing views of the surrounding mountains. Trekkers have the opportunity to see snow-capped mountains in the Mahalangur Range, including Everest, Lhotse, Cho Oyu, and Makalu, all of which are above 8,000 m.

There are several options to reach Everest Base Camp, with itineraries ranging from 9 to 15 days. Among luxury options, one popular Everest trekking package is the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Return. Over 9 days, the helicopter return option offers a comfortable and luxurious experience. While the trek starts on a standard trekking route, trekkers have the option to skip the return walk and leave the Khumbu region by helicopter from Kala Patthar. The helicopter option offers an escape from the physical drain of walking during the return journey. Similarly, it offers a breathtaking aerial view of Nepal’s mountainous region, giving a completely different perspective on the adventure.

The trek starts with a flight to Lukla, which lands at the Tenzing-Hillary Airport. From there, trekkers start the EBC trek through numerous traditional Sherpa settlements. The trek passes through popular villages such as Phakding, Namche, Tengboche, Dingboche, and Lobuche, ultimately reaching Everest Base Camp. Throughout the journey, trekkers see mountains such as Mount Everest (8848.86 meters), Lhotse, Cho Oyu, Ama Dablam, Nuptse, Thamserku, Pumori, Makalu, and others. Besides the mountain views, trekkers can also see the massive Khumbu Glacier and Khumbu Icefall, which most of the climbers encounter during the Everest Expedition.

On the EBC with Heli Return, trekkers reach the highest altitude of 5,545 m at Kalapatthar. Kalapatthar is a vantage point that showcases the grandest view of Mount Everest. As Everest is blocked by Nuptse (the mountain in front of Everest) and only a part of it is visible from Everest Base Camp, Kalapatthar is the popular option to witness the best view of Everest. Similarly, Kalapatthar is known for its sunrise and sunset views. So, looking at the first rays of the sun reflecting off the white summit of Everest is sure to mesmerize any traveler. Photographs from Kalapatthar are also extraordinary, like nothing you can capture on the trekking route.

On the other hand, during the trek, trekkers will enter the protected UNESCO World Heritage Site of Sagarmatha National Park. The National Park harbors various wildlife, including the elusive Snow Leopard and Red Panda. If trekkers are lucky enough, they may see such animals. Besides that, there are opportunities to see other animals such as the Himalayan Thar, the Himalayan Monal, the Blue Sheep, and the Musk Deer.

The best seasons for the Everest Base Camp with Heli Return are Spring and Autumn. As helicopter flight requires stable, clear weather, these seasons offer clear skies that enable better flying conditions. Although the trek is possible during the off-season, which includes winter and summer, weather-related disruptions may delay the helicopter flight. So, the off-season is recommended only for experienced trekkers. Also, the trek is moderately difficult, so adventure seekers, beginner trekkers, and photographers with decent physical fitness can complete it. Now, get ready to explore the Khumbu region and blend in with the Sherpa community. Understand more about the Sherpa culture, traditions, and customs, and get the opportunity to witness Mount Everest.

itinerary.title: Fly From Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft) and trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html:
Flight Duration: 35- 40 minutesFlight Distance: 136 kmTrek Duration: 3- 4 hoursLukla Elevation: 2,860 mPhakding Elevation : 2,610 m

Your Everest Base Camp Trek with helicopter return will start through a scenic and thrilling flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. Our team will receive you from your hotel in Kathmandu and drive you to Tribhuvan International Airport. You will catch a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla from the domestic departure. The duration of the flight is around 35- 40 minutes. The flight from Kathmandu to Lukla is thrilling and exciting, rewarding you with beautiful views of forests, waterfalls, green hills and the villages. After arriving in Lukla, you can have your breakfast enjoying the beautiful scenery. Then, you will trek to Phakding which marks an official start of your adventure. You will cross suspension bridges to reach the settlements.

On the first day of your trek you will pass through beautiful villages like Cheplung and Thado Koshi. The first day itself is full of breathtaking scenery. You will get a glimpse of the Himalayan culture and experience the warm reception of the locals. The serene ambiance and the beautiful scenery will enrich your experience. Your first overnight stay will be in a beautiful village of Phakding where you get your much needed rest and be served with a delicious warm meal prepared by the hosts.

itinerary.title: Trek From Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Trek Duration: 6- 7 hours
Namche Bazar Elevation: 3,440 m

The second day of the trek requires you to cross the suspension bridge over the Dudh Koshi river witnessing the beautiful foothills of the region. After trekking for almost 2 to 3 hours you will reach Monjo Village which is a gateway to Sagarmatha National Park. which is a world heritage site and is home to diverse flora and fauna. You have to show your permit at the entrance of the Park.

As you move further, you will see a variety of plant species, pine trees and rhododendrons which creates a vibrant environment. There are many monasteries, beautiful teahouses, and villages along the trail. Your eyes will be blessed with the views of stunning peaks while trekking towards Namche Bazaar.

After covering the distance of 9.4 kilometers by foot you will reach Namche Bazaar, which is a trading center and gateway to the Himalayas. Your overnight stay on the second day will be at a guest house or lodge in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day at Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft).
itinerary.html: On the third day you are required to stay at Namche Bazar for acclimatization. Acclimatizing will help you to reduce the risk of altitude sickness. Namche Bazaar, a beautiful town nestled in the Himalayas, which is also a tourist hub offers you the gorgeous views of the surrounding mountains. Many travelers spend at least one or two days acclimatizing. After having a hearty and delicious breakfast you can explore the beautiful place. You can witness enchanting views of Mount Everest, Ama Dablam, Nuptse from this beautiful place. There are numerous stores where you can shop for any souvenir and many cafes where you can relax and enjoy your time. You can find many internet cafes in Namche Bazaar. You can explore the local areas and interact with the natives getting insights about their lifestyle. You can also visit the Sherpa Museum to learn about the culture, tradition and history of the Sherpa people. The night views of Namche Bazaar are stunning, the backdrop of the mountain is enchanting to witness. The majestic beauty of the Himalayas is phenomenal which offers tranquility. Try unique local dishes like Sherpa stew and butter tea while exploring the area. Enjoy your warm dinner and rest well in your comfortable room being prepared for exploring the beautiful landscapes of the region in the remaining part of the journey.

itinerary.title: Trek From Namche Bazaar to Tengboche Monastery (3,860 m / 12,664 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Trek Duration: 5- 6 hours
Tengboche Elevation / Tengboche Monastery: 3,860 m

On the fourth day you will start your trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche Monastery. Towards the trail to Tengboche monastery you need to walk through uphill initially followed by downhill till you reach the suspension bridge. Along the trail there are few sections of stairs, and dense forests.

Some paths are uneven and rocky which may be a bit challenging. You will find many tea shops along the trail and meet the kind locals who will always greet you with a smile. You will be rewarded with the enchanting views of Nuptse and Cho Oyu, which are the most beautiful peaks of Everest Region.

Tengboche Monastery is among the major attractions of the region which offers peace and solitude to trekkers. You will get a chance to witness the rituals and ceremonies performed by the monks. The architecture and artwork of the monastery is beautiful, representing the rich culture and history of the region. You will stay in one of the beautiful guest houses or lodges overnight.

itinerary.title: Trek From Tengboche Monastery to Dingboche (4,410 m / 14,468 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Trek Duration: 5- 6 hours
Dingboche Elevation: 4,410 m

As you trek from Tengboche monastery you first pass through a dense forest of pine trees and the beautiful wildflowers. You are required to cover a distance of 9 km and it will take around 5- 6 hours to make it to Dingboche. While trekking you will notice a change in the landscape, the trail becomes more rugged than before. You are required to pass through the flat land first and make a steep descent through the dense forests. You will need to cross the bridge of the beautiful Imja river with a beautiful view of Ama Dablam which rewards you with picturesque scenery.

After walking through the barren and rocky landscapes you will also encounter small farming settlements and get a sight of yaks grazing. You will see a beautiful Buddhist stupa surrounded by the vibrant colorful flags in the entrance of Dingboche.

You can freshen up, rest and enjoy a warm cup of tea or coffee in your guest house. You will be served with a hearty and nutritious dinner helping you to restore the energy. You will stay overnight in Dingboche to get the required rest.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization in Dingboche (4,410 m / 14,468 ft), day trip to Chukkung Valley (optional).
itinerary.html:
After having breakfast at Dingboche , you will make a day trip to the Chukkung Valley which is also called a lodge valley. You are required to stop in the valley for the acclimatization and adapt to the climate. This short hiking will help you adjust in the high altitude zones reducing the risk of getting altitude sickness. You will ascend gradually through the stone walled fields.

As you arrive in Chukkung valley your eyes will be blessed with the views of Lhotse, Ama Dablam, Island peak, Makalu and other surrounding peaks. You will stay in the beautiful Chukkung Valley which is remote and full of pristine landscapes.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche (4,910 m / 16,109 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Trek Duration: 5- 6 hours
Lobuche Elevation: 4,910 m

On the seventh day you will need to trek to Lobuche which requires you to cover a distance of 10.61 km. You will be rewarded with the mesmerizing sights as the whole surrounding is breathtakingly beautiful. It is advised to trek slowly as this is a high-altitude zone.

You will be able to witness breathtaking views throughout the trail. You are required to walk up to slightly inclined paths in this trail. Walking through the challenging wavy path you will finally reach Thugla pass.

After taking gradual ascents along the route you will reach Lobuche, which lies at an elevation of 4,940 m You will stay at a comfortable lodge in Lobuche overnight. You will be served with a warm and hearty meal which will help you to gain energy.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche to Gorak Shep (5,164 m / 16,942 ft) and continue to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m / 17,598 ft). After exploring Base Camp, retrace the trail to Gorak Shep for an overnight stay.
itinerary.html:
Trek Duration: 7-8 hours
Everest Base Camp Elevation: 5,364 m
Gorakshep Elevation: 5,164 m

You will trek to Everest Base Camp on the eighth day of your trek. It is highly advisable to start the trek early in the morning. Your first destination is Gorakshep which will be your last stop before moving towards Everest Base Camp.

You will get a glimpse of the Nuptse and other snow covered peaks along the trail. It takes around 3 hours to reach Gorakshep. Passing through the rough and uneven path you will finally reach Gorakshep and settle for lunch.

After lunch in Gorakshep, you will traverse along the ridge of the Khumbu Glacier towards the Everest Base Camp. You will be rewarded with the stunning views of mountains and valleys along the trail. You will pass through the rocky terrains as you progress towards the base camp.

You will witness the magnificent view of Mount Everest and Nuptse when you finally make it to the base camp. The surreal sight of Khumbu glacier and Khumbu icefall is phenomenal to witness. After seeing the amazing sights of the stunning landscapes you will now return back to Gorakshep where you will stay overnight.

itinerary.title: Trek to Kala Patthar (5,545 m / 18,192 ft) and return Gorakshep and fly to Kathmandu by Helicopter.
itinerary.html:
Trek Duration: 1-2 hours
Flight Duration: 1:30-2 hours
Kala Patthar Elevation: 5,445 m

Day 9 is an exciting day for the trekkers as they will have to advance to the highest point - Kala Patthar, which stands at 5,644 m Kala Patthar offers one of the best experiences of this entire trek. It is the viewpoint of Mt. Everest and a very popular spot for viewing the sunset which extends trekkers with a sensation of warmth and treats them with a golden glow magical moment.

The starting point of the ninth day is Gorakshep. This is where you will leave all your belongings and start hiking up. As you start your hike, you will pass through a sandy landscape. The path is not so difficult for some time before you reach Kala Patthar, you will even get to experience the magical view of Pumori mountains among the hills.

The trek is rather short but the trail gets rocky mid-way, so you might want to look out and safely ascend while taking your time so as to avoid any kind of injuries. It will only take you a few hours to reach your destination, Kala Patthar, which is also the highest point of your entire Everest Base Camp trip. As a matter of fact, you will see the entire Everest region much closer than anywhere else. The highest peak in the world, covered with snow, offers you the best experience and will make your trip worth the effort you put in.

Several other stunning mountains can also be seen from this viewpoint. The place is also popular for the Glaciers and Lake view. All these aspects add up and make your trekking experience the most beautiful one. You might want to stay at Kala Patthar for a while and soak up all the beauty of the most amazing view and take lots of pictures of your achievement.

Soon afterwards, you will have to descend to Gorakshep, the starting point of today's journey. After a long walk and the amazing experience, you will be served with a wholesome breakfast before you head further down with all your belongings, to where the helicopter rests in Gorak shep. This is where you will take Helicopter flight to Kathmandu which will take approximately 1:30 hours. However, it is important to note that the flight time is determined by the weather condition of that particular day and hence, can fluctuate.

Everest base camp trek with helicopter return rewards you with the bird eye view of the Everest Region. This provides you with a time to relax and chill, while enjoying the broader aspect and the entire landscape of the Everest Region at a single glance.

sections.title: Why Choose Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return?
sections.html:
For many, the uphill trek to Everest base camp itself can be extremely tiring, and they may be unable to walk the way back. For others, there may not be enough time. Having a return trip on a helicopter instead of walking the entire path back on foot can be both safer and time-saving. And as a bonus, you get to see the majestic mountains in the Himalayan region from an eagle-eye view.

Thrilling Adventure

Everest Base Camp Trek requires you to walk through challenging terrain. You will pass through lush green forests, crossing multiple suspension bridges. You need to walk uphill, downhill and rocky terrain throughout your journey. Crossing the suspension bridge creates bouncy sensations, and many trekkers have described this feeling as epic, particularly when they experience it for the first time. Walking through dense forests, in uneven terrains can be intriguing to many trekkers which is a thrilling adventure.

Views of Majestic Mountains

The trails of Everest Base camp are renowned for its picturesque landscapes which rewards you with the views of majestic mountains. You will get to witness the stunning views of snow covered mountains throughout your journey. The spectacular views of Mt. Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Amadablam, Thamserku and many more are visible throughout the journey. The aerial views of the mountains and villages visible while returning from the helicopter are magnificent.

Exploring Cultural Gems of the Region

Trekking in Everest Base Camp you will get an opportunity to explore the lifestyle of the people living in the mountain region. The region is home to Sherpa people, who are known for their outstanding mountaineering skills and warm reception. They hold a deep respect and admiration for the mountains.

You will have a chance to explore their rich culture which will enrich your trekking experience. The traditional villages, their customs, their food and generosity will help you gain a new perspective of life. You will also get a chance to witness many monasteries on the route of Everest Base Camp which will provide you insight on the faith and beliefs of the local people. The tranquil atmosphere of the surrounding will elevate your inner peace.

The sherpas are practitioners of Tibetan Buddhism. You will get to witness many colorful prayer flags along the trail which holds a strong belief in the Buddhist community. The vibrant prayer flags along the trail are believed to spread goodwill, blessings, peace and prosperity. They celebrate Mani Rimdu, a vibrant festival of the Everest Region which is celebrated in the tenth month of the Tibetan Calendar, ( October and November). They pray, perform masked dances and feast during the festival. They believe that the festival will bring blessings, peace and prosperity to the region. The rich culture, the history, the serenity of the region and the warm reception of the locals will captivate your heart, make your journey more intriguing.

A Visual Treat

Everest Base Camp Trek with helicopter return is a visual treat to your eyes. Your eyes will be blessed by the beautiful scenery throughout your journey. The picturesque landscape, the charming villages that look surreal are truly the wonders of this region which creates unforgettable memories for the visitors. The blooming rhododendrons in the forests make the whole environment vibrant, enhancing the beauty of the surrounding. All the stopovers along the trail will present you with the mesmerizing sights.

The region is also the paradise for the photographers as they get to capture beautiful landscapes which look unreal. They can get the masterpiece shots capturing the rare moments that will create a huge impact on the viewers letting them witness the beauty of the mountains in still cuts. Each and every pathway is scenic which creates a picturesque setting. The panoramic view of the vistas, pristine beauty of the valley truly offers an aesthetically pleasing environment. The region is blessed with mesmerizing sights, making visitors feel fulfilled.

When is the best time for Everest Base Camp with Helicopter Return?

The best times for the EBC with the helicopter trek are spring and autumn. Spring lasts from March to May, and Autumn lasts from September to November. These seasons are considered the best among all other seasons because of their stable weather and moderate temperatures. The skies are clear during these months, which provide the best view of the mountains. Also, neither too hot nor too cold temperatures make walking comfortable. These seasons also provide safe walking conditions without the risk of flooding, landslides, or other natural disasters.

Spring (March to May)

The spring season marks the end of winter, so the trails filled with snow and ice begin to melt. The forest areas in the lower regions come alive with rhododendron in full bloom and lush greenery. The vegetation adds beauty to the mountain peaks, clearly visible on the horizon. The average daily temperature is around 15 °C, and it may drop to -5 °C at night. Also, there is little to no chance of rainfall, so slippery trails and insect or leech infestations are minimal.

However, as one of the best seasons, the Everest Base Camp trekking route can be crowded with a large number of visitors trekking during these months. The sense of solitude may be lost, and accommodation options can fill up quickly. In such cases, it is necessary to book in advance with a reliable company like Base Camp Adventure, which will arrange all accommodation.

Autumn (September to November)

Autumn begins with the end of the monsoon. The heavy rain that used to persist during the monsoon season subsides in autumn, leaving a clear, visible path. The autumn season offers the best visibility and moderate temperatures, making for a comfortable walking experience.

The daytime temperature in the region is around 14 °C, and it may drop to -10°C at night. So for the night, proper warm clothes are still essential. Also, autumn is regarded as the best of all trekking seasons. This is because it aligns with Nepalese festivals. Nepal’s grand festivals like Dashain and Tihar are celebrated during the autumn season, which allows for a better cultural understanding than anything else. In the Everest area, festivals like Mani Rimdu are celebrated in the Autumn season. So trekkers can participate in the daily rituals, enjoy grand feasts, music, masked dances, and prayers, and gain a complete experience of the mountain's traditions and customs.

Off Season (Monsoon and Winter)

Monsoon/Summer lasts from June to August, and Winter lasts from December to February. These months are often regarded as the off-season in Nepal, when trekking activity is at a minimum. Due to harsh climatic conditions, trekking in such seasons is potentially dangerous and is only recommended for experienced individuals. Summer marks the onset of heavy rainfall, which makes the trails slippery. At higher altitudes, rain can convert to ice and snow, making navigation difficult. In the absence of rain, the temperature can reach up to 20 °C during the day, which makes walking difficult and can quickly exhaust trekkers. Also, during heavy rainfall, avalanches, landslides, and floods can occur frequently in prone areas. So safety is a crucial concern.

On the other hand, winter brings extreme cold condition where temperature can easily reach below freezing point. High altitude places like Everest Base Camp and Kalapatthar can face temperature up to -20°C. Walking in such temperatures is extremely difficult and can cause problems such as hypothermia and frostbite. Due to poor visibility, mountain views are obstructed, and emergency evacuation, if necessary, can be delayed. Also, due to bad weather, the helicopter return option may be delayed or even canceled. So it is necessary to add some buffer days if you are intending to trek during such seasons. However, there are still perks of trekking in the off-season. The trails are quiet and peaceful, with very few trekkers traveling. Accommodation options become readily available, and costs can be lower due to lower demand.

Accommodation Options Available During the Everest Base Camp Heli Return Trek

The accommodation option in the Everest Region varies according to the location. While the lower areas like Lukla, Phakding, Namche, and Dingboche can provide comfortable sleeping options, higher-altitude areas like Lobuche and Gorakshep have only basic accommodation facilities. Throughout the lower region, accommodation options can range from normal teahouses to luxury resorts. However, in places like Lobuche and Gorakshep, the only available options are the teahouses.

Teahouses are the most basic accommodation options available in the Everest trek. These places typically have local owners and provide at least a bed and a blanket. A typical teahouse room has two single beds and often a shared bathroom. So, private bathroom facilities are not available and are mostly built outside of the teahouse. Due to its minimal facilities, teahouses are the cheapest available option for an overnight stop. Also, in Lobuche and Gorakshep, trekkers need to stay at these teahouses, as other accommodation options are not available due to their remote, rural setting.

But if you want upgraded accommodation with private bathrooms, lodges can be a suitable option. Lodges have twin-sharing rooms with a communal dining area. Also, these options offer hot showers and Wi-Fi, which can come in handy during the trek. Depending on the lodge, the rooms are equipped with an attached bathroom and electricity. Also, some provide hot water, electric blankets, charging, and heating, but using these amenities may incur an extra cost.For the most luxurious options, resorts are available in larger settlements like Namche and Dingboche. Resorts are the most expensive option, where Wi-Fi, electricity, hot showers, electric blankets, and charging are included in the room cost. You will find the highest level of hospitality in these places, ensuring a comfortable and luxurious overnight stay.

Note: Camping is allowed but not necessarily required for the Everest Base Camp trek. Camping is permitted only in designated areas and is not permitted inside the Sagarmatha National Park. Camping requires more logistical preparation, but if interested, please get in touch with Base Camp Adventures.

Food Options During the EBC Trek

Dal Bhat is the most stable and common food option for trekkers in the Everest region. Most teahouses and lodges serve Dal Bhat, especially for dinner. Dal Bhat (Rice with Lentil Soup) is also the national dish of Nepal and represents a balanced diet, helping you regain your strength after a long, tiring walk. Western food options such as pizza, burgers, Apple Pie, Pasta, French Fries, and omelets are also available, especially in towns like Namche.

What are the Permits Essential For Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return?

Two permits are essential for trekkers who wish to undertake the EBC trek. These permits are the Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit and the Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit.

1. Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit

This permit is required to enter the protected area of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Sagarmatha National Park. The permit can be acquired at the Nepal Tourism Board Office in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, or at the Monjo Check post. Similarly, these permits are checked at the national park entry gate in Monjo. If you do not have this permit, then you will not be allowed to enter the region. Also, the cost of the permit depends on the nationality, which is as follows:

  • For SAARC Nationals: NRs 2,000 per person, excluding VAT.
  • For Foreign Nationals: NRs 3000 per person, excluding VAT.

2. Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit

This is a local permit issued by the local Khumbu community and has thereby replaced the Trekker’s Information Management (TIMS) Card. The authorized permit helps fund tourist infrastructure and supports rural development and cultural conservation projects in the Khumbu region. You can obtain the permit at the Lukla or Monjo checkpoints. The cost of the permit also depends on the nationality, which is as follows:

  • SAARC countries and China: NRs 2,000 per person.
  • Other Countries: NRs 3,000 per person.

Likewise, if you are traveling with Base Camp Adventures, the company will obtain these permits on your behalf to ensure a smooth experience.

3. Other Necessary Documents Required to Obtain the Permit

  • Original Passport
  • Passport Photocopy
  • Passport-Sized Photographs
  • Nepal Visa Details
  • Trekking Itinerary
  • Travel Insurance Details
  • Emergency Contact Details

Note: Obtaining the TIMS Card in not mandatory, as it has been replaced by the local permit.

Altitude Sickness During the EBC Trek with Helicopter Return

The maximum altitude you will reach during the trek is 5,545 m, where the chances of altitude sickness exist. The occurrence of altitude sickness does not depend on physical fitness, so even physically fit trekkers are susceptible if they ascend too quickly. Also, the main cause of altitude sickness is the persistent low oxygen levels at high altitudes. If your body fails to adapt to low oxygen levels, you may develop altitude sickness, or Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS). So trekkers are advised to walk slowly at a natural pace while maintaining proper acclimatization procedures.

What are the Symptoms of Altitude Sickness?

  • Headache
  • Nausea
  • Vomiting
  • Difficulty in Breathing
  • Difficulty in Sleeping
  • Fatigue
  • Dizziness
  • Loss of appetite

If these symptoms persist for multiple days, then you must apply countermeasures to reduce the risk of altitude sickness.

How to Prevent Altitude Sickness in Everest Base Camp?

Here are a list of things you must do to prevent (or at least minimise) altitude sickness during your trip to Everest Base Camp:

  • Slow ascend
  • Follow the planned acclimatization schedule.
  • Avoid pushing higher when experiencing altitude-sickness symptoms.
  • Stay adequately hydrated without forcing excessive amounts of water.
  • Eat regular, balanced meals.
  • Avoid alcohol during the trek.
  • Maintain a comfortable trekking pace.
  • Inform the guide immediately if symptoms appear.
  • Discuss natural altitude-related illness remedies, such as garlic soup.

However, if altitude sickness is not taken seriously, it can take life-threatening forms. These include High-Altitude Cerebral Edema and High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema.

Common Altitude Sickness Complications

EBC visitors may suffer from two types of altitude sickness complications:

1. High Altitude Cerebral Edema (HACE)

It is one of the more complex forms of altitude sickness, in which fluids build up in the brain after the body fails to adapt to low oxygen levels.

2. High Altitude Pulmonary Edema (HAPE)

It is another complex form of altitude sickness in which fluids build up in the lungs after the body fails to adapt to low oxygen levels. In such severe cases, the only prevention is to drop to a lower elevation and reach a nearby medical facility. In most cases, emergency helicopter evacuation is required, and purchasing travel insurance is a must.

Is Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return Difficult?

The Everest Base Camp Trek is moderately difficult. While the return trip requires no effort because of the helicopter ride, the trek to EBC requires walking for multiple days over uneven terrain as you progress to high altitude. So the trek does demand some level of physical fitness. Trekkers who are not fit enough for long walks that include about 6-7 hours daily may find the trek difficult.

Some of the factors to consider for the difficulty are as follows:

Altitude

Trekkers reach an elevation of 5,545 m on foot. So at this elevation, low oxygen levels come into play, making each step taken difficult. Thus, to cope with the altitude challenge, the Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return includes two acclimatization days in the itinerary, allowing trekkers to adapt to low oxygen levels. However, if the altitude concerns are not taken seriously, then complications like HACE and HAPE can cause life-threatening effects.

Long Walking Days

Trekkers need to walk for 5-7 hours regularly for 8 days. Some days can be longer. While distance may not seem to be the problem, consecutive days of walking can make the trek feel tiring. It drains the body, and at altitude, the trek becomes physically demanding. Trekkers also need to walk on uneven terrain, starting from forested areas to more open, rugged, glaciated terrain at high altitudes.

Weather Condition

The mountain weather can change very fast. At high altitudes year-round, cold temperatures persist. The temperature requires thick layers of clothes, which makes walking difficult. Similarly, the wind, snow, clouds, and reduced visibility can make the conditions even worse. Problems like hypothermia and frostbite can occur if you are not careful enough.

Physical Fitness

You do not need any extensive training for the trek. However, a reasonable level of fitness is required. Although no mountaineering skills are required, trekkers must be accustomed to walking long distances while carrying a backpack. It is important to focus the training on cardio. Hiking, walking, stair climbing, swimming, running, or cycling are popular exercises to prepare for the trek.

Mental Endurance

Along with physical fitness, trekkers need to be mentally prepared. Trekking is not a luxury holiday option. It is in a remote setting with limited infrastructure. Things may not go according to your plan. Maybe you may not like the food or the bathroom facilities. With altitude, you may get irritated fast. However, it is important to know what you have signed up for. Keeping realistic expectations and patience is necessary.

How to Prepare for the Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return?

Our Base Camp Adventure guides recommend the following activities to prepare for your EBC trek with helicopter return:

  1. Build fitness: Train for 6-8 weeks with cardio and strength exercises.
  2. Practice hiking: Take regular 5-7 hour hikes on uphill and uneven terrain.
  3. Strengthen your legs: Focus on squats, lunges and step-ups.
  4. Prepare for altitude: Follow a gradual itinerary with proper acclimatization.
  5. Walk steadily: Maintain a slow, comfortable pace and avoid overexertion.
  6. Pack suitable gear: Bring proper trekking boots, warm layers, trekking poles and essential equipment.
  7. Stay hydrated: Drink water regularly and limit alcohol.
  8. Eat well: Choose regular, nutritious meals to maintain energy.
  9. Prepare mentally: Expect cold weather, fatigue and challenging walking days.
  10. Plan for the flight: Keep your schedule flexible because helicopter operations depend on weather and visibility.

Travel Insurance for Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return

As you are traveling to a high altitude, getting travel insurance can safeguard against any unforeseen circumstances. Although purchasing travel insurance is not mandatory, it is highly recommended. In the event of physical injury, loss of baggage, or trip interruption, your travel insurance will remain in effect. However, travel insurance comes in many forms, which can sometimes create confusion. Trekkers need to purchase insurance that specifically covers high-altitude trekking, altitude-related illness, or helicopter evacuation. Here is what your travel insurance should cover:

  1. High-altitude trekking: Confirm that your insurance covers up to 5,545 m
  2. Helicopter Evacuation: The policy should explicitly mention emergency helicopter evacuation and not just general medical evacuation.
  3. Altitude Sickness: The policy must cover certain altitude sickness conditions, such as HAPE and HACE.
  4. Emergency Medical Treatment: It should cover medical bills for injuries or illnesses.
  5. Trip Cancellation: The policy should protect you against any sudden cause that will hinder your trip.
  6. Flight Delays and Cancellations: Lukla flights or Helicopter flights are weather-dependent. Your policy should cover any delays or cancellations of flights.
  7. Lost or Damaged Baggage: Travel Insurance should cover loss or damage to personal belongings and trekking equipment.

Note: Purchasing travel insurance is mandatory in the event of an emergency helicopter evacuation. If you do not have travel insurance, then the company is not liable for a helicopter evacuation.*

Some Tips for Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return

1. Take care of your nutrition and stay hydrated.

It is highly recommended to maintain a healthy diet for better energy levels. Trek requires you to cover a lot of distance on foot which requires a good amount of energy. Incorporating nutritious food in your diet is required for building stamina which is essential for trekking. Consume right calories which will help you to sustain and maintain your energy level throughout the journey. Make sure to carry energy snacks, dried fruits as they are easy to carry and will help you to gain energy during the journey. It is recommended to carry a reusable water bottle and refill it often. Drink enough water and stay hydrated to minimize the risk of altitude sickness.

2. Do your research before you go.

It is extremely essential to stay prepared for all the challenges once you decide to embark on this journey. Having knowledge about the kind of trails you are walking on, the difficulty level of trek, the weather conditions of the region will help you to conclude the journey smoothly as intended. Before embarking on any journey, especially while trekking you must know about the routes, and decide if you can take up the journey or not.

Researching also will help to gain proper understanding of the local culture and rules that need to be followed while exploring the region. Doing your own research helps you make more informed decisions. Being aware about the potential obstacles will help you be well prepared to find effective solutions and increase your problem solving ability.

3. Stay well informed about all the rules.

Following the rules and the relegation is extremely important during the trekking. You should be well informed about all the guidelines and need to follow them accordingly. Make sure to follow the designated routes, trek slowly, be respectful to the locals and obtain the necessary permits. Make sure to bring vital documents like your passport, visa etc.

4. Check weather forecasts.

Weather in the mountain region can change quickly so it is essential to be prepared for any changes and make plans accordingly. It is advisable to embark on trek only checking the weather conditions and be ready to adjust your schedule if required. You should look for reliable sources or take advice from the experts before and during trekking. Make sure to pack essential items, especially the rain gear and protect it from moisture to have a safe trekking experience. Make sure to follow your guide’s advice as they are knowledgeable about the weather conditions and challenges and will inform you if it’s unfavorable to trek on any day.

5. Communicate well with your guides.

Initiating communication with the guides is essential for smooth completion of the trek. Guides are well experienced and have all the knowledge about the terrains, the paths and the possible challenges. Thus, communicating with guides can ensure you the much needed assistance. They will inform you about the challenging terrains, about the distance you need to cover in a day, and listen to your concerns. Communicating well will also help guides to know about your preferences so that they can make the arrangements accordingly.

They will share the interesting stories and facts about the culture, customs and tradition which will help you to develop a better understanding of the region. Interacting throughout the journey makes the trek engaging, interesting and enjoyable.

Safety Tips for Helicopter Return

After completing your trek, you will be returning by helicopter. You will be rewarded with the enchanting views of the beautiful landscapes and snow-covered mountains. Your eyes will be blessed witnessing the natural beauty of the stunning landscapes through the helicopter. While on a helicopter, there are some safety rules which are essential to ensure a safe tour.Some of the safety guidelines for the helicopter return are as follows:

  • Fasten your seat belt.
  • Put your cell phone on flight mode during the flight.
  • Follow the instructions given by the helicopter crew.
  • Be informed about the emergency procedures.
  • Make sure to stay well hydrated.
  • Know the emergency exits.
  • Inform the helicopter crew if you feel any discomfort.
  • Avoid smoking and drinking during your flight.

Training and Exercises Needed for the Trek

Trekking in Everest Base Camp requires a certain level of physical fitness. In this trek you are required to walk a variety of trails, ascent and descent. So, training yourself well is very essential before embarking on this journey. By training yourself you can improve your fitness level, develop stamina, develop your mental health, reduce risk of any possible injuries and improve your ability to perform daily activities. It will help you conclude the trek safely as intended. Some training and exercises you can incorporate before starting the trek are as follows - :

Strength Exercises

Gentle, consistent strength exercises can enhance your balance, lessen any discomfort and improve the strength required for the trek. Some examples of strength exercises are:

  • Squats
  • Step - Ups
  • Plank
  • Toe Stands
  • Gripping
  • Deadlift
  • Glute Bridge
  • Walking Lunges
  • Calf Raises
  • Bicep Curl
  • Overhead Press
  • Toe Stands
  • Push -ups
  • Pull -ups

Cardiovascular Exercises

Cardiovascular exercises improve your blood circulation to enhance oxygen delivery and metabolism to boost the immune system & raise energy levels. You should always start these exercises slowly and pick up the pace once you feel comfortable:

  • Walking
  • Jogging
  • Dancing
  • Cycling
  • Swimming
  • Jumping Rope
  • Hiking
  • Rowing
  • Climbing Stairs
  • Jumping Jacks
  • Golfing
  • Martial Arts

Balance Exercises

Balance exercises improve flexibility, stability and balance, so that you become capable of walking through uneven terrains. Some of the balance exercises are:

  • Single Leg Stands
  • Side Lunges
  • Heel to Toe Walk
  • Yoga Poses
  • Balance Beam Walk
