faqs.q: Where Does the Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return Begin?
faqs.a: The starting point of the Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return is Lukla. You usually reach the starting point from Kathmandu by taking a short flight. Lukla is the entry point of the Everest region. Many treks in the Everest region begin from Lukla.

faqs.q: How Is the Helicopter Return from Everest Base Camp Arranged?
faqs.a: If you book the EBC return with helicopter trek package with us, we will book the helicopter flight. Once you trek to Everest Base Camp successfully the helicopter picks you up from Gorakshep and drops you off either in Kathmandu or any other designated place.

faqs.q: Can I Fly by Helicopter Directly From Everest Base Camp to Kathmandu?
faqs.a: No. Commercial flights cannot take off directly from the Everest Base Camp. During this trek, you will first visit Everest Base Camp from Gorakshep and the next day, you will visit Kala Patthar, return to Gorakshep again and take a helicopter flight back to Kathmandu.

faqs.q: Where Will My Main Luggage Stay During the Trek?
faqs.a:
Your main luggage will be carried by porters safely between the locations. All you need is a smaller backpack where you can pack basic necessities required for the days trek.

Your main luggage will be handled by porter while you can focus on enjoying breathtaking Himalayan scenery without worrying about having to lift heavy loads.

faqs.q: What Happens if Lukla Flight Is Cancelled?
faqs.a: In case the Lukla flight gets cancelled, we arrange the next available flight. You may need to wait until the situation improves because flights are highly weather dependent and are operated only when the weather is clear. So it is advisable to allocate some extra days in your schedule.

faqs.q: Is The Helicopter Return Included In The Trek Cost?
faqs.a: Yes. It is included in EBC trek package cost. Our Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return package covers scheduled helicopter flight back after completing the trek. You won’t need to arrange return helicopter separately.

faqs.q: Can I Request A Private Helicopter Instead Of A Shared Flight?
faqs.a: Yes, it is possible to have a private helicopter. This option will give you more freedom and comfort to you in comparison with a shared helicopter. It is relatively more costly than a shared flight. But it offers more flexibility and privacy. By choosing a private helicopter you can ensure a personalized travel experience.

faqs.q: Can I Extend My Stay In The Everest Region Before Returning By Helicopter?
faqs.a: Yes. You can extend your trip to the Everest region before your departure back via the helicopter. If you wish to extend then please inform us beforehand so that we can make arrangements accordingly.

faqs.q: How Many Days Ahead Should I Arrive in Nepal Prior to the Trek?
faqs.a: We recommend that you arrive in Kathmandu 2 or at least 1 day before your trek. This way you will have enough time to meet with your trekking crew and prepare everything. In case your schedule allows, we advise you to arrive in Nepal 2 days ahead of your trek to explore the beautiful city area.

faqs.q: Is it Possible to Get Visa in Arrival in Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. Nepal issues on arrival visas for most nationalities. But the eligibility depends on your nationality. Travelers from certain nations may have to obtain visa in advance. So before travelling to Nepal check latest requirements for your country. This helps you avoid delays at immigration.

faqs.q: What Are the Different Validity Periods of Tourist Visa for Nepal?
faqs.a: The tourist visas offered by Nepal come in different validity periods. You have options ranging from 15 days, 30 days to 90 days tourist visa for Nepal. This way, you get to pick the duration based on the length of your stay.

faqs.q: Can I Get My Tourist Visa Extended?
faqs.a: It is possible. If you want to stay beyond visa duration then you may apply for visa extension. You can visit Department of immigration in Kathmandu or Pokhara for visa extension.

faqs.q: How Difficult is Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
The Everest Base Camp's difficulty level is moderate to challenging. Climbing or technical skills are not necessary. However, being physically fit is essential.

Trekkers will need to trek for about 5 to 7 hours a day on rough paths. In addition, they will have to make steep climbs on rocky terrain. So, it is essential to train properly for the trek by doing hikes, cardio and strength workouts.

faqs.q: Is the Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return Ideal for Beginners?
faqs.a:
Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return is ideal for fit beginners. However, beginners must be ready to walk for days at high altitudes. While it is beneficial to have some trekking experience it is not mandatory.

Acclimatization, proper pace and training before journey are crucial. It ensures a smooth completion of the journey.

faqs.q: Is Helicopter Return Everest Base Camp Trek Easier Than the Standard Route?
faqs.a:
The Helicopter Return Everest Base Camp Trek can be considered relatively easier compared to the regular trek. 

While you will still trek to Everest Base Camp, you will be flying back during the return journey which means you will hike for fewer days than the standard trek and also get to minimize physical exertion while saving time.

faqs.q: What Are the Main Challenges of the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
Some of major challenges of Everest Base Camp Trek are high altitude, trekking for long hours, walking on steep paths and facing varying weather conditions in the mountains.

Nevertheless all these difficulties can be overcome through right preparation, acclimatization and careful navigation.

faqs.q: When are Best Times for Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return?
faqs.a:
The best times for EBC trek with heli return are during Autumn (September–November) and Spring (March–May). These months generally offer stable weather. In addition, during these seasons, the mountain visibility is good and trails are well defined, rewarding trekkers with a delightful navigation experience.

Also, the calm weather of Autumn and Spring presents better conditions for trekking as well as helicopter flights without any kind of disruptions. So, for a smooth adventure, it is highly recommended to trek in the spring and Autumn months.

faqs.q: How Are Weather-Related Helicopter Delays Handled?
faqs.a:
In case the helicopter flight gets delayed due to bad weather operators usually wait for  weather to become clear enough for a safe flight. 

If this cannot happen on the same day, the flight can be rescheduled for another convenient date. It is always better to be flexible with your schedule considering that mountain weather changes quite quickly.

faqs.q: Is The Everest Base Camp Trek Possible During The Monsoon Season?
faqs.a:
Yes. It is possible to do the trek in Nepal during the monsoon period but it is not considered an ideal time. Monsoon brings heavy rain and cloud cover. The visibility can also be affected at this time and there is a high chance of potential disruptions to helicopter flights.

Furthermore, during this season, trails will be slippery and muddy. Also, there may be leeches on the forested sections because of wet conditions. So, those planning to undertake the journey must learn about the challenges of this time and head out only when conditions are safe.

faqs.q: What Weather Conditions Can I Expect During Winter?
faqs.a:
During winter, the Everest Region's weather is very cold. Some higher section trails can be covered with snow and the surroundings can be windy. Though the winter season presents clear skies, excellent mountain views and fewer trekkers, the cold conditions require proper warm clothing and preparation.

In addition, in this season it is equally crucial to inquire about the trail conditions, check the weather in real time and start the day’s trek only after confirming that trails are safe to traverse at this time.

faqs.q: Can Seasonal Weather Disrupt The Helicopter Return Flight?
faqs.a:
Yes. Seasonal weather can disrupt helicopter return flights. Rain, snow, wind, clouds, fog, and poor visibility are the factors that lead to flight delays or cancellations. The highest possibility is during monsoons, while winters can bring cold related issues. 

However, weather is checked regularly and flights are conducted only when the weather is favourable and visibility is good.

faqs.q: Which are Best Months for Clear Mountain Views?
faqs.a:
The best months for clear views of Mount Everest during the Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return is October. This is because at this time weather is usually dry and clear after the end of the monsoon period when the rain clears up all the dust from the atmosphere. So, you can see distinct views of Everest and other nearby peaks. 

November is another good month known for crisp mornings and spectacular mountain views. Other months where you get to see stunning mountain views are March, April and May of spring.

faqs.q: Which Permits Are Required for the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: In order to undertake EBC Trek, you will have to acquire a Sagarmatha National Park Permit and Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit. At Base Camp Adventure, we handle paperwork for our clients. We acquire the necessary permits required for this journey on behalf of our clients.

faqs.q: Are There Permit Checkpoints on Everest Base Camp Route?
faqs.a: Yes. Permits are checked at different checkpoints along the route. Officials will need to verify your permits. As our guides will be accompanying you, they will help you to get them verified along the route, making sure that your navigation experience remains hassle free.

faqs.q: Do I Need Travel Insurance?
faqs.a:
Yes. It is advisable that you buy travel insurance policy that covers high altitude trekking before going to the Everest Base Camp. High altitude trekking does present certain uncertainties like unpredictable weather, altitude related emergencies and possible delays in flights.

Having the right insurance policy will help you reduce financial issues if you need assistance during unexpected situations while trekking in the Everest region.

faqs.q: What Should the Travel Insurance for EBC Trek with Heli Return Cover?
faqs.a: For the EBC trek we recommend that you buy the insurance policy that provides coverage for high altitude trekking. It should cover emergency medical treatment, helicopter evacuation, trip interruption/ cancellation, flight delay and lost baggage.

faqs.q: Are Trekking Equipment Rentals Available in Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Yes. There are many stores/ shop that provide rental facilities in Kathmandu especially in the Thamel area. Hiring trekking gear is convenient and affordable as alternative for those who do not wish to buy expensive equipment and carry gear from their hometown.

faqs.q: What Clothing Should I Pack for the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
For EBC trek with helicopter return, you should pack in layers. This helps you easily cope with changes in temperature at different locations. Make sure to carry base layers, warm middle layers, water proof outer layers, trekking pants and good quality down jacket in case it gets cold at night.

In addition, you should also pack socks, gloves, beanie and sun hats. Choose lightweight and quick drying clothing. The weather conditions become colder as you ascend and it is important to pack warm clothes to protect yourself from wind, rain and snow.

faqs.q: What Essentials Should I Carry in My Daypack for Everest Base Camp?
faqs.a:
In your daypack, you may store all essentials that are needed throughout the day hike. 

The porter will be handling the main luggage and in your daypack you may store snacks, sunscreen, sunglasses, lip balm, light jacket, gloves, hat, water bottle, medicines, small first-aid kit, some tissues, sanitizer, passport, permits and a power bank. 

Make sure to carry a light daypack with comfortable straps for smooth navigation along the Khumbu trail.

faqs.q: Can I Bring My Own Sleeping Bag?
faqs.a:
Yes. You can carry your own sleeping bag. Many trekkers feel much more comfortable with their own sleeping bag. However, if you don't have one, you may request it from us and return it after the completion of the journey. 

A good sleeping bag is essential for high altitude trekking adventures like EBC trek with helicopter return because the upper section of the trail is usually on the colder side and blankets may not be sufficient to keep you warm.

faqs.q: Which Medicines and First Aid Supplies Should I Pack for the Trek?
faqs.a:
You may carry small first aid kit with you on the trek. You may consider packing blister patches, bandages, antiseptic wipes and painkillers. Make sure to carry enough medicines they regularly use.

In addition, you will also need Oral rehydration solutions. You can bring medicine for altitude sickness but we recommend that you take advice from your doctors before taking it.

faqs.q: What Snacks Should I Pack for Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a:
You should carry snacks that are light to carry and provide you with much-needed energy on the trails. Some good options are nuts, dried fruits, energy bars, chocolate, biscuits and trail mix. 

Keeping snacks in your daypack is recommended as it is required when you get hungry or need quick energy between meals. 

You also purchase snacks from tea houses and villages on the way but with the rising elevation, prices rise accordingly. Also, the snack of your choice or favorite brand might not be available at the stores along the trail. So, we advise that you bring it from the city area.

faqs.q: What Kind of Accommodation Can I Expect During the Trek?
faqs.a:
During your trek, you will stay at cozy teahouses or mountain lodges located along the way. The teahouses are simple, clean and comfortable for trekkers offering either shared or single twin bed rooms.

At higher altitudes, the facilties might be limited. However, the good service and warm hospitality will make your stay memorable as well as delightful.

faqs.q: Do Teahouses Provide Blankets?
faqs.a: The teahouse accommodations provide a bed with a mattress, pillows and one blanket. At higher altitudes, the temperature is usually low. Therefore, bringing a high quality sleeping bag is a wise way to stay warm and comfortable for cold nights.

faqs.q: Can I Expect Charging Facilities During the Trek?
faqs.a:
Charging facilities are available in most of the teahouses. At most places, you will have to pay extra for this service as electricity is limited and generated mostly through solar power at high elevation.

Prices of charging devices such as phones, cameras, and other electronics vary depending on location. The cost usually ranges from 2 to 10 USD per device or session with prices increasing at greater elevations.

You may bring a power bank or solar charger so that you can keep your devices charged. Also, make sure to get all your devices and power bank fully charged whenever there is an opportunity.

faqs.q: What Meals Are Served During the Trek?
faqs.a:
Teahouses on Everest Base Camp trek route provide a range of hearty meals. The menu is designed to keep you energized during the journey. The popular dishes include dal bhat, pasta, fried rice, potato dishes, veggie soup, momo, toast, pancakes, porridge, thukpa, eggs and Tibetan bread.

In addition, various beverages such as tea and coffee are also available at most of the teahouses.

faqs.q: Are Vegetarian and Vegan Dishes Available?
faqs.a:
Vegetarian meals are easily available. Common vegetarian meals include dal bhat, noodles, soups, potatoes and momo. 

Vegan options are also available and dishes can be modified accordingly. If you are vegan please inform us beforehand and we will make requests at the teahouses to modify the dishes accordingly.

faqs.q: Is Safe Drinking Water Available Along the Trail?
faqs.a:
Safe drinking water is available on Everest Base Camp trek route. You can buy boiled water from the teahouses. You may carry a refillable water bottle and fill the boiled water at the teahouses. 

The cost of boiled water on the Everest Base Camp trek typically ranges around 2–4 USD at lower elevations. At higher sections, it may cost around 6–9 USD per liter. 

If you want to drink water from natural sources then you may use water purification tablets, filters, or UV purifiers to treat the water. Please make sure not to drink the water without purifying it.

faqs.q: Are Hot Showers Available at the Teahouses?
faqs.a: Many teahouses provide hot shower facilities. Usually, the hot showers are an additional service and are available for an extra fee. The water may be either gas-heated or solar-heated. In remote high altitude areas, owners heat the water and provide it in a bucket after getting request by the owners.

faqs.q: Is Wi-Fi Available at Teahouses Along the Route?
faqs.a:
Most of the teahouses on the Gokyo Valley Trek offer Wi-Fi access at extra cost.  However, the connectivity can become unreliable at higher altitudes. Usually, teahouses charge extra for Wi- Fi. 

These days, many trekkers also choose to buy an Everest Link card for internet access on the trails of the Everest region. The card can be purchased from Kathmandu, Lukla, Namche Bazaar, Gokyo, or even from some lodges.

faqs.q: How Safe Is The Everest Base Camp Trek With Helicopter Return?
faqs.a:
The Everest Base Camp trek with the helicopter return is safe. For a secure journey you need to hike with experienced guides. In addition, you should make sure that you follow the recommended acclimatization schedule and hike at a comfortable pace.

High altitude, changing weather and challenging terrain require proper preparation. In addition, you also need to exercise caution. But if you follow guidelines then this trek can be completed safely.

faqs.q: What If I Become Unwell During The Trek?
faqs.a: In case, you feel unwell during the trek, let your guide know about it immediately. He will analyze your situation, provide advice on rest or descent and if required, they will organize medical assistance for you. In critical cases they will arrange emergency evacuation.

faqs.q: How to Identify the Symptoms of Altitude Sickness?
faqs.a:
While on EBC trek, you need to be cautious about reaction of your body at the high altitude. Some symptoms include:

  • Headache
  • Shortness of Breath
  • Dizziness
  • Sleeplessness
  • Nausea/Vomiting
  • Loss of Appetite
  • Fatigue

faqs.q: Is Helicopter Evacuation Available In Case Of An Emergency?
faqs.a:
Yes. Helicopter evacuation can be arranged in case of an emergency in the Everest region. In emergencies, the helicopter can evacuate trekkers and mountaineers to other lower altitude medical centers or hospitals in the city. 

So, having travel insurance that covers helicopter evacuation at high altitudes is highly advised before starting the Everest trek.

faqs.q: What Can I Do to Acclimatize Safely?
faqs.a:
In order to adjust yourself to the altitude safely at the base camp of Mount Everest, do not rush yourself but ascend slowly and steadily. Follow a well crafted itinerary that has scheduled acclimatization days where you spend a day adjusting to the high Himalayas naturally.

Also drink enough water, eat healthy meals and rest well. Likewise, make sure to maintain your comfortable walking pace and avoid overexertion. Most importantly be attentive to how you feel at the altitude and inform your guide about any signs of altitude sickness. If you experience symptoms that do not get better then head down to lower elevations.

faqs.q: What is the Cost of Everest Base Camp with Helicopter Return Trek Package?
faqs.a: The cost of the Everest Base Camp trek with helicopter return starts from US$ 2395. This 9 day trek package includes all essential services that are required for a smooth adventure on the trails.

faqs.q: What Steps Should I Follow to Reserve the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Return Trek?
faqs.a:
To book your Everest Base Camp trek with helicopter return trek package with us, you may visit the trek package page on our website and click the “Book This Trip” button. Then choose your preferred departure date. 

Enter the number of trekkers and complete the form with required information. Afterwards, you may pay deposit and your trek reservation will be officially confirmed.

faqs.q: Do I Need to Pay Deposit Before the Trek Begins?
faqs.a: Yes. You need to pay a deposit to reserve the EBC trek with the helicopter return package. A 30% deposit is required to book the package. If you need any asistance with booking, please send us an email at info@basecampadventure.com. You may also call us or text on WhatsApp or Viber at +977 9851 029616.

faqs.q: How Much Extra Cash is Recommended?
faqs.a:
For the Everest Base Camp Trek, you may carry 250 to 350 USD (converted to Nepalese rupees). You will need cash during this journey to cover the costs that are not included in the package.

These might include snacks, Wi-Fi, charging, extra food and other purchases. There are no ATMs beyond Lukla and Namche Bazaar and even at these places the ATM service may not be reliable. So, you need to withdraw enough money before you start your trekking journey.

faqs.q: How Much Should I Tip the Trekking Crew?
faqs.a:
Tipping is highly appreciated during Everest Base Camp Trekking and is an important way of acknowledging the efforts of guides, porters and other staff members involved which makes your trekking journey successful.

Trekkers generally tip about 10-15% of the total cost of trekking. But there is no fixed amount. You may tip the amount depending on your experience with the team on the trail.

faqs.q: Can I Get the EBC Trek with Helicopter Trek Package Customized?
faqs.a:
Yes. It can be personalized. The itinerary can be crafted on the basis of your convenience, fitness level and other preferences.

It is possible to modify trekking duration, lodging type and acclimatization days. We can make changes to itinerary according to your convenience.

overview:
Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche is an incredible adventure that rewards you with enchanting views of the awe-inspiring vistas of the Khumbu Region. Throughout the trek, you will get an opportunity to witness the grandeur of nature as you traverse through the pristine landscapes and scenic places of the beautiful Everest Region and return via helicopter, gazing upon the same from an aerial perspective. The views of the snow mountains, such as Mount Everest (8848.86 m), Pumori (7,161 m), Thamserku (6,608 m), Lhotse (8,516 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), and many other surrounding peaks, can be seen during the trek. The exhilarating 10-day journey starts with an exciting flight from Kathmandu to Lukla and passes through beautiful places like Phakding, Namche Bazaar, Tengboche, Dingboche, Chukhung Valley, and Lobuche. Exploring the Everest Base Camp and hiking to Kala Patthar are the special attractions of the trek. After covering the long distances by walking in diverse terrains of the Khumbu Region, you will take an exciting helicopter flight from Pheriche to Kathmandu, which provides you comfort as well as is time efficient. The journey is special as it offers you a chance to witness the grandeur of the Everest Region on foot, initially followed by the adventurous helicopter flight on return. Trekking along the beautiful terrain of the Everest Region, you get a chance to experience the invigorating feeling of being in the high-altitude zones and the return flight makes the journey intriguing, providing unique aerial views of the beautiful Everest Region. EBC Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche is a perfect package of scenic adventure and luxury which is designed to let you witness the sheer magnificence of the Himalayas in two ways; by trekking through the varied terrains and by comfortable helicopter flight on return.

Ideal Time for Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche

The best time for Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return is Autumn and Spring. In Autumn (September, October, and November), the weather is pleasant, and the temperature is moderate, which provides a pleasant walking experience. It is the most preferred time for trekking because of the stable weather and favorable walking conditions. The days are sunny, yet the air is cool and fresh, which allows the trekkers to have a delightful journey. There is minimal to no rainfall during autumn, especially after mid-September, so you will get to see the unobstructed views of the snow-covered peaks. The environment is clean, which is washed by the rainfall of the monsoon season which makes the whole atmosphere refreshing. The views of the mountains are crystal clear even from a distance, which makes it stand out as the perfect time for Everest Base Camp Trek. Another ideal time for trekking to Everest Base Camp is the spring season (March, April, May). During the spring season the weather is mild and the trails are decorated with the vibrant blooming rhododendrons which makes the whole surrounding lively. The moderate temperature creates a pleasant ambiance and you can have an immersive trekking experience. Trekking in the Everest Region in spring also allows you to capture aesthetic shots of flowers blooming in the green forests with an amazing backdrop of the lush hills. Trekking in Summer/ Monsoon (June, July, August) can be relatively challenging because of the muddy and slippery trails due to the downpours. So, you need to have rain gear with you for protection from the rain. In addition, you must be cautious about every step in the slippery pathways. It is also the time when bugs and leeches are present on the trail, which can cause discomfort, so it is important to carry insect repellent. While there are challenges of trekking in the summer/ monsoon season, there are also certain rewards the trails are quieter in this season as it is not the peak season, so you can trek while feeling the tranquility of nature. When the weather gets cleared after rainfall, you can witness the mesmerizing views of lush surroundings and clear views of the snow-covered mountains. In the winter season (December, January, and February), the Everest Region gets very cold, especially in the higher zones. So, you must have the ability to handle the cold if you are planning to trek in winter. In addition, the weather might be foggy which may interrupt the views of the mountains. Similarly, when there is snowfall and paths are covered with thick layers of snow, navigation can be challenging and require more effort. However, there are also pros of trekking in the winter, like the trails are less crowded, and you can traverse through the serene paths, feeling the serenity of nature and enjoying the trek to the fullest. The snowy landscapes will be a visual treat to your eyes, uplifting your sightseeing experience. The views of the majestic mountains covered with a thick layer of snow are the most beautiful in winter. However, you must be dressed in layered and warm clothes to stay protected from cold weather and not catch a cold. Every season offers something different with a distinct charm. However, it is important to select the season that provides you with the excellent views and pleasant walking environment and as autumn and spring provide both, they stand as the ideal time for Everest Base Camp Trek.

itinerary.title: Flight from Kathmandu to Lukla and Trek to Phakding
itinerary.html: Kathmandu Elevation: 1,400 m Lukla Elevation: 2,860 m Phakding Elevation: 2,610 m Flight Duration: 35 minutes Trek Duration: 3 to 4 hours The first day of the journey is an exhilarating one as we take a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. We will receive you from your hotel and transfer you to the airport. The 35-minute flight from Kathmandu to Lukla is thrilling and scenic, where you can see the mesmerizing view of the verdant hills, lush trees, hilly settlements, water streams, and snow-covered mountains. The beautiful scenery will keep you captivated throughout the flight. After the aircraft lands, you can take your time observing the beautiful surroundings around the airport, and soon afterward, the trek will start. You will trek from Lukla to Phakding, witnessing the beautiful sight of the flowing Dudh Koshi River. Several traditional villages can be seen along the way, which will allow you to get glimpses of the way of life of the people living in the Himalayan villages. You will pass through the lush forests, feeling the calmness and peacefulness of the surroundings. Crossing the suspension bridges along the way with spectacular views of the surroundings is truly exhilarating. After walking through the trail, which is a mix of flat, uphills, and downhills sections you will finally arrive in Phakding for an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek to Namche Bazaar from Phakding
itinerary.html: Phakding Elevation: 2,610 m Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours After a wholesome breakfast at your teahouse in Phakding, you will make your way towards Namche Bazaar, walking through small villages and crossing many suspension bridges. You will see the entrance of Sagarmatha National Park as you arrive in Monjo village. The trail requires you to walk along the river and then ascend through the steep section. After making your way through the forests and climbing up through rocky terrains, you will finally reach Namche Bazaar. You can then head towards your teahouse and take a much needed rest.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day at Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m The third day is acclimatization day at Namche Bazaar. You can spend your day exploring the beautiful nearby places. Namche Bazaar is a famous tourist hub of Everest Region. You will see many teahouses, shops, restaurants, and bakeries in Namche Bazaar. You have options to hike to several scenic nearby places of Namche Bazaar. You can hike to Khunde Hospital or visit Hotel Everest View. Similarly, you can also visit the Sherpa Museum where you can get insights into the history and culture of the locals. Hiking to Hotel Everest View, you will get rewarded with the beautiful views of Everest, Lhotse, Ama Dablam and many other surrounding peaks. After exploring the beautiful places, you will return to Namche Bazaar for an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek to Tengboche from Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m Tengboche Elevation: 3,860 m Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours Your destination for the fourth day of the journey is Tengboche. You will start the trek after having a warm and wholesome breakfast in your teahouse in Namche Bazaar. The trail requires you to walk uphills and downhills and also cross the suspension bridge over the DudhKoshi after which you will arrive in Phungi Thenga. Progressing further you will cross the suspension bridge and ascend through the steep paths. After walking through rugged terrains and climbing up through narrow trails, you will finally reach Tengboche. Upon your arrival in Tengboche you will be presented with beautiful views of Everest, Ama Dablam, Nuptse, and other surrounding peaks. You can also visit Tengboche monastery, which will add a spiritual touch to your journey. Your overnight stay for the fourth day will be at a teahouse in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Trek to Dingboche from Tengboche
itinerary.html: Tengboche Elevation: 3,860 m Dingboche Elevation: 4,410 m Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours On this day you will trek to Tengboche from Dingboche. After a fulfilling breakfast in Tengboche, you will head towards Dingboche. In the initial section of the trail, the paths are flat and then it descends through the lush forest. Progressing further, you need to cross the suspension bridge over Imja Khola, with a mesmerizing view of the hills and mountains in the background. The trail then takes you to the beautiful Pangboche village. Soon afterward, you will trek through the barren and rocky terrains. You can also see the small stone settlements along the trail. The beautiful stupa decorated with vibrant colorful flags can be seen as you arrive in Dingboche. You will stay overnight at a teahouse in Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day in Dingboche (Trip to Chukhung Valley)
itinerary.html: Dingboche Elevation: 4,410 m Chukhung Valley Elevation: 4,730 m You will have your second acclimatization day on day 6 where you will explore Chukhung Valley. Acclimatization day is necessary for getting accustomed to the changing altitudes when you are up for high-altitude treks. Chukhung is a popular place where trekkers do a side trip for acclimatization and there are also many lodges. The trail passes through beautiful Imja Khola and beautiful fields. If you choose to hike to Chukhung Ri, the beautiful views of Lhotse, Island Peak, and Ama Dablam are seen, making the whole journey memorable. You will spend the acclimatization day exploring the beautiful places of the Everest Region.

itinerary.title: Trek to Lobuche
itinerary.html: Dingboche Elevation: 4,410 m Lobuche Elevation: 4,940 m Trek Duration: 5 to 6 hours After a rest day at Dingboche and exploration of the beautiful Chukhung Valley, you will trek to Lobuche on the 7th day of the trek. You will make it to Thukla after trekking along the glacier moraine and small charming villages. You can see some tea houses where many trekkers take a short break and have lunch. Soon afterward, you will walk through the rugged and rocky path and ascend to reach Lobuche. After you reach Lobuche, you can head inside the teahouse, freshen up, and have a warm meal prepared by the hosts. Your overnight stay will be at a teahouse in Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Trek to Everest Base Camp
itinerary.html: Lobuche Elevation: 4,940 m Gorakshep Elevation: 5,164 m Everest Base Camp Elevation: 5,364 m Trek Duration: 8 to 9 hours On this day, you will trek to Everest base camp. The trek will start early in the morning from Lobuche after breakfast at a teahouse. Firstly, you will trek to Gorak Shep and then explore the Everest Base Camp. Trekking can be quite challenging as the trail is mostly rocky and rugged. However, the beautiful views of the snowy peaks will captivate your heart throughout the trek. After traversing through the rocky sections, you will reach Everest Base Camp and witness the mesmerizing beauty of Khumbu Glacier and Khumbu Icefall. You can take your time to explore the beautiful base camp and capture beautiful pictures of this incredible moment that you will cherish in your heart forever. After exploring the beautiful base camp, you will then return back to Gorak shep enjoying the stunning views of Everest Region. You will stay overnight in Gorak Shep.

itinerary.title: Hike to Kala Patthar and Trek to Pheriche
itinerary.html: Gorakshep Elevation: 5,164 m Kala Patthar Elevation: 5644.5 m Pheriche Elevation: 4,371 m Trek Duration: 7 to 8 hours Day 9 is an interesting one as you will trek to Kala Patthar from Gorakshep. It is a famous vantage point that offers panoramic views of Mount Everest and many other surrounding peaks like Pumori, Lhotse, and Nuptse. Many climbers start the trek early to view the mesmerizing sunrise from the vantage point of Kala Patthar. The trail gets rocky as you advance, so it is advisable to take gradual ascents. When the sun rises and the mountains are hit by its golden rays, the most enchanting scenery can be seen, enhancing your sightseeing experience. You can also capture beautiful aesthetic photographs of the sun rays illuminating the beautiful mountains After getting a chance to witness the grandeur of the snowy mountains and pristine landscapes of the Khumbu Region from Kala Patthar you will return back to Gorak Shep again for breakfast. The destination for today is Pheriche so after the hearty breakfast, you will trek to Pheriche. You will walk along the beautiful moraine of Khumbu Glacier and arrive in Lobuche. The trail then takes you to Thukla, treating you with mesmerizing views of the snowy mountains. Traversing through the varied terrains and traditional villages, you will finally arrive in Pheriche. You can see many tea houses and lodges in Pheriche. It is also the final day when you cover the long distances by walking as you will take a flight to Kathmandu from Pheriche. Your overnight stay on day 9 will be at one of the finest teahouses in Pheriche.

itinerary.title: Pheriche to Kathmandu on Helicopter
itinerary.html: Pheriche Elevation: 4,371 m Kathmandu Elevation: 1,400 m Flight Duration: 1 to 1.5 hours On this day you will be taking a helicopter flight from Pheriche to Kathmandu on a helicopter. The aerial adventure is exhilarating and scenic, rewarding you with incredible views of the pristine mountains and beautiful landscapes of the Khumbu Region. The trekking routes and spectacular village settlements are seen from the aerial perspective, making your journey filled with wonder and awe. The breathtaking vistas of the Everest Region from an aerial perspective are amazing to witness. The overall flight is scenic, as you will get a chance to gaze upon the breathtaking views of verdant hills, deep valleys, water streams, and snowy peaks throughout the journey. After the helicopter makes its landing at Kathmandu Airport, we will drop you to the hotel, which marks the completion of this incredible 10 day journey.

sections.title: Useful Info
sections.html:
What Makes Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche Special?

Sagarmatha National Park

You will trek through the Sagarmatha National Park which is a world heritage site established in 1976. The exceptional area is gifted with iconic snow-capped mountains, pristine glaciers, and deep valleys. The protected national park is home to several bird species like the impeyan pheasant, Tibetan snowcock, Himalayan griffon vulture, alpine chough, etc. Similarly, animals like red panda, musk deer, Himalayan tahr, snow leopard, and black bear can also be found in the national park.

Tengboche Monastery

During the Everest Base Camp trek, you will get a chance to visit many monasteries and also Tengboche Monastery, which is the largest monastery in the Khumbu Region. You can see the beautiful building of the monastery with a large courtyard and also many paintings. It is culturally significant to the locals, and the architecture represents Tibetan Buddhist designs. Visiting the Tengboche Monastery, you can get insight into the beliefs of the locals and add spiritual warmth to your journey.

Cultural Exploration

You can get many chances for cultural exploration during the Everest Base Camp Trek. You will be passing through many traditional villages and meeting many locals along the way. The locals are friendly and will always greet you with a smile. As you stay in the different tea houses throughout the trek, you will get numerous opportunities to interact with the owners of the teahouses and learn about the culture and traditions of the locals. Similarly, if you trek to the Everest Region in the autumn season, then you can get a chance to observe the Mani Rimdu festival, which holds great importance to Sherpa People, and many shows are also held at the Tengboche monastery during the festival. The sherpas perform masked dances, pray, and organize a feast to celebrate the festival. Observing the festival will make the journey more rewarding and intriguing as you can witness the vibrant and joyful moments of the Himalayan Region.

Spectacular Sceneries

Everest Base Camp Trek is renowned for offering the beautiful sceneries of iconic snow-capped peaks. Throughout the trek, you will get a chance to visit many scenic places and witness the breathtaking beauty of the pristine Everest Region. The beautiful lush forests, rivers, hills, and mountains will captivate your heart and make the entire journey invigorating. Similarly, you will hike to Kala Patthar, from where you can see the beautiful Mount Everest, Nuptse, and Changtse.

Stunning Aerial Views

The trek to Everest Base Camp with Helicopter Return from Pheriche also provides you an opportunity to gaze upon the exhilarating vistas of the Everest Region. On the first day of the journey itself, you will get a chance to witness the aerial views of verdant hills, lush forests, and beautiful settlements on a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. Furthermore, you will take a helicopter flight from Pheriche, which presents you with stunning views of the unique landscapes, charming villages, and alluring mountains of the Everest Region.

Preparation for Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche

During the Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche, you will walk in diverse, uneven, wavy, and rugged terrains. You will walk uphill and downhill in many sections of the trek, which requires a good level of physical and mental endurance. It is important to prepare well before embarking on the journey for the smooth completion of the trek. You can prepare for the trek by including physical exercises and going for hikes in the local places. It helps you to stay fit, develop stamina, and be well-prepared for the challenges that come along while trekking. It is highly recommended that you include strength training exercises and cardiovascular exercises into your routine to be well prepared for high-altitude adventures like Everest Base Camp Trek. The kinds of training and exercises that you can include in your routine are; Strength Training Exercises : Push Ups, Pull Ups, Planks. Squats, Deadlift, Lunge, Calf Raises, Upright Rows, Bicep Curl, etc. Cardiovascular Exercises: Walking, Swimming, Stair Climbing, Cycling, Jumping ropes etc.

Challenges

Altitude Sickness

Altitude sickness is one of the key concerns while trekking in the high-altitude zones. During Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche, you will cover long distances, making ascents and descents in steep and narrow sections. The risk of getting altitude sickness is always there during high-altitude treks. Some symptoms of Altitude Sickness are:
  • Headache
  • Fatigue
  • Having difficulties to sleep
  • Rapid heartbeat
  • Shortness of breath
There are some ways in which you can minimize the risk of altitude sickness. For the reduction of the risk, it is highly recommended to follow these methods:
  • Take gradual ascents.
  • Maintain proper hydration and have a balanced diet.
  • Be mindful of how your body is reacting in changing altitudes.
  • Descend to lower areas when you feel symptoms aren’t going away.
  • Incorporate acclimatization days during the journey.
  • Consult with your doctor before taking medications like Diamox, which helps in minimizing the risk of altitude sickness.
  • Ensure proper communication with your guides and follow their guidance properly and during the trek if you feel any discomfort at any moment then inform them immediately.

Exhaustion

As you will be covering long distances by walking through steep and narrow sections of the trail so, you may get weary or exhausted at some point in time. The uphills and narrow sections can make you feel tired, which is also one of the challenges that trekkers face during high-altitude treks. So, it is advisable to walk gradually and not over-exhaust yourself. Take small breaks, incorporate rest days for acclimatization and don't hurry to reach the destination. If you feel exhausted during trekking, then you cannot enjoy the journey, and you may even fall ill, which may cause trip interruption. So, you must trek at a gradual pace to avoid exhaustion and for the successful completion of the trek.

Weather Fluctuations

One of the major challenges of high-altitude trekking is weather fluctuations. The weather changes rapidly in the mountain regions, which stands as one of the major challenges. The sunny weather can turn gloomy rapidly in a short period of time. So, it is crucial to be well prepared for the weather related challenges of the Himalayan Region and be equipped with the essentials that will help you to be protected from the adverse weather conditions. You may also like:
  • Everest Gokyo Trek With Helicopter Return
  • Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek
  • Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return

Tips for Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche

Research

The first and foremost thing one must do before embarking on a journey is research. You can conduct the research in many ways. You can look for information about the trek on the internet, watch informative videos or directly contact the trekking agencies. Research helps you learn about the nature of the trek and also helps you to make informed decisions for choosing the right time for the trek. With the proper research you can know about the cost, required level of fitness, terrain conditions, and essentials that are required for trekking. It also helps you do the proper planning and be well-prepared for the challenges that come with trekking. So, do research and determine if the trek is suitable for you.

Maintain Proper Hydration and Nutrition

Maintaining a good level of hydration and nutrition is important while trekking to Everest Base Camp. When you are properly hydrated and incorporate nutritious food into your diet, you can maintain your energy levels. You should make sure to drink enough water and not get dehydrated. Similarly, maintain a balanced diet as it helps you to develop the stamina that is required for trekking.So, hydration and nutrition is important for the successful completion of the trek.

Be well-informed about the routes.

When you are planning for any trek, it is crucial to be familiar with the routes. When you know your itinerary, it will help you know about the route, and you will trek through the designated paths only, which will reduce the possibility of getting lost. Similarly, when you know about the routes, you can manage your time properly and you can distribute your time effectively for rest stops and reach the teahouse in time. So, you should know to know about the routes. It is highly advisable to ask for information about the routes with the guides and also read the itinerary to stay well-informed about the routes.

Be Flexible with the Itinerary

When going for treks especially in the high altitude zones, it is important to be flexible with the itinerary. If during any particular day during your trek, a situation arises that may not be suitable for trekking then you may have to add an extra day to your schedule so, it is highly advisable to be flexible with your schedule and itinerary for any kind of modifications needed during the journey.

Pack All Essentials

Packing wisely is necessary for a convenient and enjoyable Trek. You need to be well-equipped with all the required items that are required during the journey. As you will walk in diverse terrains of the Khumbu Region for more than a week you will need important items that will help you have a comfortable journey. Buying all the essentials may not be possible when you are in remote areas, so do research about the required items and make sure to pack them for maintaining hygiene and comfort during the trek.

Accommodation and Meals

You will stay in teahouses and lodges during the EBC trek with helicopter return from Pheriche. It is among the popular trekking destinations and you will find many tea houses and lodges along the trail. As you advance in the remote zones, the facilities might be basic, but you will have a comfortable stay. The tea houses provide a cozy and warm room with a single bed, warm blankets, and a pillow. Many trekkers bring sleeping bags as blankets alone may not be sufficient to keep yourself warm. Similarly there are a variety of options available in the food menu. The most common and popular dish that is served by many tea houses along the trail is Dal Bhat. It is a typical Nepali dish served warm and is very fulfilling. Other food items such as Bread, Fried, and Boiled Eggs, Noodles, Thukpa Soup, and Chapatis are also served in the teahouses, which you can order as per your preference.

Travel Insurance

Travel Insurance is important when you partake in any high-altitude treks in Nepal. You must have travel insurance that provides financial protection against the possible risks that you may encounter during the journey. There are certain possible risks that may occur during the trekking, so to have a financially secure journey, it is highly recommended that you have travel insurance that provides coverage against risks like Medical expenses because of any illness or accidents during the trip, lost /stolen baggage and trip cancellation or delays. Similarly, there may be a situation of urgency that may need emergency evacuation through helicopter, and the trip can get interrupted because of any natural calamities so it is highly recommended that you select the plan that provides the financial protection against such risks. So, travel insurance is crucial for the Everest Base Camp Trek with a Helicopter Return from Pheriche.

Permits Required For Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche

To trek to the Everest Base Camp, you must obtain permits. The revenue collected through the permits is important for the development of the local infrastructure conservation of the natural environment and There are two permits required for Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return from Pheriche, and they are:
  • Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit
The Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality permit costs Rs.2000 per person (USD 15).
  • Sagarmatha National Park Permit
The cost of the Sagarmatha National Park permit is Rs. 3000 per person (USD 22.48) for foreigners and Rs.1500 (USD 11.24) for the citizens of SAARC countries.

Safety Guidelines For Helicopter Return from Pheriche

Some of the safety protocols that you should follow when returning to Kathmandu from Pheriche
  • Keep your phone in flight mode during the flight.
  • Fasten your seat belt.
  • Follow the instructions of the pilot and the crew.
  • Step in and out of the helicopter only after receiving the instructions of the pilot.
  • Be familiar with the luggage restrictions.
  • Know about all the emergency procedures.
  • Stay hydrated.
  • Take advice from your doctor before the helicopter tour if you have any health issues.

title: Everest Base Camp Trek with Island Peak Climbing
summary: Everest Base Camp Trek with Island Peak Climbing deals with climbing Island Peak-located on top of the Chukung glacier between Ama Dablam and mt. Lhotse.

seo.title: Everest Base Camp Trek with Island Peak Climbing
seo.description: Everest Base Camp Trek with Island Peak Climbing deals with climbing Island Peak-located on top of the Chukung glacier between Ama Dablam and mt. Lhotse.

cover.alt: Everest Base Camp Trek with Island Peak Climbing

map.alt: Everest Base Camp Trek With Island Peak Climbing Map

overview:
Everest Base Camp Trek with Island Peak Climbing is a perfectly combined trip that offers an opportunity to experience trekking in the wilderness of the Himalayas and climbing one of the most beautiful peaks of the Khumbu region, Island Peak (6,189 m). The trek is an excellent opportunity to traverse the Khumbu region to be at the foot of the world's highest mountain Everest (8,818 m) and also make a non-technical climb to the mesmerizing Island Peak (6,189 m) situated in the Imja valley.

The 20-day Everest Base Camp Trek with Island Peak Climbing is a challenging trek that is designed for the energetic and physically strong trekkers. To climb the Island Peak, it is not necessary to have advanced and experienced climbing skills. It is perfect for those trekkers or climbers who have the interest to experience challenging and thrilling adventure. The trek to Everest Base Camp offers the surreal view of world’s tallest mountain Mt. Everest (8,848 m) along with the gorgeous peaks of Lhotse (8,414 m), Pumori (7,161 m), Ama Dablam (6,812 m), Cho Oyu (8,188 m), and many others. The base camp also provides an amazing view of the Khumbu Glacier and the Ice-fall. The trail to base camp passes through the Sagarmatha National Park where trekkers may encounter different wildlife like musk deer, Danphe, snow leopard, Himalayan Thar, etc. Trekkers also come across beautiful glacial lakes and climb Kala Patthar viewpoint to see the amazing 360-degree view of different Himalayas. The trekking trail also passes through several Sherpa villages on a way where trekkers get an opportunity to experience Sherpa lifestyle and culture. The climb to Island Peak can be challenging due to the rocky ridge along the glacial moraine. Upon reaching the high point of Island Peak, trekkers are rewarded with the most amazing view of the massive Himalayan peaks that every climber dreams to conquer.

Base Camp Adventure has been ruling the tourism industry since 2009. We ensure to provide our client with every kind of services available and needed for trekking and expedition. We also provide our clients with communication facilities to make necessary phone calls back to their country in case they miss their family. We accommodate you to the best place and provide the best transportation throughout the journey.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla and trek to Phakding (2610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: We catch our early morning 40-minute scenic flight over the Himalayas to Lukla. Upon arrival at Lukla Airport, we begin our trek walking alongside the Dudh Koshi River, and passing by a few villages, we reach Phakding. Overnight at lodge in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Continuing our trek alongside the Dudh Koshi River, we cross suspension bridge several times. We then enter the Sagarmatha National Park, where we may get a glimpse of different wild Himalayan animals before reaching Namche. Namche is one of the most famous Sherpa towns in Nepal and is also the commercial center of Khumbu region. Overnight at lodge in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Rest day in Namche (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), or side trip to Khumjung vaillage and Hotel Everest View.
itinerary.html: We take a rest day in Namche to get used to high altitude. We can also explore nearby Khumjung village visiting Khumjung Monastery, which displays a Yeti skull in its premises. Khumjung is also the largest Sherpa settlement in Khumbu. We then hike back to Namche via Hillary School in the twin village of Khunde. An amazing vista of Everest (8,848 m) and surrounding peaks are seen throughout the day. Overnight in Namche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche to Tengboche (3,860 m / 12,664 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: We continue our trek towards Tengboche walking through the flat and forested trail full of colorful rhododendron, oak, and pine trees. Enjoying the stunning view of Everest (8,848 m), Ama Dablam (6,856 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), Thamserku (6,623 m), and Kangtega (6,782 m) in the background, we arrive in Tengboche, which is home to the largest monastery in Khumbu region. Overnight at lodge in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Pheriche (4,371 m / 14,340), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today our trail descends through a forest for about half an hour before crossing a river. As we ascend higher, the landscape changes to the drier side. We continue our trek towards Pheriche passing through Sherpa village of Pangboche. Overnight at lodge in Pheriche

itinerary.title: Rest day in Pheriche Pheriche (4,371 m / 14,340) for acclimatization.
itinerary.html: To adjust to the high altitude, we take a day off trekking for acclimatization. We can stroll around the beautiful village of Pheriche located at the side of the river. This is also an opportunity for us to learn about the Sherpa way of life and get an insight of Buddhism practiced in the Khumbu region. Overnight in Pheriche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pheriche to Lobuche (4930 m), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Our trail today is easy up to Dughla. We then ascend along the steep moraine of the Khumbu Glacier and pass through rocky and pebbly slopes which lead us to Chupki Lhara. We continue our trek towards the village of Lobuche located at the foot of massive Lobuche Peak (6,145 m). Overnight at lodge in Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche to Gorak Shep and continue to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m / 17,598 ft), then return to Gorak Shep for an overnight stay, 7–8 hours.
itinerary.html: Leaving behind Lobuche, we trek towards Everest Base Camp walking along the Khumbu Glacier. The trail to base camp is challenging due to thin air, rocky dunes, moraines, and glacial streams. We also come across Gorakshep Lake on our way. Upon reaching the base camp, we can get the stunning view of Nuptse (7,861 m), Khumbutse (6,636 m), Everest (8,848 m), Pumori (7,161 m), and other snow-capped peaks of the Khumbu region. The base camp also offers an amazing view of Khumbu Icefall. We return back to Gorakshep for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gorak Shep to Kala Patthar (5,545 m / 18,192 ft), then return to Gorak Shep and continue trekking to Dingboche (4,410 m / 14,468 ft), 6–7 hours.
itinerary.html: We take an early morning hike up to Kala Patthar (5,550 m) to watch the sunrise over the mountains in orange color. Upon reaching the top, we are rewarded with the magnificent panorama of different peaks like Everest (8,848 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), Pumori (7,161 m), Changtse (7,543 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), and many other peaks. After taking few pictures, we head back to Dingboche following the rocky path. Overnight stay in Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Chukhung (4,750 m / 15,584 ft), 2-3 hours.
itinerary.html: Walking through the stone walled fields and alpine landscapes, we make our way up further to Bibre (4,750 m). Relishing the magnificent view of Island Peak (6,189 m), Ama Dablam (6,856 m), and Amphu Lapcha (5,663 m) in the background, we descend towards Chhukhung. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chukhung to Island Peak Base Camp (5,087 m / 16,690 ft), 5-6 hours
itinerary.html: Leaving behind Chhukhung, we head towards Island Peak Base Camp (4,970 m). We ascend through steep trail climbing towards the south then turning east to the main line of the valley. We continue our trek through the winding moraine path then walk through the crisscross path of Imja River that leads us to Island Peak Base Camp. Overnight in the camp.

itinerary.title: Climb Island Peak (6,189 m / 20,305 ft) and back to Chhukung, 9-10 hours.
itinerary.html: We start our climb to the summit of Island Peak (6,189 m) early in the morning. Ascending through the rocky gully on a steep trail, we make our way up to a wide stone field. Climbing through few short rock steps, we reach the right side of the gully. We continue our climb crossing the ridges of glaciers and crevasses, and finally arrive at the high point of the peak. We will be rewarded with the extraordinary view of several Himalayan peaks including Lhotse (8,414 m), Everest (8,848 m), Makalu (8,481 m), and Ama Dablam (6,856 m) among others. After taking a few pictures and spending quality time at the top, we trek back to Chhukung for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Contingency Day
itinerary.html: This day is usually used as a contingency day in the event of bad weather preventing a summit attempt. If the summit attempt the day before was successful, you will proceed to descend.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chhukung to Deboche (3,820 m / 12,533 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Leaving behind the Island Peak and Chhukung Valley, we trek back to Deboche. We pass through colorful Chortens, monasteries, Mani walls, and prayers flags. We also walk through the dense forest filled with oak and pine trees. Finally crossing the suspension bridge over Imja Khola, we reach Deboche. Overnight at lodge in Deboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Deboche to Namche (3,450 m / 11,319 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today we walk past several villages like Tengboche, Phunke Tenga, Sanasa, and Kyangjuma as we make our way to Namche Bazaar. Accompanied by the stunning landscapes and mountain peaks, we arrive in Namche for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: For our last day of the trek, we head towards Lukla passing several Sherpa villages on our way. We also walk through the forest of oaks and pines. Following the flow of Dudh Koshi River, we trek past many monasteries, Mani walls, Chortens, and prayer wheels before reaching Lukla. Overnight at lodge in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu, (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html: We catch our early morning scenic flight to Kathmandu from Lukla. The 40-minute flight takes us over the mountains and later the hills one more time. Upon reaching Kathmandu airport, we transfer you back to your hotel. Later in the evening, we host a farewell dinner to celebrate the completion of the journey. Overnight at hotel in Kathmandu.

title: Everest Base Camp and Gokyo Trek
summary: Everest Base Camp with Gokyo and Cho La Pass Trek combines EBC, the Gokyo Valley, and the challenging Cho La Pass for an unforgettable Everest Region Trek.

seo.title: Everest Base Camp and Gokyo Trek | Itinerary | Map | Cost
seo.description: Everest Base Camp with Gokyo and Cho La Pass Trek combines EBC, the Gokyo Valley, and the challenging Cho La Pass for an unforgettable Everest Region Trek.

cover.alt: Gokyo and Cho La Pass Trek

overview:
Everest Base Camp with Gokyo and Cho La Pass Trek is one of the most loved and adventurous trekking destinations in the Khumbu region. The trail is strenuous that goes through the pass called Cho La (5,420 m) which connects the beautiful Gokyo valley with Everest Base Camp. You will get to witness mighty Himalayan ranges, tranquil lakes, gorgeous sceneries, picturesque villages, old monasteries, and colorful festivals of the legendary Sherpas along your way.

You will begin your journey by taking a short flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. After reaching Lukla, you will begin your trek and reach Namche Bazaar which is also the largest residing area of the famous Sherpas. In Namche Bazaar, you will take a break to get acclimatized with the altitude. From here, you will walk on the Everest Base Camp trail and the rocky summit of Kala Patthar (5,550 m) via the famous Tengboche Monastery. You will observe the most heart-pounding views of Mt. Everest (8,848 m) and its neighboring mountains from both the base camp and Kala Patthar. You will then trek to Gokyo valley crossing the frozen pass of Cho La (5,420 m). You will visit all the high valleys of Khumbu and also get to explore the upper valley of Gokyo. On the way to Gokyo valley, you will witness the grand Ngozumpa glacier, which is the longest glacier in Nepal. You will then head to Gokyo Lake where you will observe the breath-taking reflection of the stunning snow-covered peaks of Khumbu in the green water below. You can also take an excursion to Gokyo Ri (5,360 m) for a panoramic view of Mt. Everest (8,848 m), Cho Oyu (8,188 m), and Lhotse (8,414 m), among others. All of the six pristine Gokyo lakes can also be seen from the top of Gokyo Ri (5,360 m). On your way back, you can buy souvenirs in Namche Bazaar to take back home for your loved ones.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: As you arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, you will be welcomed by one of our airport representatives who will then transfer you to your hotel. Stay overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft) and trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: We take the early morning flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. Various landscapes and beautiful mountains are seen throughout the flight. The trek begins shortly after reaching Lukla. Walking downhill over the Dudh Koshi gorge and crossing barley and potato fields, we finally reach Phakding. Overnight stay in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: From Phakding, the track goes to the Dudh Koshi valley north, twisting through the pines and passing on the suspension bridges to reach the village of Monjo. Monjo is the main entrance to the Sagarmatha National Park. From Monjo, the path moves past waterfalls, Sherpa villages, and forests of rhododendron, magnolia, and fir. One can witness the first views of Mt Everest (8,848 m) if the weather is clear. Reach the busiest junction for the trekkers and locals, Namche Bazaar. Later, explore Namche Bazaar which is also the gateway to Everest. Overnight stay in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day at Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft).
itinerary.html: We will have a full day rest so that we won't face any difficulty ahead. Today we make a short acclimatization hike up to Khumjung, a pleasant Sherpa village above Namche. Also, while returning down, one can visit Everest View Hotel for impressive views of Everest (8,848 m), Ama Dablam (6,856 m), Thamserku (6,623 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), and Lhotse (8,414 m). You have the full day free to enjoy the perfect panoramic views or to wander around the market. Overnight stay in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche (3,860 m / 12,664 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Walking towards Tengboche with the superb views of mountains will be the best part of this day. Breathtaking views of Everest (8,848 m), Ama Dablam (6,856 m), Nuptse (7,861 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), and a close-up view of Thamserku (6,623 m) can be seen on the way. Continuing the gradual trail with few ups and downs, Sanasa is reached, which is the major trail junction to Gokyo Valley and Everest Base Camp. After climbing steeply through the pine forest, we arrive in Tengboche. Tengboche is home to the famous Tengboche Monastery, which is the biggest monastery in the Khumbu region. Overnight stay in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche (4,410 m / 14,468 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: The track crosses Imja River via a suspension bridge to reach Dingboche. The village of Pangboche is passed en route. Dingboche is also known as the “Summer Valley” of Khumbu and contains long wall built to guard the village’s crops against the cold winds that incline down the Imja Valley. Dingboche, as the name echoes, gets more sun too. Elegant views of Lhotse (8,414 m), Ama Dablam (6,856 m), and Island Peak (6,189 m) from Dingboche are quite amazing to see. Overnight stay in Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day at Dingboche (4,410 m / 14,468 ft) / day hike to Chhukung Ri.
itinerary.html: This day will be the rest day in Dingboche. We can carry a short ascend of 400 m to the Nangkartshang Gompa situated on the ridge north of Dingboche. Witness a mesmerizing view of Makalu (8,463 m) from here. You can trek uphill to Chhukhung Ri (4,730 m) which takes approximately 4 to 5 hours from Dingboche. To the north of Dingboche, there are remarkable views of Lhotse’s huge South Face. Overnight stay in Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche (4,910 m / 16,109 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: On the trail towards Lobuche, there is the Trekker’s Aid Post, located in Pheriche (4,210 m). The Chupki Lhara is then reached from where mesmerizing mountains can be seen. The path then goes downhill to the Khumbu Glacier moraine. The views of mountain peaks like Khumbutse (6,665 m), Lingtren (6,749 m), and Pumori (7,165 m) emerge in the skyline. Mount Nuptse (7,861 m) also appears up ahead once the glacier pass is crossed. Slowly, walk further on from Lobuche alongside the world’s highest glacier—the Khumbu Glacier. Moving further for about 2-3 hours from Lobuche, reach Gorakshep, a tranquil place to be at. Overnight stay in Gorakshep.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche to Gorakshep (5,164 m / 16,942 ft), continue to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m / 17,598 ft), and return to Gorak Shep, 7–8 hours.
itinerary.html: We walk on frost blanketed paths and then climb on steep trails above Gorakshep. As we make our way towards Everest Base Camp, the snowy peaks can be seen becoming closer and bigger. After two hours of strenuous trekking, we finally reach Everest Base Camp. The view of the mighty Everest (8,848 m) is surreal when seen from its very foot. Various other peaks of the Mahalangur Himalayan Range are also seen ravishing from Everest Base Camp. Later, we walk down the slippery trails back to the lodge in Gorakshep. Overnight stay in Gorakshep.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gorakshep to Kala Patthar (5,545 m / 18,192 ft), return to Gorak Shep, and continue to Dzongla (4,830 m / 15,846 ft), 6–7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today we start our journey early to watch the sunrise from Kala Patthar. We ascend on an icy and rocky path till we reach the large upland of Kala Patthar. From Kala Patthar, stunning view of Everest (8,848 m) and the lovely peaks of Lingtren (6,749 m), Khumbutse (6,665 m), and several others can be seen along with the absolutely gorgeous sunrise. We then head back to Gorakshep and continue to descend alongside Khumbu lacier until reaching Lobuche. We first descend alongside the river from Lobuche, enjoying the view of the gorgeous mountains in the backdrop. Afterward, we climb gradually towards Dzongla via Chola Tsho. The view of Cholatse (6,335 m) and Lobuche (6,145 m) stand out in Dzongla. Overnight stay in Dzongla.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dzongla to Cho La Pass (5,420 m / 17,782 ft), continue to Gokyo village (4,790 m / 15,715 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Walk early morning for three hours to reach on top of the high mountain pass, Cho La (5,420 m). Before you get to the top of Cho La, we have to walk on ice for about 20 minutes. From the top of the pass, we are able to view a breathtaking panorama of Cho Oyu (8,188 m), Everest (8,848 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), and several other snowy peaks. Continuing straight, we come across the Indian army mountaineers' monuments. The trail can be misleading hence it is important that we follow our guide attentively. We cross Chola pass with rocky banks and moraines of Ngozumpa Glacier, the longest glacier in Nepal, before reaching the tranquil Gokyo Lake. We explore the quaint Gokyo village in the evening while relishing the spectacular view of Cho Oyu (8,188 m). Overnight stay in Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gokyo Village to Gokyo Peak (Gokyo Ri), return to Gokyo, and continue to Machhermo (4,470 m / 15,715 ft), 7–8 hours.
itinerary.html: Climb up to Gokyo Ri (5,360 m) for beautiful views of Cho Oyu (8,188 m), Chamar (7,287 m), Everest (8,848 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), and so on along with the view of the pristine Gokyo lakes. Hike back down to Dudh Pokhari, the third Gokyo Lake, and enjoy the peaceful environs. Leaving Gokyo village behind, we descend on the banks of Ngozumpa Glacier via second and first Gokyo lakes. Then we follow the downstream trail of Dudh Koshi River all the way to Machharmo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Machharmo to Namche Bazaar (33,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Continuing to follow the Dudh Koshi River, we descend through lovely rhododendron forests on our way to Namche Bazaar. We arrive in several popular places like Dhile, Phortse Thanga, Mong, and Sanasa, and cross the longest Mani wall of Khumbu to finally reach Namche Bazaar. You can interact with the locals and get to know about their culture and tradition while having a cup of their special tea. Overnight in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Bidding goodbye to Namche Bazaar, today we return to Lukla where the trip started. We’ll take time to enjoy the accomplishment as a group and as an individual. You’ll also have enough time to explore the place. Enjoy the environment and share stories with the local people since today is the last day of the trek. Overnight stay in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html: We take an early flight back to Kathmandu. On arrival, you will be taken to the hotel so that you can rest and freshen up. Later, you can wander around the streets of Kathmandu and do some shopping for your loved ones back home. Feel free to get the taste of food and lovely ambiance of Kathmandu. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Transfer to International Airport for your onward destination.
itinerary.html: Your adventure in Nepal ends today. A representative will drop you off at Tribhuvan International Airport a few hours before the scheduled flight.

sections.title: More information
sections.html: Q: I’ve never trekked before.  Can I do this trek? Answer: As long as you are reasonably fit, mentally prepared and can walk for 6-7-hours a day then no matter who you are and what your background is, a bit of training may be necessary, but even that is not 100% essential for most. Q: How many miles do you walk each day? Answer: It is about 40 miles from Lukla to EBC and another 60 miles from EBC to Gokyo and back to Lukla. In average you walk around 4-7 miles per day while going up and 8-12 miles while coming down. Q: Is there battery charging facility? Answer: The tea houses have charging ability via their solar panels but if it has been cloudy for several days, there may not be enough reserves to charge barberries for your camera, and thus it is better to have an extra battery. Teahouses usually charge for it – maybe a 300-500 rupees per hour. Many people want to charge their batteries so try to plug your stuff in as soon as you arrive. Q: Can I do laundry on the trek? Answer: Yes, you can. You can take this service with guest house. This will not be by machine, it will be by hand. Or, you can do your own laundry in a bucket. Q: Is there bottled water on the Everest Base Camp, Gokyo and Cho La Pass Trek? Answer: Yes, there’s bottled water from Lukla all the way up to base camp, Cho La Pass and Gokyo Valley. But, the price goes up the higher you go. One liter bottle of water cost start around 70 rupees and at base camp cost well over 300 (around $3). A budget solution to this is to use water treatment solution or use water purifier tablets. Some purification tabs and drops make the water taste weird. Please be aware of that too. Buying boiled water can be a solution to save money from expensive bottled water but make sure if water was fully boiled or not before you buy. Q: Is there age limit for this trek? Answer: There isn’t any official age limit saying you can and cannot trek to this trek. Q: How difficult is Everest Base Camp -Gokyo and Cho La Pass Trek route? Answer: In terms of terrain there are no ropes needed and no ice picks needed. There is no vertical climbing involved. The ground is not paved. It is rough, rocky and gravel strewn. Most of the trek involves long paths that go up and then down. People with weak ankles should take caution. Depending on the time of year you go there can also be snow and ice in the trails. But crossing Cho La pass is more challenging. It is recommended to carry Ice axe. Q: Can children go on the Everest Base Camp -Gokyo and Cho La Pass Trek ? Answer: Yes is the general rule. It’s advisable that your child is reasonable and able to understand and follow instructions immediately. Your child should be mature enough to recognize altitude sickness symptoms.
