overview:
Everest Gokyo Ri trek is a moderately challenging trekking adventure in the Everest region. The trail of this incredible trek passes through the foothills of the Himalayas. The magical landscapes provide you with an excellent opportunity for trekking. Walking alongside the diverse cultural settlements of the region is another advantage of this trek.

The Sagarmatha National Park is a beautiful conservation area along the trails of this trek. This natural heritage site is home to rare and endangered wildlife species, including Himalayan Tahr, snow leopard, Danphe, etc. The incredible adventure is the once in a lifetime opportunity for avid trekkers all around the world.

Moreover, the awe-inspiring views of snow-capped mountains are another highlight of the trek in Everest Gokyo region. You can get magical views of Mt. Everest, Nuptse, Lhotse, Kwangde Peak, Mt. Ama Dablam, Kusum peak, Kangaru peak, Tawache, etc. Besides that, there are various ice glaciers, waterfalls, lakes, and rivers in the Himalayan region as well.

Furthermore, the culture and lifestyle of the Sherpa community will enchant travelers. You will stay in the teahouses and lodges along the trail. Namche Bazaar and Gokyo are ideal places to acclimatize in this trek. This outstanding trekking package is available at a reasonable cost. Read further for the Everest Gokyo Ri Trek and other related information in detail.

Highlights of the Trek

  • Magical views of sunrise and sunset views from various viewpoints along the trail
  • Awe inspiring views of Mt. Everest, Mt. Ama Dablam, Lhotse, Nuptse, Kangaru peak, Kwangde Peak, Tawache, Kusum peak, and others
  • Ascending the trekking peak of Gokyo Ri (5,357 m)
  • The exploration of serene Gokyo Lakes
  • Exploring the culture of the Sherpa community
  • Spotting rare flora and fauna of region including the Himalayan Tahr, snow leopards, and Danphe
  • Tasting the local delicacies of Nepalese people
  • Warm hospitality in the tea houses

The Trekking Route

Our Everest Gokyo Ri Trek will start with a scenic flight from Kathmandu (1,350 m) to Lukla (2,860 m). After this incredible flight, we will continue our trek from Lukla to Phakding (2,610 m) and then trek to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m). We will tackle altitude sickness with acclimatization at Namche and other regions along the trek.

Moreover, you will then pass through various settlements including Phortse (4,038 m), Machermo (4,470 m), and Gokyo (4,480 m). After acclimatizing, you will also have a chance to climb Gokyo Ri (5,357 m). The Gokyo Ri trekking peak is also a great viewpoint. From the viewpoint you can observe magical views of the snow-capped mountains of the Everest region.

Furthermore, you will also trek back to Lukla to Namche and Dole. You will also complete this trek in a great adventurous flight from Lukla to Kathmandu. After landing, we will take you to a hotel in Kathmandu, where our tour ends.

Similar Packages: Gokyo Valley Trek | Gokyo Valley with Renjo La Pass Trek | EBC - Gokyo - Chola Pass Trek

Ideal Time for the Everest Gokyo Ri Trek

Spring (March-May) and Autumn (September- November) are the peak season for the trek. These seasons ensure stable weather conditions and moderate temperatures in the Everest region.

Autumn (September-November)

The Autumn months of September to November are the best time for taking this Everest Gokyo Ri Trek. The ideal temperatures in the Everest region make it suitable for a great adventure.

Moreover, Autumn also has minimal precipitation, and there are clear blue skies. You can also observe the cultural and religious festivals in this season.

Spring (March-May)

The Spring months of March to May are also ideal for travel in the region. You can also observe magical views of snow-capped mountains and other natural diversities. Moreover, There are wildflowers like rhododendrons and wild oaks all over the area. You can also experience moderate temperatures in the region with minimal rainfall.

Moreover, the off-seasons treks in the summer monsoon and the winter season can get quite challenging. The slippery and muddy trails in the wet monsoon season will get quite tricky for all travelers. There are avalanches and landslides that you need to consider as well.

Furthermore, there are heavy snowfall and extreme freezing temperatures in the winter season. Overall, with packing and preparation, you can complete this trek.

How Difficult is the Everest Gokyo Ri Trek?

This incredible trek in the Everest Gokyo region is more challenging than a regular Everest base camp trek. The high altitude region has many challenges, including altitude sickness. The trails take you to a maximum height of 5,357 m at Gokyo Ri. There is minimal oxygen and temperatures that can get tricky for trekkers.

Moreover, trekkers should acclimatize regularly during the trek to tackle altitude sickness. The rugged region trails move up and down a lot, making it challenging for all travelers. Besides that, the narrow path can be a threat to all skill levels. Therefore, trekkers must have proper fitness and stamina to complete this trek. Travelers should also perform a training regime that includes various activities like physical exercise, cardio vascular exercises, mental exercises, and others.

Furthermore, there are highly unpredictable weather conditions in the higher altitude region. You should check for the forecast of weather before starting on the trek. Overall, with proper training and preparation, you can complete this trek with ease.

Food And Accommodation along the Trek

The facilities of food and accommodation are pretty standard in this trail of the Everest Gokyo Ri Trek. There are tea houses along trails that provide basic facilities, including twin beds, a mattress, a pillow, a warm blanket, and others.

Trekkers need to book all these facilities of food and accommodation in advance. Toilets are outside of the teahouse and in squat style, which can be pretty challenging for some trekkers to use. There are facilities like Wi-Fi, charging, and hot water in these teahouses. However, they might come at an added cost.

Meals in these teahouses are pretty basic, with bread toasts, eggs, and porridge for breakfast. Tea, garlic soup, coffee, and other hot beverages. The typical Nepalese meal of "Dal Bhat" gets served in teahouses. It includes rice, lentils, dal, meat, spinach, pickles, and others.

Some tea houses also offer momo, noodles, chowmein, pizza, burgers, and others. Besides that, you can also diet on various protein bars, dry fruits, granola bars, snacks, and energy drinks during this tour.

itinerary.title: Day 01: Arrive in Kathmandu
itinerary.html: <strong>Maximum altitude:</strong> 1,350 m After arriving at Tribhuvan International Airport, our local staff will pick you up and transfer you to the hotel. In the hotel, you will get greeted and provided with everything you need during your stay. You can also take a short tour of Kathmandu city and its important cultural heritages. Various landmarks around the city will enchant travelers from all around the world. After exploring around the city, you can return to your hotel and rest for the night.

itinerary.title: Day 02: Sightseeing at Kathmandu and preparation for trek
itinerary.html: <strong>Maximum altitude</strong>: 1,350 m After the meal, we start our scenic journey with a panoramic vista of the diverse cultural heritage of Kathmandu. There are various cultural settlements, temples, and monasteries in Kathmandu. The <strong>UNESCO world heritage sites</strong> of Kathmandu valley are significant attractions of this city. The diverse cultural heritage and traditions of this Kathmandu valley will enthrall you. Travelers can also consume fusion street foods and the delicious local cuisine of Newar people. In addition, there are various shopping stalls, souvenir shops in and around Kathmandu. You can get ideal souvenirs for your family and friends back home. Kathmandu heritage includes <strong>Malla-era durbar squares</strong> in three cities of Kathmandu, Patan, and Bhaktapur. Moreover, there are many temples, monuments, and bihars in these durbar squares. You can also observe old settlements of the Newar community and their lifestyle. You can also taste their delicious cuisine in local eateries. Various museums have ancient monuments that provide travelers with an insight into local history. In addition, there are various religious landmarks in the city, including Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, Swayambhunath, and others. After observing around the beautiful region, you will return to your hotel, where you will stay overnight.

itinerary.title: Day 03: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla and then Trek to Phakding
itinerary.html: <strong>Flight duration:</strong> 3-4 hrs <strong>Hike duration:</strong> 1-2 hrs <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 2,800 m We will have a meal and then head to Lukla from Kathmandu on a scenic morning flight. Travelers will land at <strong>Tenzing/Hillary airport,</strong> which is a small and narrow airstrip. There is a runway of just 500 m with a deep cliff on the other side. After arriving at Lukla, we will start our trek to Phakding. The trails of this trek pass through various scenic landscapes of the region. There are incredible natural landmarks in this region that will enchant any traveler. We will stay at Phakding local teahouse.

itinerary.title: Day 04: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 3,438 m Our trail starts from Phakding as we trek alongside the Dudh Koshi River. We will cross various suspension bridges and then pass through Buddhist monasteries and chortens of the region. <strong>Mt. Thamserku</strong> looks incredibly beautiful from this Benkar village. After showing our trekking permits at Monjo, we will enter the Sagarmatha National Park. After a gradual trek, we will continue our journey to Jorsale. The trail passes through a river bed which we cross through the <strong>Hillary Suspension Bridge.</strong> As we climb through various small sections, we will arrive at Namche Bazaar, the region's commercial hub. The magical views of snow-capped mountains include Mt. Everest, Kusum peak, Kwangde Peak, Kangaru peak, Tawache, Lhotse, etc. We will stay in Namche Bazaar teahouse.

itinerary.title: Day 05: Acclimatization at Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 3,438 m Acclimatization is essential when it comes to high-altitude trekking in the Everest region. There are great sightseeing points in the area, including various cultural and natural landmarks. It is essential to help you tackle <strong>Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS)</strong> or altitude sickness along the region. We can hike to the beautiful Khumjung village and observe magical views of snow-capped mountains from Syangboche or tour the cultural heritage of Namche Bazaar settlements. There is also a Tourist Visitor Center in Namche where you can see various Sherpa culture monuments and heritage of Everest ascenders. There are also various flora and fauna of the region that you can observe along the trail. Khumjung monastery also houses a yeti scalp which is quite an attraction. There is also an airstrip above Syangboche and from where you can observe and enjoy magnificent views of Thamserku, Kongde, and <strong>Khumbila mountains.</strong> We will rest at Namche Bazaar teahouse and spend the night.

itinerary.title: Day 06: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Phortse
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek duration</strong>: 5-6 hrs <strong>Maximum Altitude</strong>: 3,810 m We will have an early morning breakfast and leave Namche Bazaar to Phortse on a gradual trail. We can also spot various rare and endangered wildlife of the region, including musk deer, Himalayan pheasants, and Himalayan Thars. We will then descend back to Kyanjuma and then to Sansa. From Sansa, we will continue our trail to Gokyo, observing majestic views of snow-capped mountains, including <strong>Mt. Thamserku,</strong> Ama Dablam, Khumbila, Tawoche. Our descending path leads you to Dudhkoshi Khola, from where we will then take an uphill trail. We will then pass through various rhododendron forests before finally arriving at Phortse. The Tawache and Cholaste mountains look incredibly beautiful from this viewpoint in the region. A teahouse is our resting place on the Phortse.

itinerary.title: Day 07: Trek from Phortse Village to Machhermo
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek duration:</strong> 5-6 hrs <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 4,470 m We will start our trek by crossing the Koshi River on a suspension bridge. We will observe various rare and endangered wildlife of the region, including mountain goats, pheasants, and musk deer. Our trail then passes through diverse green forests, serene waterfalls, and suspension bridges as you reach Dole. We will take an uphill scenic trail while observing majestic views of snow-capped mountains, including Cho Oyu, Thamserku, Kantega. We will then ascend Luza village and pass through the <strong>Dudh Koshi River</strong> across various suspension bridges. We will then pass through small villages and sandy trails before arriving at Machhermo. We will also visit the Himalayan Rescue Hospital, where we know more about altitude sickness, precaution, and primary treatment. We will stay in Machhermo teahouse for the evening.

itinerary.title: Day 08: Trek from Machhermo to Gokyo
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek duration:</strong> 5-6 hrs <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 4,800 m We will ascend the hills and cross Dudh Koshi valley while observing majestic views of snow-capped mountains, including Kangtega, Cho-Oyu, Thamserku. The trail then takes you alongside the ridge, and the valley widens. You will then pass through this chorten before finally arriving at Phanga. We will first descend to the river bank and climb up to the Ngozumpa Glacier terminal moraine on a steep trail. We will pass through various regional settlements, including Dudh Pokhari, Raboche Tsho, before finally arriving at Gokyo. You will arrive at the first Gokyo lake, where we can observe a <strong>Lama (Buddhist priest)</strong> footprints. We will explore the Dudh Pokhari area and rest overnight at a teahouse in Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Day 09: Gokyo Valley exploration, Climb Gokyo Ri and hike to fifth lakes
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek duration:</strong> 5-6 hrs <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 5,357 m We will explore Gokyo valley and then acclimatize and adapt to the changing high altitude region. We will also climb the trekking peak of Gokyo Ri in case of stable weather conditions. We can observe majestic views of snow-capped mountains and the tranquil Gokyo lakes from the Gokyo Ri summit. We can also hike to the fourth and the fifth Gokyo lakes. The 4th lake is around 3km north of Gokyo. We will continue our journey to arrive at the 5th lake. A sightseeing spot on a hill providing views of Everest, Cho-Oyu, Gyachung Kang, Lhotse, Makulu, and Nuptse. This viewpoint is also known as Scoundrel's Viewpoint. From the 5th lake, we can observe the Cho Oyu base camp and <strong>Ngozumpa Glacier,</strong> the highest glacier in the world. We will hike back to Gokyo and spend the night at a teahouse.

itinerary.title: Day 10: Trek from Gokyo to Dole
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek duration:</strong> 3-4 hrs <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 4,038 m We will start our trail back to the Dudh Koshi River and arrive at Gokyo lakes. The magical views of Himalayan vista including <strong>Cholatse and Taboche peaks.</strong> Our path then leads us through a hill that we descend gradually. After arriving at the edge, we can observe Thamserku, Kangtega, and Cho Oyu mountains. We will pass through Machhermo, and other settlements before Dole. We will stay in the Dole teahouse.

itinerary.title: Day 11: Trek from Dole to Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek duration:</strong> 4-5 hrs <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 3,438 m We will first descend along a steep trail to Phortse Thanga, while observing wildflowers like rhododendrons and waterfalls. We can also watch musk deer, mountain goats, pheasants, etc. From there, we can keep the <strong>Khumbila peak.</strong> The view of the Himalayan vista, including Ama Dablam, Taboche, Thamserku, and Kangtega, will enchant you along the trail. After trekking for a few hours, we will arrive at an intersection where we meet a trail from Sanasa. We will continue our journey to a Kyangjuma forested slope, passing through several bends. After arriving at Namche, we can observe Lhotse, Everest, and Tengboche from a viewpoint. Namche Bazaar has many teahouses and lodges where you will stay overnight.

itinerary.title: Day 12: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla
itinerary.html: <strong>Trek duration:</strong> 4-5 hrs <strong>Maximum Altitude:</strong> 3,438 m We will descend from Namche along a rocky trail and pass through several suspension bridges. The course gets easier as you move along the path and provide you with incredible views of snow capped mountains. After arriving at Lukla, you will rest at a Lukla teahouse.

itinerary.title: Day 13: Fly to Kathmandu
itinerary.html: <strong>Maximum altitude:</strong> 1,350 m After having a sumptuous breakfast, we will take an early morning flight to Kathmandu from Lukla. We will arrive at this destination after around 35-40 minutes of flight. Moreover, you can observe majestic views of snow-capped mountains, including <strong>Mt Everest.</strong> We will then take you to a hotel where you can rest for the evening.

sections.title: Things You Should Know
sections.html:
Why Everest Gokyo Ri Trek?

Adventurous trails

A trekking adventure among a large number of crowds is another advantage of this trek. The Everest region boasts various wildflowers, including rhododendron, oak, juniper, and others, providing a beautiful atmosphere. A solo trek will also provide you with an experience of group trekking. This incredible once-in-a-lifetime adventure will enchant any traveler.

Magical mountain vista

The Mahalangur Himalayan range looks incredibly beautiful along the trails of this trek. Mt. Everest and other snow-capped mountains of the region will enchant all travelers. Moreover, there are clear blue skies and other vistas of snow-capped mountains. The mystical gorgeous sunrise and sunsets are another highlight of this trail.

Exploring flora and fauna

The wildlife of the region, including snow leopards, Himalayan Tahrs, danfe, and others are highlights in this trek. The rare and endangered wildlife get preserved in Sagarmatha National Park. The region's natural habitat has many diversities in terms of landscapes as well. This includes the snow-capped Himalayas, green hills, valleys, meadows, and others.

Cultural exploration

Everest region is also known for its cultural heritage. The Sherpa Tibetan community will enchant any traveler as there is a unique lifestyle and heritage. You can also explore the local settlements of the region.

Besides that, there are various cultural explorations through monuments, chortens, and main walls. Buddhism heritage across the region is quite significant. Temples and monasteries across the region are significant as you can observe monks and devotees offering these prayers.

Things to Consider for Everest Gokyo Ri Trek

Acute Mountain sickness

Altitude sickness is one of the challenging aspects of the trek. This altitude sickness is quite tricky as there are high altitude trails, and therefore, you should perform acclimatization and hydration.

Himalayan Rescue Mission in this region provides required medical treatment and consultation to trekkers in Pheriche. The necessary preparation is essential to tackle altitude sickness along the trail.

Professional Guide

Everest region trails have rugged and remote landscapes. These professional guides will help you explore the culture, lifestyle, and tradition of local people. Moreover, a porter will carry all your luggage during your trek. Porter guides also work as both porters as well as guides.

Physical Fitness

Fitness and stamina are essential when it comes to trekking in the Everest Gokyo region. Thus, training routines in this trek require cardiovascular activities like cycling, swimming, hiking, and others. Acclimatization will also help you tackle altitude sickness and gain both physical and mental fitness.

Trek Permits

Travel permits are essential for this Everest Gokyo Ri Trek in Nepal. Trekkers require Pasang Lhamu rural municipality's area permit, local area permit, and others. You can either get these permits in Lukla or Monjo. The trekkers can also get them from the Nepal tourism board in Kathmandu.

Travel insurance

Travel insurance is another essential aspect of this trek. Accidents, medical emergencies are pretty common on this trek. Moreover, the travel insurance also provides you with a helicopter evacuation that can cost anywhere between $5000 to $10000. Therefore, the right travel insurance is essential to cover all your necessities.

Essentials Tips For Everest Gokyo Ri Trek

  • Acclimatize and hydrate regularly
  • Get a proper training regime before starting on this trek
  • Start your trek early during this trek
  • Meal and accommodation need to get booked in advance
  • Carry tablets for water purifying along with a water bottle
  • Pack only those items that are necessary
  • Get a power bank, solar charger, and extra batteries
  • Carry protein bars, snickers, granola bars, chocolate bars to munch on during your trek

Final Say

The Everest Gokyo Ri Trek is an outstanding adventure in the beautiful landscape of the region. The atmosphere of this trekking adventure will enchant you along the trail. There are moderate temperatures in the Everest region. The magical Himalayan vista of the area will delight any traveler.

The Gokyo Ri trails will provide you with an ideal trekking climate. A scenic adventure of this region includes unobstructed views of the snow-capped mountains. Mount Everest, Lhotse, Mt. Ama Dablam, Nuptse, and others are some of the significant mountains that you can observe on this trek.

Moreover, food and meal facilities are pretty standard in this trail as you will stay in local tea houses and lodges. We hope you learned about Everest Gokyo Ri Trek in detail. Contact us for more information on the itinerary and book your trip now.

overview:
Everest Gokyo Trek would definitely be a life time experience for a trekker. Yearly thousands of adventure aspirant come here to explore the natural land and breath-taking Gokyo valley. From Gokyo Ri (Gokyo Peak) one can view the scenic view of fascinating mountains from north to south of Everest region including the mighty Everest as well.

Trekking to Gokyo valley deluges you with the great opportunity to witness the Ngozumpa glacier which is the biggest in Nepal’s Himalaya. The most fascinating benefit of Everest Gokyo Trek is extreme view of huge ice ridge located between Cho You and Gyachung in Khumbu region. It is known for the existence of high altitude lakes as well. These mountains, ridges and glaciers are supernatural as are your experiences with the Sherpa individuals, the well-known mountain inhabitants of this Himalayan wonderland. The glow and cordiality stretched out by the neighbourhood tenants of this district, the Sherpas, will add a further dimension to your experience of trekking in Nepal.

Your trek starts after a forty minute flight from Kathmandu and landing at a tiny Lukla’s airport. The trek trail follows Phakding, Namche bazaar, Dole all the way to Machhermo. Along the way you can encounter many farm villages along with striking views of the high snow-capped peaks of the world. The trekking trails eventually leads you to the famous point of Gokyo Ri (Gokyo Ri- a famous trekking peak) from where you can have a awe-inspiring view of hundreds of pleasing scenery.

Gokyo Ri, also known as Gokyo Peak (5,357 m, 17,575 ft above ocean level), is a top in the Khumbu region of the Nepal Himalayas. It is situated on the west side of the Ngozumpa glacier, which is the biggest glacier in Nepal and rumoured to be the biggest in the entire Himalayas. At the base of Gokyo Ri, is a small hamlet of few stone houses and one of the highest settlements on the planet. The vintage point of Gokyo Ri will reward you with staggering views of four of the eight highest mountains on earth; Cho Oyu (8153-m), Lhotse (8501-m), Makalu (8463-m) and the Everest (8848-m). The Gokyo trek ends at Gokyo Ri, and trekkers commonly turn around at this point and follow their progressions back to the trail-head.

The Gokyo valley trek is considered as a typical trek that is suitable for everyone. Our schedule gives two evenings in Namche Bazaar for acclimatization, with the goal that you won’t be in a risk from acute mountain sickness. This minimizes your shots of getting AMS and helps you make it securely to the highest point of Gokyo. So, if you are fairly fit and have a sense of adventure, you will definitely enjoy the Gokyo valley trek.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Tribhuwan International Airport (TIA), Kathmandu and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: Upon your arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, you will be greeted by our office representative who will then transfer you to your hotel. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft) and then same day trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: After this 40 minutes flight, the trek from Lukla to Phakding (2,640 m) which takes approximately three hours. You begin today trek from Lukla following a gentle climb up the mountainside on the left bank of the Dudh Koshi river. Nupla (5,885 m) can be seen in the distance on the opposite bank, is a peak atop the Kongde Ridge. You descend a mountainside path that merges into your route to Everest, with views to a valley to your right; and at its far end, Kusum Kang (6,367 m) The Dudh Kosi approaches as you pass a Mani wall and arrive at Ghat teahouse. You continue along a small path with many climbs and descents following the left bank of Dudh Koshi to Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: This day you trek and cross the river on high suspension bridges. Beyond Monjo (2,800 m) is the entrance to the Sagarmatha National Park which was set-up in order to protect and preserve this fragile mountain environment. You then ascend quite steeply to Namche and along the way, if the weather is clear, catch a first glimpse of Mt Everest in the distance. You can also enjoy the view of Mt. Kusum Kangaru, Thamserku, Konde-Ri and Tawache peak. You can also visit some of the village monasteries on the way of trekking to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m). Namche is the main trading village in the Khumbu region and holds a busy Saturday market. There is set a meeting place for the Hindu traders from the lowlands and the Tibetan yak caravans that have reached there by crossing the glaciated Nangpa La.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft).
itinerary.html: Namche is tucked away between two ridges amidst the giant peaks of the Khumbu and has an abundance of lodges, tea shops and souvenir shops as well as a magnificent outlook. It is an ideal place to spend a rest day for acclimatization at the high altitude before heading higher elevation. For the acclimatization you walk up to Khunde Hospital which was set-up by Sir Edmund Hillary, or Everest View Hotel.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Dole (4,200 m / 13,780 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: From Namche the route heads up all the way to Kumjung, a picturesque village which also has its own Gompa at the top end of town. Here you can have excellent views of Thamserku, Kantega and Ama Dablam. Soon after leaving Khumjung the trail climbs to a large chorten on top of a ridge. This ridge descends from Khumbila, a 5,734 m peak, said to be the abode of the patron God of the Khumbu region. The trail descends slightly towards the Sanasa and then trail ascends up to Mongla (4,000 m). From here, you can see panoramic views of various mountains. You trek steeply descend passing through Phortse Tenga and from there, the trail climbs steeply to Dole, through rhododendron and birch forest festooned with hanging mosses and lichens.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dole to Machhermo (4,470 m / 14,665 ft). 4-5 hours
itinerary.html: From Dole you climb steadily along the side of the valley, where the small and thorny bushes give way to scrub juniper as the altitude increases. The trail passes many summer settlements, which are used when yaks are taken to these pastures to graze in the summer months. Ahead of you are excellent views of Cho Oyu, while back down the valley are the peaks of Kantega and Thamserku. This is a short day and you will arrive at Machhermo in time for lunch.

itinerary.title: Trek from Machhermo to Gokyo (4,790 m / 15,715 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you head for the lakes at Gokyo. You follow a very scenic path to Pangka and then descend slightly, following one of the melt-water rivers which flow down the west side of the Ngozumpa Glacier. You climb a steep rocky inclined into the valley by the side of the glacier, passing the first of the holy lakes. You soon arrive at the second of the lakes, crossing the path which heads across the glacier to Cho La (5,420 m), your route to Lobuche and Everest and later in the trek. The third lake is known as Dudh Pokhari and on its eastern shore is the settlement of Gokyo. Walking by the side of the lake, the scenery is magnificent with the summits of Cho Oyu and Gyachung Kang reflected in its emerald green waters.

itinerary.title: Trek Gokyo Ri (5,357 m / 17,575 ft) and trek back to Machhermo (4,470 m / 14,665 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Gokyo Ri looms above the village on the northern edge of the lake and you leave camp just after first light, following a steep path up the hillside. As you climb, the summits of Everest, Lhotse and Makalu slowly come into sight and the view from the summit of Gokyo Ri itself, is one of the finest to be had in the Everest region, some say that the Everest view is even better than from Kala Patthar. After lunch it is a short walk to the village of Machhermo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Machhermo to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail gently descends to Dole and then starts descending steeply to Photse Tenga (3,650 m) passing through rhododendron forests. Then the path immediately ascends steeply to Mongla Danda (4,000 m) and gently descends up to Kyanjoma (3,500 m) following small ups and down to Namche Bazar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (22,860 m / 9,383 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: The last day of your trek leads from Namche Bazaar via Monjo to Lukla. The trek is pleasant, except for few short uphill climbs and then down to the Bhote- Koshi River crossing it three times. The last uphill climb of 45 minutes will bring you to Lukla for your overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu, (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html: You take an early morning flight back to Kathmandu. Upon arrival in Kathmandu, you will be transferred to your hotel. You can spend your leisure time either exploring the vibrant markets of Kathmandu or just resting in your hotel room. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Airport for your onward destination.
itinerary.html: You will be dropped at Tribhuvan International Airport from your hotel for your return flight to your country.

faqs.q: I’ve never trekked before. Can I do this trek?
faqs.a: As long as you are reasonably fit, mentally prepared and can walk for 6-7-hours a day then no matter who you are and what your background is, a bit of training may be necessary, but even that is not 100% essential for most.

faqs.q: How many miles do you walk each day?
faqs.a: In average you walk around 4-7 miles per day while going up and 8-12 miles while coming down.

faqs.q: Is there battery charging facility?
faqs.a: The tea houses have charging ability via their solar panels but if it has been cloudy for several days, there may not be enough reserves to charge barberries for your camera, and thus it is better to have an extra battery. Teahouses usually charge for it – maybe a 300-500 rupees per hour. Many people want to charge their batteries so try to plug your stuff in as soon as you arrive.

faqs.q: Can I do laundry on the trek?
faqs.a: Yes, you can. You can take this service with guest house. This will not be by machine, it will be by hand. Or, you can do your own laundry in a bucket.

faqs.q: Is there bottled water on the Gokyo trek?
faqs.a: Yes, there’s bottled water from Lukla all the way up to Gokyo Village. But, the price goes up the higher you go. One liter bottle of water cost start around 70 rupees and at base camp cost well over 250 (around $2.5). A budget solution to this is to use water treatment solution or use water purifier tablets. Some purification tabs and drops make the water taste weird. Please be aware of that too. Buying boiled water can be a solution to save money from expensive bottled water but make sure if water was fully boiled or not before you buy.

faqs.q: Is there age limit for Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a: There isn’t any official age limit saying you can and cannot trek to Gokyo .

faqs.q: How difficult is the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a: In terms of terrain there are no ropes needed and no ice picks needed. There is no vertical climbing involved. The ground is not paved. It is rough, rocky and gravel strewn. Most of the trek involves long paths that go up and then down. People with weak ankles should take caution. Depending on the time of year you go there can also be snow and ice in the trails. There are some boulders that need climbing, but you can also walk around many.

faqs.q: Can children go the Gokyo Valley trek?
faqs.a: Yes is the general rule. It’s advisable that your child is reasonable and able to understand and follow instructions immediately. Your child should be mature enough to recognize altitude sickness symptoms.

overview: Everest Gokyo Trek with Helicopter return is undoubtedly one of the mesmerizing trekking options to be considered as this trek takes you to the heart of mountains and Gokyo Valley along with a befitting helicopter flight directly from Gokyo Valley to Kathmandu. It indulges you with the scenic beauty of the mountainous range, along with giving insights into the Himalayan lifestyle. Everest Gokyo Trek is the stirring journey to the Gokyo Lakes and Gokyo Ri through sightseeing stunning Himalayan landscapes, local settlements, monasteries, and cascading waterfalls alongside the roaring Dudh Koshi and Bhote Koshi River. This trek is a magical journey that is infused with lively moments along the way. Traversing through staggering mountainous regions and diverse topography with the scenic beauty of the Himalayan region and its habitat is indeed a wonderful experience. You’ll be stunned by the magical beauty of the pristine Himalayas reflecting through tranquil Gokyo Lakes while a clear day summons a vibrant atmosphere all around. Being a shorter and more accessible trekking site, it invites thousands of people from all around the world to relish the outstanding views of the Himalayas and Gokyo Lake. The six lakes are Thonak Cho (largest), Taujung Cho, Gyazumpa Cho, Ngozumpa Cho (smallest), Longpongo Cho, and Gokyo Cho. Gokyo Cho is the main lake of six of them and is the major attraction site which is also known as Dudhpokhari. This trek takes you through a series of stopovers and is 9 Days trek in total. You’ll be heading through local villages from Lukla to Phakding and finally acclimatizing at Namche Bazaar, which is a stunning marketplace and beautiful village in the Solukhumbu District. The exhilarating Everest Gokyo Trek takes you to the Gokyo Valley through famous stopovers on the way, like Dole and Machhermo, that present you with the sights of the stunning vistas of mountains like Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Kanchenjunga, and Gokyo Ri. Moreover, this trek offers you a splendid time with one of the highest freshwater lakes in the world and magnifies your trekking experience by double through a moderately challenging journey.

itinerary.title: Arrival at Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.html: Your Gokyo Trek with Helicopter return begins after you arrive at Kathmandu. Our team will receive you from the Airport and transfer you to a cozy hotel. Our team will also help in your checking process at your hotel. You’ll wander around local places while trying some delicious foods in Kathmandu on your first day. You can visit numerous places around along with cultural heritage sites like Bhaktapur Durbar Square, Kathmandu Durbar Square, Patan Durbar Square, Swoyambunath, Pashupatinath, Bouddhanath and many more. Being not able to visit all the places in a single day, you’ll have to pick some of the places. Also, this day marks the preparation day with packing the necessary clothes, gear and equipment for your epic adventure to the lap of mountains.

itinerary.title: Flight from Kathmandu to Lukla and trek to Phakding
itinerary.html: Kathmandu Elevation: 1,400 m Lukla Elevation: 2,860 m Elevation gain: 1,460 m Flight duration: 45 minutes Trek duration: 3-4 hrs The rip-roaring adventure to the heart of Gokyo Ri begins today. After your early morning breakfast at your hotel, you’ll be picked up by our team and transferred to the domestic terminal of the Tribhuwan International Airport. Then, you’ll catch a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla, which is about 45 minutes. This flight takes you through different monuments, lush green valleys, forests, local settlements, and temples. This flight generates your excitement through aerial views of stunning landscapes covered in lush greenery. The sights are truly awesome as the entangled sea of forests makes an appearance, along with thundering rivers and gushing waterfalls along the way. Then, the flight takes you closer to the eastern part of Nepal, which offers you magical views of distant mountain ranges. You’ll be catching glimpses of routes and mountain passes that you’ll be trekking situated at a distant location. After that, the excitement reaches its peak during the stirring landing at the Lukla Airport. You’ll discover the local villages of Lukla and nearby settlements after you land at Lukla. The journey has just begun, and it has pushed you out of your comfort zone since this day. As you’ll be trekking through trails and routes to reach Phakding, you’ll sightsee local settlements and distinct lifestyles. You’ll be trekking through places like Chheplung, Ghat, and Nurning alongside the roaring Dudh Koshi River. You’ll be taking a short break at one of the teahouses of the famous stopovers known as Ghat, and the place will serve you the beautiful sights of Nupla (5885) and Kusum Kang (6,367 m) as a welcoming gesture. You’ll also see Mani walls along the way that are scripted in Buddhist mantras. It holds religious value, and devotional designs of Buddhism are painted on the wall. It is also believed that visiting such places and showing gratitude invites great fortune into your life. Today, Phakding shall welcome you with warm hospitality to have a warm night along with delicious food.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: Phakding Elevation: 2,610 m Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m Elevation gain: 830 m Trek duration: 6-7 hrs The actual trekking journey begins today after you depart from Phakding. The trek takes you through a series of places and local village settlements before reaching one of the major towns in Solukhumbu, Namche Bazaar. This trek begins along the bank of Dudh Koshi River and lush forests of Rhododendron, Fir, and Pine trees. After that, you’ll be blessed with riveting moments of crossing the thundering river over the suspension bridge. Following the trails, you’ll walk through forests and catch magical glimpses of Mt. Kusum Kangaru, Konde-Ri, and Kusum Kanguru. Along the way, you’ll also encounter numerous monasteries, guesthouses and mountain settlements. Then, you’ll reach one of the major stopovers, where you’ll be stunned after beholding the beauty of the tallest mountain in the world, Mt. Everest. After fulfillment of your sightseeing majestic mountain ranges, we’ll push our trek towards Namche Bazaar. Considering your case of luck, you may also sightsee Himalayan wild species like Himalayan Tahr, Musk deer, and monkeys. We’ll be registering our trekking details at the entrance of Sagarmatha National Park in Monjo. You’ll be crossing the soaring Bhote Koshi River over the suspension bridge and finally arrive at Namche Bazaar. We’ll spend our night at one of the finest lodges of Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization at Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: By our 4th day, we’ve ascended by 3,440 m in altitude. We’ll face a change in atmospheric pressure and decreased oxygen level at this altitude. Therefore, in order to adapt to the changing environment and have a safe and steady trekking journey, we’ll be acclimatizing at Namche Bazaar. Though it is your rest day, you can still wander around the local villages and explore different settlements. Namche Bazaar is a staging point for Everest Base Camp Trek and Everest Gokyo Trek. The village includes Tibetan settlements and has a colorful market. You can delve into local practices and cultural artifacts and also prepare yourself for your trekking journey. Along with that, Namche Bazaar has access to trekking gear and equipment that you can look after. Namche Bazaar is famous for local yak butter and cheese and along with that, you can try numerous delectable cuisines. This village also serves the magical sights of the stunning mountain range. Moreover, you can also explore local Sherpa culture and visit Sherpa museums. Also, you’ll be presented with options to trek to local places like Syangboche and Khumjung and explore the local community. There is the presence of the Khumjung Monastery, which shall give you insights into Buddhism, along with Hillary School, which was named after the New Zealand mountaineer who reached the Summit of the Everest for the 1st time with Tenzing Norgay Sherpa.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Dole
itinerary.html: Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m Dole Elevation: 4,040 m Elevation gain: 600 m Trek duration: 6-7 hrs After fully resting and acclimatizing at Namche Bazaar, we begin our trek to Dole through sightseeing staggering peaks like Ama Dablam, Thamserku and Kantega. We ascend along the trails of Khumjung and reach the mountain pass of Mongla. We may also encounter distinct Himalayan wild species along with the Himalayan Monal, the national bird of Nepal. We stop for a tea break at Mongla, and this place presents you with stunning views of the mountain range. After relishing the magical beauty of the Himalayas, we continue our trek along the trails of pine and rhododendron forests and descend along the route to Phortse Thanga. Phortse Thanga is a small village that is situated on the bank of the river and lies at an altitude of 3,680 m This place also serves you majestic glimpses of the mountain range. As your trek advances, you’ll feel the sensation of approaching the mountains. Along with that, you’ll also encounter Himalayan settlements and the remoteness of the region. From Phortse Thanga, we’ll start ascending for a few hours, and we’ll arrive at Dole. Dole is the famous stopping point for trekkers and serves you great views of the Himalayan range. From here, you can enjoy the majestic Mt. Everest, along with surrounding snowy landscapes.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dole to Machhermo
itinerary.html: Dole Elevation: 4,040 m Machhermo Elevation: 4,470 m Elevation gain: 430 m Trek duration: 4-5 hrs We’ll leave for our trekking journey after our early morning breakfast at Dole. Dole serves you a delicious breakfast that keeps you fueled for a few hours until you reach for tea stop by. The trail to Machhermo is full of bushy trails and summer settlements. Being a relatively shorter hike for the day, we’ll maintain a steady pace and move along while enjoying the magical beauty of the Himalayan region. As we start to approach Machhermo, we’ll catch spectacular views of the mountain range. Stunning views of Cho Oyu and snowy landscapes are clearly visible. Our path then follows alongside the trails of Dudh Koshi River for about 2-3 hours, sightseeing local settlements and distant mountainous peaks. Then we reach Machhermo, where we’ll be resting overnight. Machhermo is a small village that is located in the northern direction of Dole and the southern direction of Gokyo Valley. It is located directly beneath the Ngozumpa glacier's terminal moraine, which is the longest glacier in the Himalayas. This place beholds incredible Himalayas views and has facilitated teahouses and lodges. Today, we’ll be enjoying the ambiance of the Macchermo village while also exploring local settlements and preparing for our incredible trek to Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Machhermo to Gokyo
itinerary.html: Machhermo Elevation: 4,470 m Gokyo Elevation: 4,750 m Elevation gain: 280m Trek duration: 4-5 hrs This day marks a glorious day as you’ll be trekking to Gokyo Valley to sightsee Gokyo lakes. You’ll follow a scenic path through Sherpa villages, monasteries, and stupas alongside the banks of the Dudh Koshi River before reaching the moraine of Ngozumpa glacier. On the way, you’ll be treated to the epic scenes of the Khumbu Himalayas. The Gokyo Lakes comprise six lakes and lie in between the glacial moraine and Cho Oyu (the sixth tallest mountain in the world with a height of 8,188 m). The largest of the six sizable freshwater lakes in the Gokyo Valley Lakes is Thonak Cho, which is followed by Gokyo Cho. Gokyo Cho is also known as Dudh Pokhari, while the third lake is known as Gyazumpa Cho, which is followed by Tanjung Cho, Longpongo, and Ngojumba Cho. These lakes have hydrological value and offer wonderful experiences to the trekkers and visitors. Experiencing the tranquil state of these lakes situated in the lap of mountains emerges a sense of peace and calmness within. The Gokyo Lakes is beautiful and as the ripples of the lake soars towards its banks, it reflects clear blue sky and surrounding mountain ranges. Gokyo lakes are sacred as they hold religious significance. This lake is worshipped by Hindus and Buddhists and it is considered that taking a holy bath in this lake shall bring fortune in one’s life. Numerous people visit Gokyo Lake for its stunning beauty, while more than 500 people emerge themselves in this holy lake for a holy bath during the Janai Purnima Festival of Nepal. We’ll arrive at Gokyo Lakes after relishing the beauty of the region, we head towards one of the local teahouses for our nightstay.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gokyo to Gokyo Ri and flight from Gokyo to Kathmandu
itinerary.html: Gokyo Elevation: 4,750 m Gokyo Ri Elevation: 5,483 m Elevation gain: 733 m Trek duration: 6-7 hrs Flight duration: 1 hour 30 minutes This is the last day of Everest Gokyo Trek with Helicopter return. As our trek is leaning towards an end, we’ll trek to Gokyo Ri to sightsee the stunning mountain range. Gokyo Ri is a gigantic mountain with a height of 5,357 m We ascend along the trails and after 2-3 hours of strenuous trekking, we’ll reach our destination. From here, you’ll witness the magical view of the Ngozumpa glacier and surrounding peaks. You’ll be treated to the stunning appearance of Everest, Lhotse, Cho Oyu, Taboche, and Cholatse. Gokyo Trek offers you spectacular up-close views of Mt. Everest. You may see several smaller, snow-covered 7000-meter mountains from this vantage point. Formerly, Gokyo Ri top was regarded as the best vantage point in the entire Everest region. The Gokyo trek offers you majestic views of the Himalayas, gives insights into the Himalayan lifestyle, and fulfills your trek with an exhilarating and wonderful experience, rewarding you with a great sense of achievement. After fulfillment of relishing the beauty of the Himalayas, you’ll retrace back to Gokyo Valley. Normally, you’d have to trek back to Lukla through the same route ascended but through our special package, you’ll catch a direct flight from Gokyo Valley to Kathmandu. This takes around 1 hour and 30 minutes, and until then, you shall enjoy the magical glimpses of the Himalayan range from the window of the chopper. You’ll be reminiscing these marvelous experiences you have collected through the Everest Gokyo Trek with Helicopter return. While you may be missed by the gigantic mountains and Himalayan settlements, you shall relish the nostalgic memories you have accumulated.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Airport for your departure
itinerary.html: This marks the end of your Everest Gokyo Trek. With a remarkable journey, you’ve made many memories in the heart of mountains. There is space for exploration of more places, and it's completely up to you to visit local places or begin another trek. Our team will pick you up from your hotel and transfer you to the Tribhuwan International Airport as per your flight schedule. You will have a tale to tell your folks and country.

sections.title: Best time for Everest Gokyo Trek
sections.html:
Best time for Everest Gokyo Trek

When it comes to enjoying the majestic beauty of the Gokyo Ri, Mt. Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Gokyo Lakes through Everest Gokyo Trek, planning your trek during a suitable time is crucial. The best time for the Everest Gokyo Trek is during Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November). During this time you shall enjoy the magical beauty of the Himalayas with less forthcoming challenges on the way. You shall experience a stable climate and have a secure and enjoyable experience in the Himalayan region. It reduces the risks of rainfall, snowfall, and windstorms along with minimizing the consequences like slippery tracks or snowy trails. Being an easy trek, planning your journey during Spring or Autumn lets you immerse into the beauty of the Gokyo Ri and Gokyo Lakes with warm and dry weather. Furthermore, this presents you with a transparent view of the snowy peaks, and clear visibility smoothes your trek with the minimization of forthcoming obstacles. Spring and Autumn summons clear weather, and you shall enjoy the breathtaking sunrise glancing upon the Himalayas peaks. The peaceful environment and majestic sights of the mountainous range and Gokyo Lakes present in its lap shall invite tranquility within. Overall, Everest Gokyo Trek is a fusion of magical sightseeing and Himalayan exploration, and planning your trek during a suitable time shall add beauty to this region while you also get insights into the Himalayan lifestyle, distinct culture, and festive atmosphere. Moreover, Everest Gokyo Trek with Helicopter Return serves you with excellent experience and comfy traveling service directly from Gokyo Valley to Kathmandu.

Why Everest Gokyo Trek?

Mesmerising views

Everest Gokyo trek offers you the scenic beauty of the Himalayas, Gokyo Lakes, and surrounding landscapes. From the beginning of your journey from flight to Lukla, you’ll be treated to stunning sights of mountainous vistas and Himalayan landscapes. The journey is stirring, from the dramatic landing at the Lukla airport to trekking through trails and forests alongside the river to the high Himalayan region. You’ll be presented with magical sights of the Himalayan range that shall magnify your trekking journey to the fullest. This trek serves you with the magical sights of Everest, Makalu, Lhotse, Cho Oyu, and Gokyo Ri. What’s more, is that this trek presents you with clear and unobstructed views of the Himalayan vistas compared to Everest Base Camp with a delightful experience. There are numerous stopovers along the way to Gokyo Ri from where you’ll observe the outstanding gigantic Himalayas peaks. This trek takes you to the Gokyo Valley through numerous village settlements and monasteries where you shall get insights into the local culture and high Himalayan settlements. A clear and warm day summons naked picturesque views of mountainous vistas dancing in the vibrant atmosphere of the stunning sunrise. Moreover, the pristine mountain twirling in the reflection with the swaying waves of the Gokyo Lake shall leave you stunned. The tranquil state of the Gokyo Lakes, the whipping cold breeze of the Himalayas, and the Himalayan culture shall give you insight into the Himalayan region, marking an expression of reaching heaven. While the destination is truly awesome, the journey itself is mesmerizing and stirring. Everest Gokyo Trek takes you through a series of rugged trails and challenging terrain that boosts your trekking experience thrice. Furthermore, it presents numerous Mani walls, Buddhist practices, and Monasteries that shall give you insights into the local traditions and enlighten spirituality. Along with that, you shall be treated to the stunning appearance of Cascading waterfalls and Ngozumpa Glacier. You’ll enjoy the unspoiled grandeur of beautiful alpine landscapes and majestic peaks with a stable atmosphere and crystalline skies.

Rip-roaring journey

Trekking is really fun when you’ll have to surpass the forthcoming challenges and pave your way securely and safely to the heart of the mountains. You’ll be ascending in altitude during the Everest Gokyo Trek through acclimatizing and maintaining a steady pace. The Everest Gokyo trek with Helicopter return is undeniably a wonderful journey to the lap of Gokyo Ri in a short period of time. While it serves you excellent views of the stunning Himalayan Vistas and snowy landscapes, the journey itself is full of action-packed moments. You’ll be thrilled by the epic landing at Lukla Airport, and passing through challenging terrain, bushes, and lush forests prolongs your excitement. The journey to the lap of mountains and Gokyo lakes is indeed beautiful, but the route following it is rip-roaring. You’ll have to deal with rugged terrain, steep ridges, and numerous forthcoming challenges like steep ascents and descents. Furthermore, your trek shall be filled with stirring moments when you overpass the climatic challenges like light rainfall and snowfall. This journey allows you to disconnect from the world for a while and purely relish the beauty of the Himalayan region. Besides challenging terrain, rocky trails, and steep ridges, this journey invites extreme coldness and gushing windstorms that make this journey challenging and interesting. On the way, you’ll encounter high Himalayan settlements and local culture that provides you with a variation of Human lifestyle. You’ll be trekking through steep ascents and descents while dividing your attention to the trails and mountainous vistas alongside the roaring Dudh Koshi River and Bhote Koshi River. Crossing these thundering rivers over sweeping Suspension bridges, passing through rollercoaster terrains, and meeting new heights shall add depth to the marvelous experience of the rip-roaring journey to the heart of Gokyo Ri and Gokyo Lakes

Himalayan culture and lifestyle

The fascinating Himalayan culture and lifestyle introduce you to the traditional Sherpa villages that are rich in customs and traditions. On the way to Gokyo Ri and Gokyo Valley, you’ll witness the lifestyle of the Himalayan region, their agriculture, animal husbandry, and farming. This lets you delve into the lifestyle of Himalayan people and get insights into the nature-dependent lifestyle. You shall be welcomed by the local villagers with warm hospitality, and it is also the best opportunity to learn about their traditions and way of living. They share the same Himalayan breeze and live under the same roof of a mountainous range while their way of living resembles the ancient way of living. Besides breathtaking views of the snow-capped mountains, you shall be infused with ethnic diversity and different customs of the high Himalayan region. Moreover, you shall get the opportunity to immerse yourself in the rich festivals of the region. Festivals in Nepal arrive one after another, leaving the beautiful ambiance of the cultural atmosphere. The village will be decorated with medium light following local customs, while people shall be garnished with traditional costumes. The Himalayan people are kind and warm-hearted and engage in each other's culture happily. Unity is their strength, and they celebrate each festival enthusiastically. The people of this region mainly celebrate Mani Rimdu and Lhosar by performing traditional dances to their local music. Being rich in cultural and festive atmosphere, Everest Gokyo Trek lets you relish the beauty of the stunning mountainous peaks while blending in the Himalayan culture and lifestyle.

Sagarmatha National Park

Everest Gokyo Trek is rich in biodiversity as the region is home to Sagarmatha National Park. Sagarmatha National Park is a world heritage site that is spread over an area of 1,148 sq km in the Solukhumbu district of Nepal and encircles gigantic mountains, glaciers, and deep valleys. You’ll experience its ecological value from the start of your trek while you’ll be witnessing distinct flora and fauna after you enter the entrance of Sagarmantha National Park from Monjo. You’ll be passing through lush green valleys and dense forests of rhododendron and pine trees which shall let you immerse in the beauty of the region. This park encompasses gigantic mountains, gushing waterfalls, and soaring rivers. This region includes the world's tallest mountain, Mt. Everest, along with many sibling mountains, Lhotse, Nuptse, Thamserku, Cho Oyu, Amadablam, and Pumori. It is comprised mainly of Buddhist settlements and has many monasteries. Places like Tengboche, Khumjung, Thame, and Pangboche are home to the celebration of different festivals, including Mani Rimdu. Moreover, you’ll encounter glimpses of Himalayan wildlife species like Himalayan Tahr, Musk deer, Red Panda, and Snow Leopard that invite thrills within. Sagarmatha National Park is home to more than 118 species of birds, such as the Impeyan pheasant, blood pheasant, and Snow cock, including the Himalayan Monal, the national bird of Nepal. It is rich in ecology and contributes to the overall biodiversity and climatic conditions of the region. Being home to ecological value, it invites trekkers and visitors from all parts of the world. It has majestic sights and wonderful experiences to offer while delving into the Himalayan atmosphere.

Secure, accessible, and short trek

Everest Gokyo Trek serves you magical sights of the Himalayan peaks along with the local Himalayan lifestyle. Breathing in the breeze of the Himalayan region deprived of pollution is a wonderful experience but the secure route of the Everest Gokyo Trek enhances the trekking journey by two or three. It is an easy and short trek and is accessible to a wide range of people. While it also demands sheer determination and physical strength, this trek is moderate level with no difficulties like Everest Base Camp Trek and Langtang Valley Trek. Your journey passes through the safe route where few adventurer souls travel. This lets you have a quality and peaceful time with the Himalayas while deepening your connection with nature. There won’t be any competition in acquiring accommodation and a less crowded atmosphere lets you delve into the local traditions and customs. This opens your room for more exploration of the local areas of the Himalayan region, and you can relish the beauty of the pristine Himalayas while wandering around.

Everest Gokyo Trek Challenges

Though Everest Gokyo Trek is a safe trek, trekking to the high Himalayan region imposes numerous challenges along the way, which need to be considered. You’ll be passing through elevated and rugged surfaces along the way, and ascending in altitude results in changes in atmospheric pressure and decreased oxygen level, which can impose altitude sickness. Altitude sickness or Acute Mountain Sickness is caused if your body can’t adapt to the changing environment and decreased oxygen level. It can cause mild headaches, nausea, and appetite loss during your journey. Therefore, it is important to maintain a steady pace and acclimatize properly during your trekking journey. Moreover, you should be mindful of the weather conditions of the Himalayan region. Even if you plan your trek during a suitable time when the chances of fluctuations in weather are low. You should take necessary precautions for any sudden changes and prepare accordingly. The Himalayan region’s weather can’t be trusted, and it may bring challenges like rainfall, snowfall, and windstorms. Therefore, being mindful of these conditions and packing your backpack with warm clothes is essential. Along with that, you must pack trekking poles and trekking boots that shall help you during your journey and ensure you a safe and amusing trekking experience. Furthermore, the foggy weather may reduce visibility during your trekking. You should monitor weather forecasts on a regular basis to know the weather conditions of the region. While the Everest Gokyo Trek with Helicopter Return is a moderate-level trek, you should still practice some lightweight exercises and stretching to reduce the risks of injuries and back pain. Steep ridges and trekking through ascents and descents shall impose leg pain and joint pain as well, which is why squats, pushups, pullups, running, walking, and swimming shall aid in the development of your endurance and physical strength. Also, stretching shall enhance flexibility and prepare you for the rip-roaring journey. You may also like:
  • Everest Gokyo Ri Trek
  • Everest and Gokyo Lakes Trek 14 Days
  • Gokyo Lakes and Everest Base Camp
  • Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return

Some helpful tips to overcome Everest Gokyo Trek Difficulties

Here are some helpful tips that play a vital role in minimizing the Gokyo Trek challenges. Even though the Everest Gokyo Trek with Helicopter return won’t indulge you descending through the same route you ascended, it is important to be mindful of circumstances. Take your time researching properly before heading for the Everest Gokyo Trek.
  • Stay hydrated and maintain a steady pace during your trekking journey.
  • Eat a healthy diet, rest enough, and take necessary acclimatization during your trek.
  • Consider trekking to Gokyo Valley and Gokyo Ri during a suitable time when there is less chance of fluctuation in weather, i.e., Spring and Autumn
  • Pack your bags with winter and summer clothes, being mindful of the climatic conditions of the Himalayan region
  • Bring along pairs of adjustable trekking poles, trekking boots, gaiters, and necessary gear for your trekking journey
  • Hire an experienced guide and porters that will ensure safety
  • Purchase your packages through reputed and licensed trekking agents
  • Practice physical exercises like squats, pullups, pushups, chin-ups, and crunches and cardiovascular exercises like running, jogging, trekking, cycling, and others 3-4 weeks before your trekking journey
  • Carry along the first aid box with oral rehydration solution and Diamox
  • Walk in groups and don’t go anywhere alone
  • Avoid smoking and alcohol during your trekking days
  • Check weather forecasts from time to time and stay attentive
  • Bring along nutrient snacks and energy drinks
  • Get insights into the trekking routes and terrain before your trekking journey
  • Follow the given instructions by villagers and guide
  • Carry a map and compass along with you, be attentive, and look after landslide-prone areas
  • Be mindful of the wildlife species and approach alone
  • Ascend steadily through challenging and rocky terrains
