title: Everest Three Passes Trek
summary: Experience the Everest Three Passes Trek, crossing Kongma La pass, Cho La Pass, and Renjo La Pass, with Everest Base Camp and the Gokyo Lakes

seo.title: Everest Three Passes Trek | Itinerary | Cost | Route Map | Reviews
seo.description: Experience the Everest Three Passes Trek, crossing Kongma La pass, Cho La Pass, and Renjo La Pass, with Everest Base Camp and the Gokyo Lakes

gallery.alt: Everest Base Camp Three Passes Trek

overview:
The Everest Three Passes Trek is one of the most challenging and rewarding trekking routes in Nepal's Everest Himalayan region. The trek forms a tough high-altitude loop that connects the Everest region valleys (Imja, Khumbu, Gokyo and Thame).  

They are linked by three challenging high passes: Kongma La (5,535 m), Cho La (5,420 m) and Renjo La (5,360 m). The trek includes rough alpine trails, glacial moraines and remote mountain landscapes making it well-suited for experienced and thrill seeking trekkers.

Along the way, you can explore everything that the world renowned Everest region has to offer. The must see stops include well known Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar to hidden gems like Gokyo Lakes and the remote upper valleys.

The ascent typically begins from Lukla and follows along quaint Sherpa villages like Namche, Tengboche and Dingboche. Cultural weave and warm hospitality add to your trekking experience.

Physically, the path demands strength, endurance and acclimatization as it repeatedly crosses 5,000 m with hard ascent and descent across glaciated ridges. Psychologically, it tests your patience and tolerance, especially in dealing with bad weather or going over passes. 

But the reward is enormous, from sunrise over Everest from Kala Patthar to traversing icy terrain under Himalayan giants. The landscape constantly shifts daily: pine forests, glaciated passes, blue lakes and huge alpine valleys, so it seems to be several treks in one.

The Three Passes Trek offers the most complete and immersive Himalayan journey. It is the ultimate Everest region trekking experience. This expedition through the core of the Himalayas pushes your limits and reveals views few others are ever privileged enough to experience.
highlights: Test your limits by crossing Kongma La (5,535 m), Cho La (5,420 m) and Renjo La (5,360 m), each providing you with stunning Himalayan views and a true wilderness high altitude experience.
Stand at the foot of the world's highest mountain, famous and iconic Everest Base Camp, encircled by majestic peaks and glaciers.
Witness one of the best panoramic sights of Mount Everest, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, Pumori, Thamserku, Lhotse and more at sunrise from Kala Patthar.
Explore the turquoise glacial lakes of Gokyo, framed by high snow peaks and the quiet charm of alpine scenery all around.
Ascend Gokyo Ri for a fantastic 360 degree view of Everest, Cho Oyu, Makalu and the Ngozumpa Glacier.
Stay in traditional teahouses, savor local delicacies and experience genuine Sherpa hospitality.
Visit sacred spiritual site of Tengboche Monastery, the biggest and most significant in the whole Khumbu Valley.
Experience both well frequented Everest Base Camp trekking trails and remote and less trodden routes like Chhukung, Dzongla and Lungden.
Trek through forests, glacial valleys, alpine moorlands and high mountain passes in one journey.
Witness Himalayan Tahr, musk deer, pheasants and bask in the glory of rhododendron forests and snow covered landscapes.

itinerary.title: Arrival at Tribhuwan International Airport, Kathmandu and drive to your hotel.
itinerary.html:
On your arrival at TIA, Kathmandu, you will be received by a representative who will have a name card. On clearing immigration and claiming your bags, you will be escorted to the airport exit where the vibrant environment of Nepal welcomes you right away.   

From the airport, a brief ride will take you along the busy streets of Kathmandu to your hotel. The ride is your first genuine impressions of the capital: whirling markets, temples wedged between modern buildings and a mix of history and daily life on the streets. Depending on when you arrive, you will get some time to relax at your hotel or take a walk around to see the area.

itinerary.title: Early morning flight from Kathmandu to Lukla (2,840 m / 9,318 ft) and trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours..
itinerary.html:
Lukla Elevation: 2,840 m
Phakding Elevation: 2,610 m
Flight Duration: 35-40 minutes 
Treking Distance: 8 km
Trekking Duration: 3-4 hours 

The day begins early with a drive to Tribhuvan Airport to board your flight from Kathmandu to Lukla. This is among the world’s most adrenaline-pumping flights. In the course of the flight, you have the fleeting views of Himalayan snow capped peaks to the horizon.

When the plane lands on the very narrow airstrip of Tenzing Hillary Airport (Lukla Airport), which clings to the side of a hill, you will have the initial thrill of adventure. After meeting your porters and organizing gear, there is time for a light breakfast and final preparations before hitting the trail.

Your hike actually begins as you leave Lukla and follow along the Dudh Koshi River valley. The hike to Phakding is relatively gentle as you pass through charming Sherpa villages, mani stones with Buddhist mantras carved into them, prayer flags flapping in the breeze and suspension bridges hanging high above the river. 

The landscape is green with foliage and the air is fresh and crisp. At Phakding, you will be residing in a teahouse where you can relax, enjoy a hot meal and begin to acclimatize with the mountain atmosphere.

itinerary.title: Trek From Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m
Trekking Distance: 10-11 km.
Trekking Duration: 5-6 hours

Leaving Phakding behind, your route continues along the popular trail of the Dudh Koshi River valley, gradually climbing as you move toward Namche Bazaar. The trail passes through several quaint Sherpa villages, such as Monjo, where permits are checked at the Sagarmatha National Park entrance gate. It then continues to Jorsalle, a small village nestled among pine forests and rhododendron groves. Following the Everest 3 Passes Trek map, we will move forward. 

Along the way, you cross on a series of thrilling suspension bridges spanning the shimmering rivers below. One of them is the fabled Hillary Suspension Bridge with a stunning sight when you gaze down into the enormous river gorge.

As you ascend dense forests gradually give way to expansive views of huge mountains like Thamserku and Kwangde. After some time, you reach Namche Bazaar, the bustling Sherpa town. Colorful bazaars, cafes and lodges create a pulsating contrast with the remote and serene mountain terrain. This bustling town is a relief resting ground before moving further into the Everest region.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day at Namche Bazaar (3,440 m), day hike to Hotel Everest View and Khumjung Village
itinerary.html:
We are on day 5 of the 3 Passes Trek Nepal itinerary. You require a rest day in Namche Bazaar for acclimatizing your body to higher altitudes. Break in the trek will allow you to rest, recharge and prepare for more difficult sections of the trip that lie in front of you.

You can spend the day exploring crowded bazaars, browsing local coffee shops and taking vistas of the Himalayan mountains from various viewing points around the town. Fresh mountain air and lively Sherpa culture make for a nice place in which to rest your body and rejuvenate your mind.

To further aid acclimatization, a popular outing is a brief walk from Namche to the nearby village of Khumjung at roughly 3,780 m. This gentle stroll will take 2–3 hours round trip and passes through terrace fields and woodland cover with even more stunning mountain vistas en route. 

In Khumjung, you will be able to tour the village monastery, which is famous for having a yeti scalp and observe typical Sherpa village life. Returning to Namche by the afternoon, you will be better acclimatized and ready to continue your Everest experience.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche (3860 m / 12664 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Tengboche Elevation: 3,860 m
Trekking Distance: 6-7 km.
Trekking Duration: 5-6 hours

Namche Bazaar to Tengboche trek is the most scenic and spiritually rewarding part of the Everest Base Camp trail. Leaving behind the bustling market town of Namche the trail meanders across the mountainside with captivating views of Ama Dablam, Everest, Lhotse and Thamserku.

Moving forward, you will gradually drop down through pine and rhododendron forests. The route takes you through small Sherpa villages like Sanasa and Phunki Tenga. A short halt by the Dudh Koshi River flowing alongside these charming villages is a welcome break before the trail climbs steeply to Tengboche. Mani stones and prayer flags along the way remind you of the deep spiritual traditions that underlie the Khumbu area.

Eventually, you will arrive at Tengboche which is home to the popular Tengboche Monastery, the biggest and most noteworthy in the Everest region. The monastery, with incredible backdrop of Ama Dablam, is an ideal place to meditate, reflect or observe the daily prayers of local monks.

Tengboche is a viewpoint and a peaceful retreat that nicely balances the day's steep climb. You will overnight in a local teahouse, unwinding and enjoying the tranquil ambiance.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche (4,410 m / 14,469 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Dingboche Elevation: 4,410 m
Trekking Distance: 9-10 km.
Trekking Duration: 5-6 hours

We will depart Tengboche after a hearty morning breakfast. Then, we will follow the trail that passes along woodland paths before climbing gently into the higher zones. Pangboche is a quaint hamlet along the way where you can visit ancient monasteries and observe traditional stone houses nestled among terraced fields. 

As you ascend higher, the scenery of the lofty peaks such as Ama Dablam, Island Peak (Imja Tse) and Lhotse becomes prominent. The Everest Three Passes Trek map​ leads us through the trails. The atmosphere gets thinner and flora diminishes as a marking of your entrance into the rough high altitude environment of the Everest area.

Continuing further, you will arrive at Dingboche, a mountain village renowned for its peaceful valley setting and stunning views of the surrounding peaks. You can unwind and explore the vicinity with walks to viewpoints which treat you to the marvelous views of Ama Dablam and its adjoining mountains. There are several teahouses in the village where you will get warm food and cozy surroundings to refuel and prepare for the journey ahead.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Chhukung (4, 730 m / 15,518 ft), 2-3 hours.
itinerary.html:
Chhukung Elevation: 4,730 m
Trekking Distance: 5-6 kilometers
Trekking Duration: 2-3 hours

The ascent from Dingboche to Chhukung is gradual and moderate through the stark alpine landscape of the high Imja Valley. As you leave Dingboche behind, the valley widens out and sweeping yak grazing fields and rolling hills replace the lower trail's terraces and densely populated villages. 

The air is thinner, the skies clear more regularly and the silence of the high Himalayas is more profound. The route ascends slowly, thereby giving you an ideal place to acclimatize as you climb progressively without steep slope exhaustion. All around, you are presented with breathtaking views of mountains like Ama Dablam, Lhotse and Island Peak.

Finally, you will arrive at the small, windswept settlement of Chhukung beneath the towering faces of Lhotse and the Imja Glacier. This high altitude settlement is quiet and remote with a handful of teahouses offering warm meals and shelter. 

Chhukung is often used as a base for climbers heading to Island Peak or trekkers preparing for the Kongma La Pass. The latter one is what we are doing. Time permitting, you can take a rewarding side excursion to Chhukung Ri, a close by ridge with stunning vistas over the valley.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chhukung to Lobuche (4,910 m / 16,109 ft) crossing Kongma La Pass (5,535 m / 18,159 ft).
itinerary.html:
Lobuche Elevation: 4,910 m
Kongma La Pass Elevation: 5,535 m
Trekking Distance: 11-12 km.
Trekking Duration: 8-9 hours

Chhukung to Lobuche via the Kongma La Pass is one of the toughest and rewarding trail sections of the Everest region. It gives you the sheer sense of remoteness and high altitude exposure. Early morning, you will ascend step by step through glacial moraines and rocky terrain.

Eventually, you will reach the base of Kongma La, the tallest and most challenging of the three major passes in the Khumbu. The climb is steep and demanding, especially in thin air but the brilliant views are worth it. A 360 degree panorama of mountains like Lhotse, Makalu, Ama Dablam and the vast sweep of the Khumbu Glacier thousands of feet below makes you feel like you have entered into a dream world.

As you come down off the pass, you will drop down towards the glacial valley and ultimately rejoin the main Everest Base Camp trail in Lobuche. The ground beneath your feet may be rough, loose boulders and icy patches depending on the season, so tread carefully. The day is long and demanding but highly rewarding with raw Himalayan views, solitude and one of the most iconic high-altitude traverses in the Khumbu.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche (4,940 m / 16,207 ft) to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m / 17,598 ft) via Gorakshep (5,170 m / 16,962 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Gorakshep Elevation: 5,170 m
Everest Base Camp Elevation: 5,364 m
Trekking Distance: 9-10 km.
Trekking Duration: 7-8 hours

The trek to Everest Base Camp is one of the most highly appreciated and memorable days of the whole trek. The walk begins with an easy stroll on a boulder covered trail that meanders between glacial moraines and along the edge of the Khumbu Glacier. The Himalayan giants like Pumori, Lingtren and Nuptse loom overhead on the skyline. 

Within some 2 to 3 hours, you reach Gorakshep. It is the final village before you head toward Base Camp.

From Gorakshep, the route goes up the jagged moraine of the Khumbu Glacier, gradually ascending to Everest Base Camp. Not steep but high altitude and rocky terrain make this section difficult to cover. 

Upon reaching Base Camp, you will stand at the foot of the world’s loftiest mountain, encircled by colorful prayer flags, tents during climbing season and massive walls of ice from the Khumbu Icefall. 

After soaking in the atmosphere and taking a few snaps, you will return to Gorakshep for the night. This untamed area, a former base camp, is now an overnight spot where you drop your packs, enjoy a hot meal and acclimatize for the final push.

itinerary.title: Early morning trek to Kala Patthar (5,545 m / 18,192 ft) to enjoy the sunrise, return to Gorakshep and then a trek to Dzongla (4,830 m / 15,846 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Kala Patthar Elevation: 5,545 m
Dzongla Elevation: 4,830 m
Hike Distance: 13 km.
Hike Duration: 6-7 hours

You will begin the dawn hike from Gorakshep to Kala Patthar. It is one of the most spectacular and renowned vantage points in the Everest region. The ascent is steep and challenging, especially in the thin, cold air and rugged ground. But the sunrise over the Himalayas from the top is something surreal and unforgettable. 

As the sun's first golden rays touch the summits you will have the mesmerizing sight of Everest, Nuptse, Pumori, Lhotse and more glinting in the radiance of daybreak. Kala Patthar offers the best close-up view of Everest's summit that you cannot even achieve from Base Camp itself, so this is a treat of the entire trek.

After having absorbed the views and trekking back down to Gorakshep for breakfast, you will continue with a long but rewarding trek down the valley and west towards Dzongla.

The path diverges from the standard Everest Base Camp trek. The onward path is a more isolated and less-trodden with ethereal views of the Khumbu Glacier, Cholatse and Taboche. The terrain changes from glacial rocks to alpine pastures and the pace slows as you head down. 

At Dzongla, a small, scenic village under huge cliffs, you stay overnight prior to the challenging Cho La Pass the following day.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dzongla to the Gokyo Lakes (4,790 m / 15,715 ft) via Cho La Pass (5,368 m / 17,612 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Cho La Pass Elevation: 5,368 m
Gokyo Lake Elevation: 4,790 m
Trek Distance: 10-11 km.
Trek Duration: 7-8 hours

It is an early start with a steep climb from Dzongla over rocky terrain, icy stretches and snowy grounds towards the Cho La Pass. The ascent up to the pass is challenging and requires caution, especially the glacier near the summit. 

But the reward is huge because from the top of Cho La, you can look out in wonder at the extensive panoramas of towering mountain peaks like Cholatse, Ama Dablam and Baruntse and massive glaciers stretching across the upper Himalayas.

Once you come down the pass, the route drifts gently onto a glacier to the base of the valley. Afterward, the path meets up with the Ngozumpa Glacier, the longest in the Himalayas. You will make your way through this rugged area before you come to the serene beauty of the Gokyo Valley where a chain of greenish-blue lakes sparkle at high altitude.

Gokyo village, which is situated along the third and largest lake, is a peaceful and lovely place to relax. With its clear glacial water, reflecting images of Cho Oyu and fewer trekkers than the Everest Base Camp trail, Gokyo offers an otherworldly high-altitude haven well worth the effort of the pass.

itinerary.title: Morning hike to Gokyo Ri (5,357 m / 17,575 ft) and back to Gokyo.
itinerary.html:
Gokyo Ri Elevation: 5,357 m
Trekking Distance: 6 km.
Trekking Duration: 4-5 hours

After several days of trekking at high altitudes, Gokyo is the ideal place to relax and restore. Lying next to the turquoise waters of the third Gokyo Lake, this peaceful village is surrounded by giant mountains and glacier-fed water bodies. 

You can spend the day lazing in a teahouse, strolling along the shores of the lake, or simply soaking up the peace of this wilderness area. It's an important acclimatization day before ascending towards higher terrain, i.e., the Renjo La Pass.

If the skies are clear and your energy is high, an early morning hike to Gokyo Ri is a rewarding optional adventure. The ascent is well worth the effort, as the top provides one of the most striking panoramas in the entire Khumbu region. The four of the world's highest peaks: Everest, Lhotse, Makalu and Cho Oyu majestically stand before your eyes. 

You will also see the enormous Ngozumpa Glacier and the wide spanning hidden Gokyo Valley. On your way down, you can relax or go to the nearby lakes for the rest of the day before preparing for the next leg of your trek.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gokyo to Lungden (4,380 m / 14,370 ft) crossing Renjo La Pass (5,360 m / 17,585 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Lungden Elevation: 4,380 m
Renjo La Pass Elevation: 5,360 m
Trekking Distance: 13 km.
Trekking Duration: 7-8 hours

Today's part of the hike is challenging as well as incredibly rewarding along the scenic and off-the-beaten sections of the Everest region. In the early morning, the trek ascends steadily towards the Renjo La Pass, the final one of the three high passes of the Khumbu. 

According to the Three Passes Trek map, the climb is steep and potentially snow-covered but the dramatic alpine views and sense of isolation make it unforgettable. From the top of the pass, you are treated to an eye-popping vista of Mount Everest, Lhotse, Makalu and Cho Oyu, set against shimmering turquoise lakes of Gokyo below.

From Renjo La, the route goes downhill through outcrops of boulders and grassy slopes to peaceful Bhote Koshi Valley. You ultimately reach Lungden after a long hour of downhill walk, which is a peaceful village surrounded by snow-capped ridges. It is a peaceful overnight stay with basic teahouses where you can relax and look back on the trek till now.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lungden to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m
Trekking Distance: 18-19 km.
Trekking Duration: 6-7 hours

After a quiet overnight halt at Lungden, the trail resumes its gentle downward journey once again to the vibrant heart of the Khumbu, the beautiful village of Namche Bazaar. 

On the way, it passes through picturesque Sherpa settlements such as Marlung and Thame. Thame is a historic village with a monastery and also the home of some famous mountaineers such as Tenzing Norgay. 

The downhill is scenic and a gentle one with hillside terraced landscape, wind-blown prayer flags and distant snow-covered summits. It is a chance to observe the day-to-day life of the villagers on a track less traveled by tourists. 

As you descend, the trail merges into the Everest main trail and takes you back to the bustle of life in Namche Bazaar. After days of high-altitude solitude and traversing jagged high passes, back to Namche is like a warm hug full of hot meals, comfortable lodges and even bakeries or cyber cafes. 

It is the perfect place to rest, recover and reflect on the incredible high altitude adventures you have had before the final descent to Lukla.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2,840 m / 9,318 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Lukla Elevation: 2,840 m
Trekking Distance: 18-19 km.
Trekking Duration: 7-8 hours

The final trekking day begins as you leave Namche Bazaar on the same long, winding trail down through pine groves, suspension bridges and familiar villages. While much of the trip is downhill, the path can be tough on the knees and requires sure-footedness, especially on the stone steps down to the Dudh Koshi River.

You will pass through Jorsalle, Monjo and Phakding where the air is denser and the forests greener. As you make your way back to Lukla, where your Himalayan trek began, most often there is a sense of accomplishment mingled with reminiscence. Your final night is a time to celebrate the victory with fellow travelers and guides, enjoy a hot meal and bask in one final view of the surrounding peaks.

You will be flown tomorrow by scenic flight back to Kathmandu but tonight you rest in the place where you began your adventure towards Everest, now successfully achieved.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu, 35-40 minutes.
itinerary.html:
After your morning breakfast, you will be flying from Lukla to Kathmandu. The short but picturesque flight is your last chance to see the majestic Himalaya peaks up close before landing in the Kathmandu Valley.

About 45 minutes of flying returns you to the sounds of the capital city. It is a stark contrast after the days spent in the midst of the quiet, unblemished beauty of nature.

Once you return to Kathmandu, you will be driven to your hotel and have time to shower and rest. You can spend the remainder of the day exploring around the city's temples and bazaars or you would rather rest. It is a time to unwind and absorb the vibrant culture of Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu to oward destination.
itinerary.html: Today, you will make your way to Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu to take the flight to your destination. Depending on your schedule, you may get a chance for one final stroll around the city, picking up last minute souvenirs or just basking in the chaos of activity at the capital. Airport transfer will be arranged so that you make a smooth and timely departure.

sections.title: Useful Info
sections.html:
Tips for Easy, Smooth and Successful Everest Three High Pass Trek​

Training 

Train intensively at least 2 to 3 months before your trek focusing on cardiovascular (heart and lung) endurance and strength (leg and core) training.

Itinerary Selection 

Choose an itinerary that incorporates a number of rest days. Use these days to make short treks to higher altitudes and drop down to sleep lower.

Likewise, choose your direction wisely. It is best to go counter-clockwise (Kongma La, Cho La and Renjo La). This itinerary supports gradual acclimatization, placing Everest Base Camp and Gokyo Ri midway through the trek.

Starting Early 

Start trekking early, especially when crossing the three high passes since the morning has more predictable weather and the snow conditions are less risky prior to the sun melting the ice.

Snacks and Hydration  

Always carry plenty of snacks and drink at least 3-4 liters of water daily. Bring water purification solutions since clean drinking water is not guaranteed along all sections of the trail.

Footwear 

Invest in high quality, broken in trekking boots with good ankle support and grippy soles, because you will be walking across varied terrain including rocky paths, glacial ice, scree slopes and occasionally deep snow.

Clothes 

Have a complete clothing system, which is layered and designed for cold, wind and wetness. 

Walking Poles

Use trekking poles to reduce knee stress and balance on steep inclines or icy trails, especially useful on high pass navigation days and long descents.

Sleeping Bags 

Nights are cold and teahouses may be unheated and not insulated. So, bring a four-season sleeping bag rated to at least -10 to -15 degrees Celsius and a silk liner for warmth and hygiene.

Flexibility 

Have extra time in your itinerary for weather delays, acclimatization issues or illness.

Route Finding 

Trail markings around the passes can be vague or invisible in snow or fog. Download offline GPS apps before the trek and always keep a physical map with you.

Pace

Walk at your own pace and don't attempt to keep up with faster walkers, especially at higher altitudes. Slow walking allows you to absorb oxygen more effectively, become less fatigued and take in more scenery.

Guide and Porter

You can also consider the services of an experienced guide and a local porter. Guides help with directions, offer cultural knowledge and are also responsible for your safety in challenging trail segments. Similarly, porters can greatly reduce your physical load by carrying your heavy backpacks.

sections.title: Packing Checklist
sections.html:
Necessary Preparation

The Everest Base Camp Three Passes Trek is a challenging journey and embarking on this journey requires necessary preparations to deal with all the forthcoming challenges. The journey will take you through challenging terrain and rugged trails and it is crucial to engage in weightlifting exercises before embarking on the exciting voyage, which calls for strong physical strength, mental resilience, and unwavering dedication. To deal with the physical difficulties necessary exercises are required. Weightlifting exercises like squats, deadlifts, pushups, pullups, crunches, planks, and others will train your muscles and increase the strength of your body.

Similarly, cardiovascular exercises like running, walking, jogging, swimming, cycling, and others are necessary to boost the stamina of the body. This will help build your endurance which will play a crucial role while trekking through the challenging trails of mountains. Along with that, it is necessary to practice stretching exercises to reduce strain in joints and muscles. Performing stretching exercises will enhance your performance by boosting the flexibility or mobility of the body. These necessary preparations are essential to perform 3-4 weeks prior to the trekking journey and practicing these exercises will train you and your body to deal with the challenging aspects of the trek which will alleviate most of the injuries or sickness along the way. It doing this, you’ll ensure yourself a safe, secure, and amusing experience.

Essential Packing

The essential packing for the Everest Three Passes Trek includes:

Upper wear

  • Tshirts
  • Full sleeve t-shirts
  • Fleece jackets
  • Longsleeve thermal tops
  • Waterproof jackets
  • Windsweater
  • Neck gaiter

Lower wear

  • Comfortable pants
  • Trekking pants

  • Trekking trousers
  • Thermal trousers

Headwear

  • Hat
  • Cap
  • Sunglasses
  • Headband

Footwear

  • Trekking boots
  • Sports shoes
  • Gaiters
  • Sandals

Innerwear

  • Vests
  • Underwear

Travel documents

  • Valid visa
  • Travel Insurance
  • Passport
  • 2-4 passport-sized photos

Personal hygiene and toiletries

  • Toothbrush
  • Toothpaste
  • Shaving cream
  • Razor
  • Deodorant
  • Nail clippers
  • Sanitizer
  • Lip balm
  • Face wash

First aid items

  • Antihistamines
  • Ibuprofen
  • Safety pins
  • Medical glove
  • Insect repellant cream

Other essential items

  • Phone
  • Charger
  • Extra batteries
  • Powerbank

  • Snacks

faqs.q: What is the Everest 3 Pass Trek?
faqs.a:
Everest Three Pass Trekking is a challenging and awe-inspiring high-altitude trek in Nepal's Everest region. It crosses the Khumbu's principal valleys via three high mountain passes, Kongma La, Cho La and Renjo La. 

The trek also features the best of the region, such as Everest Base Camp, Kala Patthar and Gokyo Lakes. It is the ultimate Everest trek for anyone seeking both physical and mental challenge and breathtaking Himalayan views.

faqs.q: How Long is the Three Passes Hike?
faqs.a: The whole Everest Three Passes trek takes about 17 to 21 days, depending on your itinerary, walking pace, rest days and side trips. Schedules have space for acclimatization, Kathmandu sightseeing and the Everest Base Camp section.

faqs.q: How Hard is the 3 Passes Trek?
faqs.a: This is a tough, high-altitude hike with long trekking days, steep climbs, rough terrain and high passes above 5,000 m  A solid physical fitness and strong mental resilience are required to conquer this mountain journey. Hence, it is recommended only for seasoned trekkers or people with prior knowledge of high-altitude trekking.

faqs.q: When is the Best Time to do the Trek?
faqs.a:
The best times to go for the Everest Three High Passes Trek are:

  • Spring (March to May): Blue skies, stable weather, rhododendron flowers in bloom and mild temperatures.
  • Autumn (late September to November): Clear and predictable weather, good visibility and comfortable cool conditions.

Avoid:

  • Monsoon (June–August): Too much rain, landslides, leeches and flight delays.
  • Winter (December–February): Very cold; high passes are likely to be closed due to snow.

faqs.q: Do I Need a Guide and Porter for Everest 3 Pass Trek?
faqs.a:
It is strongly recommended that you hire a licensed guide. Starting 2023, Nepal encourages guided trekking for safety and support, especially in remote areas like the Three Passes route. Guides are helpful to get across the three passes, which are technical, confusing and potentially hazardous in bad weather. 

Likewise, you can have your heavy backpack carried by a porter so that you can walk with more comfort.

faqs.q: What Permits Do I Need for This Trek?
faqs.a:
You will require the following permits:

  • Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit
  • Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Entrance Permit

Permits are usually arranged by your trekking agency (us) or can be acquired in Kathmandu or Lukla.

faqs.q: What is the Highest Point of the Everest 3 Pass Trek?
faqs.a: The highest trekking point is often Kala Patthar (5,545 m), which offers the best view of Mount Everest and other surrounding Khumbu Himalayas. Among the passes, the highest and most demanding one is Kongma La (5,535 m).

faqs.q: What is the Terrain Like During the Journey?
faqs.a:
You will encounter mixed landscapes:

  • Wooded trails and river crossings in lower valleys
  • Rocky steep ascents and glacier crossing higher up
  • Windswept alpine scenes, glacial lakes and windy mountain passes

faqs.q: How Do I Prepare for the Trek?
faqs.a:
Train with focus on:

  • Cardiovascular fitness (hiking, running, swimming, dancing, cycling)
  • Strength training for legs and core (planks, lunges, squats, push ups)
  • Hiking uphill with a loaded pack
  • Altitude acclimatization walks (if possible)

Start training at least 2–3 months in advance.

faqs.q: Is Altitude Sickness a Risk?
faqs.a:
Yes. The trek goes to very high altitudes and acute mountain sickness (AMS) is a real risk.

Recognize AMS symptoms early (headache, dizziness, nausea) and never ascend if they worsen.

Preventative tips:

  • Ascend gradually
  • Take acclimatization days seriously
  • Hydrate well
  • Avoid alcohol
  • Sleep properly
  • Eat nutritious meals
  • Take Diamox (consult with a doctor before use)

faqs.q: How is the Accommodation On the Everest Three Pass Trekking​ Trail?
faqs.a: Accommodation is in village teahouses or lodges along the way, which are basic but tidy. Rooms will normally be twin-share with a warm blanket, mattress and pillows. Bathrooms and dining spaces are normally shared. Some teahouses offer hot showers, WiFi and charging of electronic devices, usually at an added cost.

faqs.q: What Food is Served on the Everest Three Pass Trekking​?
faqs.a:
You will find Dal Bhat (lentils, rice, vegetables) wherever you make a stop. Other common dishes are:

  • Noodles and pasta
  • Momo (dumplings)
  • Fried rice
  • Pancakes and eggs
  • Flat breads 
  • Sherpa stew 
  • Potatoes 
  • Sandwishes
  • Thukpa (Tibetan noodle)

Both vegetarian and non vegetarian food is abundant. You can also place an order for a meal as per your specific dietary plan. The cuisine becomes plain and expensive at higher altitudes.

faqs.q: Is There Wi-Fi and Electricity on the Everest Three High Pass Trail?
faqs.a:
Electricity is available in most teahouses to charge your equipment, usually for a modest charge.

Wi-Fi connection prevails in the majority of villages but can be slow, unreliable or weather-dependent. Mobile signal exists in some areas (Ncell/Nepal Telecom), but not on the high passes and other elevated zones.

faqs.q: Are There ATMs or Money Exchange Locations Along the Trails?
faqs.a: Namche Bazaar is the last reliable ATM and money changing point. Carry enough cash (Nepalese rupees) for the whole trek. It is best to withdraw the required amount from abundant ATMs in Kathmandu.

faqs.q: Is Travel Insurance Required for the Everest Three High Pass Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes absolutely. Your travel insurance must:

  • Provide high-altitude trekking coverage (to 6,000 m)
  • Have emergency helicopter evacuation coverage
  • Cover delays and cancellations of the trip
  • Provide for medical treatment and lost, delayed or stolen baggage

Keep a printed and digital copy of your insurance while trekking.

faqs.q: How Much is the Everest Three High Passes Trek Cost​?
faqs.a: The Everest Three Passes Trek cost​ depends on itinerary, group size, logistics involved and level of services. On average, Three Passes Trek cost is USD 1,500 – USD 2,500 per person for a guided package (permits, flights, meals, accommodation, guide/porter included). Our all inclusive  Everest Three High Passes Trek Cost is just USD 1,560.

overview:
Everest View Trek is a mini trek that provides an opportunity to hike in Everest region of Nepal. It is one of the popular treks in Everest, for those not willing to walk all the way to Everest base camp yet who dreams to have closer view of Mt. Everest and other Khumbu mountains as well as explore the cultural insights on the lives of the legendary Sherpa people. This exceptional 9 days trek features a wide range of remarkable scenery combined with unique cultural encounters with the local inhabitants of high altitude region.

After a short yet adventurous flight from Kathmandu to the beautiful village of Lukla (2,800 m), the journey heads directly towards Sagarmatha National Park, which is the second most popular trekking area in Nepal. The trek endures through the lush vegetation of Sagarmatha National Park with, rhododendron forests, pine forests and plenty of wildlife, to Namche Bazaar, a lively market that is a junction for trekkers and the biggest Sherpa residence in Everest region where a day rest is essential in order to get acclimatized to higher altitudes.

Following the trek trails leads you to several Sherpa Villages like, Khunde village, Phortse village, Khumjung village and many other small villages which rewards you with spectacular views of snow-capped mountains that rise above the clouds. From each village you can not only see these incredible mountains but also get an opportunity to experience Sherpa culture, visit monasteries and learn the way of living style of the Himalayan people. Ultimately, the trek trail leads you to famous Tengboche Monastery.

Tengboche Monastery, situated at the altitude of 3,867 m is one of the biggest monasteries in Khumbu area. Surrounded by rhododendron forest all around, the monastery is located on a ridge top with impressive views of Everest Landscape. The view from this stop is absolutely delightful view of different mountains like the mighty Everest, Lhotse, Amadablam, Nuptse, Thamserku, Kangtega, Kusum, Kangaru, Malaphula , Tawoche along with many others. Residence of about 40 Tibetan Buddhist Monks, Tengboche Monastery is also the spiritual center for Sherpas. Moreover, this monastery is also reputed by photographers as one of the best places to capture the remarkable beauty of Mt Everest and its neighboring peaks. So, be prepared to have your camera permanently in hand to record this astonishing experience.

The closing days of this experience will be spent in the delightful and lovely villages of Khunde (3,500 m) and Khumjung, where you will have the chance to further interact with the legendary Sherpa people and take part in their astounding conventional way of life. After that, you will return back to Lukla and ultimately to Kathmandu, appreciating the last views of the spectacular mountains and the people.

All in all, Everest view trek is not only for its nearness to the world’s highest mountain but also for its friendly Sherpa people, great variety of cultures and tradition, charming villages, colorful festivals and monasteries. This trek will definitely provide you a good insight into Sherpa culture without much struggle of high altitude trekking.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA), Kathmandu and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: Namaste and welcome to Nepal. Our representatives will be waiting for you at the arrival section at Tribhuvan International Airport. You will be greeted and be transferred to the hotel. Overnight at a 3-star hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft) and then trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: Early morning, we drive to the domestic airport to board on a scenic mountain flight to Lukla (40 minutes). The flight takes us over the splendid lush hills and snow-capped peaks. We arrive at the most dangerous airport in the world, Tenzing-Hillary Airport in Lukla.  In Lukla, we will meet the rest of our staffs and start the incredible trek to Phakding. Just to acclimatize and adjust to the environment, we do a short walk today. Overnight in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: After having our breakfast in Phakding, the track leads to reach the famous mountain town of Namche Bazaar. Encounter numerous smaller villages like Jorsalle and Monjo. Monjo lies north of Phakding and is the entrance point of the Sagarmatha National Park. The trail goes through the national park following Dudh Koshi River to finally arrive in Namche. Namche Bazaar, because of its amazing location, is the marketable center of the Khumbu region. The peaks of Everest (8,848 m), Thamserku (6,608 m), Taboche (6,367 m), and the sacred Khumbila (5,761 m) can be seen from Namche Bazaar. Overnight in Namche.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day at Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft).
itinerary.html: Today we ascend to Everest View Hotel for an amazing 360-degree view of the snowy peaks. It takes about 2 hours to reach the hotel and enjoy the view of the surroundings. Then we descend to Khumjung (3,780 m) village to encounter the imposing monastery and Khumjung Hillary School. We can observe the Skull of Yeti displayed inside Khumjung Monastery. This is one of the larger Sherpa villages in this region. We reach our lodge in Namche via Syangboche village. Overnight in Namche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazar to Tengboche (3,860 m / 12,664 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: An easy trail leads to us to the Dudh Koshi Valley towards the settlement of Phunke Tenga. From the settlement, following the trail upward leads to the village of Tengboche. Experience astonishing natural scenery composed of rivers, hills, and Himalayan peaks along the way. The village of Tengboche is famous for Tengboche Monastery, one of the largest and the most sacred monasteries in Khumbu region. The monastery also hosts stunning views of Ama Dablam (6,856 m), Mount Everest (8,848 m), Taboche (6,367 m), Thamserku (6,608 m), and other snowy peaks. Overnight in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Monjo (2,835 m / 9,301 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: From Tengboche, we go downhill through rhododendron bushes and fir trees towards the Dudh Koshi River. We cross Tashinga and Sanasa villages before reaching Kyangjuma. We first reach Namche Bazaar and then continue descending to Monjo. The trail goes through the lush forest, winding via several ups and downs. A sharp incline downhill leads us to a bridge over Dudh Koshi River, crossing which we exit Sagarmatha National Park. Then we walk on an even trail to reach Monjo. Overnight in Monjo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Monjo to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail from Monjo to Lukla is adorned with many small monasteries and painted Mani walls. Passing through several small Sherpa settlements, we descend to Chauri Kharka via Phakding. The steep ascends from Chauri Kharka to Lukla is the last ascend of the trek. Upon reaching Lukla, we can rest for a while and later stroll around the village, listening to the stories of the locals. Overnight in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html: We take a flight back from Lukla to Kathmandu early in the morning. The 40 minutes flight serves us the aerial views of the high mountains and lush hills one more time before we land in Kathmandu. On arrival, we transfer you to the hotel. Refresh and relax. Later, stroll in the streets of Thamel. Overnight in hotel.

itinerary.title: Transfer to international Airport for your next destination.
itinerary.html: Depending on your flight schedule, you will be transferred to the airport three hours before your scheduled departure time.

sections.title: More information
sections.html: We are advised to consider the following equipment as these are essentials while packing for the Everest Base Camp Trek. Adjustments to the list can be managed according to the requirements, interests, duration of trip, and season of trip.  We can find variety of these gears to rent or buy in Kathmandu. Majority of the gears which are in sale in Kathmandu are locally manufactured and some are imported from china and they are much cheaper. And there are some famous branded gear shops in Kathmandu, Thamel. Equipment List: – Lightweight and comfortable hiking boots: fit them with hiking socks and wear them wherever possible before you go to trekking. – Sleeping bag and liner – Sandals/ Flip flop – Hiking socks – at least 2 pairs of cotton socks and 2 pair of wool socks – Lightweight long sleeve hiking shirts – Windproof/Waterproof pants and jacket – Plastic rain poncho – Light weather protection and warmer weather – Hat for sun and wind – Windproof gloves – Warmer clothes – Long underwear – Thermals (socks, t-shirts, sweater) – Wool hat/beanie (for winter) – Shorts – Hiking trousers – Down jacket Accessories: – Sunglasses with good UV protection – Sunscreen – Lightweight bag to carry your personal needs during the day – Insect repellent – Camera with extra battery – Flashlight – Backpack – Aluminum water bottle – Head lamp – Trekking Poles

faqs.q: I’ve never trekked before. Can I do this trek?
faqs.a: Of course if you are reasonably fit, mentally prepared and can walk for 6-7-hours a day then no matter who you are and what your background is, a bit of training may be necessary, but even that is not 100% essential for most.

faqs.q: How many miles do you walk each day?
faqs.a: It is about 20 miles from Lukla to Tengboche and it should take a minimum of 3 days excluding 1 acclimatizing day on Namche Bazar. In average you walk around 4-7 miles per day while going up and 8-12 miles while coming down.

faqs.q: Is there battery charging facility?
faqs.a: The tea houses have charging ability via their solar panels but if it has been cloudy for several days, there may not be enough reserves to charge barberries for your camera, and thus it is better to have an extra battery. Teahouses usually charge for it – maybe a 300-500 rupees per hour. Many people want to charge their batteries so try to plug your stuff in as soon as you arrive.

faqs.q: Can I do laundry on the trek?
faqs.a: Yes, you can. You can take this service with guest house. This will not be by machine, it will be by hand. Or, you can do your own laundry in a bucket.

faqs.q: Is there bottled water on this trek?
faqs.a: Yes, there’s bottled water from Lukla all the way up to Tengboche. But, the price goes up the higher you go. One liter bottle of water cost start around 70 rupees and at Tengboche cost well over 200 (around $2). A budget solution to this is to use water treatment solution or use water purifier tablets. Some purification tabs and drops make the water taste weird. Please be aware of that too. Buying boiled water can be a solution to save money from expensive bottled water but make sure if water was fully boiled or not before you buy.

faqs.q: Is there age limit for Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: There isn’t any official age limit saying you can and cannot trek to this route.

faqs.q: How difficult is this Everest View Trek?
faqs.a: In terms of terrain there are no ropes needed and no ice picks needed. There is no vertical climbing involved. The ground is not paved. It is rough, rocky and gravel strewn. Most of the trek involves long paths that go up and then down. People with weak ankles should take caution. Depending on the time of year you go there can also be snow and ice in the trails.

faqs.q: Can children do Everest View Trek?
faqs.a: Yes in the general rule. It’s advisable that your child is reasonable and able to understand and follow instructions immediately. Your child should be mature enough to recognize altitude sickness symptoms.

seo.description: Ganesh Himal trekking route lies on the central eastern region of Nepal. This trek has enough combination of all the necessity for adventure nature lovers.

overview:
Trekking in Ganesh Himal means you are traveling in a completely different part of the world. Ganesh Himal Trekking takes you to the foothills of the gorgeous Ganesh Himal Range, situated in the north-central region of Nepal. The trek allows you to connect with the local Tamang people while being close to pristine nature and witnessing surreal snow-capped mountains. Although a neighbor to the famous Langtang valley, Ganesh Himal Trek is still an off-beaten path that waits to be explored diligently.

You will have the first glimpse of Ganesh Himal Range when you cross the hills and leave Kathmandu behind to arrive in Betrawati. Gradually, the trek takes you through several Tamang villages like Kispang, Gongga, Tipling, Jyamrung, and several others, each hosting amazing views of the Ganesh Himal and Langtang Himal ranges. As you stop at some of these villages, you will get plenty of time to learn about the culture, tradition, and lifestyle of the Tamang ethnics. The innocence and warmth of the Tamang people here on the foothills of Ganesh Himal Range is a unique experience altogether.

During this trek, you pass through dense forest and beautiful meadows crossing the passes of Sing La (4,045 m) and Pangsang La (3,850 m) that offer you stunning views of various snow-capped mountain ranges, especially the Ganesh Himal Range. The trek follows a quite trail offering you to immerse in the most pristine form of nature. You are able to witness layers of lush hills that make astonishing views for you to relish. The beautiful rivers, waterfalls, terrace farms, and traditional houses add charm to this already satisfying Ganesh Himal Trek.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Betrawati and start the trek to Kispang (1,600m / 5,249ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Leaving Kathmandu behind, your trip into the Himalayas starts with a picturesque drive to Betrawati, which is a beautiful village on the banks of the Trishuli River. As you descend into Trishuli valley, you will pass through adjoining hillsides to Trishuli Bazaar, where a thin road crosses several edges to reach the small town of Betrawati. After arrival in Betrabati yo start trek to Kispang (1,600 m), the path mounts gradually all the way to Kispang through villages and jungles for four hours. Kispang is a small village, which is inhabited by the Tamang community. You can rest for sometimes and then roam around the village. Overnight in Kispang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kipsang to Thulo Chaur (2,200m / 7,218ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: You will reach Thulo Chour after walking 6 hours approximately, after passing many monasteries, stupas, farms, and waterfalls. You will be able to cross many Tamang villages and observe the Tamang way of life. After ascending on a ridge through the forest, you finally reach a pastureland, from where it is a gradual walk to Thulo Chaur. Overnight in Thulo Chaur.

itinerary.title: Trek from Thulo Chaur to Gongga (2,800m / 9,186ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: You climb slowly through a thick, mixed forest of rhododendron and pine. Several wild lives such as deer, langur, and wild boar are seen as you trek along the trail to Gongga.  On reaching Gongga, one can experience the most stunning views of Ganesh Himal Range. Overnight in Gongga.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gongga to Rupchet (2,850m / 9,350ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will walk through the forest enjoying stunning views of the gigantic Himalayas against the lush forest of Pikhuri Danda. You will be making a lot of uphill and downhill climbs amid the picturesque landscape to reach Rupchet. Overnight in Rupchet.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gongga to Sing La Pass (4045m) to Kharka (2,500m / 8,202ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Today it will be a vertical trek to cross Sing La Pass (4,045 m). After the exhausting hike to the top of the pass, you will be rewarded with astonishing views of the Ganesh Himal Range along with the gorgeous peak of Langtang Lirung (7,227 m). After relishing the alpine atmosphere on the pass, you climb down sharply for 4 hours to reach Kharka. Overnight in Kharka.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kharka to Borang (1,700m / 5,578ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today, you will ascend through the lush forest filled with mixed vegetation. The trail then descends to Borang, where huts laid with black slate stones are seen with a colorful vibrancy. Walk through fields of barley and maize accompanied by the beautiful view of Ganesh Himal I (7,429 m) and II (7,118 m) in Borang. Overnight in Borang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Borang to Jharlang (1,500m / 4,921ft), 6-7 hours
itinerary.html: The early part of your trail goes slightly up until you arrive at a ridge above Netrawati River. From here, you can enjoy remarkable views of Ganesh Himal Range, farming terraces, cascades, and several villages at a distance. Afterward, your trail turns downhill and uphill respectively to reach Jharlang. It can be best labeled as a Tamang village with its rich culture. Overnight in Jharlang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Jharlang to Kintang Phedi (1,000m / 3,281ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Beginning the trek from Jharlang, you walk through a narrow path leading out of the village. Descending along lush forests dotted with small hamlets, you make your way to Kintang Phedi. Finally descending along the river basin of Netrawati, you reach Kintang Phedi. You can spend your free time in Kintang Phedi by breathing in the cool breeze on the banks of the confluence of Netrawati River and Kintang River. Overnight in Kintang Phedi.

itinerary.title: Kintang Phedi to Khahare and then drive to Kathmandu. 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: The trails from Kintang Phedi to Khahare Bazar are filled with magical views, which can bring a smile to your face. You proceed through the rice fields while walking on a flat easy trail following River bank. Overnight in Khahare.

title: Ganjala Pass Trek
summary: The Ganja La Pass Trek in the Langtang Helambu region takes you through the stunning Langtang Valley, surrounded by spectacular Himalayan peaks.

seo.title: Ganjala Pass Trek | Langtang | Cost | Itinerary | Guide | Map
seo.description: The Ganja La Pass Trek in the Langtang Helambu region takes you through the stunning Langtang Valley, surrounded by spectacular Himalayan peaks.

overview:
The Ganja la route of Langtang region brings you to the Langtang Valley surrounded by Himalayan Peaks. You follow a rugged trail with dramatic views; to the west- Himal chuli (7,893 m) and Manaslu (8156mm). On a clear day, even the Annapurna range can be seen rising up behind and to the north across the valley is Langtang Lirung 7,240 m and Ganesh Himal is the highest in the region. Trek up to Kyanjin gompa and excursion to Tshergo Ri would acclimatize you well for further trek to Ganja La pass. The trek then turns straight south into the valley of Helambu via the Ganja La pass which is more exciting and challenging as well. To explore Ganjala Pass Trek further isolation, through some of the magnificent villages, least ventured before, pristine Himalaya view etc.

Teahouse facilities are not available in Ganja La region, hence Ganjala Pass Trek should be fully supported and self-sufficient to meet all requirement and contingencies that come up. The highest point of this trek is Ganja La Pass (5,122 m). This region remains one of the alluring trekking corners of Nepal where your effort becomes meaningful.

overview:
Ghalegaun Home Stay Trek offers a close observation of the culture of Gurungs at their home stays and through cultural program. The local people perform traditional Ghatu, Krishna Charitra, Jhankri Lama dances for visitors dressed in traditional attire. There are Gurung pilgrimage sites in and around this region, including the Samba Chhyoling Gompa at Nassar Danda. Devotees throng Ghalegaun during Maghe Sangranti, when a fair is held at Uttar Kanya Temple.

The villages offer spectacular mountain views of Annapurna massif when weather is clear. The peaks such as Annapurna range, Lamjung, Ganesh Himal, Manaslu and several other unnamed can be seen from here.

title: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek
summary: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is ideal for those with limited time who want to experience the natural beauty of the Himalayas and enjoy magnificent mountain views.

seo.title: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek | Cost | Itinerary | reviews
seo.description: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek is ideal for those with limited time who want to experience the natural beauty of the Himalayas and enjoy magnificent mountain views.

overview:
Ghorepani Poonhill Trek is a perfect and suitable trek route for all age bunches. The towering mountains, the high slopes, and the colossal scene it presents drag numerous trekkers to this impeccable region. Other than the wild display of the Himalayan mountain like Mount Dhaulagiri (8,167 m), Annapurna I (8,091 m), Mount Machhepuchhre (6,998 m), Nilgiri (7,041 m), Annapurna South (7,219 m), Annapurna II (7,939 m), Annapurna III (7,555 m) and Tukuche (6,920 m), Poonhill Trek furnishes trekkers with the occasions to mix together with the nearby villagers and understanding their way of living.

The trek commences after a short drive from Pokhara, at Nayapul where you come across a suspension bridge over the Modi Khola (River). A short hike along the bank of Modi Khola leads to a small village called Birethanti and as you climb the winding stone-paved trail through villages and adjoining farmland, you get remarkable glimpses of gigantic Machhapuchree Mountain. This trek then goes to Ghorepani

ni and ultimately to Poon hill, the center attraction of Ghorepani Poon Hill trek.

The major highlight of this trek is to see the sunrise from Poon Hill, 3,210 m, an hour climb from Ghorepani, 2,887 m On this short expedition to Poon Hill, one can observe the entire mountain ranges of Annapurna Region, covered in red, orange, and pink shades of the sun at the sunset and sunrise, making it a truly magnificent view.  The sense of joy that comes to you while you see these beautiful mountains right in front of you is inexpressible; you can just feel and enjoy it.

After the revitalizing and awe-inspiring view of sunset and sunrise from Poon Hill, you descend steeply through forests and then the trail eases as you reach to Ghandruk (one of the favorite destination of internal tourists), a distinct village of Gurung ethnic group known for its traditional houses, great landscape, and rich culture. This village is the popular tourist destination that offers excellent close-up views of Annapurna South, Machhapuchare and Himchuli.

This short yet spectacular trek is sure to make you fall in love with the beautiful Mountains. The memory you carry with you about the amazing diversity of landscape and unique merger of ethnicity will make you want to see more. So, explore the unexplored, live through the magnificence of nature with the best trek experience.

itinerary.html: On arrival to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA), you will met our airport representative who will transfer you to the hotel. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara (820 m / 2,690 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Early morning, we drive to Pokhara enjoying the green landscape and villages along the highway. Driving alongside rivers and streams, we arrive in the City of Lakes, Pokhara.  Enjoy the beauty of Lakeside, Pokhara. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Drive to Nayapul (1,010 m / 3,314 ft) and trek to Ulleri (1,920 m / 6,299 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: After an hour quick drive to Nayapul we start the trek as we cross the suspension bridge over Modi Khola and climb up on steep stone stairs towards Ulleri. In Ulleri, we will get a beautiful view of Annapurna south (7,219 m), Hiunchuli (6,441 m), and other peaks. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ulleri to Ghorepani (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 4-5 hours
itinerary.html: Leaving Ulleri we walk through the rhododendron forest on carefully placed stone steps to reach Ulleri. Later, we pass through the villages of Banthanti and Nangge Thanti situated on the bank of Bhurungdi Khola. Continuing our trek alongside Bhurungdi Khola whilst enjoying the view of the Annapurna massif, we arrive in the Gurung village of Ghorepani. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ghorepani to Poon Hill (3,210 m / 10,531 ft) for sunrise views, then return to Ghorepani and continue trekking to Tadapani (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 6–7 houus.
itinerary.html: Before sunrise we hike up to Poon Hill to experience the majestic sunrise and its enchanting effects on the mountains including Annapurna and Dhaulagiri massifs, Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), and Patal Hiunchuli (6,441 m) among others. Afterward, we hike back to Ghorepani and head on to Tadapani via Deurali Pass (3,090 m). Tadapani also hosts a mind-blowing view of Annapurna South (7,219 m) and Machhapuchhre (6,993 m) and many other mountains and valleys. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tadapani to Kyumi (1,690 m / 5,545 ft), followed by a scenic drive to Pokhara. The trek and drive take approximately 6–7 hours.

We walk through lush rhododendron forest to reach to Ghandruk. After lunch in Ghandruk  we descend on the stone staircases to Kyumi to take bus to Pokhara. 
In the evening, you can hang around the pubs and restaurants of Pokhara. Overnight at guesthouse.

reviews.author: dothy67-Compiegne, France
reviews.body: Namaste everyone! I made 2 treks last june (one in the Langtang, the Gosaikunda trek and the other one in the Annapurna region the Ghorepani- Poon hill trek) and visited the Chitwan national park with Base Camp adventure and I really don't regret it. Shree, the tour operator organized everything as I wished and was full of good advices as I never went on a trek before and made everything very easy for me. And the guide, Raj, was also really nice, patient as I was never on a trek before, and made me feel very comfortable. I had only to enjoy the wonderful sceneries! I can only warmly recommand this agency very serious and professionnal! Dorothée

reviews.author: momosg-asia
reviews.body: Took up city and trekking package with bAse camp. They do take care of their guests well. The city hotel and the lodging during trekking were very good. Our first day city tour guide Ramesh (DK'coussin)was very knowledgeable and was flooding us with information and we really appreciate his offer of information cos the subsequent city guide we got was total opposite ( we had to poke him for information and he wasn't too sure or keen, I am not so sure) Trekking was fun just wished we had trekked longer ( we took up the trek to Poon hill) and spend more time chilling up there instead of trekking such long hours. We enjoying taking tons of photos, stopping for tea breaks and also chatting away. Love the village of our last day up in the mountain but at last too little time. We sweat a lot a lot and we walked more like old folks than the foggies themselves.. Our kneel/ thigh/ ankle/calves were screamin on the 3/4th day. On the whole, we enjoyed this trip a lot and will be back for a longer trek! One of my top 3 trips ! Our crew was fantastic with guide Prakash, porters Rohit and DK. Prakash is very patient and knowledgeable andfun to chat during the Trek. There were superb. Thumbs up. They took really good care of us and we totally enjoyed the fun chat with them. Some side entertainment was also provided as Rohit is an excellent dancer/ photographer as well. DK, our serious looking porter who turned smiley at the end of the trip :) Great and unforgettable experience! Note: our van broke down otw to Pokhara and we were hot and fuming for 2 Hours while waiting for repair. And that's abt the only bad thing :/

reviews.author: Mark X
reviews.body: After looking around Thamel for trekking guides and getting a couple of quotes, Base Camp Adventures was our third quote and best. Shree was able to plan a custom trip within the time frame and budget we wanted. Everything on the trek ran just perfectly. All of the meals and accommodation were sorted and all we had to do was walk and enjoy this amazing part of Nepal. Our trek travelled through Ghandruk, Tadapani, Ghorepani and Poon Hill and finally Tatopani and the hot springs! Prakash, our guide, was awesome, always making sure we were OK, giving us information about everything from the mountains to buffalo and generally making us feel like one big family. I couldn't have asked for a better trek. Thanks for all the wonderful memories!

reviews.author: CHUK2006-Singapore, Singapore
reviews.body: While it took us some time to write this review (we visited Nepal in December 2013), we are still in awe of Shree's genuine friendliness and his impeccable service which is second to none. We stumbled upon Base Camp Adventure after talking to some other providers for a last minute request for organizing a trek to the Gorepani Hills. Shree welcomed us to into his office at 21:00 and it took us less than an hour to discuss and plan the whole thing and seal the deal at an exceptional price. Shree chose a great guide (Prakash) and provided for a perfectly organized yet flexible four day trek in the spectacular Gorepani hills including transport to Pokhara (while we usually enjoy taking public transport, it is simply more comfortable and more flexible to go for private transport if your budget allows it). On the way back to Kathmandu, Shree also arranged for a friend of his to drive us back in his Jeep after our flight got cancelled at the last minute. The epitome of great customer service however was his offer to give us a ride to the airport on the last night because he was going to collect a group of tourists from Canada. I'm sure you will read many company reviews and be torn by which one to take but it really is this simple - if you are looking for an honest, experienced, friendly and value for money company to explore the Himalayas with - choose Base Camp Adventure, you will not be disappointed! We are already planning to contact Shree for our 2014 trip to Tibet.

reviews.author: Emerald C-Ho Chi Ming City,Vietnam
reviews.body: We did the 5 day Poon Hill Trek. This was the first trek I have ever done and everything about it was perfect! Basecamp organise everything from transport, hotels and food which made it super easy. The trek itself was very easy going - quite a few stairs to climb but nothing to crazy. And our wonderful guide Jwala was super supportive and told us to take it as slowly as we liked!! (Vistari, Vistari!!!) I would highly recommend Jwala to anyone! ... He was absolutely fantastic. He was extremely patient, funny, kind and taught us so much about the mountains and Nepali culture. At one point my knee started acting up and he insisted carrying my bag for me untill I was feeling better, he really made the trek wonderful. We stayed up every night playing cards and chatting which was also great. Definitely request him if you go on any of the treks, he is now a life friend of ours. The scenery itself is also the most beautiful thing I've seen! You go past rivers, jungle, forest, terraces, villages, mule (mountain trucks haha) and beautiful Himalayan scenes. Don't pass this trek up! :)

title: Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek And Helicopter Return
summary: Experience the ultimate adventure with our Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return package. Trek through the stunning landscapes of the Everest region, crossing the challenging Cho La Pass and reaching the iconic Everest Base Camp.

seo.title: Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek And Helicopter Return
seo.description: Experience the ultimate adventure with our Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return package. Trek through the stunning landscapes of the Everest region, crossing the challenging Cho La Pass and reaching the iconic Everest Base Camp.

cover.alt: Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek And Helicopter Return

map.alt: Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek And Helicopter Return Map

overview:
Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return offers a lifetime experience of exploring several places of the pristine, remote high-altitude Himalayas in a single trip. It is the combination of two incredible treks in the Everest region, the Gokyo Lake Trek and the Everest Base Camp Trek. The perfect blend of the world-famous Everest Base Camp trek and the less-trodden Gokyo Valley through Cho La Pass is a perfect option to cover the entire wonders of the Khumbu region. During this enriching journey, you can delve deep into the rich culture, resilient people, diverse natural landscapes, and religious landmarks of the alpine mountainous regions. For worldwide thrill seekers, this journey is a fulfilling experience that covers all the breathtaking landscapes and pristine wilderness wonders around the Khumbu region and a thrilling return by helicopter. You will reach the base camp of the world's tallest mountain in just eleven days. Other important highlights of the journey include traversing the largest Himalayan Glacier, Ngozumpa, visiting the turquoise Gokyo Lakes, climbing the Gokyo Ri viewpoint, crossing the high-mountain Pass, Cho La, and hiking to the highest elevation of Kalapathar. Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return journey rewards you with an unparalleled adventure experience through the diverse scenic landscapes and remote settlements of the Himalayas. This trek, which takes you over 5,000 m altitude, is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to experience remarkable adventure in high altitudes and rugged Himalayan terrains. Crossing high-altitude passes and glaciers during the journey tests your physical strength and mental preparedness to the core.

How is this Combined Trek Different from Others?

Although there are several trekking routes to Everest Base Camp, the one through the Gokyo Lakes and Cho La Pass is the most adventurous, exciting, and enriching. During this journey, you will witness and explore all the major attractions of both Everest Base Camp and the Gokyo Lakes region in a single trek, added with the thrill of a helicopter flight. This incredible journey involves an adventurous trek to the Gokyo lakes in the Gokyo Valley, hiking to the top of two amazing viewpoints, Gokyo Ri and Kalapathar, crossing the high pass Cho La, and reaching the classical Everest Base Camp. Finally, this unbeatable journey concludes with a helicopter return to Kathmandu. The scenic helicopter ride back to Kathmandu from Gorakshep is the most exciting part of the Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return journey. You need not trek a long distance down to Gorakshep and finally to Lukla to board a plane to fly back to the capital city. Instead, you can enjoy the Himalayan views from a different angle. You can catch a bird-eye view of the snow-covered mountains, Khumbu glaciers, forests, hills, and valleys during your return journey.

toc.text: How is this Combined Trek Different from Others?

highlights: Starting the journey with a thrilling and scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla
Trekking with experienced and professional guides who are well-known about the highlights, terrain, and culture of the region

Enjoy the wide 360-degree panoramic views of the majestic Himalayas, including Everest, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, Cho Oyu, Lhotse, Makalu, Thamserku, Baruntse and several other peaks in the Everest region
Crossing the challenging high mountain pass, Cho La Pass, at an altitude of 5,420 meters/17,782 feet
