Concluding the trek with an adventurous and exhilarating helicopter flight from Gorakshep to Kathmandu

itinerary.title: Fly to Lukla from Kathmandu and Trek to Phakding
itinerary.html: Lukla Elevation: 2,800 m Phakding Elevation: 2,640 m Flight Duration: 35-40 minutes Trek Duration: 3-4 hours We will start our Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return journey from Kathmandu by taking an early morning flight from Tribhuvan International Airport to Lukla. The exciting scenic flight, which takes around 35-40 minutes, will take us to Lukla Airport (Tenzing Hillary Airport). After landing at the gateway to the Everest region, Lukla, our adventurous trekking journey begins towards the Dudh Koshi River Valley. We will enjoy lunch in the picturesque Lukla village and prepare to trek towards Phakding. We will make our way descending through lush green forests, and enroute, we will traverse several small Sherpa villages (Cheplung, Thado Koshi, Ghat) alongside the Dudh Koshi River. You will be treated to the breathtaking views of the captivating Himalayas on the way. After covering around 9 kilometers distance from Lukla, you will reach the riverside village of Phakding. We will accommodate you at a notable traditional teahouse in Phakding, where you will spend your first night of the trekking days.

itinerary.title: Trek to Namche Bazaar From Phakding
itinerary.html: Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m Trek Duration: 5-6 hours The Phakding to Namche Bazaar trek allows you to immerse yourself in the picturesque Himalayan landscapes. After breakfast, we will leave Phakding and start walking alongside the banks of the Dudh Koshi River. We will ascend gradually at a relaxed pace, taking in the peaceful ambiance and gentle flow of the river. After trekking uphill on the remote trails for about 2-3 hours, we will reach Monjo. At Monjo, we will check in at the entrance gate of the Sagarmatha National Park. On the way, you can witness the diverse plant and animal life of the protected area. The trail leads us through the lush, dense forests of rhododendrons and pines and passes through the quaint Jorsalle and Larja Doban villages. Throughout the trek, you will cross numerous suspension bridges over the Dudh Koshi River, along with the famous Hillary Suspension Bridge. Slowly, the trail ascends to Namche Hill, where you have to make a steep climb. On the way, you can marvel at the stunning vistas of Everest, Ama Dablam, Nuptse, and Lhotse from different parts of the trail. After walking for 8-9 kilometers from Phakding, you will reach Namche Bazaar, the vibrant Sherpa town and bustling hub of the Khumbu region. You can have a cozy retreat at one of our pre-booked teahouse accommodations in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day at Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: Namche Bazaar is the important acclimatization stop before continuing to trek higher into the Himalayas. We will spend this day acclimatizing to the higher altitudes (over 3,000 m) of Namche Bazaar. Initially, we will enjoy the delicious breakfast at our place of stay. Take time to relax and enjoy the delicacy of traditional dishes in the teahouse. After a nice rest and fueling up with nutritious local foods, you can take short acclimatization hikes to the nearby renowned places of Namche Bazaar. Climbing heights and returning to rest/sleep at a relatively lower altitude help you to adjust to the changing altitudes. You can set out to explore and discover the bustling Namche surroundings, which will also help your body adjust to the altitude. You can visit Khunde Hospital, Namche Monastery, and the Sherpa Cultural Museum for a deeper understanding of the history and culture of the place. Along the way, you can have a friendly interaction with the native Sherpa people and learn about their unique costumes, culture, traditions, and resilient lifestyle. You will experience the warm welcome, friendly nature, and genuine hospitality of these mountainous communities. Immerse yourself in the captivating beauty and vibrant atmosphere of Namche Bazaar before returning to the teahouse for a hearty meal and cozy sleep.

itinerary.title: Trek to Dole From Namche Bazaar
itinerary.html: Dole Elevation: 4,000 m Trek Duration: 4-6 hours After waking up in the Namche Bazaar well-rested and acclimatized, we will have breakfast and continue our Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return journey, heading towards Dole. The distance between Namche Bazaar and Dole is approximately 6-7 kilometers. The route from Namche Bazaar gradually ascends towards Syangboche. From there, we will make a slight descent to Khyangjuma, the meeting point of the Gokyo and main EBC trail. While passing through several Buddhist settlements on the way, you can have rich insights into numerous chortens, historical monasteries, Buddhist monks, mani walls, and prayer flags. Trekking further, we will pass the forested trails, a small settlement, Sansa, and ascend to reach the Mong-la Pass. From this pass, you can witness the breathtaking 360-degree views of the surrounding mountains like Everest, Nuptse, Lhotse, Khangtega, Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and more. Descending from the pass, you will reach the Phortse Tenga village beside the Dudh Koshi River. From there, we will follow the trail, passing through yak pastures, pine, and rhododendron forests, which gradually ascends to Dole at 4,000 meters. In the mountainside village of Dole, we will spend an overnight at a teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek to Machhermo From Dole
itinerary.html: Machhermo Elevation: 4,450 m Trek Duration: 3-5 hours Today, we will wake up early at Dole and prepare to embark on a remote trek toward Macchermo. We will follow the off-the-beaten trails from Dole, initially walking beside the Dudh Koshi Riverbed. We head toward the north along the rhododendron and juniper forests and pass through yak pastures, sparse vegetation, and rugged mountainous terrains. On the way, you will traverse several small settlements, such as Luza, Lhabarma, and Kele, where you can catch a glimpse of the day-to-day life of the mountainous people. On the final stretch of the trek, you will ascend to the picturesque Macchermo village, encircled by snow-covered mountains and rocky boulders. Macchermo has several lodges and teahouses offering decent meals and comfortable accommodations. We will unwind and settle in at one of the traditional teahouses in Macchermo.

itinerary.title: Trek to Gokyo from Macchermo and Hike to the Fifth Lake and Back to Gokyo
itinerary.html: Gokyo Lake Elevation: 4,750 m Total Trek Duration: 9-10 hours Today, we will trek towards Gokyo Valley, which has six Gokyo Lakes: Gokyo Cho (Dudh Pokhari), Thonak Cho (largest), Gyazumpa Cho, Taujung Cho, Ngozumpa Cho (smallest), and Longpongo Cho, at an altitude of around 4,700-5,000 m These glittering lakes offer a dramatic reflection of the surrounding Himalayas on their surfaces. We will leave Machhermo and pass through the traditional settlement of Buddhist people, Phangka. Continuing further on the trek, you will descend by the river and ascend slightly uphill to the moraine, where you can see the Ngozumpa Glacier closing up. Climbing steeply over rocky and rugged terrains, you will encounter a glacial river. After crossing the river, you will see the symphony of sparkling Gokyo Lakes. After traversing the first and second Gokyo Lakes, we will reach the Gokyo village beside the third Gokyo Lake. You can see the Cho Oyu mountains standing majestically at the backdrop of this turquoise lake. We will have our lunch in this scenic village and set out to hike up to the fifth Gokyo Lake. We will follow the trails which ascend gradually toward the upper Gokyo Valley. On the way, we will pass the third and fourth Gokyo lakes, with magnificent views of snowy mounatins, glacial lakes, and rocky cliffs. After around 3-4 hours of uphill trek, you will reach the fifth Gokyo Lake amidst the Himalayas. Explore the mesmerizing scenery of the fifth Goykyo Lake in its tranquil ambiance, and after enjoying some worthwhile time, retrace your footsteps back to the Gokyo village. Upon returning to the Gokyo village, you can spend a glorious night marveling at the magnificence of the mountains and pristine Gokyo Lake. Note: The sixth Gokyo Lake is less visited due to its remoteness and no well-marked trails leading directly to the lake.

itinerary.title: Hike up to Gokyo Ri and Trek to Dragnag(4600m)
itinerary.html: Gokyo Ri Elevation: 5,340 m Dragnag Elevation: 4,650 m Trek Duration: 5-7 hours Today, we will embark on an exhilarating hike to the Gokyo Ri at 5,340 m. We will wake up before the break of the day to scale up this high-altitude vantage point. We will catch the mesmerizing first ray of the sun from this amazing viewpoint. The sun casting its golden hues rays and illuminating the Himalayas is a grand view to behold. Moreover, from the top of Gokyo Ri, you can marvel at the stunning panorama of the lofty Khumbu Himalayan, such as Everest, Lhotse, Cho Oyu, Makalu, Taboche, Cholatse, and several other adjacent mountains. Enjoy some time gazing upon the marvelous vistas as seen from the Gokyo Ri and start descending towards Dragnag. On the way, you will navigate the Ngozumpa Glacier one more time to reach the small mountainous settlement of Dragnag. You can experience warm hospitality in this culturally rich village of Sherpa. At night, enjoy a comfortable teahouse accommodation and a delicious dinner. Rest well for the challenging crossing of Cho La Pass the next day.

itinerary.title: Cross the Cho La Pass and Trek to Dzonghla
itinerary.html: Cho La Pass Elevation: 5,420 m Dzonghla Elevation: 4,830 m Total Duration: 6-8 hours This day of the trek begins early in the morning after having breakfast at Dragnag. The early start is important to avoid the possible high winds and fogs after midday during the pass crossing. Initially, the trail from Dragnag heads toward Cho La Phedi. From there, we will make a steep climb to the Cho La Pass, which can be quite challenging at times with some sections of ice and snow. Following the rugged Himalayan terrains, you will reach the top of this high mountain pass, from where you can witness the amazing views of hills, valleys, and mountains as far as your eyes can see. Next, make a cautious descent through the steep and rocky terrains of the Pass towards the Dzonghla village. After an adventurous journey of reaching Dzonghla through Cho La Pass, we will reside in a cozy teahouse accommodation to spend the overnight.

itinerary.title: Trek to Lobuche from Dzonghla
itinerary.html: Lobuche Elevation: 4,980 m Trek Duration: 3-5 hours Today, we will embark on a scenic trekking journey from Dzonghla to Lobuche. The trek from Dzongla follows a descending trail to a river and ascends to an open landscape of grassy patches and rocky terrains. From there, the trail leads towards the moraines with the majestic presence of the Himalayas on all sides. You will ascend the small pass, often known as the Lobuche Pass. The steady uphill walking through this pass lets you enjoy the majestic views of the snow-clad mountains and verdant hills at farsight. You can catch the magnificent sight of Khumbu Glacier from the trail, manifesting its pristine beauty. On the way, you can also see the memorials dedicated to the climbers who lost their lives on the way to Everest. You will pass through several Buddhist settlements with chortens, mani walls, and Tibetan monasteries while heading towards Lobuche. After covering approximately 6-7 kilometers distance from Dzonghla, we will finally arrive at Lobuche. Upon reaching this beautiful mountainside village, we will accommodate a local teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche to Gorekshep to Everest Base Camp, Then Back to Gorakshep
itinerary.html: Gorakshep Elevation: 5,164 m Everest Base Camp Elevation: 5,360 m Trek Duration: 6-8 hours On the 10th day of our incredible Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return journey, we will finally reach the base camp of Mount Everest. We will wake up early in the morning and embark on the adventurous and enticing trek to the lap of the world's highest mountain. After leaving Lobuche, we will start to make an ascent towards higher elevations, taking in the grand closing-up views of the towering Himalayas. You will have to traverse the rugged high-altitude terrains with loose rocks and moraines to reach Gorakshep. Gorakshep is the last settlement in the Everest region along the trek to EBC, with few stone houses. We will have lunch at one of the teahouses in Gorakshep and proceed on a trek toward the Everest Base Camp, which takes several hours to reach. It is a tough journey to make it to the Everest Base Camp. As you gain elevation, the air becomes more thinner, and the oxygen level in the atmosphere decreases. You might get caught by altitude sickness, so take a slow pace and regular hydration breaks. While tackling and overcoming the challenges on the way to EBC, you will also experience every moment filled with excitement and astonishment. As the base camp approaches nearer, you can feel the majestic presence of Everest before you. From the base camp, the gratifying vistas of the sky-craping mountain ranges, Khumbu Icefall, and Khumbu Glacier take your breath away. Enjoy the rewarding moments at this iconic base camp and retrace your footsteps back to the Goerakshep. On this day, we have walked a total distance of around 9-10 kilometers. So, give your legs a nice break, spending a restful time at the teahouse.

itinerary.title: Climb up to Kalapatthar, Descend Down to Gorakshep, and Fly to Kathmandu by Helicopter
itinerary.html: Kala Patthar Elevation: 5,643 m Kathmandu Elevation: 1,400 m Trek Duration: 4-5 hours Flight Duration: 1 to 1.5 hours Gorakshep is the common point for both Everest Base Camp and the Kalapatthar viewpoint hike. Today, we will start our trek from Goarkshep at dawn to reach the Kalapatthar before sunrise. The steep, narrow trails on the rough, rocky Himalayan terrains take you to the popular viewpoint of the Everest region, Kalapatthar. This high-altitude vantage point is surrounded by the gigantic Himalayas. You can enjoy the dramatic scenery and captivating sunrise view rising over the pristine white mountains from Kalapatthar. Moreover, you will be treated to the breathtaking 360-degree panorama of the Everest region Himalayas, such as Everest, Ama Dablam, Cho Oyu, Pumori, Changtse, Nuptse, Lhotse, Khumbutse, Island Peak and more. After enjoying the views from Kalapatthar, you will board a helicopter to return to Kathmandu. Helicopter return from Kalapatthar is a unique experience and a convenient alternative to the standard return journey. The direct helicopter flight from Gorakshep is the fastest and easiest way to return to the capital city after a long trek in the challenging high-altitude mountainous terrains of the Everest region. The helicopter service is the best option for trekkers who want to save time or need a quick descent due to health issues. The adventurous helicopter flight allows you to enjoy the magnificent bird’s eye aerial views of the high-Himalayan landscapes. You can get unique insights and perspectives on the spectacular mountains, Sherpa settlements, historical monasteries, terraced fields, vibrant hills, rushing rivers, shimmering lakes, and lush valleys you have been exploring through your feet. After around 1 hour of scenic helicopter flight, we will reach the Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. Once we arrive at Kathmandu, our unforgettable Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return journey comes to an end.

sections.title: Useful Info:
sections.html:
Difficulties and Counter Measures for Gokyo Cho La EBC Trek with Helicopter Return

The Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return takes you to an elevation above 5,000 m. So, there is a chance of altitude sickness during this journey, which starts to appear after crossing the elevation of 2,500 m For altitude sickness, keep yourself regularly hydrated by drinking enough fluids. Take nutritious foods and avoid the consumption of harmful beverages and alcoholic drinks. Emphasize the slow pace of elevation gain by allowing ample time for acclimatization. Acclimatization helps the body to adjust to rising elevations and prevents altitude sickness. If the symptoms of altitude sickness start to get severe, you can descend down to familiar elevations and stay there until the sickness improves. During each day of trekking, you need to walk for around 6 to 8 hours. So, the journey can be tiring and exhausting. Although the trails are well-marked, some parts of the trek involve steep slopes, moraines, and rocky, uneven terrains. Still, rock climbing and mountaineering skills are not required for this journey. Though previous trekking experiences are not necessarily required, you need to have a reasonable level of fitness to overcome the physical demands and exertion of the trek. In order to improve overall physical strength and endurance, consider engaging in fitness and cardiovascular training. To uplift and ensure your physical readiness for this adventurous journey, you can do exercises such as planks, squats, push-ups, plunges, deadlifts, swimming, aerobics, cycling, skipping, jogging, etc. You can also practice hiking with a backpack in hilly terrains, which prepares you for the challenging high-altitude trekking. You can wear lightweight trekking boots with good ankle support to prevent possible foot injuries while walking over the remote Himalayan terrains. Carry trekking poles for balance and stability when walking on rugged surfaces. The temperature at higher elevations is usually chilly. Likewise, the weather conditions can be adverse during the off-trekking seasons like monsoon and winter. Cho La Pass may be impassable in case of heavy snowfall and other bad weather conditions. So, it is advisable to carry appropriate gear for seamless navigation and layers of clothes to stay warm in the colder alpine environment while trekking during these unfavorable seasons. Conversely, for a comfortable and enriching experience, opting for the suitable trekking seasons, spring and autumn, is the best option. You may also like:
  • Gokyo Lakes and Everest Base Camp Itinerary
  • Everest Base Camp Three Passes Trek
  • Everest Base Camp Luxury Lodge Trek
  • Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek

When to Embark on this Journey?

To get the most out of the Gokyo Cho La Pass Everest Base Camp Trek and Helicopter Return journey, you need to embark on peak trekking and mountaineering seasons, spring and autumn. These are the most suitable times for this adventurous trip, presenting stable weather and moderate temperatures. The arrival of spring brings the full bloom of rhododendron forests and wildflowers in the Himalayan landscapes. You will experience the vibrant and colorful trekking trails during this time. The comfortable warmth in spring makes your journey easy, smooth, and more enjoyable. Additionally, in autumn, the breezy wind on bright sunny days will let you enjoy the trek even more. Likewise, the colorful fall foliage all over the mountainous terrains and trails during this time mesmerizes the trekkers. Spring and autumn feature long days, which allow for relaxed and thorough observation of the high Himalayan beauty. Skies are less cloudy and crystal clear, offering sharp visibility and unobstructed views of the mighty snow peaks. Due to dry and clear weather, the helicopter can take a seamless flight. The upgraded clarity of the Himalayan surroundings in a clean climate can enrich your viewing experience from the helicopter. Trekking during the monsoon/summer and winter seasons is a wise decision due to the extreme temperatures and unpredictable weather conditions. The monsoon brings heavy rainfall, making the trekking trails muddy and slippery and adding challenges to the trek. Likewise, heavy snowfall in winter makes it difficult to navigate the routes due to snow accumulation and blockage.

overview:
Gokyo Valley is a hidden gem in the Khumbu region of Nepal, with its iconic turquoise water in Gokyo Lakes. It lies at an altitude of about 4,790 m (15,715 ft) above sea level in the Solukhumbu district of northeastern Nepal, to the southeast of Chharchung. The valley sits within the Sagarmatha National Park, which offers dramatic views of mountains, glaciers, and deep valleys. Most trekkers choose the Gokyo Valley trail even on the Everest Base Camp trek because it is a quieter trail, and they can experience beautiful views of some of the highest mountain peaks, like Mount Everest, Cho Oyu, and Lhotse, along with six bright turquoise glacial lakes formed by melting ice along the way.

The Gokyo Valley trek is one of the most adventurous and unforgettable treks, taking around 10-13 days. A 13-day itinerary is a safe and practical option that includes an acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar. This valley offers scenic views of Gokyo Lakes, Ngozumpa Glacier, and Gokyo Ri. The Gokyo Valley trek is the best choice for those who love Himalayan scenery without going to Everest Base Camp, the busiest trail. 

The trek starts in Lukla, where we have to take a flight from Kathmandu. From Lukla, the whole trail is walked, passing through Phakding and climbing to Namche Bazaar. You should spend an acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar. From Namche Bazaar, we will trek to Dhole, leaving the main Everest Base Camp trail. The trek passes through Machhermo before reaching Gokyo, which is our last destination. During your journey, you can also see the beautiful Rhododendron forest, the Himalayan landscape, and the Sherpa villages, along with their traditions and culture, which you may find welcoming.

During the Gokyo Valley trek, trekkers reach the highest altitude of 5,357 m (17,575 ft) at Gokyo Ri. Gokyo Ri is the highest peak in the Khumbu region, located on the west side of the Ngozumpa Glacier, Nepal's largest glacier. Gokyo Ri offers a breathtaking sunrise, revealing panoramic views of glaciers, a turquoise lake, and snow-capped mountains. Gokyo Valley lies within the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Sagarmatha National Park. In the National Park, you can find rare wildlife, including Red Panda and SnowLeopard, forest, and beautiful landscapes. You can also see various animals such as the Himalayan Thar, the Himalayan Monal, the Blue Sheep, and the Musk Deer.

The best time for trekking is always Spring from March to May, and Autumn from September to November. These seasons generally offer clear views, dry weather, and better trail conditions. The trek is moderately challenging, which involves several hours of uphill walking in a single day. Trekking becomes more challenging on steep, high-altitude trails. If you are physically fit and can walk a long uphill route, then even beginners without trekking experience can attempt the Gokyo Valley trek. If you want to experience moderate and rewarding trekking where you can enjoy breathtaking views, the Gokyo Valley is definitely a must-visit destination.

Gokyo Valley Trek Altitude Chart
highlights: Admire the breathtaking beauty of the Ngozumpa Glacier, the largest glacier in the Himalayas,situated beneath the majestic peaks of the Himalayan range.
Experience the calmness of turquoise lakes and some of the world’s tallest snowcapped mountains like Mount Everest, Lhotse, and Cho Oyu.
Trek to Gokyo Ri, one of the highest settlements in the world, from where we can see four 8,000-meter peaks: Mount Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu.
Explore the beauty of Namche Bazaar, where you will stay overnight for acclimatization.
Experience the most adventurous and thrilling trek in the Everest region, hiking to Gokyo Peak at an altitude of 5,357 meters.
Gaze upon the most captivating and magical sunrise from Gokyo Ri, which is the highest viewpoint of the Gokyo Trek.
Walk through the traditional Sherpa village and admire their welcoming nature, culture, and the Buddhist traditions of the Khumbu region.
Explore Sagarmatha National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its rare wildlife, flora, and fauna, Himalayan sceneries, and high-altitude ecosystem.
Capture unforgettable Himalayan photographs with calm blue lakes, glaciers, and a Sherpa village, which will be one of the most wonderful memories in your life.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Tribhuwan International Airport Kathmandu and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html:
After you arrive in Kathmandu on an international flight, we will take you to the hotel. Our staff will transfer you to a hotel in a private vehicle. You will get proper welcome reception from the hotel staff. Then, you will get briefed about this Gokyo valley trek itinerary in detail.

You can also explore the beautiful landmarks of this city, including temples, palaces, alleyways, etc., before returning to your hotel. Moreover, you can also rest in the hotel and prepare for your trek.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft) and then same day trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html:
Phakding Elevation: 2,610 m
Flight Duration: 35-40 minutes
Walking Duration: 3-4 hrs

We will start our journey on this day with a mountain flight that takes you above beautiful landscapes to Lukla. The incredible flight provides you with stunning views of the Himalayas. It takes around 40-45 minutes to complete this flight.

After arriving at Lukla, we will rest for some time before trekking to Phakding. You will pass through various Sherpa settlements of the region before arriving at your destination. The trails on the foothills of the Himalayas will enchant you along this trail. It is a short duration trek that only takes around 3-4 hrs. After arriving at Phakding, you can stay in a local teahouse or a guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Namche Bazar Elevation: 3,440 m
Walking Duration: 6-7 hours

The trail to arrive at Namche from Phakding passes through outstanding landscapes. This incredible section of the trek takes you to Namche Bazaar passing alongside the Dudh Koshi River. There are rhododendron, juniper, and forested magnolia trails that will lead you to your destination.

Trekkers will get their permits at the Sagarmatha National Park checkpoint at Monjo. You can observe beautiful snow-capped mountain views from various viewpoints along these trails, including Mt Everest (8,848 m). We will then cross the beautiful Dudh Koshi River through wooden bridges.

There are other suspension bridges that you need to cross to arrive at Namche Bazaar. After an excursion to these places for some time, we will come back to our tea house and rest for a night.

itinerary.title: Rest at Namche Bazar for acclimatization (3,440 m / 11,286 ft).
itinerary.html: On this day, you will rest and acclimatize at Namche Bazaar. Various landmarks in this region provide trekkers with ideal acclimatization points. Everest View hotel is a perfect viewpoint to observe the stunning snow-capped mountains. This highest placed hotel provides you with a spectacular 360-degree panorama view of the Mahalangur Himalayas. Namche has a vibrant atmosphere full of tourists and travelers arriving for their trekking journey. Besides that, there is a significant Sherpa Museum in Namche. The museum remains dedicated to the traditional lifestyle of the Sherpa community. If you want, you can go hiking to Khunde and Khumjung near Namche. It is a hilltop with incredible views of the entire mountain vista of the region. There is a Syangboche airstrip that probably provides the best view of the region. These hiking destinations are of short duration ranging 1-2 hours. Staying idle on acclimatization days is not recommended. Hence, covering some distance and hiking short hills is essential to keep your body fit. It helps you to tackle altitude sickness along these trails. After exploring, we will return to rest in the Namche guesthouse and prepare for our trek the next day.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazar to Dole (4,200 m / 13,780 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Dole Elevation: 4,200 m
Walking Duration: 6-7 hours

After breakfast in the teahouse, we will start our trek to Dole from Namche. This section passes through the side of Dudh Koshi River. It then climbs uphill, ascending on a colorful trail with Buddhist landmarks. The track then arrives at Dole after a few hours’ treks, providing outstanding views of mountains. You can explore several Sherpa settlements and rural monasteries along these trails. We will rest at Dole teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dole to Machhermo (4,470 m / 14,665 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Machhermo Elevation: 4,470 m
Walking Duration: 5-6 hours

The Dole to Machhermo trail is our next route in this trekking journey. There are beautiful snow-capped mountain views of lesser-known peaks like Cholatse (6,335 m), Taboche (6,367 m), and Cho Oyu (8,188 m) in this section of the trek. You will climb alongside the Dudh Koshi River and pass various village settlements. We will finally arrive at Machhermo after a hike of a few hours. Then, we will rest and prepare for our next day trek at Machhermo teahouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Machhermo to Gokyo (4,790 m / 15,715 ft), 4-5 hours
itinerary.html:
Gokyo Elevation: 4,790 m
Walking Duration: 4-5 hours

The trail from Machermo to Gokyo has unique landscapes. You will start your trek climbing gradually on the banks of serene rivers like Dudh Koshi. You will pass through multiple settlements of locals and monasteries to reach Gokyo Lakes. The trail then leads you through Ngozumpa Glacier moraines to reach the second Gokyo lake. There is a third Gokyo lake a few meters away. Moreover, you can find a beautiful Sherpa village in the surrounding of the Gokyo lake. We will end our day in Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Gokyo Excursion day, hike to Gokyo Ri / Gokyo Peak (5,357 m / 17,575 ft).
itinerary.html:
Gokyo Ri Elevation: 5357  meters
Walking Duration: 2-3 hours

You will wake up early in the morning as it is your excursion and acclimatization day. You will explore these beautiful lake areas in Gokyo. You can also take a short day hike to Gokyo Ri (5,357 m) trekking peak. From the summit of this incredible trekking peak, you can observe Everest (8,848 m), Cho Oyu (8,188 m), and other mountains. The Gokyo Valley looks unbelievably awe-inspiring from the summit.

Gokyo lakes, Ngozumpa glaciers, and other landmarks are also observable from Gokyo Ri. After exploring further and capturing memories in your camera, you will return to Gokyo village. You can also interact with the locals with the help of your guide. You will rest and prepare for this trek at Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Trek back from Gokyo to Dole (44,200 m / 13,780 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Dole Elevation: 4,200 m
Walking Duration: 5-6 hours

An early morning rise will provide you with an opportunity to observe the scenic sunrise. We trek through the stunning geographical landscapes of the valley. You will pass through the Gokyo Lakes, passing through Phangan and Machhermo village settlements to arrive in Dole.

Taboche (6,367 m) and Cholatse (6,335 m) are the two mountain peaks you can observe in this trek route. Finally, we will arrive at Dole after a trek of a few hours. We will then explore, interact with locals and rest in local accommodation.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dole to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Namche Ekevation: 4,200 m
Walking Duration: 5-6 hours

We will leave Dole early in the morning to start our trekking adventure on this day. There are various forested trails and village settlements that you need to pass to arrive at Namche Bazaar. You will first descend to the village of Sanasa, passing them through Phortse Thanga and Mong to arrive at Namche.

You will also pass through small monasteries to reach Namche Bazaar. There are various scenic points and places to visit in Namche. After exploring these villages, we will spend the night at a teahouse and prepare for the final day of the trek.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Lukla Elevation:2,860 mWalking Duration: 7-8 hours

You will start your trek on this day by following the Dudh Koshi River trails from Namche Bazaar to Lukla. The tracks of this trek then pass through forested trails with rhododendron trees and other ancient settlements.

Many local Sherpa villages, Mani walls, and Buddhist monasteries are present along this trail. After arriving at Lukla, you can rest for the evening and interact with locals. Our trekking journey comes to an end in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu, (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html:
Flight Duration: 35-40 minutes

You will finally take the mountain flight from Lukla to Kathmandu. We can observe various landscapes, including slow-clad mountains, for the last time on this journey. You will then have the option to tour around various local landmarks of Kathmandu valley or rest in your hotel.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu to your onward destination.
itinerary.html: Today, you will be transferred to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for your onward flight.

sections.title: What is the Best Time For Gokyo Valley Trek?
sections.html:
Choosing the right season is a major part of the Gokyo Valley Trek because the weather affects almost every part of the journey. The trek largely depends on weather, trail conditions, visibility, and temperature at higher elevations. Weather with clear skies and stable, dry conditions is the most suitable for trekking. For this reason, spring and autumn are considered the most favorable seasons for trekking. Monsoon and winter bring unstable weather, cloudy conditions, rainfall, and snowfall. This does not mean trekking is impossible during these seasons, but an experienced person with proper gear and preparation can still trek.

Spring 

Spring starts in March and lasts until May. It is the most favourable season for trekking, as it offers clear mountain views and skies. During Spring, the weather and climate conditions in and around the Gokyo Valley are usually stable, providing good visibility, which is best on high-altitude treks. Skies are often clear in the morning, giving trekkers a chance to see panoramic views of Mount Everest, Mount Makalu, Mount Lhotse, Cho Oyu, and the surrounding Khumbu mountains from Gokyo Ri.

The daytime temperature during the spring can range from 0°C to 12°C (32°F to 59°F), while at night the temperature drops to -5 °C to -15°C (23°F to 5°F). March is normally the coldest, April becomes milder, and May is warmer. The Gokyo trail is very attractive in spring because of dense green forests and blooming rhododendrons that add color to the landscape before the scenery becomes more alpine at higher elevations. The route also became very safe due to the lack of rainfall and dry trail conditions.

Although this is a very beautiful season for trekking, it has some disadvantages. Spring is one of the busiest trekking seasons. The section from Lukla through Namche is shared with many Everest region trekkers, so the trail becomes busy and crowded. You should book accommodation, flights, and guides in advance so you won’t face any difficulty.

Monsoon 

The Monsoon season runs from June to August and is considered off-season for travel and trekking. Monsoon brings heavy rainfall, overcast skies, thunder and lightning, slippery trails, poor visibility, and flight obstruction. Trekkers may not get a chance to see beautiful Himalayan peaks and surrounding Khumbu mountains. There will always be high risks of floods and landslides on the route you travel to reach your destination. Due to mud and wet trails, there are many leeches and insects along the trail. 

During the monsoon, daytime temperatures in the Gokyo Valley range from 10°C to 20°C (50°F to 68°F), while nighttime temperatures drop between 0°C and -12°C (32°F to 10°F). June is usually the wettest and cloudiest period. Temperatures are actually warmer than in spring, but the biggest problems are rain, humidity, and cloudy skies. However, the trail is much quieter, less crowded, more peaceful, less demanding, and cheaper this season. Landscapes at lower elevations also become green and fresh, with fast-flowing rivers and waterfalls. Gokyo Valley has yak pastures during summer, giving the valley a different appearance from the colder seasons.

An experienced trekker can still trek during the monsoon with proper gear and preparations. But trekkers must also know that the monsoon is not for beginners. Trekkers choosing the monsoon season should carry waterproof clothing, rain protection, reliable trekking shoes, and extra flexibility in their schedule in case of flight or trekking plan delay. So, booking is highly recommended because trekkers need more logistical preparation. Overall, the monsoon is the least favourable season for the Gokyo Valley Trek. It suits best for those who are daring and adventurous, who value quiet trails and do not mind rain. 

Autumn

Autumn is the best overall season for travel and trekking, which lasts from September to November. Autumn is considered the best season for travel and trekking. Autumn offers excellent visibility, clear skies, stable temperature, and stable weather conditions. Due to dry trails, trekkers can walk comfortably. As autumn provides excellent mountain views, we can enjoy beautiful views of the world’s highest mountains like Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu. From Gokyo Ri, trekkers can enjoy the views of deep valleys, glaciers, the Sagarmatha National Park area, and mountains above 8,000 m

In the Gokyo Valley during autumn, daytime temperatures range from 5°C to 15°C (41°F to 59°F), while night temperatures drop sharply between -10°C and -3°C (14°F to 287°F). The nights become much colder than the day. September is warmer, October offers more balanced weather, and November brings clear skies along with considerably cooler mornings and nights. Autumn offers breathtaking views of nature. The cleaner post-monsoon atmosphere also creates excellent conditions for Himalayan photography, especially around the Gokyo Lakes and from Gokyo Ri.

Autumn is also special in Nepal, as the greatest festivals, Dashain and Tihar, fall during this season. Trekkers can experience festivals and get a closer look at Nepali culture and traditions. The colorful lights, oil lamps, flowers, and traditional decorations during Tihar are so captivating that trekkers will truly enjoy the festival. These festivals bring a special charm to the autumn season. Autumn is one of the busiest trekking seasons. The trails are very crowded, and popular lodges along the route can see high demand. Booking in advance is a must if you are planning to trek during the peak autumn weeks. 

Winter

Winter starts from December and lasts until February. It is the quietest period on the trail because this season offers cold weather and snowfall. Gokyo Ri stands at an altitude of 5,357 m, so trekking above 4,000 m becomes particularly cold in winter, with snow and ice affecting the high. altitude routes. Clear views cannot be guaranteed in the winter season due to snow-covered landscapes, clouds, fog, and strong winds. There are also shorter daylight hours in winter, which ultimately means less time to enjoy the views. 

In the Gokyo Valley, daytime temperatures range from -5°C to 5°C (23°F to 41°F), while nighttime temperatures range from -15°C to -25°C (5°F to -13°F). Snowfall can cover parts of the trail, while ice makes it slippery. The strong wind makes it feel even colder on the climb to Gokyo Ri. Snow-covered mountains, frozen waterfalls, and icy landscapes create a different Gokyo experience. In winter, the trails are less crowded, and accommodation is comparatively cheaper and less demanding than in spring and autumn. The trails are also peaceful and silent.

However, extremely cold temperatures and persistent snowfall can lead to flight delays, hypothermia, frostbite, and avalanches in exposed mountain areas. Proper preparation is very important during a trek. Trekkers should carry warm insulated sleeping bags, thermal base layers, insulated jackets, warm gloves, socks, a winter hat, and comfortable trekking boots. Spare warm layers are useful if the temperature drops suddenly. As teahouses and lodges reduce or shut down their services, trekkers must book in advance. Overall, winter is less favourable than spring and autumn, but experienced trekkers who are comfortable with freezing temperatures can still trek.

Why Go on Gokyo Valley Trek?

Gokyo Lake

The main reason to go on the Gokyo Valley Trek is to see the Gokyo Lake. Gokyo lake is a group of six high altitude alpine freshwater lakes which is surrounded by panoramic mountains. The Gokyo lake is the primary attraction in the Gokyo valley. The turquoise, deep blue water lake gives fantastic scenery. Photography opportunities or simply witnessing its natural beauty is enough to make the trip memorable.

Mountain View

Throughout the trek, various snow-capped mountains are visible. Visitors will get a chance to see some of the most beautiful mountains from the Mahalangur range including the world’s tallest mountain, Mt Everest (8848.86). Other notable mountains like Cho Oyu (8,188 m), Makalu (8,485 m), and Lhotse (8,516 m) are also visible during the trek. Smaller mountains like Cholatse, Taboche, Kangtega, and Ama Dablam are also visible making it a primary destination for mountain lovers.

Gokyo Ri

Gokyo Ri (5,357 m) is within the Khumbu region on the west side of Ngozumpa glacier, which is the largest glacier in the whole Himalayas in Nepal. Gokyo Ri offers one of the best viewpoints in the world. It takes 2-3 hours to reach from Gokyo village (4,750 m). Gokyo Ri provides not only the majestic view of the Gokyo Lake and the peaceful surrounding but also gives a clear view of the four of the world’s fourteen 8,000 meter peaks at the same time including a clear view of Everest’s summit. The amount of crowd is also less compared to Kala Pathhar or EBC so you can enjoy the spiritual peace and silence without being surrounded by dozens of other tour groups.

Scenic natural beauty

The beautiful trails and viewpoints of this trek are incredible. There are various Gokyo lakes that you can visit in this region. There are multiple viewpoints of this trek from where you can observe the mountains of the Everest Mahalangur range. Besides, serene rivers, waterfalls, glacial rivers, icy glaciers, and others are significant landmarks in this region. Hence, this trek route is ideal for trekking.

Off the beaten trails

This unique Gokyo valley trek takes you through remote and untraversed terrains. It is ideal for those who love to tour in a quiet and peaceful environment. Various diverse landscapes in this region will make you fall in love with the area. These off-the-beaten trails make it quite appealing among trekkers.

Moderate trails

The Gokyo Valley Trek has moderate trails. This trail does not require technical skills. You do not pass through the challenging routes of Everest base camp and Kalapathar. These relatively easy trails are doable by all skill levels. Hence, this moderately challenging trail is therefore perfect for all. Beginner trekkers, photographers, family members and corporate workers who want to have a subtle mountain adventure can go on this trek.

Cultural exploration

This trek traverses through various cultural settlements of the region. There are majestic ancient monasteries, chorten, mani walls, and others. Besides that, there are various local cultural settlements in this region. Dole, Machhermo, and Gokyo valley will welcome you with great hospitality and cultural immersion. Trekking guides will help you with interacting with locals and translating the local language. Besides that, if you travel in the Autumn season, you will experience and celebrate festivals with locals.

Accommodation in Gokyo Valley Trek

Proper sleep and rest make the next day of walking much easier, so good accommodation is useful in the Gokyo Valley Trek. Accommodation changes as you move higher elevation because it is difficult to supply goods. Lukla and Namchee Bazaar offer teahouses, lodges, guesthouses, and some better hotels. Farther up the trail, the accommodation becomes more simple and you can mostly find teahouses and mountain lodges. Teahouse accommodation is the most common accommodation throughout the Gokyo Trek.

Teahouse

Teahouses are the most common and the cheapest accommodation option on the Gokyo Valley Trek. Teahouses are locally owned by the people living in Gokyo Valley and are mostly available through the trekking route. These teahouses provide basic facilities rather than luxury. Rooms are usually twin-sharing with two single beds, mattresses, pillows and blankets. At the lower region, you may see the attached bathroom with a hot shower usually for added costs but moving higher, shared bathrooms are very common. Meals are served in the common dining hall which is also a place to talk, relax, and warm-up. Trekkers can experience the local hospitality and everyday mountain life. Simplicity is the best feeling that you get during traditional trekking in Khumbu region. 

Lodges and Guesthouses

Lodges and Guesthouses provide slightly better standards of accommodation than basic teahouses as they are expensive. Rooms are normally private or twin-sharing with basic beds, mattresses, and blankets. Some lodges may also have dormitory-style rooms. Most of the lodges have common bathrooms, while some of them may have attached bathrooms. Hot showers may be available by paying additional costs. Lodges and Guestrooms have a common dining hall serving breakfast, dinner, local meals, tea, coffee, and other hot drinks. Few hotels may have a small bar or lounge where guests can relax in the evening. Electricity, charging facilities, Wi-Fi may be available with additional cost for charging and Wi-Fi. At higher elevation, heating or air conditioning is limited to common dining rooms rather than individual bedrooms.

Hotels

Hotels are comparatively more expensive than teahouses, lodges, and guesthouses as it provides the highest level of accommodation, and found in larger settlements in Khumbu region like Lukla and Namche Bazaar rather than in the upper region. Rooms are normally larger that include private bathrooms, better beds and furnishing, hot water, heating, Wi-Fi, and electricity. Some of them also provide restaurants, bars or lounges, room service, spa facilities, laundry, luggage storage, and reception services as well.

Food in Gokyo Valley Trek

Food is an important part of the Gokyo Valley Trek. It provides energy during the trek and enables you to walk further. Especially during the high elevation walk, food is important. All the accommodation options and restaurants during the trek provide a mixture of food options. While Dal Bhat  (Rice with Lentil Soup) is the most staple food option, it is also the national dish of Nepal. You can find Dal Bhat in almost all the places during the trek and besides Dal Bhat, other Tibetan Dishes, and famous international or western meals are available.

What Foods are Available on the Gokyo Valley Trek?

Food Type

Common Options

Nepali Food

Dal bhat, vegetable curry, rice, roti, thukpa

Tibetan-style Food

Sherpa stew, thukpa, Tibetan bread, momo

Breakfast

Porridge, eggs, pancakes, Tibetan bread, toast, muesli

Lunch & Dinner

Dal bhat, noodles, pasta, fried rice, potatoes, soups

Snacks

Biscuits, chocolate, popcorn, nuts, energy bars

Drinks

Tea, coffee, hot lemon, hot chocolate, soft drinks

Vegetarian Options

Dal bhat, vegetable curry, noodles, pasta, potatoes, soup

The availability of food options depends upon the altitude. A general rule of thumb is, the higher you go the less options there will be for food and the cost will go higher. This is because, in high altitude transportation of supplies is harder so the options are limited and do cost more. In your package, three meals, which are Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner are included for the duration of your trekking days in the Gokyo Valley Trek itinerary. However, foods like soft drinks, dry nuts, fruits, chocolates, beers, electrolytes, and energy bars should be paid separately.

Vegetarian Options

It is better to stick with a vegetarian diet while you are on the Gokyo Valley Trek. Consuming meat is not a good idea as it will take longer time to digest and requires high energy to burn. Also meat and meat products on the trekking trail are stored and may not be fresh. This causes concern in food hygiene. So, there are many vegetarian options during the trek where accommodations provide and prepare meat-free meals. Common vegetarian choices can include Dal Bhat with vegetables, vegetable curry, noodles, fried rice, pasta, potatoes, soups, Tibetan breads, porridge and pancakes. Similarly, if you have any dietary requirements like gluten free food, allergies or medical dietary restrictions, consult with Base Camp Adventure. Your guide can communicate the requirement with the accommodation owners and cater to your needs.

How Difficult is Gokyo Valley Trek?

The Gokyo Valley Trek difficulty is graded as moderate to challenging. The trek features long walking hours for multiple days in high altitude which can challenge the physical limit. Besides that, the terrain shifts from lower green region to high alpine environment where altitude and altitude sickness becomes a major concern. Another factor that adds up the difficulty of Gokyo Valley is the weather. Bad weather conditions can create difficulty in sleeping and walking. Especially extreme cold conditions can also make the experience challenging.

The difficulty factors of Gokyo Valley Trek are discussed below:

High Altitude: Altitude is one of the biggest challenges in the Gokyo Trek. You will reach the maximum altitude of 5,357 m (17,575 ft) where altitude difficulty prevails. Reaching this elevation requires immense physical fitness. Breathing is difficult and simple activities like walking can become challenging. You can experience headache, nausea, vomiting, shortness of breath and difficulty in sleeping. So it is necessary to gradually ascend and acclimatize.

Long Walking Hours: The 13 Day Gokyo Valley Trek requires long walking hours. Trekkers need to walk at least 6-8 hours every day to reach the next camp. For beginners who are not used to walking for that long period may find the trek difficult.

Off-beaten Trail: The Gokyo Valley trekking route follows uneven, off-beaten trails. The route is well under the mountain sections which is difficult to navigate. Some of the sections are uneven and slippery which causes safety concerns. So it is necessary to carry good trekking shoes and follow guide instructions while walking in such areas.

Steep Ascent and Descents: The trekking trail is not always flat and you will need to walk through steep ascent and descent. The climb towards Namche Bazaar from Phakding, and climb to Gokyo Ri is particularly demanding. The walk also involves repeated uphill walk through multiple days. Especially the walk to Gokyo Ri, the most challenging one. With the combination of altitude, ascent becomes difficult.

Weather Condition: Bad weather conditions can make the trek extremely challenging. As mountain weather is itself unpredictable, cold temperature, wind, snowfall, rain and reduced visibility can make the walk more demanding. In colder months, especially in high altitude, snowfall and ice can make the trek slippery and difficult to navigate.

What Permits are Needed for Gokyo Valley Trek?

The Gokyo Valley Trek requires two permits. As it is in the Khumbu region, a local permit which is the Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit is important to acquire. Similarly, as the trek progresses inside the Sagarmatha National Park, a Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit is also essential. There are checkpost stationed in various points of the trek where officials check these permits. If you do not have these permits, then you will not be allowed to enter further.

1. Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit

The Gokyo route runs inside the Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality so you should acquire this permit. You can obtain the permit at Lukla or in Monjo. The cost of the permit is NRs. 3,000 (USD 25-30) per person per entry. Now, the permit replaces the Trekker’s Information Management Card (TIMS). It is issued by the local municipality to manage and support the number of trekkers entering the area. The fund is later used for improving the trekking routes, managing waste and supporting infrastructures.

2. Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit

After Monjo, you will enter the Sagarmatha National Park which is a government protected area (UNESCO World Heritage Site). To enter the area, the Sagarmatha National Park permit is issued. The cost of the permit depends upon the nationality which is as follows:

  • NRs. 3,000 per person for foreign nationals.
  • NRs. 1,500 per person for SAARC nationals.
  • Free for children under the age of 10. 

You can obtain the permit from Nepal Tourism Board Office in Kathmandu or the national park entry checkpost in Monjo. The permit is non-negotiable and frequently checked at various checkpoints along the route.

Necessary Documents for the Permits

  • A valid passport with a current Nepali visa
  • 2 to 4 passport-size photos
  • A detailed trekking itinerary, especially if applying through an agency
  • Proof of travel insurance

Note: Base Camp Adventure will obtain these permits on your behalf after your arrival in Kathmandu. So, you do not need to personally go and get the permits. We want you to have a smooth, hassle-free experience.

Do I Need Travel Insurance for Gokyo Valley Trek?

Travel Insurance is important for Gokyo Valley Trek. It is not mandatory to purchase travel insurance but getting one can assure safety and help with emergency evacuation on the trek if necessary. Before the start of the trek, you are obligated to provide a copy of your Travel Insurance to Base Camp Adventure. This is because, as the trek is above 5,000 m, there are chances of altitude sickness. So in case of emergency, helicopter evacuation might be required. So to conduct the emergency rescue via helicopter, obtaining travel insurance is essential.

A travel insurance policy may come in different manners. But you should pick the policy which will cover all the costs associated with medical and emergency evacuation. Also insurance that covers for high altitude trekking, personal injury, flight delays or cancellation, loss of baggage, and equipment coverage is a plus. Likewise, Base Camp Adventure does not provide insurance facilities and must be obtained from a reputable insurance company. You are welcome to consult with us for recommendations.

How to Prepare for Gokyo Valley Trek?

Although the trek is difficult, it is doable with a good level of preparation. Mainly trekkers need to understand how to prepare themselves before actually undertaking the journey. Many also believe trekking is a physical journey. Which is somewhat true, but it is necessary to understand that, as much as trekking involves physical fitness, it also requires mental preparation. As the area is remote, and well over 5,000 m it is better to understand the area and mentally prepare accordingly. For physical training it is better to start several weeks before the trek. The training should primarily focus on cardio fitness, leg strength, endurance and altitude awareness.

Cardio Exercise: Focus your physical fitness around cardio vascular exercises. You do not need to do heavy weight lifting and can practice swimming, running, jogging, and cycling. You can also go on a short hike while carrying a bag pack to simulate trekking experience. Cardio exercise is intended to build your endurance and helps you with the regular walk during the trek.

Leg Exercise: Begin to do leg exercises which will help you with the steep ascent and descent in the trek. You can include stair climbing, squats, lunges, step-ups, and glute bridges for  the leg exercise.

Prepare for Altitude: As altitude is a major concern during the Gokyo Trek, you will need to strategize to counter the effects of altitude sickness. You should know that physical fitness does not prevent altitude sickness. For that, you will need to choose an appropriate itinerary that includes acclimatisation day. Also, do not treat acclimatization day as a rest day, you will need to hike to a certain elevation and adapt the body to low oxygen level.

Hydration and Nutrition: You should eat regularly and drink at least 4-6 liters of water per day. You should also drink necessary fluids and eat a balanced diet to keep your body warm and hydrated. Do not drink alcohol or smoke during the trek as both will cause dehydration and raise concern for altitude. Avoid consuming meat as your body will require more energy for digestion. Focus on a vegetarian diet and eat protein, fruits and vegetables for energy.

Proper Clothing: Pack and wear your clothes according to the season. Use a layer clothing system to keep your body warm. Wear base layer, insulating layer, down jacket and waterproof outer layer in the high altitude to keep away from cold. Other clothes like boots, socks, gloves, sunglasses and trousers are necessary for the trek.

Mental Preparation: Prepare yourself to walk long hours in uneven terrain for multiple days. It is better to research about the area and know what facilities you can get in the Gokyo region. As the area is remote, the facilities are limited so it is not a luxury holiday beside a beach or resort. Check the weather forecast, crowd level, and trail condition before beginning the trek.

Altitude Sickness During Gokyo Valley Trek

Altitude sickness is a condition where a body fails to adapt to the low oxygen level existing in the high altitude. Concern of Altitude Sickness or Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) can rise above 3,000 m So, AMS is a major challenge during the Gokyo Valley trek and there are chances that trekkers might get affected by it. However, there is a common misbelief that fit people do not get altitude sickness. Altitude sickness mainly occurs due to rapid ascent without proper acclimatization so it can happen to anyone, even fit trekkers. You can understand more about altitude sickness here:

Common Symptoms of Altitude Sickness

  • Headache
  • Difficulty breathing
  • Nausea
  • Loss of appetite
  • Constant irritation
  • Vomiting
  • Difficulty in sleeping
  • Dizziness
  • Unusual tiredness

These are the early symptoms of altitude sickness and do not pose life threatening concerns. Many trekkers take these symptoms lightly and continue further on the trek. However, if not paid attention, the risk rises, and can get complicated. If altitude sickness gets worse, it can have a huge impact on health and sometimes even cause death.

Complication of AMS

  • High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema (HAPE): Accumulation of liquid in lungs.
  • High-Altitude Cerebral Edema (HACE): Accumulation of liquid in heart.

So, it is necessary to understand the symptoms and complications of altitude sickness for a better treatment. While prevention is better than cure, trekkers should minimize the risk of altitude sickness through prevention procedures.

How to Prevent Altitude Sickness?

  • Follow a well-planned itinerary and ascend gradually. Take time to adapt to the atmosphere.
  • Walk slow with your natural pace. The trek is not a race and there is no advantage of reaching first.
  • Insert acclimatisation days in your itinerary to give your body additional time to adjust. 
  • Take acclimatization hikes seriously and do not treat it as a rest day. Your itinerary includes an acclimatization in Namche Bazaar.
  • Drink plenty of water throughout the day. Dehydration can make you feel worse at altitude.
  • High elevation can decrease your appetite however, eat regularly. Carrying snacks like chocolate, nuts, dried fruits and energy bars can help.
  • Avoid smoking or consuming alcohol during the trek. It can interfere with sleep and causes dehydration.

What Happens If Symptoms of Altitude Sickness Appear?

If any symptoms of altitude sickness appear consult with your guide. Your guide will check your pulse and oxygen level through an oximeter. The reading of the oximeter and your personal body condition will determine the next step. If the condition is normal, you can proceed further above. Also, if the symptoms are mild, then you might need to stay an additional day in your accommodation until the symptoms go away. However, if the condition is bad, then you have to descend immediately to a lower elevation. In life-threatening condition, emergency helicopter evacuation will be immediately conducted where you will be rescued from the place and transferred to the medical facility in Kathmandu.
