faqs.q: Can I Get Visa on Arrival?
faqs.a:
Yes. Most foreign nationals can acquire a visa on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. For an on arrival visa you need to have a valid passport, a completed visa application form, a passport photo and the necessary visa fee.

Make sure to requirements for visa on arrival in your country before arrival. If your country is not eligible for a visa on arrival then you may obtain it in advance from diplomatic missions (consulates and embassies).

faqs.q: Can the Visa Be Extended?
faqs.a: Yes. It can be. If you wish to extend your stay then you may extend it by visiting the Department of Immigration in Kathmandu and Pokhara. Please renew it before the expiration date.

faqs.q: Is Airport Pickup Available for the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a: Yes. At Base Camp Adventure, we provide airport pick up service for the Gokyo Valley Trek and almost all other trekking packages. Our team will be waiting for you at the international airport and will transfer you to your booked accommodation in the city ensuring a hassle free start of the journey.

faqs.q: How Difficult is the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a:
The Gokyo Valley Trek is considered moderately challenging. It involves daily walks of 5 to 7 hours. The trek requires you to make steep ascents on rocky trails and high altitude path that reaches over 5,300 m 

While the route is physically demanding proper acclimatization, a steady pace and reasonable fitness make this achievable for most physically fit trekkers

faqs.q: Is the Gokyo Valley Trek Suitable for Beginners?
faqs.a:
Yes. Beginners can complete the Gokyo Valley Trek as long as they are prepared enough and have good level of fitness. Prior trekking experience is always beneficial but is not necessary. 

If you are a well prepared beginner, follow a gradual itinerary and advice of the experienced guides, then you can successfully complete the trek.

faqs.q: How Long Do You Trek Each Day?
faqs.a: Usually, trekking days take from 5 to 7 hours depending on the itinerary, condition of the trail and altitude. Sometimes there are shorter days when you just need to spend a few hours trekking. Some days might be longer ones, which can take about 8 hours of trekking. Taking breaks every hour during the journey can make the navigation more pleasant and manageable.

faqs.q: How Fit Do I Need to Be for the Gokyo Lakes Trek?
faqs.a: The Gokyo Valley Trek demands a good level of physical fitness. You need to be physically fit enough to walk several days through rugged terrain carrying a small light backpack. Cardiovascular exercises, hiking, stair-climbing, and strength training exercises for at least 3 to 4 months prior to the trek are strongly recommended.

faqs.q: Is the Ascent to Gokyo Ri Challenging?
faqs.a:
The trek to Gokyo Ri is among the most difficult portions of the trek because of its steep elevation and altitude of 5,357 m 

The trail is a steep uphill one and trekkers have to traverse steep trails at an altitude where the thinness of the air adds more difficulty in each step. However, it does not require any technical expertise in mountaineering. So, proper caution should be taken while ascending.

faqs.q: Do Lukla Flights Depart From Kathmandu or Ramechhap?
faqs.a: Lukla flights generally take off from Kathmandu. During the peak trekking seasons of spring and autumn, flights can also operate from Ramechhap Airport. This is because of increased air traffic congestion at Kathmandu Airport. The departure airport depends on the season, the weather conditions and the schedule of the airline.

faqs.q: How Long is the Flight to Lukla?
faqs.a: The journey to Lukla is truly an exciting one. The flight from Kathmandu is about 30 to 35 minutes. From Ramechhap it takes about 15 to 20 minutes. During the flight, you can witness Himalayan mountains, valleys, rivers and mountain villages which will keep you captivated throughout the journey.

faqs.q: What Happens if My Lukla Flight is Canceled?
faqs.a: Lukla flights are strongly influenced by weather. Delays or cancellations are common when visibility is poor or strong winds develop. If your flight is canceled, a new flight date will be arranged for the next available day. If you are short on time, you may choose a helicopter flight, subject to weather and seat availability, by paying extra.

faqs.q: What Is The Allowed Luggage Weight On Domestic Flights?
faqs.a: For domestic flights between Kathmandu and Lukla 15 kg total baggage is allowed: 10 kg checked baggage and 5 kg hand luggage. Before packing you must check the luggage limit as excess baggage may cost extra.

faqs.q: What is the Best Time to Do the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) are the best times for the Gokyo Valley Trek. During these months, you will be rewarded with stable weather, enchanting mountain views and ideal trail conditions which will let you experience a smooth and successful adventure according to your intended plan.

faqs.q: Does It Snow During the Trekking Season?
faqs.a:
Yes. It can snow any time of the year in the upper areas of Gokyo Valley. But it is more common during late autumn, winter, and early spring. 

In the main trekking season, the snow is generally light and is manageable with proper caution. However, heavy snowfall during winter may make trails harder to navigate  requiring the right gear, the support of an experienced guide and good planning.

faqs.q: Can Weather Affect Lukla Flights?
faqs.a: Yes. It can. It is due to flights' dependence on good visibility and wind conditions. Though morning flights are more reliable, mountain weather conditions may change rapidly. So, when the weather is not good, the flights can get cancelled. So, you should give an extra day or two to your itinerary.

faqs.q: What are the weather conditions like in the Monsoon Season?
faqs.a:
In the monsoon season, the lower zones of the Gokyo trail get frequent rain. So, the paths can be wet and slippery. In addition, the heavy rain can affect visibility and clouds can cover the surrounding mountains. 

As it also coincides with the summer season, the lower zones can be sunny and warm. But it can get cooler after rainfall. Also, higher sections are mostly cold even in this season. So, proper layering is necessary. 

Likewise, the wet conditions let leeches thrive in the forested area, adding to the discomfort. Though this season offers considerable challenges, it offers tranquil trails, lush, nourished landscapes and unique scenery of misty mountains and clouds floating in the sky. 

Those who wish to undertake Gokyo Valley trek in monsoon must understand  challenges presented by this season and prepare accordingly.

faqs.q: What is Winter Trekking Like in the Gokyo Valley?
faqs.a:
Winter turns the Gokyo region into a serene mountain valley with fresh snow covering the high altitudes. In this season, you can see magnificent snowy mountain vistas and will also get to trek on the quiet path with few trekkers around compared to the peak seasons. 

The high altitude landscapes are covered with snow and the surroundings look like a winter wonderland. However, this season is extremely cold and the snowy terrain requires more effort for navigation. Also, extreme Himalayan cold can be difficult to handle for some. 

However, despite these difficulties, winter provides a wonderful opportunity for anyone in search of quiet trails and beautiful winter scenery. With the right preparation, proper equipment and guide' support winter trek to Gokyo Valley can become truly memorable.

faqs.q: Which Season Offers the Best Mountain Views?
faqs.a:
The autumn season (September to November) offers clearest and most impressive mountain views in Gokyo Valley. This is the post monsoon season. So, after the monsoon ends, the weather becomes clear and the atmosphere is dust free allowing you to see stunning views of Mount Everest, Cho Oyu and other Himalayan peaks under bright open skies.

Spring (March to May) is another good time of year for stunning mountain views. During this time, too, the skies are clear mainly in the mornings and the surrounding landscapes are covered with blooming flowers including rhododendrons. 

The snow covered peaks remain stunning and the combination of vibrant nature and impressive Himalayan scenery makes spring a good time for exploration.

faqs.q: Can I Rent Trekking Gear in Kathmandu?
faqs.a:
Yes. You may rent trekking equipment in Kathmandu prior to joining Gokyo Valley Trek. The most popular place to rent or buy trekking gear is in Thamel. It is a tourist hub of Kathmandu city.

Renting is highly recommended if you do not wish to purchase expensive gear or bring bulky items along from your home.

faqs.q: How Many Layers of Clothing Should I Bring for the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a:
For the Gokyo Valley Trek right layering system is crucial because temperatures can vary throughout the day. You should bring three layers for this adventure specifically, a moisture wicking base layer, an insulating layer and waterproof outer layer.

Also, additional warm clothes like down jackets, gloves, socks and beanie are recommended because the early morning and evenings at high altitudes are usually cold.

faqs.q: What Should I Bring in my DayPack?
faqs.a:
In your day pack, you should include all the things needed during the day trek such as water bottle, high-energy snacks, sunscreen, sunglasses, rain gear, a camera, medicines, hand sanitizer and extra jackets. 

A comfortable 20-30 liter daypack is more than enough for carrying the essentials that is needed during the day's trek.

faqs.q: Are Trekking Poles Essential for Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a:
Trekking Poles are strongly recommended for Gokyo Valley Trek. The trekking pole will provide you with extra support while hiking up in rocky and uneven terrain. This can ease the pressure on your knees while hiking down the hill.

Trekking Poles are extremely helpful in navigating through snowy areas. So to enhance your balance, comfort, and confidence while trekking we suggest that you carry trekking poles.

faqs.q: Is Sleeping Bag Required for the Gokyo Trekking?
faqs.a: Yes. Sleeping bags are highly recommended for the Gokyo Valley Trek. Although all tea houses provide blankets they might not provide enough warmth especially in high altitude areas. So, you will need a good quality sleeping bag to endure the cold weather at higher elevations.

faqs.q: What Personal Medications Should I Carry?
faqs.a:
For this trek, you can carry a personal first aid kit with all the medications that are necessary for you during the trekking journey. These include medications for headaches, stomach issues, allergic reactions, pain relief and blister treatment. 

In addition, you may also pack altitude sickness medications such as Diamox after consultation with your doctor. Also, you need to bring any regular prescription medications that you may need while trekking.

faqs.q: How Can I Be Prepared for the Gokyo Lakes Trek?
faqs.a:
For the Gokyo Lakes Trek, you may start to train for the trek atleast 3 to 4 months prior to the beginning of the trek.

You may start the training by building up endurance through cardio exercise such as: 

  •  Walking
  •  Running
  •  Cycling
  •  Swimming
  •  Climbing stairs 

You may also choose to do strength exercises to enhance balance and endurance. Some examples of strength exercises include: 

  • Squats
  • Push Ups
  • Lunges
  • Step-ups
  • Planks
  • Calf raises

Cardio, strength workouts and hikes are the best ways to train for the Gokyo Valley trek. To get familiar with the conditions of the actual trek, you can go hiking in the nearby hilly areas.

faqs.q: What is the Highest Point Reached During the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a: The highest point of the Gokyo Valley Trek is Gokyo Ri. It is situated at 5,357 m This viewpoint offers amazing views of snowy Himalayan peaks. Trekkers generally hike to the top during the early morning to get rewarded with breathtaking mountain views under vivid skies.

faqs.q: What Are the Symptoms of Altitude Sickness?
faqs.a:
When your body cannot cope with the decreased level of oxygen due at high altitudes then altitude sickness can occur. Some of the symptoms are:

  • Headache
  • Dizziness
  • Nausea
  • Weakness
  • Loss of Appetite
  • Difficulty Sleeping
  • Breathlessness

faqs.q: Where Are Acclimatization Days Included in the Gokyo Valley Trek Itinerary?
faqs.a: Almost all Gokyo Valley Trekking packages feature at least one acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar. This day helps your body adapt to the higher altitude. Additional acclimatization can be scheduled at Machhermo if required or if you want to spend one more day to adapt to the high altitude.

faqs.q: What Precautions Should I Take to Prevent Altitude Sickness?
faqs.a:
To prevent altitude sickness you should ascend gradually and give your body enough time to adjust. In addition, you must be well hydrated, eat nutrient rich meals, avoid alcohol and get rest when needed. Also, make sure to follow the acclimatization schedule that is listed in your itinerary. 

Still, if you happen to experience any of the symptoms and it does not get better, the best possible solution is to head down to the lower elevations.

faqs.q: What Happens if I Experience Altitude Sickness?
faqs.a: Your guide will observe your condition and recommend what should be done after the assessment. It might be solved by rest in case of mild symptoms. However, in case of severe symptoms, descending to a lower elevation is highly recommended.

faqs.q: Is Emergency Helicopter Evacuation Available?
faqs.a: Yes, it is available. Evacution on helicopters are mainly done for severe altitude sickness, injuries and medical emergencies. The guides will make rescue arrangements by coordinating with local authorities, us and the rescue team.

faqs.q: What Are the Required Permits for the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a:
You will need two permits for the Gokyo Valley Trek:

  • Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit
  • The Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit

These permits are required to enter the Khumbu region. Its revenue is mainly used to protect the Himalayan environment and the development and maintenance of the local infrastructure.

faqs.q: Are Permit Fees Included in the Package?
faqs.a: Yes. At Base Camp Adventure, permit fees are included in the package price. In fact, we handle the permit-obtaining process and get the right permits that are required to trek in the Everest Region. Our guides will also help you get your permits verified at different check points along the trail.

faqs.q: What Accommodation Options Are Available During The Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a:
The popular accommodation type during the Gokyo Valley trek is traditional tea houses and lodges. At the teahouses/ lodges, you will get a decent room with a twin bed, blankets, and a communal eating space. 

At high altitudes, facilities are limited. However, tea houses offer a cozy place to stay, enjoy meals and meet other trekkers and enjoy the hospitality on the route.

faqs.q: Are Hot Showers Available Along the Trail?
faqs.a:
Yes. Hot shower facilties are available at most of the teahouses of the Gokyo Valley trekking trail. However, at many teahouses, you have to pay extra for its use. At many high-altitude villages, you may get hot water in a bucket. If you need it, then you may ask it with the owners and they will arrange it accordingly. 

The hot shower's cost ranges from US$ 3 to US$ 12 depending on the altitude. In higher zones,  prices generally increase as fuel or gas is usually transported to remote areas by porters or mules which makes operating costs much higher.

faqs.q: Can I Charge My Phone and Camera at the Teahouses?
faqs.a:
Yes. Tea houses provide charging facilities for mobiles, cameras, and other electronic gadgets. However, charging will cost you extra since the power supply is limited at high altitudes. It can cost around US$ 2 to US$ 6 per device. 

Please carry a power bank and get it fully charged when you get a chance, as it is a reliable backup for your electronic devices when charging facilities are limited at higher elevations.

faqs.q: Is Wi Fi Available in Gokyo Valley Route?
faqs.a:
Most of the tea houses along the Gokyo Valley Trek route offer Wi-Fi services at an extra cost. Usually, the fee increases as the elevation rises due to the rugged terrain, changing weather conditions, and limited infrastructure. 

For a relatively better internet experience, many hikers choose to buy an Everest Link card, which works well in many parts of the Everest area. You can buy these cards at sales stations at Kathmandu, Lukla, Namche Bazaar and Gokyo or at the local lodges where you stay.

faqs.q: What Meals Are Included in Gokyo Valley Trek Package?
faqs.a:
Almost all trek packages include three daily meals. Breakfast, lunch and dinner are served at the tea houses and feature a mix of Nepali and some international cuisines. 

Usually, trekkers have breakfast and dinner in the teahouse where they stay, while lunch is arranged on route at a designated eatery or teahouse.

faqs.q: What Food Options Are Available at the Tea Houses?
faqs.a:
The Everest region is very popular for exploration and trekking. So, you can find wide variety of dishes on the menu. 

Some food options available at the teahouses include roti/chapati, Tibetan bread, eggs, toast, porridge, pancakes, dhindo, sandwiches, burgers, dal bhat, and thukpa. Fried noodles, sherpa stew, chowmein, momo, pasta, veggie soup, spring rolls, garlic soup, potato dishes, vegetable soup, rice and bread.

faqs.q: Can I Find Vegetarian And Vegan Meals Easily During The Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes. Vegetarian as well as vegan dishes are easily available. It will not be difficult for you to find vegetarian dishes on the trail. Typical examples include dal bhat, vegetable fried rice, veggie noodles, soups, potatoes, and curry. 

If you are vegan then inform us in advance, and the tea house owners will modify it accordingly. Most of the dishes are already vegan friendly. Still, make sure to inform us about your dietary restrictions before you start the journey so that we can manage accordingly.

faqs.q: How to Get Safe Drinking Water On the Gokyo Valley Trail?
faqs.a:
You can get safe drinking water on Gokyo Valley Trail. However, you must be careful and choose only boiled and purified water. You should not drink water from natural sources without purification. If you want to drink water from natural sources then make sure to use purification tablets or UV filters.

Even though there are teahouses where you can buy bottled water, it becomes costly with elevation and adds to plastic waste. That's why we highly recommend that you drink boiled or purified water.

faqs.q: How Can I Refill My Water Bottle?
faqs.a:
Refilling your water bottle will be easy on the entire trail. Tea houses provide hot water for drinking at a small fee. You may carry your own reusable water bottle and fill it at the teahouses on the route. 

This is the safest and option and most environmentally friendly option. It lets you stay hydrated and by following this method, you are also reducing the use of single use plastic bottles.

faqs.q: Can I Buy Snacks Along The Trekking Route?
faqs.a:
Yes. You can. Snacks available at the tea houses as well as small shops on the trail. Popular choices include chocolates, biscuits, chips, and energy bars. But everyone’s tastes differ, and you may not always find your favorite brand or snack. 

All supplies are brought to the mountain regions via porters and mules; prices get higher as you trek higher. So, it is wise to carry some of your favorite snacks with you from city area.

faqs.q: Is Travel Insurance Mandatory for the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a: Yes. It is. The exciting Gokyo Valley Trek takes you to different high altitude zones where there are certain risks, such as altitude sickness, trip disruptions and accidents. Having travel insurance is necessary for financial protection against such risks. It gives you peace of mind throughout your trek.

faqs.q: What Should My Travel Insurance Policy Cover?
faqs.a:
For the Gokyo Lake Trek, you will have to purchase a travel insurance plan that will cover medical emergencies, cancellation or interruption of trip, loss or delay in baggage and emergency evacuation.

You should analyze your insurance plan and its inclusions prior to purchasing it to make sure that you are adequately covered from potential risks you may face during your trek.

faqs.q: How Do I Book the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a:
Booking the Gokyo Valley Trek package with us is an easy process. You can directly book from the website. You may open the package page and press the “Book this Trip” option. 

Then, you need to select a suitable departure date for you, pick the number of participants, and fill out the required details in the form. Afterwards, you have to pay the deposit of 30% and your booking will be confirmed.

faqs.q: Can I Get Customized Gokyo Valley Trek Itinerary?
faqs.a:
Yes. You can make adjustments to your Gokyo Valley Trek according to your travel schedule, walking pace and interests. For instance you could add some extra acclimatization days, cross Renjo La Pass and even combine this trek with Everest Base Camp.

If you want to customize the trek, you can make a request and we will craft it accordingly.

faqs.q: What Payment Methods Do You Accept?
faqs.a: We accept deposit payments through credit and debit cards (Visa, American Express, MasterCard, UnionPay and JCB), online payments and bank transfers.

faqs.q: Is Tipping Mandatory?
faqs.a: Tipping is not mandatory. However, it is a very common custom. Usually, trekkers tip around 10 to 15 % of the total trip cost. However, there is no fixed amount for tipping. You may choose the tipping amount based on the service received and your overall experience on the trail.

faqs.q: How Much Should I Budget for Extra Expenses During the Gokyo Valley Trek?
faqs.a:
For the Gokyo Lakes trek you can bring around US$250 to US$350 converted to Nepali rupees to cover for your expenses that are included in your trekking package such as snacks, boiled water, hot showers, souvenirs and others.

There are no reliable ATMs after Lukla and Namche Bazaar along the trail so you will have to take some extra cash with you from Kathmandu.

Shree even arranged a time for us to meet our guide prior to the trek was a great idea and helped us get to know each other a lot better. The trek itself was an amazing experience. We went with a guide and a porter, both of whom were fantastic, they had excellent english, were very knowledgeable about the area and let us do the trek at our own pace and were open to adjusting the itinerary where necessary. The main reason we booked with Base Camp Adventures was due to the price and we found this tour to be fantastic value for money! If you're tossing up whether to include Gokyo in your trek, do it! The side trip was the highlight of our trek - the view of Everest from Gokyo Ri is awesome and the Cho La Pass, while difficult was an incredibly rewarding experience. We would absolutely recommend booking through Base Camp Adventures and if we ever return to Nepal we will definitely be using them again.

reviews.author: thng738-Singapore, Singapore
reviews.body: We are amateur trekkers at best, and this was by far the longest and most physically demanding trek we had been on. For such a daunting challenge, we were extremely fortunate to have been in the experienced and dedicated hands of Base Camp Adventure's guides. Even before the trek, Base Camp Adventure was incredibly responsive to our email queries, and was accommodating of our special requests. Base Camp Adventure's boss, Shree, was also very personable and both received and sent us off to the airport. During the trek, the three guides we had (Jwala, Tika, Bhim) were patient and adjusted our itinerary to suit our walking pace. title: Gokyo Valley with Renjo La Pass Trek
summary: The Gokyo Valley with Renjo La Pass Trek is an ideal choice for those who want to experience the breathtaking beauty of the Everest region while avoiding the busier trekking routes.

seo.title: Gokyo Valley with Renjo La Pass Trek | Itinerary, cost and map
seo.description: The Gokyo Valley with Renjo La Pass Trek is an ideal choice for those who want to experience the breathtaking beauty of the Everest region while avoiding the busier trekking routes.

overview:
Gokyo Valley with Renjo La Pass Trek is the perfect trek for those who want to enjoy the beauty of the Everest region avoiding the busier trails. This trek takes you into the beautiful Gokyo valley, Gokyo lakes, Gokyo Ri, and the high mountain pass of Renjo La (5,360 m), and provides magnificent views of the Khumbu Himalayas including a close view of the world's sixth highest mountain, Cho Oyu (8,188 m).

Gokyo Valley with Renjo La Pass Trek starts with fly to one of the most dangerous airports in the world situated in Lukla. The flight to Lukla provides wonderful views of the landscapes and the high mountains. From Lukla, you begin the trek to Phakding and then to Namche Bazaar. You enter Sagarmatha National Park and follow the Dudh Koshi River as you make your way to Namche Bazaar, the main trading hub of Khumbu region .

After resting in Namche, the journey takes you to Gokyo Valley. Gokyo Valley is famous for its delightful turquoise lakes which lie on the foot of the snow-capped mountains. Ngozumpa Glacier, the largest glacier of Nepal, and Gokyo Ri vantage point (5,360 m) are two of the major attractions of Gokyo Valley. From the top of Gokyo Ri, you can see Everest (8,848 m), Cho Oyu (8,188 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), and many other snow-capped peaks.

Another main feature of this trek is the traverse through the frozen mountain pass of Renjo La (5,360 m), which provides the equally enchanting view of the Khumbu Himalayas. If you travel in monsoon season, you can witness the flowers pop out in Nagpala, giving you an illusion of walking on textured carpet. Gokyo Renjola Pass Trek is a beautiful Himalayan journey guaranteed to give you memories to last a lifetime.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Tribhuwan International Airport (TIA), Kathmandu and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: The trip begins with your arrival in Kathmandu. Our team representative will welcome you at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA), and from there, you will be taken to the hotel for your overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft) and then same day trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: Today early morning the van will pick you up for the departure to Lukla. A forty minute spectacular flight will take you to Lukla. After a brief rest, the trek begins. You start the trek with a descent to Dudh Koshi River and follow the wider trail to the village of Ghat, and then you will make an easy uphill walk to Phakding. Overnight in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail leads you to Namche Bazaar as you ascend alongside Dudh Koshi River. You can see the first glimpse of Everest (8,848 m) as you cross Hillary Bridge. Then you pass through the village of Jorsalle to reach Namche Bazaar. Namche Bazaar is a Sherpa town serving as the commercial hub of Khumbu region and is also known as the gateway to Everest. Overnight in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar (33,440 m / 11,286 ft).
itinerary.html: In order to avoid altitude sickness, it is very important to get adjusted to the climate of high altitude. You will spend the day in Namche Bazaar and explore its outskirts. Check out the Sherpa Museum for an overview of the Sherpa culture and history of mountaineering. The nearby Thame village is also worth checking out. Hat Bazaar, the local marketplace, is open for trading on Saturdays. It is part of the larger Namche Bazaar, a shopping hub for all manners of trekking and mountaineering clothing and equipment. Overnight in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Dole (4,200 m / 13,780 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: You ascend Mongla Hills and head downwards to Phortse Tanga. Then follow the path upwards through rhododendron and birch forests as the peak of Cho Oyu (8,188 m) starts to appear in the horizon. Reach Dhole after an easy climb through the forested trail. Overnight in Dole.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dole to Machhermo (4,470 m / 14,665 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: Today’s trek is short and pleasant. The day starts with a climb over Dhole via a scenic ridge. Crossing yak pastures and the tiny village of stone huts, you will reach Luza. Follow the trail along the valley high over the river to reach Machhermo by midday. You will have a stunning view of various snow-capped mountains throughout the day that gets even more beautiful from Machhermo. Overnight in Machhermo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Machharmo to Gokyo (4,790 m / 15,715 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: Ascend the hill and you can enjoy the views of Dudh Koshi Valley and Mt Cho Oyu (8,188 m). The valley widens beyond the ridge and the trail passes through a Chorten and reaches Phangga. Then you descend to the river and climb up to terminal moraine of Ngozumpa Glacier on a steep trail. Pass two Gokyo lakes before arriving at the third one, the holy lake named Dudh Pokhari, behind which the rugged Gokyo village is located. Overnight in Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Day trip from Gokyo Village to Gokyo Ri / Gokyo Peak (5,357 m / 17,575 ft).
itinerary.html: Climb Gokyo Ri (5,360 m), a hill that rises above the northern shore of Dudh Pokhari. From the top, you can admire the Khumbu Himalayas, the tranquil Gokyo lakes, and Nepal's largest glacier—Ngozumpa Glacier. Then you hike to the fourth Gokyo Lake. There is a spot called Scoundrel's Viewpoint from where you can get super excellent views of Everest (8,848 m), Cho Oyu (8,188 m), Lhotse (8,414 m), and other peaks. After the hike, you return back to Gokyo and take rest. Overnight in Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gokyo to Renjo La Pass and continue to Lumde (4,380 m / 14,370 ft), 5–6 hours.
itinerary.html: The trek kicks off at dawn and will pass through Renjo La Pass (5,360 m). Follow the Gokyo Valley downward, depart from the main trail, and turn towards the pass. You will reach the top of Renjo La after a careful climb through on a frozen trail amid glacier. From the top, you will get an unforgettable view of the Khumbu Himalayas. Then descend carefully and follow the trail on the east bank of Bhote Khosi River to reach Lunde. Overnight in Lunde.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lumde to Thame and continue to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: The trek route from Lumde to Thame follows a traditional route used by the Tibetan traders for centuries. Cross Bhote Khosi River and then descend to Taranga. The trail then winds through Bhote Koshi River ending in Thame village. Visit Thame Monastery, one of the largest monasteries in the Khumbu region. Pass through a check post today before arriving at the world’s uppermost hydropower station which provides electricity for most of the upper Khumbu region. You will pass prayer flags, Mani walls, Gompas, Chortens, and beautiful Sherpa settlements en route to Namche Bazzar. Overnight in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Cross the Hillary Suspension Bridge and pass through several local villages. In about 2 and a half hours, you will arrive in Jorsalle. Then trek down further, crossing bridges to reach Phakding. Lunch will be in Phakding, and from there, trek up and down the hill for 2 hours to reach Lukla. Overnight in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu, (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html: After a good breakfast, take the flight from Lukla to Kathmandu. Enjoy the view of the Himalayas from above. Upon landing, you will be picked up by our company ca or van and taken to the hotel. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Transfer to the Kathmandu Int’l airport for your onward journey
itinerary.html: Transfer to the airport by private vehicle three hours prior to your scheduled flight.

seo.description: Explore sacred Gosaikunda Lake, stunning Himalayan landscapes, lush forests, and traditional mountain villages on this Gosainkunda and Helambu.

overview:
In the heart of the Asia, Nepal offers some of the world’s best hiking and trekking opportunities. Characterized by picturesque mountain villages and dramatic peaks, the country also boosts some of the world’s finest lakes. Due to varied geographical structure of Nepal, a trekker can do a short trek which only take a day to complete, to the longest trek up to 35 days. One of such treks which takes 8 days to complete yet provides you the opportunity to experience Hindu and Tibetan culture complemented with mesmerising Mountain View and wide range of flora and faunas is Gosainkunda Helambu Trek.

Gosainkunda Helambu Trek is a classical and exciting trekking destination for all adventure aspirants all over the world. It is an amazing trekking opportunity to explore the ancient villages with a wide range of animals like Red Panda, Musk Deer, Himalayan Thar, Black Bear, Common Langur and delightful Himalayan scenery of Langtang Lirung, Gaurishankar, Yala Peak and many other along with wonder Tibetan Sherpa culture. The fascinating view of tiny lakes with icebergs floating on them and water of crystalline brightness makes the Helambu Trek even more interesting. This region is also very famous for sweet apples and artistic Buddhist Monasteries.

This ideal adventure for those who have limited time to explore the entire region, starts in Kathmandu itself. The normal trailhead starts off at Sundarijal, a small dam and hydroelectricity station in the north-east corner of Kathmandu Valley. After an hour walk, we enter the Shivapuri National Park that is rich in various floras and faunas. The ridge in Shivapuri offers striking views of Shivapuri Mountain and other Himalayan ranges as well. Following a ridge-line the trek heads off Thare Pati before turning east to Melamchi Gaon and Tarke Gyang, the principle villages of this area. Finally, the trek ends at the Melamchi Pul Bazar in Helambu region from where we then drive back to Kathmandu.

The Gosainkunda Helambu Trek not only offers you remarkable alpine scenery in one hand, but also provides an opportunity to experience old Tibetan culture followed by the Sherpa people residing in Helambu Region of Nepal for centuries in the other. This trek also surprises you with the magnificence of its natural beauty and wonderful climate with outstanding view of snow-covered mountains.

So, a visit to the Helambu region offers you tremendous opportunities to explore villages, to climb small peaks and to visit glorious glaciers at a comfortably low elevation. If you are an adventurous person who loves being in the lap of nature and is always eager to gain new knowledge and experience, then trekking in Helambu region is the best option for you.  Whether you are an experienced trekker or a first timer, with the company of our magnificent crew, you are sure to have one memorable and rewarding trip of your life. Thus, feel blessed with exciting landscapes and amazing flora and fauna filled exploration, that comes only once in a life time.

seo.description: Island Peak Climbing is one of the most climbing destinations in Nepal. As the peak resembles an island in a sea of ice when viewed from Dingboche,

overview:
Island Peak  climbing (Imja Tse) is one of the most famous climbing destinations in Nepal. It stands in the Everest Region, reaches a height of 6,189 m and is popularly known as Island Peak, a name given to it by Eric Shipton’s party in 1951, as the peak resembles an island in a sea of ice when viewed from Dingboche. Later in 1983, the peak was given the Nepali name Imja Tse. The Island peak was first ascended in 1953 by a British team as part of their preparations for climbing Everest. Tenzing Norgay was one of the members of the first ascent team. The peak is actually part of the south ridge of Lhotse Shar and forms a semicircle of cliffs that rise to the north of Nuptse, Lhotse, Middle Peak and Lhotse Shar.

In order to acclimatize prior to climbing Island Peak (20,305ft/6,189 m), we offer a trek through the Himalayan Khumbu. Island Peak Climbing expedition offers wonderful trekking through the glorious Khumbu region and any fit enthusiast is welcome to join the team. All team members will have the opportunity to summit Kala Pattar (18,187ft/5,545 m), a wonderful location to view and photograph Mt. Everest, and then we head for a visit to Everest Base Camp. While climbing team members make the summit attempt of Island Peak, trekking only team members will spend 2-3 days walking in the stunning valleys around Island Peak.

Island Peak Climbingalso walks you through the countryside, where you partake in Nepalese and Tibetan cultures as they have existed for centuries. The journey offers some of the most striking scenery in the Khumbu via the enchanting village of Dingboche. This trek is filled with Buddhist shrines and this village of stone charms your path to the mountains. The summit of Island Peak stands adjacent to the South Face of Lhotse, one of the world’s largest ice walls, and offers stunning views of beautiful Ama Dablam and Makalu. It is an excellent opportunity to participate in and fully experience a Himalayan mountain climbing expedition

title: Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek
summary: Experience the adventure of a lifetime with our Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek. Discover the rich Sherpa culture, and the majestic beauty of the Himalayas.

seo.title: Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek | Itinerary, Guide, Map and Cost
seo.description: Experience the adventure of a lifetime with our Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek. Discover the rich Sherpa culture, and the majestic beauty of the Himalayas.

map.alt: Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek Map

overview:
Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek is one of the most rewarding and adventurous Himalayan journeys, beginning in the lower Solukhumbu region and following the historic trail to Everest Base Camp. Unlike the classic Everest Base Camp Trek, which typically starts with a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla, the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek takes you through a longer and more traditional route that offers a deeper connection with the Himalayan landscape, local communities, and mountain culture.

This historic trail follows the footsteps of legendary mountaineers Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay Sherpa, who used the Jiri route during their historic 1953 expedition to Mount Everest. Trekking to Everest Base Camp via Jiri allows you to experience sections of one of Nepal's original trekking routes before joining the main Everest trekking trail. The journey combines peaceful lower-hill trails, traditional villages, lush forests, dramatic mountain scenery, and the iconic landscapes of the Khumbu region.

Beginning at a lower elevation, the trek provides a gradual approach to the high Himalayas while passing through culturally diverse communities. Along the route, you can encounter people from different ethnic groups, including Rai, Tamang, Newar, Thakali, and Sherpa communities. Their traditional lifestyles, Buddhist monasteries, prayer wheels, chortens, and welcoming mountain villages add an authentic cultural dimension to the adventure.

The Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek is an excellent choice for trekkers seeking a longer and more immersive Himalayan experience away from the standard Lukla route. It combines natural beauty, rich cultural heritage, challenging mountain trails, and breathtaking Himalayan scenery, making it a memorable journey for those who want to experience the Everest region in a more traditional way.

Best Time for Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek

The best seasons for the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek are spring, from March to May, and autumn, from September to November. During these months, the weather is generally stable, the skies are clearer, and the trekking conditions are more favorable, making them ideal for a long Himalayan journey.

Spring is one of the most beautiful seasons to trek from Jiri to Everest Base Camp. The lower valleys and forested trails become lush and vibrant, while rhododendrons and other Himalayan flowers add spectacular colors to the landscape. The pleasant temperatures and generally favorable weather make spring an excellent time for trekking. It is also a great season for enjoying Nepal's diverse flora, wildlife, and birdlife along the lower sections of the trail.

Autumn is another excellent season for the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek and is widely considered one of the best periods for trekking in Nepal. Following the monsoon, the atmosphere becomes clear and the mountain views are often spectacular. The trails are generally dry, the temperatures are comfortable, and the stable weather provides excellent conditions for long trekking days. Autumn also offers opportunities to experience local festivals and cultural celebrations, adding another memorable element to the journey.

Although spring and autumn are the most popular trekking seasons, the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek can also be undertaken during other months with proper preparation. However, winter can bring very cold temperatures and snow at higher elevations, while the summer monsoon season can bring rain, muddy trails, clouds, and reduced mountain visibility.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu and hotel transfer
itinerary.html: After your arrival at the Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA), the representative from base Camp Adventure will receive you at the terminal. After assisting you with the luggage, our staff will transfer you to a private vehicle, and you will enjoy a smooth ride to your hotel located at the core of the capital.

itinerary.title: Driving from Kathmandu to Jiri to Bhandar (2,190 m / 7,185 ft), 8 to 9 hours.
itinerary.html:
Bhandar Elevation: 2,190 m
Elevation Gain: 790 m

Your exciting adventure on this will start with a thrilling and scenic drive from Kathmandu to Jiri. You will start your thrilling drive on the Arankuko Highway, and on the driving route, you will also move past the beautiful Newar settlements of Banepa and Dhulikhel during the first part. Although the drive is slightly long, driving past the lush forested trails, terraced farms, and traditional settlements, enjoying the epic views of eastern Himalayan mountains such as Ganesh Himala, Dorje Lakpa, Langtang Lirung will make the drive feel shorter.

As the trail switches, the driveway descends down to Panchkhal and then again ascends to Dolalghat, from where you will follow the trails alongside the Sun Koshi River to reach Lamasangu. After passing several traditional further ahead, you will then arrive at Jiri; a short drive up ahead will then take you to Bhandar.

itinerary.title: Trekking from Bhandar to Sete Village (2,575 m / 8,448 feet), 4 to 5 hours
itinerary.html:
Sete Village Elevation: 2,575 m
Elevation Gain: 385 m

This is the first day of trekking in this traditional Everest Base Camp Trek route. After a warm breakfast at Bhandar, you will first follow the trekking trail that drops down to the bank of Lunkhu Khola. Then, you will cross the river to reach Kenja Village from where you will take on the steep section to reach Chimbu Village. You will continue trekking on the gradually inkling route across the terraced farms and farmhouses to reach Sete Village. This small Sherpa village is situated on a ridge in the middle of the rhododendron forest, and you will be able to enjoy incredible views of the surrounding mountains.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sete to Junbesi via Lamjura Pass (2,700 m / 8,858 ft), 6 to 7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Junbesi Village Elevation: 2,700 m
Lamjura Pass Elevation: 3,530 m
Elevation Gain: 955 m

It's an exciting part of the trek on this traditional route; you will trek across the beautiful rhododendron, Mongolia, and birch forest that cover the Solukhumbu region and head toward the Lamjura Pass. This thrilling Himalayan pass is the highest point between the Jiri and Namche Bazaar routes, and it will take you about 3 hours to complete this part of the trek. You will also be able to catch the incredible view of Mt. Everest for the first time from this pass.

Then, after descending from the pass, you will follow the steep trail for about an hour and a half to reach Taktor Village. You will continue walking on the north side of the valley and follow the descending trail to reach the charming Sherpa village of Junbesi.

itinerary.title: Trek from Junbesi to Nunthala (2,440 m / 8,005 ft), 5 to 6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Nunthala Elevation: 2,440 m
Elevation Loss: 260 m / 853 ft

From Junbesu, you will follow the descending trail below the village and cross the Jubesi Khola over a wooden bridge. After crossing the bridge, you will come across a junction point, and you will see the path on the left leads to Khumbu Valley to the north. Moving further ahead, you will then make your descent to Sailung Village and move along the lush trails of the Dudh Koshi River.

In this exhilarating section, you will pass through the popular Sherpa settlement of Ringmo Village and then take on the Tak Shindo Pass before switching to the path across dense forest. Moving further in your trail, you will cross several mountain streams on the wooden bridges to reach Nunthal Village which is also known as Manidingma.

itinerary.title: Trek from Nunthala to Khari Khola Village, (2,020 m / 6,627 ft), 5 to 6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Khari Khola Elevation: 2,020 m
Elevation Loss: 420 m

This day’s trek will take you across the terraced farmlands of the Rai and Sherpa villages. Leaving Nunthala Village after a warm breakfast, you will continue following the banks of the Dudh Koshi River. Most part of this day’s trail is well-defined, although it sometimes does pass through the yards of houses and terraced fields. The trail further ahead passes across the forests and descends to Chautara, which overlooks the cascading river.

You will then continue to follow the flow of the river and climb across the terraced farmlands to reach the beautiful Rai settlement of Jubing. After crossing the village, you will then follow the ridge and head toward the Khari Khola, your resting destination tonight.

itinerary.title: Trek from Khari Khola Village to Surkhe, (2,230 m / 7,316 ft) 5 to 6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Surkhe Elevation: 2,230 m
Elevation Gain: 210 m / 688 ft

After leaving Khari Khola, you will start your trek following the steep hill of the Buspa Danda. From here, you will continue following the ascending route toward the Bhumsing Village and trek across the tributary valley of lush oak and rhododendron forests. On the next part, the trail descends across the valley for about an hour on the north side, which then leads you to Puiyan Village.

You will then continue following the trail on the ridge and head toward the Surkha Village, which is situated on top of the tributary river of Dudh Koshi. This will be the last thrilling trekking adventure in this traditional route as you will me joining the mainstream path on the next day.

itinerary.title: Trek from Surkhe to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,562 ft), 4 to 5 hours.
itinerary.html:
Phakding Elevation: 2,610 m
Elevation Gain: 380 m

It's a short but exciting day’s trek today; after enjoying a warm breakfast at Surkhe Village, you will trek through rhododendron and oaks forests and small Sherpa settlements. Encircling the path above Surkha, the trail then leaves the tributary valley and heads toward the Chaurikharka Village. From this beautiful Sherpa village, you will continue trekking on the banks of the Dudh Koshi River and cross Dudh Koshi Ghat before reaching Phakding Village.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 5 - 6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m
Elevation Gain: 830 m

This is one of the most scenic parts of this base camp trek. After enjoying your breakfast at Phakding Village, you will then walk on the trail through the pine forest that stretches toward the north side of the Benkar Valley. After crossing the Dudh Koshi River, you will then trek past the Chumoa Village to reach Monjo, the entrance to the Sagarmatha National Park. After getting your permits checked here, you will then continue along the trail and cross a suspension bridge to reach Jorsale Village.

After crossing the bridge, you will then continue trekking on the riverbanks of both Dudh Koshi and Bhote Koshi. During the final part, you will follow the steep trail of the Namche Ukalo to reach the beautiful Sherpa capital. This day’s trail will unveil the first-ever epic views of Mt. Everest, and you will also be able to admire the beauty of surrounding peaks like Nuptse and Lhotse after reaching Namche.

itinerary.title: Rest day at Namche or day hike to Khunde and Khumjung Village (3,840 m / 12,598 ft)
itinerary.html:
Khunde Village Elevation: 3,840 m
Khumjung Village Elevation: 3,790 m
Elevation Gain: 400 m

After a long journey on the traditional route and climbing to significant altitudes, on this day, you will take a rest day. You will take this day to acclimatize properly to the rising altitude and do a morning hike to Khunde and Khumjug Village. Both of these villages are beautiful Sherpa settlements that have preserved the ancient culture, traditions, and norms to this date. From these high-altitude villages, you will also be able to enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding peaks such as Everest, Thamserku, Nuptse, Lhotse, Ama Dablam, Cholaste, Taboche, and others.

During the day, you can explore the other popular highlights of Namche Bazaar, such as the Sherpa Museum, Sagarmatha National Park Museum, Everest View Hotel, Hillary School, etc.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche to Tengboche Monastery (3,860 m/ 12,664 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Tengboche Monastery Elevation: 3,860 m
Elevation Gain: 420 m

After letting your body properly rest and taking time with the acclimatization, its time to head further in your iconic Himalayan journey. From Namche, following the uphill, downhill, and gentle flat trail on the ridge line, you will head toward the Kyangjuma Village. From here, you will continue trekking on the charming trails of Dudh Koshi Valley, enjoying the stunning beauty of Ama Dablam, Lhotse, Everest, and Taboche to reach Phunki Thenga.

You will take your lunch break here enjoying the beautiful scenery, and after lunch, you will trek on an uphill trail through lush forests to reach Tengboche Monastery. This beautiful Buddhist monastery is of significant value and is even considered the spiritual hub of the Khumbu Valley.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche (4,360 m / 14,304 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Dingboche Elevation: 4,360 m
Elevation Gain: 500 m

This day’s exciting trail passes through the beautiful birch, confer, and rhododendron forests with spectacular mountain views on the backdrop. During the first part of this day’s trek, you will move along the descending trail toward the Debuche Village and cross the Imja River to reach another beautiful Sherpa village of Pangbohce. You will then take a break at this beautiful traditional Sherpa village before following the winding-up trail that stretches toward the Somare Village.

At the Somare, the path heading further divides into two sections; one leads to the Pheriche Village, and another one will take you to Dingboche Village. You will follow the gentle uphill trail to the Imja Valley and cross the Lobuche River to reach Dingboche. This charming high-altitude Sherpa village is popular stone-fenced farmlands where villages mostly grow buckwheat, barely, and potato.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day at Dingboche and optional hike to Chhukung Ri (5,546 meters/ 18,195 feet).
itinerary.html:
Chhukung Ri Elevation: 5,546 m
Elevation Gain: 1,186 m

By this day, you have crossed the alpine zone, and the next part of the route will take you to the trans-Himalayan zone. Thus, before switching the climatic zone, you will take another rest day here in order to adapt to the new altitude and give your body enough rest. For the acclimatizing hike, there is an option to hike to Chhukung Ri. You can also hike to the Nangkartshang Hill (5,100 m), which is another popular hiking destination on this acclimatization day.

Both of these amazing viewpoints will reward you with breathtaking views of the mountain ranges, such as Island Peak, Lhotse Shar, Taboche, Ama Dablam, Cholastee, Baruntse, Thamseku, and other surrounding peaks. After the hike, you can just stroll around the village, checking out the local culture, traditions, and lifestyle.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche (4,940 m / 16,174 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Lobuche Elevation: 4,940 me / 16,174 ft
Elevation Gain: 570 m

After enjoying a warm breakfast at Dingboche, you will continue to push toward the higher altitude points of this mainstream route. You will follow the trails on the ridgeline, enjoying the views of the towering peaks over the Pheriche Valley. After trekking past the Dusa, you will move along the descending and curbing trails to cross a mountain stream and follow the uphill trail to reach Dughla Village. You will head toward the memorial shrine of the Dughla Pass, where people pray for the lost souls during the Everest expedition.

Moving further in your trail, you will traverse across the boulder-strewn segment and make you ascend to Chupki Lhara. Enjoying the epic mountain views from this ridge, you will then trek along the trail decorated with prayer flags and chortens. The path then drops to the moraines of the Khumbu Glacier, enjoying the up-close views of Lingtren, Pumori, Khumbutse, and Mahalangur Himal; you will then head toward Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lobuche (4,940 m / 16,207 ft) to Gorakshep (5,140 m / 16,864 ft), then continue to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m / 17,598 ft). After exploring Everest Base Camp, trek back to Gorakshep for an overnight stay. 7–8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Gorakshep Elevation: 5,160 m
Everest Base Camp Elevation: 5,364 m
Elevation Gain: 434 m

Today is a grand day in this Himalayan adventure; after enjoying your breakfast at Lobuche, you will head toward the main objective of this trek. Following the ascending and descending trail alongside the lateral moraines of the glacier, you will first head toward Gorakshep. You will leave your luggage at your designated teahouse, then continue trekking toward the Everest Base Camp alongside the moraines. After reaching the Everest Base Camp, you will take your time to relish the magical ambiance of the world’s highest peak at its foothills.

The base camp is surrounded by mountains and massive glaciers; you will be able to enjoy the incredible views of Khumbutse, Nuptse, Pumori, Lingtren, and others from the Everest Base Camp. After soaking in the incredible Himalayan atmosphere, you will then make your descent back to Gorakshep for an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Morning hike to Kala Patthar and trek back to Pangboche (3,985 m / 13,074 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Kala Patthar Elevation: 5,644 m
Pangboche Elevation: 3,985 m
Elevation Gain: 484 m

As you will not be able to enjoy a wide mountain view from the base of the towering peaks, on this day, you will do an early morning hike to Kala Patthar. This is the most popular viewpoint in the Khumbu Valley, and from here, the panoramic views of the mountain ranges, such as Everest, Changtse, Nuptse, Lhotse, Thamserku, Ama Dablam, Pumori, Lhotse, and others are simply spectacular.

Then, after the morning hike, you will return back to Gorakshep for breakfast and follow the descending route toward Pangboche across Lobuche, Thukla, and Pheriche villages.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pangboche to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m
Elevation Loss: 545 m

From the Pangboche Village, you will descend to lower altitudes on the same iconic trail heading toward Namche Bazaar. After leaving Pangboche Village, you will re-enter the spiritual atmosphere of the Tengboche Monastery and further descend down to the lush trail of the Dudh Koshi Valley. Follow the uphill and downhill trail below the treeline, you will cross Phunki Thenga and the Kyangjuma to return back to Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,186 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Lukla Elevation: 2,860 m
Elevation Loss: 640 m

On the descending part of the trail, you will continue to trek down to Lukla, the gateway of Everest from Namche Bazaar. As the first part of this trek took the traditional driving route, you skipped the landing at this starting point of the Everest region. After enjoying your breakfast at Namche, you will continue trekking on the side of the Dudh Koshi River and trek past Monjo, Phakding, and Chaurikharka Village to reach Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu (35-40 minutes).
itinerary.html: Unlike the roadway during the initial part of the trek, where you drove from Kathmandu to Jiri to Bhandar, you will take a more conventional transport option for your return back to Kathmandu. You will fly to TIA from the Tenzing Hillary Airport at Lukla to conclude this remarkable Himalayan journey. Your morning flight that takes off from Lukla will reward you with incredible views of the Himalayan peaks, and you will fly over the lush valleys to reach Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for international departure
itinerary.html:
Kathmandu Elevation: 1,400 m

After your long Himalayan journey, it is time to bid farewell to this remarkable Himalayan country. Representatives from Base Camp Adventure will assist you with the checkout procedure and take you to TIA for your flight. We hope that you enjoyed this traditional Himalayan trekking opportunity with us. We hope to see you again. Have a safe journey.

sections.title: Useful Info
sections.html:
Who Can Do Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek?

Compared to the standard Everest Base Camp Trek, which generally lasts around 15 days, the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek is a slightly longer venture, which has a length of 21 days. So, even if this classical trekking route is slightly longer than the modern-day standard route, the difficulty level of Everest Base Camp via Jiri is at a moderate level. From the acclimatization prospects, this traditional route is, in fact, much easier as you will gradually follow the inclining route going through an effective acclimatization procedure. From the physical demand prospects, the trail can be slightly challenging as it lasts for three weeks. So, without proper physical preparation, taking on such a long-haul trek won’t be easy. The gradual ascend will make the acclimatization process much easier, but you will still need to trek to significant altitudes during the trek. In this 21-day exploration of this mainstream trekking destination via the traditional route, you will cover an approximate trekking distance of around 205 km (127 miles). Similarly, from the starting point of the trek on this classical route, Bhandar (2,190 m), all the way to the highest point of the trek, Kala Patthar (5,644 m), the total elevation gain is around 3,454 m (11,332 feet). So, neither the total trekking distance nor the overall altitude gain in this trek should be underestimated. Thus, this trek is recommended for trekkers with some prior experience in high-altitude explorations and with enough time on hand to set out on the long Himalayan adventure.

How to Prepare for Everest Base Camp From Jiri?

Despite having a lengthy trekking trail, the preparation for the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek is not so different from regular high-altitude adventures. For the moderately difficult nature of this classical route, a standard 3 to 6 weeks of preparation will be quite sufficient if you have a basic level of fitness. If you exercise regularly, you don’t have to put in much effort during the preparation part. The trails aren’t strenuous like a mountain climb, nor will you need to overcome any technical sections. Thus, with good health, basic fitness, and a few weeks of light preparation, it won’t be that much of a challenge to take on the trekking trails of this Classic Everest Base Camp Trek From Jiri. For the preparation part, the main focus of your training should be working on your strength and endurance level. As you will be trekking for long days, covering significant trekking distances at rising altitudes, you will need to improve both of these aspects. You can test out your endurance level with practice hikes by carrying a backpack with reasonable weight on the steep section nearby. Similarly, stamina and cardiovascular exercises are equally important; not only do they improve your overall stamina reserve, but they also make the acclimatization process much easier.

What Makes This Trek So Special?

The standard Everest Base Camp Trek is undoubtedly one of the most renowned trekking routes across the world. This thrilling Himalayan journey that takes you to the base of the tallest mountain in the world is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. Even if the journey to the summit of the wondrous marvel of earth is a demanding endeavor traveling to immersive into its radiating ambiance is an exciting adventure for everyone. Distinct from the regular mainstream trekking route, this trek starts from the very base of the Everest region. You will be able to explore the path that the first ascenders of the tallest peak in the world took, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, for their first expedition in 1953. Unlike the standard trek that starts directly with a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla, on this traditional route, you will have the opportunity to experience diversity in the culture and landscape as you start from the lower regions. You will also

Travel Insurance

Travel Insurance is very important if you are setting out on a long adventure, especially more so if you are doing a high-altitude trek. Travel insurance takes care of medical needs, delays, loss of belongings, accidents and injuries, etc. For high-altitude treks such as this Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek, travel insurance also covers emergency evacuation operations. So, getting travel insurance will not only take care of several unforeseen circumstances during your trek, but it will also boost your confidence, and you will be able to enjoy the exploration feeling more assured. There are several types of travel insurance that you can get for Classic Everest Base Camp Trek From Jiri. Most standard insurance plans provide coverage upto 3,000 m and cost around US$ 30 to US$ 100. Similarly, with the slightly extensive package that offers coverage plans upto 6,000 m, the cost starts at US$ 100. If you want ti include the helicopter rescue operation coverage in your travel insurance, the starting cost for such a plan is around US$ 3,000.

Altitude Sickness

The altitude gain in Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek is quite significant. Thus, it is natural to worry about the risk of altitude sickness during your trek. From the trekking start point, Bhandar, to the highest point of the trek, Kala Patthar, the overall altitude gain is around 3,454 m (11,332 feet). So, an effective acclimatization process is very important to mitigate the risk of altitude sickness during the trek. As you don’t have to ascend on the alpine slopes, Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) is the only risk on the trail and not other severe forms of altitude sickness such as High Altitude Cerebral Edema (HACE) and High Altitude Pulmonary Edema (HAPE). AMS is a light form of altitude sickness that can be treated easily and prevented with good rest and a proper acclimatization process. The Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek itinerary plans of Base Camp Adventure have been designed with the help of industry-leading experts and veteran trek guides. Our trekking package follows a slow and gradual ascent, providing the trekkers the opportunity to adapt to the rising altitude even on the trekking trail. Similarly, each day’s trek route is carefully designed, and you will get enough breaks along the route. On top of that, we have also included enough acclimatization days so you can properly follow the effective acclimatization process and don’t have to push your body to its limit.

Packing for Trek

Packing for the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek will mostly depend on which season you are doing this trek. If your adventure date is set for any of the high seasons, such as spring or autumn, you will not have to bring any additional gear to tackle the weather challenges. Just the right layers for different climatic zones, from tropical to trans-Himalayan, and some useful gear will be enough to make your journey a memorable and comfortable experience. However, if you are planning this trek in any of the off-seasons, such as monsoon and winter, you will need to sort out your packing for the season-specific climate. For the monsoon season that sees continuous downpours, you will have to prioritize the waterproof outer layers, bagge coverage, and raincoats. As the trails are slippery and muddy, to navigate across them comfortably, you will need to have footwear with good traction. Similarly, for the winter season, the layers and gear to keep yourself warm in this coldest month of the mountain should be your top priority. Insulated or heated boots, thick-warm layers, micro spikes to walk over snow, ski goggles, portable heaters, etc., are some packing considerations for the Everest Base Camp From Jiri during the winter exploration. faqs.q: How far is Jiri to Everest Base Camp?
faqs.a: The total trekking distance you will cover during the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek is approximately 205 km(127 miles).

faqs.q: How long to trek from Jiri to Lukla?
faqs.a: The standard duration of the Classic Everest Base Camp Trek From Jiri is around 21 days. The overall duration of the trek can be shorter or longer depending on the itinerary plans, rest days, highlights explorations, etc.

faqs.q: Is Mount Everest visible from Jiri?
faqs.a: Although Mount Everest is not clearly visible from Jiri, as you proceed further in the trekking route from the village, Lamjura Pass, will reward you with the stunning views of the tallest peak in the world.

faqs.q: How long to trek from Jiri to Lukla?
faqs.a: From Jiri, it will take approximately 5 days to reach Lukla, the trekking trail will stretch from Surkhe Village to Phakding via Chaurikharka Village.

faqs.q: Can a beginner do Everest Base Camp via Jiri?
faqs.a: The standard Everest Base Camp trek is also recommended to beginner trekkers as sufficient training will make it easy to traverse across the physically demanding route. Similarly, beginners can also take part in the long route Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek if they are confident about their physical capabilities.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to do Everest Base Camp From Jiri?
faqs.a: The standard duration of the Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek is around 21 to 24 days, and the cost margin of the package for the standard duration trek is around US$ 1,500 to US$ 2,500.

faqs.q: Can I do Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek without training?
faqs.a: Technically, yes, you could do Everest Base Camp From Jiri without training but it's really a bad idea. This high-altitude journey is a physically demanding endeavor, and if you are not well prepared, the journey can be physically exhausting.

title: Jomsom Muktinath Trek
summary: Jomsom Muktinath Trek is kind of trekking experience to a place far from modernity, no any stress of any pollution and a totally classic trek.

seo.title: Jomsom Muktinath Trek | cost | Itinerary | Reviews | Base Camp Adventure
seo.description: Jomsom Muktinath Trek is kind of trekking experience to a place far from modernity, no any stress of any pollution and a totally classic trek.

overview:
Jomsom Muktinath Trek is an exciting journey that goes through the world’s deepest gorge of Kali Gandaki River into world’s highest regions via almost tree- less barren land; a steep rocky trail up and down hill. Throughout the journey, you can have the dramatic views of mountains like Mt. Dhaulagiri, Mt. Annapurna south, I, Mt.Nilgiri, Mt. Annapurna II, Annapurna III, Mt. Annapurna IV, Mt. Hiunchuli, Mt. Machhapuchhre, Tukuche peak and many more.

This magnificent trek initiates after an hour drive from Pokhara to Nayapul. A short trek along the bank of Modi Khola, leads you to a small village called Birethanti and as you climb the winding stone paved trail, you get noteworthy looks of beautiful Machhapuchree Mountain. This trek then leads you to Poon Hill via Ghorepani for appreciating the glory of fabulous sunrise and sunset form amidst the peaks of awe inspiring mountains.

Jomsom Muktinath Trek is not just a trek that is famous for its jaw dropping sceneries but for Muktinath temple as well. This temple situated at the height of 3,750 m holds a very high value among the Hindu and Buddhist Pilgrimages. Thousands of devotees from all over the world make their journey to this ‘Land of Salvation’ every year and take bath under ice cold water of 108 waterspouts, “Muktidhara”, considering that it brings them salvation. From Muktinath you can enjoy amazing scenery around with  your quality time in this fully pristine land.

This amazing Jomsom Muktinath trek offers you to experience variety of changes in dramatic way within a few hours walking distance. Diversity of flora and fauna, landscape, culture and climate within few hours of walking distance makes your journey very exciting. Along with that you can communicate with the local Thakali people living on the trail for centuries and know more about them, their ancient tradition, interesting stories and amazing faiths.

The final days of this trekking will be spent in the delightful and lovely villages like Jomsom, Kaghbeni and Marpha where you get chance to further interact with the locals.  After which you will return to Pokhara, appreciating the last views of the Mountains and the local people

itinerary.title: Arrival at Kathmandu (1,400 m / 4,593 ft) and Transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: After your arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA), Kathmandu, you will be met by our airport representative who will then transfer you to the hotel. Later, you can roam the streets of Kathmandu and observe the activities of the local people. Overnight at a 3-star hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara (820 m / 2,690 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: A tourist bus ride to Pokhara will initiate the lovely day that has been waiting for you. You follow Trishuli and Marsayangdi Rivers on the picturesque Prithvi Highway to reach the amazing lake city. Upon reaching Pokhara, feel free to explore the beautiful lakeside area and enjoy the view of Machhapuchhre (6,997 m). You can enjoy cycle riding, boating, and other fun activities in Pokhara. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Drive to Nayapul (1,010 m / 3,314 ft) and trek to Ulleri (1,920 m / 6,299 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: It will be a short drive from Pokhara to Nayapul, the starting point of the trek. Ascend along the trails of Modi River and cross the suspension bridge to reach Birethanti. Then passing the mesmerizing villages of Sudame and Hille, you ascend alongside Bhurung Khola to reach Ulleri. The wide path of the village towards the stone steps leading to Ulleri  village. Overnight in Ulleri.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ulleri to Ghorepani (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you walk further through the wide path of the villages of Banthanti and Nangethanti. After a short walk, climb thousand more stone stairs before you come to the entry point of the village of Ghorepani. Upon arrival, explore the area and enjoy the view of the snowy peaks around you. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ghorepani to Poon Hill (3,210 m / 10,531 ft) and back to Ghorepani, then continue to Tatopani (1,190 m / 3,904 ft), 7–8 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will wake up early in the morning and ascend through the reach Poon Hill, which is popular for its enchanting sunrise view. From Poon Hill, you can get a breathtaking sunrise view over Dhaulagiri and Annapurna massif along with the views of Nilgiri (7,061 m), Machhapuchhre (6,997 m), Tukuche (6,920 m), Baraha Shikhar (7,847 m), Lamjung Himal (6,983 m), and others. Then you will return to Ghorepani for breakfast and then continue your trail towards Tatopani. After arrival in Tatopani, you can take a soothing bath in the natural hot spring. Overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tatopani to Kalopani (2,300 m / 7,546 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail today leads you along the bank of Kali Gandaki River, which flows through a deep gorge, towards Ghasa. You continue ascending past Dana, Rupse Chhahara, and Kopchepani, enjoying the view of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges. Further, a decent climb takes you to the Thakali village of Ghasa, which is a paradise for bird watchers. After reaching Ghasa, you continue to Kalapani for the overnight stay. Overnight in Kalopani.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kalopani to Marpha (2,650 m / 8,694 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: From Kalapani you pass by beautiful villages with the backdrop of Dhaulagiri massif on one side and Annapurna massif and Nilgiri (7,061 m) on the other side, en route to ancient Marpha village. Overnight in Marpha.

itinerary.title: Trek from Marpha to Muktinath (3,760 m / 12,336 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail goes through the settlements of Jomsom Bazar, EkleBhatti, Khingar, Jharkot, and Ranipauwa and passes a couple of monasteries en route to Muktinath. Enjoy the scenic landscape and the view of the amazing mountains that surround the area. The trail ends finally after climbing through a desert landscape to reach Muktinath.

itinerary.title: Trek from Muktinath to Kagbeni to Jomsom (2,720 m / 8,924 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: You start the day today with an early morning visit to the sacred Muktinath Temple. Muktinath is one of the most important religious destinations for Hindus from all over the globe. It holds an important place for Buddhists and other religions as well. It is believed that all your sins are washed after taking a bath in the 108 holy water taps in the Muktinath premises. After offering your prayers to the God of Salvation, you retrace your way to Jomsom via Kagbeni. Overnight in guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Fly from Jomsom to Pokhara, 15-20 minutes.
itinerary.html: You will board an early morning flight back to Pokhara from Jomsom, which flies you through the deepest gorge in the world, Kali Gandaki. You also get to catch amazing mountain views from the plane. Upon arrival in Pokhara, feel free to explore the lakeside area. You can also stroll cycle around the city or boat on Phewa Lake. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive back to Kathmandu, 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Take a tourist bus to reach the capital. You will be transported to your hotel as you arrive in Kathmandu. You can rest for some time and later stroll around the nearby market. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Airport for your departure to home.
itinerary.html: Our staff will drop you at the airport around 3 hours before the scheduled time of your flight.
