faqs.q: How long will it take to complete the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: Our regular Langtang Valley Trek lasts for 10 days, which includes airport pick-up/drop-off, 2 nights stay in Kathmandu, a travel by road from Kathmandu to Syabrubesi, 7 days of trekking, and return to Kathmandu. Modification of the itinerary or duration is possible according to your choice.

faqs.q: What is the maximum height reached during the trek?
faqs.a: The maximum altitude while trekking on the way is that of Kyanjin Gompa (3,870 m). On the day of acclimatization, the trekkers may either reach Tserko Ri (4,984 m) or Kyanjin Ri (around 4,773 m).

faqs.q: Can someone with no prior experience do the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: Yes. The Langtang Valley Trek is considered to be among the best beginner treks in Nepal. Although it requires several days’ walking at higher altitudes, anybody who is reasonably fit and prepared can easily manage to complete the trek.

faqs.q: What makes the Langtang Valley Trek stand out from other treks in Nepal?
faqs.a: Langtang Valley Trek provides you with a unique combination of the Himalayas, rich Tamang culture, quiet hiking routes, beautiful forests, glaciers, yak grazing grounds and ancient monasteries, among others, in just a brief trekking route.

faqs.q: Can this trek be customized?
faqs.a: Of course. We provide full customization of the itinerary according to your schedule, physical condition, interests, and budget. You can have additional acclimatization days, private transport, a cultural tour of Kathmandu and a combination of trek with other destinations.

faqs.q: How hard is the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: The Langtang Valley Trek is moderately difficult. Each day you will walk for about 5 to 7 hours over well-marked mountain routes. There are some portions that require a steady upward climb; however, no technical skill is required.

faqs.q: Is previous trekking experience necessary?
faqs.a: Previous trekking experience is an advantage but not a mandatory requirement. There have been many people who have successfully undertaken the Langtang Valley Trek for the first time.

faqs.q: What level of fitness am I supposed to have?
faqs.a: You must be moderately fit. Engaging yourself in exercises like hiking, running, biking, swimming, or stair climbing for many weeks prior to the trip will make it easier for you to undertake the trekking activity.

faqs.q: Is the Langtang Valley Trek suitable for older trekkers?
faqs.a: Yes. Many people in their fifties, sixties, or even seventies have been able to accomplish this trek successfully. As long as your physical condition is good, determined to take the challenge and are well prepared, age is not usually a barrier.

faqs.q: What type of accommodation is provided for the journey?
faqs.a: During the trek, you will be accommodated in local tea houses which provide twin sharing room facilities. In Kathmandu, you will be accommodated for two nights in tourist standard hotels with breakfast.

faqs.q: What are the meals provided?
faqs.a: During the trek, meals consisting of breakfast, lunch and dinner are included. Teahouses' menu usually has Dal Bhat as a main meal and different options for a mix of traditional Nepali, basic Western and Tibetan items. Breakfast is provided when you are in Kathmandu and for lunch and dinner, you can have of your choice in any place you want in the city.

faqs.q: Are there any vegetarian or vegan meals that could be prepared?
faqs.a: Yes. Vegetarian meals are common everywhere during the trail, and vegan meals are also prepared in many tea houses upon request. We request that you let us know your dietary restrictions in advance.

faqs.q: Will there be safe drinking water available?
faqs.a: Yes. Drinking water is readily available for purchase from teahouses, either boiled, bottled or filtered. You can use purification tablets or filters if you want to drink water from natural sources. It is advised to carry a reusable water so that you can refill it with purchased water from teahouses. Avoid bottled water as it is costly and not eco-friendly either.

faqs.q: Is there any provision for a hot shower and Internet facilities while trekking in the Langtang Valley?
faqs.a: Yes. Teahouses in the Langtang Valley Trek provide hot showers and internet facilities, especially in larger and popular trail villages. Nevertheless, they are normally provided after paying extra charges that may differ according to the teahouse. The availability and reliability of the services become low at higher altitudes.

faqs.q: Can I charge my phone and camera in the teahouse?
faqs.a: Charging facilities are available at most of the lodges (for a minimal charge) on the trail. However, there will be shared charging spaces and electricity is not always guaranteed, so carrying a power bank is advised which serves as a reliable backup.

faqs.q: Do tea houses provide blankets?
faqs.a: Yes. Blankets are usually provided in most tea houses; however, temperatures might go to very low levels especially at high altitudes. We advise you to make use of the sleeping bag provided in your package.

faqs.q: Do I get private rooms and bathrooms?
faqs.a: Private rooms may be available in off-peak seasons, mostly in the lower elevation teahouses. There are no private bathrooms in most tea houses along the route except for a few villages where there are additional costs involved.

faqs.q: Are teahouses heated?
faqs.a: There is usually a firewood or yak dung-heated stove in dining areas in the evenings. There is no heating at all in the bedroom areas.

faqs.q: What is the means of getting to the starting point of the trek?
faqs.a: The Langtang Valley journey starts with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to the trailhead of Syabrubesi. This overland countryside travel is estimated to take about 6-8 hours.

faqs.q: Will there be a guide and porter with me?
faqs.a: Yes. Your trek will be facilitated by an English-speaking government licensed guide. We also employ porters to help you carry your luggage (one porter per two trekkers).

faqs.q: What is the amount of luggage that can be carried by a porter?
faqs.a: Each porter carries the luggage of two trekkers and the total weight limit is normally 20-25 kg. It is advisable to pack only the necessary trekking clothes, gear and accessories.

faqs.q: What are the required permits for the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: You would require the Langtang National Park Entry Permit for the Langtang Valley trek. The permit will ensure that you have access to the protected area for the purpose of trekking. All permit formalities will be handled by Base Camp Adventure.

faqs.q: Is it possible for me to go on this trek alone?
faqs.a: Even though there could be changes to independent trekking rules, going on the trek accompanied by a seasoned guide is much safer, easier, and more interesting as they offer greater safety, local knowledge, cultural insights and logistical support.

faqs.q: What are the best times to go to the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: The best time is spring (March-May) and autumn (September-November), since it’s always stable weather-wise bringing in dry trekking trails and mild temperatures. Besides, the mountains can be seen clearly during these seasons.

faqs.q: Can I trek during winter?
faqs.a: Yes, trekking can be done during the winter months of December to February as you get an opportunity to explore the calm tracks with fully snow covered peaks. But it is important that you keep yourself ready for extremely cold weather conditions and heavy snowfall at high altitudes.

faqs.q: Is the trek feasible in the monsoon season?
faqs.a: The trek is possible in the monsoon, from June to August, although you will experience rain almost all the time. Besides, muddy tracks, poor visibility, and leeches in the lower forests can make trekking more challenging.

faqs.q: What do I need to pack for this trek?
faqs.a: You need to pack items that will be appropriate for the Himalayan weather conditions, such as waterproof boots, warm clothes, a down jacket, a rain jacket, trekking poles, sunglasses, sunscreen lotion, a hat, gloves, a headlamp, a reusable water bottle, and any personal medications that you may have. It is strongly advised to get good quality trekking gear.

faqs.q: What trekking gear will you provide?
faqs.a: Base Camp Adventure offers you a down jacket, a sleeping bag, and duffle bag in the package. Besides, we also provide basic first aid medical kits as well as an oximeter to monitor your pulse, oxygen saturation and heart rate.

faqs.q: What temperatures am I likely to experience?
faqs.a: The daytime temperature usually fluctuates between 10°C and 20°C in the lower areas. At Kyanjin Gompa and above, the night temperature is often below freezing, particularly during winter.

faqs.q: How can I book my trip?
faqs.a: You can make your reservation through our website or by means of email, messages or call. You will have to pay 30% non-refundable deposit and the rest amount upon reaching Kathmandu before the start of the trek.

faqs.q: What should I do if I have to cancel my trek?
faqs.a: In case of cancellation of your Langtang Valley Trek, you are required to write a cancellation letter to Base Camp Adventure. You will have to pay a cancellation fee of 30% of the total cost of the trip. In case of cancellation within less than 7 days prior to your journey, 100% of the cost of the service will be lost. We would like to advise you to purchase travel insurance that covers cancellation.

faqs.q: What are the advantages of booking the Langtang Valley Trek with Base Camp Adventure?
faqs.a: Base Camp Adventure has been known for many years for organizing various kinds of treks all across Nepal. The company has extensive experience in arranging treks with professional guides, well-planned itineraries, personal services, high-quality equipment, logistics support and safety concerns.

faqs.q: Is it necessary to buy insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. Travel insurance must be purchased, which covers high altitude trekking and emergency medical care as well as evacuation by helicopter.

faqs.q: What will happen if I am sick while on the trip?
faqs.a: The guide will be trained to recognize problems associated with altitude sickness as well as other health issues. In case of need, the schedule can be changed and an emergency evacuation can be arranged. Full travel insurance that covers helicopter evacuation is required.

faqs.q: What are the common health issues associated with the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: Adjustment to altitude, fatigue, body aches, coldness and changes in appetite are some of the common health issues. The expert guides accompanying the trek will monitor your health throughout the adventure and help you wherever necessary.

faqs.q: Will I suffer from altitude sickness?
faqs.a: The trek will take you around 5,000 m in day hikes which have a high risk of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS). However, the slow climbing rate makes it easy to avoid altitude sickness. Our itinerary includes an acclimatization day in Kyanjin Gompa which significantly reduces the chance of AMS.

faqs.q: How do I avoid altitude sickness during the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: In order to avoid altitude sickness, you need to climb slowly, walk at a consistent pace, keep yourself hydrated, avoid alcohol and get enough sleep. There is sufficient acclimatization time in our Langtang Valley itinerary at Kyanjin Gompa before tackling the Kyanjin Ri or Tserko Ri ascent.

faqs.q: What will happen in an emergency situation during the trek?
faqs.a: In the event of an emergency such as severe illness, injury or altitude sickness our guide will evaluate the situation and make the necessary arrangements which may include evacuation in some cases. Since there are no medical facilities available in mountainous regions, all the trekkers need to have trekking insurance with helicopter cover.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa to undertake the Langtang Valley Trek in Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. You need a visa to enter Nepal and the tourist visa can be acquired on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. It is necessary to fill out a form, pay the required fees and have your passport with a validity for at least six months from the date of travel.

faqs.q: What am I supposed to do once I arrive at the Kathmandu airport?
faqs.a: Our representative will welcome you upon your arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport and take you to your hotel. Here, you will be briefed about the trek and meet your guide afterwards.

faqs.q: Is it possible to purchase trekking gear in Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Yes. There are numerous options from where you can get your trekking gear, clothes and accessories in Kathmandu. Trekking items can be purchased or rented prior to embarking on the journey, especially in Thamel which has several shops with a variety of items.

faqs.q: Is it necessary to change money before the trek?
faqs.a: Yes. It is advised to change money into Nepalese currency before venturing into the mountains. Access to ATMs and card payments is not available in many villages. Therefore, carrying some cash will help to cater to personal needs and other requirements.

faqs.q: Will there be any mobile network coverage while trekking the Langtang Valley?
faqs.a: Yes. The mobile network coverage is available in most parts of the trail. Local SIM cards like NTC and NCELL can be used throughout much of the trek. However, the higher the elevation, the less coverage is expected.

faqs.q: Will my international SIM card work in Nepal?
faqs.a: Some international SIM cards can function in Nepal by way of roaming but using a Nepal SIM card such as that offered by NTC and Ncell will be cheaper and more efficient.

faqs.q: How much additional money should be taken for the trek?
faqs.a: While all major costs are included in your package, there is always a need to keep some extra Nepalese money for your own needs, such as hot showers, internet connections, recharging, snacks, drinks, souvenirs, and tips. An average of USD 10-30 per day will be enough in any case.

faqs.q: Is it possible to use credit cards in the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: Credit cards are not usually accepted in mountain villages. That's why we strongly recommend keeping some extra Nepalese money for daily trail expenses.

faqs.q: Is it mandatory to tip during the trekking journey?
faqs.a: No. There is no obligation to tip but it is always a good way to express your gratitude to your guide and porter who make your trekking experience enjoyable for you. The exact amount is up to you.

faqs.q: What kind of culture will I be able to observe during the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: This trek provides you with a chance to learn about the culture of the Tamang people, one of the indigenous tribes in Nepal. Traditional villages, Buddhist temples, prayer flags, local cuisine and other cultural practices are part of the experience.

faqs.q: What is there to see in Kyanjin Gompa?
faqs.a: Kyanjin Gompa is among the most visited places on this trek. The trek is popular due to the presence of the Buddhist monastery (Kyanjin Gompa), beautiful mountains, and a cheese factory nearby, which produces traditional Yak cheese.

faqs.q: Will I get to interact with the local community on the trek?
faqs.a: Yes. The trek passes through traditional villages, where you will be able to interact and experience the hospitality of the locals, get to know the mountain lifestyle and learn more about the culture of the Tamangs.

faqs.q: What is the maximum size of a group for the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: We provide flexible group sizes according to your choice. There is a choice of private trek for couples, family and small groups, or join a shared trekking group. Small groups ensure personalized attention and greater flexibility.

faqs.q: Can I join the Langtang Valley Trek as a solo trekker?
faqs.a: Yes, we have provisions for solo trekkers as well to go to Langtang Valley. They can either opt for a private trek along with the guide and porter or join the group departures.

faqs.q: Is there any chance that families with children would undertake the Langtang Valley Trek?
faqs.a: Absolutely, there is an opportunity for families with children to undertake the trek if their health conditions and physical preparations are good. In this case, the route will be adjusted by including shorter walks, extra resting days  and a slower pace to make it more comfortable.

faqs.q: What does a typical day in the Langtang Valley Trek look like?
faqs.a: The typical trekking day begins with breakfast at around 7:00 AM which is followed by about 5 to 7 hours of walking. There will be a lunch break at a teahouse along the route. In the evening, you will reach the destination of the day and have plenty of time for relaxation or walking around in the village area.

faqs.q: How long is my daily walking time?
faqs.a: Most of your trekking days will include 5 to 7 hours of walking. Sometimes it will be shorter, and the hike to Kyanjin Ri or Tserko Ri on the acclimatization day might take more time.

faqs.q: Are there any signboards for trekking?
faqs.a: Yes. The Langtang Valley Trek is done along a famous trekking trail that has clearly laid-out routes and signboards at many places.

faqs.q: What can I do to help conserve the Langtang area while on the trek?
faqs.a: You could help by avoiding single-use plastics, using reusable bottles, disposing of litter appropriately, using the local tea houses and adhering to the principles of leave no trace.

faqs.q: Does the Langtang National Park have any wildlife?
faqs.a: Yes. The Langtang National Park is a sanctuary for various types of plants and animals, some of which include red pandas, Himalayan black bears, musk deer, langur monkeys and several bird species. You will get a chance to spot some of them while on the trail.

faqs.q: Can I purchase snacks during the trek?
faqs.a: Yes. Tea houses and stores offer snacks such as chocolates, biscuits, noodles, energy bars and beverages. The prices rise as altitude rises because of transportation charges.

faqs.q: Are alcoholic beverages available along the way?
faqs.a: Yes. Various alcoholic beverages, including beer, whiskey and local alcohols are available in most tea houses. It is advised not to consume alcohol while trekking at a higher altitude as it increases dehydration.

faqs.q: Can I purchase coffee during the trek?
faqs.a: Yes. Black and milk coffee are available in most tea houses. Sometimes, freshly brewed coffee might also be available in bigger villages.

overview: Lobuche at the height of 6,145 m is an attractive summit, offering a variety of existing routes and a wide scope for new lines. Lobuche Peak Climbing lies in the Everest region of Solu Khumbu district and is reached by trekking for about 7/8 days from Lukla the nearest airport. There exist two distinct summits to Lobuche Peak: Lobuche East (6,119 m) and Lobuche West 6,145 m). The true East Peak is quite striking and is reached by descending into a marked notch and climbing steep snow/ice slopes to the top. The top is exposed and often covered with rotten ice

title: Luxury Lodge Trek To Everest Base Camp With Helicopter Return
summary: Experience the ultimate adventure with our Luxury Lodge Trek to Everest Base Camp, complete with a helicopter return. Enjoy breathtaking views, luxurious accommodations, and a seamless journey to the heart of the Himalayas.

seo.title: Luxury Lodge Trek To Everest Base Camp With Helicopter Return
seo.description: Experience the ultimate adventure with our Luxury Lodge Trek to Everest Base Camp, complete with a helicopter return. Enjoy breathtaking views, luxurious accommodations, and a seamless journey to the heart of the Himalayas.

cover.alt: Luxury Lodge Trek To Everest Base Camp With Helicopter Return

overview:
A luxury lodge trek to Everest Base Camp with Helicopter return is a new approach to behold some of the highest mountains in the world through a comfortable, secure, and amusing journey. The stunning and riveting journey stretches through places like Lukla, Phakding, Namche Bazaar, Deboche, Dingboche, Lobuche, and Gorak Shep to the heartland of the tallest mountain in the world, Mt. Everest (8848.86m), with comfort backing you up. The thrilling journey takes you to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m) and Kala Patthar (5,644 m), which is the highest point of this trek. This stunning journey combines the thrilling aspects of the trek with the indulgence of spending time at culturally rich places in some of the finest lodges and concludes the stunning journey with a scenic Helicopter flight to Kathmandu. The journey presents you with the spectacular beauty of Mt. Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, Thamserku, Makalu, Nuptse II, Lhotse Shar and many more. You’ll be presented with the up close and panoramic beauty of the Himalayas by embarking on this journey. On top of that, the journey presents you with wonderful Himalayan experiences by extending your cultural and Himalayan exploration.

Major Highlights

  • Mesmerizing views: You’ll be presented with the outstanding beauty of Mt. Everest along with other sibling mountains like Lhotse, Nuptse, Lhotse Shar, Nuptse II, Thamserku, Makalu, Ama Dablam, and many more.
  • Scenic and adventurous flight: After the strenuous journey, you’ll hop on the adventurous and scenic flight to Kathmandu. This flight will take you flying across the mountains and present you with the aerial panoramic beauty of the mountains.
  • Luxurious accommodations: The luxury package deals in providing you with first-class accommodation facilities. You’ll be staying in the best lodges or teahouses of the region during your journey.
  • Cultural Exploration: During this journey, you’ll pass through numerous culturally rich places like Phakding, Namche Bazaar, Debechoe, Dingboche, and others, and along the way, you’ll be able to explore the culture of Sherpas and immerse in a festive atmosphere.
  • Visit Monasteries: You can visit and explore numerous monasteries during this journey. Some of them are Tengboche Monastery, Pangboche Monastery, Khunde Monastery, Khumjung Monastery, Thame Monastery and others. The journey will also present you with the opportunity to witness stupas, mani walls, prayer flags, and prayer wheels.
  • Riveting journey: The Everest Base Camp Trek is not like a short walk to the park, and it demands strong physical strength, mental resilience, and sheer determination. Navigating the steep paths and challenging terrains requires strong willpower and dedication while the journey tunes your experience with thrilling aspects.
  • Scenic beauty: While you’re embarking on the journey to Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar, you’ll pass through numerous distinct Himalayan settlements. During this journey, you’ll catch the beauty of the region and sightsee elevated hills, lush forests, magical glaciers, tranquil lakes, snow-capped mountains, thundering rivers, and cascading waterfalls.
  • Exploration of Himalayan flora and fauna: Considering the case of luck, you can catch glimpses of wandering Himalayan wild species during the journey. The trails take you through rhododendrons, pine, and oak forests, where you can explore the distinct flora of the region along with distinct bird species. As you move forward, you can catch glimpses of Himalayan Tahr, Musk Deer, Snow Leopard, Red Panda, Eagle, Vulture, Himalayan Monal and many more.

Best time for Luxury lodge trek to Everest base camp with helicopter return

The best time for the luxury lodge trek to Everest Base Camp with Helicopter return is considered to be Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November). This is because, during this time, the climatic conditions of the region tend to remain stable, and this ultimately provides you with a comfortable and amusing experience. The stable weather conditions alleviate the major challenges like rainfall, snowfall, extreme coldness, temperature fluctuations, windstorms, slippery tracks, and summoning of blood-sucking insects, along with minimizing teh risks of landslides and floods. Along with this, planning the journey during this time will let you relish the beauty of the mountains in peace without any hurdles along the way. The stable weather during this time will present you with the clear and transparent beauty of the mountainous vistas. On top of that, numerous festivals align during the time of Spring and Autumn which makes your trekking journey more fruitful and amusing. You’ll be able to immerse in the rich culture and explore Himalayan settlements in depth. Furthermore, the vibrant atmosphere during this time invites glimpses of the Himalayan wild species while you embark through the blooming rhododendrons and lively pine forests.

Altitude Sickness

Altitude Sickness is the major concern during trekking to any high Himalayan region. The Everest Base Camp Trek takes you to an extreme altitude of 5,644 m (Kala Patthar), and this has risks of altitude sickness as you ascend higher in altitude. As you ascend over 2,500 m, you’ll start to notice changes in the atmospheric pressure and oxygen level. The deprived oxygen level and changing atmospheric pressure at the higher altitude can pose a threat of altitude sickness if your body can’t adapt to such changes. The symptoms of altitude sickness, which is also known as acute mountain sickness, include nausea, headache, loss of appetite, insomnia, and loss of coordination and balance. This can range from mild to extreme, and if the case worsens, it can turn into high-altitude cerebral edema (HACE) and high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). This can cause a serious problem during your journey, which is why it is important to take necessary precautions regarding it. It is important to stay hydrated all the time and maintain a steady pace during the trekking journey. Acclimatizing twice during this journey is very crucial to let your body adapt to the changing surroundings. While the journey can pose risks of altitude sickness, you have the advantage of the premium package that will take you to a higher altitude at a steady pace, proper acclimatization, and comfortable lodges to rest the night. Moreover, it is also important to avoid smoking and alcohol during the journey and consume healthy and nutritious food to support your health. Be mindful of such conditions, and in case you catch altitude sickness, you’ll be given diamox by our team and descend to the lower region to acclimatize properly. In case the sickness worsens, you can seek emergency helicopter evacuation at any time.

Travel Insurance

Travel Insurance is another important aspect to consider before embarking on the rip-roaring adventure to the heartland of Mt. Everest. The journey can pose risks of sickness, injuries, and accidents along the way, which is why it is important to have travel insurance before you head for any high Himalayan trekking journey. On top of that, the Everest Base Camp Trek is considered to be more challenging and can pose more threats compared to other trekking sites in Nepal. To give you a clear picture of its importance, here are the lists of reasons why you should seek Travel Insurance.
  • Travel Insurance covers medical expenses related to the trekking. During the journey, if in case you happen to have any injuries or sickness, travel insurance will pay for all your expenses.
  • It deals with compensation for any loss of a friend or family during the journey
  • It deals with loss or stolen items during the trekking journey
  • It deals with the cancellation of the trekking adventure
  • Travel Insurance lets you access immediate Helicopter evacuation in case an emergency need
  • Deals with Natural disasters and severe weather conditions that affect your travel plans
  • Coverage for personal responsibility in the event that you injure someone or their property
  • Search and rescue operation in case of any emergency
  • Travel Insurance also covers accidental death or disability

Required travel documents

The required travel documents for this trek are:
  • Travel Insurance
  • Valid Visa
  • Passport
  • 2-4 Passport sized photos

You’ll be hopping on the adventurous flight while sightseeing the magical beauty of Kathmandu, Nagarkot, and Jiri Hils. After the stunning flight, while enjoying the aerial beauty of the surroundings, you’ll arrive at Lukla. Your thrilling trekking adventure begins with a hike from Lukla to Phakding. You’ll pass along places like Chheplung, Ghat, and Nurning until you finally arrive at Phakding. The trails will take you through lush forests alongside the thundering Dudh Koshi River. The journey takes you through numerous settlements like Bengkar, Toktok, Monjo, and Jorsalle before arriving at Namche Bazaar. You’ll issue the required permits of Sagarmatha National Park at Monjo and head for Namche Bazaar from there. As you begin the journey through Sagarmatha National Park, you’ll have chances of spotting Himalayan wild species. The Sagarmatha National Park is rich in biodiversity and species of wild animals. Considering the case of your luck, you’ll get a chance to spot wandering wild species like Himalayan Tahr, Red Panda, Monkeys, Snow Leopard, Eagle, Vulture, Himalayan Monal and others while traversing through the rich flora of the region. You’ll pass through blooming rhododendron, oak, and pine trees along the journey to Namche Bazaar. The journey will be alongside the Bhotekoshi River until you arrive at Namche Bazaar, where you’ll spend the night. Also, your trekking journey will continue at a steady pace by letting you have time to adapt to the changing surroundings. Along with that, the luxury package will deal you with having a comfortable and warm night to rest your tired body.

itinerary.title: Rest at Namche Bazar for acclimatization
itinerary.html: By today, you’ve ascended by more than 3,000 m in altitude. As you reach higher than 2,500 m in altitude, you’ll start to feel changes in atmospheric pressure, and the air starts to get thinner. Changing atmospheric pressure can result in altitude sickness if the body can’t adapt to such changes. This is why it is important to acclimatize properly before heading for higher altitude. As the journey takes you to an extreme altitude of 5,644 m, it's important to acclimatize and let your body adapt to the changing surroundings. And for that, Namche Bazaar is the perfect spot to acclimatize and prepare your body for upcoming adventure because you’ll also get to immerse in the rich culture of the region, see Tibetan art crafts, and explore some nearby settlements as well. On this day, you’ll visit the local market, Namche Monastery, and explore the local practices of the region. Though it's an acclimatizing day, you’ll head to nearby places like Tengboche or Syangboche to sightsee magical Himalayan beauty, immerse yourself in rich culture, and explore Himalayan places. The mesmerizing journey will give you insights into the traditional way of living and also let you savor the delectable cuisines by glimpsing the beauty of the Himalayas. There is a reason why Namche Bazaar is considered to be one of the best stopovers for the Everest Base Camp Trek and it is rich cultural practices of this region. The place is beautiful, the people are kind, and they shall welcome you to their village warm-heartedly. You may stroll about the neighborhood to see various shops, eateries, markets, and tourist attractions. Additionally, as Syangboche, Thame, and Khumbjung are close to the Namche Bazaar, they can be visited on this day. These places hold spiritual significance as they have Monastery like Thame Monastery, Khunde Monastery, Khumjung Monastery, and others.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazzar - Deboche(3820m/1253ft): 5-6 hrs
itinerary.html: Namche Bazaar Elevation: 3,440 m Deboche Elevation: 3,820 m Elevation gain: 380 m Trek duration: 5-6 hrs On this day, you’ll pass through the trails to reach Deboche from Namche Bazaar. You’ll cover a total distance of 10km and pass through rhododendron and pine forests. The trekking journey will be alongside the Dudh Koshi River. The day's hike includes flat, incline, and descending terrain with lots of excitement and breathtaking views. The journey will take you through Phuki Tenga and Tengboche along the way, which will present you with the magnificent beauty of the Himalayas. During the trek through Tengboche, you’ll also be able to visit Tengboche Monastery along with glimpsing the stunning mountainous views of Thamserku, Everest, and Ama Dablam. After 5-6 hours of trekking through the trails of the EBC trek, you’ll arrive at Deboche. This is a small village that holds religious and cultural significance besides providing access to the clear and magical beauty of the Himalayas. There is also a monastery called Deboche Monastery, which is also known as Pangboche Monastery in this village. This place is another one of the famous stopovers during the Everest Base Camp Trek. Additionally, possessing top-notch lodges, this place invites travelers to spend their nights assuring themselves comfortable and warm nights. You’ll spend your time at one of the finest lodges in this place and prepare yourself for the next adventure to come.

itinerary.title: Deboche - Dingboche (4360m): 4-5 hrs
itinerary.html: Deboche Elevation: 3,820 m Dingboche Elevation: 4,360 m Elevation gain: 540 m Trek duration: 5-6 hrs The journey now stretches towards Dingboche from Deboche. The trek from Deboche to Dingboche is a mesmerizing and yet challenging journey of the Everest Base Camp Trek. On this day, you’ll pass through places like Pangboche and Somare and then trek alongside the Imja Khola before reaching Dingboche. The journey is beautiful as it serves you with stunning mountainous vistas and snowy landscapes. The journey can also be challenging as you’ll pass through steep ridges and continuous ascents and descents. You’ll be elevated by more than 500 m in altitude, which is challenging, but the mesmerizing views of Everest, Lhotse, Ama Dablam, and others will keep you occupied. You’ll cover a total distance of about 11 km by walking through the trails for about 5-6 hours. The initial trail of today’s journey is gentle and involves passing through rhododendrons and lush forests. Before reaching Pangboche, you’ll have to cross the Imja Khola via a sweeping suspension bridge. Then, the journey will be alongside the Imja Khola, and this will provide you with the stunning beauty of Ama Dablam. As you ascend from there, the scenery grows more stony and desolate, reflecting the increased altitude. Upon arriving at Dingboche, you’ll be able to relish the spectacular beauty of Ama Dablam, Island Peak, Lhotse, Tabuche Peak, and Makalu.

itinerary.title: Rest at Dingboche for acclimatization
itinerary.html: This day marks another acclimatization day during this journey. Dingboche is another famous stopover and is considered to be one of the cozy restaurants. By today, you have ascended by more than 4,000 m and acclimatizing at such a time is very crucial to prevent from catching altitude sickness. Though, this is another acclimatizing day, on this day, you’ll explore some nearby settlements. You can head for Nagarjuna Hill on this day and catch stunning mountainous panoramas of Cho Oyu, Island Peak, Lhotse, Everest, and Ama Dablam. This area is renowned for offering views of Himalayan wildlife and enlightening you on the marvels of the Himalayas. The wonderful times spent at Namche Bazaar and Dingboche make the exciting parts of the trekking expedition to Everest's heartland favorable and magical.

itinerary.title: Dingboche (4350m) - Lobuche (4930m)
itinerary.html: Dingboche Elevation: 4,360 m Lobuche Elevation: 4,930 m Elevation gain: 540 m Trek duration: 5-6 hrs The trek from Dingboche to Lobuche is one of the significant trekking journeys of the Everest Base Camp Trek. The journey begins after an early morning breakfast through the trails that ascend to a wide valley. With the steps you put forward, you’ll be left awestruck by the stunning mountainous glimpses. The clear day summons clear skies and the transparent beauty of the mountainous vistas. Then, the route passes to Dughla by crossing the soaring river over a suspension bridge. Then, after taking a short break at Dughla Pass, you’ll ascend through the trails. Along the way, you’ll sightsee memorials and stone cairns dedicated to the climbers who lost their lives on Everest. From there, the trails ascend toward the lateral moraine of the Khumbu Glacier, and the path will present you with the staggering beauty of the tallest mountain in the world, Mt. Everest. Upon reaching Lobuche, you’ll spend the night at one of the finest teahouses in the region. A quick tip for all adventurer souls is that heading to the Kala Patthar is no short walk to the park, which is why it is important to maintain a steady pace and stay hydrated all the time. Also, be mindful of the fluctuating weather conditions of the Himalayan region and bring the necessary clothing to protect you from heat and extreme cold.

itinerary.title: Lobuche - Gorak Shep (5170 m) - Everest Base Camp (5364 m/17,594 ft) – Gorak Shep: 8-9 hrs
itinerary.html: Lobuche Elevation: 4,930 m Gorak Shep Elevation: 5,170 m Elevation gain: 240m Trek duration: 4-5 hrs On this day, you’ll pass through the trails to reach Gorak Shep and spend the night there in order to prepare your body to head for the summit of Kala Patthar. This is the 2nd last day of the Luxury lodge trek to Everest Base Camp with a Helicopter return. This is the major day of this trekking journey as you’ll reach Gorakshep and head for the Everest Base Camp on the same day. You’ll pass through the snowy trails to reach Everest Base Camp to catch the marvelous beauty of Everest. The trek to EBC begins at 5,164-meter-high Gorakshep and goes along the Khumbu Glacier through stony glacial moraine country. The hike usually takes two to three hours total, with a distance of roughly four kilometers covered each way. Upon reaching the Everest Base Camp, you’ll be able to catch the stunning mountainous landscapes.

itinerary.title: Gorak Shep - Kala Patthar and fly back to Kathmandu on Helicopter
itinerary.html: Gorak Shep Elevation: 5,170 m Kala Patthar Elevation: 5,644 m Elevation gain: 474 m Kathmandu Elevation: 1,400 m Trek duration: 2 hours Flight duration: 45 minutes This is the major day of this trekking journey. On this day, you’ll stretch your journey all the way to Kala Patthar to seek the close-up views of Everest. You’ve been trekking through the places and trails for days to finally arrive for this day. Today’s journey will take you to an extreme altitude of 5,644 m to let you catch the outstanding and spectacular beauty of Everest. Along the way, you’ll also catch the stunning Himalayan landscapes of sibling mountains like Nuptse, Lhotse, Pumori, Changtse, Ligtren, and many more. When you present yourself to the majesty of nature after working tirelessly for days on end with nothing but dedication, you'll feel incredibly accomplished and at ease within. It is undoubtedly a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, and you will treasure the lovely memories you made along the way. The lively interaction with the grandeur of nature will keep you occupied and amazed. You’ll be astonished by the magical beauty of the region as your hard work has been repaid with mesmerizing mountainous landscapes of some of the highest mountains in the world. Upon relishing the beauty of the region enough, you’ll bid farewell to the mountainous vistas and Himalayan settlement and hop on the scenic flight from Kala Patthar to Kathmandu. This will be a once-in-a-lifetime memory as you’ll be flying over the mountains and catching the stunning, clear, transparent, and close beauty of the mountains. The scenic flight will take you flying over the route you ascended and give you access to an aerial view of the entire Himalayan region and Himalayan settlements. In conclusion, the efforts placed for days to reach the summit of Kala Patthar are well rewarded by the stunning, panoramic mountainous views, personal reflection, comfortable ride, scenic flight, and a great sense of achievement within.

sections.title: Useful Info
sections.html:
Accomodation and Meals

The accomodation during this journey will be in the top-notch lodges of the region. The luxury package deals in providing you with first-class services in extravagant hotels and lodges. Since the start of your journey, you’ll be presented with outstanding facilities. You’ll be staying in the 5-star hotel during your time in Kathmandu and will be offered a private vehicle to explore some nearby settlements. Similarly, while trekking, you will stay in opulent lodges that offer a very cozy and alluring ambiance amid the far-off mountains. The rooms during the journey will be single or twin shared with private washrooms. You’ll get to take a hot shower and dine in the communal dining hall. You’ll be treated with amenities like WiFi, charging stations, and hot showers without any additional charges. The decor and experience of luxury lodges are very different from those of inexpensive lodges, and the luxury package won’t compromise in presenting you with first-class facilities during your stay. Furthermore, regarding food during your stay, you’ll be presented with a wide menu to choose from. Some of the dishes that you can have for lunch, breakfast, and dinner are Momo, Chowmein, Daal Bhat, Soup, Mushroom, Non-veg items, macaroni, Burger, Pizza, Stew, Chapati, Porridge, Sel roti, Bread Butter, Oatmeal, Aalu Chana, Newari dishes and many more traditional Nepalese cuisines. Nevertheless, you’ll be treated with warm and delicious foods.

Preparation and Packing

When it comes to heading for the Everest Base Camp Trek, preparation and packing are necessary. Being mindful of the weather conditions, trekking hours, and strenuous journeys, it is important to be equipped with the necessary equipment, gear, and clothes and to make the necessary preparations.

Necessary preparations

Necessary preparations for the Everest Base Camp Trek include performing lightweight exercises. Along with that, performing cardiovascular exercises increases your endurance, which helps in overcoming the hurdles you face along the journey. Exercises like squats, deadlifts, pushups, pullups, chin-ups, and others will help in training your muscles and uplift your strength. By doing this, you can boost your muscle work and train yourself for the strenuous journey. Along with that, exercises like running, walking, jogging, swimming, hiking, cycling and others will help in building stamina. This wil increase your productivity and help you to cope with long trekking hours. These both exercises will tune your body and muscles for the Himalayan trekking with productive flood flow to the whole body. In turn, this enhances the trekking experience by alleviating risks of falls, sickness, and injuries along the way. Furthermore, to prevent yourself from pain and injuries and enhance the mobility of your body, you can consider practicing stretching exercises or yoga. This will enhance your flexibility and alleviate the risks of joint pain, back pain, and others. Ultimately, these preparations will prepare you for the journey and ensure you a safe, secure and amazing experience.

Necessary packing

The necessary packing for this trek involves being equipped with essential gear and clothes. Packing the bags by being mindful of the high-altitude climatic conditions is essential. This involves packing like: Upperwear: Tshirts, full sleeve t-shirts, thermal outer, fleece jackets, wind sweaters, raincoats, etc Lowerwear: Trekking pants, trousers, comfortable pants, half pants, thermal trousers, etc Innerwear: Vests, underwear, etc Headwear: Hat, sunglasses, scarf, neck covers, etc Footwear: Trekking boots, sports shoes, sandals, etc Toiletries: Toothbrush, toothpaste, shampoo, soap, razor, shaving cream, body wash, face wash, nail clippers, deodorant, etc First aid: Tweezers, bandages, diamox, oral rehydration tablets, water purification tablets, insect repellant cream, etc Other essential items: Camera, phone, extra batteries, charger, powerbank, snacks, water bottle, maps, compass, etc

faqs.q: How is drinking water during the Luxury lodge trek to Everest base camp with Helicopter return?
faqs.a: During the trek, you can purchase mineral water from the shops of the region. However, do not drink water directly from wells, taps, or rivers. Instead, carry your water bottle and refill it in the teahouses.

faqs.q: How hard is the Luxury lodge trek to Everest base camp with Helicopter return?
faqs.a: While the trek can be challenging and is coined as a moderately challenging journey, it can be done smoothly by making the necessary preparations. The trek may pose challenges along the way and demands the body’s ability to adapt to the changing surroundings. Those who have prior trekking experience to higher altitudes will have no issues or difficulties during the trek. For beginners, it is important to go under proper preparations and be equipped with the necessary gear and clothes. Remember, the journey just demands ascending Kala Patthar, and on the way back, you’ll catch the direct Helicopter flight to Kathmandu that settles your tiredness and relieves you from the hassle of the journey.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for this trek?
faqs.a: While it is not compulsory, it is important to trek alongside an experienced guide. The honed skills and experiences of the guide will come into play while navigating the paths of the Everest Base Camp Trek. Trekking alongside a guide will ensure you a safe and smooth journey and present you with outstanding Himalayan experiences. You will be able to explore the Himalayan region extensively and carry broden knowledge if you hire an experienced guide. On top of that, a guide will be able to acquire top-notch accommodation for you during your stay.

faqs.q: What kind of luxury can I expect during this trek?
faqs.a: This package is designed carefully by taking into account extreme comfort and top-notch facilities. It is created by being mindful of the adventurer souls who seek comfort and relaxation during the trek. We understand that accommodation and food are vital segments of this trek and we do not compromise in providing you with adequate facilities. We will offer opulent rooms with attached bathrooms and heating for this luxurious journey. Your body can fight off bacterial or viral infections and replenish lost energy with a healthy diet, which will get you ready for the hike the following day.

faqs.q: How the luxury package is different to normal Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.a: The luxury package is different from the normal Everest Base Camp Trek in many aspects. The luxury package deals with picking you up from the airport and dropping you off in a cozy private vehicle. To let you have a wonderful time, the package deals with your staying in 5-star hotels in Kathmandu before and after the trek. Along with that, the package deals with providing comfortable and first class accommodation facilities during the journey. Where available, you’ll spend the time at luxury hotels during the trek while not available in higher altitude regions, you’ll stay at comfortable and best teahouses in the region.

faqs.q: What should I do if I get sick in the middle of the trek?
faqs.a: The major sickness that you can suffer from during this journey is Altitude sickness. To avoid this sickness, its important to stay hydrated, maintain a steady pace, and acclimatize properly. Taking a dose of diamox will prevent you from catching the sickness. In case you catch the sickness, it's important to descend to a lower altitude and rest. If the case worsens, you can seek an emergency medical evacuation.

title: Makalu Base Camp Trek
summary: Explore Makalu Base Camp Trek, the world’s fifth-highest mountain, journey through pristine landscapes, high mountain passes, remote villages

seo.title: Makalu Base Camp Trek | Guide | Itinerary | Cost | Map
seo.description: Explore Makalu Base Camp Trek, the world’s fifth-highest mountain, journey through pristine landscapes, high mountain passes, remote villages

overview:
Makalu Base Camp trek is an exhilarating adventure through one of Nepal's most pristine regions. During the trek, you can explore the tranquil trails with fewer visitors. In addition, the trek provides you with a chance to witness the raw beauty of the Makalu region which will enhance your overall experience.

The trek takes place within the Makalu Barun National Park. This protected area is known for its rich biodiversity. At this park the rare species such as Snow Leopards, Himalayan Black Bears, Musk Deer and Red Pandas can be spotted. This trek passes through terraced hillsides, rivers, lush forests and thrilling ridgelines.

The trek offers mesmerizing views of Everest, Chamlang, Lhotse, Makalu and many other nearby peaks. This exciting adventure starts in Num village. Afterward, it takes you through quiet and traditional settlements where people from the Rai, Sherpa, Gurung and Sherpa communities reside. So, you can explore their daily life, culture and experience their warm hospitality.

The cultural exploration opportunities will make your experience more enriching. Reaching Makalu Base Camp at 4,870 m and immersing yourself in its incredible vistas is one of the key highlights of this trek.

The trek is undertaken by fewer people especially when compared to treks of other popular regions. Nevertheless, it has gradually managed to attract the attention of the adventurers looking for a tranquil experience in the Himalayas.

The Makalu Base Camp Trek often gets described as a hidden gem by the trekkers because of its exceptional scenery. Furthermore, the availability of good accommodation and the warm local hospitality has attracted more trekkers. The trek treats you to stunning scenery and provides a deep sense of adventure which makes it one of Nepal’s most incredible treks.
highlights: Exhilarating flight between Kathmandu and Tumlingtar.
Trek through Makalu Barun National Park.
Beautiful views of peaks like Baruntse, Everest, Lhotse, Chamlang, Makalu and other surrounding peaks.
Experience the vibrant cultures of ethnic groups such as Rai, Gurung and Sherpa along the trekking trail.
Navigate the serene and off the beaten routes.
Trek alongside the beautiful Barun River feeling the crisp mountain air.

itinerary.title: Fly to Tumlingtar and Drive to Num (1,505 m / 4,938 ft), 4-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Kathmandu Elevation: 1,400 m 
Tumlingtar Elevation: 518 m 
Num Elevation: 1,505 m 
Flight Duration: 35 minutes 

Your adventure begins with short and thrilling flight from Kathmandu to Tumlingtar. As the aircraft lifts off Kathmandu’s streets and lush green hills can be seen from an aerial perspective, which is truly fascinating.

The descent into Tumlingtar is equally exciting. The beautiful views of hills and cliffs can be seen before landing on a small and simple airport at Tumlingtar. After the airplane lands, the journey continues by road and you will drive to the hilltop village of Num, situated at 1,505 meters. 

The drive can take around 4 to 6 hours. The drive to Num from Tumglingtar is an adventure in itself. The scenery changes constantly. You can see dense forests, scattered villages and terraced fields. After a scenic drive through winding roads, you will finally reach Num and settle at one of the best teahouses of the village.

itinerary.title: Trek from Num to to Seduwa (1,530 m / 5,020 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Seduwa Elevation: 1,530 m 
Trek Duration:  6 to 7 hours

You will start your day with a hearty breakfast and descend steeply toward the Arun River. You make your way through terraced fields, witnessing beautiful scenery. Then, you will navigate a dense forest to reach high suspension bridge. After crossing the bridge, the trail starts to rise. Make sure to be careful while navigating the varied terrains.  
You will pass through beautiful landscapes, walking along the traditional villages and cardamom farms. By late afternoon you will reach Seduwa. It is a picturesque village located at 1,530 m It is known as the gateway to Makalu-Barun National Park. Here, you will register your permits. In the evening, you can have authentic local food and rest overnight in the village.

itinerary.title: Trek from Seduwa to Tashi Gaon (2,065 m / 6,775 ft), 5-6 hours
itinerary.html:
Tashi Gaon Elevation: 2,065 m
Trek Duration: 5-6 hours 

After enjoying breakfast you begin your trek toward Tashi Gaon. You will make your way walking through an area that is surrounded by tranquil, lush forest. The trail starts off gently and you will walk through fertile farmland, cardamom groves, and small villages where locals focus on their daily routines.

After around two hours on the trail, you will follow uphill path steadily through thick bamboo and rhododendron forests. As you gain altitude you may feel the change in elevation, but the views become more stunning.

You can immerse yourself in the wide and open glimpses of the surrounding mountains after trekking for 5 to 6 hours at Tashi Gaon. This quiet mountain village gives you chance to connect with Sherpa traditions and lifestyle. You settle into local tea house for the night where warm meals and welcoming hosts make you feel right at home.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tashi Gaun to Khongma Danda (3,562 m / 11,686 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Khongma Danda Elevation: 3,562 m
Trek Duration: 6 - 7 hours

You will leave Tashi Gaon after breakfast. You will begin your ascend toward Khongma Danda, entering the higher alpine zone. Then, you will follow a gentle trail winding through forested hills. However, terrain quickly changes as you start to ascend continuously.

After a couple of hours, you will make it to Danda Kharka. It is a scenic ridge that offers mesmerizing views of the surrounding landscapes. It is an ideal place to enjoy the view. Then, you will take the steeper ascent. Afterwards, the trail takes you through lush rhododendron forests. 

Parts of the path are narrow. So, make sure to trek gradually but steadily. As you gain more elevation you will be treated to the expansive views of the valleys below. Also, glimpses of distant Himalayan peaks will captivate you the entire time. 

Afterwards, you will walk for around an hour and reach the ridgeline, where the village of Khongma Danda finally comes into sight. Khongma Danda offers stunning mountain vistas and a peaceful atmosphere. You will settle in at the teahouse in Khongma danda for the night to rest before getting ready for the next stage of your journey.

itinerary.title: Trek from Khongma Danda to Dobate (3,550 m / 11,647 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Dobate Elevation: 3,550 m
Trek Duration: 6 - 7 hours 

You will set out early from Khongma Danda, heading deeper into the high Himalayas. You will walk through the uphill path and reach an area around the wide alpine meadows. As you ascend the landscape opens up and views of deep valleys below and snow capped peaks rising above can be seen.

On this day, you will cross scenic mountain passes. Also, you can witness stone chortens and prayer flags along the trails. 

The terrain becomes more challenging as you push higher. You will cross remote alpine plateaus and also see icy mountain streams on the route. The first pass you will navigate is  Ghungru La. It stands at 4,055 meters. You can reach this pass after trekking along ridgeline. From here, you will continue on to the second pass, Keke La ( 4,170 m).

Every step while climbing these high altitude passes is exhilarating and rewards you with stunning views of the glacial terrain and towering peaks making the effort entirely worth it. 

After trekking for around 6 to 7 hours in total you will reach Dobate. It is peaceful high altitude village. You will stay overnight at one of the teahouses where you can feel fresh mountain air and feel quiet stillness.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dobate to Yangle Kharka (3,610 m / 11,844 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Yangle Kharka Elevation: 3,610 m
Trek Duration: 5 - 6 hours

You will begin off the day’s journey by following a downhill path from Dobate into a thick pine and rhododendron forest. On this day, you will make gentle climbs and descents through narrow paths. As you push forward, the landscape starts to get more remote. You can see big cliffs rise beside you and also beautiful waterfalls.

You will walk alongside the Barun River and also cross old wooden bridges. Then, you will follow a path of quiet alpine fields. The beautiful views of Chamlang and Tutse peaks can be seen along the trail. In addition, you can also spot herds of yaks grazing.

Continuing further, you will reach Femtang. It is an ideal place to stop to enjoy a peaceful break with unforgettable views. From Femtang, the path becomes flatter. So, you can ensure a more relaxed journey toward Yangle Kharka. As you arrive at Yangle Kharka, you can see a few simple lodges. Here, you will stay overnight immersing yourself in the peacefulness of the area.

itinerary.title: Trek from Yangle Kharka to Langmale Kharka (4,510 m / 14,797 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html:
Langmale Kharka Elevation: 4,510 m
Trek Duration: 7 - 8 hours

On this day, you will depart Yangle Kharka. You will begin the trek taking a steady ascent heading towards alpine zone. The trail requires you to walk along the Barun River and climb gently through expansive yak pastures.

As you move higher, the Himalayan scenery is truly stunning. You can witness mesmerizing views of Makalu Mountain. Along the way, you will pass through herds of yaks and also see a few scattered stone huts. Here, you may spot temporary shelters built by local herders.

Afterwards, the path begins to widen and you can see snowy ridgelines around. You will follow the uphill path and finally reach Langmale Kharka, which is a remote high-altitude spot that lies between cliffs and snow capped slopes.

Once you arrive you may settle in at your teahouse or choose to explore nearby ridge and enjoy panoramic views of surroundings. It is the perfect place to explore, rest and prepare for another thrilling day.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day in Langmale Kharka (4,510 m / 14,797 ft).
itinerary.html:
During the high altitude treks like Makalu Base Camp giving your body time to adjust to the high altitude is necessary. The air is thinner at higher altitude. So, it is important to slow down and rest. This day, you can explore, nearby hills of Langmale Kharka to give yourself time to acclimate properly.

Scheduling a day for acclimatization at Langmale Kharka helps your body adjust to higher altitude. In addition, it also gives you the chance to discover scenic gems of the area. By exploring the nearby hilly section, you will get rewarded with alluring scenery. 

Stunning views of Makalu and Peak 6 can be seen while strolling around Langmale Kharka. Your guide will make sure to take you to scenic places so that you can witness beautiful scenery.

After completing the acclimatization hike, you will head back to your teahouse. Here, you can rest, chat with your team or simply sit quietly and admire the high Himalayas. You can have a nutrient-rich, have warm dinner and rest to be prepared for the next adventurous day to Makalu Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek from Langmale Kharka to Makalu Base Camp (4,870 m / 15,978 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Makalu Base Camp Elevation: 4,870 m
Trek Duration: 6 - 7 hours 

You will depart Langmale Kharka in the morning. The journey to the base camp of Makalu begins with a gentle walk along the Barun River. You will walk through the forested path, which starts to thin out as you ascend. Continuing further, you will reach high altitude grasslands and traverse the rocky terrain. The landscape becomes remote with each step.

You will navigate the uphill trail witnessing barren yet beautiful highland scenery. The sights of glaciers and massive icefalls, and Mount Makalu ridges can be seen clearly on the route which is truly fascinating. In addition, the view of glacial streams and sharp ridges stretching along the route is stunning.

After a few hours of navigating scenic trails you make it to Shershong. It is an open plain area which is considered as the ideal place for a rest. 

From Shershong, the trail splits into two paths. There are two routes, a lower and a higher route, and both of them lead to the base camp same time. Generally, trekkers prefer the upper trail because of its drier conditions and mesmerizing scenery.

Continuing on by hiking through this raw, high-altitude terrain, you finally reach Makalu Base Camp. It is one of the most remote and spectacular locations in the Himalayas. 

This scenic base camp is surrounded by snow clad peaks, and presents the raw beauty of nature. There are a few teahouses at the base camp and you will stay at one of them overnight.

itinerary.title: Explore Makalu Base Camp (4,870 m / 15,978 ft).
itinerary.html:
On this day, you will stroll through the picturesque Makalu Base Camp. You may explore whole day exploring the area at your own pace. A few short hikes around base camp present stunning views of Mount Makalu and its surroundings.

The base camp of Makalu lies in a rugged landscape. You may spend a full day here wandering around the tranquil glacial lakes. If you like adventure, you can try visiting Makalu Advanced Base Camp. The route to base camp is challenging. You will have to navigate across glaciers following the steep snow covered slopes.

This section of the trek requires solid footing and strong focus.  At the Advanced Base Camp, you can witness awe inspiring and close-up view majestic peaks like Lhotse, Nuptse, Cho Oyu and several other Himalayan peaks. 

In addition, the sights of the glacier from the base camp are also truly fascinating. You can take your time to admire the experience before descending back to Makalu Base Camp, where you will stay for the night.

itinerary.title: Trek from Makalu Base Camp to Yangle Kharka (3,610 m / 11,844 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Yangle Kharka Elevation: 3,610 m
Trek Duration: 6 - 7 hours

After breakfast at Makalu Base Camp, you will begin your return journey to Yangle Kharka. You will follow a downhill path from the base camp. You will navigate the scenic trails, which lead to Shershong meadow and then take a short break. Afterward, you will continue the trek heading towards Langmale. 

From Langmale Kharka you will descend into the Barun River Valley. Continuing the adventure, you can see the landscape gradually transforming into lush green. You will move forward trekking along the rhododendron and juniper forests, feeling the serene ambiance.

Afterwards, you will trek for about 1.5 hours and reach Merek. Soon afterward, you will navigate forested section of pine trees. From here, you will trek for around 2 to 3 hours to reach Yangle Kharka which is your stop for the night.

itinerary.title: Trek from Yangle Kharka to Dobate (3,550 m / 11,647 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Dobate Elevation: 3,550 m
Trek Duration: 6-7 hours

Your destination for the 12th day of Makalu Base Camp Trek is Dobate. You will trek down through the Barun River Valley and walk through the dense forested section. The spectacular sights of Chamlang and many other nearby mountains can be seen on the route.

You will descend a path with blooming rhododendrons, cross a bridge with fluttering prayer flags and walk peacefully along the winding river on the way to Themathang. Afterwards, you will need to proceed carefully through a narrow and landslide-affected section.

As you walk through the dense rhododendron forest, you can enjoy the stunning mountain panoramas surrounding you. Continuing, you will navigate rocky trails and then pass through the green forest until you arrive at Dobate, which is your stop for the night.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dobate to Khongma (3,562 m / 11,686 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Danda Kharka: 3,562 m
Trek Duration: 6 - 7 hours

On the 13th day, you will return to Khongma Danda. You will navigate the Keke La Pass and Ghungru La Pass again on this day. From the top of each pass, the incredible mountain scenery can be seen. Navigating these pass again and witnessing the beautiful views is truly fascinating. 

You will enjoy navigating scenic trails and finally reach Sano Pokhari Danda, where you can spot a Hindu shrine. Continuing further, you will descend through stone steps and finally arrive in Khongma Dada. You will stay overnight in a teahouse in Khongma Danda.

itinerary.title: Trek from Khongma Danda to Seduwa 1,530 m / 5,020 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
Seduwa Elevation: 1,530 m
Trek Duration: 6 - 7 hours 

You will begin your journey to Seduwa on this day after a wholesome breakfast. You will follow a downhill path over long stone staircases and cross some suspension bridges. Afterwards, you will navigate the lush forest and make your way while enjoying the refreshing air of this tranquil area. 

Along the way, you can also see cardamom plantations. Then, you will walk through hillside farms, traditional Mani walls and and descend through the stone steps before finally arriving in the Seduwa village.

itinerary.title: Trek From Seduwa to Num and drive to Tumlingtar (518 m / 1,700 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Tumlingtar Elevation: 518 m
Drive Duration: 5 - 6 hours

This is the final day of the scenic Makalu Base Camp trek journey, when you will be traversing on foot. On this day, you will start your hike through a lively mountain village. You will walk through the vast bamboo forests, witnessing the exceptional natural beauty of the region. 

You will follow a winding trail and gradually make your way through the stunning Arun River. Afterwards, you will pass through a bridge and continue the journey while witnessing the alluring views of this scenic region. 

As you descend, you can see a stone staircase alongside the river. You will follow a series of uphill and downhill path.  You will then navigate the serene forest before you reach the peaceful Num Village.

From there, you will enjoy a scenic drive toward Tumlingtar, along winding roads. The scenery of distant snow capped peaks and green hillsides can be seen during this scenic drive.

The sight of terraced fields and hillside houses on the route makes your road journey intriguing. After a road journey of 5 to 6 hours, you will finally reach Tumlingtar and stay at one of the lodges overnight.

itinerary.title: Fly to Kathmandu from Tumlingtar
itinerary.html:
Kathmandu Elevation: 1,400 m
Flight Duration: 35 minutes 

On the 16th day, you will take a flight from Tumlingtar back to Kathmandu. In this short flight a stunning bird’s eye view of stunning landscapes of the country can be seen, elevating your overall sightseeing experience.

From your window seat, you can enjoy stunning sights of the Himalayan range.

After the airplane lands in Kathmandu we will transfer you directly to your hotel. After completing your trek, you may take a rest day to recover.

You may have concluded your exciting journey to Makalu Base Camp. But the exhilarating experiences and heartfelt memories you made during adventure are something that will be with you for long time.
