Weather in the Himalayas is never completely predictable. Snowfall, rain and strong wind can occur outside their usual seasons, so we advise trekkers to prepare for changing conditions regardless of the departure month.

Manaslu Circuit Trek in Spring

Spring brings milder daytime temperatures, longer daylight hours and colorful forests along the lower and middle sections of the trail. You can trek the Manaslu Circuit in March, April or May, although the weather and trail conditions change as the season progresses.

March

March marks the beginning of the main spring trekking season, with rising temperatures along the lower route and lingering winter conditions around Samdo, Dharamsala and Larkya La Pass. If you trek in early March, you may still encounter extreme cold, deep snow, or icy sections near the pass, so carry warm layers and gaiters along with microspikes if your guide recommends them. The snow usually begins to clear as the month progresses, and the trail becomes easier to follow later in March.

April

April is one of the best months for the Manaslu Circuit Trek because it brings comfortable daytime temperatures and favorable conditions at higher elevations. Rhododendrons flower along the forested sections, while clear mornings often reveal wide views of the surrounding mountains. Clouds can build during the afternoon, so you may need to begin longer walking days early. These favorable conditions attract more trekking groups, and teahouses in Samagaun, Samdo and Dharamsala can fill quickly, so arrange your accommodation in advance.

May

May brings warmer temperatures and longer daylight hours, while the snow around Larkya La Pass is usually less extensive than it is in early spring. However, afternoon clouds and pre-monsoon rain become more frequent as the month progresses. You may feel hot and humid while walking through the lower valleys, even though mornings and nights remain cold at higher elevations. Pack light, breathable clothing for the warmer sections along with insulated layers for Samagaun, Samdo, Dharamsala and the Larkya La crossing.

Manaslu Circuit Trek in Autumn

Autumn is the most popular season for the Manaslu Circuit Trek. Once the monsoon rain begins to clear, the air becomes cleaner, and mountain visibility improves. The main autumn trekking period runs from late September through October and November.

September

September marks the transition from the monsoon to autumn, so rain, cloud and landslides may still affect the lower route during the first half of the month. Conditions usually become drier and more stable towards late September, when the green valleys, full waterfalls and smaller crowds can make the trek especially rewarding. However, you should keep some flexibility in your schedule because lingering rain may still delay road travel or affect sections of the trail.

October

October is widely considered the best month for the Manaslu Circuit Trek because it usually brings stable weather, clear mountain views, and comfortable daytime temperatures for long walking days. These conditions also make it the busiest month, and the limited rooms at teahouses can fill quickly, particularly in Dharamsala, so book early and ask your trekking company to arrange accommodation in advance. Dashain and Tihar may also fall during this period, and although trekking services continue operating, increased transportation demand and changes to office schedules or staff availability can affect your travel arrangements.

November

November usually brings dry weather, clear skies and excellent mountain views, with the first half of the month offering particularly favorable conditions for crossing Larkya La Pass. But as winter approaches, temperatures fall steadily, and nights in Samagaun, Samdo and Dharamsala can drop well below freezing, sometimes causing water left outside to freeze overnight. If you depart later in November, carry a warmer sleeping bag and sufficient insulated clothing, and be prepared to change your schedule in case snowfall delays the pass crossing.

Can You Trek the Manaslu Circuit in Winter?

The Manaslu Circuit can be attempted in winter, but December, January and February bring freezing temperatures, shorter daylight hours and a greater risk of snow blocking Larkya La Pass.

January is typically the coldest month. During this month, high-altitude teahouses can close temporarily when visitor numbers decrease or heavy snow limits access. Frozen water pipes, limited food choices, and unheated rooms are also common in winter.

If you plan to trek the Manaslu circuit during winter, you need:

  • A flexible itinerary with contingency days
  • A sleeping bag suitable for severe sub-zero temperatures
  • Insulated boots, gloves and layered clothing
  • Microspikes or other traction equipment when advised
  • Confirmation that high-altitude teahouses are operating
  • Current information about snow depth and pass conditions
  • Willingness to turn back if Larkya La is unsafe

Winter offers quieter trails and clear mountain views on stable days. But the journey should not proceed simply because a fixed schedule states that the group has to cross the pass on a specific day.

Can You Trek the Manaslu Circuit During the Monsoon?

The Manaslu Circuit remains technically accessible during the monsoon, but June through August is not recommended for most travelers. Heavy rain can affect the lower trail, road access, and mountain visibility.

Common monsoon challenges include:

  • Landslides and falling rocks
  • Muddy or slippery paths
  • Swollen streams and waterfalls
  • Leeches in warm forested areas
  • Cloud obscuring mountain views
  • Flight and road delays
  • Damage to bridges or trail sections
  • High humidity and difficulty drying clothing

The upper Nubri Valley receives less rain than some lower sections, but trekkers must still travel through monsoon-affected roads and river valleys to reach it. This makes additional travel days and a flexible return schedule essential.

Manaslu Circuit Trek Temperatures

Temperatures on the Manaslu Circuit change considerably as you gain altitude. They can also vary with the season, sunlight, and wind. During the journey, you willl walk through warm lower villages during the day and face below-freezing conditions at Dharamsala or Larkya La Pass.

Approximate spring and autumn temperature ranges are:

Location or elevation

Spring and autumn daytime

Spring and autumn night

Lower route below 2,000 m

15°C to 25°C

5°C to 12°C

Namrung and upper Nubri Valley

8°C to 18°C

0°C to 7°C

Samagaun and Samdo

3°C to 12°C

-8°C to 2°C

Dharamsala and Larkya La

-5°C to 5°C

-15°C to -5°C

Use these figures as general packing guidelines, not guaranteed forecasts. Strong winds can make Larkya La feel much colder than the recorded temperature, while direct sunlight may make daytime walking feel warmer, even when the air remains cold.

How to Choose the Best Trekking Month?

Choose your trekking month according to the weather, scenery, trail traffic and amount of flexibility you have in your schedule:

  • Best overall conditions: October
  • Warmer spring trekking: April
  • Clear views with colder nights: November
  • Flowering forests: April and early May
  • Green post-monsoon scenery: Late September
  • Quieter trails: March, late November or early December
  • Lowest chance of monsoon disruption: October and November

If your international flights are fixed, give greater importance to stable roads and trail conditions than to finding a quieter month. A less crowded period offers little benefit if rain or snowfall delays the drive, closes part of the trail or prevents you from crossing Larkya La on schedule.

At Base Camp Adventure, we always check the latest weather reports, road access, teahouse availability and trail conditions around Larkya La Pass before you leave. Your guide can then adjust departure times or daily plans when necessary, but weather and mountain conditions mean that no specific date can guarantee a safe pass crossing.

Accommodation on the Manaslu Circuit Trek

Accommodation on the Manaslu Circuit Trek is provided in locally operated teahouses. The rooms are simple but functional; they usually have two single beds, mattresses, pillows and blankets. The package includes two nights in a Kathmandu hotel and twin-sharing teahouse accommodation during the trek. Facilities become more basic as you climb towards Samagaun, Samdo and Dharamsala.

What are Teahouse Rooms Like?

A standard teahouse room provides 2 single beds, foam mattresses, pillows, blankets, a small table or shelf, basic wooden or stone walls, and a door that locks from the inside. Most bedrooms do not have heating, even when the dining room has a stove. Furthermore, rooms above 3,000 m get very cold, and the thin walls may allow noise from neighbouring rooms, so if you are a light sleeper, you should carry earplugs.

Are Private Rooms Available?

Private rooms may be available, but they cannot be guaranteed at every stop. You may need to share during busy months, bad weather or overnight stays in villages with limited accommodation, especially Dharamsala. A single-room supplement only applies where a private room can be secured.

Are Attached Bathrooms Available?

Attached bathrooms are not common along the trail. Instead, shared toilets are standard along most of the route. Lower villages may have Western-style or squat toilets with running water, while higher facilities are more basic and may freeze overnight. Carry toilet paper, hand sanitiser, biodegradable soap, wet wipes, personal hygiene products, a quick-drying towel and a headlamp. Use the designated waste container unless the teahouse confirms that toilet paper can be flushed.

Can You Take a Hot Shower?

Yes, some teahouses provide hot showers for an additional charge. Lower villages may have gas-heated showers, while higher settlements often provide a bucket of warm water. Availability depends on water, fuel, temperature, solar heating and demand. At higher elevations, wet wipes are more practical until you descend to a warmer village.

What Food is Available During the Trek?

Teahouses serve simple, filling meals that provide energy for long walking days. The menu varies by village but commonly includes:

  • Dal bhat with rice, lentil soup, vegetable curry, pickle and seasonal side dishes
  • Fried rice
  • Noodles and pasta
  • Potatoes and vegetable curry
  • Momos
  • Soup
  • Tibetan bread and chapati
  • Porridge
  • Eggs
  • Pancakes and toast
  • Seasonal vegetables
  • Tea, coffee and hot lemon

Food choices become more limited at higher elevations because ingredients must be carried over long distances.

What is Dal Bhat?

“Dal” is lentil soup and “bhat” is a Nepali word for rice. Dal bhat is a traditional Nepali meal of rice, lentil soup and vegetable curry, often served with pickle, spinach or other side dishes. Its combination of carbohydrates, protein and salt makes it a practical trekking meal. Some teahouses also provide extra rice and lentils at no additional charge.

Is Meat Available?

Yes, meat appears on many teahouse menus, but because refrigeration is limited, it may not always be  fresh. Vegetarian meals are safer at higher elevations, while eggs, lentils, beans and cheese can provide alternative sources of protein.

Are Vegetarian and Vegan Meals Available?

Yes, vegetarian meals are widely available, including dal bhat, veg noodles, fried rice, potato dishes, soup and Tibetan bread. Vegan meals are also possible, but explain your requirements clearly because apparently plant-based dishes may contain butter, milk, cheese or eggs. Carrying a written Nepali explanation can prevent misunderstandings.

Can Special Diets Be Managed?

Some dietary requirements can be accommodated, but choices are limited compared with Kathmandu. Tell us about your allergies, coeliac disease or strict dietary needs beforehand so we can prepare a special diet plan for you. Carry suitable snacks and prescribed emergency medication, and ask how each meal is prepared because separate cooking equipment may not be available.

Is the Food Safe?

Freshly cooked food served hot is safe. Avoid raw or unpeeled produce, uncovered food, and unfresh meat, particularly at higher elevations. Wash or sanitise your hands, drink treated water and carry oral rehydration salts as well. Tell your guide immediately if you feel vomiting or diarrhoea developing because dehydration can make acclimatization more difficult.

Is Drinking Water Available?

Yes, drinking water is available at teahouses and settlements throughout the Manaslu Circuit, but you should never drink untreated tap, stream or river water.

Safe drinking water options include:

  • Boiled water from teahouses
  • Water treated with purification tablets
  • Water passed through a reliable trekking filter
  • Filtered water followed by chemical treatment
  • Factory-sealed bottled water where available

Boiled water becomes more expensive as you gain altitude because fuel is limited. Carrying refillable bottles and treating the water yourself costs less and reduces plastic waste. You need at least two bottles or a hydration system with enough capacity for each walking day, while an insulated bottle can prevent your water from freezing near Dharamsala and Larkya La Pass.

How Much Water Should You Drink?

Drink steadily throughout the day instead of waiting until you feel thirsty. The amount you need depends on your body size, the temperature and how hard you are walking. Dark urine can indicate dehydration, but forcing yourself to drink too much can also be harmful. Tea and soup contribute to your fluid intake, while alcohol does not help with hydration.

Are Electricity, Charging and Wi-Fi Available?

Yes, many teahouses provide electricity, device charging and Wi-Fi for an additional fee, but these services become less reliable at higher elevations. Solar power can be affected by cloud, cold weather, high demand and limited operating hours, so carry a fully charged power bank and keep your batteries warm. Wi-Fi can be slow or unavailable, and mobile coverage is inconsistent. Tell your family before the trek that several days without contact can be normal and use your guide or Base Camp Adventure’s operations team as the main point of contact during an emergency.

Trekking Responsibly in the Manaslu Region

Responsible trekking means protecting the environment, respecting local communities and reducing the pressure your visit places on this remote Himalayan region. Simple choices involving waste, water, energy, clothing and behaviour can make a meaningful difference.

The Manaslu Circuit passes through settlements influenced by ancient Tibetan Buddhist traditions, which the locals value immensely. To show respect to their beliefs and values, trekkers should follow local customs, request permission before photographing people and avoid treating villages or religious sites as tourist displays.

  • Reduce Plastic Waste: Minimize waste by carrying reusable water bottles, using refillable containers, and packing out all trash like snack wrappers and batteries, as disposal in remote villages is difficult.
  • Use Water and Energy Carefully: Conserve limited resources by taking short showers, switching off lights, using only necessary devices, and following teahouse guidelines for water and heating.
  • Respect Local Culture: Show appreciation for Tibetan Buddhist traditions by walking clockwise around religious monuments, dressing modestly, asking before taking photos, and avoiding physical contact with sacred objects.
  • Support Local Communities: Contribute to the local economy by patronizing community-owned businesses, purchasing genuine handicrafts, and paying fair prices rather than aggressive bargaining; avoid giving money or sweets directly to children.
  • Respect Porters and Trekking Staff: Prioritize staff well-being by keeping luggage within strict weight limits, packing securely, respecting their professional boundaries, and tipping fairly without pressuring them to work in unsafe conditions.
  • Do not Harm Wildlife and Natural Areas: Observe animals from a distance without feeding or disturbing them; do not remove natural objects or use rivers for washing with chemicals, and never fly a drone without permission.
  • Use Toilets and Campsites Properly: Use teahouse facilities whenever available and adhere to "Leave No Trace" principles by packing out all sanitary waste and avoiding independent camping without proper authorization.
  • Follow Leave No Trace Principles: Protect the environment by staying on established trails, disposing of waste responsibly, leaving all natural and cultural artifacts in place, and being considerate of others.

sections.title: What to Pack for the Manaslu Circuit Trek?
sections.html:
Pack layered clothing, trekking boots that fit comfortably, a warm sleeping bag, rain protection and the essential personal items needed for warm valleys, freezing nights and possible snow or strong wind. Keep your kit lightweight because unnecessary equipment adds fatigue and increases the load carried by you or your porter.

Essential Trekking Equipment

  • Medium-sized trekking daypack
  • Duffel bag for porter-carried luggage
  • Waterproof daypack cover
  • Sleeping bag rated to approximately -15°C
  • Adjustable trekking poles
  • Headlamp with spare batteries
  • Two reusable water bottles or a hydration system
  • Water-purification tablets or a reliable filter
  • UV-protective sunglasses
  • Microspikes when recommended
  • Lightweight gaiters
  • Dry bags or waterproof packing sacks

Base Camp Adventure provides a sleeping bag, down jacket and duffel bag as part of the package. Confirm the size, temperature rating and availability before leaving Kathmandu.

Clothing for the Upper and Lower Route

Layer your clothing so you can adjust it as the altitude, temperature, wind and walking intensity change. Choose synthetic or merino wool materials where possible because cotton dries slowly and becomes cold when wet.

Base Layers

  • Two or three moisture-wicking trekking shirts
  • One or two thermal tops
  • One or two pairs of thermal leggings
  • Trekking underwear
  • Sports bras where required

Insulating Layers

  • Lightweight fleece jacket
  • Warm mid-layer
  • Insulated down or synthetic jacket
  • Warm trekking trousers
  • Comfortable clothing for teahouse evenings

Keep your insulated jacket in your daypack during the Larkya La crossing rather than packing it in the porter’s duffel bag.

Outer Layers

  • Waterproof and windproof shell jacket
  • Waterproof over-trousers
  • Rain poncho, if preferred
  • Wind-resistant trekking trousers

Your outer shell protects you from rain, snow and wind. An insulated jacket provides warmth but cannot replace a waterproof and windproof layer.

Footwear

Wear water-resistant trekking boots with ankle support and a reliable sole. Make sure they fit around the shape of your feet before travelling and test them with the same socks you will wear during the trek, as new or poorly fitted boots can cause blisters, bruised toes and pain on long descents. Also carry lightweight shoes or sandals for teahouses, 3 to 5 pairs of trekking socks, 2 pairs of warm socks, sock liners if needed, blister treatment and preventive tape, as well as microspikes, depending on trail conditions.

Cold Weather Protection Gear

Carry enough insulated clothing for temperatures below freezing. Keep your jacket, gloves and hat in your daypack on the pass-crossing day because the weather can change before you can access the porter’s duffel bag.

Essential cold-weather items include:

  • Insulated down or synthetic jacket
  • Thermal top and leggings
  • Warm hat or beanie
  • Neck gaiter or buff
  • Insulated gloves
  • Lightweight inner gloves
  • Warm trekking socks
  • Windproof outer layer
  • Cold-rated sleeping bag
  • Insulated water bottle
  • Hand warmers, if desired

Sun and Rain Protection

Carry protection from strong UV exposure, rain and snow throughout the trek. Sunglasses are especially important around snow because reflected sunlight can damage your eyes. Along with UV-protective sunglasses, carry high-SPF sunscreen, SPF lip balm, sun hat or cap, waterproof jacket and trousers, daypack rain cover, and waterproof bags for documents and electronics.

Personal Hygiene Items

Teahouse bathrooms are basic and hot showers are not always available. So you need to carry a small hygiene kit. Take all non-biodegradable waste with you until you reach a suitable disposal point.

Your hygiene kit should include toothbrush, toothpaste, toilet paper, hand sanitiser, biodegradable soap, wet wipes, quick-drying towel, personal sanitary products, moisturiser, nail clippers, small rubbish bags, prescription toiletries, and earplugs if needed.

First-Aid Supplies & Medication

Your guide carries a group first-aid kit, but for personal use, you must bring your prescribed medication and basic supplies. If you need altitude medication, speak with a qualified medical professional about it rather than taking prescription drugs based on another trekker’s advice.

Consider packing:

  • Prescribed medication
  • Blister plasters
  • Adhesive bandages
  • Medical tape
  • Antiseptic wipes
  • Pain relief
  • Oral rehydration salts
  • Diarrhoea medication
  • Antihistamine
  • Throat lozenges
  • Personal allergy medication
  • Elastic support bandage
  • Insect repellent for lower elevations

Carry essential medication in your hand luggage when flying to Nepal and keep it in your daypack during the trek. Bring extra doses in case weather or transport delays extend your journey.

Documents and Money

Bring:

  • Original passport
  • Nepal tourist visa
  • Copies of your passport and visa
  • Travel insurance certificate
  • Insurance policy number
  • Emergency-assistance contact details
  • Trekking permits
  • Passport-style photographs
  • International flight details
  • Emergency contact information
  • Nepalese rupees in smaller denominations
  • Bank card for use in Kathmandu

You need to carry their printed copies in a waterproof bag because internet access is unreliable. Still, for added security, store digital backups on your phone and in secure cloud storage.

Electronics

Bring only the electronics you expect to use, along with a power bank, suitable cables and spare batteries. Charging costs extra and can be unavailable at higher elevations, so keep your phone and batteries inside your sleeping bag or an insulated pouch at night.

  • Mobile phone
  • Camera, if required
  • Power bank
  • Charging cables
  • Universal travel adapter
  • Spare camera batteries
  • Spare headlamp batteries
  • Waterproof electronics pouch
  • Offline maps and important documents

Snacks and Comfort Items

Teahouses provide meals throughout the route, but familiar snacks can give you extra energy during long walking days. Choose compact items with minimal packaging to reduce the waste you carry. Consider carrying snacks and comfort items like electrolyte powder, sweets or chocolate, instant coffee or tea, a small book, a journal and pen, playing cards, an inflatable pillow, a lightweight clothesline, repair tape, and a multipurpose pocket tool.

What Should Be in Your Daypack?

Your daypack should hold everything you may need before reaching the next teahouse. Keep it under 7 kgs (15 lbs) so you don’t get tired during long climbs. You should carry water & purification supplies, waterproof jacket & trousers, insulated jacket, gloves, hat & neck gaiter, sunscreen, lip balm, sunglasses, snacks, personal medication, first-aid essentials, passport and permit copies, phone, camera, power bank, headlamp, toilet paper, hand sanitiser, trekking poles, money, rain cover, and emergency contact details.

How Much Luggage Can a Porter Carry?

One porter can carry up to 25kg (55 lbs) of combined luggage, normally shared by 2 trekkers. Each traveller should pack only the agreed weight and avoid adding unreported items after the duffel bags have been checked. A porter may leave earlier or arrive later than the trekking group, so do not place medication, water, rainwear, warm layers, documents or other immediately required items in the porter’s load.

Final Packing Tips

  • Wear your boots until it fits the shape of your feet before travelling.
  • Test your sleeping bag and trekking poles.
  • Pack clothing that can be worn in several combinations.
  • Use waterproof inner bags rather than relying only on a rain cover.
  • Label your duffel bag clearly.
  • Bring spare batteries for the headlamp.
  • Avoid carrying large bottles of toiletries.
  • Leave unnecessary city clothing in Kathmandu.
  • Check seasonal snow and rain conditions before finalising the list.
  • Confirm which rental equipment Base Camp Adventure provides.
  • Weigh your daypack and duffel bag before departure.
  • Keep all essential items with you during the Larkya La crossing.

sections.title: FAQs
sections.html:
How many days does the Manaslu Circuit Trek take?

The Base Camp Adventure itinerary takes 13 days, including arrival and departure days in Kathmandu. The trekking route begins from Machha Khola and finishes at Dharapani before returning to Kathmandu.

What is the highest point of the trek?

Larkya La Pass is the highest point at 5,106 m (16,752 feet). It is crossed during the long trekking day from Dharamsala to Bimthang.

How difficult is the Manaslu Circuit Trek?

The Manaslu Circuit is a moderate to strenuous high-altitude trek. Long walking days, steep terrain, basic accommodation, cold weather and the Larkya La crossing require good fitness, suitable preparation and gradual acclimatization. However, well-prepared beginners can complete the Manaslu Circuit safely.

Is previous trekking experience required?

No. Previous high-altitude trekking experience is helpful but not compulsory. Physically active beginners can attempt the route with proper training, realistic expectations, appropriate equipment and professional guidance.

Can beginners complete the Manaslu Circuit?

Yes, well-prepared beginners can complete the trek. They should train consistently before travelling, walk at a controlled pace and immediately report any altitude-related symptoms to the guide.

Is the Manaslu Circuit harder than the Everest Base Camp Trek?

The Manaslu Circuit includes longer and more remote trail sections and provides fewer facilities, which can indeed make it feel harder. Still, difficulty depends on the itinerary, weather, fitness, and individual response to altitude.

Can I trek the Manaslu Circuit alone?

No, foreign travellers must arrange the restricted-area permits through a registered Nepali trekking agency and trek with a licensed guide. Independent trekking is not permitted in the controlled Manaslu area.

Is there a minimum group-size requirement?

Restricted-area permit rules can require at least two trekkers to be registered together with a licensed guide. But if you are alone, you can still go on the trek by asking travel agencies to arrange a private departure or join another confirmed trekker.

What permits are required?

The Manaslu circuit trek requires four permits: Manaslu Restricted Area Permit, Manaslu Conservation Area Permit, Annapurna Conservation Area Permit, and a TIMS card. Travel agencies can process these documents before the trek.

What is the best month for the Manaslu Circuit Trek?

October is the most popular month because it normally provides stable weather and clear mountain views. April and November are also excellent choices, while late September and early May can be suitable with greater flexibility.

Is altitude sickness a concern?

Yes, the route climbs above 5,000 m, so Acute Mountain Sickness is a genuine risk. Gradual ascent, hydration, rest, honest symptom reporting and timely descent when necessary are essential.

Is the Manaslu Circuit Trek safe?

The trek can be completed safely with suitable acclimatization, professional guidance and careful decisions about weather and altitude. However, mountain trekking always involves risks such as illness, snowfall, landslides, trail damage and transportation delays.

What accommodation is available?

Trekkers stay in locally operated teahouses with simple twin-sharing rooms. Bathrooms are usually shared, bedrooms are generally unheated and facilities become more basic near Samdo and Dharamsala.

Is food included in the package?

Yes. Breakfast, lunch and dinner are included during the trekking days. Breakfast is included at the Kathmandu hotel, while lunch and dinner in Kathmandu are separate personal expenses.

Is drinking water available along the trail?

Yes. Teahouses provide boiled water, and natural water sources are available in many locations. All untreated water must be filtered, boiled or chemically purified before drinking.

Is Wi-Fi available on the Manaslu Circuit?

Wi-Fi is available at selected teahouses, but the connection can be slow, expensive or unavailable. Mobile-network coverage is also inconsistent, especially in remote and high-altitude sections.

Do I need a sleeping bag?

Yes. A warm sleeping bag is essential because teahouse bedrooms are not heated. Base Camp Adventure provides a sleeping bag for trekking use, but travellers should confirm its temperature rating before departure.

Is a porter included in the trek cost?

No. Porter service is optional and currently costs USD 275 per porter for the trek. One porter is normally shared by two travellers, subject to the confirmed luggage limit.

How much cash should I carry?

Carry enough Nepalese rupees for drinks, charging, Wi-Fi, showers, snacks, tips and unexpected expenses throughout the trek. ATMs and card-payment facilities are not reliably available along the route.

Can the itinerary be customized?

Yes, the itinerary can be adjusted according to available time, fitness, acclimatization needs and preferred services. Additional trekking days, private transportation, porter support or a Tsum Valley extension will change the final cost and permit arrangements.

Can I combine the Manaslu Circuit with Tsum Valley?

Yes, the circuit can be combined with the Tsum Valley Trek, but the journey becomes considerably longer. An additional restricted-area permit and a revised itinerary are required.

What travel insurance do I need?

Your policy must cover trekking up to at least 5,106 m, emergency medical treatment and helicopter evacuation in Nepal. Check the altitude limit and exclusions carefully because standard travel insurance may not provide sufficient coverage.

Can children complete the Manaslu Circuit?

Older children with strong trekking experience and suitable physical preparation may be able to complete the route after professional medical advice. The cold, altitude, remoteness and long pass-crossing day make the trek unsuitable for most young children.

What happens if Larkya La Pass is closed?

The guide will assess current weather, snow and trail conditions before attempting the crossing. The group may wait, modify the itinerary, descend or turn back when continuing would be unsafe.

How far in advance should I book?

Book several weeks or months ahead for an October, November, April or May departure. Early confirmation allows enough time to arrange permits, guides, accommodation, transportation and any requested porter or private-jeep services.

faqs.q: How Much Does the Manaslu Circuit Trek Cost?
faqs.a: The 13-day Manaslu Circuit Trek currently costs USD 1,130 per adult with Base Camp Adventure. This package covers the main accommodation, meals, transportation, permits, guide service and trekking support required for the journey. Your final spending will depend on whether you hire a porter, upgrade to private transportation, purchase equipment or pay for drinks, insurance, tips and other personal expenses.

faqs.q: Is Porter Service Included?
faqs.a: No, porter service is optional and currently costs USD 275 per porter. One porter is normally shared by two trekkers, so confirm the luggage limit before departure. Keep water, clothing, medication, documents, snacks, electronics and other daytime essentials in your daypack because you may not access the porter’s duffel bag while walking.

faqs.q: How Much Does a Private Jeep Cost to Machha Khola and Dharapani to Kathmandu or Pokhara?
faqs.a: A private jeep currently costs USD 250 per vehicle, per way from Kathmandu to Machha Khola or from Dharapani to Kathmandu or Pokhara. It makes your departure more flexible and offers fewer passenger stops, but rough roads, weather and construction can still affect the journey.

faqs.q: What Personal Expenses Should You Budget For?
faqs.a: You should budget for drinking water, tea, coffee, snacks, showers, charging, Wi-Fi, laundry, extra meals, souvenirs, tips and unexpected purchases. Carry enough Nepalese rupees for the entire trek because ATMs and card payments are unreliable outside Kathmandu. Include smaller notes (NPR 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100) because teahouses may struggle to change large denominations.

faqs.q: Does the Trek Price Include Travel Insurance?
faqs.a: No, you must purchase your travel insurance separately. Your policy should cover trekking up to at least 5,106 m, helicopter evacuation, medical treatment, hospitalization, trip disruption, repatriation and baggage problems. Confirm the altitude limit in writing because standard holiday insurance may exclude high-altitude trekking.

faqs.q: Are Tips Included in the Package Price?
faqs.a: No, tips are not included. Tipping is voluntary, but you may thank your guide, porter and supporting staff according to the service provided, the trek’s difficulty and any extra assistance received. Give tips directly to the staff members at the end of the trek.

faqs.q: Can the Package Price Change?
faqs.a: Yes, the price may change if permit fees, fuel costs, hotel rates or local service charges increase. Private transport, porter service, single rooms, hotel upgrades, extra nights, additional acclimatization days, customized routes and adding Tsum Valley Trek will also increase the total.

overview:
As a home of the Himalayas, Nepal boasts innumerable trekking trails for adventurers who want to escape the ruckus. Nepal's every trek destination is incredibly charming with splendid sceneries, dramatic landscapes, and snow peaks.

But, despite so many of them, it’s Mardi Himal that often draws the attention of hikers and compels them to stop by this charming village. It comes with eye-popping scenery, major attractions, and a serene atmosphere.

With the dramatic hills and limitless steep terrains, Mardi Himal is not an easy endeavor. However, for those hiring a private chopper, the trek is nothing but a walk in the park for just a cost of a few bucks and a day. The trip will take no longer than an hour to reach the camp and offer panoramic views.

Mardi Himal Base Camp helicopter tour is a scenic expedition of the Himalayas over sweeping valleys, towering hills, and waterfalls. It’s a short trip of the Mardi Himal without taking the winding trails that have lots of twists and turns.

It scraps the long walking trails for visitors and offers them an extravagant trip to the base camp. The heli tour is an alternative for those who are down to crunch time or uninterested in climbing the hills and valleys.

The flight normally takes off from Tribhuvan airport and hover above sweeping landscapes and cliffs to arrive at the base camp. The trip will last for about 20-30 minutes, during which the passengers will get a peek of glistening mountains, picture-perfect landscapes, and vast meadows.

Highlights of Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter Tour

  • Pleasing flight with the glimpses of lofty hills, vast meadows, and river valleys
  • A pristine view of snow-capped mountains, including Mardi Himal and Gangapurna
  • Exposed to diverse culture, rich tradition, and festivities
  • Witness a unique species of wild animals and birds
  • Scout the traditional villages inhabited by Tamang people
  • Reposeful hot spring at Jhinu Danda

sections.title: Best time for Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter Tour
sections.html:
Given the unforeseeable weather of the Himalayas, you must choose the right time to visit Mardi Himal Base Camp. Most visitors often ignore the importance of picking the best time for the trip and get it canceled.

Naturally, Autumn is the best time for the Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter tour with mild weather and scenic views. After months of blazing summer and downpour, Autumn stands in a placid climate with warm days and cold nights.

It’s easy for aviators to flee the aircraft in the Annapurna region with sunny days and great visibility throughout autumn. Chances of flight cancelation are rare during the season to hire the chopper anytime you like.

The base camp’s average temperature is around 15-20 Degrees Celsius during the month, making the trip even better. The sceneries are impeccable in Autumn with colorful tree leaves, an eye-striking view of snow peaks, and vibrant valleys.

Spring is another delightful time to be at the Mardi Himal Base Camp as it too offers a pleasant atmosphere. With the winter fading slowly, the weather gets tender in the season. The trails are easy to navigate in spring with the incessant cool breeze and warmer weather.

The views are magnificent during the season, with blooming flowers, green verdures, and stunning landscapes. With the start of the season, hikers will have a chance to witness exotic wildlife and migratory birds in the forest.

Outdoor activities are much more fun in spring, with fresh air and sunlight all day long. Trekkers can hear the sounds of birds chirping from far off while also taking a peek at the soaring mountains.

Monsoon and winter are arguably the terrible times for Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter Tour, with the flight often getting called off. The weather is awful during the season, with continuous rainfall and windstorm. In winter, flights are often delayed or postponed due to foggy weather and snowfall.

Meanwhile, the aviators have to tackle the gloomy weather with storms and rain to reach the base camp. They’ll also face the challenges of landing the helicopter at the airstrip, often drenched and slick in monsoon.

Food and Accommodation

You might not need food and accommodation during the 1 day helicopter tour to Mardi Himal Base Camp.

But, if you change your plan from a helicopter tour to a trek, the following information might be helpful to you.

Food and accommodation are often a matter of concern for travelers visiting Mardi Himal Base Camp, especially during the trekking season. With visitors swarming from all around the world, it’s hard to find lodging that’s not filled.

Most of the trekkers climbing the base camp will make reservations of the accommodation in advance to avoid all the fuss. Visitors waiting until the last minute to get a room will often find themselves without the dwelling.

However, those who take a heli flight to Mardi Himal Base Camp will not have to worry about the accommodation and rather have a comfortable ride. Foods available in the tea house at the base camp are incredibly delicious and nutritious.

The menu often makes switches depending on the season due to the accessibility of goods. Most of the ingredients are fresh produce from the farm and prepared using local spices, making the food delicious.

It’s often the authentic Nepali dish such as rice, vegetables, and pulses that make it to the dining table. However, travelers can also order other cuisines, including Western and Asian, based on their palette.

Things to be considered during Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter Tour

Trekking Mardi Himal Base Camp via helicopter may be easier than walking the trails, but even the excursion has its own shortcomings. Travelers will have to overcome multiple challenges to arrive at the base camp and catch a glimpse of dazzling snow peaks and unique landforms. Some of the difficulties that travelers of Mardi Himal Base Camp might have to face are as follows.

1. Altitude Sickness

The chances of trekkers suffering from altitude sickness are always higher when traveling to high altitudes without rest. Considering that, hikers of Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter Tour are always concerned about the acute mountain sickness during their excursion.

Due to time constraints to adapt to the base camp’s temperature, they often witness the mildest altitude sickness. But, when ignored, the illness can become severe and even cause hypoxemia. This is exactly why Mardi Himal Base Camp’s trekkers are recommended to get a break before going high.

Acute mountain sickness usually happens due to the low air density at high elevation, causing trekkers to feel unease and disquiet. Symptoms like dizziness, headache, and trouble sleeping are common when exposed to the base camp.

Hence, visitors of Mardi Himal Base Camp must take preventive measures before flying to the village. They must take a trip to the base camp with the prescribed medicines or get help from the physician if the situation worsens.

2. Weather

Another major challenge for travelers of the Mardi Himal Base Camp helicopter tour is the severe weather and climate, often impeding the trip. The climatic condition in the Annapurna region is uncertain, with the weather changing every now and then.

This apparently makes it tough for visitors to decide when to do the Mardi Himal Base Camp helicopter tour and when not. Winter, out of all seasons, bears extreme weather with snowfall and mist, which inhibits vision and makes it tough for aviators to fly the chopper.

The continuous rainfall can also bring the trip to a halt, making the landing difficult. Hence, visitors must pick the right time to take a flight to Mardi Himal Base Camp and avoid delays. They can also stay up-to-date with the weather forecast, book the heli tour accordingly or take necessary precautions.

Why take the Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter Tour?

With endless troughs and valleys, climbing Mardi Himal Base Camp is not merely difficult but also tiring. It takes a lot of time to navigate the trail, discouraging the holidaymakers who have planned the trip for a little time. Thanks to the private helicopter service in Nepal, which offers multiple flights to the base camp and makes the journey a lot easier. Here are a few of the reasons why visitors prefer to take a helicopter tour of Mardi Himal Base Camp.

1. Easy accessibility

Traveling to Mardi Himal Base Camp gets real easy with the helicopter as one can book the chopper at any time needed. With so many airlines offering numerous packages, the flights are easily accessible.

Travelers can choose to board the helicopter from Kathmandu or Pokhara to end up at the base camp. They can rent the heli online or through the agent, whichever is convenient. Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter tour will give the trekkers access to remote locations and even provide mesmerizing views.

2. Scenic views

Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter Tour offers breathtaking scenery to travelers from the outset of the trip. It will provide travelers an aerial view of snow-capped mountains, deep valleys, and gorges. Reaching up to an elevation of 18,000 ft, the view is exquisite and soul-stirring. Visitors will be able to get a panoramic view of Mardi Himal along with Annapurna and Machhapuchhre.

3. No delays

Unlike commercial flights, travelers won’t have to wait for the other passengers to start a private helicopter trip. It’s rare for the flights to get canceled when hiring the chopper unless the weather gets bad. The flight won’t stop at different points and straight off land at the base camp, providing spectacular views.

Cost of Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter Tour

The cost of the Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter tour depends on the number of passengers on board. The more the number of travelers, the lesser the cost with the price being shared amongst the flyers. That being said, the helicopter won’t accommodate more than five passengers at a time that may see the changes in cost.

Unless you choose to go single, the cost to charter a helicopter for Mardi Himal Base Camp is US$200 to US$2500 per person for a group of five. The price will gradually see a rise if the passengers traveling on the helicopter fall off.

Those who choose to go solo will be charged US$1,100 or more, depending on the service available. The flight will take around 30-40 minutes to arrive at the ridge and proffer the sublime view of mountains, glaciers, and cliffs.

faqs.q: 1. What is the total weight limit on the helicopter?
faqs.a: Passengers embarking on the flight to Mardi Himal Base Camp aren't allowed to carry more than <strong>50 kgs </strong>of luggage. The maximum weight limit of a charter commuting the ridge is <strong>450 kg, </strong>including the passenger of 5 and their luggage.

faqs.q: 2. Do I have to get travel insurance?
faqs.a: Travelers of Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter tour are always recommended to get travel insurance. This will protect them from unfortunate events, including medical emergencies, theft, and damage or loss of luggage.

faqs.q: 3. How long does the helicopter land at Mardi Himal Base Camp?
faqs.a: At Mardi Himal Base Camp, the helicopter will stop for about<strong> 30 minutes </strong>for visitors to explore the village. During the time, you can catch sight of medieval villages, captivating highlands, and beautiful monasteries. Visitors flying to the camp before will get to witness the beautiful sunrise over the snow-capped mountains.

faqs.q: 4. Are children allowed to take the flight to the base camp?
faqs.a: Of course, children are allowed for a helicopter tour of Mardi Himal Base Camp. However, the kids must be accompanied by their parents or caretaker so that they are looked after. It must be ensured that they are comfortable riding the chopper.

faqs.q: 5. What kind of clothes is required during the trip?
faqs.a:
The gears required for Mardi Himal Base Camp Helicopter Tour rely heavily on which time of the year you’re traveling the region. If you’re traveling the camp during spring and autumn, lightweight clothes with an extra down jacket are needed to withstand the winds in the ridge.

Likewise, if the trip is happening in winter, travelers will need warm clothes with thermal, a fleece jacket, and a mitten. They are also suggested to stay updated with the weather to forbid any dramatic events.

faqs.q: 6. What types of flights are available in the Annapurna region?
faqs.a: Travelers normally have two options either to fly solo or with the group. If you want to enjoy a private trip along with your friends and family, then take a private flight. On the contrary, you’ll be joined by a group of at most five on the chopper.

faqs.q: 7. Are the pilots well-trained and experienced?
faqs.a: All our pilots flying to the base camp are professionals with experience of decades. They are used to flying in the Himalayas and know how to handle situations.

faqs.q: 8. Are there medical emergency facilities available?
faqs.a: Our pilots and ground crew members and personnel staff are always there to help the passengers. We provide emergency evacuations and supplement oxygen to those who’ve critical health conditions.

overview:
Mardi Himal Trek is a new short and amazing trekking route in the east of Annapurna Base Camp (4,130 m). This circuit trek leads you too dense forested areas through rocky hilly terrains with no human settlement en route. This is a perfect trek for travelers who want to spend time in nature with no crowd. This trek offers breath-taking views of valleys and beautiful landscapes of the Annapurna region. The trek also features gorgeous views of the Annapurna massif, Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), and Mardi Himal (5,553 m) making it a visually satiating retreat.

Your trek will start from Pokhara. You will drive to Kande which is a 1-hour drive and begin your trek. The trail will give you an amazing view of the Himalayas. The trail will lead you to Australian Camp (2,060 m), and after a little walk downhill, you will reach Pothana. Climbing up ahead you will reach Deurali, and after an hour walk through pine forests and rhododendron forests, you will reach Forest Camp. It is a quiet walk from Forest Camp to Low Camp as there are no settlements along this route. The trek moves through tranquil bamboo, rhododendron, and oak forests with the peace only broken by the hissing of streams and chirping of birds. The trail gives you exceptional views of snow-capped mountains like Annapurna South (7,219 m) and Patal Hiunchuli (6,441 m). The final destination of the trek, Upper View Point, offers a mind-blowing vista of the Annapurna massif along with the peeking peak of Machhapuchhre (6,993 m) and a close-up view of Mardi Himal (5,553 m). The return trail takes you to the Siding village which is located very close to the beautiful waterfall from where you retrace your way to Pokhara and then to Kathmandu.

Distance: 200 km
Duration: 7 Hours
Accommodation: Hotel
This city is full of natural as well as cultural heritage sites such as lakes, caves, temples of Buddhist and Hindus along with mountains. As you approach the city, there are wonderful views to the north across the hills and Phewa lake to the white peaks of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. This drive will take most of the morning, leaving much of the afternoon for a relaxing boat ride on Phewa Lake

itinerary.title: Drive for approximately 30 minutes from Pokhara to Kande, followed by a scenic trek to Deurali (2,100 m / 6,890 ft), 3-4 hours
itinerary.html:
Trek Duration: 3-4 Hours
Accommodation: Guest House

Today after breakfast, you will drive to Kande via Pokhara Baglung Highway which will be about 1-hour drive. From Kande, you will start the trek as you ascend past Australian Camp with a stunning view of Machhapuchhre (6,993 m) in the backdrop. The trail will give you a panoramic view of the Annapurna range and Pokhara valley that will further lead you to Deurali.

itinerary.title: Trek from Deurali to Low Camp (2,970 m / 9,744 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: From Deurali, you will climb uphill towards Forest Camp. Trekking through a forested trail full of rhododendron trees, you reach Forest Camp and then you will gradually climb through beautiful rhododendron, bamboo, and oak forests to reach Low Camp. The walk will be 4 hours long, and you will get stunning views of Machhapuchhre (6,993 m) and Mardi Himal (5,553 m). You will stay overnight at Low Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek from Low Camp to High Camp (3,600 m / 11,811 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will climb to High Camp (3,600 m) through the lush forest of rhododendron and oak. The uphill climb will provide you with gorgeous views of the snow-capped Himalayas like Annapurna South (7,219 m), Patal Hiunchuli (6,441 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), and Mardi Himal (5,553 m). The trail has no settlements whatsoever, so it will be a quiet journey through the forest to reach High Camp. Overnight at High Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek from High Camp to Mardi Himal Base Camp or Upper Viewpoint (4,200 m / 13,780 ft), then descend to High Camp and continue to Siding (1,700 m / 5,577 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: After having breakfast, you will climb uphill through a forested trail to reach the Upper View Point (4,200 m). After reaching Upper View Point, you will have a magnificent view of Mardi Himal (5,553 m), Annapurna I (8,091 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), and other mountains. You will trek back to High Camp and and continue to Sidding.

itinerary.title: Drive from Sidding to Pokhara (820 m / 2,690 ft), 2-3 hours.
itinerary.html: Today after having a delicious breakfast, you will you will drive to Pokhara by a private jeep. After reaching Pokhara, you will stay overnight at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu, 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Early in the morning, we leave Pokhara as we drive back to Kathmandu on a tourist bus. (You can either drive or take flight). Enjoying the amazing greenery and the villages along the highway, we arrive in the capital. Upon arrival, you can either rest in your hotel room or explore the nearby markets.

itinerary.title: Transfer to International Airport for your onward destination.
itinerary.html: You will be transferred to Airport 3 hours before your scheduled flight.

title: Mera Peak Climbing
summary: Mera Peak is situated at the edge of the Khumbu region, south-east of Everest, the approach trek for Mera peak climbing is through the beautiful valley.

seo.title: Mera Peak Climbing | Cost | Itinerary | Route Map | Base Camp Adventure
seo.description: Mera Peak is situated at the edge of the Khumbu region, south-east of Everest, the approach trek for Mera peak climbing is through the beautiful valley.

overview:
Mera Peak is situated at the edge of the Khumbu region, south-east of Everest, the approach trek for Mera peak climbing is through the extremely beautiful Hinku valley. The unspoiled and uninhabited Hinku valley below the Mera Peak is one of the wildest and most beautiful in Nepal with its massive moraines, glacial lakes and stunning mountain views.

The trail to Mera Peak goes through lush forests of rhododendron and pine up to Mera Base Camp via several small settlements. While moving upward, you will see uninhabited alpine areas of the upper Hinku valley. Climbing through rocky paths filled with ice and snow, you will reach the summit of Mera Peak (6,476 m) to get the most spectacular view of the Mahalangur Himalayan Range as well as the Makalu Range.

Like in all the treks and climbing trips to Everest, our approach trek to Mera Peak starts with an exhilarating mountain flight to Lukla airstrip. Climb of Mera Peak is possible in a single day from the base camp but we avoid rush. We allow proper rest and acclimatization and make use of high camp to ensure success. Finally we ascend the three summits of Mera from where we would enjoy absolutely stunning summit panorama that includes 5 of the worlds highest 8,000 m peaks – Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Lhotse, Cho Oyu and Everest.

title: Mohare Hill Trek
summary: Experience the Mohare Hill Trek (Mohare Danda Trek) and enjoy breathtaking Himalayan sunrise views, local villages, and a peaceful trekking adventure.

seo.title: Mohare Hill Trek | Mohare Danda | Cost | Itinerary | Route Map
seo.description: Experience the Mohare Hill Trek (Mohare Danda Trek) and enjoy breathtaking Himalayan sunrise views, local villages, and a peaceful trekking adventure.

overview:
Mohare Hill Trek also called as Mohare Danda Trek. The view of the first rays of sun draping the Himalayas is a sight no one would want to miss, and from Mohare Hill, one can make that wish come true. Mohare Hill trek is a recently developed trekking route in the Annapurna region to promote and support sustainable eco-tourism in Nepal and uplift the lifestyle of locals by fostering local community projects. Mohare Hill trek takes you into the peaceful path of Annapurna foothills and provides you with a stunning panorama of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Mohare Danda trek is for those travelers who want to explore the unlimited culture and nature of Nepal in short time.

This short trek to Mohare Hill starts with a drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara. After reaching Pokhara, you will drive to Galeshwor via Beni and then begin the trek. Walking through rich forests and crossing a suspension bridge over world's deepest gorge, Kali Gandaki River, you reach Bans Kharka. The trek then takes you to the beautiful Magar village of Nangi which is famous all around the world for the production of Lokta paper, commonly known as Nepali paper. The trail passes through the beautiful forest of oak, bamboo, and rhododendron and leads you to Mohare Danda. You will get to witness both the sunset and sunrise from Mohare Hill which hosts a panoramic view of the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna massifs and also the surrounding snow-capped peaks. During the return, the trek reaches the picturesque village of Ghandruk, which hosts amazing vista of Annapurna South (7,219 m) and Machhapuchhre (6,993 m). You will also get to learn about the Gurung culture in the region by visiting the Gurung Culture Museum in the village. The trail then follows a stone paved path as you descend to Nayapul to return to Pokhara, and later, you drive back to Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Arrival at Kathmandu airport and transfer to hotel.
itinerary.html: Welcome to Kathmandu. One of our team representatives will be at the airport to receive you. You will then be transferred to your hotel. In the evening, you will meet with your guide and he will brief you about your trek. Overnight at the hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu - Pokhara by bus. Driving 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
After a delicious breakfast, you will begin your drive to Pokhara. You will drive along Prithvi Highway enjoying the view of Trishuli River for the most part of the drive.
The drive will be roughly around 5-6 hours and will present you with impressive views of landscapes and vegetation. After reaching Pokhara, you will check in to your hotel where you will stay overnight.

itinerary.title: Pokhara to Galeshwor by bus and trek to Bans Kharka (1525 m). 6-7 hours
itinerary.html:
Driving 4 hours and walking for 3 hours. Overnight at guest house.
Today after breakfast, you will begin your drive to Galeshwor and it will take around 4 hours to reach there. The drive will follow the bank of Kali Gandaki River, and after arriving in Galeshwor, you will begin your trek, which is a 3-hour ascent to Bans Kharka. The trail includes walking through the green forest and crossing the suspension bridge over Kali Gandaki River to reach Bans Kharka. You will stay overnight at a guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Bans Kharka to Nangi (2300 m). Walking for 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: After having breakfast, you will begin your trek further to Nangi, which requires 5-6 hours walk through a forested path. The trail features the stunning view of the mountains and landscapes along with beautiful villages. Following the winding trail through the forest, you will arrive in the Magar village of Nangi. In Nangi, you will visit the organic farm school and the famous Nepali (Lokta) paper making spot. You will stay overnight at a guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Nangi to Mohare Hill / Mohare Danda (3300 m). Walking for 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: After having breakfast, you will begin your trek to Mohare Danda. The trail will lead you through the beautiful forest of oak, bamboo, and rhododendron to the top of Mohare Danda from where a magnificent view of Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), South Annapurna (7,219 m), Nilgiri (7,061 m), Dhaulagiri (8,167 m), and other mountains. Mohare Danda is also famous for the amazing view of sunset and sunrise. You will stay overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Mohare Hill / Mohare Danda to Deurali (3090 m) via Poon Hill. Walking 6 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will wake up early in the morning to watch the sunrise and its mesmerizing effect over the stunning mountains like Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna massifs, Nilgiri (7,061 m), and others from the top of Mohare Danda. After having your breakfast, your trek will begin. The trail will ascend and descend through lush rhododendron forests to Deurali via Ghorepani from Mohare Danda after walking about 6 hours. You will stay overnight at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Deurali to Ghandruk (1940 m). Walking for 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today, leaving Deurali, you will trek to the Gurung village of Ghandruk. The trail will pass through forests, flatlands, cultivated lands, and suspension bridges. After trekking for 6-7 hours, you will reach Ghandruk. This village will give you breathtaking views of Annapurna South (7,219 m) and Machhapuchhre (6,993 m). You can also visit the Gurung Culture Museum in Ghandruk and get to know about the culture, tradition, and lifestyle of the Gurung people. You will stay overnight at a guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Ghandruk to Kyumi and drive to Pokhara. Walking 1 hour.
itinerary.html: Today is the last day of your trek. After having a delicious breakfast, you will descend to Kyumi, which is about 1 hour walk. You will follow the trail paved with flagstones that will further lead you to Kyumi bus stand. From here, you will drive to Pokhara enjoying the countryside view. After reaching Pokhara, you can explore the lakeside area. You will stay overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Pokhara to Kathmandu by bus. 7-8 hours
itinerary.html: After having breakfast, you will drive back to Kathmandu via Prithvi Highway. Driving past the markets of Damauli, Dumre, Mugling, and Kurintar, you will reach the capital city. You can spend your free time in the capital exploring the vibrant markets and eateries. You will stay overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Transfer to airport for your final departure from Nepal.
itinerary.html: Today, you will be taken to the airport by our team representative for your flight back home.

title: Mount Kailash Tour
summary: The amazing Mt-Kailash-Tour will lead you to one of the most revered holy sites in the entire world. Our trip will also take us to Lake Mansarovar.

seo.title: Mt. Kailash Tour | Holy Lake Mansarovar Tour
seo.description: The amazing Mt-Kailash-Tour will lead you to one of the most revered holy sites in the entire world. Our trip will also take us to Lake Mansarovar.

overview:
This amazing Mt-Kailash-Tour will lead you to one of the most revered holy sites in the entire world. The Hindus, Buddhists, and Bon followers all believe that a walk around this site erases all the sins of your life. Simply gazing up at this 6714 meter high peak is a memory which will last forever. Do not miss this rare opportunity to immerse yourself in ancient culture and religion!
Our trip will also take us to Lake Mansarovar, another holy site close to Mt. Kailash. Experience more religion and culture as you walk with around this wondrous lake with both Indian and Tibetan Pilgrims. The trip will end with an unparalleled drive through the Tibetan Plateau.

itinerary.title: Arrive in Kathmandu: Stay overnight in Kathmandu
Drive to Nylam (150km), 3750m
itinerary.html: Morning after breakfast leave Kathmandu to commence yatra to Nyalam [3,750 m]. We reach Friendship Bridge [Nepal â€“ China Boarder] by mini-coach. Walk along for 10 minutes to cross the bridge and there get acquainted with Chinese guide and land cruiser drivers. They will give a brief information regarding the further trip then proceed the journey to Zangmu, where all the immigration and custom formalities are ought to be accomplished. After the accomplishment of all formalities, we proceed to Nyalam. Arrival at Nyalam and overnight stay at guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Rest Day at Nylam, 3750m: It is more a day for acclimatization.
Saga/4450m: (Labug-La 5150m, Peku-tso and Saga, 232km)
itinerary.html: On the first long driving day over the sandy and rocky land of Tibet, other things like lake, nomads chasing thousands of yaks and sheep keep you busy. By the late afternoon you will cross Bhramha Purtra River way to typical Chinese and Tibetan town, Saga for night.

itinerary.title: Paryang (4600m) 230 km 7-8 hrs
itinerary.html: Jeeps and trucks roll on the wide valley following rivers and grazing land of yaks and sheep. Far south you can see snow covered peaks near by you, lots of rocky peaks and sand duns give you an ideal world. Depends on season, nomads and other mobile shopkeepers are attired by beautiful traditional costume, waiting your arrival with hot tea and other supplies along with big smile.

itinerary.title: Drive Paryang to Manasarover (4558m) 277km 8 hours
itinerary.html: The longest driving day starts with full of excitement, by the late afternoon you can have the first sight of Holy Kailash Parbat and Manasarovara. Hore, a small village near by Lake Manasarover. Holy-Manasarovara: At 14950-ft/ 4,558 m The highest lake of fresh water with turquoise complexion in the world is full of fishes and swans. Holy Kailash Parbat, Mt. Gurula-Mandala, Lake Rashekshi are lying on its surrounding. The region is considered rich for gold and other mines, hot springs and hundreds of wild living creatures. Night will be spending at Chu Gumba.

itinerary.title: Puja and drive to Tarchen (14975ft) 40km
itinerary.html: Manasarovara is the lake of compassion, tranquility and bliss. After completing the memorable morning Bath and Puja we will be heading towards Tarchen. It is considered as a base camp for the Holy Kailash Parikrama.

itinerary.title: Trek to Dehara Puk/5000m
itinerary.html: It is one of the exciting days walking along the beautiful rocky cliffs; water falls with some clouds in the clear blue sky make you feeling that Great God Shiva is every where with tons of blessing to you. Time to time the face of Kailash Parbat will be keep on appearing. For 15 km trail it takes almost 7 hrs.

itinerary.title: Hardest but Holiest day of your pilgrimage Yatra with Dolma-La (pass) of 18600ft between two valleys
itinerary.html: Yamasthal should be crossed to reach the Shiva-sthal while your steps go closer to the pass. Once you reach the top, just do the holiest offering and sit down for meditation to forget yourself. Once your steps go down, Parvati-stal and Gauri Kunda are on the way. By the late afternoon you will arrive Zuthal Puk (the cave of Miracles. The great ascetic Milerappa is supposed to have performed miracles here).

itinerary.title: End of Kailash Parikrama and drive to Manasarovara
itinerary.html: After walking 3 hours, all the driving crew will be waiting your arrival. By the late afternoon you will be at your lodge/camp.

title: Mt Everest Expedition
summary: Mt Everest Expedition takes you to the top of the world with the majestic view snowcapped mountains before making our summit push.

seo.title: Mt Everest Expedition - Base Camp Adventure
seo.description: Mt Everest Expedition takes you to the top of the world with the majestic view snowcapped mountains before making our summit push.

gallery.alt: Everest Base Camp Trek with Kids

overview:
Mount Everest, the highest mountain peak in the world, is the proud possession of Nepal. Known locally as Sagarmatha, Mount Everest stands 8,848 m above the sea level. Mountaineers from all over the world come to Nepal to scale this ultimate challenge of Mt Everest Expedition. It has been close to 50 years since Mt Everest was first scaled but this peak still attracts the highest number of mountaineers. Apart from the Mount Everest, there are other peaks too that are famous among hikers.
Mount Everest is standing 8,848 m tall, standing 5 and 1/2 miles above the sea level. Named after Sir George Everest, the British surveyor-general of India. Everest is known in Tibet as Chomolungma (it means ‘Mother Goddess of the world’) and the Nepalese call it Sagarmatha (it means ‘Forehead touching the sky’ or ‘Head in the sky’) Mount Everest is located half in Nepal and half in Tibet. Tenzing Norgay Sherpa ( Nepal ) and Sir Edmund Hillary

( New Zealand ) were the first climbers of Everest. Via the South East Ridge Route on 29 th May 1953 . In 1975, first woman ever Ms. Junko Tabei ( Japan ) summitted, via the South East Ridge.

SOUTH-EAST RIDGE

After final preparations in Kathmandu , we take a flight to Lukla and begin our teahouse trek up the Khumbu Valley to Everest base camp. We will establish our base camp at 5,500 m at the foot of the notorious Khumbu Icefall before making our way to Camp 01 at 6,200 m We’ll climb to Camp 02 at 6,600 m smack in the middle of the Western Cwm, up the Lhotse face to Camp 03 at 7,200 m Finally, we’ll head up the South Col. to Camp 04 at 8,000 m before making our summit push.

seo.title: Mt Ama Dablam Expedition | 32 Days Trek to Ama Dablam
seo.description: Mt Ama Dablam Expedition is one of the most impressive expeditions in the world, not for its altitude, but for its beauty, aesthetics and the

overview:
Ama Dablam is known as one of the most impressive mountains in the world, not for its altitude, but for its beauty, aesthetics and the pure exposure encountered high on its flanks. Most parties attempt the SW ridge, climbing expedition style, fixing ropes, ferrying loads, and acclimatizing slowly. The mountain has gained in popularity over the past 8 years. It’s common to encounter high altitude Everest veterans having problems with the technical difficulties encountered on the crux pitches of this climb. Mt Ama Dablam Expedition is unique and challenging trekking.

The climb feels like a 5.8 – 5.9 depending on conditions but it’s really hard to say because I have always worn plastic boots, and all the climbing is above 6,000 m I would have to recommend allowing 5 weeks for this expedition, taking into consideration bad weather, sickness, and multiple summit attempts.

Information about how the peak gets its name:

Mother and her Necklace , Mother’s Charm Box , Mother’s Jewel Box “Ama” means mother, grandmother or even world. “Dablam” means charm box, and is a special pendant worn by elder Sherpa women that holds precious items. The mountain has a hanging glacier that resembles a dablam and the two extending ridges are outstreched like a maternal embrace.”

title: Mustang Tiji Festival Trek
summary: The Tiji Festival is an annual Buddhist festival celebrated in Lo Manthang, Upper Mustang, Nepal, usually in April or May.

seo.title: Mustang Tiji Festival Trek and Tour | Itinerary, Cost, Map & Guides
seo.description: The Tiji Festival is an annual Buddhist festival celebrated in Lo Manthang, Upper Mustang, Nepal, usually in April or May.

overview:
Tiji Festival is one of the most colorful festivals celebrated in the Mustang region of Nepal and has been successful in inviting many culture enthusiasts to the country with its unique features. Celebrated in Lo Manthang, the capital city of the former Kingdom of Mustang, Tiji Festival holds the virtue of the pure form of Tibetan Buddhism practiced in Upper Mustang.

Tiji festival also called as “Teeji” is an annual festival native to Lo Manthang, upper Mustang village of Nepal. This three day festival is hugely popular among the Buddhists living there. This ritual known as “the chasing of the Demons’ honors the victory of Lord Buddha’s reincarnation- Dorje Sonnu over a demon called Man Tam Ru. Man Tam Ru supposedly ate human flesh and caused storms and droughts in the kingdom, who was finally killed by Dorje Sonnu over 500 years ago. Since then, this festival is celebrated every year in the honor of Dorje Sonnu. During this festival monks usually wear their traditional dress along with the mask and dances to drive away the spirit of Man Tam Ru away to save the kingdom of Mustang from destruction. Villagers from all over the ancient kingdom come to watch and to participate in this festival. Moreover, this festival is also celebrated asking god for good crops and water.

During this festival, you can see the town filled with monks in robes and masks dancing and spelling Mantras over the onlookers. Throughout the festival, the story of the myth are reenacted so that spectators can easily understand the rituals. One thing is sure that during this festival, you will witness so extraordinary and unexpected that you dare not believe your eyes.  After enjoying the 3 day long Tiji festival, we trace our way back to Ghami, Sama, Kagbeni and lastly to Jomsom and return back to Pokhara with mind full of memories.

So, if you want to witness this colorful festival then you can do so in April and May. Join us for this special trip as we are always ready to provide you comfort, safety and security in each and every step. We assure yo that you are definitely going to enjoy the festival while learning the culture and tradition behind it.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive from Kathmandu Pokhara, 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Early morning, drive to Pokhara via a tourist bus, which will take about 7 to 8 hours to reach. En route, we will get plenty of the beautiful Nepalese scenery composed of lush hills and many streams and rivers along with highway side settlements bustling with the daily activities of the locals. On reaching, stroll around the lakeside street and enjoy the astonishing view of the Annapurna massif and Machhapuchhre (6,997 m). Overnight at a hotel in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Fly from Pokhara to Jomsom and then trek to Kagbeni (2,840 m / 9,318 ft),3-4 hours
itinerary.html: A short flight (20 min) through the deepest gorge in Nepal, Kali Gandaki River, takes us Jomsom. The windy town is the headquarters of Jomsom district and features a desert-like terrain, completely different than the typical Nepalese landscape. After a short rest in Jomsom, we trek to Kagbeni following the trails of Kali Gandaki River. Overnight in Kagbeni.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kagbeni to Chele (3,100 m / 10,171 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Leaving Kagbeni, we enter the restricted area of Mustang as we ascend along the sandy trails of Kali Gandaki River. On the way, there will be lots of mules carrying goods to transfer to the remote areas of Mustang. We walk past several monasteries and caves as we walk enjoying the landscape filled with barren rocky hills. Accompanied by the peak of Nilgiri (7,061 m), we make our way to Chele through several small settlements. Overnight in Chele.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chele to Syambochen (3,570 m / 11,713 ft), 6-7 hours
itinerary.html: We climb on to a subdivision and ascend along the steep canyon to cross two passes, Taklam La (3,624 m) and Dajori La (3,735 m). We then descend on the ridge until we reach Samar. Then we trek on a cliff and visit Chungsi Cave, situated above the gorge of Syambochen Khola. We then make a steep climb to reach Syambochen. Overnight in Syambochen.

itinerary.title: Trek from Syambochen to Charang (3,560 m / 11,680 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: We climb uphill towards Geling where huge barley fields are seen. Then ascend to cross Nyi La (4,010 m), which hosts a distant view of Annapurna I (8,091 m) and Nilgiri (7,061 m) peaks. Continuing the gentle trails downhill from Nyi La, we reach the village of Ghami, where we cross the longest Mani wall of Mustang before heading towards the red cliffs of Dhakmar. We then make a gradual descend to Charang, a large village situated on the top of Charang Chu Canyon. In the evening, we will visit the 400 year’s old Gelup Sect monastery in Charang. Overnight in Charang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Charang - Lo Manthang (3,840 m / 12,598 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today we start climbing alongside Charang Khola, which takes us to the ancient monastery, Ghar Gompa. Ghar Gompa is one of the most sacred monasteries in Upper Mustang and hosts the scriptures of Guru Padmasambhava. Then ascending alongside the ridge, enjoying the colorful desert hills, we make our way towards the walled capital of the former Kingdom of Lo i.e. Lo Manthang, where the Tiji Festival takes place.  Overnight in Lo Manthang.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang (3,840 m / 12,598 ft), start of Tiji Festival.
itinerary.html: Start Tiji Festival, day trip around Lo-Manthang area (Chosar, Chonup, Namgyal by horse. Enjoy the first day of the festival. An ancient three-story high Thanka is shown at the south wall of the square which showcases Padmasambhava who started the festival in the 8th century. Eleven monks in maroon and gold attire, wearing high red hats come from the palace and take their places along the wall beneath the Thanka. The monks come from various places to chant sacred mantras. A masked dance starts to show the incarnation of Buddha and repel the demon through the dance. This dance resembles peace, harmony, and purity. In the spare time, we will also visit the monasteries of Choser, Chonup, and Namyal on a horse. Overnight in Lo Manthang.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang (3,840 m / 12,598 ft), enjoy Tiji Festival.
itinerary.html: Numerous Loba people arrive from different hamlets and the small square is packed with women and children in traditional dresses. The royal family of the former Kingdom of Mustang joins the festival. The masks, dresses, 12 feet horns, the gold cup of wheat, snow leopard, pigeon, Saligram, and so on are brought into the festival. Overnight in Lo Manthang.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang (3,840 m / 12,598 ft), Tiji Festival ends.
itinerary.html: Tiji ends with the ceremonial destruction of the evil. The demons are set out on the old tiger skin and are attacked by bow, arrow, and old guns. The day brings the festival to end by performing all the spiritual folklore. People of Upper Mustang finally feel relieved and they believe now there will be only good days after all the reign of the devil has been ended. Overnight in Lo Manthang.

itinerary.title: Trek back from Lo Manthang - Drakmar (3,820 m / 12,533 ft), 6-7 hours
itinerary.html: Leaving Lo Manthan behind, we head towards Drakmar via Ghar Gumba. We start with a gradual ascend and later descend gently on a quiet trail through the Rocky Mountains and sand dunes. The trail is filled with colorful deserts leading us to climb a ridge to reach an alley to Dhakmar. Overnight in Dhakmar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Drakmar to Syambochen (3,570 m / 11,713 ft), 6-7 hours
itinerary.html: Descend along a stream and past the village fields before climbing a ridge to reach Upper Ghemi. Walk down to Lower Ghemi to cross Nyi La (4,010 m). Descend past the settlements of Jhaite, Chhunggar, and Tamagaon, and then climb to a large Chorten near the ridge below Syambochen La (3,850 m). Ascend and walk down to Syambochen for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek from Syambochento Chhuksang (2,980 m / 9,777 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Retrace the upward trail through Yamdo La (3,860 m) and Bhena La (3,860 m) to reach Samar. After a short walk, we ascend to cross Dajori La (3,735 m) and Taklam La (3624) to reach Chele. We then trek downhill to cross Kali Gandaki River on a bridge and follow it downstream towards Chhuksang. Encounter the amazing place and surrounding around you. Overnight in Chhuksang

itinerary.title: Trek from Chhuksang to Kagbeni (2,840 m / 9,318 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Retracing our trail through the Gurung village of Tangbe, we descend through the riverbed of Kali Gandaki to reach Kagbeni. Enjoying the dry yet picture-perfect landscape in the backdrop, we reach Kagbeni, bidding goodbye to Upper Mustang. Overnight in Kagbeni.

itinerary.title: Fly from Jomsom to Pokhara, 20 minute.
itinerary.html: Today we start the day with a short walk to reach Jomsom. Then we take a mountain flight back to Pokhara flying over the Himalayas. Upon reaching, feel free to explore the amazing places of Pokhara. You can visit the World Peace Pagoda, Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave, Mahendra Cave, and Davis Falls, among other major attractions of Pokhara. You can also enjoy a boat ride in Phewa Lake. Overnight in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu, 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today the trek ends as we drive back to Kathmandu. You can show gratitude to the team members through tips or incentives. Enjoy the landscape with the feeling of accomplishment. Rest upon reaching the hotel, and later you can stroll around the city. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.
