title: Tengboche Monastery Trek
summary: Book your 7-Days Tengboche Monastery Trek and explore the Everest region, Mt. Everest view, Sherpa culture and the iconic Tengboche Monastery.

seo.title: Tengboche Monastery Trek | Route Map| Cost | Guide | Reviews
seo.description: Book your 7-Days Tengboche Monastery Trek and explore the Everest region, Mt. Everest view, Sherpa culture and the iconic Tengboche Monastery.

overview: This 7-days of Everest Tengboche Monastery trek features the culture of the Sherpas along with great views of Mt. Everest and many other Himalayan peaks.  Accompanied by a Sherpa guide you will stay for two nights and acclimatize to the altitude at Namche Bazaar which is the hub of all trekking and climbing in the Everest region. You have the option to take a day hike to the beautiful twin-villages of Kunde and Kumjung. Later trek to the holiest Sherpa Buddhist monastery at Tengboche situated below the flanks of Mt. Everest. Look for the rare musk deer and the national bird of Nepal – the colourful danphe pheasant . Above all, enjoy the most spectacular mountain scenery on the face of this Earth. Along the way you will overnight at comfortable lodges run by the charming Sherpas who have won many admirers for their hard work and endurance. If you do not have too much time but still want to sample the charms of the Everest Area this is the best way to do it.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft) and then same day trek to Phakding (2,610 m / 8,563 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: We take a 40 minutes' flight to the Lukla in the early morning. Upon arrival in Lukla, we move alongside Dudh Koshi River on a trail blazed with rhododendron and pine trees. Passing several Sherpa settlements on the way, we cross few suspension bridges to arrive in Phakding. Overnight in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: The walk becomes a little tough today. The trek begins with a steep climb to Namche Bazaar. After crossing the large and stable suspension bridge high above Dudh Koshi River, we slowly climb on a steady pace through the settlements of Monjo and Jorsalle to arrive in Namche Bazaar. Namche is a picturesque Sherpa town which is also the commercial hub of Khumbu region. Overnight in Namche.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day at Namche Bazaar (3,440 m / 11,286 ft).
itinerary.html: We will spend a day in Namche Bazaar to get acclimatized to the growing altitude. Namche is a popular town from the ancient times for its trade between Tibet and Nepal. The place hosts stunning view of Everest (8,848 m) and other peaks of Khumbu region. Or, perhaps, we will hike to the Sherpa villages of Khunde and Khumjung where we visit the local monasteries and schools. Overnight in Namche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazar to Tengboche Monastery (3,860 m / 12,664 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: From Namche Bazaar, we will climb alongside Dudh Koshi River until Phunke Tenga and then follow the trails of Imja Khola up to Tengboche. Today's trek includes a chance to spot the national bird, Danfe, as we walk through the forest filled with pine, fir, black juniper, and rhododendron trees. Upon arrival in Tengboche, we visit the ancient Tengboche Monastery, which is considered the most sacred by the Sherpas of Khumbu region. Ama Dablam (6,856 m), Mt. Everest (8,848 m), Taboche (6,367 m), and other peaks of Khumbu can be seen on the backdrop of Tengboche Monastery. Overnight in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Namche Bazaar and continue to Monjo (2,835 m / 9,301 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today we will trek back to Namche. Descending alongside Dudh Koshi River, we walk past various monasteries and Mani walls adorned with prayer flags on our way to Namche Bazaar. We then retrace our way to Jorsalle, where we cross the suspension bridge over Dudh Koshi River to exit Sagarmatha National Park and arrive in Monjo. Overnight in Monjo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Manjo to Lukla (2,860 m / 9,383 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: On our last day of trekking, we descend through the villages of Bengkar, Phakding, Nurning, and Cheplung and past many Mani stones, we arrive back in Lukla. You can spend the evening exploring the village and interacting with the Sherpa locals. Overnight in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly from Lukla to Kathmandu, (35-40 minutes)
itinerary.html: We wake up early in the morning and have a delicious breakfast. Then, we catch our flight back to Kathmandu which takes us above the mountains one more time. Our representative will pick you up at the airport and drive you to the hotel. You have the whole day to yourself to explore the markets and eateries of Kathmandu.

title: Tilicho Lake Trekking
summary: Tilicho Lake Trek is one of the world’s highest lakes at 4,919 m, offering stunning mountain views and dramatic high-altitude landscapes.

seo.title: Tilicho Lake Trekking | Route Map | Cost | Review | 2026 & 2027
seo.description: Tilicho Lake Trek is one of the world’s highest lakes at 4,919 m, offering stunning mountain views and dramatic high-altitude landscapes.

facts.label: Destinations
facts.value: Tilicho Lake and Thorang La Pass

overview:
Tilicho Lake Trekking is one of the most attractive trekking destinations in Nepal which passes through some of the most prominent places in the Annapurna Region with the highlight of the trek being Tilicho Lake (4,920 m) itself. The trek to the highest lake in the world is full of incredible view of breath-taking Himalayas, lush green hills, wide meadows, and traditional villages of the Buddhist community. Tilicho Lake Trekking is an ideal trek for nature lovers who seek peace in the lap of the Himalayas but do not mind a little tough walking.

Tilicho Lake Trekking route attaches with Annapurna circuit route which is one of the world's most popular trekking routes  starts  from Chamje from where you follow the trails of Marsayangdi River leading to the villages of Tal, Dharapani, Chame, Pisang, Manang, Khangsar and finally Tilicho Lake. With every new destination, the climate and landscape are bound to change. The trail then takes to the tranquil Tilicho Lake sitting peacefully amid bare hills behind which the snowy peaks glitter.

Afterward, the trek again joins the main trekking route and moves on to the meadows of Yak Kharka. One of the highlights of this trek is the tough climb to cross the highest pass in Nepal, Thorung La Pass (5,416 m) from where a stunning view of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges can be seen. Crossing Thorung La Pass (5,416 m), the trek leads to Muktinath temple, one of the holiest shrines of Hindus all over the world.

While trekking in Manang valley featured the continuous view of the Annapurna range, trekking in Mustang district features a splendid view of the Dhaulagiri range. Hence, enjoying the view of Dhaulagiri massif, you head down to the windy town of Jomsom via Kagbeni before flying above the deepest gorge in the world, Kali Gandaki River to arrive in Pokhara. Tilicho Lake Trekking, therefore, is an excellent chance to explore the Himalayan life in Nepal.

Tilicho Lake is one of those places that have had mythic connotations. The Annapurna undoubtedly provides some of the world’s best trekking routes, including as it does a greater variety of scenery and culture than can be found in any other comparable area.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu and transfer to the hotel.
itinerary.html: Welcome to Nepal. One of our representatives will be at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA), Kathmandu, to welcome you. You will then be transferred to the hotel. Overnight at the hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kathmandu to Bhulbhule (8,40 meters), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Early in the morning, you start your drive to Bhulbhule, the starting point of this trek. You will be following Trishuli River for the first half of your drive and Marsyangdi River for the second half. Enjoying the view of lush hills and highway-side settlements, you arrive in Bhulbhule via Besi Sahar. Overnight in Bhulbhule.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bhulbhule to Dharapani (1,960 m / 6,430ft), 6 - 7 hours.
itinerary.html: From Bhulbhule we take an hour's public jeep to Vhamje and the start trek to Dharapani on a high road with the incredible view of high hills, waterfalls, gorge, snow-covered peaks, and scattered settlements. Crossing the suspension bridge over Marsayangdi River below Chamje and following the river upstream, you will reach the village of Tal, the first village in Manang district. You will cross the waterfall at Tal and continue walking uphill until you reach Dharapani. Overnight in Dharapani.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dharapani to Chame (2,710 m / 8,891 ft), 5 - 6 hours.
itinerary.html: After getting your permit checked, you will exit Dharapani and ascend to Bagarchhap via Odar. You will cross Marsyangdi River several times as you continue to follow the trails of Marsayangdi to reach Chame. As you gain altitude, the air starts to get cooler. Throughout the trail, you will be accompanied by the view of Annapurna II (7,937 m), Lamjung Himal (6,983 m), and Kangaru Himal (6,981 m). Overnight in Chame.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chame to Pisang (3,300 m / 10824 ft), 5 - 6 hours.
itinerary.html: Leaving Chame, you will enter a forested path filled with pine trees and continue to move alongside Marsyangdi River. With the panorama of Annapurna II (7,937 m) and Annapurna IV (7,525 m), you arrive in Dhikur Pokhari before crossing the suspension bridge over Marsyangdi River to enter Pisang. In the evening, you can visit the temple and monastery in Pisang that host a stunning view of Pisang Peak (6,091 m). Overnight in Pisang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pisang to Manang (3,500 m / 11,482 ft), 6 - 7 hours
itinerary.html: You cross the suspension bridge over Marsyangdi River and ascend towards Ghyaru from where you will cross a Mani wall to arrive in Ngawal. You will continue to walk through the alpine forest to reach Manang via Lophelling Monastery, Sher Gompa, Braka Monastery, and Bodzo Gompa. You will have the breath-taking vista of snow-capped mountains including the Annapurna range, throughout the trek. If time would suffice, you can also visit Gangapurna Lake, situated on the base of Gangapurna Himal (7,454 m). Overnight in Manang.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day in Manang.
itinerary.html: Today, we spend the day exploring the outskirts of Manang. We hike up to the beautiful Gangapurna Lake from where an amazing panorama of Marsayangdi River valley, the Annapurna range, Gangapurna (7,454 m), and Tilicho Peak (7,134 m) can be seen. We also visit the ancient monasteries and the old village of Tenki while in Manang. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek from Manang to Khangsar (3,745 m / 12286 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: You leave Manang to start walking on the trail filled with pine trees to reach the village of Khangsar. As you walk onward, Tilicho Peak (7,134 m) starts to appear on the horizon. Surrounded by the snowy peaks from all sides, you ascend until you reach Khangsar. In Khangsar, you will visit the local monastery sitting quietly in the lap of the Himalayas. Overnight in Khangsar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Khangsar to Tilicho Base Camp (4,140 m / 13,583 ft), 5-6 hours
itinerary.html: As you leave Khangsar, you will come across wide pasturelands dotted with grazing yaks. You will ascend on a hill from where you get to observe the glorious view of the entire valley as you climb up the hill. You will then walk by the cliff above Kangsar Khola to arrive at Tilicho Base Camp. Enjoy the peaceful environment amid the mountains. Overnight at the base camp.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tilicho Base Camp to Tilicho Lake (4,949 m / 16,138 ft) Tilicho Base Camp, 5-6 hours
itinerary.html: Today, you will visit the enchanting Tilicho Lake. You will make a steep climb uphill on a path filled with snow and ice almost throughout the year. After the tough climb, you will reach the mesmerizing Tilicho Lake, the highest lake in the world for its size. After spending some time around the lake, you will move back to base camp. The descent is as tough as the ascent, so you must be careful while walking and must maintain the pace of your walk. Overnight at the base camp.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tilicho Base Camp to Yak Kharka (4,040 m / 13,020 ft), 6-7 hours
itinerary.html: Today's trail will lead you out of Marsayangdi valley as you leave behind the trees and enter a rather sparsely vegetated area. The trail will pass through Khangsar village and continue uphill alongside Thorung Khola. You will cross a long Mani wall and walk through meadows with grazing yaks to arrive at the temporary yak herders' settlement in Yak Kharka. You will have a beautiful vista of the surrounding mountains like Tilicho Peak (7,134 m), Khatungkang (6,484 m), Chulu (6,584 m), and so on from Yak Kharka. Overnight in Yak Kharka.

itinerary.title: Trek from Yak Kharka to Thorung High Camp (4,800 m), 5-6 hours
itinerary.html: Leaving Yak Kharka, you will ascend towards Ledar. Accompanied by the continuous view of the surrounding peaks, you will walk through towering cliffs to reach Thorung Phedi. You'll pass small teashops on your way to Thorung Phedi. From Thorung Phedi, a close-up view of Thorung Peak (6,144 m), Syagang (6,026 m), Khatungkang (6,484 m), Purbung Himal (6590), and others can be observed. Overnight in Thorung Phedi.

itinerary.title: Trek from Thorung High Camp to Muktinath (3,800 m / 12,467 ft ) via Thorong La Pass (5416m/17764ft): 7 - 8 hours
itinerary.html: Today's trek will begin early in the morning as you will be crossing one of the highest passes in Nepal, Thorung La Pass (5,416 m), which connects Manang with Mustang. The climb to Thorung La Pass is quite challenging as you will be required to walk on the moraines on a frozen path. After reaching the top, however, you will realize that your journey was worth it as the snow-capped mountains smile back at you. Later, you will descend alongside Thorung Khola to arrive at the holy temple of Muktinath. Overnight in Muktinath.

itinerary.title: Trek from Muktinath to Jomsom (2,715 m / 8,910 ft), 5-6 hours
itinerary.html: Early in the morning, you will visit Muktinath, one of the great religious sites of Hindus. The trail will then lead you to the apple orchards of Kagbeni. Then, you will follow the trails on the riverbed of Kali Gandaki River as you move forward with a view of Mt. Dhaulagiri (8,167 m) and other snowy peaks. You will cross a concrete bridge over Kali Gandaki River to enter the windy town of Jomsom. Overnight in Jomsom.

itinerary.title: Fly from Jomsom to Pokhara, 20 minutes
itinerary.html: After a hearty breakfast in Jomsom, you will take the morning flight to Pokhara. You will fly above the beautiful Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges and through the deepest gorge in the world, Kali Gandaki River. Upon arrival in Pokhara, you will rest for a bit before heading on to explore the lake city. You can go for a boat ride in Phewa Lake under the reflection of Machhapuchhre (6,993 m). Overnight in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Tourist bus drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu, 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: You will catch an early morning bus from Pokhara to Kathmandu.  You will again be dropped at the hotel so that you can freshen up and rest. Later, you can visit the nearby market to shop for souvenirs to take back home. Overnight at the hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.html: You will be driven to the airport for your scheduled flight back home.

overview:
Trip Details

Trip Destination: Trishuli River

Trishuli River rafting is the most popular river rafting in Nepal among beginners who seek for short river trip without much challenge of huge rapids. This rafting is considered as an ideal trip for family as it gives the right length of time, exciting rapid complemented with scenic views of adjoining hills. So, if you are looking for more of wilderness experience, rafting in Trishuli River is the must.

For the most of the year the rapids experienced on the Trisuli River are direct, effectively arranged and well-spaced out. However, amid the monsoon months the power of the rapids expands and pulls in a drastically diverse arrangement of rafters. During these months, the river promises a more challenging ride, with powerful rapids which attracts professional rafters from all over the world. During this season, you can come across numerous exciting rapids named Snail’s nose, Teendevi, Monkey rapid, Upset, Surprise, Ladies Delight, Monsoon and Pinball rapids. These make you fun more interesting during high current with a good mixture of nonstop rapids and warm water.

This extremely popular rafting day tour usually starts off at Fishling, a raft put in point which is around 82 kilometers west of Kathmandu. Prior to the rafting, a river guide provides a thorough briefing about the safety procedures and guidelines after which the journey really starts. This exhilarating rafting journey usually lasts around 4 hours with short lunch breaks in between. Once this thrilling experience completes, we return back to Kathmandu, Pokhara or Chitwan with mind full of memories.

Hence, be part of this exciting one day trip and observe the diverse demography, landscape and flora and fauna of Nepal while cruising down the gigantic Trishuli River. Rafting in TrishuliRiver is definitely an exciting and heart pounding experience.

title: Tsum Valley and Manaslu Trek
summary: The Manaslu Circuit Trek with Tsum Valley takes you through a sacred Himalayan pilgrimage valley of Nepal. It is deeply rooted in Buddhist culture.

seo.title: Tsum Valley and Manaslu Trek | Cost | Map | Itinerary | Review
seo.description: The Manaslu Circuit Trek with Tsum Valley takes you through a sacred Himalayan pilgrimage valley of Nepal. It is deeply rooted in Buddhist culture.

map.alt: Tsum Valley and Manaslu Trek Map

overview:
An extraordinary journey to the isolated valley in the Manaslu region, Tsum Valley Trek is an ideal trek for curious travelers who seek peace in the off-beaten. Trekking in Tsum Valley was restricted until 2008 hence the nature and culture of the valley have remained divine and pristine. This trek allows you to explore the pure virtue of Tibetan Buddhism whilst being in the lap of the Manaslu Himal Range.

You will begin your trek after the seven hours drive from Kathmandu to Arughat. The first half of the trek ascends to the Budhi Gandaki Valley crossing terraced fields, dense forests, hills, and villages. After leaving the main Manaslu trail, you will move towards Tsum Valley crossing glacial rivers and alpine forests. You will visit historic Gompas of this region like Mu Gompa, DhephuDoma Gompa, and Rachen Gompa. The locals of this region belong to Tibetan origin, speak a unique dialect, and also have their own rich ancient culture, religion, and art. The trail is filled with various artistic Chortens and Mani walls made of thousands of stone slabs carved with deities and prayers.

Traditionally Tsum valley was a culturally distinct geographical area called ‘Tsum Tso Chuksum’, which means thirteen provinces ruled as a single territory. The ancient remains of the Tsum Kingdom are still visible today. Due to its remoteness and inaccessibility, this sacred valley and its people have been bypassed by mainstream development for centuries. As a result, the unique culture of this valley has remained intact. Only few trekkers have made it to this mysterious valley which also used to be the important trade route between Nepal and Tibet.

Tsum Valley has an ancient history of Buddhism, and it is believed that Buddhist saint Milarepa used to meditate in the caves of this region. After exploring Tsum Valley, the trek takes you to the main Manaslu Circuit Trail and traverses across the dramatic Larkya La (5,160 m) pass on the way back.

Tsum Valley and Manaslu Trek Altitude Trek

toc.text: Tsum Valley and Manaslu Trek Altitude Trek

itinerary.title: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu (1,400 m / 4,600 ft), where you will be warmly welcomed by our representative and transferred to your hotel.
itinerary.html: After your arrival in Kathmandu, we will welcome you at the airport and then transfer you to the hotel. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Machha Khola (863 m / 2,831 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Early morning drive from Kathmandu toMachha Khola. The roads are dirty and difficult to walk on but the landscapes of the rice fields, waterfalls, and greenery through the villages is amazing to watch. Arkhet bazaar is an interesting old market and the Arkhet Khola is the main attraction to see. You can see at least one lodge and beautiful local houses with slate roofs as you walk to the north.  Overnight in Machha Khola.

itinerary.title: Trek from Machha Khola to Jagat (,340 m / 4,396 ft), 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: You walk to Tatopani on the narrow trails between Budhi Gandaki and a cliff. After an hour walk, you reach Dobhan and then Shyaule Bhatti and finally Yaru, where the scenes of Budhi Gandaki will leave you in awe as it descends rapidly in nice cascades. After 2-3 hours, you will reach Jagat to find slate-paved streets. There is a campsite in the lower part of the village as well as lodges with basic accommodations. The local people here make their living via tourism, agriculture, education, and government services. Overnight in Jagat.

itinerary.title: Trek from Jagat to Philim (1,570 m / 5,151 ft), 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: Today’s route goes through rugged rocky terrain alongside Budhi Gandaki River. You will come upon many up and down en route. Despite the ruggedness, the route provides you with good views of Shringi Himal (7,161 m). Finally, you will reach a large Gurung village with fields of corn and millet, which is Philim. Overnight in Philim.

itinerary.title: Trek from Philim to Chumling (2,386 m / 7,828 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Continuing to ascend alongside Budhi Gandaki River, you will pass a beautiful waterfall before reaching Lokpa. You will then cross many small streams and climb alongside Siyar Khola enjoying the views of Ganesh Himal range until reaching Chumling. Shringi Himal (7,161 m) appears to look closer as you reach Chumling. Overnight in Chumling.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chumling to Chhokang Paro (3,031 m / 9,944 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will trek alongside Siyar Khola all the way to Chhokang Paro, which is a Tibetan-Buddhist settlement. The route passes through various ancient monasteries like Tanju, Rainjam, and Gho until you reach the Dzong in Chhokang Paro. From the village, spectacular views of the Ganesh Himal range and the Tibetan Himalayan range can be seen. Overnight in Chhokang Paro.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chhokang Paro to Nile (3,361 m / 11,027 ft) via Milarepa cave, 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: From Chhokang Paro, you will trek to the Nile via the Milarepa Cave, a sacred meditation cave used by the revered Yogi Milarepa. You also visit the Chi Phu Gompa before ascending alongside Siyar Khola to reach the Nile. In the evening, you can cross the river and walk for a while to visit Gonhgye Gompa. Overnight in the Nile.

itinerary.title: Rest day at Nile (3,361 m / 11,027 ft), day hike to Mu Gumba or Tibet boarder.
itinerary.html: You will take a day off trekking in Nile. You can spend the day exploring to Mu Gumba or Bhajyo village and the neighboring villages. You can hike alongside Yangdol Khola and reach the Nepal-Tibet border or follow Changman Khola to reach Thapla Bhanjyang (5,104 m), another entry point to Tibet. Enjoy an unobstructed view of Shringi Himal (7,161 m). Overnight in Nile.

itinerary.title: Trek from Nile to Chumling (2,386 m / 7,828 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, begin your return trek from Nile, following the beautiful trail back through the hidden Tsum Valley. Pass traditional Tibetan villages, ancient monasteries, colorful prayer flags, and scenic farmlands while enjoying magnificent views of the surrounding Manaslu peaks. Descend gradually to reach to Chumling.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chumling to Deng (1,860 m / 6,102 ft ), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, descend along the same trail to Lokpa before crossing the suspension bridge over the Budhi Gandaki River. Continue to Nyak Phedi for lunch, then hike through scenic forests to Deng, enjoying impressive views of Siringi Himal along the way. Overnight at a local teahouse in Deng.

itinerary.title: Trek from Deng to Namrung (2,630 m / 8,629 ft) 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Through most of the trek today, you will be passing through a plain terrain. Then after the plain trail, the trail moves uphill through the forest with mixed vegetation. Passing a waterfall and a few monasteries in Ghap, you make your final ascend to reach Namrung. In Namrung, you can visit the Namla Gumba, which hosts an amazing panorama of Ngadi Chuli (7,871 m), Himal Chuli (7,893 m), and Boudha Himal (6,672 m). Overnight in Namrung.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namrung to Sama Gaon (3,530 m / 11,581 ft) 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail from Namrung to Sama Gaon through a winding path on a ridge above the thinning Budhi Gandaki River. Passing through the villages of Lama and Sho, you reach the home of Ribung Gompa, Lho. Later, it is a steep uphill climb until Shyala, from where the trail is flat and easy. Upon arrival in Sama Gaon, you can visit the sacred PemaChyolingLhakang. Overnight in Sama Gaon.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sama Gaon to Samdo (3,875 m / 12,713 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: Today’s trek offers you fantastic views of the mountains, especially the Manaslu (8,163 m). You ascend to reach the frozen lake of Birendra Tal and then climb slowly on a quiet path to reach the village of Samdo. Cross a stunning Mani wall and visit the Taka Choeling Gompa in Samdo. Overnight in Samdo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Samdo to Dharamsala/Larkephedi (4,460 m / 14,633 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: You will cross a couple of streams which will take you to Larkya Bazaar. The trail is steep and crosses Mani walls to reach the base of the dramatic Larkya La (5,160 m). A steady climb from Larkya Bazaar takes you to the stone hut of Dharamsala, also known as Larke Phedi. Overnight in Dharamsala.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dharamsala Across Larkya La Pass (5,160 m / 16,929 ft) to Bimthang (3,590 m / 11,778 ft), 8-9 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will ascend along the lateral moraine of Larkya Glacier to reach the frozen pass of Larkya La (5,160 m). The top of the pass provides you with magnificent views of the Manaslu and Annapurna massifs. You will then climb down the icy path with the views of various glaciers to reach Bimthang. Overnight in Bimthang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bimthang to Dharapani (1,860 m / 6,102 ft) 7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will descend through alpine forests which lead you to the village of Gho. Trekking along, you will come across several small settlements, including Tilje. Leaving Tilje behind, you will descend to Dharapani when you cross the suspension bridge over Dudh Khola. Overnight in Dharapani.

itinerary.title: Jeep drive from Dharapani to Besisahar, followed by a bus journey to Kathmandu or Pokhara, 8–9 hours.
itinerary.html: Drive by jeep from Dharapani to Besisahar, followed by a scenic bus journey from Besisahar to Kathmandu or Pokhara. The total travel time is approximately 8–9 hours, depending on road and traffic conditions.

itinerary.title: Transfer to international Airport for next destination.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, you will be taken to the airport 3 hours prior to the scheduled time of your flight back home.

sections.title: Equipment List:
sections.html:
We are advised to consider the following equipment as these are essentials while packing for the Manaslu Trek. Adjustments to the list can be managed according to the requirements, interests, duration of trip, and season of trip.  We can find variety of these gears to rent or buy in Kathmandu. Majority of the gears which are in sale in Kathmandu are locally manufactured and some are imported from china and they are much cheaper. And there are some famous branded gear shops in Kathmandu, Thamel.

List:

– Lightweight and comfortable hiking boots: fit them with hiking socks and wear them wherever possible before you go to trekking.
– Sleeping bag and liner
– Sandals/ Flip flop
– Hiking socks – at least 4 pairs of cotton socks and 2 pair of wool socks
– Lightweight long sleeve hiking shirts
– Windproof/Waterproof pants and jacket
– Plastic rain poncho
– Light weather protection and warmer weather
– Hat for sun and wind
– Windproof gloves

– Since we will be walking a lot, carry a lightweight hiking backpack. You can check out these best hiking backpacks under 100 USD of 2017.
– Warmer clothes
– Long underwear
– Thermals (socks, t-shirts, sweater)
– Wool hat/beanie (for winter)
– Shorts
– Hiking trousers
– Best ultralight down jacket

Accessories:
– Sunglasses with good UV protection
– Sunscreen
– Lightweight bag to carry your personal needs during the day
– Insect repellent
– Camera with extra battery
– Flashlight
– Backpack
– Aluminum water bottle
– Head lamp
– Trekking Poles

faqs.q: Will the trek require oxygen?
faqs.a: No, you will not require any supplementary oxygen during the trek.

faqs.q: What is the price for Manaslu and Tsumvally Trek?
faqs.a: The cost of the Manaslu and Tsum Valley Trek ranges from approximately USD 1,300 to USD 1,500 per person. The final price depends on the level of service, accommodation, transportation, and other options you choose.

faqs.q: How are the Manaslu Region's wifi and telecommunications infrastructure doing?
faqs.a: Since the area still falls under the secluded area, you might have limited accessibility to network reception and WIFi. Although the teahouses have WIFi facilities, you cannot expect much in terms of speed and connectivity.

faqs.q: Will the hike cause me to experience altitude sickness?
faqs.a: The Manaslu region trek takes you to an incredible height of 5,106 m in Larke La pass, so you can fall prey to altitude sickness. Moreover, people have the symptoms of altitude sickness above 3,000 m above sea level.

faqs.q: How long can the Manaslu and Tsum Valley Trek last?
faqs.a: The Manaslu and Tsum Valley trek can last between 15 to 20 days depending upon the itinerary and highlights you choose.

title: Upper Dolpo Trekking
summary: Upper Dolpo Trek is an incredible trek into Nepal’s remote Himalayas, offering stunning landscapes, ancient villages, pristine lakes, and spectacular mountain views.

seo.title: Upper Dolpo Trek | Itinerary, Cost and Guide service
seo.description: Upper Dolpo Trek is an incredible trek into Nepal’s remote Himalayas, offering stunning landscapes, ancient villages, pristine lakes, and spectacular mountain views.

overview:
Upper Dolpo is a beautiful region that remains hidden behind snow-covered mountains in the mid-western part of Nepal. The unique culture and lifestyle along with incredible natural beauty will make you fall in love with the place.

The region remains one of the most unexplored regions of Nepal. 24 days Upper Dolpo Trekking adventure will take you through off-the-beaten trails in the remote parts of the country. The spectacular trek is a perfect opportunity to explore the wilderness of the Himalayan region of Nepal.

It is less popular when compared to classic treks like Annapurna Base Camp Trek or Everest Base Camp Trek but is quite adventurous. Trekkers will also pass through natural habitats of rare and endangered species in the protected area of Shey-Phoksundo National Park.

Besides, you will fly to Nepalgunj from Kathmandu and then fly to Juphal, a town of Dolpo. Afterward, you will then trek for around four days to reach beautiful turquoise Phoksundo Lake.

You can explore the lake and its surrounding, as you enter the Dolpo region crossing high passes and trekking rugged terrains. Moreover, it will take around two weeks until you reach Juphal from where you take for your flight back to Nepalgunj and finally to Kathmandu.

For the most part, you will observe numerous Buddhist gompas and monasteries along trails. Tibetan influenced culture, tradition and lifestyle will enchant you. Trekkers need to stay overnight at a tented camp as tea houses are not available in most parts of the trek. One of the prime highlights of this trek is a chance to meet nomadic tribes and people.

Highlights of the Trip

  • Observing scenic views of snow-capped mountains including Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, Mt Api, Mt Saipal, etc.
  • Exploring turquoise Phoksundo Lake and the Shey-Phoksundo National Park
  • Exploration of culture, heritage, and lifestyle of Tibetan Buddhists villages and ancient Bon culture and tradition
  • Spotting rare and endangered wildlife species including Musk deer, Snow leopard, and others
  • Passing through pristine waterfalls, streams, and riverbeds
  • Majestic view of Kanjirowa and Crystal Mountain Range (Ribo Drugta)
  • Observing people looking for Yarchagumba, a precious herb used as medicines
  • Exploring Shey-Gompa (4,500 m) via Kang-La Pass at 5,360 m (the highest point of this trek)
  • Passing through nomadic tribes and settlements
  • Visit monasteries, stupas, and gompas like Shey Gompa, Yangze Gompa, Bon Gompa, Namgung Monastery, and others

You may also like:

  • Chisapani Nagarkot Trek
  • Ghalegaun Home Stay Trek
  • Tilicho Lake Trekking

The Final Say

Upper Dolpo is a beautiful hidden trek in the mid-western part of Nepal. The culture and lifestyle along with incredible natural beauty is a highlight of the trek. Trekkers will also pass through natural trails of Shey-Phoksundo National Park.

24 days Upper Dolpo Trekking lets you explore remote parts of the country. In particular, trekkers also have the opportunity to explore Buddhist culture and traditions and gompas and monasteries along trails. You can also meet nomadic tribes and people. Overall, this spectacular trekking adventure is a once in a lifetime opportunity. Contact us for more details regarding this exciting trek

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu To Nepalgunj (1,450 m / 4,757 ft), 1 hour
itinerary.html:
Maximum Altitude:1,450 m
Travel duration: 1 hour 

After early morning breakfast, we board a flight to Nepalgunj from Kathmandu. The flight takes around an hour to reach Nepalgunj in Western Nepal near the Nepal-India border. You will have an entire day to spend exploring the culture and traditions of people and tasting delicious local cuisine. You will stay overnight at a hotel in Nepalgunj.

itinerary.title: fly from Nepalgunj To Juphal, trek from Juphal To Dunai 2,150 m / 7,054 ft, 2-3 hours.
itinerary.html:
You will take an early morning flight to Juphal from Nepalgunj early in the morning. The 45-minute flight takes you through scenic landscapes as you can observe Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Nilgiri, and other snow-capped mountains. After you arrive at Juphal, you can meet the guides, porters, and prepare logistics regarding this trek.

You will then start your trekking adventure with a short trek to Dunai. The trek duration is around 2-3 hours and also depends upon your trekking pace. Dunai is a small village in Thuli Bheri Municipality lying on the bank of Bheri River. It is also the district headquarter of Dolpa and you will stay overnight in Dunai.

itinerary.title: Trek From Dunai To Ankhe (2,900 m / 9,514 ft), 7 - 8 hours.
itinerary.html:
After having breakfast, we start our trek from Dunai to Ankhe. Trekkers need to cross a suspension bridge over the Thuli Bheri River and then walk westwards. You will ascend Thuli Bheri Valley and continue into Phoksundo Valley.

The trail passes through Dhara and Rahatgaon villages. We will then continue to a dense forest to arrive at Ankhe where we stay overnight.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ankhe To Sulighat (2,800 m / 9,186 ft), 5-6 hours
itinerary.html:
We have our breakfast, we start our trek from Ankhe, and continue walking towards Sulighat. You will walk on a rocky trail passing many water streams. The hard and steep rocky trail can get too challenging for some trekkers especially if you are a beginner.

However, if you walk slowly and carefully, you can complete the trek with ease and also enjoy the scenic views of snow-capped mountains before arriving at Sulighat after 5-6 hours of walk. You will stay overnight in Sulighat.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sulighat To Phoksundo Lake (3,611 m / 11,847 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html:
We start our trek from Sulighat to Phoksundo lake after having breakfast. You will begin your journey early in the morning after breakfast. After trekking for a few hours, you will arrive at the junction of the Phoksundo River and Pungmo River.

After crossing a bridge, we trek alongside the Pungmo River. We walk through a cedar forest along a trail that leads you to Palam Village. You will then ascend a ridge from where you can observe magical views of Phoksundo Lake and a huge waterfall.

You will trek along birch forests to reach Phoksundo Lake. We will arrive at Ringmo village. Ringmo is a Tibetan Buddhist settlement lying next to Phoksundo Lake. After trekking for 4-5 hours you will arrive at turquoise Phoksundo lake and you will stay at a camping site near the lake.

itinerary.title: Explore Phoksundo Lake (3,611 m / 11,847 ft).
itinerary.html: We will spend the day exploring Phoksundo Lake. The turquoise lake is the deepest in Nepal. Taking a bath in this sacred lake is prohibited as it hurts the religious sentiments of local people. There is a Tshowa Monastery at the shore of Phoksundo Lake. You can learn about the art, culture, tradition, and Tibetan Buddhism in the monastery. After exploring the lake, we will come back to Ringmo village. You can rest or explore Ringmo village. You will spend the night at Ringmo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phoksundo lake to Phoksundo Khola (3,507m / 11,506ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html:
We will start our trek with a 4-5 hours walk to reach Phoksundo Khola after breakfast. You will walk along the cliff path on the western bank of Phoksundo Lake. This part of the trail is quite challenging and dangerous. After passing through Phoksundo Lake on the western cliff, you will enter the remote region.

This unexplored region remains far away from modern developments and infrastructure. We then cross a lush meadow and cross the floodplain of Phoksundo Khola to reach our camping site. We will stay overnight in a camp at the bank of the Phoksundo River.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phoksundo Khola to Phoksundo Bhanjyang (3,910m / 12,828ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: We will start our trek on the flat trail on the glacial valley after breakfast. The views of snow-capped mountains including Chamlang Peak and others will enchant you. As the flat trial ends, you will arrive at a steep and challenging trail. After ascending along the trail, we will arrive at a valley with breathtaking views of Kang-La Pass. we then reach Phoksundo Bhanjyang where we will stay overnight at a camp.

itinerary.title: Trek Phoksundo Bhanjyang to Shey Gompa (4,126 m / 13,537 ft) crossing Kang-La Pass (5,360 m / 17,585 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
The trek starts with a steep ascent to Kang-La Pass after breakfast. We can observe magical views of the large valley and snow-covered mountains from the top of the pass. We will descend from Kang-La Pass, and climb down towards the valley. The steep descent in the early parts turns easy in the latter part.

As you walk alongside a river and cross it through a suspension bridge to arrive at a green lush grassland. You will pass through the meadows and mud caves on the cliffs. After a trek of 6-7 hours, you will reach Shey Gompa where we stay overnight at a tented camp.

itinerary.title: Rest day at Shey Gompa (4,126 m / 13,537 ft)
itinerary.html: Today is the rest day and you will spend acclimating your body to the high altitude region. You will explore the monastery, Shey Gompa village, and the region around Gompa. Shey Gompa lies in the junction of Kanju Nala and Yeju Nala rivers. The Shey-Gompa Monastery is the prime attraction of the Dolpo Region. There is also Shey-Phoksundo National Park which works in the conservation of flora and fauna of the region. Shey Gompa built in the 11th century is a famous religious site for Tibetan Buddhists. You can find ancient statues, Tibetan Murals, prayer walls, and Buddhist arts and artifacts.

itinerary.title: Trek from Shey Gompa To Namuna Gaun (4,430 m / 14,534 ft) crossing Saldang La Pass (5,200 m / 17,060 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html:
After having breakfast early in the morning, we start our long and taxing walk to Namuna Gaun. Trekkers will need to pass through Saldang La Pass (5,200 m). From Shey Gompa, a rocky trail leads you into a canyon as you ascend Saldang La Pass.

You will walk through beautiful yak pastures and landscapes around Saldang La Pass. From Saldang La Pass, you will descend towards Namuna Gaun where you can observe the famous Namgung Monastery. The monastery is a religious site for Tibetan Buddhists of the region. You will stay overnight at Namuna Gaon

itinerary.title: Trek From Namduna Gaun To Saldang (3,620 m / 11,877 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html:
The trail takes you through dusty and barren trails towards Saldang. After trekking for around 4 to 5 hours, you will arrive at Saldang village. You will then descend towards Saldang village.

Saldang is a large village settlement in Inner Dolpo spreading over two kilometers and with a population of around 600 people. You will see cultivable lands in Saldang, a prosperous village of Dolpo where you will stay overnight at Saldung.

itinerary.title: Trek from Saldanha to Yangtze Gompa (4,960 m / 16,273 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: You will trek alongside Nagaon River and pass through Marang and Ki settlements. There is also a tributary of Panzang Khola along the trail. You will cross the river to arrive at Yangtze Gompa which is an ancient and popular Bonpo monastery in Dolpo Region. You will stay overnight at a camp in Yangtze gompa.

itinerary.title: Trek From Yangtze Gompa To Sibu (4,560 m / 14,961 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: You will trek back to Saldang from Yangze Gompa and continue towards Sibu. Trekkers will trek alongside a river, and then cross the terraced fields of Saldang, and pass Chaiba Gumba to reach Namdo Village. We will have our lunch in Namdo, and continue our trek to Sibu. We will stay overnight at a camp in Sibu.

itinerary.title: Trek From Sibu To Jeng-la Phedi (4,430 m / 14,534 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: Trekkers can start their trekking Sibu To Jeng-la Phedi after having breakfast. The trail is easy as it follows the river. You will have to cross the stream after a trek of a few hours to arrive at the side valley. A little steeper trail will lead you to the grassland covered in rocks. You will camp at a site in Jeng La Phedi.

itinerary.title: Cross Jeng La Pass and Trek to Tokyu Gaon (4,900 m / 16,076 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
After breakfast, you will start your trekking adventure to Tokyu Gaon ascending Jeng-La Pass after a trek of 2-3 hrs. The awe-inspiring views of snow-capped mountains including Mt Dhaulagiri from top of the pass will spell bind you.

You will descend to Tarap valley and then ascend to Tarap Chu via green valley 20 kilometers from the Tarap Chu river. You can find villages, cultivable fields, monastery, Chorten, Gompas, along trails. You will spend the night at a camp.

itinerary.title: Trek From Tokyu Gaon to Dho Tarap (4,000 m / 13,123 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, we will start our trek to Dho Tarap from Tokyu Gaon. The trail passes through quite easier trails but you should be careful. Thick leafy grass at either side of the river makes for a different landscape than other parts of Inner Dolpo. You can find Magars and Tibetans villages. French school outside the Dho Trap village is another highlight of the trek. You will stay overnight at a camp in Dho Tarap.

itinerary.title: Rest day in Dho Tarap (4,000 m / 13,123 ft).
itinerary.html: On this day, we will rest and acclimatize at high altitude regions to save from altitude sickness. We will also explore Dho Tarap. You can visit farms and observe locals harvesting the crops. There are asymmetrical walls to protect crops from winds and wild animals. Magars and Tibetans settlements inhabited by Bonpo and Buddhists. The people wear traditional dresses like Bakhu (a heavy warm outer). You will also visit Buddhists Gompa and spend a night at a teahouse in Dho Tarap.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dho Tarap to Tarap Khola/Kamakharka (3,800 m / 12,467 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html:
Trek today is long and taxing. We will trek for some time to arrive at desert-like landscapes around Tarap. You will trek along with Juniper bushes and wild roses passing through a wide valley in the inner Himalayan valley above the treeline.

We trek further to Kamakharka, from where we can observe herds of blue sheep and arrive at the junction of Tarap Chu and Lang Khola rivers. After trekking for a few hours, we will arrive at the grassy area (meadow) called Kamakharka. You will stay overnight at a camp in Kamakharka.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tarap Khola to Khani Gaon (3,150 m / 10,335 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, we start our trek from Tarap Khola to Khani Gaon that takes around 4-5 hours. You will walk through the wooden bridges and staircases. These small adventures will make the trek more exciting. Trekkers need to cross damaged bridges above the icy stream on foot along the trail to Kahani Khola. You will finally arrive at Khani Gaon where you will stay overnight at a camp.

itinerary.title: Trek From Khani Gaon To Tarakot (2,540 m / 8,333 ft), 4-5 hours.
itinerary.html: Trek today takes you from Khani Gaon to Tarakot. The trail leads you to Lalberi village from where you will cross the Pine, junipers, and some apples and walnuts trees. Trekkers need to cross a stream to reach Tarakot, an old fortress town from where you can observe breathtaking views of mountains at the altitude of 2,537 m You will stay overnight at Tarakot.

itinerary.title: Trek From Tarakot To Dunai (3,240 m / 10,630 ft), 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: We start our trek from Tarakot to Dunai on this day. We pass through Pine trees beside Bheri river from where we can observe scenic views along the trail. After 6 hrs of walking, we arrive at Dunai where we stay overnight.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dunai to Juphal (2,140 m / 7,021 ft), 2-3 hours
itinerary.html: After breakfast, we descend from Dunai back to Juphal after trekking for a few hours along the path of the Bheri River. You will stay overnight at Dunai village with scenic views.

itinerary.title: Fly from Dunai to Nepalgunj and to Kathmandu.
itinerary.html: After breakfast, you will fly back to Kathmandu. Beautiful views of Mt Dhaulagiri and Mt Annapurna and other snow-capped mountains will enchant you.

sections.title: Useful Trip Info
sections.html:
About The Route

The 27 days Upper Dolpo trekking adventure will test you to the core. You will get to experience unexplored and remote parts of the country. You will fly to Nepalgunj from Kathmandu and then fly to Juphal from Nepalgunj. Juphal is the starting point of this trek. Trekkers will pass through settlements of Dunai, Ankhe, Sulighat to finally arrive at Phoksundo Lake. Shey-Phoksundo Lake is the prime attraction of this trek. You will also pass through high mountain passes, ancient monasteries, caves, and other landscapes. The Shey Gompa (4,500 m) via Kang La Pass (5,360 m) is one of the most challenging sections of the trek. After spending some time exploring Shey Gompa, you will descend to Namduna Gaun via Saldang La Pass (4,785 m). You will pass through Yangze Gompa, Jeng La Phedi, Sibu, and Tokyu Gaon via Jeng Pass. Trails also follow Nang Chu, Panzang, Nam Khong, and other rivers. From Tokyu, you will trek to the fertile valley of Dho Tarap. Bon Gompa and other Buddhist shrines are highlights of the trek. Trails also pass through Tarap Khola, Khanigaon, and Tarakot village settlements. You will walk through various gorges, pastures, forests, and cross famous riverbeds. After arriving at Juphal from Dunai, you will fly back to Nepalgunj and finally fly back to Kathmandu.

When is the Best Time for Upper Dolpo Trekking?

This outstanding trekking adventure is ideal during Autumn and Spring seasons. These transition seasons come between the Summer and Winter seasons and have favourable temperatures and stable weather conditions. The Autumn season provides great views of snow-capped mountains along with good weather. The daytime weather is ideal for trekking as it is warm and there are fewer chances of rainfall. The Shey Phoksundo lake looks incredibly beautiful in Autumn. The Spring season means beautiful atmosphere and green meadows. The clear sky is another highlight of the trek in this season. Rare and endangered wildlife also becomes active after a harsh winter. Also, the weather remains stable and temperatures moderate that is ideal for trekking. Winter is cold and there are high altitude passes along trails on this trek. These passes remain covered in deep snow in winters. Crossing the snowy passes in mid-winter is quite tough. The weather also remains unpredictable and adds complexity to trek. Summer monsoon rains make the trails get very slippery and wet. The dangers of avalanches and landslides also make it difficult to trek in these seasons. Hence, Autumn and Spring are the best times for Upper Dolpo Trekking Nepal.

How Difficult is the Upper Dolpo Trekking?

This magical trek requires you to walk for a long duration and stay in camps overnight. There are no tea houses or lodges for an overnight stay at most places along the trail. You will have to stay at campsites, arranging your own tent and sleeping bags. There are many high altitude passes along the trail that require extensive strength and endurance. A proper training regime will help you immensely during the trek. Upper Dolpo trek itinerary moves above 5,000 m at all times. Altitude Sickness is another huge problem in high altitude treks. You will be trekking to higher altitudes at all times and hence you should take necessary precautions. The oxygen in the air is considerably less in high altitude along with air pressure. You should also drink plenty of water and trek slowly to tackle altitude sickness along the trail. The length of this trek is also a major difficulty in this trek. You need to trek for 27 days for its completion. Rough and rural terrains require strong physical and mental build. Previous trekking experience is always a plus. Trekkers also need to pack proper gear and clothing. Inadequate trekking gears will cause difficulties for trekkers. Hence, upper Dolpo trekking Nepal is quite challenging especially for beginners trekking high altitude regions for the first time.

Food and Accommodation Along the Trek

Upper Dolpo Trek is an adventurous trek that requires fully-catered camping facilities. There are no teahouses and lodges in most parts of the trail. You need to carry all the food materials to be safe. There are also food shortages in the region. You must therefore make proper food and accommodation facilities before starting this trek. Thus, trekkers should trek through an agency that will organize a complete camping trek and prepare all necessary arrangements. You will get proper camping equipment along with food and other facilities. Porters will help you with luggage and setting up tents where you can sleep. A well-trained cook will prepare hot meals or you can cook it yourself. Camping in one of the remote parts of Nepal is one of the highlights of this trek. Similar articles you may like:
  • Everest Base Camp Trek in October
  • Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek
  • Annapurna Base Camp Trek In January

Permit & Regulation for Trek

You will require three permits for this trek as it is restricted area trekking. They are Shey Phoksundo National Park Entry Permit, Lower Dolpo Restricted Area Entry Permit, and Upper Dolpo Restricted Area Entry Permit. You can get permits at Nepal Tourism Board Office in Kathmandu or the National Park entry. You also need to follow strict rules and regulations during the trek. At least two people in the trekking group is a must as you can't go to restricted areas alone. You must also get a local agency to help you with the trek. A compulsory trekking guide or a porter is essential for trekking. Your trekking agency will do all these arrangements for you.

Packing List for the Upper Dolpo Trekking

Clothing

  • Trekking pants and jackets
  • Thermals underwear
  • Insulating jackets
  • Trekking boots
  • Fleece-lined jacket
  • Long-sleeved trekking shirts
  • Rainproof pants and jackets
  • Woolen cap/ beanies
  • Lightweight Sweaters
  • Short-sleeved trekking shirts
  • Pair of Gloves

Toiletries

  • Shampoo
  • Toilet Paper
  • Sunscreen
  • Soap
  • Hand sanitizer

Accessories

  • Cameras
  • Power Banks
  • Solar Chargers
  • Extra Batteries
  • Sleeping bag
  • Sunglasses
  • Water Bottle
  • Upper Dolpo Trek Map

First Aid

  • Diamox tablets
  • Band-aids
  • Anti-nausea Medicines
  • Pain relief Sprays
  • Mosquito repellent spray or ointment

Important Documents

  • Passport
  • Travel Permits
  • Travel insurance

Essential Tips for the Trek

  • You should follow all rules as it is a restricted area trekking. The rules such as trekking with a guide, and through a trekking agency is a must.
  • Trekking through an agency will give you many facilities like meals and camping at a reasonable Upper Dolpo Trekking cost
  • Carry Diamox tablets that help to tackle altitude sickness in high altitude regions.
  • You should carry proper and adequate means and accommodation facilities.
  • Check the weather forecast before starting on the trek.
  • You should not consume alcohol as it can cause dehydration which can further lead to altitude sickness.
  • Proper acclimatization and hydration will help you immensely during the trek.
  • Train well to gain physical as well as mental strength.
  • You should walk gently along the trail with regular breaks and rest.
  • If you feel early symptoms of altitude-related problems, you need to descend immediately.

seo.title: Upper Dolpo to Mustang Trek 27 Days Itineraries - Remote Trek
seo.description: Do you have any idea how cool Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang is? If not, we’ve brought you all details of excellent places and historic sites from the trail.

overview:
It’d be a big waste for trekkers to visit Nepal without scrambling the way up from Upper Dolpo to Mustang. The trek is incredibly adventurous whilst the place absolute heaven with raging rivers and glacial lakes

Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek epitomizes thrill to the deserted ravine of Kang La and Nangdala’s arid steppe. Its classic trail is a moving portrait of dramatic landscapes, epic valleys, and wilderness.

So many places near and far from Mustang are abandoned with no human settlements and still, it looks wonderful. Navigating the trails is more like playing with a daredevil stunt, given the narrow canyon, and rock cliffs.

Trails clambering the hills are jagged and meanders through hills and rocks so get ready to be challenged. After every successful trek, trekkers will stop at the most angelic places that have spectacular scenery to offer.

Like most hikes to the Himalayas, Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek also starts with a short flight to Nepalgunj. We’re still short of a 45-minutes flight to Juphal before starting the trek, so we do that first and then make our way to Dunai.

Taking steppe routes that winds up and down, we reach Chhepka and gradually move to Sumduwa. Walking on a trail with small but sharp stones, we arrive at Phoksundo Lake which defines the beauty of nature.

After a day of acclimatization, we carry on with the trek, heading to Sallaghari. The dramatic walk to Upper Dolpo will see us crawling Nangdola High Camp and almost a thousand years old Namgong Gompa.

The trail from Saldang to Sangda runs through high cliffs, multiple passes and remote settlements including Thinje and Chharka. Walking downhill to the Phalek Village, we trace our steps back to Jomson and then Pokhara through a scenic flight. Finally, on the last day before you catch our international flight, we’ll fly you back to Kathmandu.

Highlights of Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek

1. Shey Phoksundo Lake

It’s hard to resist the elegance of Shey Phoksundo Lake when on a trip from Upper Dolpo to Mustang. The lake is a pure joy to ease off after all those strenuous walks and ascends up to the destination.

There’s such utter silence in the place that you can even hear the moving air and even your own breath. Resting at a surface elevation of 3,589 m in a stunning national park, Shey Phoksundo is an oligotrophic lake. It’s a chosen Ramsar wetland with turquoise water that’s delightful to see.

2. Lo Manthang

Natives of Mustang know how incredible Lo Manthang is, given they are just a minute away. But for trekkers, it’s 135 miles far-off from Kathmandu through a mix of a well-paved road and cragged surface.

Moving through an arid region and desert, the trail is definitely not a piece of cake. Still, it keeps people occupied with mesmeric plateaus, red cliffs, and mud walls. Not too far, Lo Manthang is stacked with ancient palaces, Chortens, and sacred temples including Jampa Lakhang.

3. Muktinath and Jomsom

No hiker can afford missing Jomsom and Muktinath while trekking Upper mustang. It’s a fabulous place to be with all exciting sites and sceneries. Jomsom has a wild forest with animals for nature lovers while Muktinah gives secluded places to people looking for alone time.

Both the places have got everything from rock cliffs to eco museum, Buddhist monastery and scenic mountain view. Devotees visit Muktinath, a sacred pilgrimage to Hindus and Buddhists at the foot of Thorong La Pass.

4. Tshowa Gompa

Tshowa Gompa has become a symbol for Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek. It’s a glorious monastery with more than 800-years-old history and Tibetan line art. Carved idols and paintings in the monastery will take you back in the time. Continuous chants, flapping prayer flags and rotating wheels compel the visitor to immerse in Buddhist culture.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu
itinerary.html:
As discussed, our officials will meet you on this day at Kathmandu's International Airport where the flights arrive. You shall find them at the waiting zone where they’ll be eagerly looking forward to hosting you.

After a quick meet and greet, you’ll be driven to your residence in Thamel. Expect to stay here at least one more day since the Upper Dolpo trek begins only on the third day. Till then, visit the glorious cities of Kathmandu, taste scrumptious dishes, and live the vibrant culture and festivals.

itinerary.title: Sightseeing in Kathmandu
itinerary.html: Residents of Kathmandu know they have it good but you probably don’t. So, we kick off the second day of Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek with a bang and visit the capital city. We’ll briefly visit some of the UNESCO World Heritage Sites including Swayambhunath stupa. We’ll do Pashupatinath Temple in the early morning when devotees come for prayer and chanting can be heard from the street. Next, we’ll ride to Boudha stupa where again worshipers are seen spinning prayer wheels, lighting scented candles, and humming six-syllable Sanskrit Mantra. To look down Nepalese civilization, we can go through a couple of historic sites like durbar squares, palaces, and old museums. These places own ancient art, Pagoda style temples, and pottery.

itinerary.title: Flight to Nepalgunj
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 150 meters Flight Distance: 364 km Flight Duration: 1 hr Coming off the happy days at Kathmandu, we’ll long way travel Nepalgunj on the third day of Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek. So, have breakfast early in the morning and we can drive to the airport for our flight. The 226 miles flight to Nepalgunj lasts almost an hour and yet you won’t feel bored even for a second. Scenes from the aircraft are so lovely that every flyer is put into a trance. During the flight, you can spot dynamic landscapes, flat meadows, and a crowded city at Terai plains. We’ll call off the night at a hotel in the city.

itinerary.title: Flight to Juphal and trek Dunai
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 2,369 m Flight Distance: 149 km Flight Duration: 45 minutes Trek Duration: 3 hrs After a quiet night at Nepalgunj, it’s time for us to move ahead and get on a flight to Juphal. The aircraft takes 45 minutes on a whole to reach the village so you can grab your breakfast there. The flight to Juphal runs over scenic views so your time in the jet will pass quickly. A short tea-break and we’ll start tracking the route to Dunai. Initially, the trail scrambles southeast, high up to Thuli Bheri Valley, then runs the field with maize until reaching Kalagunda. Navigating the trail along the southern bank of Bheri River, we’ll emerge at Roop Ghar. Having a peek into the traditional water mill, we’ll keep scrambling until it takes us to Dunai village. Overnight in a local lodge at Dunai.

itinerary.title: Trek to Chhepka
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 2,670 m Trek Duration: 6-7 hours The first thing you’ll do after getting up in the morning is to grab breakfast and prepare for the long day ahead. A few times later, we'll climb down the narrow streets of Dunai and come across the bridge above the Bheri River. Tracking the bank of the river on the northern side, we proceed to Shey Phoksundo National Park through Sulighat. We register at the permit check post before the park and then mount the rock-strewn trail above Suli Ghad River. Moving to Kageni, we pass a section of hemp trees and also some maple and tropical walnut forest Trekking along the route, we'll find traces of Tibetan culture in prayer flags and gompa. Feel refreshed watching the rolling rivers and waterfalls on the way to Shyanta. From here, we ascend uphill on a narrow trail, which will take us to Chhepka.

itinerary.title: Trek to Sumduwa
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 3,370 m Trek Duration: 5-6 hrs It's just the 6th day of Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek so we better go easy on you. Henceforth, we only trek up to Sumduwa on a jagged trail, rolling a deep forested riverbed and many small streams. Watching nature at its finest could really boost our energy and help us finish the trail earlier. Coming back to the trail, it moves along the bottom of the valley and to the confluence of Pungmo Khola and Phoksundo. We’ll cross Phoksundo Khola to the west and approach Sumduwa, a central junction of the trails. After walking around 5-6 hours, we’ll eventually reach Sumduwa. As we’re left with some spare time, you can do a quick sightseeing and also interact with the villagers. Teahouses are available for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek to Phoksundo Lake
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 3,600 m Trek Duration: 6-7 hours After breakfast, we leave Sumduwa and reach out to the trail that connects Phoksundo Lake. As the walk is going to be a little harder in the end compared to the initial, we’ve to increase our pace right from the get-go. To begin, we stroll through a luscious forest filled with cedar and arrive at Palam, the natural home to Ringmo’s community in winter. Track from here inclines down until it doesn’t come to 10,826 feet and then shifts to pitch, climbing high. Unlike the one that we descend, this is slightly tougher as the route is in terrible shape. They meander on a dusty trail through peaks and troughs, making a way to the highest waterfall cascading from a ridge. En route to Phoksundo National Park, we come upon beautiful Ringmo village and its prolific mani walls. Leaving the village behind, we now follow the route to Phoksundo Lake and even cross the river. To spend the night, we set up a camp on the outstretched land of the park.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization and exploration at Phoksundo
itinerary.html:
How disgraceful it is to the grandeur of Phoksundo Lake if we don’t even spend a day in the region. Therefore, we take a day rest at the lake on the day 8 of Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek. Tucked between luscious vegetation and high mountains, Phoksundo lake is so spectacular.

It’s hard to take the eye off its beauty but we still have to take some time to explore Ringmo. This glorious village is too close to Phoksundo and in fact, rests at the landslide dam from the lake. It has got glaciers and a lot of monasteries to discover including Shey and Thashung Gompa.

itinerary.title: Trek to Sallaghari
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 4,600 m Trek Duration: 6-7 hrs After spending a wonderful day at Phoksundo, it’s about time we return to the trail and start walking. Moving forward from the lakeside, we ascend steppe hill and a secluded trail with chunks of small rocks. After one point, we descend the route that will take us all the way to Sallaghari. We can do a little sightseeing here as the village offers a great mountain view and landscapes. We’ll rest the night in a guest house at Sallaghari.

itinerary.title: Trek to Pass Camp, Nangdola High Camp
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 5,350 m Trek Duration: 8-9 hrs It’s already day 10 of Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang trek and we still have more than half a trip to go. That’s why we rush to the alley predawn and start hiking to Kangla base camp. To make it to the top at Nagdola High Camp, we go through a mix of trails and pass Mandala Camp. The locals residing near the camp are highly influenced by Bon Po of Tibet. Walking a few miles further from the camp, we’ll get to our destination. To rest the night, we ‘ll place the tent on the green meadow of Nangdola.

itinerary.title: Trek to Shey Gompa via Nangdola
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 4,345 m Trek Duration: 5-6 hrs Trek to Shey Gompa may be short in contrast to Nangdola but it’s as tough as it can get. The entire expedition lasts 5-6 hours during which we’ll walk past famous Crystal Mountain. After officially entering the Dolpo region, we’ll tramp over Kangla Pass and traverse west on the narrow Devil’s trail. Coming to a head of a fabulous cliff at 400 meter, we’re rewarded with the breathtaking view of Sonam Kang. From here, the trail steeply slopes downward to the valley and over the river. Few more walks and we’ll reach the red chorten which indicates that we’ve entered Shey. The place is also where we’ll camp for the night. Highlights along the route to Shey Gompa also include Kang Chunne and Shey Shikkar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization in Shey Gompa
itinerary.html: Today, we’ll spend our day exploring the primal Shey Gompa and also take a few short treks. We’ll start with something big and visit Shey monastery which came to rise in the 11th century. Made with an ocher, the gompa is a great landmark from a religious point of view and consists of Tibetan murals and ancient statues. Kagyugpa Gompa is another incredible site to visit. The monastery has stacked 400-years-old idols and statues that’s worth exploring. In case you’re lucky, there's a possibility of you getting to read the ancient scroll of Buddhism. As an alternative, you can also take a quick tour of Tsakhang Gompa, which is named after a cliff. The monastery too has store hundreds of years old paintings and thanka. The Buddhist flag around the gompa keeps fluttering in the wind, making a visual display.

itinerary.title: Trek to Namgong Gompa via Sela La
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 5,100 m Trek Duration: 6-7 hrs Namgong Gompa trek is no mean feat as we’ve to walk for almost 6 hours. To reach the monastery that’s believed to be 800 years old, we’ll cross the Ge La Pass on the west of Shey. Along with splendid views of Mustang on the east and shimmering Crystal Mountain, we walk a few more miles to reach the village. It’s an old herding settlement of nomadic locals and our dwelling place for the night. The village has a scintillating view to offer which includes Mt. Kanjiroba, Riu Dhukta, and Tibet in the north.

itinerary.title: Trek to Saldang
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 3,800 m Trek Duration: 5-6 hrs It’s another long and tiring day on the trail to Saldang. So better keep going on the trail from Namgong gompa to Yanger which is the ancient trade route to Tibet. Passing the old villages and tea houses, we take a high trail leading to Saldang. Along the route, we get a fair chance to see the area’s monastery, high ridge, and migrating cranes. After almost 4 hours of a trek through uphills and down, we’ll stop by Caravan Thinley to fill our stomach with some local dishes and tea. After the much-needed energy, we’ll make a further 1 hour trip to Yanger Gompa through Nagon Khola.

itinerary.title: Trek to Khoma Village
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 4,200 m Trek Duration: 6-7 hrs Starting at the trail of Saldang, we trace our steps towards Khoma Village on Day 15 of Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek. Shipping away from the fabulous Saldang Gompa and the sceneries along Dho route, we reach Nagon Khola via Sugugaon. It’s a small but terrific village with long-stretched mani walls, white painted chorten and the ancient gompa standing at the ridge. We’ll cross the Nagon Khola at Chagaon and rise up the soiled steep cliff for about an hour. We’ll start climbing down the black riverbed and once reached there, ascend the verdant elevated plain. Before passing the Khoma La, we take a short lunch break and then plummet to the lovely Khoma Gaon. Overnight stay in a lodge at the village.

itinerary.title: Trek to Mendo
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 4,000 m Trek Duration: 6 hrs Giving a boost to our trek to Mondo with a delicious breakfast, we’ll come far away from the village through a dense forest. Given it’s a habitat to wild animals like snow leopards and blue sheep, we’ve a pretty good chance to see a few of them. Walking for a too long time, we stop in Simen village to get brunch and also explore its primordial gompa. After spending a quality time, we’ll give a continuity to our trek and traverse further old chortens and mani walls. From then on, we’ll plummet to the river and stick with the route for another good hour and finally reach the campsite. The place is slightly cold but enjoyable with stunning stone fields and mani walls. To spend the night in the location, we put up a camp.

itinerary.title: Trek to Thinje
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 4,110 m Trek Duration: 5-6 hrs Mendo’s trek route twists and turns its way from south of Panjyan Khola passing two trails. Heading north to the border of Tibet on our left, we’ll be treated with gorgeous mani walls and Pu Gompa on the next side of the river. Transiting a seasonal village and Phalwa’s hamlet, we’ll meet a small stream at-grade junction. Crossing over it, we scale the trail racing alongside mani walls, fluttering prayer flags and chortens till Thinje. It’s a small village with a lot of diversity among people and yet all are kind and reverent to each other. For the night, we’ll stop in a lodge at Thinje.

itinerary.title: Trek to Rapka
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 4,535 m Trek Duration: 6-7 hrs On another beautiful day of our Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek, we’re committed to traverse Rapka. The trail is a combination of highs and lows so we’ll go easy in the beginning and speed up after looking good. Going after the Panzang River and south, we’ll reach the intersecting river where the former turns to Sulun Khola. Onwards our trail becomes narrow and frequently climbs up and down until it leaves all the greenery behind. Taking in the tedious canyon, we walk miles till the valley opens out again. Following the trail, we so often ascend and descend while walking towards the plateau of Rapka. There are two campsites at Rapka so we can choose either of them. But it’s better to have the one that provides a clearer view.

itinerary.title: Trek to Chharka
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 4,410 m Trek Duration: 6-7 hrs Trek to Chharka is as good as it gets. It has an easy-to-follow route that descends from the minute we start walking. It then follows the cold-shallow river to enter Chharka La. The Lakkyan Khola becomes narrow and small allowing us to walk across easily. After then, we ascend the trail on the right of the river for a good time and descend later on. Arriving at the pass, we switchback trail and climb for about an hour to Chharka La. We’re not done yet as there's still some walking left to reach the tented camp. So, we make a few climbs and descend the trail, passing farm fields and a series of chorten. Leaving behind a village school, we descend the route and pass through Kane that marks our into the village. Down the road, we’re offered a marvelous view of Mt. Dhaulagiri and unique landscapes to wipe out our fatigue. Overnight stay in a tented camp at Chharka.

itinerary.title: Trek to Yak Kharka
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 4,780 m Trek Duration: 5-6 hrs From Chharka, our trek continues on a trail descending hills through a flowing river. After that we follow the right fork south of Chharka, traversing to and fro the valley on a rocky pitch. As the valleys narrow gradually, we slow our pace and speed up soon entering the steppe meadows and stroll to Yak Kharka. Night is spent at a camp under shimmering stars.

itinerary.title: Trek to Ghok Pass
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 5,460 m Trek Duration: 5-6 hrs Make sure that you’re in time for breakfast today as we’ve a long journey to make. We start our day by clambering up to a pasture at Molum Sumdo where locals graze their yak. Farther into the meadows, and we make a steep long ascent to Ghoka Pass which lies at an elevation of 5,460 m. We have an easy slant route from here to reach the campsite which only takes a few minutes from the pass.

itinerary.title: Trek to Sangda Village
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 5,909 m Trek Duration: 6-7 hrs Our day begins with a lovely morning and local breakfast of Sangda to complete. We’ll make a relaxed start and pack all our stuff before heading to the trail. Slowly, we’ll escalate the lower Sangda La and climb down on the mudstone that heads Sangda village. From here on out, our trail descends to the Chalung Khola and scales sharply from the other end of the river. The long-rising trail leading Sangda is a rollercoaster, ascending to cairn and immediately falling down the hill to a stream. Few more distance to cover and we’ll reach the magnificent Sangda village. It’s a small settlement in the himalayan region with a majority of people being Gurung. The sloppy hills in the region are the playground of blue sheep. Therefore, we can enjoy our free time watching these adorable animals.

itinerary.title: Trek to Phalek Village
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 4,280 m Trek Duration: 5-6 hrs Hike to Phalek Village is a bit easier following a sloppy trail at the back of Sangda. But saying so, we still have to be quick and reach out the trail to spare ourselves a few moments of sightseeing. Starting with uphill in the wake of Sangda, we spent the better part of the trek climbing high and coming across ridges to the top of the hill. Next, we descend towards the Kali Gandaki Valley and ramble beneath the cliff to reach Phalek. It’s a typical Mustangi village with a larger population celebrating Buddhism and the rest of them different cultures. The place offers astounding mountain views and the shot to watch everything from Thorung La to Kagbeni and Kali Gandaki. We’ll keep you comfortable in one of the Phalek homestays at night.

itinerary.title: Trek to Jomsom
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 2,743 m Trek Duration: 4-5 hrs Since today’s trek is short and moderate, we take slow steps down the ridge from Phalek. Steering through a rough and dry trail filled with loose rocks, we descend the route below 2,670 m and finally arrive at Jomsom. To spend the night, we’ve pre-booked rooms in a nearby lodge.

itinerary.title: Flight to Pokhara
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 1,400 m Flight Distance: 67 km Flight Duration: 20 minutes Flights are available every hour or two from Jomsom. Thereby after having breakfast at the lodge, we steadily move to the airport to take our flight. The air trip will last mere 20 minutes and it’s still so fun with a soothing view of landscapes, trickling streams, and mountains. Meanwhile, you can even make an escapade to the quiet lakes of Pokhara and try out some adventures in idle time. Overnight stay in a hotel.

itinerary.title: Flight to Kathmandu
itinerary.html: Maximum Altitude: 1,350 m Flight Distance: 146 km Flight Duration: 30 minutes This is the final day of our Upper Dolpo to Upper Mustang Trek as we officially leave the region today. After breakfast, we walk down the dusty trail and make headway towards the airstrip. The flight to Kathmandu takes roughly 30 minutes and provides a breathtaking view of snow peaks and land formation. Sneak out of the window and there’ll be a lush-green forest and high cliff to serve you anytime. Upon reaching Kathmandu, you can take a rest at your hotel, or visit the remaining heritage site and even shop around the corner, the choice is all yours.

itinerary.title: Final Departure
itinerary.html: As per the scheduled flight, our representative will drop you at the airport today. If needed, they will even escort you to the premises and help with the security so that you can safely board the flight.
