summary: Mustang Trek lets you view ancient Himalayan Kingdom in the northern central part of Nepal. Join our 14 days adventure trek to Mustang at budget price.

seo.title: Upper Mustang Trek | Cost | Itinerary | Route Map
seo.description: Mustang Trek lets you view ancient Himalayan Kingdom in the northern central part of Nepal. Join our 14 days adventure trek to Mustang at budget price.

overview:
Upper Mustang Trek is one of the preserved destinations of Nepal and was restricted to outsiders for years. In 1992, trekking in this region was officially opened for foreigners, but only limited numbers of trekkers are allowed to visit this place in order to conserve and protect the fragile environment and the local Tibetan tradition and culture. Mustang Trek features ocher and arid valleys, treeless barren landscape, yak caravans, colorfully painted mud-brick houses, and striking canyons. The stunning views of mountains like Annapurna (8,091 m), Nilgiri (7,061 m), and Dhaulagiri (8,167 m) makes the medieval walled Kingdom of Mustang more fascinating and gorgeous.

Mustang is considered as one of the most picturesque regions of Nepal because of its gorgeous colorful landscape: colored by natural earth pigments—red, blue, brown, and yellows—set opposite the backdrop of distant snow-capped Himalayas. The trail to Upper Mustang goes through high altitude desert, climbing along the huge valley of the Kali Gandaki River. The gorge from which Kali Gandaki River flows through is considered the world's deepest gorge.

You will find some of Nepal's oldest Buddhist monasteries along with ancient and rustic villages with beautiful whitewashed houses during this trek. Later you leave Kali Gandaki valley and head higher into the tranquil environment of Upper Mustang, with its peaceful vibes enclosed by its many rocky and barren hills. Passing through the villages of Chele, Geling, Dhakmar, and Charang, you finally reach the walled capital of the Forbidden Kingdom, Lo Manthang. The colorful deserts of Lo Manthang shine brilliantly behind the whitewashed monasteries of the ancient kingdom, making it a treat for the eyes.

Apart from the breathtaking landscapes, the trek exposes you to the culture of the famous Thakali community and also to the unique culture of the Lhopa community in Lo Manthang. This area is considered as one of the most interesting and picturesque places in Nepal. The whole area has an isolated and mystical feel to it, enchanting and inspiring visitors to this region. Since Mustang is a rain-shadow area, one can go for this trek during any time of the year.

Upper Mustang Trek Altitude Chart

itinerary.title: Arrive in Kathmandu (Tribhuwan International Airport) and transfer to your hotel.
itinerary.html: Upon arrival in Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, you will be warmly welcomed and picked by our representatives who will then drop you at the hotel. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Travel by tourist bus from Kathmandu to Pokhara, 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you will take an early morning bus to Pokhara. (as an option you can take a 20 minute's flight to Pokhara). Upon arrival in Pokhara, you will be transferred to your hotel. You can rest for a while and then wander around the Lakeside streets or do fun activities such as boating and cycling. Overnight at a hotel in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Fly from Pokhara to Jomsom and trek to Kagbeni (2,810 m / 9,219 ft), 2-3 hours.
itinerary.html: Another 20 minutes short flight will take you straight from Pokhara to Jomsom, the headquarters of Mustang district and also the starting point of this trek. The flight takes you through the deepest gorge in the world, Kali Gandaki Gorge, to reach the windy town of Jomsom. Shortly after arriving in Jomsom, you will ascend through the riverbed of Kali Gandaki River to reach Kagbeni, a beautiful village serving as the gateway to Upper Mustang. Overnight in Kagbeni.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kagbeni to Chele (3,050 m / 10,006 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: After the permit check, you continue to move upstream through the Kali Gandaki riverbed, enjoying the picturesque sceneries along the trail. This route will first take you to Tangbe village with the white-washed houses, apple plantations, and buckwheat and barley fields. You then cross the river and walk gradually along the edges to reach Chele, where you can see beautiful houses made in Tibetan style. Overnight in Chele.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chele to Syambochen (3,800 m / 12,467 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: This is the day of crossing many small passes. The trek leads on a steep trail uphill to Dajori La (3,735 m) via Taklam La (3,624 m) taking you to the village of Samar. From there, the trail goes up and down over a gorge and crosses Bhena La (3,860 m) and Yamdo La (3,860 m) to reach Syambochen.

itinerary.title: Trek from Syambochen to Charang (3,560 m / 11,680 ft),7-8 hours.
itinerary.html: After crossing Syamgboche La (3,850 m) and descend steeply along the barley fields until you reach Geling. The trek from Geling to Charang climbs amid barren hills and is dotted with many small monasteries and Chortens, emitting peaceful vibes. You ascend on a quite path to reach the village of Ghami, and then you cross the longest Mani wall of Mustang before walking on a cliff above a stream to reach Dhakmar. The trail from Dhakmar to Charang is filled with colorful bare cliffs, and you may also notice few blue sheep grazing along the way. You can visit the 4 centuries old monastery of Charang after a short rest. Overnight in Charang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Charang to Lo-Manthang (3,809 m / 12,497 ft), 5-6 hours
itinerary.html: From Charang, you move uphill over an edge before entering the Tholung valley where trek takes you to the dry scenery that is so often seen in the photos of Mustang. Except for a small Chorten and a few abandoned herders’ huts, the trail is quite as you climb uphill bounded by sand dunes on each side. You eventually reach Lo La (3,950 m) and get the first glimpse of your destination, the walled city of Lo Manthang. You will then descend along the picturesque trail until you reach the ruins of the ancient fortress protecting the hidden kingdom. Overnight in Lo Manthang.

itinerary.title: Exploring day in Lo-Manthang (3,809 m / 12,497 ft).
itinerary.html: Today you stay in Lo-Manthang discovering the majesties of the city adorned with ancient monasteries, traditional shops, and the king’s palace. You will visit the Monastery of Victory in Namgyal and also visit many other monasteries preserving the true virtue of ancient Tibetan Buddhism. The colorful deserts of Lo-Manthang accompany you as you explore this capital city of the former Kingdom of Lo. Overnight in Lo-Manthang.

itinerary.title: Trek back from Lo-Manthang to Ghami (3,520 m / 11,549 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Waving goodbye to Lo Manthang, you make a gradual climb to reach Chogo La (4,280 m), which serves the last view of the fortress city. Continuing to follow the trail, you first ascend and then descend along the grey mountains to reach Ghar Gumba. Ghar Gompa is one of the oldest monasteries in Upper Mustang which is still active till date and bears breathtaking rock paintings. From Ghar Gompa, the trail descends to Dhakmar, and then in a while, you will step in the vicinity of Ghami village where you will stay for the night.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ghami to Samar (3,660 m / 12,008 ft), 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Leaving Ghami, you ascend to cross Ghami La (3,765 m) and you continue the uphill climb until reaching Nyi La (4,010 m). An amazing view of Nilgiri (7,061 m) can be observed from the top of Nyi la (4,010 m). After spending some time at the pass, you descend past small villages until you reach Samar. Overnight in Samar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Samar to Kagbeni (2,810 m / 9,219 ft), then drive from Kagbeni to Jomsom, 6–7 hours.
itinerary.html: After an early breakfast, you begin your trek back toward Kagbeni. The trail follows the Mustang Khola before climbing above its dramatic gorge and passing through Chele. You then rejoin the Kali Gandaki River and retrace the scenic route along its valley, enjoying the changing landscapes before reaching the charming village of Kagbeni, known for its traditional houses and apple orchards. From Kagbeni, you will drive to Jomsom, where you will spend the night.

itinerary.title: Fly back from Jomsom - to Pokhara, 20 minutes.
itinerary.html: Today marks the end of your trekking adventure. After breakfast, you will take a scenic flight from Jomsom to Pokhara, enjoying spectacular aerial views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges. Upon arrival, you will be transferred to your hotel. The rest of the day is free to relax or explore the beautiful lakeside city of Pokhara at your own pace. Overnight at a hotel in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Travel by tourist bus from Pokhara to Kathmandu.,7-8 hours
itinerary.html: To return to Kathmandu, (as an option you can take a 20 minute's flight to Kathmandu) take a 7-8 hour bus long drive. You will witness amazing landscapes either way. Upon reaching Kathmandu, feel free to stroll around the places of Kathmandu.. Overnight at a  hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Transfer to airport for your onward destination
itinerary.html: Our representatives will drop you at the airport 3 hours before the scheduled time of your flight.

faqs.q: Where is Upper Mustang?
faqs.a: Upper Mustang is an exotic destination that is situated in the north of the Mustang district, Nepal, near the border with Tibet. It is part of the Annapurna region and known for its unique trans Himalayan scenery, Tibetan Buddhist culture and picturesque villages.

faqs.q: Why is the Upper Mustang Trek unique?
faqs.a: The Upper Mustang Trek offers a completely new experience when compared to other trekking destinations in Nepal. Instead of green forests and snowy landscapes you will explore a high-altitude desert with impressive cliffs, sandstone rocks, caves and ruins of ancient settlements.

faqs.q: What are the prime attractions of the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a:
The main sights of the trek include:

  • Tibetan culture and way of life
  • Lo Manthang – capital city of the former Kingdom of Lo
  • Ancient monasteries and Buddhist chortens
  • Caves of Chosar and cave settlements
  • Kali Gandaki Gorge – the deepest gorge in the world
  • Sights of Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Nilgiri and other Himalayan peaks

faqs.q: What is the duration of the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a:
The standard trek to the Upper Mustang by Base Camp Adventure requires 10 days. The itinerary features

  • A flight from Pokhara to Jomsom
  • Treks from Kagbeni, Chele, Geling, Tsarang to Lo Manthang
  • One day excursion in Lo Manthang
  • Trek back to Ghami and Jomsom
  • And then a flight to Pokhara.

If you want, you can extend your itinerary into a longer one as well.

faqs.q: Why is Upper Mustang named the "Mini Tibet of Nepal"?
faqs.a:
Upper Mustang is called the Mini Tibet of Nepal due to the fact that its nature, climate, architecture, and culture are similar to Tibet. On this trek, you will be able to see:

  • Monasteries of Tibetan Buddhism
  • Prayer flags and mani walls
  • Stone villages
  • Food and way of life similar to those of the Tibetans
  • Tibetan influenced religious customs and traditions

Isolation of the region helped to keep this culture alive.

faqs.q: Is the Upper Mustang Trek appropriate for all age groups?
faqs.a: Upper Mustang Trek can be done by trekkers of various age groups if they have good physical fitness and are well prepared for the journey. In addition, trekkers must be ready to walk several hours a day in high altitudes. Positive attitude and good endurance are important.

faqs.q: At what altitude does the Upper Mustang Trek reach its peak?
faqs.a:
The Upper Mustang Trek features Lugri La Pass, which is located at 4,200 m or 13,780 feet above sea level that you will cross on your way back from Lo Manthang. 

There are several high-altitude villages where you'll stay overnight such as Lo Manthang, which is 3,730 m above sea level, Tsarang (3,490 m) and Kagbeni (2,800 m).

faqs.q: Is the Upper Mustang Trek difficult?
faqs.a:
The Upper Mustang Trek is considered a moderate journey. The trek doesn't have technical requirements. However, trekkers must be ready to walk and spend a number of days in mountainous terrain at high altitude. In the course of the trek you will experience:

  • 5-7 hours of walking each day
  • Climbing and descending the high passes such as Taklam La, Choya La, Lo La Pass, Lugri La Pass etc
  • Dry and windy environment
  • High altitude conditions

With proper preparation, the trek is doable for a beginner.

faqs.q: Is experience necessary for the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a:
Previous trekking experience for the Upper Mustang Trek is not mandatory but it will be helpful if you have some. For beginner trekkers it is necessary to:

  • Do regular walking 
  • Develop a strong cardiovascular system
  • Work on leg and core muscle strength
  • Practice hiking with a backpack

Good physical condition will help you make your trek more comfortable.

faqs.q: How physically fit do I need to be for the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a:
For the Upper Mustang Trek, you'll have to be reasonably fit. This trek isn't technical; however, you have to be able to walk around 5 to 7 hours a day, on rugged mountain trails with a daypack. 

Good stamina and endurance for the trek are necessary since you have to pass some mountain passes. You should train for one to two months before the trek to be able to enjoy it better and not feel too tired along the way.

faqs.q: What items do I need to carry for the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a: You will have to pack comfortable trekking clothes like a down jacket, thermal base layers and waterproof outer layers. In addition, carry trekking shoes, socks, gloves, a hat, sunglasses, sunblock, a water bottle, medicines, and other trekking gear.

faqs.q: Can I rent or buy my trekking equipment in Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Yes, you can. There is a range of trekking gear available to either rent or buy in Kathmandu particularly in Thamel. The necessities for trekking such as jackets, sleeping bags, trekking poles, backpacks and boots can be found in most stores.

faqs.q: From where does the Upper Mustang Trek begin and what route does it follow?
faqs.a:
The Upper Mustang Trek generally starts with a scenic flight from Pokhara to Jomsom, which is the gateway to the Mustang region. From Jomsom onwards, the trekking trail is along the Kali Gandaki valley and takes the travelers through several traditional Himalayan villages. 

Some of these villages are Kagbeni, Chele, Geling, Tsarang, Lo Manthang, and Ghami. These villages have something unique in terms of landscape, Tibetan culture, monasteries built hundreds of years ago, and majestic views of the mountains.

faqs.q: What are the main villages to be visited on the trek?
faqs.a:
There are several scenic villages that are encountered along the way on the Upper Mustang Trek. Jomsom is from where start on the trail, Kagbeni is the entrance point to the Upper Mustang, you will proceed to Chele where Tibetan culture can be experienced. 

Further down the trek are Geling, which is a traditional village surrounded by a number of monasteries and barley farms, and Tsarang, which contains an old palace and monastery. The most remarkable site on the tour is Lo Manthang which is the former capital of the Kingdom of Lo with its royal palace and monasteries.

faqs.q: What is explored during the leisure day in Lo Manthang?
faqs.a:
Exploration day in Lo Manthang is when the best cultural, historical, and spiritual sights in the ancient walled city will be visited while your body will have an opportunity to get used to the altitude. 

You will visit the historic King's Palace, Namgyal Gompa, Chamba Lhakhang, Thugchen Gompa, and Chosar Caves, which are very old meditation chambers and archaeological sites. Besides, you will see the surrounding villages, meet the locals, and learn more about their lifestyle influenced by Tibet.

faqs.q: How much time do we walk every day?
faqs.a:
For the Upper Mustang Trek, you have to walk an average of about 5 to 7 hours per day depending upon your route. Some days can be short while others can be long as per the weather, trail conditions, and the overall pace of the group. 

There will be a steady pace with occasional breaks for resting, photographing and enjoying the wonderful natural vistas around you.

faqs.q: Is there a chance for customization of the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a:
Yes, indeed. Itineraries of the Upper Mustang Trek can be customized according to the availability of your time, physical condition, budget, and interests. 

Depending on whether you want to take more time to visit Lo Manthang, explore monasteries and cave structures, have cultural interaction with the people, attend the Tiji festival or any other adjustments to make, we will plan a customized journey accordingly.

faqs.q: Which permits are required for the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a:
The required permits for the Upper Mustang Trek include

  • Upper Mustang Restricted Area Permit
  • Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP)

Base Camp Adventure arranges all necessary permits and paperwork allowing you to enjoy a hassle free journey. The permits are made available to you prior to the trek.

faqs.q: Why is a special permit needed for Upper Mustang?
faqs.a:
The Upper Mustang region is situated close to the border of Tibet and comprises many natural and cultural heritage sites. Restricted permits help in:

  • Protection of ancient culture
  • Conservation of the environment
  • Management of tourism impact
  • Maintain local traditions

faqs.q: Can I make an independent trek to Upper Mustang?
faqs.a:
No. It is not possible to undertake an independent trip to Upper Mustang. According to the guidelines set by the Nepalese government, a trekker should travel with:

  • A licensed guide
  • A registered trekking agency

We offer our customers experienced guides for their safe and comfortable travel.

faqs.q: Which is the Best Season to Visit Upper Mustang?
faqs.a:
Upper Mustang Trek can be undertaken in all seasons since it falls in the rain-shadow zone of the Himalayas where monsoon rains are minimal. Still, spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) are the best seasons for trekking. 

During spring, there will be pleasant weather, clear sky, and beautiful mountain scenery, and trekkers will have a chance to experience the wonderful Tiji Festival, which is the most important festival of Upper Mustang. Autumn too will offer stable weather and excellent visibility.

faqs.q: Is the Upper Mustang Trek possible during the monsoon?
faqs.a: Yes. Unlike other trekking sites in Nepal, Upper Mustang gets very little rainfall in June, July and August. Upper Mustang is one of the best places for trekking during the monsoon due to its location in the rain shadow of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountains.

faqs.q: Is it feasible to undertake the trekking journey in the winter season in Upper Mustang?
faqs.a:
It is possible to trek in the winter season in Upper Mustang, but it is comparatively harder due to extremely cold temperatures, strong winds, the snow at higher elevations and the limited operations of teahouses. 

Appropriate winter equipment and preparations are a must if you want to enjoy your trek during this time.

faqs.q: What weather conditions can I anticipate?
faqs.a: The weather in the Upper Mustang area is usually dry and windy. The days at low altitudes are quite warm and sunny, and you will experience strong winds in exposed areas. Likewise, you expect cold mornings and nights and freezing temperatures in the winter months.

faqs.q: What kind of accommodation will be available during the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a:
Accommodation will be organized in local tea houses during the Upper Mustang Trek. 

Tea houses offer basic facilities such as twin-sharing rooms, toilets, and common dining areas. Facilities become less available as the trek approaches more remote areas but still they offer comfortable places for sleeping after long days of trekking.

faqs.q: What kind of food is available during the trek?
faqs.a: Tea houses along the Upper Mustang Trek serve trekkers a variety of nutritious food to keep them energized during the trip. Some of the food items served are Dal Bhat, noodles, pasta, soup, momo, bread, pancakes, eggs and traditional Tibetan meals.

faqs.q: Is there any availability of drinking water on the trekking route?
faqs.a:
Yes. There is drinking water available in tea houses and villages throughout the Upper Mustang Trek. You can get boiled water in tea houses at an additional charge (USD 1-3) per liter. 

It is recommended to have reusable water bottles to refill and have regular hydration. Also carry along water purification tablets for safe water from natural sources like taps or streams.

faqs.q: Is there a facility to charge my devices?
faqs.a: Yes, charging facilities are available in most tea houses on the Upper Mustang Trek trail, but they come at extra costs (1-4 per hour). Since the electricity may be scarce in remote locations, which means it is wise to carry a power bank.

faqs.q: Is the mobile network and Wi-Fi available?
faqs.a: Mobile network and Wi-Fi are available in certain villages and tea houses, but the connection may not be strong enough or even unavailable in remote high areas. It is recommended to download important information and maps in advance.

faqs.q: How much does the Upper Mustang Trek costs?
faqs.a: The standard Upper Mustang Trek costs around $1,500-$1,800 per person, depending on various factors such as group size, services provided, transport, and customization. The package includes all kinds of accommodation, food, transport, permits, guide, porter and other trekking-related logistics.

faqs.q: How do I make a booking for the Upper Mustang Trek through Base Camp Adventure?
faqs.a: The Upper Mustang Trek can be booked easily by mailing us, making calls on our contact number, messaging on WhatsApp or using our online inquiry form. A 30% deposit is required to confirm your booking and arrange the necessary trek logistics.

faqs.q: Is it necessary to have travel insurance for the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a: Yes, travel insurance is very important for the Upper Mustang Trek. The insurance must include coverage for trekking at the high altitudes, emergency medical care, helicopter evacuation and cancellation or disruption of the journey.

faqs.q: How will I reach the starting point of the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a: The starting point of the trek is Jomsom where you fly from Pokhara. After reaching Jomsom, you trek through the Kali Gandaki valley, reach Kagbeni and enter the region of Upper Mustang.

faqs.q: What will happen in case of the delay or cancellation of the flight from Pokhara to Jomsom?
faqs.a: Flights from Pokhara to Jomsom may be influenced by weather changes. In case of any delay or cancellation of the flight we will do our best to accommodate the next available flight. Please consider some flexibility in your schedule.

faqs.q: Is it possible to reach Upper Mustang by jeep rather than trekking?
faqs.a: Yes. The Upper Mustang region can be explored by jeep. In addition, you can also combine the Jeep tour with trekking according to the specific route, time, and your personal preferences. This option lets you ride in a jeep for some parts of the rough road and hike on local trails for other parts.

faqs.q: Is the Upper Mustang Trek safe?
faqs.a: Yes, the Upper Mustang Trek is safe if you prepare well for it and have an experienced guide with you. But at high altitude, winds, rough terrain, and changing weather conditions could pose some problems; therefore, it is wise to listen to your guide’s safety tips.

faqs.q: What happens in case of an emergency during the trek?
faqs.a: Your guide will evaluate the situation if any emergency arises during the trek. Then he will make sure that appropriate help is provided according to the severity of the problem such as descending to a lower altitude or arranging emergency evacuation.

faqs.q: Is there any helicopter evacuation facility available in Upper Mustang?
faqs.a: Yes, helicopter evacuation can be organized in case of emergency, depending upon the weather conditions, visibility, availability of the helicopter and various other operational considerations. A comprehensive insurance cover including helicopter evacuation is highly recommended.

faqs.q: Is there a chance of altitude sickness while trekking through the Upper Mustang?
faqs.a: There can be chances of suffering from altitude sickness when trekking in the Upper Mustang as it passes through terrain that exceeds 4,000 m Though the risk is relatively low as compared to other alpine treks, but every individual is different and reacts differently at heights. So it is important to acclimatize properly.

faqs.q: How to prevent altitude sickness?
faqs.a:
In order to reduce the risk of altitude sickness, it is imperative to move slowly and steadily, drink lots of water, have nutritious meals, have enough rest and do not indulge in drinking alcohol. 

Our professional guides are capable of recognizing the early symptoms of altitude sickness and will keep an eye on your condition throughout the journey. If any symptoms arise, then they are well equipped to deal with the situation.

faqs.q: Is it essential to give tips on the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a: Tips are not a compulsion but it is always seen as a good idea for expressing your gratitude to your guide, porter and all other support staff who assisted you during your trekking trip. It is a part of the trekking culture of Nepal.

faqs.q: What amount of cash will you require for the Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.a:
It is advisable to keep some extra cash in Nepali rupees (USD 250-500) for personal expenditures like food, beverages, recharging of phone, Internet connection, hot water, souvenirs, and other optional facilities. 

There are limited banking facilities in the remote areas; hence, it would be wise to withdraw enough cash before beginning your trek.

faqs.q: How much should I tip my guide and porter?
faqs.a: It completely depends on you and our level of satisfaction with the service that they have provided during the trekking period. It is advisable that the tip for the guide should be USD 10 to 20 per day and for the porter, USD 5 to 10 daily.

summary: In Weekend Hiking Tour, we make a tour of some of the most important as well as interesting cultural and natural landscapes of Kathmandu Valley.

seo.title: Weekend Hiking Tour in Nepal | 6 Days Tour and Hiking in Kathmandu
seo.description: In Weekend Hiking Tour, we make a tour of some of the most important as well as interesting cultural and natural landscapes of Kathmandu Valley.

cover.alt: Weekend Hiking Tour to Nepal IV

overview:
The 6-days of Nepal tour has been designed to cater to the needs of those who wish to make a cultural tour of the valley, or those who are on a pilgrimage tour in Nepal. The Kathmandu valley boasts of a considerably high number of cultural sites recognized by UNESCO as the World Heritage Sites. All these sites in the Kathmandu Valley are related to the spiritual traditions practiced in the region. The valley blends different culture and lifestyle practiced in the region in its own way. The thousands of temples, stupas, pagodas and monuments inside the valley have made Kathmandu famous in the world as the City of Temples. The mountains encircling the valley surround three medieval cities – Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur. Each city inside the valley has an artistic exposition of graceful temples, elegant palaces, brick-paved courtyards and quaint streets. Besides the three cities, there are also a number of other important sites in the periphery of the mountains. In this trip of Weekend Hiking Tour, we make a tour of some of the most important as well as interesting cultural and natural landscapes of Kathmandu Valley.

For those visitors who are inexperience in walking up and down on hills and who have little time to experience the high mountains of Majestic Himalayas and Nepalese culture they can choose these short and easy hiking trips around Nagarkot and Nala /Dhulikhel. Here are the collected of opportunities for short lowland hiking trip and walking tours in Nepal. Here is not much difference between Hiking and Trekking in Nepal. Hiking is an initial part of trekking and relatively easier that still involve up and down on rural hilly areas below 3,000 m but offers glimpse of High Mountains view. Nagarkot and Dhulikhel Hill stations of Nepal are very popular for hiking tours and as well as cultural and historical tours.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Kathmandu (Tribhuwan International Airport) and transfer to Hotel. Overnight stay in Kathmandu.
itinerary.html: Upon your arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, our representative will receive you and then transfer you to your hotel. Overnight in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Full day Kathmandu city Sightseeing:
itinerary.html: Today you go for a directed tour to four of the seven UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Kathmandu. After breakfast, you will visit Swayambhunath temple from where you can get a panoramic view of the Kathmandu valley. Then you will visit the palace and temples of Kathmandu Durbar Square before visiting the holy temple of Pashupatinath. The Aryaghat alongside Pashupatinath, on the banks of the Bagmati River, is a famous cremation site for the Hindus. Afterward, you will visit the Buddhists shrine of Boudhanath, which is one of the largest stupas in the world. You will then drive back to the hotel for overnight stay.

itinerary.title: An hour of drive from Kathmandu – Sundarijal and hike to Chisapani Village (2150M) 5:30HRS
itinerary.html: You start the day with a short drive from Kathmandu to Sundarijal and begin your hiking from Sundarijal towards Chisapani. Getting your permit tickets from the check post inside the verdant forest of Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park, you begin to climb through the forest enjoying the peaceful environment. As you hike, you come upon the first settlement en route i.e. Mulkharka which is a small Tamang village. After ascending for some hours, the trail takes you downhill through the ridge amid a forest of oak and rhododendron to reach Chisapani. Overnight in Chisapani.

itinerary.title: Chisapani – Nagarkot (2163M) 05 to 06 hrs
itinerary.html: Today you will witness the breathtaking view of sunrise and the play of its colors upon the gorgeously spread mountains on the skyline in Chisapani. Then you make your way towards Chisapani via the beautiful forests filled with various trees and beautiful birds. Nagarkot is one of the most popular destinations around Kathmandu to witness the majesty of the Nepal Himalayas and also the views of mesmerizing sunrise and sunset. Overnight in Nagarkot.

itinerary.title: Nagarkot – Nala / Dhulikhel - Kathmandu. 6- 7 hrs.
itinerary.html: Starting the day early, you will hike up to Nagarkot View Point to watch the ever-so-gorgeous sunrise over the various mountain ranges dominating the skyline of Nagarkot; from Langtang range to Mahalangur Himalayan range, Nagarkot features it all. Afterward, you start your journey to Dhulikhel. The trail features walking through beautiful rural villages and lush forests with different vegetation. The trail lights up in colors during the spring season as the rhododendrons are in full bloom along with other wildflowers. After the long hike, you reach Nala and then transfer to Kathmandu. Overnight in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Transfer to international airport for final departure.
itinerary.html: Today you will be driven to the international airport to catch your scheduled flight back home.

title: Yala Peak Climbing

seo.title: Yala Peak Climbing, cost, itinerary, reviews - Base Camp Adventure
seo.description: Yala Peak climbing is an ideal peakfor beginners, this is one of the many climbing peaks of Nepal Himalayas which is located in the famous Langtang region.

overview:
Yala Peak climbing is an ideal for beginner climbers, this peak is one of the many climbing peaks of  Nepal Himalayas which is located in the famous Langtang region. Standing on top of Yala Peak (5,500 m), you get to relish a stunning view of Langtang Lirung (7,227 m), Dorje Lakpa (6,966 m), and Shishapangma (8,046 m), and Gangchempo (6,388 m), among others. Climbing Yala Peak (5,500 m) is non-technical and easy, yet adventurous. This trek is perfect for people having good physical fitness and little to no climbing experience.

You will take an early morning drive passing through the terraced field, small villages, and wonderful sceneries to reach Syabru Besi from Kathmandu. You will go through dense oak and rhododendron forests, meadows, and glaciers to reach beautiful Tamang villages en route, where you will get a chance to observe their lifestyle, rich culture, and tradition. Many Mani walls, monasteries, and Chortens decorated with colorful prayer flags are reached during the trek. A day’s rest in Kyanjin Gompa, the most sacred monastery in this region, to climb Tserko Ri (5,011 m) prepares you for climbing the summit of Yala Peak (5,500 m).

The trail to Yala Peak summit (5,500 m) will be covered with ice, and you have to use different climbing tools like rope, ice-ax, and crampons for a successful ascent. After reaching the summit, you will spend some quality time there as you get the most majestic views of the Langtang Himal range, Ganesh Himal range, Langshisa range, and Dorje Lakpa (6,966 m) in Nepal and Shishapangma (8,013 m) in the Tibet.

With a heart filled with the sense of achievement, you head back down to Kyanjin Gompa and follow the trails of Langtang valley via Langtang village, Ghodatabela, and Lama Hotel and later traverse through the forest to reach Syabru Besi as a mark of the end of your exciting journey.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu and meet our staff and transfer to hotel
itinerary.html: As you arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, you will be met by our office representative and then be transferred to the hotel by private car. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Syabru Besi. 6-7 hours.
itinerary.html: Today you move north of Kathmandu driving along the picturesque view of lush hills, terraced fields, and roadside settlements to reach Syabru Besi. You can explore Syabru Besi Bazarin the evening after arrival. Overnight in a Guest House.

itinerary.title: Trek to Lama Hotel (2500m). 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: You first descend to Langtang River and crossing the suspension bridge over Langtang River, you ascend towards Lama Hotel following the trails of the river. You cross the damp bamboo forest in Bamboo village and then follow the trail along rhododendron trees to finally reach Lama Hotel. You may see different wildlife such as yellow-throated martens, wild boars, red pandas, and black bears en route to Lama Hotel. Overnight in Lama Hotel.

itinerary.title: Trek to Langtang (3100m). 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: The day starts with a gentle climb and later goes on steeper trails through oak and rhododendron forests above Langtang River. As you ascend, you can get amazing views of Langtang Lirung (7,227 m), Naya Kanga (5,844 m), and other snowy peaks. Cross the wooden bridge over the Langtang River and come across the field of Ghodatabela. The trail then widens to take you to the large Tamang settlement of Langtang, a picturesque village situated below the gorgeous Langtang Lirung (7,227 m). Although significantly affected by the 2015 earthquake, most of the village has been rebuilt; an opportunity for you to listen to the stories of resilience is shown by the locals. Overnight in Langtang.

itinerary.title: Trek to Kyanjin Gompa (3750m). 3-4 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail to Kyanjin Gompa winds through small villages and ascends past a large Chorten. Climb slowly through the impressive Mani wall and cross a stream to the village of Mundu. After crossing small streams with wooden bridges, you can finally reach the most sacred monastery of Langtang region, Kyanjin Gompa. Langtang Lirung (7,227 m), Yubra (6,264 m)

itinerary.title: Excursion to Tserko Ri (5033m)
itinerary.html: Today is the rest day to acclimatize. You can hike up to Tserko Ri (4,984 m) for a 360-degree mountain view, including the peaks of Yala (5,500 m), Dagpache (6,567 m), PangenDopku (5,930 m), and so on. You later hike back to Kyanjin and visit its Yala Cheese factory, where you can also taste the freshly made cheese. Overnight in Kyanjin.

itinerary.title: Trek to Yala Peak Base Camp (4800m). 5-6 hours
itinerary.html: You start your climb to Yala Peak Base Camp by walking through the Basin of Langtang River. Then you climb on rocky moraines past a few dry meadows to finally reach the base of the peak that you will be summiting the next day. Upon reaching, you can practice your climbing techniques with the Yala Peak (5,500 m) as your spectator. Overnight in Yala Peak Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Base Camp-Yala Peak summit (5500m)-Kyanjing Gompa. 9-10 hours
itinerary.html: Today is the day you reach the summit of Yala Peak (5,500 m). You will start the climb early following the instructions of your climbing guide diligently. You continuously make your way through the slippery trails to finally conquer the peak of Yala (5,500 m). From the summit, you will get a ravishing 360-degree view of various mountain ranges and also of the Langtang valley below. After the successful summit, you climb back down to Yala Peak Base Camp, from where you head to Kyanjin Gompa for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Trek to Ghodatabela (3050m). 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: After having your breakfast, clicking photos in this wonderful place, and admiring the mighty Himalayas around you, you follow the same trail back to reach Ghodatabela. You descend and ascend through the bumpy trails to reach Langtang village, from where you descend gradually to finally reach Ghodatabela. Overnight in Ghodatabela.

itinerary.title: Trek to Syabru Besi. 5-6 hours.
itinerary.html: The trail slopes down through the forest where you come across small Chortens. The trail gets bumpy and stony as you walk further, but you may encounter red pandas, boars, monkeys, and various species of birds en route. Retracing your way throughout the trek, you reach Thulo Syabru for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Drive back to Kathmandu.
itinerary.html: You drive back via Dhunche. Kalikasthan, Betrawati, Trishuli Bazaar, and Ranipauwa to finally arrive in Kathmandu. Back in Kathmandu, you can celebrate your successful Yala Peak Climbing with a fun-filled evening in Thamel. Overnight at a hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Transfer to airport to return to home.
itinerary.html: Today is your final day at Nepal. After breakfast, our team member will drop you at the airport before the scheduled time of your flight.
